title: bun changeset publish in monorepo does not update the "workspace:*"
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.2+b131639cc
What platform is your computer?
macos
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Hi,
I'm reopening this issue (previously closed as not planned) for follow-up:
#16074
Migrating from pnpm to bun causes all published packages to include workspace:* in their final package.json. As a result, anyone who tries to install the package receives an error such as:
Cannot resolve package version "workspace:*"

A related issue on the Changesets side:
changesets/changesets#1468
What is the expected behavior?
all 'workspace:*' would be replaced by the related package version (after publishing)
  "dependencies": {
    "@myPackage/config": "1.2.3",
  }
What do you see instead?
  "dependencies": {
    "@myPackage/config": "workspace:*",
  }
Additional information
As a temporary workaround, I manually replace all occurrences of workspace:*.
Ideally, this should be fixed directly within the bun publish command by:

Incrementing the version
Replacing workspace:* at publication time

Alternatively:

Ensuring compatibility with Changesets

Feel free to share any advice or suggestions for a temporary fix

What steps can reproduce the bug?
import { test, expect } from 'bun:test'

test('Bun.spawn captures echo output', async () => {
  const proc = Bun.spawn(['echo', 'hello'] , { stdout: 'pipe' })
  const stdout = await new Response(proc.stdout).text()
  await proc.exited
  expect(stdout).toBe('hello\n')    // fails - returns empty string
  expect(proc.exitCode).toBe(0)
})

✓ Bun.spawn captures echo output

- "

// standalone.ts
const proc = Bun.spawn(['echo', 'hello'], { stdout: 'pipe' })
const stdout = await new Response(proc.stdout).text()
console.log('stdout:', JSON.stringify(stdout))

$ bun standalone.ts
stdout: "hello\n"  # Works correctly!

There are ongoing issues with MongoDB memory leaks when using the current nodejs MongoDB driver under Bun. A native implementation could help avoid these problems and provide more stable, predictable behavior.
#24118
#12117
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I’m proposing a built-in MongoDB driver for Bun, similar to Bun’s existing built-in SQL drivers. A native driver could offer better performance, tighter integration with Bun’s runtime, and improved memory management.

What is the problem this feature would solve?
Isolating only running the tests who failed for your next test run. Today you would have to select it manually through a file or a specific test name match.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Similar to pytest, there is a --lf flag that lets you run the tests who last failed. This means that pytest keeps state over which tests failed/succeeded the last time it was ran.
What alternatives have you considered?
No response

title: Shim express to bun.serve
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
The title speaks for itself really. Even though there are many fun and new api frameworks these days, people aren’t going to re-write many of their existing apps, especially in the enterprise, to support a fancy new framework when express works fine. Express is huge with a large community.
It’s probably a significant effort, but I think bun would benefit having a native implementation of express 4/5. Express is pretty unopinionated, it doesn’t change that often and not by much, it should be easy enough to keep track with it once the full feature set is supported.
This would also speed up popular frameworks like nestjs.

title: Better logging
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
I'm writing my first library for Bun, and I've got no experience in writing JS/TS libs, so maybe it's not standard approach, but I tend to leave TRACE logs...
Unfortunately, despite there being logLevel in bunfig.toml. And all browsers supporting at least 4 levels of logging it's not easily possible to hide/disable console.trace() or console.debug() logs, which leads to my console being extremally bloated by all the requests and responses (I'm making API library)
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
The feature is quite simple. And has been implemented by multiple libraries, and other programming languages.
It's logLevels support for all console functions
Given that there are different console functions so it would make sense that they are not just all aliases to each other.
My proposal are those levels which you could set in bunfig.toml:

Error - for console.error()
Warn - for console.warn()
Info/Log - for console.info() & console.log()
Trace/Verbose/Debug - for console.trace() & console.debug() (or separating them into 2 levels)

Or something like this.
It's pretty trivial to implement such functionality in Runtime so I reckon it's not the highest priority, but it would be cool if Bun had a proper logging system.
Implementing such functionality natively should also include logging to file (i.e. on stderr and stdout only show INFO level and save all Debug level to some file, of course it should be customizable, but that shouldn't be too hard to implement)
It doesn't have to be something complicated.
Alternatively, you could leave current console functionality as is and add some special Bun.log functionality
What alternatives have you considered?
The simplest alternatives are:


if (bun.env.TRACE != 0) console.trace = () => {}

Deleting all console.trace(), but it really makes it easier to debug, when you can simply look through all requests/responses when something needs fixing
Using external logging libraries, but that would force users of my library to use the chosen library. Also, I'm trying to make my own library without using anything not included in Bun APIs (everything I need is WebSocket, fetch(), Bun.serve())

title: Support WASM components and WIT files for richer types
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
I would like to be able to import WASM components directly from Bun and get rich type support (including complex object types). Currently it's not supported by Bun, and can only be partially supported by a custom loader (which I wrote here)
Notably, my loader

requires storing intermediate files (kind of ugly) because it's not built into Bun
may cause issues if you have a custom WASM loader for your project that are not WASM components (regular WASM modules). See #5303
generates a .d.ts file next to your WASM component due to #5314 as the type depends on the WASM file (i.e. I can't tell typescript to give every import the same type like "css -> string". It depends on the WIT of the specific WASM component)

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Background
This problem is meant to be solved using WASM Components which allows specifying richer details on what a WASM component expects in order to run properly, and importantly for us what types it expects in its public API (specified through an interface language (IDL) called WIT - WebAssembly Interface Types)
The dream of WASM components and WIT has been around since it reached stage 1 back in May 2022. Progress has been slow, but steady. With WASM components being one of the main topics of talks at the WASM I/O conference, interest is growing
WASM Components, although planned to work with browsers, has mainly come from the server-oriented side of the WASM community. As such, WASM Component version has been done in line with WASI - WebAssembly System Interface. WASI 0.2 which was the main release with WASM components came out in January 2024 (included WASM Components 0.2). WASI 0.3 though is in release candidate as of August 2025, with release planned later in 2025, and WASI 1.0 (which includes Component Model 1.0) is planned for 2026,
Hopes
Although WASM Components are not v1 yet, tooling is already in place to help solve the core reason for this issue creation.

Rust programs can already be compiled to WASM Components using cargo-components. Similar efforts with Zig could help Bun compile to something that works in the web easier, which is something people have discussed before
You can already generate JS interfaces from JCO using jco transpile. This is how I built my custom Bun loader
It is implemented in wasmtime so they're supported in one wasm runtime already

title: `fs.watch` stops emitting `change` events for a file after it is deleted and recreated (Linux: WSL2/Ubuntu)
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.3-canary.71+9a9473d4b
What platform is your computer?
Linux 5.15.167.4-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Disclaimer: this is a bug that Gemini 3 seems to have surfaced while extending some code that I'd started myself. I noticed that a directory with a file I was watching stopped surfacing change events after I deleted a watched file and then recreated it. The rename event for the recreated file would be emitted, but subsequent changes weren't being detected, even while changes to neighbouring files were picked up (neighbouring files not having been deleted and then recreated, in this context). Gemini tried numerous approaches to figure out the issue, and discovered that the repro script didn't reproduce the issue on Node - only on Bun. At that point it seemed worth raising as an issue, so I asked it to describe the problem concisely and to generate a minimal reproduction script with clear logging and comments.
---- Gemini's description of the issue, with subsequent notes and reproduction code: ----
When watching a directory using fs.watch, if a file within that directory is deleted and then immediately recreated (e.g. programmatically), the watcher correctly emits rename events for the deletion and the creation. However, subsequent modifications to the recreated file do not trigger any change events.
Reproduction Steps:

fs.watch(dirPath, ...)
Create test.txt inside dirPath.
Delete test.txt (Watcher emits rename).
Recreate test.txt (Watcher emits rename).
Modify test.txt (append/write).

What is the expected behavior?
Watcher emits change for step 5.
What do you see instead?
Watcher emits nothing for step 5. The file is effectively "dead" to the watcher.
Additional information

Restarting the directory watcher after step 4 does not fix it.
Starting a new non-polling fs.watch directly on the file path after step 4 also fails to detect changes.
fs.watchFile (polling) is the only workaround that currently works.
This appears to be specific to how the underlying inotify handle tracks (or fails to re-track) the inode after the delete/create cycle.

title: Bun.html`{unsafeInput}` to provide an easy way to sanitise input for html (like sql)
excerpt: Is there a suggested way to prevent XSS with server-generated HTML? eg let xss = '' Bun.serve({ routes: { '/': () => new Response(`Hi ${xss}`, { headers: { 'content-type': 'text/html' } }) } }) ... will result in the alert/malicious-js appearing for the user. Hono has html for tagged template literals which escape XSS (similar to how Bun's sql prevents against SQL injection method) so this is XSS safe: import { Hono } from 'hono' import { html, raw } from 'hono/html' let xss = '' export default new Hono().get('/', (c) => c.html(html`Hi ${xss}`)) Perhaps a Response.html (or Bun.html) could work like this: '/': () => Response.html`Hi ${xss}` '/': () => Bun.html`Hi ${xss}` ... as well as saving having to add the text/html content-type header (even better if it adds a if one is missing, too), similar to how Response.json() adds the JSON equivalent.

title: Sign the docker images or provide a method to validate them
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
I would like to verify the integrity of your Docker images using tools such as cosign. This allows me to ensure that the images, even if proxied or downloaded from alternative sources, remain uncompromised
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Before the Docker images are published, they should be signed using tools like cosign

For example, a validation would look like this
cosign verify \
      --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
      --certificate-identity-regexp https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/.github/workflows/ \
      oven/bun:1

What alternatives have you considered?
I am not aware of any secure alternative

title: Globals reference docs use outdated MDN/lib.dom.d.ts descriptions
excerpt:
What is the type of issue?
Documentation is incorrect, Documentation is confusing
What is the issue?
I believe TextEncoder + TextDecoder (and probably other things) use outdated strings from MDN, possibly via an oudated lib.dom.d.ts generation. Specifically for those two classes, they mention an ancient StringView proposal which is a bit confusing. I imagine there are other things this would clean up.
Related: microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#1940 (the string in lib.dom.d.ts was the same as the one used in bun/reference/globals until that PR), and - specifically - microsoft/TypeScript-DOM-lib-generator#1909.
The generated lib.dom.d.ts in the TS repo is 'correct' (typos aside), and this string hasn't mentioned StringView since at least TS5.3 (just from checking an old d.ts I had lying around), so it doesn't seem to be related to the dependent TS version
I couldn't find where the reference docs get built in the repo after a cursory search but happy to help if the right direction is easy enough to find.
Where did you find it?
https://bun.com/reference/globals/TextDecoder
https://bun.com/reference/globals/TextEncoder

imported content

imported content edited

title: Windows install script architecture check is broken due to operator precedence
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
Not relevant
What platform is your computer?
Windows on ARM
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Run the powershell install script on a Windows on ARM system.
powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1 | iex"
What is the expected behavior?
It should fail to install and print the following
Install Failed:
Bun for Windows is currently only available for x86 64-bit Windows.

What do you see instead?
Instead it installs successfully
########################################################################################################################################################## 100.0%
Bun 1.3.2 was installed successfully!
The binary is located at C:\Users\JoeyRobertson\.bun\bin\bun.exe

To get started, restart your terminal/editor, then type "bun"

Additional information
This is due to operator precedence rules in the powershell install script.
if (-not ((Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem)).SystemType -match "x64-based") {
  Write-Output "Install Failed:"
  Write-Output "Bun for Windows is currently only available for x86 64-bit Windows.`n"
  return 1
}
The conditional will always evaluate to $False because the -not operator has higher precedence than the -match operator.

title: Bun.Glob scan escapes `cwd` boundary with patterns like `.*/*`
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
No response
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.1.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
import { Glob } from "bun";

const glob = new Glob(".*/*");
const iterator = glob.scanSync({
  cwd: "/some/project/path",
  onlyFiles: false,
});

for (const item of iterator) {
  console.log(item);
}
Output:
../sibling-directory
../another-directory

What is the expected behavior?
Glob.scanSync() with a cwd parameter should never return paths outside that directory. All yielded paths should be relative to cwd and must not start with ../ or contain /../.
What do you see instead?
Returned paths escape current working directory when patterns match .. (parent directory reference).
Minimum pattern: .*/*
ie. pattern starts with . followed by a wildcard (*, ?, +), then contains / separator.
Mechanism:

. matches first dot in ..
* (or ?, +) matches second dot
/ acts as path separator
Pattern continues matching in parent directory

Globs that are safe:

.* - No matches (safe but useless)
.*/ - Matches only dirs within cwd
.git/**/* - Literal string after dot
./**/* - Explicit current dir prefix
**/* - Standard recursive glob

Additional information
The vulnerability persists even when in GlobScanOptions we pass dot: false and onlyFiles: true
This suggests that, too, onlyFiles does not work since scanning yields .. which points to directory.

title: Support for `bunx --package` to force download from npm instead of node_modules/.bin
excerpt:
Summary
Add support for the --package (or -p) option to bunx, matching the functionality available in npx. This option allows explicitly specifying which package(s) to install while running a different command, which is especially useful when the binary name differs from the package name or when a package contains multiple binaries.
Current Behavior
bunx some-command
# Attempts to install and run the "some-command" package
Desired Behavior
bunx --package=foo bar --bar-argument
# Installs the "foo" package but executes the "bar" binary from it
Use Cases

Binary name differs from package name: Some packages have different names than their executable commands
Multiple binaries in one package: When a package provides multiple executables and you want to run one that doesn't match the package name
Multiple packages needed: Install multiple packages to make their binaries available in PATH for the executed command

npx Reference Documentation
From the official npm documentation:
Syntax

npx --package=<pkg>[@<version>] <cmd> [args...]
npx -p <pkg>[@<specifier>] <cmd> [args...]
Multiple --package options can be specified

Description
Whatever packages are specified by the --package option will be provided in the PATH of the executed command, along with any locally installed package executables. The --package option may be specified multiple times to execute the supplied command in an environment where all specified packages are available.
References

npx documentation
Ubuntu manpage for npx

title: `upgradeTLS` is not supported server-side sockets.
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.3
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.1.0 arm64 arm
Description
At the time of writing, invoking upgradeTLS on server-side sockets is not supported.
As per a discussion with @cirospaciari, the issue seems to stem from the fact that it is impossible to trivially swap us_socket_context_t on a us_socket_t. Some of the issues are:

@cirospaciari mentioned that us_socket_context is shared between different sockets.
@cirospaciari also mentioned that there's no way for us to check whether a context is an SSL context or not.

Historically, our behavior has been to silently allow users to call upgradeTLS on server sockets, but this resulted in a plethora of crashes and unreliable behavior. As a stop-gap, we've decided to better communicate our lack of support in #25043.
The issues linked to this one all demonstrate the issue and could be used as reproductions.

Check whether the argument is an integer or typed array. If not, throw a TypeError.

title: override system environment variables with the local .env file env vars
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, Bun automatically loads environment variables from .env files, but it strictly prioritizes system environment variables over them. If a variable is already defined in the shell or system (e.g., process.env), Bun ignores the value in the .env file.
This behavior makes it difficult to locally override global environment variables (like USER, NODE_ENV, or CI-injected variables) without manually unsetting them in the shell before running Bun. It breaks the workflow where a developer expects their local .env file to be the "source of truth" for that specific execution context, regardless of what is set globally in their Zsh/Bash profile or CI environment.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I propose overriding system defined env vars
I acknowledge this is a breaking change so it would probably have to wait for bun 2.0.0
What alternatives have you considered?
Manual Unsetting: Running unset VAR && bun run .... This is tedious and error-prone.
Using dotenv-override: Installing a third-party package like dotenv-override or dotenv-flow and manually configuring it in the application code. This negates the benefit of Bun's built-in zero-config .env support.
Modifying System Shell: Changing global shell profiles (e.g., .zshrc), which is not a viable solution for project-specific overrides.

title: bun v1.3.3 ignores .npmrc / bunfig scoped registry auth (401 against AWS CodeArtifact)
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.3
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Description
bun install v1.3.3 does not send auth for a scoped registry (@vsb) defined in both .npmrc and bunfig.toml, resulting in 401 from AWS CodeArtifact, while npm and yarn succeed.
Reproduction Steps

Add .npmrc with registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ and @vsb:registry=https:///npm/vsb-packages/ plus _authToken=${CODEARTIFACT_AUTH_TOKEN} entries.

Example:
# AWS CodeArtifact Configuration

registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/

@vsb:registry=https://<codeartifact-domain>/npm/vsb-packages/

# Configure authentication for the registry
# Note: Yarn 1 can be picky about trailing slashes, so we include both variations to be safe.
//vsb-packages-<codeartifact-domain>/npm/vsb-packages/:_authToken=${CODEARTIFACT_AUTH_TOKEN}
//vsb-packages-<codeartifact-domain>/npm/vsb-packages:_authToken=${CODEARTIFACT_AUTH_TOKEN}


Add bunfig.toml:

[install]
registry = "https://registry.npmjs.org/"

[install.scopes]
"@vsb" = { url = "https://<codeartifact-domain>/npm/vsb-packages/", token = "$CODEARTIFACT_AUTH_TOKEN" }


Export CODEARTIFACT_AUTH_TOKEN (valid token).
Run bun i in a project that depends on @vsb/types.

What is the expected behavior?
Bun uses the provided token, installs scoped packages from CodeArtifact just like npm/yarn.
What do you see instead?

bun migrates from yarn.lock, then fails with GET https:///npm/vsb-packages/@vsb/types/-/types-0.1.0.tgz - 401.
npm (npm i) and yarn (yarn install) succeed with the same env and config.

Additional information
Currently have to fall back to npm or yarn for installs.

title: Critical: `bun rm -rf` causes data loss by following symlinks on Windows
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.3+274e01c73
What platform is your computer?
Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Clone the reproduction repository:
https://github.com/rubenferreira97/bun_rf_bug
Open a terminal in Windows.
Navigate to the project_link directory and create link.
cd project_link
bun link

Navigate to the project/ directory:
cd ../project

Install dependencies (this establishes the symlink inside node_modules pointing to the sibling project):
bun install

Run the clean script (defined as rm -rf node_modules in package.json):
bun clean

Check the contents of the sibling directory ../project_link.

What is the expected behavior?
When bun rm -rf node_modules is executed:

The node_modules directory should be removed.
The symlink file located at node_modules/project_link should be unlinked (deleted).
Crucially: The actual contents of the target directory (../project_link/) should remain completely intact.

What do you see instead?

The node_modules directory is removed.
Bun erroneously traverses the symlink.
The contents of the target directory (../project_link/) are deleted, resulting in source code loss for the linked package.

Additional information
Directory Structure Context:
The issue occurs specifically when a dependency is linked locally (common in monorepos or local development).
├── project/              # Working directory
│   └── node_modules/
│       └── project_link  # SYMLINK (Followed incorrectly during deletion)
└── project_link/         # TARGET (Source code gets deleted here)


Warning: This is a critical issue that causes unintended data loss on local development environments. Users on Windows should avoid using bun rm -rf on directories containing symlinks until patched.

title: Missing the ability to list only packages linked in a workspace
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
I am currently building dynamic Docker images in a monorepo (managed by NPM) with multiple workspaces. In these minimal images, I only want to include the files that the app/workspace actually needs, rather than copying the entire monorepo.
Currently, I do this in a dedicated stage with the NPM command npm ls -w path/to/workspace --package-lock-only --link,  then I add the files of the previous result.
Unfortunately it's impossible to do this with Bun.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
An option/feature that mimicry npm ls -w  --link or pnpm list --filter  --only-projects or better pnpn deploy
What alternatives have you considered?
bun pm ls --filter  but it doesn't work
#

We use esbuild to compile our projects with an external config file that's injected into the container:
esbuild --sourcemap=linked --minify --platform=node --external:"./config"  --outfile=index.min.js --bundle  index.ts
During testing with building using bun we've found that relative paths are not translated well:
bun build --sourcemap=linked --minify --target=bun --external:"./config" --outfile=./index.min.js --production index.ts

title: WebSocket Upgrade communication not possible with http.createServer
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.2.21+7c45ed97d
What platform is your computer?
Windows and Linux tested: works on Node, not on Bun
What steps can reproduce the bug?
A server made with http module is unable to transfer WebSocket traffic and there appears to be no way to respond to the client who sent an Upgrade request.
A test server:
const http = require('http')
const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain' })
  res.end('Normal HTTP request works\n')
})

server.on('upgrade', (req, clientSocket, head) => {
  clientSocket.write(raw_response)  // Not actually sending anything
  clientSocket.end()
})

const raw_response = (
    'HTTP/1.1 418 I\'m a teapot\r\n' +
    'Content-Type: text/plain\r\n' +
    'Content-Length: 30\r\n' +
    '\r\n' +
    'Upgrade request not supported\n'
)

server.listen(3000, () => { console.log('Server listening on port 3000') })
It can then be queried with:
curl http://localhost:3000/ -v
curl -H "connection: upgrade" -H "upgrade: websocket" http://localhost:3000/ -v
What is the expected behavior?
Expected: 200 OK, 418 Teapot, both with response bodies.
What do you see instead?
Running on Bun this example returns 200 OK (normal HTTP) but for Upgrade an empty response (no status, headers or body).
If the upgrade handler was expecting to receive anything from client, it would hang. This causes http-proxy and vite dev proxy server hang while trying to proxy WebSockets, because the client never sees the 101 Switching Protocols response, and keeps on waiting.
Additional information
Running the server with Node v25.2.1 we get the expected responses. We also find that the vite proxy works fine for HTTP and WS, while on Bun WS connections hang and only HTTP works.
Any Upgrade header (enabled via Connection) causes this, it is not specific to WebSockets although that is the typical application.

What steps can reproduce the bug?
The userInfo() output from Bun contains "unknown" as the shell and as the username:
# Run a Fedora 42 container
docker run -it --rm fedora:42 bash

# Install bun and node
dnf install -y unzip nodejs
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
source ~/.bash_profile

# Compare os.userInfo() output
echo "=== Node.js ===" && node -e "console.log(require('os').userInfo())"
echo "=== Bun ===" && bun -e "console.log(require('os').userInfo())"

Output:
=== Node.js ===
[Object: null prototype] {
  uid: 0,
  gid: 0,
  username: 'root',
  homedir: '/root',
  shell: '/bin/bash'
}
=== Bun ===
{
  homedir: "/root",
  username: "unknown",
  shell: "unknown",
  uid: 0,
  gid: 0,
}

What is the expected behavior?
Node.js correctly reads /bin/bash from /etc/passwd:
$ cat /etc/passwd | head -n 1
root:x:0:0:Super User:/root:/bin/bash

What do you see instead?
Bun returns the literal string "unknown" for both username and shell.
Output:
=== Node.js ===
[Object: null prototype] {
  uid: 0,
  gid: 0,
  username: 'root',
  homedir: '/root',
  shell: '/bin/bash'
}
=== Bun ===
{
  homedir: "/root",
  username: "unknown",
  shell: "unknown",
  uid: 0,
  gid: 0,
}

Additional information
This causes issues when using child_process.spawn() with shell: os.userInfo().shell, as Bun tries to execute a binary literally named "unknown":
const { spawn } = require('child_process');
const os = require('os');
spawn('echo', ['hi'], { shell: os.userInfo().shell });
// Error: Executable not found in $PATH: "unknown"

Seems like the bug is in src/bun.js/node/node_os.zig. Bun reads username and shell from environment variables $USER and $SHELL, not from /etc/passwd:
Possible fix could be to use libuv's uv_os_get_passwd() to read from /etc/passwd like Node.js does:
var pw: libuv.uv_passwd_t = undefined;
const ret = libuv.uv_os_get_passwd(&pw);
defer libuv.uv_os_free_passwd(&pw);

if (ret == 0) {
    // Use pw.username and pw.shell from passwd file
} else {
    // Fallback to env vars
}

title: Full npm workspaces compatibility: Auto-detect and symlink workspace packages with standard syntax
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun claims to support npm workspaces (https://bun.com/docs/pm/workspaces), but there's a critical incompatibility that breaks interoperability with npm-based workflows:
npm workspaces behavior:

Workspace packages are automatically symlinked to root node_modules/
Dependencies can reference workspace packages using regular version syntax (e.g., "@abapify/adt-cli": "*")
npm install automatically treats local workspace packages as workspace dependencies

Bun workspaces behavior:

Requires explicit workspace:* protocol in package.json
Does NOT automatically symlink workspace packages to root node_modules/
Does NOT treat "package": "*" as a workspace reference

Why this breaks npm compatibility:

The workspace:* protocol is Bun/pnpm/Yarn-specific and causes npm to fail or fetch from registry instead
Projects using "package": "*" syntax work with npm but fail with Bun
Cannot seamlessly switch between npm and Bun in the same monorepo
Breaking existing npm workspaces when trying to adopt Bun

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Full npm workspaces compatibility mode:
When using npm-style package.json with "workspaces" field, Bun should:

Auto-detect workspace packages - Treat any dependency matching a workspace package name as a workspace reference (regardless of version syntax: *, ^1.0.0, etc.)
Auto-symlink workspace packages - Automatically symlink all workspace packages to root node_modules/ (just like npm does)
Support both syntaxes - Accept both "package": "*" AND "package": "workspace:*" for workspace references
Interoperability - Allow package.json files to work with both npm install and bun install without modification

Example:
{
  "name": "my-monorepo",
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"],
  "dependencies": {
    "@myapp/core": "*"  // Should work like workspace:* in Bun
  }
}
What alternatives have you considered?
Current workarounds:

Using workspace:* protocol → Breaks npm compatibility
Manually declaring all workspace dependencies → Tedious and error-prone
Using pnpm instead → Loses Bun's speed benefits
Using --linker=isolated → Doesn't solve the core compatibility issue

Why these don't solve the problem:

Teams need to support both npm and Bun users
CI/CD pipelines may use different package managers
Legacy projects use npm syntax and shouldn't require mass refactoring
The goal is drop-in compatibility, not a different protocol

Proposed Solution
Add a npmWorkspacesCompat mode (or make

title: Auto-enable TLS1.2 and TLS1.3 Session Resumption
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Enable TLS Session Resumption by default? I believe it requires setting BoringSSL.c.SSL_CTX_set_session_cache_mode to SSL_SESS_CACHE_BOTH in bun-usockets/crypto/openssl.c (unsure what this means for bun-usockets/quic.c).
Node explicitly disables BoringSSL/OpenSSL's internal Session Resumption mechanisms (with SSL_SESS_CACHE_NO_INTERNAL) in favour of (server side) newSession (called by BoringSSL/OpenSSL's  SSL_CTX_sess_set_new_cb) and resumeSession callbacks (called on on ClientHello done) callbacks and returns a valid SSL_SESSION to be loaded in (which is broken for Node's TLS1.3 implementation anyway: nodejs/node#60847).
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
In TLS1.2, with session resumption (stateful with Session Identifiers and stateless with Session Tickets), the TLS handshake round-trips go down from 2 to 1.
In TLS1.3, with session resumption (stateless with Pre-Shared-Key aka Session Tickets), the TLS handshake bandwidth consumption may be reduced by 2KB+.
What alternatives have you considered?
NodeJS compat mode.

$ bun remove prettier

4.0.0-alpha.13  # Still there!
Evidence of stale packages

Source

bun pm ls
prettier not listed


node_modules/.bun/
Contains 3 versions: 2.8.8, 3.6.2, 4.0.0-alpha.13

So bun pm ls correctly shows prettier is not a direct dependency, but the stale installations remain in node_modules/.bun/ and the symlinks in node_modules/ and node_modules/.bin/ are not cleaned up.
Expected behavior
After removing prettier from package.json and running bun install (or bun remove prettier):

Stale versions should be removed from node_modules/.bun/
node_modules/prettier symlink should be removed
node_modules/.bin/prettier symlink should be removed

Put this package.json in an empty directory dir1:
{
    "name": "test",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "devDependencies": {
        "foo": "workspace:."
    }
}
Then run this command in empty directory dir2 adjacent to dir1:
bun i ../dir1
What is the expected behavior?
bun creates package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "name": "file:../dir1"
  }
}
and copies or symlinks node_modules/test to ../../dir1
What do you see instead?
bun add v1.3.3 (274e01c7)
info: cannot move files from tempdir: RenameAcrossMountPoints, using fallback
   - "name": "../dir1" - name@../dir1

and bun never exits, consuming 100% CPU and increasing amounts of memory (I killed it at 30% of my 32GB).
Additional information
npm handles this scenario successfully, symlinking dir1 as node_modules/test
yarn requires dir2 to contain a valid package.json, copying dir1 to node_modules/test
bun handles bun i dir1 from the parent directory (instead of ../dir1 from a sibling directory) successfully, copying dir1 to node_modules/test

I was running my checks outside of Bun.build and returning early instead of starting the build process, but that meant I couldn't use any of the other features of Bun.build around my checks.

excerpt:

As we all know, Date.now() can only generate millisecond-level timestamps, whereas Bun has extremely high concurrency performance. For example, when doing redis zadd, to ensure that scores are unique, nanosecond-level timestamps are required. Please add this feature based on the existing API. Thank you very much.

# Base stage for shared settings
FROM oven/bun:1 AS base
WORKDIR /app

# Dependencies stage - Cache optimization
# This stage installs ALL dependencies (including dev) for building
FROM base AS deps
WORKDIR /app
# Copy package files first to leverage Docker layer caching
COPY package.json bun.lock ./
# Copy prisma schema because postinstall script might need it (though we ignore scripts now)

# This avoids errors because prisma.config.ts and DATABASE_URL are missing in this stage

# Production dependencies stage
# This stage installs only production dependencies for the final image
FROM base AS prod-deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock ./
COPY prisma ./prisma/
# Install only production dependencies

# Builder stage
FROM base AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

# Generate Prisma client explicitly to ensure it exists and matches the environment
# This populates src/generated which is needed for the build and runtime
# We provide a dummy DATABASE_URL because prisma.config.ts validates its existence,

title: Prettier experimental-cli parallel mode returns undefined rejection reason
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.3
What platform is your computer?
Darwin arm64 (macOS 26.2)
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a directory with some TypeScript/JavaScript files
Run prettier's experimental CLI with the --bun flag in parallel mode (default):

bunx --bun prettier --experimental-cli --check .
What is the expected behavior?
Prettier should check all files and report formatting status.
What do you see instead?
A TypeError crash in prettier's experimental CLI:
12466 |     } else {
12467 |       const error = fileResult.reason;
12468 |       if (error.name === "UndefinedParserError") {
                  ^
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'error.name')
      at runGlobs (/path/to/node_modules/.bun/prettier@3.7.3/node_modules/prettier/internal/experimental-cli.mjs:12468:11)

The issue is that fileResult.reason is undefined when it should be an Error object.
Workarounds that confirm this is Bun-specific
All of these work correctly:



Command
Result




bunx --bun prettier --experimental-cli --check .
❌ Crashes


bunx prettier --experimental-cli --check . (Node runtime)
✅ Works


bunx --bun prettier --experimental-cli --check . --no-parallel
✅ Works


bunx --bun prettier --check . (regular CLI)
✅ Works



Analysis
The experimental CLI uses Promise.allSettled() for parallel file processing. When a promise is rejected, the reason property should contain the error. Under Bun's runtime, some rejected promises have reason: undefined instead of the actual error object.
This suggests a bug in how Bun handles Promise.allSettled() with rejected promises in worker threads or parallel execution contexts.
Additional information

Prettier version: 3.7.3
Node version (for comparison): v22.19.0
The bug is reproducible consistently

title: Glob negation logic is inverted
excerpt:
The glob matching logic for negated patterns in src/glob/match.zig is incorrect.
Currently, if a pattern is negated (e.g., !foo) and the path matches the pattern (e.g., foo), it returns .negate_match, which is treated as a match. It should return .negate_no_match.
Conversely, if it doesn't match (e.g., bar), it returns .negate_no_match, which is treated as no match. It should return .negate_match.
This PR fixes this by swapping the return values.

What is the expected behavior?

The 1st level dependency "vitest" is downgraded to respect minimum release age
The 2nd level dependency "vite" is downgraded  to respect minimum release age

What do you see instead?

The 1st level dependency "vitest" is downgraded
The 2nd level dependency "vite" is NOT downgraded, instead bun.lock uses already existing version which is too new

With minimumReleaseAge setting in use, bun update --latest seems to be a nice way to update the whole project. It nicely shows which dependencies were downgraded. However I would expect it to update all dependencies according to release age, not just the 1st level.

title: bun build should fallback to bun run build when no entrypoints are provided
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.3
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.1.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Add a build script to package.json:

"scripts": {
  "start": "bun run index.ts",
  "build": "bun build index.ts"
}

Run bun build (no arguments):

bun build v1.3.3 (274e01c7)
error: Missing entrypoints. What would you like to bundle?

Usage:
  $ bun build <entrypoint> [...<entrypoints>] [...flags]

To see full documentation:
  $ bun build --help
What is the expected behavior?
bun build is always treated as Bun’s built-in build subcommand. However, many projects define a build script, and when users run bun build with no arguments, it’s natural to expect it to behave like bun run build.
Expected: if bun build is invoked with no positional args/flags and a build script exists, Bun should fall back to running the project script (bun run build).
Actual: Bun still treats it as the internal build command.
What do you see instead?
bun build v1.3.3 (274e01c7)
error: Missing entrypoints. What would you like to bundle?

Usage:
  $ bun build <entrypoint> [...<entrypoints>] [...flags]  

To see full documentation:
  $ bun build --help
Additional information
Of course, strictly speaking, this isn't a bug, but I think fixing this usage is more in line with Bun's all-in-one philosophy.

title: Bun keeps optional peer dependencies of dependencies installed despite explicit removal
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?

What platform is your computer?

What steps can reproduce the bug?

Install a package with optional peer dependencies (in this example drizzle-orm) as dependency
Install an optional peer dependency of the package from step 1 (in this example better-sqlite3) as dependency
bun remove the optional peer dependency from step 2 (but keep the original package from step 1)

In commands to run:
cd $(mktemp -d)
bun add drizzle-orm
bun add better-sqlite3
bun remove better-sqlite3

test -d "node_modules/better-sqlite3" && echo "better-sqlite3 is installed" || echo "better-sqlite3 is not installed"
# => better-sqlite3 is still installed
What is the expected behavior?
The optional peer dependency (better-sqlite3) is removed from package.json, bun.lock and node_modules, since it's optional and I explicitly requested removal.
What do you see instead?
The optional peer dependency (better-sqlite3) is correctly removed from package.json, but stays in bun.lock and installed to / available in node_modules.

$ bun why better-sqlite3
better-sqlite3@12.5.0
  └─ optional peer drizzle-orm@0.44.7 (requires >=7)

This can also cause issues/confusion because it "desyncs" bun.lock and node_modules from package.json, in a sense that bun would never install better-sqlite from the resulting package.json alone:

test -d "node_modules/better-sqlite3" && echo "better-sqlite3 is installed" || echo "better-sqlite3 is not installed"

title: Bun applies cwd's `bunfig.toml` to hashbang scripts from linked packages, breaking bun-created cli's
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.4+5eb2145b3
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.1.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Minimal reproduction repo: https://github.com/Inlustra/bun-bunfig-cwd-issue


Clone this repo and install:
bun install


Build and link the CLI:
cd packages/cli && bun run build && bun link


Run the CLI from packages/example:
cd ../example && example-cli


Observe:

Bun attempts to load @test/plugin/bun
Resolution fails (module not found)
The CLI cannot run at all



OR:

Create a monorepo with three packages: a CLI, a plugin, and an example project.
Structure
my-repro/
├── package.json              # workspaces: ["packages/*"]
└── packages/
    ├── cli/
    │   ├── package.json      # bin entry + build script
    │   └── bin/cli.ts        # simple console.log with #!/usr/bin/env bun shebang
    ├── plugin/
    │   ├── package.json      # exports "./bun" pointing to src/bun.ts
    │   └── src/bun.ts        # simple console.log (just needs to exist)
    └── example/
        ├── package.json      # depends on the plugin package (workspace:*)
        └── bunfig.toml       # preload = ["@my/plugin/bun"]

Key details

CLI package: Has a bin entry pointing to a compiled binary. Build script uses bun build --compile. The script itself can just be console.log("hello").
Plugin package: Named something like @my/plugin, exports ./bun subpath. Content doesn't matter.
Example package: Has bunfig.toml with a preload pointing to the plugin. Has the plugin as a dependency.

Steps

bun install at root
cd packages/cli && bun run build && bun link
cd ../example && my-cli

What is the expected behavior?
A compiled Bun binary should not be affected by bunfig.toml in the current working directory. The CLI is a standalone tool from a separate package.
What do you see instead?
error: preload not found "@my/plugin/bun"

Bun reads bunfig.toml from the cwd and attempts to apply preload to the compiled binary. Resolution fails because:

Reads bunfig.toml from cwd (packages/example)
Tries to resolve @test/plugin/bun from the compiled binary's location (packages/cli)
Fails because @test/plugin is a dependency of packages/example, not packages/cli

Additional information
This also affects non-compiled #!/usr/bin/env bun shebang scripts—the compiled binary was an attempted workaround that didn't help.
This implies that any Bun-based script or binary cannot be executed from a directory that has a bunfig.toml with a preload. This severely limits the usa

title: 🚀 Feature Request: Support env variables (process.env) or --define in HTML bundling via `bun index.html`
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
When bundling a project that uses an index.html pointing to a module like main.tsx, there is currently no way to inject env variables directly into the client bundle when running bun index.html. unlike bun build for JS/TS, bun index.html does not accept the --define flag, so I cannot even manually replace values like process.env.PORT. This makes it impossible to inject run-time env configuration into the HTML bundle and client-side code.
Bun supports .env auto-loading for server environments. The expectation is that the requested feature should also leverage Bun’s .env auto-loading mechanism, so variables from a .env file would be automatically available for injection into the client bundle or via --define during HTML bundling. (limited to public env varaibles)
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I propose to add support for either:

Direct injection of env variables (such as process.env.*) into the client HTML bundle
bun has multiple configuration to decide which env can be bundled and how
https://bun.com/docs/bundler#env


--define flag in bun index.html, so users could manually map values (e.g., bun --define process.env.PORT="'3000'" index.html). should and could also have worked here.

we need way to

be able to use env variables in client bundle run via bun HTML bundler
be able to define how the env are embedded following the env bundling rules.

What alternatives have you considered?
Manually handling env replacement before building, but this is error-prone and does not leverage Bun’s intended features.

This is extracted from a larger library to be as simple as possible to only test performance of switch statements.

switch_bench.js
import { run, bench, summary } from 'mitata'

const array = []
const characters = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'
const charLen = characters.length

for (let i = 0; i < 100000; i++) {
  const idx = Math.floor(Math.random() * charLen)

  array.push(characters[idx])
}

summary(() => {
  bench('for switch', function () {
    let count = 0

    for (let i = 0; i < array.length; i++) {
      switch (array[i]) {
        case 'a':
        case 'b':
        case 'c':
          count += 1
          break
        case 'd':
        case 'e':
        case 'f':
        case 'g':
          count += 2
          break
        case 'h':
        case 'i':
        case 'j':
        case 'k':
        case 'l':
          count += 3
          break
        default:
          count += 4
          break
      }
    }

    count
  })

  bench('for if', function () {
    let count = 0
    let temp = ''

    for (let i = 0; i < 100000; i++) {
      temp = array[i]

      if (temp === 'a' || temp === 'b' || temp === 'c') count += 1
      else if (temp === 'd' || temp === 'e' || temp === 'f' || temp === 'g')
        count += 2
      else if (
        temp === 'h' ||
        temp === 'i' ||
        temp === 'j' ||
        temp === 'k' ||
        temp === 'l'
      )
        count += 3
      else count += 4
    }

    count
  })
})

await run()


performance results


What is the expected behavior?
Because at least for the most common use cases switch...case and if...else are interchangeable and mostly just a code readability decision, their performance should be equal to each other like it is with node.
What do you see instead?
Equal switch...case is slower than if...else.

title: HTML Imports - missing Cache-Control + Date headers
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.4
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.17
What steps can reproduce the bug?
import home from './home.html'

Bun.serve({
   development: false,
   routes: {
      '/': home
   }
})
What is the expected behavior?
HTML Imports bundle <script> and <link> tags and serves them with the hash in the file name, like: /chunk-xnzchsjf.js and /chunk-5zbgb6s5.css and /icon-076fgd38.svg (see bun.com/docs/bundler/fullstack for details)
These are served with Etag header which allows a simple 304 Not Modified response for repeated requests, but this still requires sending requests for every file on every page load, resulting in thousands of unnecessary requests per second over the network.
Facebook created the Cache-Control: immutable header in 2017 (see engineering.fb.com) which tells the browser this file name with this hash is immutable, will not change and you don't need to send a request asking if it changed. This speeds up both the client and the server as the client can immediately use the cached response without asking the server if it changed.
A simple fix is to add a cache-control: public,max-age=31536000,immutable header to the hashed file responses for a performance improvement on both the client and server using HTML Imports
What do you see instead?
No Cache-Control header

Additional information
No response

ESLint find-up resolution regression in Bun 1.3.4
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.4
What platform is your computer?
Linux (Ubuntu latest in GitHub Actions) and macOS Darwin 25.1.0
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a project with both eslint@^9.39.2 and @nuxt/eslint@^1.12.1 as dependencies
Run bun install
Run bunx eslint .

Minimal reproduction:
{
  "devDependencies": {
    "@nuxt/eslint": "^1.12.1",
    "eslint": "^9.39.2"
  }
}
What is the expected behavior?
ESLint should run successfully. This works correctly in Bun 1.3.2.
What do you see instead?
TypeError: findUp is not a function
    at ConfigLoader.locateConfigFileToUse (node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-loader.js:542:27)
    at #locateConfigFileToUse (node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-loader.js:714:40)
    at LegacyConfigLoader.findConfigFileForPath (node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-loader.js:760:63)
    at LegacyConfigLoader.loadConfigArrayForFile (node_modules/eslint/lib/config/config-loader.js:412:37)
    at entryFilter (node_modules/eslint/lib/eslint/eslint-helpers.js:322:24)

Additional context
The issue is ESM/CJS module resolution. The dependency tree has two versions of find-up:

eslint@9.39.2 depends on find-up@^5.0.0 (CommonJS compatible)
@nuxt/eslint@1.12.1 depends on find-up@^8.0.0 (ESM only)

In Bun 1.3.2, eslint correctly receives find-up@5 which exports findUp as a function.
In Bun 1.3.4, eslint incorrectly receives find-up@8 which is ESM-only and the import doesn't resolve correctly, causing findUp to be undefined.
Workaround: Pin Bun to 1.3.2 until this is fixed.

title: --ignore-scripts for bun run
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
package.json#scripts can specify a number of pre/post scripts that will run before or after any script is ran with bun run.
i.e (for your package.json#scripts)
{
  "build": "vite",
  "prebuild": "openapi-ts"
}
Where building your applications depends on generating an openapi client, for example.
bun run build
Will first run openapi-ts, followed by vite.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
An --ignore-scripts option for bun run, which disables execution of pre/post scripts. This is similar to what bun already has for install, and what npm has for npm run.
What alternatives have you considered?
You can get around this by not using pre/post scripts, and manually making a "raw" version of your command.
i.e (for your package.json#scripts)
{
  "build": "bun run pre-bulld && bun run raw-build",
  "pre-build": "openapi-ts",
  "raw-build": "vite"
}
This will allow you to do "bun run raw-build".
This is insufficient for a number of reasons:

It requires a change to package.json, which limits the ability to use bun/npm interchangeably (some people don't yet have sign off to switch their projects to bun). This can harm the ability to transition to bun if you depend on this feature.
It requires knowing what particular convention a package is using for "raw" scripts, which might be different in different packages
The number of scripts you need for this can grow quite substantially if you have scripts that depend on other scripts
This is liable for user error, where any of the pre- or raw- scripts aren't quite setup correctly or used in the right context

title: Bun.build() fails with "Unseekable reading file" (ESPIPE) on second call when file was imported at server startup
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.4
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.14.0-37-generic x86_64 x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Description
When running a server with bun run --watch that calls Bun.build() on request, the first build succeeds but subsequent builds fail with "Unseekable reading file" error for files that were imported at server startup.
Reproduction

Create a server that imports a module at startup
Have the server call Bun.build() on an entrypoint that also imports that same module
Run with bun run --watch server.ts
First request succeeds
Second request fails with error:

error: Unseekable reading file: "/path/to/imported/module.ts"
Minimal reproduction structure:
project/
├── server.ts      # imports shared.ts at startup, calls Bun.build() on request
├── entrypoint.ts  # imports shared.ts
└── shared.ts      # the file that causes the error
server.ts:
  import { someFunction } from './shared.ts';  // Import at startup

  const server = Bun.serve({
    port: 3000,
    async fetch(req) {
      const result = await Bun.build({
        entrypoints: ['./entrypoint.ts'],
        minify: false,
      });
      if (!result.success) {
        return new Response(result.logs.map(l => l.message).join('\n'), { status: 500 });
      }
      return new Response(await result.outputs[0].text());
    }
  });
entrypoint.ts:
export { someFunction } from './shared.ts';

shared.ts:
export function someFunction() { return 'hello'; }

Run with: bun run --watch server.ts

First request to http://localhost:3000/ → Success
Second request → Unseekable reading file: ".../shared.ts"

What is the expected behavior?
No error, file is served without issue
What do you see instead?
Unseekable reading file: ".../shared.ts"
Additional information
Root Cause Analysis
This issue was diagnosed with assistance from https://claude.com/claude-code.
The bug is caused by a stale file descriptor in Bun's global FileSystem.instance cache.
The sequence:

Server starts and imports shared.ts
FileSystem.instance.entries caches the directory entry with shared.ts's fd (e.g., fd 7)
First Bun.build():
- Resolver gets fd 7 from cache (resolver.zig:1015)
- Bundler reads file, then closes fd 7 (ParseTask.zig:1109)
- FileSystem.instance.entries still has stale fd 7!
Kernel recycles fd 7 for something else (pipe, eventfd, etc.)
Second Bun.build():
- Resolver gets stale fd 7 from cache
- cache.zig:178 calls seekTo(0) on fd 7 (now a pipe)
- ESPIPE error

src/fs.zig:

excerpt:
Feature Request: Windows Support for Bun.Terminal (PTY) API
Description
The Bun.Terminal API introduced in Bun v1.3.5 is a game-changer for building high-performance TUI applications and developer tools. Currently, this API is limited to POSIX systems (Linux/macOS). Bringing this support to Windows would enable developers to build cross-platform interactive terminal tools with the same incredible performance.
Reference Implementation
A comprehensive reference implementation demonstrating the full potential of the Terminal API (PTY operations, interactive I/O, Bun.stringWidth benchmarks, and real-time dashboards) can be found here:
https://github.com/brendadeeznuts1111/bun-1.3.5-exmaples
Key Features that would benefit from Windows Support:

PTY Operations: Programmatic terminal control for CLI tools.
Interactive I/O: Direct input/output handling for shell-like experiences.
TUI Rendering: Unicode-aware layouts using Bun.stringWidth.
Developer Experience: Fast, native PTY support for Windows developers without needing WSL2 or Docker.

This implementation covers 50+ test cases and multiple production-ready demos (Snake, DevOps Dashboard, Split Terminal, Surgical Precision) that would be ideal candidates for testing on Windows.

title: Feature request: optional "docs-for-llms" sync on install/update (versioned, colocated in repo)
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
LLMs (and humans) regularly end up using the wrong docs for dependencies because docs aren’t reliably tied to the exact installed version and aren’t colocated in the repo. That breaks real workflows:

Upgrade a dependency, but the local/docs context is still for the previous version
Roll back bun.lock, but docs/context doesn’t roll back with it
Auditing/diffing over time becomes messy because code changes while docs context stays out of sync

Result: wasted time + avoidable errors, especially when using LLM tooling that depends on local repo context.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add an optional Bun-native feature to fetch and colocate official versioned docs for installed dependencies, synced with the resolved versions in bun.lock.
Proposed UX:

bun install --docs (or similar): fetch docs for each resolved package@version when available
bun add <pkg> --docs: same behavior for newly added deps
bun update --docs: refresh docs for updated packages
bun update -i: show whether each package@version has “docs for LLMs” available (yes/no), and where they were stored

Storage convention (example):

.docs-for-llms/<pkg>/<version>/... (happy to align on a different convention)

Key properties:

Docs are version-matched to the installed dependency
Docs are colocated with the repo, so git history/rollbacks keep docs in sync
If docs are missing, Bun reports it clearly; developers can optionally add “addons” (extra examples, Context7-style expansion, etc.) without replacing the official baseline

Why this should be native in Bun (vs another tool):

Bun already owns dependency resolution + lockfile semantics, so syncing docs to exact versions is reliable
A third-party tool would need to re-implement lockfile behavior across package managers/lockfiles and will be more fragile

What alternatives have you considered?

Rely on web docs/bookmarks: not version-pinned; breaks on upgrades/rollbacks
Manual doc downloads into the repo: works, but tedious and easy to forget
Third-party “docs fetcher” tooling: has to support multiple package managers/lockfiles; less reliable than Bun at the source of truth
LLM-only context expansion tools: useful as a fallback, but they don’t solve official docs being version-matched and tracked in git history

title: ✨ Feature Request: Built-in LRU Cache Support in Bun
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Description:
It would be valuable for the Bun runtime to include first-class support for an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache API or utility that developers can use directly without relying on third-party libraries.
While LRU cache implementations exist in the ecosystem, Bun currently doesn’t provide a native, performant cache abstraction with eviction policies like LRU. This can lead to inconsistent behavior between environments and reliance on external packages or workarounds.
Motivation:

Standardizing an efficient LRU cache implementation would improve developer experience and reduce the need for external dependencies.
Some existing cache packages (e.g., lru-cache) have exhibited regressions or compatibility issues in Bun in the past (e.g., TTL expiry behavior or performance differences) — see related issues such as regression in lru-cache TTL handling and performance comparisons vs Node.js implementations. ([GitHub][1])

Proposal:
Add a native LRU cache API to Bun’s standard library (e.g., Bun.Cache.LRU or similar), with features such as:

Configurable maximum size
Least-recently-used eviction policy
Optional TTL (Time to Live) support
Optional serialization / persistence integration (if useful)

This could be exposed under a standard namespace (instead of requiring @std/cache or other third-party modules), similar to how Deno and Node provide standardized utilities.
Example API (suggested):
// Create an LRU cache with max 500 entries
const cache = new Bun.LRUCache({ max: 500 });

// Set and get values
cache.set("user:123", { name: "Alice" });
const user = cache.get("user:123");

// Check size & stats
console.log(cache.size);        // number of current entries
console.log(cache.evictions);   // number of items evicted so far
Use Cases:

Caching database query results in edge functions
HTTP server response cache layers
Generic memoization utility without external deps

Benefits:

Improved performance and consistency
Reduced reliance on third-party cache packages
Makes Bun more complete as a runtime out of the box

Additional Context / References:

Community has reported LRU cache behavior regressions or compatibility issues with node modules in Bun in the past. ([GitHub][1])
Performance benchmarking vs Node.js for cache eviction has shown significant differences for third-party implementations. ([GitHub][2])

title: Windows: setRawMode(true) overwrites console mode flags instead of preserving them
excerpt:
Summary
On Windows, calling process.stdin.setRawMode(true) overwrites all existing console mode flags instead of preserving them. This breaks mouse input in TUI applications because ENABLE_MOUSE_INPUT and ENABLE_EXTENDED_FLAGS get wiped out.
Reproduction
// 1. Set console mode with mouse input enabled via FFI
SetConsoleMode(stdin, ENABLE_MOUSE_INPUT | ENABLE_EXTENDED_FLAGS | ...)
// stdin mode is now 0x03b7

// 2. Enable raw mode
process.stdin.setRawMode(true)
// stdin mode is now 0x0200 - mouse flags are gone!
Test Case
I've created a minimal reproduction script that demonstrates this:
import { dlopen, FFIType, suffix } from "bun:ffi"

const kernel32 = dlopen(`kernel32.${suffix}`, {
  GetStdHandle: { args: [FFIType.i32], returns: FFIType.pointer },
  GetConsoleMode: { args: [FFIType.pointer, FFIType.pointer], returns: FFIType.i32 },
  SetConsoleMode: { args: [FFIType.pointer, FFIType.u32], returns: FFIType.i32 },
})

const STD_INPUT_HANDLE = -10
const ENABLE_MOUSE_INPUT = 0x0010
const ENABLE_EXTENDED_FLAGS = 0x0080

const stdin = kernel32.symbols.GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE)
const modeBuffer = new Uint32Array(1)

// Get current mode and add mouse input
kernel32.symbols.GetConsoleMode(stdin, modeBuffer)
const originalMode = modeBuffer[0]
console.log(`Before setRawMode: 0x${originalMode.toString(16)}`)

// Set mouse input flags
kernel32.symbols.SetConsoleMode(stdin, originalMode | ENABLE_MOUSE_INPUT | ENABLE_EXTENDED_FLAGS)
kernel32.symbols.GetConsoleMode(stdin, modeBuffer)
console.log(`After adding mouse flags: 0x${modeBuffer[0].toString(16)}`)

// Now enable raw mode - this clobbers our flags
process.stdin.setRawMode(true)

kernel32.symbols.GetConsoleMode(stdin, modeBuffer)
console.log(`After setRawMode(true): 0x${modeBuffer[0].toString(16)}`)
// Mouse flags are gone!
Expected Behavior
setRawMode(true) should:

Read current console mode with GetConsoleMode()
Modify only the flags it needs to change
Preserve existing flags like ENABLE_MOUSE_INPUT

Actual Behavior
setRawMode(true) overwrites the entire console mode, wiping out any flags that were previously set by the application.
Impact
This affects all TUI applications on Windows that need mouse input:

Any app using Ink, Blessed, or similar TUI libraries
Terminal-based IDEs and editors
Interactive CLI tools

Environment

OS: Windows 11
Bun version: latest
Terminal: Windows Terminal / ConHost

Suggested Fix
// Current (broken):
SetConsoleMode(handle, RAW_MODE_FLAGS);

// Fixed:
GetConsoleMode(handle, &c

title: Shell: Implement POSIX left-to-right redirect ordering semantics
excerpt:
Summary
Bun's shell currently applies all redirects simultaneously rather than left-to-right as specified by POSIX. This causes different behavior for complex redirect sequences like 2>&1 > file.
Current Behavior
# In Bun's shell:
/bin/sh -c "echo out; echo err >&2" 2>&1 > file.txt
# Result: Both stdout and stderr go to file.txt
Expected POSIX Behavior
# In bash/POSIX shells:
/bin/sh -c "echo out; echo err >&2" 2>&1 > file.txt
# Result: stdout goes to file.txt, stderr goes to terminal
In POSIX shells, redirects are applied left-to-right:

2>&1 - stderr duplicates to wherever stdout currently points (terminal)
> file.txt - stdout is then redirected to the file

So stderr ends up on the terminal while stdout goes to the file.
Technical Details
The current implementation in src/shell/shell.zig collects all redirects first via parse_redirects() and applies them together. To match POSIX semantics, redirects would need to be applied incrementally in parsing order.
Priority
Low priority - this is an edge case that most users won't encounter. The common patterns like > file 2>&1 (redirect both to file) work correctly.
Related

PR #25668 - Multiple redirections support

I have encountered a build failure when using the Bun runtime (bun --bun) in a Next.js project that utilizes both Better Auth and the experimental cacheComponents configuration. This issue does not appear to be a recent regression, as it has been occurring for some time.

Removing the Bun Runtime:

title: Support a mirror for compile target tarballs instead of requiring explicit tarball urls
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
When using bun compile in a restricted corporate network, the command fails because it cannot access the public npm registry to download target tarballs. While BUN_COMPILE_TARGET_TARBALL_URL allows for manual overrides, it is cumbersome because it must be set individually for each platform's binary, requiring multiple manual runs to populate the cache. Currently, bun compile does not appear to respect registry settings defined in .npmrc or bunfig.toml.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Enable bun compile to automatically respect registry settings from an existing .npmrc or bunfig.toml when fetching target tarballs. Alternatively, introduce a configuration setting to define a global registry mirror for these targets to avoid manual per-platform overrides.
What alternatives have you considered?
The BUN_COMPILE_TARGET_TARBALL_URL environment variable should remain supported for cases where tarballs must be fetched from non-registry-compatible URLs. However, utilizing a mirror seems like a more efficient solution for standard registry-based environments.

title: SIGTERM is not sent with --watch option
Provide a mechanism to close Bun.serve active connections on process end
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, WebSocket connections are terminated but proper close messages are never sent when a process ends, such as with --watch or Ctrl+C. This "leaves clients hanging" as they never receive close messages, and will consider the WebSocket open until some heartbeat or other message fails.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Either a new option for Bun.serve or a new parameter to Server.ref() that specifies that once the process ends, and the server is closed with it, that active requests will be closed, such as with Server.stop(true).
What alternatives have you considered?
I've tried listening for the process to end to manually call Server.stop(true), but process.on("exit") and process.on("beforeExit") never fire when a web server is attached. process.on("SIGINT") fires as long as it's registered before the server, but this is not called with --watch. process.on("SIGTERM") should be fired with --watch, but is not, see #25721.

Catalog entries with `file:` relative paths fail when referenced from workspace packages
excerpt:
Catalog entries with file: paths fail when referenced from workspace packages
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.5
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 15.6.1 arm64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Create this minimal monorepo structure:
my-monorepo/
├── package.json
├── vendored/
│   ├── pkg-a-1.0.0.tgz
│   └── pkg-b-1.0.0.tgz
└── packages/
    └── my-app/
        └── package.json

Root package.json:
{
  "name": "my-monorepo",
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"],
  "catalogs": {
    "vendored": {
      "pkg-a": "file:./vendored/pkg-a-1.0.0.tgz",
      "pkg-b": "file:./vendored/pkg-b-1.0.0.tgz"
    }
  },
  "overrides": {
    "pkg-a": "file:./vendored/pkg-a-1.0.0.tgz"
  }
}
packages/my-app/package.json:
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "dependencies": {
    "pkg-b": "catalog:vendored"
  }
}
Run from the monorepo root:
bun install
What is the expected behavior?
Both pkg-a and pkg-b should install successfully. The file:./vendored/... paths in the catalog should resolve relative to the root package.json where the catalog is defined.
What do you see instead?
[pkg-a] Extract ... (decompressed ... tgz file)
[pkg-a] Extracted to ... 
error: ENOENT extracting tarball from pkg-b
error: pkg-b@catalog:vendored failed to resolve

Key observation:

pkg-a succeeds because it's only referenced from the root overrides
pkg-b fails with ENOENT because it's referenced from a workspace package (packages/my-app)

Root Cause Analysis
When a workspace package references a catalog entry (e.g., "pkg-b": "catalog:vendored"), Bun resolves the file:./vendored/... path relative to the workspace package directory (packages/my-app/), not the root package.json where the catalog is defined.
So Bun looks for:

❌ packages/my-app/vendored/pkg-b-1.0.0.tgz (incorrect - workspace-relative)

Instead of:

✅ vendored/pkg-b-1.0.0.tgz (correct - root-relative)

The bug appears to be in PackageManagerTask.zig or in how catalog dependency resolution propagates the base path context. When a catalog entry is substituted for a workspace package dependency, the relative path loses its original context (root package.json location).
Workaround
You can technically use absolute paths in the catalog definition, but this is obviously suboptimal considering package.json at the workspace level is not usually gitignored.
Additional information
This bug makes catalogs unusable for vendored/local tarball dependencies in monorepos, which is a common use case for:

Pre-release packages not yet published to npm
Patched versions

excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.5+1e86cebd7
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a global ~/.bunfig.toml with path settings using ~ or $HOME:

[install]
globalBinDir = "~/.bun/bin"
globalDir = "~/.bun/install/global"

[install.cache]
dir = "~/.bun/install/cache"

Run any scaffolding command, e.g.:

bunx sv create my-project

Observe that a literal folder named ~ or $HOME is created in the project directory, containing a recursive copy of the user's actual home directory.

What is the expected behavior?
~ and $HOME should be expanded to the user's home directory path (e.g., /Users/username or /home/username), consistent with standard shell behavior.
Alternatively, if expansion is not supported, Bun should reject these values with a clear error message rather than interpreting them as literal directory names.
What do you see instead?
Bun interprets ~ and $HOME as literal folder names and creates them in the current working directory. When running commands like bunx sv create, this results in the entire home directory being copied into the newly created project.
This is a critical security/privacy risk:

SSH keys, credentials, and personal files can be accidentally committed to version control
Massive unexpected disk space consumption
Potential exposure of sensitive data when sharing or deploying projects

First time bun user here so perhaps this was a mistake by me, but I wanted to report this as it was super concering to see ~/ in my git status output while inside the project directory.

title: Unicode double-encoding when running --target=node bundle under Bun runtime
excerpt:
Unicode double-encoding when running --target=node bundle under Bun runtime
Environment

Bun version: 1.3.4+5eb2145b3
OS: macOS Darwin 25.2.0 (ARM64)
Terminal: iTerm2 with UTF-8 encoding
Locale: LANG=en_US.UTF-8

Description
When a bundle is compiled with bun build --target=node and then executed using Bun runtime, Unicode characters in string literals are double-encoded, resulting in mojibake output.
The bundler correctly stores UTF-8 bytes in the output file, but the Bun runtime incorrectly decodes them as Latin-1 and re-encodes as UTF-8 when outputting to stdout.
Reproduction
1. Create test file
cat > unicode-test.ts << 'EOF'
console.log("Symbols: ✓ ✗ ⚠ → ▶ ○");
console.log("Box: ┌───┐");
EOF
2. Build with --target=node
bun build unicode-test.ts --outfile=dist-node.js --target=node
3. Run with Bun (shows bug)
bun dist-node.js
# Output: Symbols: â â â â â¶ â
# Output: Box: âââââ
4. Compare with --target=bun (works correctly)
bun build unicode-test.ts --outfile=dist-bun.js --target=bun
bun dist-bun.js
# Output: Symbols: ✓ ✗ ⚠ → ▶ ○
# Output: Box: ┌───┐
Test Matrix



Build Target
Runtime
Result




--target=node
Node.js
N/A (errors on bun: imports)


--target=node
Bun
❌ Mojibake (double-encoding)


--target=bun
Bun
✅ Correct


No --target flag
Bun
✅ Correct



Root Cause Analysis
Hex dump comparison
--target=node bundle output (BROKEN):
00000000: c3a2 c295 c290  <- "═" double-encoded

--target=bun bundle output (CORRECT):
00000000: e295 90        <- "═" correct UTF-8

Double-encoding pattern
The UTF-8 byte 0xE2 is being decoded as Latin-1 character â (U+00E2), then re-encoded to UTF-8 as 0xC3 0xA2:



Original UTF-8
Decoded as Latin-1
Re-encoded as UTF-8




E2 9C 93 (✓)
â + control chars
C3 A2 C2 9C C2 93


E2 95 90 (═)
â + control chars
C3 A2 C2 95 C2 90



Bundle file is correct
Both bundles store the same correct UTF-8 bytes:
# Both show: e2 9c 93 (correct UTF-8 for ✓)
grep -o 'Symbols[^"]*' dist-node.js | xxd | head -1
grep -o 'Symbols[^"]*' dist-bun.js | xxd | head -1
The corruption happens at runtime, not during bundling.
Expected Behavior
Unicode characters should display identically regardless of the --target flag when running under Bun.
Actual Behavior
When running a --target=node bundle under Bun, UTF-8 string literals are double-encoded, producing mojibake.

title: Workspace packages with symlinks are not discovered during `bun install`
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.4+5eb2145b3
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.1.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a monorepo with workspaces defined in package.json
Create a workspace package as a symlink to a directory outside the monorepo
Run bun install

# Create a monorepo structure
mkdir my-monorepo
cd my-monorepo

# Create root package.json with workspaces
cat > package.json << 'EOF'
{
  "name": "my-monorepo",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "workspaces": ["./*"],
  "dependencies": {
    "backend": "workspace:*"
  }
}
EOF

# Create a workspace package outside the monorepo
mkdir -p /tmp/backend-package
cat > /tmp/backend-package/package.json << 'EOF'
{
  "name": "backend",
  "version": "1.0.0"
}
EOF

# Create a symlink to the external workspace
ln -s /tmp/backend-package backend

# Try to install
bun install
What is the expected behavior?
Bun should follow symlinks when scanning for workspace packages and successfully resolve the backend workspace dependency. The installation should complete without errors, similar to how npm, yarn, and pnpm handle symlinked workspaces.
What do you see instead?
error: Workspace dependency "backend" not found

Searched in "./*"

Workspace documentation: https://bun.com/docs/install/workspaces

error: backend@workspace:* failed to resolve

Bun fails to recognize the symlinked directory as a valid workspace package because the workspace scanning code doesn't follow symlinks by default.
Additional information
The GlobWalker used for scanning workspace patterns in src/install/lockfile/Package/WorkspaceMap.zig:230 is initialized with follow_symlinks: false, which prevents it from descending into symlinked directories.
This is a common pattern in monorepos where:

Workspace packages are stored in separate repositories
Packages are shared across multiple monorepos
Local development uses symlinks to external packages

title: Add native Windows Service support for `bun build --compile` executables
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
On Windows, long-running background applications are typically deployed as Windows Services managed by the Service Control Manager (SCM).
Currently, executables produced by bun build --compile are standard console binaries and cannot be registered as true Windows services. Users must rely on third-party wrappers (e.g. NSSM / WinSW), custom native service hosts, or Task Scheduler, which adds extra complexity and dependencies.
This makes it harder to deploy Bun-based agents and daemons cleanly on Windows.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add native Windows Service support to Bun so a compiled Bun executable can run as a proper SCM service without external wrappers.
This could be exposed via a CLI flag or a Windows-specific runtime mode that integrates with the Windows Service lifecycle (start, stop, shutdown).
What alternatives have you considered?

Third-party service wrappers (NSSM, WinSW)
Writing a separate native service host
Task Scheduler (not equivalent to SCM services)
bun:ffi / cc (cannot provide a service entrypoint)

All require additional tooling outside of Bun.
