title: Bun.Terminal: Ctrl+C (\x03) does not send SIGINT to foreground process
Feature: Workspace `overrides` with `file:` paths should resolve relative to workspace root's package.json
excerpt:
Hi, this was accidentally proactively filed by Claude Code. My intention is to consolidate this with the other issue I filed regarding file: and catalogs #25752
Summary
When using overrides in a monorepo workspace to redirect dependencies to vendored file: tarballs, Bun resolves the file: path relative to the requesting package rather than the workspace root where the override is defined. This makes it impossible to use overrides for vendored package deduplication.
Reproduction
mkdir -p bun-override-bug/{vendored,apps/editor} && cd bun-override-bug

# Workspace root
cat > package.json << 'EOF2'
{
  "workspaces": ["apps/*"],
  "overrides": {
    "@pkg/utils": "file:vendored/pkg-utils-1.0.0.tgz"
  }
}
EOF2

# Create vendored tarball
mkdir -p tmp/utils && cd tmp/utils
echo '{"name":"@pkg/utils","version":"1.0.0","main":"index.js"}' > package.json
echo 'export const ID = 1' > index.js
npm pack && mv *.tgz ../../vendored/pkg-utils-1.0.0.tgz && cd ../..
rm -rf tmp

# App that triggers the override
cat > apps/editor/package.json << 'EOF2'
{
  "name": "@app/editor",
  "dependencies": {
    "@pkg/utils": "1.0.0"
  }
}
EOF2

bun install
Expected Behavior
The override "@pkg/utils": "file:vendored/pkg-utils-1.0.0.tgz" should resolve relative to the workspace root (where package.json with overrides is located):
/bun-override-bug/vendored/pkg-utils-1.0.0.tgz  ✓

Actual Behavior
Bun resolves the file: path relative to the requesting package (apps/editor):
error: @pkg/utils@file:vendored/pkg-utils-1.0.0.tgz failed to resolve

It's looking for /bun-override-bug/apps/editor/vendored/pkg-utils-1.0.0.tgz which doesn't exist.
Use Case
This is critical for vendored package deduplication in monorepos:

We vendor packages as tarballs in /vendored/*.tgz
Workspace packages declare "@pkg/foo": "file:../../vendored/pkg-foo.tgz"
Those vendored tarballs have internal semver deps like "@pkg/utils": "1.0.0"
We want to use root-level overrides to force all @pkg/utils resolutions to use our vendored tarball
Currently impossible because path resolution is relative to the requester

Option A: Resolve override file: paths relative to where overrides are defined
When an override is defined in the workspace root package.json, resolve its file: paths relative to the workspace root.
Option B: New syntax for root-relative paths
{
  "overrides": {
    "@pkg/utils": "file:root:vendored/pkg-utils-1.0.0.tgz"
  }
}
Or using a workspace protocol:

  "overrides": {

title: spawnSync is 30x slower than expected on Linux due to close_range syscall not being used
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.5+1e86cebd7
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.12.28 aarch64 unknown
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Measure spawn overhead with default ulimit (64K)
bun -e "
const start = Date.now();
for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) Bun.spawnSync(['true']);
console.log((Date.now() - start) / 100 + ' ms/spawn');
"

Output: 13.1 ms/spawn
Compare with reduced ulimit:
bash -c "ulimit -n 1024 && bun -e \"
const start = Date.now();
for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) Bun.spawnSync(['true']);
console.log((Date.now() - start) / 100 + ' ms/spawn');
\""

Output: 0.4 ms/spawn
For comparison, Node.js on the same system: 0.9 ms/spawn
What is the expected behavior?
Spawn should take ~0.5-1ms, using the close_range() syscall to efficiently close file descriptors.
What do you see instead?
Spawn takes ~13ms because bun falls back to iterating through all 65K possible file descriptors with fcntl():
$ strace -e fcntl bun -e "Bun.spawnSync(['true'])" 2>&1 | grep -c fcntl
65546

Additional information
Disclaimer: Opus 4.5 helped me put together this bug report, but I sanity-checked it and vouch for it.
I think this behavior was introduced in #9669, this is the relevant code: 
  
    
      bun/src/bun.js/bindings/c-bindings.cpp
    
    
        Lines 207 to 211
      in
      9ab6365
    
  
  
    

        
          
           #ifdef __NR_close_range 
        

        
          
               return syscall(__NR_close_range, start, end, flags); 
        

        
          
           #else 
        

        
          
               return ENOSYS; 
        

        
          
           #endif 
        
    
  


close_range wasn't introduced until Linux 5.9, and it looks like bun was compiled for Linux 3.7.0 (I'm running in a container where bun is installed in the image via the install script at https://bun.sh/install):
$ file $(which bun)
     /usr/local/bin/bun: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked, interpreter /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1, for GNU/Linux 3.7.0, BuildID[sha1]=d63ecaded0faac9b1e109be15c88f28bd0e0cca5, not stripped

IIUC, this means that at compile time __NR_close_range wouldn't be defined, therefore only the "else" branch of that directive is taken ENOSYS is what gets compiled into the binary. Not sure what the best practice is here, checked around a few other projects and it looks like Chromium handles it by just hardcoding the syscall number [1]
[1] https://chromium.googlesource.com/chr

Summary
When using bun with React Native/Expo, Metro bundler cannot resolve transitive dependencies because bun stores them in node_modules/.bun/ rather than hoisting them to node_modules/.
Steps to reproduce

Create an Expo/React Native project using bun as package manager
Have code that imports a transitive dependency (e.g., promise which is a dependency of react-native)
Run Metro bundler

Expected behavior
Metro should be able to resolve promise since it's a dependency of react-native which is installed.
Actual behavior
Unable to resolve module promise/setimmediate/rejection-tracking from /path/to/file.ts:
promise/setimmediate/rejection-tracking could not be found within the project or in these directories:
  node_modules
  ../node_modules

The package exists at node_modules/.bun/promise@8.3.0/node_modules/promise but Metro doesn't look there.
Workaround
Add transitive dependencies as direct dependencies in package.json:
"promise": "^8.3.0"
Environment

bun: 1.x
expo: 54.0.30
react-native: 0.81.5
metro: 0.83.x

Notes
This differs from npm/yarn behavior where transitive dependencies are hoisted to the root node_modules/ and are resolvable by any package. This breaks the common React Native assumption that dependencies of dependencies are accessible.
Related Expo issue: expo/expo#41994

title: Bun as a secure sandbox runtime for AI agent code execution
excerpt:
The Opportunity
AI agents are evolving from chatbots to autonomous systems that write and execute their own code - Claude artifacts, code interpreters, coding assistants, and autonomous agents all need sandboxed execution.
These agents need to run untrusted code safely. An LLM might generate code that accidentally (or intentionally) reads sensitive files, makes unauthorized network requests, or spawns malicious processes.
The Solution
#25911 implements a Deno-compatible permissions model:
# Execute LLM-generated code with zero permissions
bun --secure generated-code.js

# Grant specific permissions the agent needs
bun --secure --allow-net=api.openai.com --allow-read=./workspace agent.js
This would position Bun as the go-to runtime for the AI agent era - fast execution with secure sandboxing.

title: Please protect users (and Anthropic??) against potential lawsuits from Apple, other WebKit contributors and TinyCC contributors
excerpt:
Bun bundles WebKit, which is LGPL-licensed, but provides instructions on how to rebuild it. It also bundles TinyCC, which is also LGPL-licensed.
When building a single-file executable, Bun gets integrated into it. Now WebKit and probably TinyCC are integrated into it too. So when a user distributes single-file executables, they must be accompanied with appropiate license info and instructions on how to relink them with a different/modified WebKit / TinyCC version. The docs should point this out! And for how to relink them, there are no easy instructions available too, yet the LGPL requires this. Perhaps single-file executables should only be used for either purely internal projects or for projects where the code of the project is open source or at least source-available so the user can build a new executable with a custom Bun version including a custom WebKit/TinyCC version.
Anthropic uses the Bun single-file executable technique for Claude Code without distributing instructions on relinking / rebuilding. Apple might be able to sue them if they want.
Actually if Anthropic fixes this within 30 days after receiving a notification (perhaps the Bun team can give a priority notification?), it might be okay IF they can upgrade to LGPL-3 for WebKit, if all of it is LGPL-2.1 OR LATER.
See also anthropics/claude-code#8517 which currently only mentions Apache and MIT. The WebKit LGPL topic is much more important as the license terminates on violation.

title: SQLite database file locked on Windows after close() with WAL mode
`FileSink` does not truncate existing file
Prefer lockfile version of dependencies on `bun add/rm <package>` & `bun install`
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
We have lockfiles for reproducible builds. However, whenever adding a new package (bun add & co), the command also updates existing packages (within their allowed semver range).
This seems generally indesirable — we all know purportedly compatible packages can introduce new issues (hence why we have lockfiles in the first place). I often want to install a new package and have everything else stay completely the same until such time I'm focus on making updates.
Another connected issue is that manual edits to package.json (as made by certain tools or even AI agents) cannot be applied without updating all packages as described above.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Either change the default behaviour to not update existing packages. Reasonable for bun add <package>, probably not for a no-args bun install.
Alternatively, add a new flag (e.g. --prefer-lockfile-versions) that only:

bun add/rm <package>: installs/remove the requested package.
bun install: does not update existing dependencies if the lockfile version is in bounds

It would still update/downgrade the version if package.json was manually edited to have a version specifier that is incompatible with the one in the lockfile.



What alternatives have you considered?
No response

title: Windows: bun install hangs indefinitely with symlink linker in large monorepo
excerpt:
Description
bun install hangs indefinitely when using the default symlink linker on Windows with a large monorepo. The process consumes 5-6GB+ of RAM per bun process and never completes.
Environment

Bun version: 1.3.5
OS: Windows 11 (also reproduced on Windows 10)
Shell: PowerShell / WSL2
Project: Monorepo with ~20 workspaces, ~1500 packages total

Steps to Reproduce

Create a monorepo with multiple workspaces (frontends, backends, packages)
Remove linker = "hoisted" from bunfig.toml (or use default)
Delete node_modules
Run bun install

Expected Behavior
Install completes successfully using symlink linker.
Actual Behavior
Install output:
bun install v1.3.5 (1e86cebd)
Resolving dependencies
Resolved, downloaded and extracted [4]
warn: incorrect peer dependency ...

Then it hangs forever. Process manager shows:

Multiple bun.exe processes
Each consuming 5-6GB+ of RAM
CPU usage drops to near 0 (not actively working)
No further output or progress

After 5+ minutes with no progress, had to kill the processes.
Workaround
Adding to bunfig.toml:
[install]
linker = "hoisted"
With hoisted mode, install completes in ~180 seconds for ~1500 packages.
Additional Context

LongPathsEnabled registry key is set to 1 (long paths enabled)
Same project installs successfully on macOS/Linux with symlink linker
The hang occurs during the linking phase (after "Resolved, downloaded and extracted")
This may be related to #23960 and #18941

Possible Causes

Symlink creation on Windows is slow/blocking
Workspace resolution loops or infinite recursion
Memory leak during symlink graph calculation
Windows-specific path handling issues in large dependency trees

title: bun install does not route tarball downloads through the configured registry
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.5+1e86cebd7
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
While testing bun install, I noticed that although package metadata is fetched from the configured npm registry, tarball downloads appear to be fetched directly from their resolved URLs rather than being routed through the registry.
With npm, tarball requests are typically proxied or rewritten through the registry, which allows private registries, mirrors, or caching proxies to control and cache package artifacts.
I'm not sure if this behavior in Bun is intentional or a limitation, so I'm opening this issue to clarify.
What is the expected behavior?
Tarball downloads should be routed through the configured registry, consistent with npm’s behavior, so that registries can proxy, cache, or control package artifacts.
What do you see instead?
Bun fetches tarballs directly from their resolved URLs, ignoring the registry’s tarball routing.
Additional information
This breaks compatibility with npm registry setups that rely on tarball proxying and makes bun install unusable in some enterprise or air-gapped environments.

Start Bun test runner with inspector enabled:
bun test --inspect=9229


Connect a WebSocket client to ws://localhost:9229

What is the expected behavior?
According to Bun's WebKit Inspector Protocol documentation and PR #15194, after enabling the TestReporter domain, the following events should fire:

TestReporter.found - when tests are discovered
TestReporter.start - when each test begins execution
TestReporter.end - when each test completes (includes status and duration)

These events should provide real-time test execution information to debugger clients.

Tests run and complete normally (all tests pass)
Zero TestReporter domain events are received on the WebSocket connection

The TestReporter domain appears to be enabled but completely silent.

Root Cause Analysis
I've traced through the Bun source code and identified what appears to be a race condition in the test discovery and debugger initialization sequence:
1. The Implementation Exists
The event reporting methods are implemented in src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/InspectorTestReporterAgent.cpp:

reportTestFound()
reportTestStart()
reportTestEnd()

if (entry.base.test_id_for_debugger != 0) {

title: Using `@types/bun` precludes checking ES2022 compatibility
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
@types/bun@1.3.5
What platform is your computer?
macOS 26.1 (25B78)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Run:
# bash
bun init -y

cat <<HEREDOC > tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "lib": ["es2022"],
  }
}
HEREDOC
cat <<HEREDOC > index.ts
const test = Promise.withResolvers();
HEREDOC

bun x -- tsc --project .
What is the expected behavior?
The project fails to type-check because Promise.withResolvers() is not part of ES2022.
What do you see instead?
No errors.
If you check the source of the definition for Promise.withResolvers(), it is in the PromiseConstructor definition on globals.d.ts.
Additional information
I came across this because I maintain a library that specifically promises ES2022 compatibility. I was confident in this because we check against it using TypeScript.
I was shocked to find that we've been shipping incompatible code for well over half a year because of ambient ES2022 types in @types/bun (which is a dev dependency). I find it surprising that @types/bun should do so, since providing updates ES types is an orthogonal concern to types for bun. It makes me really worried that we could be shipping other incompatibilities because of @types/bun as well. (Further, I have @types/bun as a development dependency in almost all my projects, which means I may need to review all of them once I've figured out what exact issues are caused by this.)
It's extra-tricky because:

TypeScript notoriously makes it hard to avoid ambient types from being available throughout a project: microsoft/TypeScript#37053
It's common to mix .test.ts (or .spec.ts, etc.) files with source files, since that makes associated tests much easier to discover. This means that the ambient declarations for the source directories need to include bun:test at the very least.

The only workaround I can think of right now is to add another tsconfig.es2022.json file to the project that excludes .test.ts files and @types/bun. This is already pretty tricky to get right when ambient declarations are involved. However, even if I can get this right it is still rather undesirable, because:

It requires running a separate lint step.

Since TypeScript linting is often the slowest step in my projects by an order of magnitude, this would nearly double the time to build/test/lint in a bunch of projects.


It doesn't show errors in source files. I would find out about incompatibilities in CI a lot, which is a significantly worse developer experience.

bun install fails with GitHub Packages scoped registry - strips scope from package name
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.6
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64 (GitHub Actions runner) and macOS ARM64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Configure a scoped registry for GitHub Packages in bunfig.toml:

[install]
linker = "hoisted"
[install.scopes]
orgname = { token = "$GITHUB_TOKEN", url = "https://npm.pkg.github.com" }

Have a dependency on a scoped package from that registry in package.json:

{
  "dependencies": {
    "@orgname/packagename": "^2.1.4"
  }
}


Run bun install with bun 1.3.6 to generate/update the lockfile


The bun.lock will contain URLs in this format:


"@orgname/packagename": ["@orgname/packagename@2.2.0", "https://npm.pkg.github.com/@orgname/packagename/-/packagename-2.2.0.tgz", { "dependencies": { "axios": "^1.6.1" } }, ""],


Run bun install --frozen-lockfile (e.g., in CI)


Bun fails with:


error: GET https://registry.npmjs.com/packagename/-/packagename-2.2.0.tgz - 404

What is the expected behavior?
Bun should fetch the package from https://npm.pkg.github.com/@orgname/packagename/-/packagename-2.2.0.tgz as specified in the lockfile.
What do you see instead?
Bun strips the @orgname/ scope prefix from the package name and tries to fetch packagename from registry.npmjs.com instead of GitHub Packages, resulting in a 404.
Additional information
Workaround
The issue does not occur when the lockfile contains URLs in the older /download/ format:
"@orgname/packagename": ["@orgname/packagename@2.2.0", "https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@orgname/packagename/2.2.0/99520e6986e2c26c45b2b2d5a8413c73be684261", { "dependencies": { "axios": "^1.6.1" } }, "sha512-..."],
With this URL format, bun correctly fetches from GitHub Packages.
Root cause hypothesis
It appears that bun 1.3.6 changed how it writes GitHub Packages URLs to the lockfile (from /download/{scope}/{package}/{version}/{shasum} to /{scope}/{package}/-/{package}-{version}.tgz). When reading back this new URL format during install, bun incorrectly parses the URL and strips the scope, then falls back to the default npm registry.
Impact
This breaks CI pipelines that use bun install --frozen-lockfile with any scoped packages from GitHub Packages registry. The lockfile generated by bun 1.3.6 locally cannot be used in CI.
Reproduction repository
This was discovered in a private repository, but the reproduction steps above should be sufficient. The key elements are:

A scoped package hosted on GitHub Packages (not npm)
bunfig.toml configured with the scoped registry
Lockfil

Steps:

title: MySQL `VARCHAR` becomes `Buffer` since version `1.3.6`
Option to bypass minimumReleaseAge when the update fixes a vulnerability
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
As a security conscious company, we use a minimal release age to protect ourselves against supply chain attacks. However, some updates need to be hastily applied - in our case, Hono having an authentication bypass vulnerability, and in such cases, it makes more sense security-wise to immediately update, disregarding the minimum release time.
Additionally, Renovate's Minimum Release Age already gets bypassed for security updates, causing renovate to create PRs that fail as it tries still to update the vulnerability, but bun rejects all updates indiscriminately. It would be more convenient to be able to have a unified behavior across the dependency management tools.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I would suggest bun adds a
minimumReleaseAgeExcludeCveLevel = "none" # | "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical"
configuration option in the bunfig.toml. It would simply exclude packets from being age-gated when the current version of the packet has a CVE of at least the level specified in the configuration, to the first update which fixes the CVE.
The default could remain at none, to not push a breaking changes onto teams that may have strict guidelines disallowing indiscriminately all versions under a certain age, but if the policy is not explicitly set, I would also add a message such as
⚠ The minimum age gate is blocking security updates from being applied.
  Set minimumReleaseAgeExcludeCveLevel to "medium" to allow security update, or to "none" to stop seeing this message again.

when installing or updating vulnerable dependencies, and the vulnerability patch is blocked from being applied by the age gate.
What alternatives have you considered?
It is possible to set excludes via minimumReleaseAgeExcludes to exclude packages.
However, this for one does not entirely solve the problem, as we're making ourselves more vulnerable to a package hijack for the duration of the release age gating, since we're completely bypassing the gate thus not gating the updates beyond the security update, but also adds overhead to dependency updating as we may need to add exclusions manually instead of relying on tools like renovate or dependabot, and there is a big risk of packages staying in the allowlist longer than they need to be, when they are not actually trusted packages that have any business being in the exclude list, ultimately mitigating the positive security impact of bun's minimumReleaseAge feature

title: HTTPS requests hanging (regression 1.2.23 -> 1.3.x)
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.x (tested with 1.3.3 to 1.3.6)
What platform is your computer?
Macos (Darwin 21.6.0 arm64) and Windows 11 (x64) and Windows 11 (Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26100.0 x64)
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a script that makes continuous HTTPS requests over time (e.g., AWS SDK v3 calls)
Run the script with Bun >= 1.3.0
After approximately 1-10 minutes of continuous requests, some requests will hang indefinitely

Minimal reproduction repository: https://github.com/stacktape/bun-bug
What is the expected behavior?
All HTTPS requests should complete (either successfully or with a proper error) - they should never hang indefinitely.
When running the same script with Node.js (npx tsx index.ts) or Bun <= 1.2.23, all requests complete normally without any hanging.
What do you see instead?
After approximately 1-10 minutes of continuous requests (around 400-500 requests), some HTTPS requests start hanging indefinitely. The request is sent but no response is ever received, causing the Promise to never resolve.
Example output:
[2026-01-14T10:47:36.476Z] #470 START: CloudFormation:ListStacks
[2026-01-14T10:48:06.474Z] #470 HANGING: CloudFormation:ListStacks (29998ms) - REQUEST NEVER COMPLETED!

The request starts but never completes - it times out after 30 seconds (our manual timeout). Without the timeout, it would hang forever.
Additional information
Affected versions

Broken: Bun >= 1.3.0 (tested on 1.3.6)
Working: Bun <= 1.2.23, Node.js (all versions tested)

Related issues

#18666 - Similar hanging behavior reported for SolidStart server actions

Real-world impact
This issue affects Stacktape, an infrastructure-as-code tool that makes many AWS SDK requests during deployments. After upgrading from Bun 1.2.x to 1.3.x, deployments started hanging randomly after a few minutes of execution.
Observations

The bug manifests after ~1-10 minutes of continuous HTTPS requests
Different AWS endpoints are affected (S3, CloudFormation, IAM, STS, Lambda, EC2)
The hang is random - different requests hang on different runs
The request appears to be sent but no response is ever received
Setting keepAlive: false on the HTTP agent does NOT prevent the issue

No known workaround
We have not found a workaround other than downgrading to Bun <= 1.2.23 or using Node.js.

What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a simple CLI app using Commander.js:

// cli.ts
import { Command } from "commander";

const program = new Command();
program
  .name("mycli")
  .version("1.0.0", "-v, --version", "output the version number")
  .action(() => console.log("Hello!"));

program.parse(process.argv);

Compile with --compile-exec-argv:

bun build cli.ts --compile --compile-exec-argv="--use-system-ca" --outfile mycli

Run with --version:

./mycli --version
What is the expected behavior?
1.0.0

What do you see instead?
1.3.3

Bun outputs its own version instead of letting the application handle the --version flag.
Additional information

Without --compile-exec-argv, the --version flag works correctly and outputs 1.0.0
The issue appears to be that using --compile-exec-argv causes Bun's runtime to claim --version as a reserved flag before user code can process it
This breaks any CLI tool that wants to define its own --version behavior
Workarounds like early process.argv checking don't help since Bun intercepts the flag before JavaScript executes

title: Consider removing Ref.None in favor of always-valid refs (align with esbuild)
excerpt:
Summary
The bundler uses Ref.None as a sentinel value for "not set" refs throughout the codebase (~105 usages). This can lead to bugs where Ref.None leaks through code paths and ends up being exported as __INVALID__REF__ in the final bundle.
esbuild takes a different approach: ExportsRef and WrapperRef are always initialized to valid values during parsing, never using an invalid sentinel.
Current Behavior
// Bun: Uses Ref.None as default, checks later
exports_ref: Ref = Ref.None,
wrapper_ref: Ref = Ref.None,
When code forgets to check for Ref.None, it can cause issues like:
export {
  socket,
  __INVALID__REF__  // Leaked Ref.None
};
Proposed Change
Two options:


Use ?Ref (optional) - Replace Ref.None with null. Compiler enforces null checks at compile time.


Always initialize (esbuild approach) - Ensure refs like exports_ref/wrapper_ref are always valid during parsing. This is cleaner and matches esbuild's architecture.


Affected Areas

src/js_parser.zig - Parser state refs
src/ast/Ast.zig - Core AST struct fields
src/ast/*.zig - Various AST node refs
src/bundler/*.zig - Bundler ref handling

Related
This issue was identified while fixing a bug where wrapper_ref was incorrectly used instead of exports_ref for force_include_exports_for_entry_point, and defensive Ref.None guards had to be added.

This issue was generated with Claude Code

What steps can reproduce the bug?

Load the parent in a JS file using RTLD_GLOBAL to expose symbols:

What is the expected behavior?
In Node.js, process.dlopen respects the RTLD_GLOBAL flag. The symbols from parent.node are added to the global symbol table, so when child.so is loaded, it successfully links against them.
What do you see instead?

Additional information
This issue breaks native addons that use a "core + plugins" architecture (like DuckDB, Kuzu, or my project lbug).

This confirms the symbols exist and are correct, but Bun's loader is isolating them by default despite the explicit RTLD_GLOBAL request.

In a monorepo with workspaces using different versions of @types/react (React 18 vs React 19), Bun incorrectly hoists @types/react to .bun/node_modules/@types/react based on alphabetical package name ordering, not based on which package actually needs which version.
Minimal reproduction

Create a monorepo with two workspaces:

package.json (root):

  },

  }
}
packages/bbb-react18/package.json:
{
  "name": "@repro/bbb-react18",
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1",
    "react-dom": "^18.3.1",
    "swr": "^2.2.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/react": "^18.3.12",
    "@types/react-dom": "^18.3.7"
  }
}


Run bun install


Check the global symlink:


ls -la node_modules/.bun/node_modules/@types/react


The symlink points to @types/react@19.x because aaa < bbb alphabetically


Now rename aaa-react19 to zzz-react19:


{
  "name": "@repro/zzz-react19",
  ...
}


Run rm -rf node_modules bun.lock && bun install


Check the symlink again - it now points to @types/react@18.x because zzz > bbb


Evidence from systematic testing
We tested this by changing ONLY the package name of a React 19 project in a monorepo that also has a React 18 project called @repro/bbb-react18:



Package Name
Global @types/react
Reason




@repro/aaa-react19
19.x
aaa < bbb


@repro/bbb-react19
19.x
bbb = bbb (same, React 19 wins)


@repro/ccc-react19
18.x
ccc > bbb


@repro/zzz-react19
18.x
zzz > bbb



The cutoff is exactly at the alphabetically first React 18 package that declares @types/react.
What is the expected behavior?
Each workspace should resolve @types/react to its own declared version. The global symlink in .bun/node_modules/@types/react should not affect type resolution for workspaces that declare a different version.
Alternatively, if a global symlink must exist, it should not be determined by alphabetical package name ordering - this is arbitrary and leads to confusing, hard-to-debug issues.

What steps can reproduce the bug?
Run a file read operation (e.g. readFileWithOptions) on a (possibly large) file in Bun v1.3.5 on Windows x86_64.
Observed stack trace:

sys_uv.zig:294: preadv
node_fs.zig:5039: readFileWithOptions
node_fs_binding.zig:31: runSync
JSCJSValue.h:753: JSC::ensureStillAliveHere

The error/panic:
panic: integer does not fit in destination type
It looks like bufs.len (usize) is being cast to an unsigned int in uv_fs_read in sys_uv.zig, but is out of range for the underlying Windows/libuv implementation, causing the panic.

Stack trace highlights sys_uv.zig at the point of @intcast(bufs.len) and bubbles up through file read calls.
Additional information
Occurs with Bun v1.3.5 on Windows x86_64; likely an integer overflow/compatibility bug in the Windows/libuv/zig interop for file reading APIs.
Other details, code references, and related context:

https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/1e86cebd74a5723e818b5c0555276b646bcf0e4c/src/sys_uv. zig#L294
The root cause appears to be using @intcast(bufs.len) where buf.len can be larger than allowed by libuv's expected Windows types.

cd bun-bug-20260126

The tsconfig uses a path pattern with .js extension (standard for moduleResolution: "NodeNext"):
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "paths": {
      "@src/*.js": ["./src/*.ts"]
    }
  }
}
And the import:
import { greeting } from "@src/lib.js";
What is the expected behavior?
Bun resolves @src/lib.js to ./src/lib.ts using the tsconfig paths mapping, matching TypeScript's behavior.
TypeScript correctly resolves this pattern:
bun run tsc:check  # passes with no errors
What do you see instead?
error: Cannot find module '@src/lib.js' from '/Users/.../main.ts'

Additional information
This pattern (@src/*.js → ./src/*.ts) is the standard way to configure path aliases in TypeScript projects using moduleResolution: "NodeNext", which requires .js extensions in imports even for .ts source files.
Bun appears to not match @src/lib.js against the @src/*.js wildcard pattern. The workaround is to use @src/* without the .js extension in the pattern, but this breaks TypeScript's strict ESM module resolution.

title: Add native CUID generator to Bun
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun already provides excellent native ID generators:

Bun.randomUUID() (UUID v4)
Bun.randomUUIDv7() (time-ordered UUID)

However, there is still no native solution for generating CUID-style identifiers, which are widely used as database primary keys and auth identifiers in modern backend applications.
While UUID v7 improves index locality, it still:

Produces relatively long identifiers (36 chars as string)
Is not commonly used as a text primary key
Is less ergonomic for systems that expose IDs publicly (URLs, APIs)

As a result, many Bun users still rely on external libraries to generate CUIDs, adding unnecessary dependencies for a very common backend need.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add a native CUID generator to Bun that complements randomUUID() and randomUUIDv7().
Proposed API (example):
Bun.randomCUID()
or
crypto.randomCUID()
Desired properties:

Collision-resistant
Time-ordered / monotonic
Shorter and more URL-friendly than UUID
Optimized for database indexes (append-friendly)
Implemented natively for better performance than JS libraries
Compatible with existing CUID2 implementations

This would position Bun as a runtime that fully covers modern ID generation use cases:

UUID v4 → randomness
UUID v7 → sortable UUID
CUID → DB-friendly, human-safe identifiers

What alternatives have you considered?


UUID v4 (Bun.randomUUID)

Cryptographically strong, but worst-case for database index locality.



UUID v7 (Bun.randomUUIDv7)

Time-ordered, but still verbose and less ergonomic for public IDs.



External libraries (@paralleldrive/cuid2, ulid)

Extra dependency, JS-level overhead, duplicated implementations.



Database-generated IDs

Not suitable for edge runtimes, offline creation, or distributed systems.



None of these fully replace CUID’s combination of compactness, ordering, and DB performance.

title: Feature request: Add `--json` flag support to `bun pm ls` / `bun list`
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, bun pm ls outputs a human-readable tree format which is great for visual inspection but difficult to parse programmatically. Many tools and scripts need to analyze project dependencies, and JSON output would enable:

CI/CD pipelines to analyze dependencies
Integration with security scanning tools
Custom dependency analysis scripts
IDE/editor extensions that need dependency information

Other package managers like npm and pnpm support this functionality via a --json flag. e.g. pnpm ls --json or npm ls --json.
Additionally, other bun pm subcommands like bun pm view already support --json output, so this would bring consistency to the CLI.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add --json flag support to bun pm ls and bun list commands to output the dependency tree in JSON format, making it easier to parse the output programmatically.
Proposed Output Format
Similar to pnpm's format, not thinking too much complex:
{
  "name": "my-project",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "path": "/path/to/project",
  "dependencies": {
    "lodash": {
      "from": "lodash",
      "version": "4.17.21",
      "path": "/path/to/project/node_modules/lodash"
    }
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "typescript": {
      "from": "typescript",
      "version": "5.0.0",
      "path": "/path/to/project/node_modules/typescript"
    }
  }
}
With --all flag, include transitive dependencies:
{
  "name": "my-project",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "path": "/path/to/project",
  "dependencies": { ... },
  "devDependencies": { ... },
  "transitiveDependencies": {
    "some-transitive-dep": {
      "from": "some-transitive-dep",
      "version": "1.2.3",
      "path": "/path/to/project/node_modules/some-transitive-dep"
    }
  }
}
Expected Usage
# JSON output for direct dependencies
bun pm ls --json
bun list --json
# JSON output including all transitive dependencies
bun pm ls --all --json
bun list --all --json
Additional Context

The --json flag is already defined in the CLI argument parser but not implemented for the ls subcommand
This would align with the existing --json support in bun pm view, bun pm audit, etc.

What alternatives have you considered?
Nothing that I could think about, as the output from bun pm ls or bun list shows the output in the tree like format, which makes it pretty complex to parse. BTW, I'm willing to create a PR for this myself.

title: Allow creating a server handler for Bun.serve without starting the server (for SSR dev servers)
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, in Bun, you can use Bun.serve({...}) to start a server, and you can get a server handler via server.fetch, but only after the server has been started and is bound to a port. This means, to retrieve the handler function for the server, you must start the server process and listen on a port immediately.
However, some development and SSR environments (notably Angular's SSR dev server, but also potentially others) require you to provide just a request handler function—similar to how you can get a handler from frameworks like Express, Hono, or Fastify)—without actually binding or starting the server. This is important when the dev server itself is responsible for binding or forking servers, but relies on a reusable handler for the request/response cycle. In current Bun, this workflow is not supported and causes issues using Bun's fast server in these modern SSR/development setups.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
The feature would provide a way to create a Bun-compatible server handler function (the same as server.fetch or equivalent) without requiring the act of binding or starting a live server. This would let users supply Bun-powered request handlers to dev servers like Angular's, so that integration and SSR/middleware works seamlessly, and improves compatibility with ecosystem tools that expect to receive a handler (not a live server instance).
What alternatives have you considered?
Alternatives considered: using existing frameworks (Express, Hono, Fastify, etc.) that do support this decoupled handler pattern. Those options work, but lose out on Bun's built-in high performance and tight integration. A workaround with Bun today is to start the Bun server (binding to a port you hope isn't taken), then attempt to extract the handler—which is awkward, error-prone, and can break if the port is in use or if the dev server needs to coordinate its own binding. So currently, there is no real alternative available for Bun users who want this modern SSR/devserver handler pattern.

title: SSE crashes when using Bun preset in Nitro
Add --strict-latest flag to bun add to prevent installation of outdated versions
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
With the rise of agentic development (using tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or specialized AI agents), there is a growing problem where agents install outdated package versions. Because AI training data is often months or years behind the current date (it is currently 2026), an agent may confidently run bun add pkg@1.0.0 unaware that version 2.0.0 is the current stable release.
Currently, Bun executes exactly what it is told. In an automated or agent-led workflow, this results in:

Legacy Debt: Project environments being initialized with outdated, buggy, or deprecated versions.
Security Gaps: Agents inadvertently installing versions with known vulnerabilities that have been patched in the latest release.
Context Mismatch: The agent attempts to write code for version 1.0.0 while the developer expects 2.0.0 features, leading to immediate integration friction.

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I am proposing a --strict-latest flag for the bun add command (and a corresponding bunfig.toml setting) that enforces a "latest-only" policy unless explicitly overridden.
Proposed Functionality:

Validation: When bun add pkg@version --strict-latest is called, Bun checks the registry for the latest tag before writing to bun.lock or package.json.
Hard Failure: If the requested version is older than the latest version, the command should exit with a non-zero status.
Error Feedback: The error output should clearly state the discrepancy so the agent (or developer) can read the log and correct the command:
Error: Version 1.0.0 is outdated. The latest version is 2.1.5. To install this anyway, use --allow-outdated.

What alternatives have you considered?
In bunfig.toml, users should be able to enforce this globally for a project:
[install]
strictLatest = true

Feature request: Support selective removal/unloading of runtime plugins
excerpt:
Feature Request: Support for Selective Runtime Plugin Removal
Background
Currently, Bun's runtime plugin system only allows for removing all loaded plugins at once. There is no official API or mechanism to selectively unload or remove a specific plugin at runtime. This limitation makes it difficult to flexibly manage plugins, especially for advanced use cases such as live-reload of certain plugins, sandboxing, or avoiding plugin conflicts.
Proposed Feature

Add API support to allow selectively removing or unloading a single runtime plugin by name or identifier, without affecting other loaded plugins.
Ideally, this should be available both via the Bun JS API and CLI (if relevant).
The API could look like:
Bun.removePlugin('plugin-name'); // Removes only the specified plugin, leaves others intact.

This would allow users to:

Dynamically enable/disable individual plugins
Reload only selected plugins
Implement more granular plugin management logic
Avoid having to tear down and rebuild the entire runtime environment for small changes



Use Cases

Live updating or hot-reloading a single plugin during development.
Disabling or replacing a malfunctioning plugin on production/long-lived processes.
Testing plugin compatibility by toggling them on/off individually.
Improving observability and debugging by isolating plugin impact.

Why This Feature Matters

Modern plugin systems (such as those in build tools, editors, etc.) often provide fine-grained control over plugin lifecycles.
The lack of plugin-level removal hinders advanced Bun usage, especially for frameworks, tools, or platforms building on top of Bun.

References

bun.sh/docs/runtime/plugins
bun.sh/docs/runtime#plugins-api


If there's a workaround for now or if I'm missing existing APIs for this feature, please let me know. Thanks!

title: WASM: wa-sqlite crashes after repeated in-memory DB creation (null reference)
excerpt:
Summary
Repeatedly creating in-memory SQLite WASM databases via wa-sqlite in Bun eventually throws a WASM runtime error: RuntimeError: access to a null reference (evaluating "func(...cArgs)"). Node.js does not reproduce the issue.
Environment

Bun 1.3.4 (linux x64)
Node.js v24.11.1 (for comparison)

Reproduction
This reproduces for me around iteration ~10-17 (nondeterministic; sometimes later):
import { loadSqlite3Wasm } from "@livestore/sqlite-wasm/load-wasm"
import { sqliteDbFactory } from "@livestore/sqlite-wasm/node"
import { Effect } from "@livestore/utils/effect"
import { PlatformNode } from "@livestore/utils/node"

const runEffect = <T>(effect: Effect.Effect<T, unknown, unknown>) =>
  Effect.runPromise(effect.pipe(Effect.provide(PlatformNode.NodeFileSystem.layer)))

for (let i = 0; i < 300; i += 1) {
  const sqlite3 = await loadSqlite3Wasm()
  const makeDb = await runEffect(sqliteDbFactory({ sqlite3 }))
  const db = await runEffect(makeDb({ _tag: "in-memory" }))

  db.execute("create table test (id text primary key, data text)")
  db.execute("insert into test values ($id, $data)", { id: `item-${i}`, data: `data-${i}` })
  db.select("select * from test")

  db.close()
  db.destroy()
}
Run:
bun run repro.ts
Result
Bun throws:
RuntimeError: access to a null reference (evaluating 'func(...cArgs)')
    at ccall (.../wa-sqlite.node.mjs:1:73944)
    at .../wa-sqlite/src/sqlite-api.js:609
    at makeInMemoryDb .../sqlite-wasm/src/in-memory-vfs.ts:16

Notes

bun --smol run repro.ts also crashes (later iteration in one run).
node runs complete all 300 iterations without error.
Pure WASM module loading (no DB creation) does not crash.

Filed by Codex on behalf of @schickling.

What platform is your computer?

What steps can reproduce the bug?
Connect to a Postgres DB (such as Neon) that requires SNI without using a connection URL. For example:
const bunSql = new Bun.SQL({
    host: process.env.PGHOST,
    username: process.env.PGUSER,
    database: process.env.PGDATABASE,
    password: process.env.PASSWORD,
    tls: true,
};
await bunSql`SELECT now()`; // -> PostgresError: Connection does not have SNI.
But the same config provided as a URL works:
const bunSql = new Bun.SQL(`postgresql://${process.env.PGUSER}:${process.env.PASSWORD}@${process.env.PGHOST}/${process.env.PGDATABASE}?sslmode=require`);
And it also works if serverName is specified explicitly, but it feels surprising (and undocumented) that I have to do this:
const bunSql = new Bun.SQL({
    host: process.env.PGHOST,
    username: process.env.PGUSER,
    database: process.env.PGDATABASE,
    password: process.env.PASSWORD,
    tls: {
      serverName: process.env.PGHOST,
    },
};
await bunSql`SELECT now()`; // -> PostgresError: Connection does not have SNI.
What is the expected behavior?
SNI should be used whenever a TLS connection is made.
What do you see instead?
It's not used unless a connectionURL is given or { tls: serverName } is explicitly specified.

title: `bun build --compile` does not actually imply `--production`?
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.6+d530ed993
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
The help text for the --compile flag states: Generate a standalone Bun executable containing your bundled code. Implies --production
And the --production flag enables minification, so we should expect the code to be minified inside the compiled executable.
I can't figure out a way to inspect the bundled code inside the executable (I assume this is impossible on purpose), so instead I'll use the example from this issue: #26371
I'm using this example because when this code is minified, it produces an error, and therefore we can tell if the code inside the executable is minified or not.
Create index.ts:
import bun, { embeddedFiles } from "bun"

console.log(embeddedFiles)
console.log(bun.argv)
Compile and run:
$ bun build --compile --outfile example ./index.ts && ./example
# no error, code wasn't minified
[]
[ "bun", "/$bunfs/root/example" ]
With the --production flag:
$ bun build --compile --production --outfile example ./index.ts && ./example
# code was minified so now there's an error
SyntaxError: Unexpected token '{'. Expected ';' after variable declaration.
      at <parse> (/$bunfs/root/example:2:1)
      at native:11:43
So it seems like --compile does not actually imply --production like it should.

Run bun test.

Observation:

Occasionally, the test fails: instead of the handler response, you get HTTP 200 text/plain with body Welcome to Bun! (the Bun default page), not the handler ("OK").
Running this test singly (bun test file.test.ts) always passes.

Comparison:

Using node:http/Express or Hono (node adapter) under the same parallel environment does not reproduce the bug. Only native Bun.serve in bun test is affected.

What is the expected behavior?
Each request to the ephemeral Bun.serve instance should receive the response from its fetch handler (e.g. HTTP 200, body "OK", or as per test). No responses should ever return the default Welcome to Bun! page when a handler is specified.
What do you see instead?
Intermittently (under test runner parallelism, e.g. 60+ concurrent tests/files), one or more requests return the default "Welcome to Bun!" body, indicating the handler was not invoked or the request was routed to a global/default handler, not the Bun.serve instance's fetch function.
Additional information

Appears to be a race condition or internal routing bug when multiple servers are created in parallel (possibly ephemeral port assigned before handler is active).
Reducing bun test concurrency greatly reduces (or eliminates) failures.
Adding an artificial delay after starting the server reduces flakiness a bit, but does not eliminate.
Using an alternative server implementation (Node HTTP, Express, Hono's node adapter) in the same conditions does not show this bug.
It's specific to Bun.serve under bun test runner parallel execution (macOS, likely affects Linux).

Possible root cause hypotheses:

Race condition with server registration/routing or ephemeral port association internally in Bun.
Request to ephemeral port handled by a default global handler before fetch is actually hooked up, when under parallel high load.

Suggestions for maintainers:

Add synchronization to ensure Bun.serve instance is fully ready before any requests may hit the port.

title: `net.createServer` socket `data` events not emitted when used with ssh2 `forwardOut`
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.4+5eb2145b3
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 24.5.0 arm64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
net.createServer socket data events are not emitted when piping to an ssh2 forwardOut stream. The connection is established but the data handler never fires.
// repro.mjs
import { Client } from 'ssh2'
import { createServer, connect } from 'net'

const sshClient = new Client()

sshClient.on('ready', () => {
  const server = createServer(socket => {
    console.log('Connection received')

    // BUG: This handler is never called in Bun
    socket.on('data', chunk => {
      console.log(`Got ${chunk.length} bytes`) // Never prints in Bun
    })

    sshClient.forwardOut('127.0.0.1', 12345, 'target-host', 5432, (err, stream) => {
      if (err) return socket.end()
      socket.pipe(stream).pipe(socket)
    })
  })

  server.listen(12345, '127.0.0.1', () => {
    // Connect and send data
    const client = connect({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: 12345 }, () => {
      client.write('HELLO') // Data is sent but never received by handler
    })

    setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 3000)
  })
})

sshClient.connect({
  host: 'your-ssh-server',
  port: 22,
  username: 'user',
  privateKey: fs.readFileSync('key.pem'),
})
Node.js: Logs "Got 5 bytes"
Bun: Never logs - data event doesn't fire
Workaround: Use Bun.listen() instead of net.createServer() - Bun's native socket API works correctly.
What is the expected behavior?
The socket.on('data') handler should fire when data is written to the socket, matching Node.js behavior:
✅ Local connection received
Got 5 bytes                        <-- data event should fire
✅ SSH stream established

What do you see instead?
With Bun, the socket data event handler is never called. The connection is established, SSH stream is created, but no data flows through:
Connecting to SSH...
✅ SSH connected
✅ Server listening on localhost:12345
✅ Test client connected
✅ Local connection received
✅ SSH stream established
⏱️ Timeout

Notice "Got X bytes" is missing - the socket.on('data') handler never fires.
With Node.js (same code):
Connecting to SSH...
✅ SSH connected
✅ Server listening on localhost:12345
✅ Test client connected
✅ Local connection received
Got 5 bytes                        <-- data event fires correctly
✅ SSH stream established

Additional information
Impact: This breaks SSH tunnel patterns commonly used for database connections (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis) through bastion hosts.

title: Child processes spawned with node:child_process and piped stdout have incorrect type data
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.7+ba426210c
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 23.1.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
When a child process is spawned with piped output streams, the type of stdout differs between bun and NodeJS. In Node, the TS typings agree that its a readable, but under the hood it is implemented as a socket.
This is important because you need to unref the streams in addition to the child_process for the process to shut down gracefully.
A similar issue exists in Deno, but there unref also doesn't exist on the returned type.
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { Socket } from 'node:net';

const cp = spawn('node', [], {
  stdio: 'pipe'
});

console.log('Stdout prototype:', (cp.stdout.constructor.name));
console.log('Stdout is socket:', cp.stdout instanceof Socket);
console.log('Stdout is unref\'able', 'unref' in cp.stdout && typeof cp.stdout.unref === 'function');
cp.kill();
What is the expected behavior?
node and bun should output similar, if not the same, output for the above prompt
What do you see instead?
$ bun tmp/test.mjs
Stdout prototype: Readable
Stdout is socket: false
Stdout is unref'able true

$ node tmp/test.mjs
Stdout prototype: Socket
Stdout is socket: true
Stdout is unref'able true
Additional information
This was discovered as a bug report in nrwl/nx where a PR was opened to remove an error check we had around this: nrwl/nx#34224
For context, in Nx we have "Plugin Workers" - these workers are started by either the main cli process or the daemon, if its enabled. The worker's lifetime is bound by the process that spawned them. They are detached and unrefed s.t. the presence of the worker doesn't keep the parent process alive. When the parent process exits, the workers see their ipc socket close, and shut themselves down quickly.
The deno issue for the same type mismatch is here: denoland/deno#31961

title: Support `"devEngines"` field in `package.json`
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
There is no widely supported, standardized way to enforce development environment requirements across contributors.
Projects often rely on tool-specific files or documentation to pin runtime and package manager versions, which leads to fragmentation and inconsistent enforcement. Meanwhile, package.json already defines "devEngines" for exactly this purpose. However, it is currently only meaningfully enforced by npm, which limits its usefulness as a cross-ecosystem standard.
Without Bun supporting "devEngines", projects that adopt it still need separate Bun-specific setup guidance, reducing reproducibility and increasing contributor friction.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add support for parsing and enforcing the "devEngines" field in package.json.
Example:
{
  "devEngines": {
    "packageManager": {
      "name": "bun",
      "version": "1.3.6"
    }
  }
}
Proposed behavior

When "devEngines" is present, Bun reads it during install/run operations.
Bun validates that the active runtime and package manager satisfy the declared requirements.
If Bun is not an allowed "packageManager", or the version does not match, Bun produces a clear error.

This would let projects use a single, standard field in package.json as the source of truth for development tooling requirements.
What alternatives have you considered?
Current approaches rely on tool-specific files, custom scripts, or documentation, which are fragmented and not consistently enforced. Supporting devEngines in Bun would provide a declarative, ecosystem-aligned alternative directly in package.json.
related to #5846

title: package.json5 support
Bun proxy-chain library compatibility issues: Connection reset and undefined connectionId
excerpt:
Description
When using the proxy-chain library with Bun, several critical issues occur that don't happen with Node.js:

Connection Reset: HTTP requests with chunked transfer encoding result in connection reset errors
Undefined connectionId for short-lived connections: The connection identifier is undefined for short-lived connections (like quick HTTPS CONNECT requests), while long-lived connections do get a connectionId but never properly close (see issue 4)
Connection statistics always zero: All byte counters (srcTxBytes, srcRxBytes, trgTxBytes, trgRxBytes) remain at zero despite data transfer
connectionClosed event never fired: The event is never called, causing long-lived connections to accumulate indefinitely in the active connections list

Reproduction
I've created a minimal reproduction repository:
Repository: https://github.com/smmoosavi/bun-proxy-chain-bug
Steps to Reproduce

Run pnpm install

title: Bun.serve WebSocket idleTimeout and sendPings do not work well together
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
We're using Bun as a websocket server capable of serving long-lived connections. We're set up in the following way:
Bun.serve({
  websocket: {
    sendPings: true,
    idleTimeout: 0,
    ...handlers,
  }
});
The idea here is simple:

Never time out a websocket due to idleness. We implement an application-layer timeout based on inactivity.
We still want ping/pong to let browsers know that the websocket is still active, just not receiving data. We prefer using ping/pong control frames over an app-level ping as it's lighter, off our plates, and well-understood by browsers.

This isn't possible right now because sendPings: true has its own timeout mechanism that can't be configured. I want pings but I don't want pings to time out the connection.
Ping/pong is unreliable - a browser might not respond to a ping/pong, or something between Bun and the user might lose the frame. We don't want the websocket to die because of a missing pong - just stay open and try the ping again. In this case we're using ping/pong as a non-destructive keepalive.
This just isn't possible with the way Bun works:

The ping-timeout calculated here can never be higher than 16 - and with an idleTimeout of 0 it'll be set to 4.
This ping-timeout is set on the socket regardless of the idleTImeout here. So even if we set idleTimeout to 0, there's no way of getting rid of this ping timeout.

I'm not sure the best way to solve this. Some ideas:

A separate pingTimeout option on the API.
pingTimeout doesn't exist when idleTimeout is 0.
Never close a WS due to a ping timeout.

What do you think? Happy to open a PR once we get direction.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
See above.
What alternatives have you considered?
Right now the best we can do is set sendPings to false and use our own .ping

title: Linux ARM64: Illegal instruction crash on older CPUs (Cortex-A53, RPi4) due to LSE atomics in WebKit
excerpt:
Summary
Bun 1.3.7 crashes with "Illegal instruction" on older ARM64 CPUs due to WebKit being compiled with inline LSE atomic instructions that aren't available on ARMv8.0-A processors.
Affected Hardware

Cortex-A53 (Raspberry Pi 3/4, Amlogic S905X)
Exynos 9611
AWS a1 instances
Any ARMv8.0-A CPU without LSE support

Root Cause Analysis
The WebKit commit 345c6b8f6a47 ([libpas] Linux should use futex instead of spinlock) introduced GCC/Clang atomic intrinsics in libpas pas_lock.h:
// pas_lock_lock() - called at startup during memory allocator init
__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&lock->futex, &expected, 1, false, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)
__atomic_fetch_sub(&lock->futex, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)
__atomic_exchange_n(&lock->futex, 2, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)
When WebKit is compiled with -mcpu=native on GitHub Actions ARM64 runners (which have ARMv8.1+ CPUs with LSE support), Clang generates inline LSE instructions:
casa    w8, w2, [x0]    // Compare-and-swap (ARMv8.1 LSE)
ldaddl  w8, w0, [x0]    // Atomic add (ARMv8.1 LSE)
swpa    w1, w0, [x0]    // Atomic swap (ARMv8.1 LSE)
These instructions don't exist on ARMv8.0-A CPUs like Cortex-A53, causing an immediate crash at program startup.
Timeline



Version
WebKit Commit
Date
Status




Bun 1.3.6
1d0216219a3c
Jan 9, 2026
✅ Working


WebKit futex commit
345c6b8f6a47
Jan 24, 2026
⚠️ Introduced LSE atomics


Bun 1.3.7
0e6527f24783
Jan 26, 2026
❌ Broken



Verification
# With LSE-capable CPU (what CI uses) - generates inline LSE
$ clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu -mcpu=cortex-a76 -O2 -S test.c
    casa    w8, w2, [x0]

# With baseline ARMv8.0 CPU - generates outline atomics (runtime detection)  
$ clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu -mcpu=cortex-a53 -O2 -S test.c
    bl  __aarch64_cas4_acq  # Calls library function with runtime detection
Proposed Fix
Option 1: Add -moutline-atomics to WebKit builds
Modify the WebKit Dockerfile to add -moutline-atomics for ARM64:
RUN if [ "$(uname -m)" = "aarch64" ]; then \
    export CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -moutline-atomics"; \
    export CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -moutline-atomics"; \
fi
This generates calls to runtime helper functions that detect LSE support, instead of inline instructions.
Option 2: ARM64 baseline builds (similar to x86_64)
Add ARM64 baseline WebKit builds using -march=armv8-a without LSE, similar to PR #137 for x86_64 baseline.
Related

Original issue: #26544
Fix PR: #26545 (ARM64 baseline build support for Bun)
WebKit x86_64 baseline PR: oven-sh/WebKit#137

Workaround
Downgrade to B

title: Bun Shell hangs with `git show` command, `spawnSync` from `node:child_process` succeeds
Implement crypto.argon2Sync / crypto.argon2 from node:crypto
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun's API reference documents crypto.argon2Sync and crypto.argon2, but these functions do not seem to actually be implemented as of Bun 1.3.8.
Importing them returns undefined:
const { argon2Sync } = await import('node:crypto');

console.log(argon2Sync); // undefined

These functions were added to Node.js in v24.7.0 and provide Argon2-based key derivation, which is distinct from password hashing.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Implement crypto.argon2Sync and crypto.argon2 per the Node.js API:
const { argon2Sync, randomBytes } = await import('node:crypto');

const parameters = {
  message: 'password',
  nonce: randomBytes(16),
  parallelism: 4,
  tagLength: 64,
  memory: 65536,
  passes: 3,
};

const derivedKey = argon2Sync('argon2id', parameters);
console.log(derivedKey.toString('hex'));  // 'af91dad...9520f15'

What alternatives have you considered?
Bun.password.hash() - This uses Argon2id internally but outputs a PHC-format string which is designed for password storage and verification. It does not provide raw key bytes suitable for use as symmetric encryption keys.
hash-wasm / argon2-browser - Third-party WASM-based implementations work but add dependency overhead and are slower than native implementations.
scryptSync - This is implemented in Bun and could work as a fallback, but Argon2id is the modern recommendation for passphrase-based key derivation.
Use Case:
I'm building a CLI tool that encrypts project directories at rest using AES-256-GCM. The encryption key is derived from a user passphrase via Argon2id. This requires raw key bytes, not a verification hash.

title: Feature Request: Runtime Filesystem Permission System
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun currently has no filesystem permission or sandboxing system. Unlike Deno (which is secure by default) and Node.js (which has an experimental permission model), Bun operates with full filesystem access, making it impossible to:

Run untrusted code safely
Limit AI agents/assistants to specific directories
Enforce principle of least privilege in production
Meet security compliance requirements
Build sandboxed plugin systems

This is particularly important for AI applications where agents need structural awareness of filesystems without accessing sensitive files (like .env, credentials, or node_modules internals).
Use Cases Blocked Today

AI Coding Assistants - Need to read source files but shouldn't access secrets
Scoped File Management - Agents that organize files but shouldn't modify originals
Multi-Project Workspaces - Isolated access across project boundaries
CI/CD Pipelines - Automated jobs that should only touch specific paths

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A comprehensive filesystem permission system with the following capabilities:
Permission Modes



Flag
Description




--allow-read=<path>
Read access to files/directories


--allow-write=<path>
Write access to files/directories


--allow-exec=<path>
Execute access to specific files


--deny-read=<path>
Exclude paths from broader grants



Path Specification Features

Absolute and relative paths: /data, ./config
Glob/wildcard patterns: *.sh, **/*.json, data/*
Path mapping (host-to-guest): /host/path:/guest/path

Example Usage
# A minimal build script 
bun run build \
  --allow-read=./src \
  --allow-read=./package.json \
  --allow-read=./node_modules \
  --allow-write=./dist

# A start script with path mapping (host:guest)
bun run start \
  --allow-read=/home/user/app/dist:./dist \
  --allow-read=/home/user/app/node_modules:./node_modules \
  --allow-write=/var/logs/app:./logs

# Restrict agent access to specific files and directories
bun run \
  --allow-write=./src \
  --allow-write=./tests \
  --allow-read=./package.json \
  --allow-read=./cfg \
  --deny-read=./cfg/**/*secrets* \
  agent.ts
Permission Models
Declarative (Static) - Permissions defined at launch, ideal for CI/CD:
bun run --allow-read=/data --allow-write=/logs script.ts
Interactive (Dynamic) - Runtime prompts for development:
const file = await Bun.file("/data/config.json", { request: { allow: 'read' } });
// Terminal: ⚠️ Bun requests read access to "/data

title: Support ReadableStream as input for `Bun.Archive` extraction
Support streaming output for `Bun.Archive` creation to avoid high memory usage
Native Zstd compression support in `Bun.Archive`
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, Bun.Archive appears to only support Gzip compression via the { compress: "gzip" } option.
To use Zstd (which is often preferred for its superior speed/compression ratio in CI/CD environments), developers currently have to generate a raw archive and manually pipe it through a CompressionStream:
const archive = new Bun.Archive(files);
const stream = (await archive.blob())
  .stream()
  .pipeThrough(new CompressionStream("zstd" as any)); // "zstd" requires type casting
This approach has two downsides:


Developer Experience: It requires verbose boilerplate code instead of a simple configuration option.


Type Safety: Since "zstd" is not yet part of the official CompressionFormat spec types, it often requires casting to any or ignoring TypeScript errors, making the code feel "hacky."


What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add native support for Zstd directly in the Bun.Archive constructor options.
const archive = new Bun.Archive(files, { compress: "zstd" });
What alternatives have you considered?


Current Workaround: Using pipeThrough(new CompressionStream("zstd")). This works but is unergonomic and requires type hacks.


Bun.spawn: invoking system tar --zstd, which adds a dependency on system binaries.

title: `--preserve-symlinks-main` should apply to test file path resolution for snapshot tests (Bun within hermetic build systems)
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun's snapshot tests fail when run in hermetic build systems (e.g Bazel) that use symlinked source files, even with --preserve-symlinks-main enabled.
Expected behavior:
bun --preserve-symlinks-main test symlink-to-test.ts
# Should find snapshots at: __snapshots__/symlink-to-test.ts.snap
Actual behavior:
bun --preserve-symlinks-main test symlink-to-test.ts
# Resolves symlink: /real/path/test.ts
# Looks for snapshots at: /real/path/__snapshots__/test.ts.snap
# Error: Failed to open snapshot file
Based on codebase exploration this comes from:
src/bun.js/test/snapshot.zig:
// Snapshot path constructed from test file's source path
var snapshot_file_path_buf: bun.PathBuffer = undefined;
// Uses: test_file.source.path.name.dirWithTrailingSlash()
src/bun.js/test/jest.zig:
pub fn getOrPutFile(this: *TestRunner, file_path: string) struct { file_id: File.ID }
// Stores file_path directly without normalization
The test file path stored in the registry appears to already be resolved (symlink followed) before reaching the test runner. The --preserve-symlinks-main flag affects module import resolution but not the test file path itself.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Extend --preserve-symlinks-main to also preserve symlinks for test file path resolution:

When a test file is loaded via symlink, store the symlink path in the file registry
Use the symlink path for test_file.source.path.name.dirWithTrailingSlash()
Construct snapshot paths relative to the symlink location

Would be happy to have a go at implementing this if deemed to be something that might be accepted.
What alternatives have you considered?
If extending --preserve-symlinks-main (or some other alternative flag) is not feasible, the snapshot dir could be made configurable via some relative path:
# bunfig.toml
[test]
snapshot_dir = "__snapshots__"  # Can be absolute or relative to cwd
bun test --snapshot-dir=__snapshots__

excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Summary
When a package is explicitly installed with a prerelease tag (e.g., bun add vite@beta), running bun update --latest overwrites it with the latest stable version, ignoring the user's intent to stay on the beta channel.

title: bun build --compile binaries fail when executed via explicit ld.so invocation (Termux/Android)
excerpt:
Description
Bun bundled executables created with bun build --compile fail to detect their embedded JavaScript when run via an explicit dynamic linker invocation. This prevents running Bun bundled binaries on systems like Termux (Android) where glibc must be loaded explicitly.
Environment

Platform: Android/Termux (ARM64)
Bun version: 1.3.3

Problem
Termux uses Bionic (Android's libc), but Bun is compiled against glibc. To run glibc binaries on Termux, users must invoke the glibc dynamic linker explicitly:
/path/to/glibc/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 ./my-bun-app
When executed this way, Bun falls back to CLI help mode instead of running the embedded JavaScript.
Root Cause
Bun bundled executables detect embedded JS by:

Reading /proc/self/exe to get the executable path
Opening that file and looking for the ---- Bun! ---- trailer

The problem: When running via explicit ld.so invocation, the kernel sets /proc/self/exe to point to ld-linux-aarch64.so.1, not the actual Bun binary:
$ /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 ./my-app -e "console.log(require('fs').readlinkSync('/proc/self/exe'))"
/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1   # ← Wrong! Should be ./my-app
Since ld.so doesn't have the ---- Bun! ---- trailer, Bun fails to find the embedded bytecode.
Proposed Solution
Add an environment variable (e.g., BUN_SELF_EXE) to override the /proc/self/exe detection:
BUN_SELF_EXE=/absolute/path/to/my-app /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 ./my-app
Suggested Implementation
In the bundled executable detection code, add a check for an environment variable before reading /proc/self/exe:
fn getSelfExePath() ![]const u8 {
    // Check for override first (for Termux/explicit ld.so scenarios)
    if (bun.getenvZ("BUN_SELF_EXE")) |path| {
        return path;
    }
    // Fall back to /proc/self/exe
    return std.fs.readLinkAbsolute("/proc/self/exe");
}
Current Workaround
Users must create a userland-exec wrapper that loads ld.so via mmap() instead of execve(), which preserves /proc/self/exe. This requires:

A Rust wrapper using the userland-execve crate
Appending the original binary's embedded data to the wrapper
Patching the file size in the trailer

This is complex and error-prone. A simple env var override would solve this elegantly.
Impact
This affects:

Termux/Android users wanting to run Bun apps
Container/chroot environments with non-standard library paths
Any system requiring explicit dynamic linker invocation

title: Deadlock: all threads permanently blocked due to lock ordering violation between allocator and thread pool (macOS arm64, Bun 1.3.5 SEA)
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.5 (Single Executable Application / --compile build)
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 arm (macOS 26.2, Apple Silicon)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
What steps can reproduce the bug?
We have not been able to produce a minimal reproduction yet. The deadlock occurs non-deterministically in a long-running Node.js-compatible CLI application compiled with bun build --compile. The application:

Runs an event loop that spawns child processes (via child_process), performs HTTP requests, and reads/writes files
Uses Bun's built-in thread pool for async I/O
Typically runs for 10–60 minutes before the deadlock triggers (when it does)

The deadlock appears to be a race condition in the interaction between Bun's GeneralPurposeAllocator and the thread pool completion/drain mechanism. It likely requires specific timing where a pool thread holds the allocator lock while the main thread is draining completed tasks.
What is the expected behavior?
The process should continue executing. Async tasks should complete and return results to the event loop.
What do you see instead?
The process freezes permanently. All threads are blocked on lock acquisition with zero CPU usage. The process never recovers and must be killed with kill -9.
Externally, the application's TUI shows a tool execution stuck at "Pending..." indefinitely. No new log output is produced. lsof shows no outbound network connections — only a dangling LISTEN socket.
Additional information
Detailed Analysis
We attached lldb and used macOS sample to capture the full thread state of the frozen process. Below is the complete analysis.
Thread State Summary



Thread
Name
State
Blocked On




#1
Main thread
__ulock_wait2
Lock A (allocator, heap)


#2–#13
"Bun Pool" workers (x12)
__ulock_wait2
Lock B (pool batch, BSS global)


#14
HTTP client
kevent64
Idle (no work to do)


#15
File watcher
__ulock_wait2
Lock (likely allocator-related)



Every thread capable of making progress is blocked. The HTTP client thread is idle in kevent64 but cannot receive work because the main thread is deadlocked.
The Two Locks
Lock A — Allocator lock (heap-resident, os_unfair_lock):
Address: 0x4e936ac2890 (heap object + 0x890)
Value:   0x00004002 (locked, with waiters)
Holder:  A pool thread (inferred from deadlock cycle)
Waiter:  Main thread

Lock B — Thread pool batch lock (BSS-resident, futex-style):
Address: 0x10434ff74 (__DATA.__bss + 609076)
Value:   0x00000001 (locked)
Holder:  M

title: Expose column type metadata (OIDs) on PostgreSQL query results
Intermittent hang on startup for Bun 1.3.7 and 1.3.8
excerpt:
Summary
Reproduction repo: https://github.com/ashleydavis/bun-hang-test
Bun sometimes hangs indefinitely on startup when running a script that uses both commander and picocolors in the same process. The hang is intermittent (often after hundreds or thousands of runs). Removing either dependency removes the hang. In practice the hang appears more frequently in the Photosphere project’s smoke tests than in this minimal repro’s loop (same underlying issue).
Impact
I have to pin Photosphere to Bun 1.3.6 until this issue is resolved; otherwise my smoke tests fail intermittently.
Environment

Bun versions that exhibit the hang: 1.3.7, 1.3.8
Bun version where hang was not observed: 1.3.6 (11 full runs of 5000 iterations each completed without hang)
OS: Linux (kernel 6.14.0-37-generic)
Dependencies: commander ^14.0.3, picocolors ^1.1.1

Reproduction
Minimal repro script (index.ts)
#!/usr/bin/env bun
import { program } from 'commander';
import pc from 'picocolors';

program
  .addHelpText('after', pc.bold('x'));

program.parseAsync(process.argv);
Steps


Create a project with commander and picocolors (e.g. bun add commander picocolors).


Save the script above as index.ts.


Run it many times; use a timeout to detect hangs:
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do
  echo "Run $i"
  timeout --foreground 60 bun run index.ts || exit 124
done


Eventually a run may hang and be killed by the 60s timeout (exit code 124).


Observed behavior

With both commander and picocolors: Hang reproduces (e.g. run 408, run 2471 in our tests).
With only commander or only picocolors: No hang observed.
Bun 1.3.6: No hang in 55,000 iterations across 11 full test runs.
Bun 1.3.7 / 1.3.8: Hang reproduces under the same repro.

Expected behavior
Every run of bun run index.ts should complete (or exit with an error); the process should not hang indefinitely.
Full reproduction repo
See the link at the top of this report, or use the script and steps above in any Bun project with commander and picocolors.
Additional notes

The hang appears to have been introduced between Bun 1.3.6 and 1.3.7.
Single manual runs can also hang occasionally; the loop + timeout is used to trigger and detect the intermittent hang reliably.
The hang shows up more frequently in Photosphere’s smoke tests than in this repo’s 5000-run test; this minimal repro is sufficient to reproduce but may require multiple full runs to see a hang.

title: bun test should produce reporter outfile when --bail is specified
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
According to bun's docs, --bail's primary purpose is CI environments. However it bails out so fast, it doesn't produce a reporter outfile when one is also specified "bun test --bail --reporter junit --reporter-outfile results.xml". CI has a lot of tooling around results files like visualization and statistics. Result file formats are the interface boundary of that tooling. With --bail all bun test provides is more or less unstructured stdout which is hard to build that CI tooling around.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
The solution is simply outputting a "reporter outfile" after a bail. Propose that tests which were not run because of a bail are labeled as skipped.
What alternatives have you considered?
Use mocha.
