title: StatWatcher GC race: finalize() doesn't clear Strong handle before WorkPool thread deinit
Range request example is off-by-one
Support custom dictionaries in "node:zlib" for (RFC 9842 CDT)
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
CDT (Compression Dictionary Transport, spec, datatracker) is a new HTTP protocol
(RFC draft) that allows browsers and servers to compress responses
using a shared pre-negotiated dictionary, achieving dramatically
better compression ratios for repeated content (APIs, HTML pages, etc).
CDT uses two new Content-Encoding values:

dcz dictionary-compressed Zstandard
dcb dictionary-compressed Brotli

To implement a CDT server in Bun today, you need to call
ZSTD_CCtx_loadDictionary / ZSTD_createCDict from libzstd,
but this is not exposed through node:zlib (bun).
What Node.js already supports
Node.js v22.19+ / v24.6+ added dictionary support to node:zlib (doc):
import { createZstdCompress, constants } from 'node:zlib'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'

const dict = readFileSync('my.dict')

const compress = createZstdCompress({
  params: {
    [constants.ZSTD_c_dict]: dict,
  }
})
What Bun currently does
Bun exposes createZstdCompress / createZstdDecompress and the
ZstdCompress / ZstdDecompress classes, but the params option
does not support ZSTD_c_dict / ZSTD_d_dict. Passing a dictionary
buffer is silently ignored.
Spec

RFC 9842 (Standards Track): https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9842
IETF Datatracker: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpbis-compression-dictionary/

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Proposed solution
In src/node_zlib.zig, expose ZSTD_CCtx_loadDictionary and
ZSTD_DCtx_loadDictionary when a dictionary buffer is provided
in the options params, matching the Node.js API surface.
What alternatives have you considered?
No response

Node.js handles the same scenario correctly — it uses inotify purely for change notification and does not attempt to open files inside the watched directory.
Steps to reproduce
# Create a directory with a file readable only by root
mkdir /tmp/test-watch
echo "secret" > /tmp/test-watch/private.txt
chmod 600 /tmp/test-watch/private.txt

# Run as non-root user
bun watch-dir.js /tmp/test-watch
# then trigger any change in the directory
// watch-dir.js
import { watch } from "fs";
watch("/tmp/test-watch", { persistent: true }, (eventType, filename) => {
  console.log(eventType, filename);
});
Expected behavior
fs.watch() should work identically to Node.js: emit events with (eventType, filename) without attempting to open files inside the directory.
Actual behavior
error: EACCES: permission denied, open '/tmp/test-watch/private.txt'
      at emitError (node:events:51:13)
      at #onEvent (node:fs:48:16)

Process crashes.
strace evidence
inotify_add_watch succeeds normally. The crash happens later in #onEvent when a file change is detected — Bun attempts to open() the changed file, which Node.js does not do.
Workaround
Using Node.js instead of Bun for this script works without issues.

title: Support bun:ffi on Windows ARM64
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Windows ARM64 support landed in #26215, but bun:ffi is still completely disabled on that target.
Today we explicitly gate it off in:

cmake/Options.cmake (DEFAULT_ENABLE_TINYCC OFF on WIN32 && aarch64)
src/bun.js/api/ffi.zig (cc(), callback(), dlopen(), linkSymbols() all throw when TinyCC is disabled)
test/js/bun/ffi/* (Windows ARM64 is treated as FFI-unavailable)

So native Windows ARM64 Bun exists, but any FFI-backed app/library still fails there.
This seems like the missing follow-up to #9824 / #26215.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Enable bun:ffi on native Windows ARM64.
Concretely, that likely means:

vendor/bump TinyCC to a revision that includes the Windows ARM64 work
get Bun’s FFI path green on real Windows ARM64
unskip/enable the FFI tests on Windows ARM64
flip ENABLE_TINYCC on for that target once stable

Relevant detail: Bun is still pinned to an older TinyCC revision in cmake/targets/BuildTinyCC.cmake, while the Windows ARM64 TinyCC work appears to have landed later upstream.
If the plan is not full TinyCC-backed support, it would still be useful to track whether dlopen() / fixed-symbol calls can be split from the TinyCC dependency.
What alternatives have you considered?

x64/baseline Bun under emulation: works around it, but not a real fix
app-level fallbacks: useful UX-wise, but doesn’t address the platform gap

x86_64 5-level page tables extend virtual addresses to 56 bits. Linux only hands out addresses < 2^48 for compatibility reasons but user space can mmap memory across the whole range (ref).

arm64 with 52 bits pointers and memory tagging (MTE) also produces addresses that don't fit, but the process has to a) mmap memory with a special flag, and b) turn on protection with a prctl

It seems like at leas the first one would be an issue for bun, right? The second one would be as well, if bun uses or wants to start using MTE.

title: Bun.secrets: secrets are accessible by any bun script without password prompt
excerpt:
What is the type of issue?
Documentation is confusing
What is the issue?
When one bun script stores a secret via Bun.secrets.set(), any other bun
script can read it silently — no Keychain password prompt, no Touch ID, no user
confirmation.
With compiled binaries (bun build --compile), macOS Keychain correctly
prompts for a password. But with scripts, all access goes through the same
bun binary, so Keychain treats them as the same application.
Reproduction
https://github.com/KarKarbI4/bun-secrets-process-isolation-test
git clone https://github.com/KarKarbI4/bun-secrets-process-isolation-test
cd bun-secrets-process-isolation-test
./run-tests.sh

Three independent scripts: writer.ts stores a secret, reader.ts reads it,
cleanup.ts deletes it. The test also compiles each into a standalone binary and
 runs again.

Results

┌────────┬────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┐
│        │  Script → Script   │         Binary → Binary          │
├────────┼────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Read   │ no password prompt │ password prompt                  │
├────────┼────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Delete │ no password prompt │ blocked (errSecInvalidOwnerEdit) │
└────────┴────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
Impact
A malicious or compromised dependency running via bun can silently read all
secrets stored by any other bun script — API tokens, database credentials, etc.
No password prompt, no user confirmation.
The documentation states "Process Isolation: Credentials are isolated per user
account" without clarifying that there is no isolation between bun scripts.
Suggestion

Update docs to clarify that any bun script under the same user can read
secrets created by any other bun script without a password prompt
Consider recommending bun build --compile for applications that need real
secret isolation
Investigate whether per-application ACLs (e.g. SecAccessCreate on macOS)
could be applied for interpreted scripts

Environment

Bun: 1.2.22
OS: macOS 15.5 (Darwin 24.6.0)
Arch: arm64

Where did you find it?
https://bun.com/docs/runtime/secrets

The fix requires a coordinated change between oven-sh/WebKit and oven-sh/bun:
Upstream (oven-sh/WebKit)
Re-add -DUSE_SYSTEM_MALLOC=ON to the cmake invocation in windows-release.ps1:

     -DPORT="JSCOnly" `
     -DENABLE_STATIC_JSC=ON `
+    -DUSE_SYSTEM_MALLOC=ON `
     ...
This was previously added in WebKit PR #97 (July 2025) but was removed in a later update. The current prebuilt WebKit for Windows (commit 00e825523d) does not have this flag.
Downstream (oven-sh/bun) — after prebuilts are rebuilt

Remove bmalloc.lib from Windows link targets in cmake/targets/BuildBun.cmake
Exclude bmallocLib(cfg) on Windows in scripts/build/deps/webkit.ts (TODO comments already added in #28098)
Add CI regression guard (assertNoBmallocOnWindows)

WebKit PR #97: Originally added -DUSE_SYSTEM_MALLOC=ON for Windows
Bun PR #20931: Removed bmalloc.lib from link targets (worked with the WebKit fix)

Description

While Bun supports standard Git dependencies, the additional path: or subdirectory resolution logic appears to trigger a memory or assertion failure during the cloning/hoisting phase.

Navigate to the specified subdirectory path.
Install the package and its dependencies as a standard linked dependency, similar to pnpm or npm.

Create a new project with bun init.
Add a Git dependency that points to a subdirectory:

title: Segfault when native code repeatedly invokes `JSCallback({ threadsafe: true })`
excerpt:
What happens
Hi, I stumbled upon an issue while adding an Electrobun (bun:ffi) backend to my lib, where event streams can fire repeatedly into the same JSCallback. A native library repeatedly calling a Bun JSCallback({ threadsafe: true }) can segfault Bun.
I reduced this to a very small repro:

one JS callback
passed directly to native, which repeatedly invokes the callback from a worker thread
callback body only increments a counter

Minimal repro shape
I've published the repro here:
https://github.com/hsjoberg/bun-ffi-crash
It creates a small Rust lib that we then load in via bun:ffi.
JS side:

create a JSCallback with { threadsafe: true } whose body only increments a counter
pass the callback pointer to native

Native side:

start a worker thread
repeatedly invoke that callback in a loop

The repro is intentionally hammering the FFI path, but I originally hit this in my library with only a small number of stream events.
Setting the worker count to 2+ makes the crash reproduce consistently for me. With 1 worker thread, it is still reproducible, but more intermittent.
To run the reproducer:
bun install
bun run repro
Stack traces
I have confirmed this crash on Windows x64, macOS arm64, and Linux x64 (via WSL2). The exact crash site varies, but on macOS and Linux the stack traces consistently pass through JSFFIFunction.cpp in Bun’s threadsafe FFI callback path.

ASan use-after-poison in WebWorker__notifyNeedTermination when terminate() called from message handler
excerpt:
Seen on debian-13 x64-asan in build #39654 running test/js/web/workers/worker.test.ts.
Stack (abbreviated)
==6014==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: use-after-poison on address 0x105c606215a0
READ of size 1 at 0x105c606215a0 thread T0
    #0 atomic.Value(bun.js.web_worker.Status).load  vendor/zig/lib/std/atomic.zig:14
    #1 WebWorker__notifyNeedTermination            src/bun.js/web_worker.zig:571
    #2 jsWorkerPrototypeFunction_terminateBody     src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/JSWorker.cpp:549
    ...
    #16 EventTarget::innerInvokeEventListeners
    #19 Worker::dispatchEvent                       src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/Worker.cpp:323
    #20 jsFunctionPostMessage::$_0::operator()      src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/Worker.cpp:669  <-- queued task lambda
    #23 EventLoopTask::performTask

Address 0x105c606215a0 is a wild pointer inside of access range of size 0x000000000001.
Shadow byte: f7 (Poisoned by user)

Analysis
Shadow byte f7 is the mimalloc poison marker for freed allocations.
The sequence:

Worker thread calls postMessage → schedules an EventLoopTask on the parent thread via a lambda at Worker.cpp:669 that captures Worker*
Worker exits and the Zig WebWorker struct is freed before the parent processes the queued task
Parent runs the task → dispatches message event → JS event listener calls worker.terminate()
terminate() → WebWorker__notifyNeedTermination → this.status.load(.acquire) on freed memory at web_worker.zig:571

The Worker C++ wrapper (or the task lambda) needs to keep the underlying WebWorker alive while message-dispatch tasks are pending on the parent event loop.
There are existing TODOs from @190n at web_worker.zig:581,584 suggesting this area is already being reworked.

title: jemalloc reserves ~485GB VSZ per process on aarch64 macOS (Apple Silicon, 16KB pages)
excerpt:
Environment

Bun version: 1.3.10
OS: macOS 15.7.4 (24G517)
Hardware: Apple M3 Pro, 36GB RAM, aarch64
Page size: 16KB (Apple Silicon)

Description
Each bun process reserves approximately 485GB of virtual address space at startup on Apple Silicon macOS, before executing any user code. This is visible immediately via ps -o vsz.
  PID    RSS      VSZ COMMAND
63053 229936 485365472 bun run (session 1)
63031 248144 485304096 bun run (session 2)

VSZ ~462GB per process. RSS is only ~230MB — the virtual reservation is ~2000x actual physical usage.
Impact
With multiple long-running bun processes, the combined virtual address space exhausts macOS's ability to handle new mmap requests. macOS begins compressing mapped pages aggressively. Once the compressed pool fills:

New allocations fail silently or get shorted
Process behavior becomes unpredictable
Eventually OOM kill or segfault

On this machine with 2 active bun processes: ~930GB combined VSZ against 36GB physical RAM. macOS is compressing ~100GB of virtual mappings at any given time during interactive use. This manifests as a slow death — the machine appears to be holding 200GB+ in compressed RAM while interactive, with allocations progressively failing.
Root cause hypothesis
jemalloc's arena initialization calls mmap(MAP_ANON) to reserve a large contiguous virtual region upfront. On x86_64 Linux with 4KB pages this is less visible. On aarch64 macOS with 16KB pages, the arena reservation is significantly larger in address space terms, and macOS's VM system does not aggressively reclaim unreferenced anonymous mappings the same way Linux does.
This is compounded by any application that mmaps additional files (e.g. git pack files for snapshot/session storage) on top of the baseline reservation.
Reproduction
# Any bun process on Apple Silicon macOS
bun run some-script.ts &
ps -o pid,rss,vsz,command -p $!

title: `bun add` fails to resolve annotated Git tag over SSH for private GitHub repo, but succeeds with the peeled commit SHA
excerpt:
I am seeing a Git dependency resolution issue with Bun when installing a private GitHub repository by annotated tag over SSH.
Bun fails to resolve the tag name, even though:

the repository exists
SSH auth works
Git itself can resolve the tag
the tag is annotated
the tag points to a valid commit
installing by the peeled commit SHA works

Bun Version
bun --version
Observed with:
bun 1.3.10

Environment

OS: Windows host + WSL Ubuntu
GitHub private repository
SSH-based Git access
Bun running inside WSL

Repository Ref That Fails
bun add -d git+ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#v0.0.3
Error
error: no commit matching "v0.0.3" found for "git+ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#v0.0.3" (but repository exists)

Expected Behavior
Bun should resolve the annotated tag v0.0.3 to its commit and install the package.
Actual Behavior
Bun reports that no commit matches the tag, even though Git can resolve it correctly.
Git Verification
These commands work correctly:
git ls-remote --tags git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git
git ls-remote git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git refs/tags/v0.0.3^{}
Output:
... refs/tags/v0.0.3

git cat-file -t v0.0.3
git show v0.0.3:package.json

the tagged package contents are correct

Important Comparison
Installing by the peeled commit SHA works:
bun add -d git+ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#<hash>
That succeeds.
So the problem appears to be specifically Bun’s tag-name resolution for git+ssh Git dependencies, not repository access or package contents.

rm -rf ~/.bun/install/cache
bun add --force --no-cache -d git+ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#v0.0.3

This suggests a Bun Git tag resolution issue rather than a GitHub or SSH configuration problem

bun add -d git+ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git#v0.0.3

title: Bun.zstdDecompress lacks decompressed size limit
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun.zstdDecompress currently appears to decompress the entire input without allowing callers to specify a maximum decompressed size. When handling untrusted input, this makes applications vulnerable to compression bombs.
This is both a security concern and an API limitation, since most decompression APIs provide a way to bound the output size.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A max output size parameter.
What alternatives have you considered?
Using node:zlib or DecompressionStream and checking its size as it gets streamed and abort after reaching a certain threshold, but those APIs are slower than Bun.zstdDecompress.

excerpt:
Bug Report
Summary
bun install hangs indefinitely on Linux after successfully downloading all packages. The hang occurs in the post-install phase (confirmed via --verbose) and appears to be the OSV security scanner hitting the OS ARG_MAX limit.
This was previously reported as #23607 and fixed in PR #23706, but we found the bug is not limited to bun 1.3.6 — it also reproduces on bun 1.3.5 and bun 1.3.10.

macOS (ARM64): works fine with the same lockfile and packages
Packages: ~1,243 packages in a monorepo

Steps to Reproduce

Create a monorepo with ~1,200+ packages using bun.lock (text lockfile)
Run on a Linux x64 machine with a cold cache:

Observe packages downloading normally for ~6 minutes
Observe complete silence for 14+ minutes before the process is killed

Skip installing fsevents - os mismatch   ← last line at T+6min
[14+ minutes of silence]

All of the following hang on Linux, all complete successfully on macOS:

 'a': a,

This sort of import and map pattern is all over our app, and so "fixes" like using a function to return the constant are not viable. too risky and easy to miss a map which looks good and should work, but doesn't because the bundler decided to sort that constant lower in the chunk.

title: Feature request: streaming / temp-file-backed multipart parsing for Bun.serve uploads
excerpt:
What is the problem?
For server-side multipart/form-data uploads in Bun.serve, the currently documented APIs appear to be eager materializers:

Request.formData()
Bun.readableStreamToFormData(...)

That is useful for small forms, but it leaves a gap for large file uploads. If an app wants to handle large uploads without large RSS spikes, it currently has to parse the multipart stream manually and spool file parts to disk itself.
In PocketBun, we just had to add a custom request-scoped multipart parser for this reason. The main goal was to avoid materializing uploaded files as in-memory blobs and instead expose temp-file-backed uploaded parts.
Why this matters
Large multipart uploads are a common server-side use case. Today there does not seem to be a first-class Bun API for:

iterating multipart parts incrementally
streaming file parts directly from the request body
spooling uploaded files to temp files
setting per-part and per-request multipart limits

Without that, frameworks and apps end up reimplementing multipart parsing themselves, which is:

easy to get wrong
duplicated across the ecosystem
likely less efficient than a native implementation

What I’m requesting
A native Bun API for streaming multipart parsing on the server side.
Any of these shapes would solve the problem:
Option A: async multipart iterator on Request
for await (const part of request.multipart()) {
  part.name;
  part.filename;
  part.contentType;
  part.headers;
  part.body; // ReadableStream<Uint8Array>
}
Option B: parser helper over a ReadableStream
const parts = Bun.readableStreamToMultipartParts(request.body!, boundary, options);
for await (const part of parts) {
  // ...
}
Option C: enhanced formData() with storage options
const form = await request.formData({
  fileStorage: "tempfile", // or "memory"
  maxMemoryFileSize: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
  tempDir: "/tmp",
  limits: {
    maxParts: 1000,
    maxFileSize: ...,
    maxFieldSize: ...,
    maxHeaderBytes: ...,
  },
});
Important capabilities
Whatever API shape Bun prefers, these capabilities would be especially useful:

stream each part incrementally
avoid buffering entire uploaded files in memory
optionally spool file parts to temp files
expose name, filename, content-type, and raw headers
support limits like:

max parts
max file size
max non-file field size
max header bytes


clean up temp files automatically or provide an explicit cleanup hook

Steps to Reproduce

{

title: `bun run` fails with `CouldntReadCurrentDirectory` when ancestor directories are not readable
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+af24e281e
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.18.18-1-lts x86_64 unknown
What steps can reproduce the bug?
bun run fatally errors when it cannot openat ancestor directories (/, /home/), even though getcwd() succeeds. This makes bun unusable in sandboxed environments that restrict filesystem access to the working directory.
Run bun inside any Landlock sandbox that grants full access to the CWD but not to ancestor directories like / or /home/. No project files needed.
I'm using https://github.com/always-further/nono v0.19
# Using nono as an example, but any Landlock sandbox would trigger this
nono run --allow-cwd --allow path/to/bun -- bun eval "console.log('hello')"
What is the expected behavior?
bun eval should print hello. getcwd() succeeds — bun knows the working directory path. It should not need to open ancestor directories to function.
What do you see instead?
error loading current directory
error: An internal error occurred (CouldntReadCurrentDirectory)

Additional information
Root cause (strace)
getcwd("/home/benjabobs/dev/minimal-repro-dir", 4096) = 34          # succeeds
openat(AT_FDCWD, "bunfig.toml", O_RDONLY) = -1 ENOENT           # fine
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = -1 EACCES  # fatal
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/home/", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = -1 EACCES  # fatal
error loading current directory

bun walks up the directory tree after getcwd() already returned the path. When any ancestor openat fails, bun treats it as a fatal error rather than gracefully continuing.
Why this is an issue
Sandboxed execution is increasingly common (Landlock, containers, CI). Tools like Node.js and tsc work fine in these environments because they don't require openat on ancestor directories. bun's ancestor traversal — likely for config file discovery — should be best-effort, not fatal. If getcwd() succeeds, bun has the information it needs.
Suggested fix
Make the ancestor directory walk non-fatal. If openat on a parent directory fails with EACCES, skip it and continue rather than aborting. Config file discovery (e.g. bunfig.toml) in parent directories can gracefully degrade when access is denied.

title: JSC/WebKit IOAccelerator GPU memory grows monotonically in long-lived Ink/React terminal apps
excerpt:
Summary
When Bun runs long-lived terminal applications using Ink (React for terminals), the JSC/WebKit compositor allocates IOAccelerator GPU buffer slabs (128 MB each) that grow monotonically and are never freed. A session running for days accumulates 10+ slabs (966 MB) of non-reclaimable dirty GPU pages. Plain Bun processes without Ink stay at ~1.3 MB.
This was discovered investigating Claude Code (a Bun-based CLI tool using Ink) where idle sessions held ~1 GB of IOAccelerator footprint each despite only 7 MB RSS.
Reproduction
Shows the issue (Ink-like sustained rendering)
Any long-lived Bun process using Ink/React for terminal rendering will exhibit IOAccelerator growth over hours. The clearest reproduction is Claude Code (claude) run for 1+ hours with active use.
Baseline (no issue)
# Plain Bun — stays at 1 slab, ~1.3 MB IOAccelerator

title: MariaDB/MySQL SSL connections broken in Bun 1.3.11 (works in 1.3.10)
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11
What platform is your computer?
Linux (Azure App Service on Linux, oven/bun:debian Docker image). Also affects compiled binaries via bun build --compile.
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Connect to a MySQL/MariaDB server over TLS using the mariadb npm package (v3.4.5) via @prisma/adapter-mariadb (v7.3.0), with a custom CA certificate:
import { PrismaMariaDb } from '@prisma/adapter-mariadb';
import fs from 'node:fs';

const adapter = new PrismaMariaDb({
    host: 'my-mysql-server.mysql.database.azure.com',
    port: 3306,
    user: 'myuser',
    password: 'mypassword',
    database: 'mydb',
    ssl: {
        ca: fs.readFileSync('/path/to/ca-cert.pem'),
        checkServerIdentity: () => undefined,
    },
});

The server is Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server presenting a certificate chain: server cert → Microsoft Azure RSA TLS Issuing CA 04 → DigiCert Global Root G2.
What is the expected behavior?
The database connection should be established successfully, as it does with Bun 1.3.10.
What do you see instead?
All connection attempts fail silently at the TLS level. Prisma reports a connection pool timeout with no connections ever being established:
Timed out fetching a new connection from the connection pool.
More info: http://www.prisma.io/docs/reference/api-reference/error-reference#p2024
(Current connection pool timeout: 10, connection limit: 10, pool: active=0, idle=0)
Key observations:

TCP connectivity is fine (verified via curl -v telnet://host:3306)
openssl s_client verifies the certificate chain successfully using system CAs
No connections are ever established (active=0 idle=0) — the TLS handshake itself fails
Providing the correct CA certificate (DigiCert Global Root G2) does not help
The exact same code, dependencies, and server work perfectly with Bun 1.3.10

Workaround
Pin Bun to 1.3.10 in CI:
image: oven/bun:1.3.10-debian
Additional information

The mariadb npm package (v3.4.5) relies on Bun's TLS implementation (BoringSSL) when compiled/run with Bun
This may be related to #23735 (Bun 1.3.0 CA certificate regression)
The issue affects compiled binaries (bun build --compile) — the compiled binary embeds Bun's runtime including its TLS stack
Tested with both the original CA cert and the correct root CA cert — neither works on 1.3.11
The MySQL server has not changed; only the Bun version changed between working and broken deploys

title: `bun install` fails to resolve GitHub dependency when it appears both as direct and transitive dependency
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.10+30e609e08
What platform is your computer?
Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Given two public GitHub repos where package-b depends on package-c:

rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c — leaf package, no dependencies
rentalhost/bun-issue-package-b — depends on "@rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c": "github:rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c"

Create this package.json where package-c appears both as a direct dependency and as a transitive dependency (through package-b):
{
  "name": "repro",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "@rentalhost/bun-issue-package-b": "github:rentalhost/bun-issue-package-b",
    "@rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c": "github:rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c"
  }
}
Then run:
bun install
What is the expected behavior?
Both packages should install successfully. pnpm install and npm install work fine with the same package.json.
What do you see instead?
bun install v1.3.10 (30e609e0)
Resolving dependencies
Resolved, downloaded and extracted [4]
error: @rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c@github:rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c failed to resolve

Additional information
Proof matrix



#
Direct package-c
Transitive (via package-b)
Result




1
github:rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c
not present
PASS


2
not present
yes (via package-b)
PASS


3
github:rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c
yes (via package-b)
FAIL


4
github:rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c#main
yes (via package-b)
PASS



The resolution only fails when:

A GitHub dependency appears both as a direct dependency and as a transitive dependency (through another GitHub package), AND
The direct specifier has no explicit ref (no #main, #branch, or #commit)

Adding #main to the direct specifier resolves the issue. Adding #main only to the parent package does not help — the ref must be on the duplicated dependency itself.
Workaround
Append #main (or a commit SHA) to the direct GitHub dependency:
"@rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c": "github:rentalhost/bun-issue-package-c#main"

title: `Bun.cron(…)` writes logs to the insecure globally shared temp dir on macOS
excerpt:

1.3.11
What platform is your computer?
macOS 26.3.1
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Register and run a job using Bun.cron(…)
What is the expected behavior?
Logs are not leaked to all other users on the system.
What do you see instead?
The daemon config at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ use the following temp dirs:
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>/tmp/bun.cron.(title).stdout.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>/tmp/bun.cron.(title).stderr.log</string>

This is shared by all users. From Apple's docs: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Security/Conceptual/SecureCodingGuide/Articles/RaceConditions.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/TP40002585-SW10

The temporary directories in macOS are shared among multiple users. This requires that they be writable by multiple users. Any time you work on files in a location to which others have read/write access, there’s the potential for the file to be compromised or corrupted.
The best way to handle this is to create a safe temporary directory that only you can access, then write the files into that directory.
To do this:
In a cocoa app, call NSTemporaryDirectory.
At the POSIX layer, call confstr and pass the constant _CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR as the name parameter.

If the path needs to be deterministically derived for a given job, placing them under https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nstemporarydirectory() would be best.
(I'd personally also use this chance to group bun cron folders under a parent folder to avoid writing a whole bunch of files at the top level, but this is not so severe an issues since it's a temp dir.)

title: CSS bundler inlines entire font as base64, including unused Unicode ranges
excerpt:
When using Bun's fullstack dev server, @font-face declarations with local font files (eg Nunito) get bundled by inlining the entire font as a base64 data URL in the CSS output.
The problem is that the font file often contains glyphs for multiple Unicode ranges (Latin, Cyrillic, Vietnamese,  etc.), and the bundler inlines all of them — even when the original CSS had separate @font-face blocks with Unicode-range descriptors to enable the browser to fetch only the subsets it needs.
This defeats the purpose of Unicode-range subsetting and significantly inflates the CSS bundle size.
Expected behaviour: The bundler should either preserve the separate @font-face blocks and their external URLs (so the browser can selectively fetch subsets), or at minimum not merge/inline font files that use Unicode-range to split subsets.
Reproduction: Import a Google Fonts-style CSS file that splits a font into multiple @font-face rules by Unicode-range, then inspect the bundled CSS output.

macOS Apple Silicon: memory invisible to RSS — bmalloc slabs, worker cleanup gaps, GC safety bugs
excerpt:
Summary
macOS Apple Silicon processes exhibit monotonically growing memory that is invisible to process.memoryUsage().rss and bun:jsc.memoryUsage().current. The real consumption — measured by footprint or vmmap — can be 100-200x higher than reported RSS, causing silent heap death on unified memory architectures where CPU and GPU share the same DRAM.
This issue aggregates findings from several related issues (#28234, #5709, #27790, #28139, #20912, #18608, #17228) and identifies root causes, missing diagnostics, and actionable fixes.
Problem
What users see

Bun process RSS is 7 MB but footprint shows 1.3 GB
37 idle Bun+Ink sessions consume 62.7 GB on a 32 GB machine (reported in #28234)
Worker spawning loop: 8 iterations → OOM crash, each worker allocates ~100 MB but RSS grows ~1 GB per iteration (#5709)
Bulk fetch (9.5k requests) → segfault in us_internal_ssl_socket_close (#20912)

What's actually happening
Three independent mechanisms consume unified memory without being reflected in RSS:
1. bmalloc/pas 128 MB IOAccelerator-tagged slabs (#28234)

Every Bun process gets at least one 128 MB slab tagged IOAccelerator (VM tag 10)
JSC's bmalloc/pas allocator uses vm_allocate() for large page-aligned allocations
These slabs are never returned to the OS — pas retains them for internal reuse
Ink/React rendering at 20fps causes rapid allocation churn → 7+ slabs (34 MB dirty) in 5 seconds, growing to 10+ slabs (966 MB dirty) over days
JSC__VM__shrinkFootprint exists in bindings.cpp:4686 but is never called during normal operation

2. Worker thread cleanup is incomplete (#5709)

VirtualMachine.deinit() (VirtualMachine.zig:1976) is a documented stub — comment says "deinit here isn't implemented, so freeing workers will leak the vm"
mi_thread_done() is declared in mimalloc.zig:31 but never called in worker exit path
JSC__VM__deinit (bindings.cpp:4739) is literally void JSC__VM__deinit(VM*) {} — empty
Thread-local variables on the main mimalloc heap are abandoned when detached worker threads exit
allWorkers() HashMap (Worker.cpp:75) grows until JS wrapper is GC'd

3. GC safety bugs cause use-after-free crashes (#27790, #28139)

node/crypto/ has 31 unprotected toString(globalObject) calls where only 1 has EnsureStillAliveScope
Pattern: toString() → allocation (triggers GC) → view() on freed string → segfault
#28139 was a specific instance (fault address decoded to ASCII "github.c"), fixed in JSHash.cpp:169
But the exact same pattern exists in JSHmac.cpp:132, JSSign.cpp:2

title: execAsIfNode doesn't resolve symlinks for entry point (breaks .bin/ scripts)
excerpt:
What version of Bun is this bug report for?
1.3.11
What platform is your computer?
darwin aarch64, linux x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
When bun runs a package script (e.g. via bun run or bunx), it sets up a fake node executable by symlinking bun to a temporary path named node and prepending that to PATH (see createFakeTemporaryNodeExecutable). This also happens with the --bun flag (ctx.debug.run_in_bun). Any child process that invokes node will actually run bun with argv[0] ending in "node", triggering the execAsIfNode codepath.
The issue manifests when a tool spawns node to run a .bin/ script (which is a symlink to the real package). For example with markdownlint-cli2:

.bin/markdownlint-cli2 is a symlink → ../markdownlint-cli2/markdownlint-cli2-bin.mjs
markdownlint-cli2-bin.mjs does import { "main" as markdownlintCli2 } from "./markdownlint-cli2.mjs" (a relative import that only works from the real package directory)

Steps:

bun install markdownlint-cli2
bunx markdownlint-cli2 or bun --bun markdownlint-cli2 — sets up the fake node symlink
If the tool internally calls node node_modules/.bin/markdownlint-cli2, it hits execAsIfNode which passes the symlink path directly to Run.boot() without resolving it

Minimal reproduction:
mkdir /tmp/test-symlink && cd /tmp/test-symlink
bun init -y
bun install markdownlint-cli2

# Create a node symlink to bun (same as what --bun / bunx does)
ln -sf "$(which bun)" ./node

# This fails — process.argv[1] is the .bin symlink, not the real path
./node ./node_modules/.bin/markdownlint-cli2
What is the expected behavior?
process.argv[1] should contain the real path (after symlink resolution), not the symlink path. This is what Node.js does by default.
Node.js resolves symlinks on the main entry point in resolveMainPath():
const preserveSymlinksMain = getOptionValue('--preserve-symlinks-main');
if (!preserveSymlinksMain) {
  const { toRealPath } = require('internal/modules/helpers');
  mainPath = toRealPath(mainPath);
}

"For the main module, we use the --preserve-symlinks-main flag instead mainly for backward compatibility... Most likely this was intended to keep .bin/ binaries working, as following those symlinks is usually required for the imports in the corresponding files to resolve."

node:http is broken for proxies — 4 PRs fixing createConnection, upgrade sockets, connection close, and socket cleanup
excerpt:
Summary
Bun's node:http implementation has several interrelated bugs that make it effectively unusable for HTTP/WebSocket proxy use cases. Libraries like http-proxy, node-http-proxy, ws, vite, and express-ws are all affected.
We run an internal proxy built on Node.js at Crunchloop, and our end-to-end test suite uncovered these issues when we attempted to run it on Bun. After diagnosing each failure, we found that most of them had already been reported as open issues — some dating back over two years. We've published a patched build at crunchloop/bun@bun-v1.3.11-dap.2 with all four fixes applied, and our full e2e suite passes against it.
Each fix has its own PR with regression tests that fail on current Bun and pass with the fix.
The four issues
1. createConnection option is completely ignored — #28207
http.request({ createConnection }) never calls the user-provided function. This is the primary mechanism proxies use to route requests over custom sockets (e.g., Unix domain sockets, tunneled connections).

Fixes #7471

2. Upgrade socket.write() silently drops data — #28347
After an HTTP upgrade, socket.write() is a no-op — the 101 handshake response is never sent, and bidirectional streaming doesn't work. This breaks every WebSocket proxy in the Node ecosystem.

Fixes #9882, #18945, #10441, #14522, #15489, #16819

3. Socket not destroyed on native close, causing server.close() to hang — #28350
When the native socket closes, Bun pushes null to the readable stream but never calls destroy(). If the readable is paused or the writable was never ended, autoDestroy never fires, leaving a zombie socket. server._connections never decrements, so server.close() hangs forever.

Fixes #13184, #19563, #23648

4. TCP connection never closed after async chunked response with Connection: close — #28390
When a server responds asynchronously (setTimeout, proxy, database query) with chunked transfer encoding and Connection: close, the response body is fully sent (including the 0\r\n\r\n terminator) but the socket FIN is never sent. The connection stays open indefinitely.
Impact
These bugs combine to make proxy workloads non-functional on Bun:

WebSocket proxying doesn't work at all (issues 1 + 2)
HTTP proxying leaks connections and hangs on shutdown (issues 3 + 4)
10+ open issues are addressed by these four PRs
Libraries affected: http-proxy, node-http-proxy, ws, vite, express-ws, and anything that uses createConnection or the upgrade event

Description
Bun crashes immediately with a panic: attempt to use null value on a Windows Server 2019 virtual machine where AVX/AVX2 instructions are not exposed by the hypervisor. Bun correctly detects no_avx no_avx2 and selects the baseline build, but the baseline build crashes on startup instead of running normally.

The baseline (no-AVX) build of Bun should run without crashing on VMs where AVX instructions are not available. "CPU lacks AVX support" is a warning, but it should not lead to a panic.

The crash happens very early in execution (5ms elapsed) with minimal memory usage (28MB RSS), suggesting this is a startup/initialization issue in the baseline code path.
This is a virtual machine environment — the underlying Xeon E5-2667 v4 supports AVX2, but the hypervisor does not pass through AVX to the guest OS. This is a common configuration in cloud and enterprise VM environments.
VMs without AVX passthrough are widespread (e.g., older Hyper-V, some VMware configurations, many cloud instances). The baseline build should handle this gracefully.

The source address fdaa:bbcc:ddee:... is a private/ULA IPv6 that cannot reach public internet. The interface reports it as deprecated:
$ ifconfig en0 | grep fdaa
inet6 fdaa:bbcc:ddee:0:1482:395a:59be:8c13 prefixlen 64 deprecated autoconf secured

Diagnostic details

curl -6 https://registry.npmjs.org/lodash/latest also fails (IPv6 is broken system-wide), but curl https://... works because curl implements Happy Eyeballs and falls back to IPv4
--dns-result-order=ipv4first flag has no effect — bun still uses IPv6
BUN_CONFIG_DNS_RESOLVER=system and BUN_DNS_RESOLVER=native have no effect
--network-concurrency=1 has no effect
Disabling IPv6 on the interface resolves the issue (networksetup -setv6off Wi-Fi)

Notes
This may be a regression or gap in the Happy Eyeballs implementation from #10731. The fix was shipped but doesn't seem to handle the case where the OS has a broken/deprecated IPv6 source address — bun picks IPv6, the SYN never

Bug: "toMatchInlineSnapshot with bad string literal"
問題 / Issue：
toMatchInlineSnapshot 必須傳入字面量字串，無法使用 JSON.stringify() 等動態方式生成期望值。
toMatchInlineSnapshot requires a string literal argument, cannot use dynamic expressions like JSON.stringify().
環境 / Environment：Bun: 1.3.10+
隱形 BUG / Hidden BUG
⚠️ 嚴重性：這個 BUG 不只是單個測試失敗，而是會導致測試框架崩潰！

當測試執行時：ELIFECYCLE Test failed 出現在測試結果底部
當測試 skip 時：所有測試正常通過

對比：toMatchObject with expect.any 的 BUG 可以被正常捕捉（不會崩潰），但 toMatchInlineSnapshot with bad string literal 的 BUG 會導致框架崩潰。
失敗案例 / Failing Case
it("toMatchInlineSnapshot 失敗 / fails", () => {
    const actual = { foo: "foo", bar: "bar" };

    // ❌ 錯誤：Argument must be a string literal
    expect(actual).toMatchInlineSnapshot(JSON.stringify({
        foo: "foo",
        bar: "bar",
    }));
});

error: Failed to update inline snapshot: Argument must be a string literal

a-001 ~ a-005    ✓ (正常印出)
a-006, a-007     ✓ (正常印出，屬於 toMatchSnapshot)
[start] a-008    ✓ (正常印出)
❌ BUG happen!   ← 錯誤發生 (expect with toMatchInlineSnapshot)
[end] a-009      ✓ (仍然印出！BUG 後的 log 仍然執行)
[start] a-010    ✓ (正常印出)
❌ BUG happen!   ← 錯誤發生 (第一個 expect with toMatchInlineSnapshot)
a-011            ✓ (仍然印出)
❌ BUG happen!   ← 錯誤發生 (第二個 expect with toMatchInlineSnapshot)
[end] a-012      ✓ (仍然印出！BUG 後的 log 仍然執行)
a-013, a-014     ✓ (正常印出)

BUG 位置總結 / BUG locations summary



BUG
位置
程式碼




BUG 1
[start] a-008 之後
expect({...}).toMatchInlineSnapshot(JSON.stringify({...}))


BUG 2
[start] a-010 之後
expect("...").toMatchInlineSnapshot(JSON.stringify({...}))


BUG 3
a-011 之後
expect(() => { expect("...").toMatchInlineSnapshot(JSON.stringify({...})) }).not.toThrow()



⚠️ BUG 3 的特殊之處 / Special behavior of BUG 3
不論是 ).not.toThrow(); or ).toThrow(); 或不管有沒有在 expect(() => { ... }) 裡面都會發生 BUG！
Whether it's ).not.toThrow(); or ).toThrow(); or whether it's inside expect(() => { ... }) or not, the BUG will occur!

BUG 發生在 toMatchInlineSnapshot 使用 JSON.stringify() 作為參數時


BUG 發生時，測試框架進入錯誤狀態


但奇怪的是，後續的 console.log() 仍然會執行！


這表明 BUG 不是發生在 JavaScript 執行層面，而是在測試框架更新 snapshot 的層面


BUG occurs when toMatchInlineSnapshot uses JSON.stringify() as argument


When BUG occurs, test framework enters error state

title: Feature Request: Add resumable multipart upload support in S3 (reuse UploadId, continue PartNumber, complete with previous parts)
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Large S3 uploads can fail because of network drops, app restarts, or system sleep. When that happens, it is hard to resume safely in Bun currently.
To resume a multipart upload, users need to:

keep and reuse the same UploadId
continue from the correct PartNumber
complete using both old uploaded parts and new uploaded parts
Without this, uploads may restart from 0, which wastes time, bandwidth, and cost.

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add official resumable multipart upload support in Bun S3:

accept resume options: uploadId, partNumber, and previous parts data (partsXML or similar)
if uploadId is set, skip CreateMultipartUpload and continue UploadPart on the existing upload
start new parts from the given partNumber
on CompleteMultipartUpload, include both old and new parts
do not switch to single PUT while in resume mode
validate option rules:

partNumber > 1 must require uploadId
previous parts data must require uploadId


for presigned URLs, include custom query params used by multipart APIs (for example ?uploads= and ?uploadId=...) in both signature input and final URL
add tests for resume validation and presign query behavior

What alternatives have you considered?


Restart upload from 0 after any failure.
This is simple, but for large files it is slow and increases bandwidth and request cost.


Build full resume logic in application code.
This works, but every app has to re-implement multipart state handling, part tracking, and completion payload building, which is easy to get wrong.


Use AWS SDK directly for resumable multipart flow.
This is possible, but it means users must bypass Bun S3 APIs for a core upload case, leading to mixed APIs and extra integration code.

Bug Description:
When running bun update -i (or bun update --interactive) in a bun workspace, it only scans and allows updating dependencies from the package.json in the current working directory. It does not consider dependencies from other workspace packages or the root package.json.
Steps to reproduce:

Create a bun workspace with multiple packages
Add different dependencies to each workspace package's package.json
Run bun update -i from the workspace root or any subdirectory

title: Serious Concerns Regarding Versioning Strategy and Production Stability, Was Migrating to Bun the Appropriate Decision?
excerpt:
To the Bun Team,
First of all, I would like to congratulate you on your recent milestones and your partnership/connection with Anthropic. It is an exciting time for the ecosystem, and seeing Bun evolve is something we have all been rooting for.
However, I am writing this as a Strategic System Architect who has made the bold decision to move numerous production projects and consultancies entirely to Bun. While we believe in Bun’s vision as a high-performance, agile alternative to Node.js and Deno, recent releases (specifically 1.3.10 and 1.3.11) have raised serious red flags regarding your release management and versioning philosophy.

The Violation of Semantic Versioning (SemVer)
The third digit in a version (the patch) is reserved exclusively for bug fixes and non-breaking internal optimizations. It is a fundamental principle of software engineering that a patch update should never break existing, documented functionality.

In versions 1.3.10 and 1.3.11, the abrupt change in how decorators are handled—shifting towards the Stage-3 standard in a way that breaks experimentalDecorators—is not a "bug fix." It is a Major behavioral change. Introducing such shifts in a patch release is a violation of the trust between a runtime and its developers. Features and breaking changes belong in Minor or Major releases, period.


Lack of an LTS (Long-Term Support) Version
For Bun to be taken seriously as an enterprise-grade runtime, it must provide a Long-Term Support (LTS) channel. In a production environment, we cannot afford to have our builds break overnight because of "stealth features" added to a patch update. We need a version that guarantees stability, where only security patches and critical fixes are applied, without any risk of architectural regressions.


Engineering Maturity vs. "Personal Project" Mentality
With the growth of Oven and your recent associations with industry leaders like Anthropic, it is time for Bun to move past the "fast-moving experimental project" phase. You are no longer a group of teenagers working on a hobbyist tool; you are building the backbone of modern web infrastructure.


Major shifts, like the decorator implementation, should:
Be hidden behind a feature flag for a significant period.
Follow a clear deprecation cycle.
Be released in a version that reflects the magnitude of the change.
Conclusion
I have staked my professional reputation and the stability of the organizations I advise on Bun’s success. I want to continue being an ad

title: bun prune --docker — pruned workspace subset for Docker builds
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
bun install --frozen-lockfile needs every workspace package.json present even if you're building one service. So every Dockerfile in a monorepo has to list out all your workspace manifests, and any lockfile change rebuilds everything.
There's a discussion about this (#12763) but no clean solution yet. The common workaround is manually listing every workspace package.json in COPY lines, which breaks whenever you add a workspace. BuildKit COPY --parents globs help but you're still shipping the full lockfile. --filter on install scopes the deps but doesn't prune the lockfile either.
None of these give you a minimal workspace subset with a pruned lockfile, which is what you actually need for Docker layer caching to work properly.
Turborepo has turbo prune --docker which does exactly this. Bun should too, especially since "prune" has been reserved in src/cli.zig since v1.0 (4b63ced72, Sept 2023).
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
bun prune <workspace> [--docker] [--out-dir=out]
Given a target workspace, output a pruned monorepo with only:

Target workspace + transitive workspace deps
Pruned bun.lock with only relevant resolutions
Root package.json with pruned workspaces array
Config files (bunfig.toml, .npmrc)

With --docker, split for layer caching:

out/json/ — package.json files + pruned lockfile (install layer)
out/full/ — full source (build layer)

Dockerfile becomes:
COPY out/json/ .
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile

COPY out/full/ .
RUN bun run build
--filter already builds the workspace dep graph internally, so prune could likely reuse that. And since bun.lock is JSON, lockfile pruning is pretty tractable. Turborepo already has a bun lockfile subgraph implementation in their Rust code as reference. Happy to contribute a TS prototype or help with Zig implementation.
What alternatives have you considered?
This is what I'm running in prod right now:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM oven/bun:1-alpine AS build
WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json bun.lock ./
COPY --parents services/*/package.json packages/*/package.json ./
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --filter '@myapp/api'

COPY packages/ packages/
COPY services/api/ services/api/
RUN bun run --filter '@myapp/api' build

FROM oven/bun:1-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/services/api/dist/server.js server.js
CMD ["bun", "server.js"]
It works but the install step still validates the full lockfile and unrelated dep changes still

title: Bun 1.3.11 hangs on Effect.runSync — event loop regression from 1.3.9
excerpt:
Minimal reproduction
import { Effect } from "effect";
console.log(Effect.runSync(Effect.succeed(42)));
Bun 1.3.9: prints 42 ✅
Bun 1.3.11: hangs forever ❌ (timeout, no output, no error)
Also affects Effect.runPromise and Effect.runFork — the entire Effect fiber scheduler is dead.
Environment

OS: Linux x64
Effect version: 3.19.19 (also tested 3.21.0 — same result)
Bun 1.3.9 (~/.bun/bin/bun): works
Bun 1.3.11 (/usr/bin/bun): hangs

Steps
# Install effect
bun init -y && bun add effect

# This hangs on 1.3.11, works on 1.3.9
bun -e "import { Effect } from 'effect'; console.log(Effect.runSync(Effect.succeed(42)))"
Node.js works fine
node -e "const { Effect } = require('effect'); console.log(Effect.runSync(Effect.succeed(42)))"
# prints: 42
Analysis
Effect's fiber scheduler relies on setTimeout / Promise.then() for cooperative fiber yielding. Something changed in Bun's event loop between 1.3.9 → 1.3.11 that prevents these callbacks from firing. Possibly related to the single-source fast path (#27362) or the event loop changes in 1.3.10.
This is a complete blocker — no Effect-based application can run on Bun 1.3.11.

title: request.signal abort not fired when client disconnects from streaming HTTP response
Concurrent dynamic import() poisons shared module bindings when one import chain fails
excerpt:
When multiple import() calls run concurrently and share a common dependency module, a failure in one import chain (e.g. a missing transitive dependency) can leave the shared module's exports in a Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ). Other concurrent importers then get ReferenceError: Cannot access 'X' before initialization instead of seeing the fully-evaluated module.
Reproduction
https://github.com/schickling-repros/2026-03-bun-concurrent-import-tdz
git clone https://github.com/schickling-repros/2026-03-bun-concurrent-import-tdz
cd 2026-03-bun-concurrent-import-tdz
bun repro.ts
Expected
consumer-ok.ts should always import successfully. The failure in consumer-broken.ts (which depends on a missing module) should be isolated and not affect other concurrent importers of the same shared dependency.
Actual
consumer-ok.ts gets ReferenceError: Cannot access 'sharedConfig' before initialization because Bun leaves shared-dep.ts in a partially-evaluated state after consumer-broken.ts's import chain fails.
Real-world impact
This affects any tool that concurrently loads user modules via import() — test runners, Storybook story loaders, config file processors, etc. With heavy shared dependencies (React, xterm.js), the evaluation window is wide enough that the TDZ race is 100% reproducible.
Notes

The minimal repro may not always trigger the TDZ due to timing — with heavier real-world modules the race is deterministic
Node.js handles this correctly — failed import chains don't poison shared dependencies

Versions

Bun: 1.3.6
OS: macOS 15 arm64

title: Date.now() returns -2147483648 (INT32 overflow) on Bun 1.3.11
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+a04817ce2
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.19.10-1-cachyos x86_64 unknown
What steps can reproduce the bug?
$ bun repl
❯ Date.now()
-2147483648
What is the expected behavior?
This is the output on Node v25.2.1
$ node
> Date.now()
1774977987860
What do you see instead?
$ bun repl
❯ Date.now()
-2147483648
Additional information
This looks like a regression in how bun internally stores or returns f64 → i32 for date millisecond values. Quite impactful since it breaks basically any code that relies on Date.now() or getTime().
Also affected
Date.parse() — returns -2147483648 for valid ISO dates
new Date().getTime() — returns -2147483648
Date.now() in template literals — ${Date.now()} produces "-2147483648"
Works correctly
new Date().toISOString() — returns correct "2026-03-31T17:16:11.403Z"
new Date().toUTCString() — returns correct HTTP date string
Impact
All timestamp millisecond values appear to be truncated to a signed 32-bit integer, causing overflow for some dates. This breaks caching headers, unique ID generation, and any code using numeric timestamps.

title: Blob/ArrayBuffer memory not reclaimed by GC after dereferencing
Bun.build() minifier identifier collision persists after #14585 fix
excerpt:
Description
The identifier collision bug reported in #14585 persists in Bun 1.3.11, despite the fix in #17930. As noted by @paperclover in that PR review, the fix was a workaround — the real bug in the renaming/hoisting/symbol-merging code was never addressed.
We hit this in Sentry CLI where Bun.build() with minify: true causes renderInline (a function in the marked library) to get the same minified name as an unrelated object. The error is:
TypeError: _4 is not a function. (In '_4(_4.tokens)', '_4' is an instance of Object)

The collision is fragile and depends on exact import ordering — removing ~380 lines of unrelated code in a different file was enough to trigger it. Any future code change could re-trigger it.
Reproduction
This is difficult to reproduce in a minimal example because the collision depends on the total number and ordering of identifiers across the entire bundle. In our case:

Clone https://github.com/getsentry/cli
bun install
In script/build.ts, change minify back to true (from the current esbuild workaround)
bun run --env-file=.env.local script/build.ts --single
./dist-bin/sentry-linux-x64 auth status → crashes with TypeError: _4 is not a function

What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.12.10 x86_64
Workaround
We switched Step 1 of our binary build from Bun.build() to esbuild, which has a more mature minifier without this collision bug. Bun.build({ compile: true }) in Step 2 still works fine with esbuild's ESM output. See getsentry/cli#617 for the initial workaround (disabling identifier minification).
Additional context: Bun's sourcemap names array is always empty
While investigating this, we also discovered that Bun's minifier produces sourcemaps with an empty names array — even with minify: true. After switching to esbuild, our sourcemaps went from 0 names to 27,860 names across 1,006 source files. This is a separate issue but worth noting: the empty names array means tools like Sentry cannot resolve original function names from Bun-produced sourcemaps, falling back to position-based mapping only.
Related

#14585 — Original report
#17930 — Workaround fix (acknowledged as not the real fix)

What is the problem this feature would solve?
When you have 30 browser tabs, 10 terminal tabs, and 3 IDE windows open.. and you're looking for that perfect package to fill a gap in your current project.. then you find it, quickly flip back to your terminal window, run bun add best-package-ever, and suddenly realise that you've just installed it to your home directory.
This results in not only a node_modules folder, but also a new package.json and bun.lock file, even though the current working directory was not actually a Bun project.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
When running either bun add or bun install, if the current working directory does not already have a package.json file, it would be awesome if the Bun CLI would prompt for confirmation before it continues.
For the sake of convenience, it could default to "yes", so simply hitting "enter" again at this prompt would continue as normal. But for situations where the command was actually run in the incorrect working directory, it gives an opportunity to stop the process before any changes are made.
This should be completely transparent when the current working directory is a valid project, as the point here is purely to try prevent accidentally initialising new projects in unexpected locations.

title: List of breaking changes for 1.4
excerpt:
This issue tracks breaking changes for Bun 1.4.
Merged
Headline

 Node.js compatibility target bumped from 24.3.0 to 26.3.0 (#31991). process.versions.node is 26.3.0, NODE_MODULE_VERSION is 147. Native addons built for Node 24 must be rebuilt.
 x64 builds are baseline-only (#34782). The separate -march=haswell x64 build is dropped; SIMD is runtime-dispatched. The old non-baseline download URLs alias to the baseline artifact. This resolves #12180.

bun install / CLI

 bun.lock default lockfileVersion is now 2 (#31539). v2 lockfiles require integrity hashes for off-registry npm tarballs and reject unsafe git .bun-tag values at parse time. Existing v0/v1 lockfiles continue to load. Older Bun versions cannot read v2 lockfiles.
 bun init templates pin "typescript": "^6" (#33265)

Bun.TOML

 Parser rewritten for TOML v1.1.0 conformance (#32953). Bun.TOML.parse now throws SyntaxError (was BuildMessage), rejects duplicate keys, rejects integers outside Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, rejects control characters and malformed UTF-8, and parses date/time literals as strings. Also adds Bun.TOML.stringify.

Node.js compatibility

 node:http: response.writeHeader() removed (Node DEP0063 end-of-life) (#31991)
 node:stream: read() in paused mode returns one chunk instead of concatenating the buffer (Node 26 semver-major) (#31991)
 node:tls: a server with requestCert: true and no explicit rejectUnauthorized now enforces client certificate verification (#31322)
 node:dgram: bind() on an already-bound socket and calls after close() throw synchronously (#33037, #33024)

fetch / HTTP client

 Duplicate response and request headers are combined with ", " per the Fetch spec instead of last-wins (#31734). A lone empty-value header now reads as "" instead of null.
 fetch() rejects the returned promise instead of throwing synchronously when option conversion throws (#33649)
 Request#clone() / Response#clone() throw when the body is disturbed or locked instead of silently returning an empty-body clone (#33129)
 Response.redirect(url) parses and serializes the URL into Location; non-ASCII and newlines are no longer passed through verbatim (#33126)
 Truncated compressed bodies on close-delimited responses now reject instead of resolving with partial data (#34922)

Bun.serve

 Out-of-range port throws RangeError instead of silently clamping (#34957)
 A status outside 100..=999 is routed through error() as a 500 instead of writing an invalid status line (#33400)
 Per-method route objects serve

title: bug(SQL): bun-sql double encodes all values inserted into `json` and `jsonb` columns with Postgres 18, their resulting type is always `string`
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+af24e281e
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.8.0-107-generic x86_64 x86_64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
The entire bug is reproduced in this test repo: https://github.com/vjancik/bun-sql-json-column-bug
Run bun script-raw.ts or bun script-raw-jsonb.ts to reproduce the following output.
Repeating the README here:

Create a table with a json (or jsonb) column
Insert a JS object, array, or number via a bun:sql template literal with a ::json cast, passing the value through JSON.stringify
Query the raw stored value and its json_typeof

await sql`INSERT INTO test_json (value) VALUES (${JSON.stringify({ hello: "world" })}::json)`;
Then inspect:
SELECT id, value, json_typeof(value) FROM test_json ORDER BY id;
Bug Explanation
When passing JSON.stringify(value) into a bun:sql template literal, Bun binds it as a text parameter. Postgres receives a quoted string literal — e.g. '{"hello":"world"}' — and with the ::json cast, stores it as a JSON string value rather than a JSON object. The value ends up encoded twice: once by JSON.stringify, once by Bun's text binding.
The double-encoding can be confirmed by stripping one layer with value#>>'{}' and re-parsing:
SELECT id, json_typeof((value#>>'{}')::json) AS unwrapped_type FROM test_json ORDER BY id;
This yields the correct types (object, array, number), proving the values are wrapped in an extra string layer.
What is the expected behavior?
stored rows:
  id=1  type=object  raw value: { hello: 'world' }
  id=2  type=array   raw value: [ 1, 2, 3 ]
  id=3  type=number  raw value: 42

The json_typeof of each stored value should match the JS type of the value that was inserted.
What do you see instead?
stored rows:
  id=1  type=string  raw value: '{"hello":"world"}'
  id=2  type=string  raw value: '[1,2,3]'
  id=3  type=string  raw value: '42'

unwrapped (stripping one layer of encoding):
  id=1  unwrapped_type=object
  id=2  unwrapped_type=array
  id=3  unwrapped_type=number

All three rows are stored as JSON strings. The unwrap query confirms a second layer of encoding is present.
Additional information

The bug affects both json and jsonb column types.
Passing a raw JS number (e.g. ${42}) directly without JSON.stringify fails with integer cannot be cast to json, because Bun preserves the native integer type and Postgres has no direct integer → json cast. This confirms Bun does not automatically serialize JS values to JSON — the caller must stringify explicitly, but doing so

title: Support resolve.conditions in bunfig.toml for custom export conditions
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
There's no way to configure custom package.json export conditions in bunfig.toml. The --conditions CLI flag exists for bun run / bun build, but having to pass it to every command is tedious in monorepos that rely on a custom condition like "source" to resolve workspace packages to their TypeScript source.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A [resolve] section in bunfig.toml that supports a conditions array:
[resolve]
conditions = ["source"]
This would apply the custom condition globally — to bun run, bun test, bun build, and the dev server — matching how customConditions works in tsconfig.json.
Why is this useful?
In TypeScript monorepos, packages often expose a "source" export condition so sibling workspace packages resolve directly to .ts source instead of built .js/.d.ts:
{
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "source": "./src/index.ts",
      "types": "./dist/index.d.mts",
      "import": "./dist/index.mjs"
    }
  }
}
TypeScript supports this via "customConditions": ["source"] in tsconfig. But for Bun, the only option is --conditions source on every CLI invocation, which means:

Every bun run, bun test, bun build command needs the flag
Scripts in package.json need it baked in
It can't be shared across a monorepo via a single config file
AI coding agents consistently fail to apply this correctly. They read bunfig.toml and tsconfig.json for project context, but since there's no declarative config for Bun's resolve conditions, they forget to pass --conditions to commands, or pass it inconsistently. A bunfig.toml setting would make the project self-describing — both for humans and for agents.

What alternatives have you considered?
Currently, adding it manually to every CLI invocation.

title: Bug: Windows global binaries (.exe/.bunx) resolve incorrect node_modules path when Bun is installed via Scoop
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
Latest (e.g. 1.2.x) - Installed via Scoop
What platform is your computer?
Windows 11 (x64)
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Install Bun using Scoop on Windows: scoop install bun
Install any package globally using bun: bun install -g agent-browser (or @larksuite/cli)
Try to run the installed global command: agent-browser

What is the expected behavior?
The global CLI command should run successfully by correctly resolving its JavaScript entry point in the global
ode_modules directory.
What do you see instead?
A MODULE_NOT_FOUND error, because it tries to look up the path in a non-existent scoop\node_modules directory:
node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1424
  throw err;
  ^

Error: Cannot find module 'C:\Users\<User>\scoop\node_modules\agent-browser\bin\agent-browser.js'
    at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1421:15)
...
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND',
  requireStack: []
}

Root Cause Analysis

When installed via Scoop, the bun.exe binary resides in ~\scoop\apps\bun\current\bin.
Running bun install -g <pkg> downloads the package into the user's global modules (e.g., ~\node_modules\<pkg>).
However, the generated executable wrapper (.exe and .bunx) inside the bin directory uses a hardcoded relative path: ..\..\..\node_modules.
Resolving ..\..\..\node_modules from ~\scoop\apps\bun\current\bin points to ~\scoop\node_modules, which is incorrect and does not exist.

Temporary Workaround
Creating a directory symlink from the incorrectly resolved path to the actual path bypasses the issue:
mklink /D C:\Users\<User>\scoop\node_modules C:\Users\<User>\node_modules
The global bin wrappers generated by Bun on Windows should reliably resolve the absolute path to the global
node_modules directory, or read from a configuration, instead of relying on a strict relative directory traversal that breaks under Windows package managers like Scoop.

Feature Request: Centralized AGENTS.md with Symlink Support for AI Agent Rules
Summary
Create a centralized AGENTS.md file by default during bun init, with intelligent handling of existing files and optional symlink creation for CLAUDE.md when Claude CLI is detected.
Problem Statement
Currently, bun init creates separate agent rule files (CLAUDE.md for Claude, .cursor/rules/*.mdc for Cursor) based on detected AI tools . This approach:

Scatters AI agent configuration across multiple files
Does not provide a unified location for all AI agent instructions
May create duplicate content across different agent files

Proposed Solution
1. Create AGENTS.md by Default

Always generate AGENTS.md during bun init (unless disabled via environment variable)
Use the same content as the current agent_rule from src/init/rule.md

2. Handle Existing AGENTS.md

If AGENTS.md exists, prompt user for approval to append
Show diff of what would be added
Respect user choice to skip, overwrite, or append

3. Intelligent CLAUDE.md Handling
When Claude CLI is detected :

Default: Create CLAUDE.md as a symlink pointing to AGENTS.md
User choice: Allow selection between symlink or actual file copy
Fallback: If symlink creation fails, create actual file (current behavior)

4. Maintain Backward Compatibility

Continue supporting existing environment variables:

BUN_AGENT_RULE_DISABLED=1
CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT_RULE_DISABLED=1


Keep existing Cursor rule functionality

Implementation Details
User Experience Flow

First run: Creates AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (symlink)
Subsequent runs: Detects existing files, prompts for action

BUN_CLAUDE_SYMLINK_DISABLED=1 - Force actual file instead of symlink

excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+af24e281e
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use Bun 1.3.11.
Build a Tailwind CSS entry file through Bun's build pipeline.
Include a top-level Tailwind layer declaration such as:

@layer theme, base, components, utilities;

Observe the generated CSS output.

In our case, this happens in a production-like build flow using bun build with the Tailwind plugin. The same file used to work before the upgrade.
What is the expected behavior?
The @layer theme, base, components, utilities; directive should be preserved in the output CSS exactly as intended by Tailwind's layer ordering.
Bun should not silently remove or rewrite this directive in a way that breaks the stylesheet.
What do you see instead?
After upgrading to Bun 1.3.11, Bun strips the @layer theme, base, components, utilities; line from the generated CSS output.
That causes Tailwind's layer ordering to break and leads to a cascade of CSS regressions across the application. In our case, the UI started exhibiting multiple unexpected style bugs immediately after the upgrade.
As a workaround, we currently have to manually prepend the missing @layer line after the build step, which is not acceptable for a production build pipeline.
Additional information
This appears to be a regression introduced in what should have been a bugfix-level release. A change like this can create far more damage than it resolves, especially in production systems that depend on stable build output.
We have operational projects relying on Bun, and a release that introduces this kind of breaking behavior makes it difficult to trust patch-level upgrades. Please reconsider the release and versioning process so that changes with this level of impact are not shipped as bugfix updates without stronger validation.
If this behavior is intentional, it would still be a breaking change for Tailwind users and should be documented prominently. Otherwise, please treat it as a regression and restore the previous behavior.

title: Bug build plugin `bun-plugin-tailwind` forcefully inlines lightweight fonts to Base64, ignoring Bun's loader and other configs
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+af24e281e
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Set up a project using Bun.build alongside the official Tailwind plugin (bun-plugin-tailwind).
Include a lightweight font (e.g., Vazirmatn.woff2 which is highly optimized and small in size) in your CSS using a relative path:
src: url('./fonts/Vazirmatn.woff2') format('woff2');
Configure Bun.build to explicitly prevent inlining by using Bun's standard APIs:
Bun.build({
  // ... other configs
  loader: {
    '.woff2': 'file',
  },
  plugins: [tailwindPlugin] 
})

Run the build script.

What is the expected behavior?
The Tailwind plugin should respect Bun's top-level build configurations. Since assetsInlineLimit is set to 0 and the .woff2 extension is explicitly assigned to the file loader, the font should be emitted as a separate physical asset in the output directory, and the CSS should reference its hashed URL.
What do you see instead?
The Tailwind plugin (likely via its internal Lightning CSS / Oxide processing phase) intercepts the asset resolution before Bun's final bundling phase. It detects that the font size is below a certain internal threshold and forcefully converts it into a Base64 string directly inside the generated CSS.
This completely ignores the assetsInlineLimit: 0 and loader: { '.woff2': 'file' } instructions, resulting in a bloated CSS file and preventing the browser from downloading the CSS and Fonts in parallel. Interestingly, heavier fonts (like Material Symbols) remain as files because they exceed the plugin's hidden internal size threshold, creating an inconsistent build output.
Additional information

No Configuration Escape Hatch: In the current version, the plugin is exported as an object, not a function. Calling tailwindPlugin() to pass custom configurations throws a TypeScript error: Type 'BunPlugin' has no call signatures. Therefore, there is no way to pass an option directly to the plugin to disable this behavior.
Workarounds: Currently, the only ways to bypass this bug are changing the CSS paths to absolute paths (e.g., /fonts/...) or appending a query string (e.g., ?url). However, the core issue remains: an official ecosystem plugin should not silently override or ignore Bun's native build configurations.

Problem

After manually downloading the aarch64 Linux build and patching its ELF interpreter from /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 to Android's /system/bin/linker64 (using patchelf), the binary still fails:
error: /path/to/bun: Android only supports position-independent executables (-fPIE)

Android's kernel enforces that all executables must be built as PIE. The official Linux aarch64 bun binary is not PIE, so it cannot run on any Android-based system regardless of the ELF interpreter.
For reference, Node.js works fine on Termux using the same /system/bin/linker64 path — it is built as PIE.
Steps to reproduce
On a Termux aarch64 session:
# Method 1 — npm
npm install -g bun
# → npm error notsup Unsupported platform … "os":"android"

# Method 2 — install script
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
# Downloads successfully, then:
~/.bun/bin/bun --version
# → no such file or directory (ELF interpreter /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 missing)

# After patching interpreter with patchelf:
patchelf --set-interpreter /system/bin/linker64 ~/.bun/bin/bun
~/.bun/bin/bun --version
# → error: ~/.bun/bin/bun: Android only supports position-independent executables (-fPIE)
Expected behavior
Either:

bun runs on Termux/Android out of the box, or
the install script / npm package detects the unsupported platform and prints a clear error message explaining why bun cannot run on Android

Possible fixes

Build a PIE-enabled aarch64 Linux binary — Android is Linux under the hood; a PIE aarch64 binary with the right interpreter (or statically linked) would run on Termux without patching.
Add android to the supported OS list in the npm package if/when a compatible binary is available.
Improve the install script to detect uname -o = Android and print a helpful "

title: bun x @scope/package can run a system command instead of the package default bin when bin name differs
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.10+30e609e08
What platform is your computer?
macOS 26.3 (Darwin 25.3.0) arm64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Inspect the package bin mapping:

npm view @paretools/git bin --json
# { "pare-git": "dist/index.js" }

Run the package with npm exec / npx:

npx @paretools/git

Run the same package with bun x:

bun x @paretools/git

Repeat with similar packages whose package name differs from the published bin name:

npm view @paretools/bun bin --json
# { "pare-bun": "dist/index.js" }
bun x @paretools/bun

npm view @paretools/build bin --json
# { "pare-build": "dist/index.js" }
bun x @paretools/build
What is the expected behavior?
bun x @paretools/git should behave like npx @paretools/git and execute the package's default published bin (pare-git).
Likewise:

bun x @paretools/bun should execute pare-bun
bun x @paretools/build should execute pare-build

If Bun cannot determine the correct bin, it should fail clearly instead of invoking an unrelated system command.
What do you see instead?

bun x @paretools/git invokes the system git command and prints Git's help output.
bun x @paretools/bun surfaces the regular Bun CLI help output.
bun x @paretools/build does not run the MCP server binary either.

In other words, Bun appears to resolve to a command name collision (git, bun, build) instead of the package's published default bin.
This is especially risky because it silently runs the wrong executable instead of failing.
Additional information

Explicitly naming the bin works:

bun x --package @paretools/git pare-git
bun x --package @paretools/bun pare-bun
bun x --package @paretools/build pare-build

This seems related to package/bin-name mismatch handling, but the problematic part here is that bun x <package> falls through to an unrelated system command instead of the package's default bin.
There is a related issue about bunx --package: #25026, but this report is specifically about bun x <scoped-package> not matching npx <scoped-package> when the published bin name differs from the package basename and collides with an existing command.

title: Feaure Request: Support version-specific entries in minimumReleaseAgeExcludes for safer package whitelisting
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, Bun's bunfig.toml allows configuration of minimumReleaseAgeExcludes to bypass the "minimum release age" protection for entire packages, e.g. ["@types/node", "typescript"]. This can lead to risk if a package is whitelisted to bypass the age gate, as all future versions of the package will also be allowed through without the delay, which defeats the point if, for example, the whitelist is not promptly removed after a critical patch.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add support for specifying explicit package versions in minimumReleaseAgeExcludes, so that a user can whitelist just specific versions instead of all future versions of the package.
For example:
minimumReleaseAgeExcludes = ["@types/node@0.12.0", "typescript@100.0.2"]

This allows:

Only the listed versions to bypass the release age check.
Fine-grained control for responding to CVEs or emergency fixes without opening the door to any future versions of trusted, but evolving, packages.

See current documentation: https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/install#minimum-release-age.
What alternatives have you considered?

Maintaining the current behavior of only allowing full-package whitelisting, and requiring strict diligence to ensure old exclusions are always removed promptly, which can be error-prone and risk supply chain attacks if forgotten.
Manual package downgrades or locks, which don’t address the usability, ergonomics, and security simultaneously.

title: Number(string) returns -2147483648 for any string value exceeding INT32_MAX
excerpt:

What platform is your computer?
