What steps can reproduce the bug?
Number(string) returns -2147483648 (INT32_MIN) for any string whose numeric value exceeds INT32_MAX (2,147,483,647). The boundary is exact at 2147483647 / 2147483648. All affected inputs collapse to exactly -2147483648, which strongly suggests a builtin/JIT specialization is lowering Number(string) to an int32 conversion path that wraps on overflow instead of returning a JavaScript double.
Minimal reproduction:
bun -e 'console.log(Number("2147483648"))'
Boundary check:
bun -e '
for (const s of ["2147483647","2147483648","9999999999","1775583264541"]) {
  console.log(s.padStart(13), "→", Number(s));
}
'

Scope check (only Number(string) is affected, every other coercion path is fine):
bun -e '                                                                                       
const s = "1775583264541";                                                                
console.log("Number(s):           ", Number(s));
console.log("Number.call(null, s):", Number.call(null, s));                                    
console.log("+s:                  ", +s);
console.log("s * 1:               ", s * 1);                                                   
console.log("parseInt(s, 10):     ", parseInt(s, 10));                                    
console.log("parseFloat(s):       ", parseFloat(s));

Number("2147483648") should return the JavaScript double 2147483648, matching every other
JavaScript runtime (Node, Deno, browsers) and matching every other coercion path in Bun itself
(+s, parseInt(s, 10), parseFloat(s), s * 1, Number(BigInt(s))). Per ECMA-262, Number(string)
should run the StringToNumber abstract operation and return an IEEE-754 double, which has no
problem representing integers up to 2^53.

title: Bug: fetch() fails with proxy.url validation error when using @npmcli/agent
excerpt:
Bug Report: Bun fetch() fails with proxy.url validation error
What version of Bun is running?
The Bun runtime is embedded in opencode-ai v1.4.3 (opencode-windows-x64 binary). Unable to get exact Bun revision, but this is a bundled Bun for the opencode application.
What platform is your computer?
Windows 11 x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Set HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY environment variables to a proxy URL (e.g., http://127.0.0.1:10808)
Run opencode-ai (which uses bundled Bun runtime for npm operations)
Attempt to install any npm plugin from registry (e.g., oh-my-openagent)
The fetch() call fails with error: fetch() proxy.url must be a non-empty string

What is the expected behavior?
The fetch() call should use the proxy correctly and succeed, or at minimum provide a clearer error message about the proxy configuration issue.
What do you see instead?
ERROR service=plugin pkg=oh-my-openagent error=request to https://registry.npmjs.org/oh-my-openagent failed, reason: fetch() proxy.url must be a non-empty string failed to install plugin

Root Cause Analysis
The issue is in how Bun's native fetch implementation handles the proxy option from @npmcli/agent:

@npmcli/agent creates a proxy getter that returns { url: URL_object } where URL_object is a JavaScript URL object
Bun's native fetch implementation expects proxy.url to be a string, not a URL object
When Bun receives the URL object, it fails validation with "proxy.url must be a non-empty string"

This is a type mismatch between the npm ecosystem's expectations and Bun's native fetch implementation.
Additional Information

This affects all npm packages that use @npmcli/agent for proxy handling (which is essentially all npm registry operations)
The issue does NOT occur when using Node.js fetch() or with HTTP_PROXY disabled
The workaround is to disable the proxy, but this is not ideal for users behind corporate proxies

title: `node:dgram` emits `ECONNREFUSED` `recv` and exits in Bun `1.3.12`, but not `1.3.11`
excerpt:
Summary
A minimal node:dgram UDP script exits with:
error: ECONNREFUSED: connection refused, recv

on Bun 1.3.12, but the same script exits cleanly on Bun 1.3.11.
This looks like a Bun 1.3.12 regression in UDP socket error handling. The script prints done, but Bun 1.3.12 still exits with code 1 because of the recv-side ECONNREFUSED.
Minimal Repro
Create repro.ts:
import { createSocket } from "node:dgram";

const socket = createSocket("udp4");

await new Promise(resolve => socket.bind(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
socket.send(Buffer.from("x"), 9, "127.0.0.1");
await Bun.sleep(250);
await new Promise(resolve => socket.close(resolve));

console.log("done");
Commands
bun repro.ts
bunx bun@1.3.11 repro.ts
Actual Results
Bun 1.3.12
$ bun repro.ts
46 |     }
47 |   }
48 |   let er;
49 |   if (args.length > 0)
50 |     er = args[0];
51 |     throw er;
                 ^
error: ECONNREFUSED: connection refused, recv
      at emitError (node:events:51:13)
      at error (node:dgram:176:22)
done

Bun v1.3.12 (Linux x64)

Exit code: 1
Bun 1.3.11
$ bunx bun@1.3.11 repro.ts
done

Exit code: 0
Expected Results
Bun 1.3.12 should not regress relative to Bun 1.3.11 for this script.
At minimum, this script should exit cleanly instead of terminating the process with:
ECONNREFUSED: connection refused, recv

after already reaching the end of the program and printing done.
Environment

Bun 1.3.12
Comparison version: Bun 1.3.11
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
Kernel: 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
Arch: x86_64

Real-World Impact
This breaks WebRTC / ICE stacks that rely on UDP sockets, including werift, because a process can terminate after peer discovery and ICE traffic begins unless the app installs a defensive UDP error handler.
In my case, a Bun CLI app using werift had to add a workaround that installs a socket error listener and ignores only:

error.code === "ECONNREFUSED"
error.syscall === "recv"

to avoid process crashes on Bun 1.3.12.
Workaround
Attach a UDP socket error listener and ignore only the affected error shape:
socket.on("error", error => {
  if (error?.code === "ECONNREFUSED" && error?.syscall === "recv") return;
  throw error;
});
That avoids the crash locally on Bun 1.3.12.

title: bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64 produces truncated code signature in v1.3.12
excerpt:
What version of Bun is used?
1.3.12
What platform is your computer?
macOS arm64 (also reproducible on Linux x86_64 cross-compiling to darwin-arm64)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
# Using Bun 1.3.12
echo 'console.log("hello")' > app.ts
bun build app.ts --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64 --outfile myapp
codesign -dv myapp  # → "code object is not signed at all"
./myapp              # → Killed: 9 (exit 137)
Same steps with Bun 1.3.11 work correctly — binary is ad-hoc signed and runs fine.
What is the expected behavior?
Binary should have a valid ad-hoc code signature and run on macOS arm64, as it does with Bun 1.3.11.
What do you see instead?
macOS kills the binary immediately with SIGKILL (exit 137). codesign -dv reports "code object is not signed at all".
Root cause analysis
The macho.zig signing code itself did not change between 1.3.11 and 1.3.12. However, the Bun runtime binary grew by ~337KB (due to Zig compiler version changes and StandaloneModuleGraph restructuring), and there is a latent bug in the sig_size calculation in src/macho.zig that is triggered by the larger binary size.
The result is a truncated code signature — the LC_CODE_SIGNATURE space allocated in LINKEDIT is far too small for the actual SuperBlob:
Reproducible locally with --target=bun-darwin-arm64:




Bun 1.3.11
Bun 1.3.12




Binary size
68,483,104
68,819,776 (+337KB)


LC_CODE_SIGNATURE datasize
550,192 ✅
196,592 ❌


codesign -dv
Signature=adhoc
code object is not signed at all



The SuperBlob header inside the 1.3.12 binary declares length=537,138 but only 196,592 bytes are allocated — the signature is truncated by ~340KB.
The conditional added in PR #26175 (commit 6f6f76f0c0) may be involved — it gates sig_size += size_of_new_hashes on CPU_TYPE_ARM64 && !BUN_NO_CODESIGN_MACHO_BINARY, but the actual hash generation still produces a full-size CodeDirectory. With the larger binary in 1.3.12, the mismatch between allocated space and generated data becomes fatal.
Workaround
BUN_NO_CODESIGN_MACHO_BINARY=1 bun build app.ts --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64 --outfile myapp
codesign --sign - myapp  # on macOS
# or: rcodesign sign myapp  # on Linux (cross-platform)
Or pin to Bun 1.3.11.

What do you see instead?

import.meta.resolve correctly returns the expected $bunfs path, but Bun.file() cannot read it and new Worker() cannot load it. This only fails with nested paths - flat paths (./my-worker.ts at project root) work as shown in the docs.
The docs at https://bun.com/docs/bundler/executables#worker only demonstrate flat file structures (./my-worker.ts). Nested paths appear to be
broken. A workaround of pre-bundling the worker to a JS file and embedding it as a with { type: "file" } asset works, but defeats the purpose of the worker entrypoint feature.

title: process.stdin keeps reading fd 0 after last 'readable' listener is removed
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11
What platform is your computer?
Darwin arm64
What steps can reproduce the bug?
After process.stdin.on('readable', fn) then process.stdin.removeListener('readable', fn), Bun continues to pull bytes from fd 0. pause() and unref() do not stop it. A child spawned with stdio: 'inherit' then races the parent for input on the same fd — the parent silently buffers keystrokes meant for the child.
This breaks the common TUI pattern of unmounting (Ink, etc.) before handing the terminal to an interactive child like vim, less, or tmux.
// repro.ts — run in a real terminal
import { spawn } from 'child_process'

process.stdin.setRawMode(true)
const handler = () => { while (process.stdin.read() !== null) {} }
process.stdin.on('readable', handler)

await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 50))

process.stdin.setRawMode(false)
process.stdin.removeListener('readable', handler)
process.stdin.unref()

// Hand terminal to an interactive child
const child = spawn('cat', [], { stdio: 'inherit' })
await new Promise(r => child.once('close', r))
Type into cat — under Bun, characters go missing (parent steals them). Under Node, cat receives everything.
What is the expected behavior?
After the last 'readable' listener is removed and nothing else is consuming, fd 0 should be released so a stdio: 'inherit' child reads it exclusively. Node releases it via backpressure (tty.ReadStream has highWaterMark: 0, so push() returns false on every chunk and onStreamRead calls handle.readStop()).
What do you see instead?
Parent keeps polling fd 0. Child receives partial/no input. With tmux as the child, the first thing stolen is tmux's terminal-capability query responses, then keystrokes — tmux exits with [server exited unexpectedly].
Additional information
Root cause: Bun's tty.ReadStream extends fs.ReadStream (not net.Socket like Node), with the default highWaterMark, and getStdinStream's internalRead loop has no backpressure-driven stop. Node's tty.ReadStream extends net.Socket with readableHighWaterMark: 0, so the handle's readStop() fires after every chunk and _read() only re-acquires when a consumer pulls.

title: os.availableParallelism() ignores cpuset / sched_getaffinity on Linux (returns host CPU count, diverges from Node)
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+af24e281e
What platform is your computer?
Linux x64 (any Linux host where the process is restricted to a CPU subset via cpuset or sched_setaffinity)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Run Bun inside a cgroup cpuset (e.g. docker run --cpuset-cpus=...) or under taskset, on a host with more logical CPUs than the restriction allows.
On a 32-core host with the process pinned to 8 cores:
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset.cpus.effective
8-15
$ nproc
8

$ bun -e 'console.log(require("os").availableParallelism())'
32
$ node -e 'console.log(require("os").availableParallelism())'
8
Further restricting with taskset:
$ taskset -c 8-9 bun  -e 'console.log(require("os").availableParallelism())'
32
$ taskset -c 8-9 node -e 'console.log(require("os").availableParallelism())'
2
$ taskset -c 8-9 nproc
2
What is the expected behavior?
os.availableParallelism() should return the number of CPUs the process can actually be scheduled on — i.e. respect the CPU affinity mask (sched_getaffinity(0, ...)) and, ideally, the cgroup CPU quota — matching Node.js and nproc.
Node’s docs for os.availableParallelism() explicitly say it accounts for CPU affinity and cgroups. Node delegates to libuv’s uv_available_parallelism(), which on Linux popcounts the sched_getaffinity mask and clamps to the cgroup v1/v2 CPU quota.
What do you see instead?
Bun returns the host’s total online CPU count (sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)), ignoring affinity and cgroup limits.
Additional information
Why it happens
src/js/node/os.ts:
availableParallelism: function () {
  return navigator.hardwareConcurrency;
},
navigator.hardwareConcurrency is populated in src/bun.js/bindings/ZigGlobalObject.cpp from WTF::numberOfProcessorCores(), which on Linux is just sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN) (vendor/WebKit/Source/WTF/wtf/NumberOfCores.cpp) — no sched_getaffinity, no cgroup check.
Note the docstring at src/bun.js/bindings/WTF.zig:6 claims numberOfProcessorCores is “min(sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN), sched_getaffinity count, cgroup cpu.max quota)” — that comment is wrong; the WTF implementation doesn’t do that.
Impact
Anything sizing a worker pool off availableParallelism() over-subscribes inside containers. Bun’s own build hits this — scripts/build/zig.ts passes -Dllvm_codegen_threads=${availableParallelism()}, so bun bd inside an 8-core cpuset on a 32-core host spawns 32 LLVM codegen threads. The cpuset still caps actual CPU time, but with several concurrent builds sliced into 8-core cpuset

title: build: parallel-compiler sharded codegen installs incomplete bun-zig.o on fresh Linux builds
excerpt:
Symptom
A fresh bun run build on Linux (no cache) links with every Zig-exported symbol undefined:
[664/666] link bun-debug
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: Bun__reportUnhandledError
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: Bun__panic
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: Bun__getVM
ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: ShellInterpreter__estimatedSize
... (every Zig export)

The Zig step itself reports success:
Build Summary: 5/5 steps succeeded
obj success
+- compile obj bun-debug Debug x86_64-linux-gnu.2.26 success 7m MaxRSS:11G
+- install generated to bun-zig.o success

Repro
The oven-sh/bun-development-docker-image Daily Docker Build has hit this on every run since March 30 (first failure: run 23747435420, most recent: run 24260266660). It does a fresh clone + bun run build on debian:trixie-slim, both amd64 and arm64.
macOS local dev does not reproduce.
Suspected cause
For non-CI, non-Windows builds, scripts/build/zig.ts:403 passes -Dllvm_codegen_threads=${availableParallelism()} and selects the parallel-sema compiler (ZIG_COMMIT_PARALLEL). Combined with obj.no_link_obj = true on Linux/macOS (build.zig:758), Zig emits N sharded .o files without merging them.
addInstallObjectFile (build.zig:815) then installs only compile.getEmittedBin() as bun-zig.o, and emitZig (zig.ts:336/356) returns just that one path to the link step. The comment at zig.ts:299–300 still says threaded codegen is "always 0 in practice — deferred", which is no longer true.
I haven't confirmed the exact shard layout the parallel compiler emits on Linux, so treat the mechanism as a strong lead rather than proven.
Workaround
bun run build --ci (forces stable compiler, llvm_codegen_threads=0) — applied to the docker image in oven-sh/bun-development-docker-image#10.
Possible fixes

Have emitZig declare and return all shard outputs so they all reach the link line, or
Have build.zig merge shards (ld -r) before install when llvm_codegen_threads > 0, or
Gate no_link_obj on llvm_codegen_threads == 0.

title: RedisClient: assigning `null` to `onclose` panics during `close()`
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.12+700fc117 (Linux x64, WSL kernel 6.6.87, glibc 2.39)
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (WSL2 on Windows, x86_64)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
The published type definitions for Bun.RedisClient declare:
// packages/bun-types/redis.d.ts
onconnect: ((this: RedisClient) => void) | null;
onclose: ((this: RedisClient, error: Error) => void) | null;
So null is documented as a valid value. At runtime, however, assigning null to onclose panics during the subsequent close().
Minimal reproduction (requires a Redis/Valkey/Dragonfly server on localhost:6379):
// repro.ts
const c = new Bun.RedisClient("redis://localhost:6379")
await c.set("test:onclose-null-panic", "v", "EX", "10")
c.onclose = null  // <-- panics on the close() below
c.close()
console.log("closed ok")
Run: bun repro.ts
What is the expected behavior?
Clean exit, prints closed ok. The type def advertises null as an assignable value, so detaching a handler via null should be a supported way to suppress post-assignment callback invocations.
What do you see instead?
============================================================
Bun v1.3.12 (700fc117) Linux x64
WSL Kernel v6.6.87 | glibc v2.39
CPU: sse42 popcnt avx avx2
Args: "bun" "repro.ts"
Features: dotenv(2) jsc tsconfig(2) valkey
Builtins: "bun:main"
Elapsed: 21ms | User: 7ms | Sys: 15ms
RSS: 1.11GB | Peak: 35.39MB | Commit: 1.11GB | Faults: 0 | Machine: 8.26GB

panic(main thread): A JavaScript exception was thrown, but it was cleared before it could be read.
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.

Bun exits with status 132 (SIGILL). The panic reproduces 100% of the time on the minimal repro above.
Workaround
Assign an empty function instead of null:
c.onclose = () => {}  // works fine — graceful close, no panic
c.close()
This is load-bearing if you're trying to suppress "connection closed" callback logic during an intentional shutdown (e.g. to avoid logging graceful close as a connection failure).
Additional information

onconnect = null was not tested — it may or may not have the same issue. The reproduction is specific to onclose.
The panic message ("A JavaScript exception was thrown, but it was cleared before it could be read") suggests the runtime is attempting to invoke the cleared callback during socket teardown and hitting an NPE that's masked by the teardown path.
Discovered while migrating a ServiceNow ops copilot from ioredis to native Bu

Bug: `Bun.SQL` MySQL: client sets CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS unconditionally, ignoring server capabilities
excerpt:
Bun.SQL MySQL: client sets CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS unconditionally, ignoring server capabilities
Version
Bun v1.3.11
Summary
During the MySQL handshake, Bun.SQL sets the CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS capability bit (0x00010000) in the client response regardless of whether the server advertised it. The MySQL protocol requires clients to only assert capability bits that the server offered in its initial greeting — the negotiated set is the intersection of both sides.
When Bun connects to a server that does not advertise CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS, Bun sets the bit anyway (protocol violation). The exact failure that follows depends on the server's behaviour:

A server that closes the connection on unrecognised multi-statement queries will do so silently, giving the client ERR_MYSQL_CONNECTION_CLOSED with no error detail.
A server that executes the statements but does not set SERVER_MORE_RESULTS_EXISTS in the intermediate EOF/OK packet will send extra result sets that Bun does not drain, corrupting the connection framing for the next query.

Note: Bun's multi-statement support itself is correct. Against a real MySQL 8 server (which does advertise CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS), sql.unsafe('SELECT 1; SELECT 2') returns [[{a:1}],[{a:2}]] and the connection survives. The bug only surfaces against servers that do not advertise the capability.
Capability flags — what was actually negotiated
Server greeting  (GreptimeDB v1.0.0, reports itself as MySQL 8.4.2):
  CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS  =  0  ← not advertised
  CLIENT_MULTI_RESULTS     =  0  ← not advertised

Bun.SQL client response:
  CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS  =  1  ← set unconditionally
  CLIENT_MULTI_RESULTS     =  1  ← set unconditionally

Raw capability words: server 0x01a88208, client 0x011b8208.
The client/server diff is exactly CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS | CLIENT_MULTI_RESULTS.
Reproducer
Option A — self-contained fake server (no external dependency)

const SERVER_CAPS_HI = Buffer.from([0xa8, 0x01]); // 0x01a8 upper bytes
// Note: 0x01a88208 does NOT include 0x00010000 (CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS)
//                                or 0x00020000 (CLIENT_MULTI_RESULTS)

title: Proposal: Implement "Modern Algorithms in the Web Cryptography API" (WICG specification)
excerpt:
The WICG is incubating a specification that adds post-quantum secure and modern cryptographic algorithms to the Web Cryptography API, much like X25519 was incubated before being merged into Web Cryptography: https://wicg.github.io/webcrypto-modern-algos/
Adoption is well underway:

Node.js already ships support
Cloudflare Workers PR is open
Chrome intent to ship
WebKit standards position
Mozilla standards position
Implementation status

The specification's Adoption Guidance section recommends the following implementation priorities:

ML-KEM (FIPS 203) — post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism. Combined with traditional key agreement it enables hybrid PQ/T key establishment as used in protocols like HPKE and its PQ and PQ/T algorithms. ML-KEM requires new SubtleCrypto methods: encapsulateKey, encapsulateBits, decapsulateKey, and decapsulateBits.
ML-DSA (FIPS 204) — post-quantum digital signature algorithm.
ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439) — widely deployed AEAD cipher used across TLS, SSH, WireGuard, HPKE.
SHA-3 (FIPS 202) — SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512 hash functions.
cSHAKE (NIST SP 800-185) — cSHAKE128, cSHAKE256 extendable-output functions used in post-quantum constructions including ML-KEM key derivation and hybrid KEM combiners. When invoked without customization parameters, cSHAKE produces output identical to SHAKE.
TurboSHAKE (RFC 9861) — TurboSHAKE128, TurboSHAKE256 XOFs based on round-reduced Keccak, roughly twice as fast as SHAKE.

The specification also introduces two important new SubtleCrypto methods that benefit all algorithms (including those already in Web Crypto):

SubtleCrypto.supports(operation, algorithm) — synchronous feature detection for algorithm/operation support. This is critical for enabling progressive enhancement and graceful fallback as runtimes adopt these algorithms incrementally.
SubtleCrypto.getPublicKey(key, keyUsages) — derives a public key from an asymmetric private key, simplifying key management and enabling protocols that commit the public key value to their outputs while accepting non-extractable private keys as input.

Web Platform Tests (WPTs) for the specified algorithms and operations are available and should be used to verify the implementation (it is okay to expect individual failures for unsupported features)

excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+af24e281e
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Given this dependency graph:
root
└── repro-uses-bundled@1.0.0
    ├── is-number@^7.0.0          ← direct dependency
    └── repro-bundled@1.0.0       ← bundledDependency
        └── is-number@^3.0.0      ← transitive dep (should be isolated inside the bundle)

repro-uses-bundled declares is-number@^7.0.0 as a direct dependency and lists repro-bundled in its bundledDependencies. repro-bundled internally depends on is-number@^3.0.0.
A full self-contained minimal reproduction is available at https://github.com/cjheppell/bun-lock-bug-reproduction.
What is the expected behavior?
The lockfile should resolve repro-uses-bundled's direct is-number dependency to 7.x (satisfying ^7.0.0). The bundled dependency's is-number@^3.0.0 should remain isolated inside the bundle and not affect the parent package's resolution.
For reference, npm handles this correctly — its package-lock.json resolves node_modules/is-number to 7.0.0 and node_modules/repro-bundled/node_modules/is-number to 3.0.0, properly isolated.
What do you see instead?
After bun install, the generated bun.lock contains:
"packages": {
    // Top-level is-number resolves to 7.0.0 — correct
    "is-number": ["is-number@7.0.0", ...],

    // But the scoped entry for repro-uses-bundled's is-number resolves to 3.0.0 — wrong!
    // This should be 7.0.0 (satisfying ^7.0.0), not 3.0.0 (from the bundled dep)
    "repro-uses-bundled/is-number": ["is-number@3.0.0", ..., { "dependencies": { "kind-of": "^3.0.2" } }],

    ...
}

title: bun build --compile: codesign fails with 'invalid or unsupported format for signature' on macOS in v1.3.12 (regression from v1.3.11)
excerpt:
Description
bun build --compile produces a binary that cannot be codesigned on macOS in Bun v1.3.12. The same codesign command works correctly in v1.3.11 and v1.3.7.
Reproduction
bun build --compile index.tsx --outfile myapp
codesign --sign - --force --entitlements entitlements.plist myapp
Error:
myapp: invalid or unsupported format for signature

Expected behavior
Binary is signed successfully, as in v1.3.11:
myapp: replacing existing signature
myapp: signed Mach-O thin (arm64) [myapp-...]

Root cause (investigated)
In v1.3.11 and earlier, the compiled binary comes out with a pre-existing linker-signed ad-hoc signature structure that codesign can replace:
flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed)
Signature=adhoc

In v1.3.12, the binary comes out completely unsigned (code object is not signed at all), and its Mach-O structure appears to be in a format that codesign cannot process, causing the error.
Without codesigning, the binary is killed with SIGKILL (exit 137) on macOS 26 (Tahoe) even with Gatekeeper disabled, due to hardened runtime enforcement.

Binary runs on macOS 26

✅ works
✅


v1.3.11
✅ works
✅


v1.3.12
❌ invalid or unsupported format for signature
❌ SIGKILL



Environment

macOS: 26.4 Tahoe (arm64)
Architecture: Apple Silicon (arm64)
SIP: enabled

curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash -s "bun-v1.3.11"

title: net.Socket.setTimeout fires under active I/O in Bun but not in Node.js (idle timeout semantics mismatch)
Support --bytecode with --format=esm without --compile (generate .jsc sidecar files for ESM bundles)
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, --bytecode without --compile only supports CommonJS. This creates two problems:


--compile duplicates the Bun runtime per binary. For a single service, --compile --bytecode --format=esm is fine — you get a standalone binary and can use a minimal base image without Bun installed. But when you run multiple services in a single Docker image (e.g. via s6-overlay for self-hosted / on-prem distributions), each compiled binary embeds its own copy of the Bun runtime (~59 MB on arm64). With 5 services that's ~295 MB of duplicated runtimes vs. a single shared Bun installation (~120 MB) running plain .js bundles.


CJS breaks top-level await and ESM import/export. Without --compile, --bytecode forces CommonJS output, so any codebase using top-level await (valid ESM) fails to build. The only workaround is refactoring every TLA call site into async IIFEs or lazy-init patterns — a non-trivial change for an existing codebase.


Together, this means multi-service ESM codebases cannot use bytecode caching at all today.
What we want — ESM + bytecode sidecar, no embedded runtime:
$ bun build index.ts --bytecode --format=esm --target=bun --outdir dist
error: ESM bytecode requires --compile. Use --format=cjs for bytecode without --compile.

CJS bytecode works, but breaks top-level await:
$ bun build index.ts --bytecode --target=bun --outdir dist
5 | const config = await getConfig();
                         ^
error: "await" can only be used inside an "async" function

ESM + bytecode + --compile works, but produces a 59 MB binary per service:
$ bun build index.ts --bytecode --compile --format=esm --outfile out
  [42ms]  bundle  1 modules
 [164ms] compile  out
$ ls -lh out
-rwxr-xr-x  1 user  staff  59M Apr 14 09:07 out

Reproduction file (index.ts):
async function getConfig() {
  return { port: 3000 };
}

const config = await getConfig();
console.log(`Server starting on port ${config.port}`);
Bun version: 1.3.12+700fc117a
Platform: Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Support --bytecode --format=esm --outdir (without --compile) by generating .jsc sidecar files for ESM bundles, the same way it already works for CJS today.
Expected behavior:
$ bun build src/index.ts --bytecode --format=esm --target=bun --outdir dist
# Produces:
#   dist/index.js   (ESM bundle)
#   dist/index.jsc  (bytecode cache)

$ bun dist/index.js  # Automatically uses index.jsc, supports top-level await

title: bun build --compile produces binaries with corrupt LC_CODE_SIGNATURE on macOS arm64 (SIGKILL on Sequoia 15.4+)
excerpt:
Summary
bun build --compile on macOS arm64 produces Mach-O binaries with a corrupt LC_CODE_SIGNATURE section. On macOS Sequoia 15.4+ (Darwin 25.4.0), AppleSystemPolicy enforces code signature validation and SIGKILL's the binary on launch from non-/tmp paths.
This is a regression — binaries compiled with Bun 1.3.10 worked fine. The issue appears in Bun 1.3.12.
Reproduction
bun -v
# 1.3.12

echo 'console.log("hello")' > test.ts
bun build test.ts --compile --outfile ./test-bin

# Check: binary has an LC_CODE_SIGNATURE but it's invalid
otool -l ./test-bin | grep -A5 LC_CODE_SIGNATURE
codesign -dv ./test-bin
# "code object is not signed at all"

codesign --force --sign - ./test-bin
# "invalid or unsupported format for signature"

# From /tmp it runs (macOS relaxes policy there), but from project dirs:
./test-bin
# zsh: killed
# exit code 137 (SIGKILL)
Kernel log confirms:
kernel: proc XXXXX: load code signature error 4 for file "test-bin"
(AppleSystemPolicy) ASP: Security policy would not allow process: XXXXX, /path/to/test-bin

Workaround
Strip the corrupt signature first, then ad-hoc re-sign:
codesign --remove-signature ./test-bin
codesign --force --sign - ./test-bin
# now it runs fine
Environment

Bun: 1.3.12 (worked on 1.3.10)
macOS: Sequoia 15.4 (Darwin 25.4.0)
Arch: arm64 (Apple Silicon)

Notes
Issue #7208 was closed after PR #17207 added proper Mach-O __BUN section support for codesigning. It seems something has regressed — the LC_CODE_SIGNATURE load command is present in the binary but points to invalid/corrupt data, which is worse than having no signature at all (macOS treats "no signature" more leniently than "bad signature" depending on path).

title: Segfault on DuckDB open/query/close loop with raw npm duckdb addon
No way to detect backpressure on `Bun.spawn` stdin `FileSink`
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.11+af24e281e
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Problem
When using Bun.spawn with stdin: "pipe", the returned FileSink has no mechanism to detect or handle backpressure.
In Node.js, child_process.spawn returns a Writable stream for stdin with:

write() returning false when the buffer exceeds writableHighWaterMark
writableLength to check pending bytes
writableEnded / destroyed to check stream state
'drain' event to resume writing

With Bun.spawn, proc.stdin is a FileSink that only exposes: write, flush, end, start, ref, unref. There is no equivalent to writableLength, no false return from write(), and no drain event.
Use case
We're building a streaming relay server that broadcasts MPEGTS data to multiple FFmpeg consumers via a fanout pattern. Before writing each chunk to a consumer's stdin, we need to check if the consumer is keeping up — if not, we drop the
chunk to prevent unbounded memory growth.
In our Node.js version, this works:
// Node.js — works
if (consumer.stdin.writableEnded || consumer.stdin.destroyed) continue;
if (consumer.stdin.writableLength > HIGH_WATERMARK) {
  droppedChunks++;
  continue;
}
consumer.stdin.write(chunk);
With Bun.spawn, none of these checks are available:
// Bun — no way to check
proc.stdin.write(chunk); // no return value signal, no writableLength
What we've tried

FileSink.write() returns number per the docs, but sometimes returns a Promise — this is inconsistent and not documented as a backpressure signal
FileSink.start({ highWaterMark }) controls auto-flush threshold, not backpressure rejection
node:child_process in Bun: write() does return false for backpressure, but writableLength is always 0 — partially working
Writing to a dead process stdin throws EPIPE with no way to check beforehand (no destroyed property)

Expected behavior
One of:

FileSink.write() returns false when internal buffer exceeds a threshold (like Node.js Writable.write())
FileSink.writableLength property exposing pending bytes
FileSink.destroyed / FileSink.writableEnded properties to check if the sink is still valid
A drain callback/event when the buffer is flushed

Environment

Bun: v1.3.11
OS: macOS ARM64

What is the expected behavior?

No response

const buildResult = await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: [serverEntryPoint],

title: `bun update --recursive` / `--filter` only edits root `package.json`, ignores workspaces
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.12
What platform is your computer?
Linux (reproduced on Fedora 43, x86_64)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Minimal monorepo:
root/
├── package.json            # workspaces: ["packages/*"], devDeps: { "some-pkg": "^1.0.0" }
└── packages/
    ├── pkg-a/package.json  # deps: { "some-pkg": "^1.0.0" }
    └── pkg-b/package.json  # deps: { "some-pkg": "^1.0.0" }

Where some-pkg@2.0.0 exists on the registry.
bun install
bun update --recursive --latest
What is the expected behavior?
All three package.json files (root, pkg-a, pkg-b) should have some-pkg bumped to ^2.0.0, mirroring the behavior of bun update -i (interactive) with --recursive, and mirroring what pnpm update -r --latest does.
What do you see instead?
Only the root package.json is edited. pkg-a/package.json and pkg-b/package.json are untouched. --filter='*' behaves the same way.
Source evidence
do.recursive is parsed and stored, but only two call sites read it:

src/cli/update_interactive_command.zig:368 — interactive update
src/cli/outdated_command.zig:86 — bun outdated

The non-interactive update path (src/cli/update_command.zig → updatePackageJSONAndInstallWithManagerWithUpdates in src/install/PackageManager/updatePackageJSONAndInstall.zig) never consults do.recursive. It opens exactly one package.json (manager.original_package_json_path) and calls editUpdateNoArgs on it once.
--filter has the same failure mode: src/install/PackageManager/install_with_manager.zig:1088-1089 gates filter handling on subcommand == .install, with a comment stating "only populated when subcommand is .install".
False-positive test
The existing test test/cli/install/bun-update.test.ts:424-484 titled "should support --recursive flag" only asserts expect(out + err).toMatch(/bun update|missing lockfile|nothing to update/). Since every bun update invocation prints the banner bun update v1.3.12 (...), the substring bun update always matches. The test never reads back any workspace package.json and never catches this bug.

title: bun build --compile: codesign regression in 1.3.12 — "invalid or unsupported format for signature"
excerpt:
Summary
Executables produced by bun build --compile with Bun 1.3.12 cannot be code-signed on macOS. Even ad-hoc signing (codesign --sign - --force) fails with:
hello-1.3.12: invalid or unsupported format for signature

This is a regression — all prior versions tested produce signable binaries.
Versions tested



Version
codesign result




1.2.4
OK


1.2.15
OK


1.3.0
OK


1.3.9
OK


1.3.10
OK


1.3.11
OK


1.3.12
FAILS



Platform

macOS arm64 (Darwin 24.5.0, aarch64)

Minimal reproduction
mkdir /tmp/bun-codesign-repro && cd /tmp/bun-codesign-repro
echo 'console.log("hello");' > hello.ts

# Download both versions
curl -fsSL "https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.11/bun-darwin-aarch64.zip" -o bun-1.3.11.zip
curl -fsSL "https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.12/bun-darwin-aarch64.zip" -o bun-1.3.12.zip
unzip bun-1.3.11.zip -d bun-1.3.11-tmp && mv bun-1.3.11-tmp/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun bun-1.3.11
unzip bun-1.3.12.zip -d bun-1.3.12-tmp && mv bun-1.3.12-tmp/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun bun-1.3.12

# Compile
./bun-1.3.11 build --compile --outfile hello-1.3.11 hello.ts
./bun-1.3.12 build --compile --outfile hello-1.3.12 hello.ts

# Sign
codesign --sign - --force hello-1.3.11    # ✅ succeeds
codesign --sign - --force hello-1.3.12    # ❌ fails
Error output
$ codesign --sign - --force hello-1.3.12
hello-1.3.12: invalid or unsupported format for signature

$ codesign -dvvv hello-1.3.12
hello-1.3.12: code object is not signed at all

Note: the binary runs fine — only code signing is broken.
Root cause analysis
The LC_CODE_SIGNATURE load command in 1.3.12 declares a datasize that is far too small for the actual embedded code signature SuperBlob:
1.3.11 (working)
LC_CODE_SIGNATURE:
  dataoff  = 60576496
  datasize = 492720

SuperBlob header size = 473394  ← fits within datasize ✅

__LINKEDIT:
  fileoff  = 60375040
  filesize = 694176
  (end = 61069216 = file size)

1.3.12 (broken)
LC_CODE_SIGNATURE:
  dataoff  = 61266768
  datasize = 139120     ← TOO SMALL

SuperBlob header size = 478770  ← 478770 > 139120 ❌ OVERFLOW

__LINKEDIT:
  fileoff  = 61063168
  filesize = 342720
  (end = 61405888 = file size)

The SuperBlob claims to be 478770 bytes, but LC_CODE_SIGNATURE only allocates 139120 bytes. codesign sees the inconsistency and refuses to process the binary.
Additionally, __LINKEDIT filesize shrank from 694176 to 342720 despite the binary being slightly larger overall (61.4MB vs 61.1MB), suggesting the Mach-O layout/section sizing logic

title: Bun workspace transitive CJS deps break Vite dev server (/@fs/.bun/ paths skip ESM conversion)
excerpt:
What is the issue?
In a Bun workspace monorepo, transitive CJS dependencies are stored in node_modules/.bun/<pkg>@<version>/ instead of being hoisted to node_modules/<pkg>/. When Vite's dev server serves these modules via /@fs/ URLs, it doesn't apply CJS→ESM conversion, causing browser errors:
SyntaxError: The requested module '/@fs/.../node_modules/.bun/bind-event-listener@3.0.0/
  node_modules/bind-event-listener/dist/index.js' does not provide an export named 'bind'

This completely breaks client-side JavaScript in SSR apps.
Cross-posted from: vitejs/vite#22247
How can we reproduce the crash?
Dependency chain
apps/web (Bun workspace member)
  → @atlaskit/pragmatic-drag-and-drop@1.7.9
    → bind-event-listener@3.0.0  (CJS only)
    → raf-schd@4.0.3             (CJS only)

Module location
Bun stores the transitive dep here:
node_modules/.bun/bind-event-listener@3.0.0/node_modules/bind-event-listener/dist/index.js

npm/pnpm would hoist it to node_modules/bind-event-listener/, where Vite's optimizer can find and pre-bundle it.
What happens

Vite's dep optimizer can't resolve bare specifier bind-event-listener (not in node_modules/)
optimizeDeps.include: ['bind-event-listener'] fails: Failed to resolve dependency: bind-event-listener
Runtime module request goes through /@fs/ path, serving raw CJS to the browser
Browser fails with SyntaxError on import { bind } from '...'

The nested syntax partially works but is fragile
optimizeDeps: { include: ['@atlaskit/pragmatic-drag-and-drop > bind-event-listener'] }
This works for known deps but requires manually mapping every CJS transitive dep chain.
Suggested fix
One of:

Hoist transitive deps that are consumed by Vite-compatible tooling (at least to a discoverable node_modules/ path)
Expose a resolution API that Vite can use to resolve bare specifiers through Bun's .bun/ layout
Add a bun install --hoist flag (or similar) for projects that use Vite dev server

Environment

Bun: 1.3.9
Vite: 8.0.7
OS: macOS arm64

title: CLI error on invalid parameters.

`bun install --force` does not re-extract local `.tgz` dependencies after file is replaced
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.6
What platform is your computer?
Windows 11 x64
What steps can reproduce the bug?

Have a workspace dependency pointing to a local .tgz file:
{
  "dependencies": {
    "my-generated-pkg": "./lib/my-generated-pkg.tgz"
  }
}

Run bun install. Package is extracted correctly into node_modules/.bun/my-generated-pkg@.+lib+my-generated-pkg.tgz+<hash>/
Regenerate / replace the .tgz file at the same path (new content, same filename)
Run bun install --force. node_modules still contains the OLD extracted content.
Even bun pm cache rm followed by bun install --force still installs the stale content.
Manually deleting the junction target in node_modules/.bun/ and the symlink in the workspace's node_modules/, then running bun install --force, also restores the old content from the .bun directory.

The junction path includes a hash suffix (e.g. +fec5f8e7aa77292d) that appears to be computed from the path rather than the file content, so it never invalidates when the tgz is replaced.
What is the expected behavior?
bun install --force should detect that the .tgz file has changed (different checksum or mtime) and re-extract it, replacing the stale content in node_modules.
What do you see instead?
The old extracted package remains in node_modules indefinitely. The only workaround we found is to manually delete the specific node_modules/.bun/<pkg>@* folder and then run bun install --force.
Workaround
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "node_modules/.bun/my-generated-pkg@*"
bun install --force
Additional information
This is especially painful for monorepos that use locally-generated packages where the .tgz is regenerated frequently during development. The stale cache causes tsc -b failures because new exports/modules are missing from the extracted package while the .tgz itself contains them.
Repro context: we use babelfhir-ts to generate TypeScript FHIR packages as .tgz files, referenced via "my-pkg": "./lib/my-pkg.tgz" in package.json. After regenerating the tgz with additional ValueSet modules, bun install --force keeps extracting the old version. Only nuking the node_modules/.bun/<pkg>@* directory forces a fresh extraction.

What steps can reproduce the bug?

title: CPU 100% on UDP error !!!!
bun install warns on valid prereleases in peer deps
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.x (reproduces on current main)
What platform is your computer?
macOS arm64 (pure semver logic, hits every platform)
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Any prerelease version validated against a peer range with no prerelease comparator on the same major.minor.patch.
Real-world hit: installing canary/nightly releases of the RN + Expo + React stack together. Verified:
bun add expo@canary react-native@nightly react@19.3.0-canary-3e319a94-20260126
# 21 × warn: incorrect peer dependency ...
# one for each package in the transitive tree whose non-prerelease peer range
# meets a canary/nightly version
Minimal self-contained repro (verified against vanilla oven-sh/bun@main and the fix in #27085):
mkdir -p /tmp/repro-29444/{producer,consumer} && cd /tmp/repro-29444

cat > producer/package.json <<'PKG'
{
  "name": "peer-consumer-pkg",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "peerDependencies": { "react": ">=18.0.0" }
}
PKG

cat > consumer/package.json <<'PKG'
{
  "name": "consumer",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": {
    "peer-consumer-pkg": "file:../producer",
    "react": "19.3.0-canary-3e319a94-20260126"
  }
}
PKG

cd consumer && bun install
# warn: incorrect peer dependency "react@19.3.0-canary-3e319a94-20260126"
# 19.3.0-canary is clearly > 18.0.0, this is a false positive
What is the expected behavior?
19.3.0-canary-3e319a94-20260126 satisfies >=18.0.0. 56.0.0-canary.1 satisfies >=14.0.4. 19.2.0-rc.1 satisfies ^19.0.0. No warning.
Matches yarn v1 (satisfiesWithPrereleases) and node-semver { includePrerelease: true }, which is what every dev on a canary channel expects.
What do you see instead?
incorrect peer dependency warning on every valid prerelease.
List.satisfiesPre in src/semver/SemverQuery.zig gates on pre_matched, which only flips true when a comparator in the range has a prerelease tag on the same major.minor.patch. So 56.0.0-canary fails against >=14.0.4 because the range has no prerelease comparator, even though 56 > 14.
Additional information
Hits every npm package on a -canary/-rc/-next/-nightly channel against a non-prerelease peer range. React Native nightlies, Expo canary packages, any lib shipping prerelease tags that another lib peer-depends on.
Prior art:

yarn v1 fixed this in 2017 (yarnpkg/yarn#3361, satisfiesWithPrereleases)
npm RFC npm/rfcs#397 still open since 2021
node-semver has { includePrerelease: true } as a built-in option

Bun auto-installs peer deps, so there's no --include-prerelease escape hatch. Users

title: FFI: passing C structs by value still segfaults on Linux x64 in v1.3.12 (blocks DuckDB and other mainstream C libraries)
excerpt:
Summary
bun:ffi cannot invoke a C function whose signature takes a struct by value
on Linux x64. Any such call — including the primary query API of mainstream
libraries like DuckDB — segfaults at address 0x0 when declared through
dlopen().
This is the second of the two FFI bugs in #29346. The first (number as
'ptr' argument corruption, Fix 1) was resolved in v1.3.3 / #25045. The
second (struct-by-value, Fix 2) is still broken in v1.3.12 — re-verified
today, Apr 18, 2026.
Related: #6139 (enhancement, add ctypes-style struct construction — open
since Sep 2023). This issue is narrower and more immediate: existing C
functions with struct-by-value signatures should be callable through FFI
at all, regardless of whether Bun ever grows struct construction.

title: Support Web Workers in Bun bundler
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.12
What platform is your computer?
Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 arm
What steps can reproduce the bug?
// worker.ts
self.addEventListener("message", (e: MessageEvent) => {
  self.postMessage(e.data);
});

// index.ts
const worker = new Worker(new URL("./worker.ts", import.meta.url));
worker.postMessage("hello");
worker.addEventListener("message", (e) => console.log(e.data));
<!-- index.html -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <body>
    <script type="module" src="./index.ts"></script>
  </body>
</html>
Dev server
bun run index.html

Or invoke bundler
bun build ./index.html --outdir=dist --target=browser

What is the expected behavior?

Web Workwr should work
dist/index.js should reference a bundled URL for the worker (e.g. new Worker("/dist/worker-HASH.js"))
dist/worker-HASH.js (or similar) should exist as a separate bundled output file containing the compiled worker code

This is the standard behavior provided by Webpack, Vite, and esbuild for this well-documented pattern: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Worker/Worker
What do you see instead?
The worker fails to load at runtime. dist/worker.ts is never emitted. Console errors from dist/index.js contains a malformed new URL("./worker.ts", import.meta.url) pointing at the unbundled TS source in file system since import.meta.url resolves to a file:// url instead. JS code stops executing with a security error.
Additional information
There is currently no workaround within bun build. Manually specifying worker.ts as a second entrypoint does not help because there is no mechanism to reference that entry's output URL from index.ts.
This pattern is detected and handled by:

Webpack: new Worker(new URL('./worker.ts', import.meta.url)) → auto code-split worker bundle
Vite: same pattern + ?worker query param
esbuild: same pattern (behind --bundle)

Without this, Web Workers cannot be used in any frontend project built with bun build.

title: 🚀 Feature Request [pm][security]: Support wildcard matching in `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` for organization and prefix-based package exclusions
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, minimumReleaseAgeExclude supports name (and soon version) based exclusions, but it does not support wildcard matching. This limits organizations that publish sets of related packages from easily configuring exclusions for their own scopes or package patterns. Each package must be explicitly listed or updated over time, rather than excluded by organization prefix or glob.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
Add wildcard support to minimumReleaseAgeExclude, enabling patterns such as:

Scoped wildcards: @myorg/* (exclude all packages under @myorg)
Name/prefix wildcards: myorg-* (exclude all packages starting with a prefix)
Global wildcard: * (exclude all packages; acts as an override to disable minimumReleaseAge—should be optional for implementation simplicity)

Implementation Suggestions:

Follow common glob conventions as seen in pnpm and possibly npm in the future.
Ensure support for both scoped and unscoped patterns.
Allow existing name and name@version exclusions to co-exist with wildcards.
If supporting * is complex, make it an optional implementation detail; document accordingly.

Implementation should consider the draft PR for version-specific exclusions (#28970), as the feature sets build on each other. Recommend implementing on top of that unmerged PR for proper integration and to reach feature parity with pnpm.
What alternatives have you considered?
Possible alternatives:

Manually update minimumReleaseAgeExclude with every relevant package name (not scalable for orgs with many packages)
Use version exclusions only, but this doesn't help in covering broad package patterns easily

Feature parity with pnpm (and likely npm in the future) suggests strong precedent for supporting wildcards over manual listing.

title: Bun.sql prepared statement cache not invalidated after DDL — connection permanently fails with `cached plan must not change result type` (SQLSTATE `0A000`)
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.12+700fc117a
What platform is your computer?
Linux 6.12.* aarch64 unknown
What steps can reproduce the bug?
bun:sql creates server-side named prepared statements and caches them per
connection. When DDL changes the rowtype of a table referenced by a cached
plan, PostgreSQL rejects subsequent executions of that plan with SQLSTATE
0A000 ("cached plan must not change result type"). bun:sql surfaces the
error to the caller but does not evict the stale plan or retry, so every
future execution of the same query on that connection fails forever —
even though a fresh parse would succeed.
Reproduction:
Run the attached repro.ts against any postgres server.
What is the expected behavior?
Sibling drivers (e.g. Porsager's postgres / postgres.js) handle this
transparently: they detect SQLSTATE 0A000 + the specific message, drop
the cached statement, and retry once. Callers never see the error.
I believe that should be Bun's approach as well.
What do you see instead?
2nd call FAILED: PostgresError: cached plan must not change result type
    errno: "0A000",

  routine: "RevalidateCachedQuery",

title: Bun install GitHub ci deadlock
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13
What platform is your computer?
GitHub action ubuntu-latest ubuntu-24.04
What steps can reproduce the bug?
add a package with post install script to your package.json like @shopify/react-native-skia
then add a GitHub action:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

env:
  CI: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: Typecheck and Test
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment: development
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Check out code
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2

      - name: Setup Node.js environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          bun install --frozen-lockfile --verbose
I have trustedDependencies in my root package.json
"trustedDependencies": [
    "@sentry/cli",
    "@shopify/react-native-skia"
  ],
What is the expected behavior?
The CI bun install step to finish quickly and successfully.
What do you see instead?
the CI step spins forever.
Additional information
According to claude while inspecting the bun install --verbose log I gave it.
What happened: bun install didn't fail with an error — it hung. Both lifecycle scripts finished
successfully (@sentry/cli at 14:47:01, @shopify/react-native-skia at 14:47:13), then bun went
completely silent for 5m58s before the job was cancelled. With --verbose, bun should be chatty at
all times — 6 minutes of zero output means bun deadlocked after Skia's postinstall.
Why: @shopify/react-native-skia's postinstall script modifies its own package.json (line 250171:
"Checksums updated in package.json"). This is a known trigger for a deadlock in bun 1.3.x: bun
detects the file change, and --frozen-lockfile prevents it from reconciling — rather than
immediately erroring, it hangs.

title: Feature Request: Support `--bun` flag in `bun install` to persist Bun-execution for CLIs (Node-free environment)
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Currently, Bun provides excellent runtime interception via the --bun flag (e.g., bun run --bun vite). However, this introduces significant friction in a "Bun-only" workflow:

Hardcoded Shebang Dependency: Most npm packages (e.g., ni, vitest, eslint) come with a hardcoded #!/usr/bin/env node shebang. This forces users to keep a Node.js runtime installed on their system just to run global CLI tools, even if they wish to use Bun exclusively.
High Mental Cost: For global packages, users expect to run the command directly (e.g., just typing ni). Requiring a prefix like bun --bun ni or setting up manual shell aliases for every single tool is inefficient and breaks developer muscle memory.
Environment Redundancy: Maintaining both Node and Bun just for CLI compatibility contradicts Bun's goal of being a faster, all-in-one replacement for Node.js.

What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
I propose adding a --bun flag to the bun install command (with a focus on global installs, i.e., bun i -g <pkg> --bun).
This flag would instruct Bun to "Bun-ify" the package's executable during the installation phase:

Automatic Shebang Patching: During the symlinking process, Bun could automatically rewrite the first line of the entry script from #!/usr/bin/env node to #!/usr/bin/env bun.
Smart Shimming: Alternatively, Bun could generate a lightweight wrapper/shim in the bin directory that executes the target script using bun --bun [path/to/script] "$@".

What alternatives have you considered?

Shell Aliases: Manually adding alias ni='bun run --bun ni' to .zshrc or .bashrc.

Drawback: High maintenance; must be updated manually for every new tool and synced across different machines.


Manual Shebang Editing: Manually locating the binary with which and editing the code.

Drawback: Brittle and will be overwritten whenever the package is updated.


Keeping Node.js Installed: * Drawback: Defeats the purpose of a streamlined, high-performance, Bun-native development environment and wastes disk space/system complexity.

title: Compiled binary: Workers leak extracted native .so/.dylib files in /tmp (never cleaned up)
excerpt:
Summary
When a Bun-compiled binary uses new Worker(), each Worker instance extracts embedded native modules (.so/.dylib files) to /tmp with unique hash-based filenames. These files are never cleaned up after the Worker is terminated, causing unbounded disk growth.
Reproduction
Setup
A compiled binary that:

Embeds a native library loaded via bun:ffi dlopen() (e.g., @opentui/core uses import("./libopentui.so", { with: { type: "file" } }) then dlopen())
Creates Workers that trigger the native module loading path

Steps
# Build a compiled binary
bun build --compile --entrypoints ./index.ts --outfile ./myapp

# Run the binary - it spawns Workers for file operations
./myapp serve
Observed behavior

Each new Worker() call extracts the embedded native .so/.dylib to /tmp with a unique hash filename (e.g., .5ffbafXXX-00000000.so)
When worker.terminate() is called, the extracted file remains in /tmp
Subsequent Worker creations extract new copies with different hashes instead of reusing existing ones
Files are hidden (dot-prefixed), so ls does not show them, but ls -a / find does

Measured impact (real-world: opencode serve)

File size: ~4.3 MB each (Linux x64) / ~860 KB each (macOS arm64)
Creation rate: ~9 files per 10 seconds when actively processing requests
Leak rate: ~14 GB/hour on Linux
Disk fill time: fills a 300 GB / partition in ~19 hours

Verification
# Monitor growth
watch -n 5 "find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name '.*-00000000.so' -type f | wc -l"

# Identify the files
file /tmp/.5ffbaf*-00000000.so
# Output: ELF 64-bit LSB shared object, x86-64

nm -gU /tmp/.5ffbaf*-00000000.so | head -5
# Shows symbols from the embedded native library (e.g., opentui renderer)
Expected behavior

Extracted native files should be reused across Worker instances (content-hash based deduplication)
OR extracted files should be cleaned up when the Worker is terminated
OR at minimum, a single extraction per unique module should be shared via the existing $bunfs mechanism

Environment

Bun: v1.x compiled binary mode (bun build --compile)
OS: Linux x64 (primary), also reproduced on macOS arm64
Native loading: bun:ffi dlopen() on a file imported with { with: { type: "file" } }

Workaround
Periodic cleanup via cron:
*/30 * * * * find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name ".*-00000000.so" -mmin +5 -delete
Context
Discovered while running opencode in serve mode on a production server. The @opentui/core library embeds a platform-specific .so via bun:ffi, and opencode creates/destroys ripgrep Workers frequentl

This silently breaks any observability library that relies on these channels

What is the expected behavior?
Node.js instruments its HTTP server internally by publishing to named

HTTP Server channels



Channel
When

Server receives a request


http.server.response.created
Server creates a response object

title: bug: `bun test --changed` ignores tsconfig `paths` aliases, silently skipping affected tests
Exit-time `tcsetattr` on fd 0 / fd 2 clobbers downstream pager raw mode (less, fzf, fx) in pipelines
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13
What platform is your computer?
Any MacOS and any Linux
What steps can reproduce the bug?
When a Bun process is started with stdin (fd 0) or stderr (fd 2) attached to a TTY, the runtime unconditionally snapshots the termios of those fds at startup (tcgetattr) and restores them at exit (tcsetattr). Because termios state is a property of the underlying terminal device, not the fd, the exit-time restore writes to the shared /dev/pts/* device and overwrites any raw-mode state a downstream pipeline consumer has set in the meantime.
Minimal repro (Linux / WSL2 / Darwin, less installed)
cat > /tmp/bun-tty-bug.js <<'EOF'
// Any script that spends ~500ms doing work before exiting reproduces this.
// `bun -e 'console.log("x")'` alone exits in ~60ms and usually wins the
// race against less's setRawMode; adding the sleep makes the outcome
// near-deterministic.
setTimeout(() => {
    console.log("hi");
    process.exit(0);
}, 500);
EOF

# Loop so the race triggers reliably. On each iteration, press 'q' to quit
# less. On broken runs, 'q' does nothing (keyboard is in cooked mode) and
# you must press Enter to unblock it.
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
    echo "run $i"
    bun /tmp/bun-tty-bug.js | less
done
strace evidence
sudo strace -f -yy -tt -s 200 -o /tmp/bun-tty.strace \
    -e trace=ioctl,rt_sigaction,openat,close \
    bun /tmp/bun-tty-bug.js | less
Relevant lines (prefix trimmed):
# Startup — Bun saves termios for fd 0 and fd 2
ioctl(0</dev/pts/2>, TCGETS, {...c_lflag=ISIG|ICANON|ECHO|...}) = 0
ioctl(0</dev/pts/2>, TCGETS, {...}) = 0
ioctl(1<pipe:[...]>, TCGETS, ...) = -1 ENOTTY (Inappropriate ioctl for device)
ioctl(2</dev/pts/2>, TCGETS, {...}) = 0
ioctl(2</dev/pts/2>, TCGETS, {...}) = 0
rt_sigaction(SIGTERM, {sa_handler=0x42d8ca0, sa_flags=SA_RESTORER|SA_RESETHAND|...}, NULL, 8) = 0
rt_sigaction(SIGINT,  {sa_handler=0x42d8ca0, sa_flags=SA_RESTORER|SA_RESETHAND|...}, NULL, 8) = 0

# ... user code runs, pipe drains to less, less opens /dev/tty and setRawMode ...

# Exit — Bun writes the saved termios back to the shared device
ioctl(0</dev/pts/2>, TCGETS, {...}) = 0
ioctl(0</dev/pts/2>, TCSETS, {...c_lflag=ISIG|ICANON|ECHO|...}) = 0   # ← clobbers raw mode
ioctl(0</dev/pts/2>, TCGETS, {...}) = 0
ioctl(2</dev/pts/2>, TCGETS, {...}) = 0
ioctl(2</dev/pts/2>, TCSETS, {...}) = 0                               # ← second clobber
ioctl(2</dev/pts/2>, TCGETS, {...}) = 0

Both TCSETS calls happen regardless of whether user JS ever touc

title: S3 needs full metadata parity, server-side copy, and a non-redirect response mode for serious server-side use
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
Bun’s S3 API is already very good for simple read/write/presign flows, but it is still hard to use as the primary storage layer in serious server-side apps.
Right now there are three important gaps:

Metadata parity is incomplete.
S3Client.stat() is documented as returning { etag, lastModified, size, type }, but many real applications need the rest of the object metadata and headers too, such as:


user metadata (x-amz-meta-*)
Cache-Control
Content-Disposition
Content-Encoding
Content-Language

Without that, apps cannot reliably treat S3 as a real filesystem/backend for stored objects with application-defined metadata.


There is no first-class server-side copy operation.
A serious object storage backend needs native copy support, including metadata behavior controls like copy-vs-replace. Without that, users end up falling back to SDKs or custom signed HTTP requests for a very common operation.


new Response(S3File) is documented as a 302 redirect to a presigned URL.
That is useful in some public download cases, but it does not work for apps that need to:



keep downloads on the application origin
apply per-request auth/authorization before serving the object
log/audit downloads at the app layer
avoid exposing bucket URLs or presigned URLs to clients

So while Bun’s S3 API is great for direct-to-bucket flows, it is still missing pieces needed for app-controlled/private/proxied object storage use.
Related existing issues:

#17339 user metadata / conditional writes
#19301 retrieving S3 response metadata
#16048 custom S3 headers/query params

This request is about the broader remaining gap for serious server-side S3 usage.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
A fuller S3 backend surface in Bun, ideally including:

Full metadata round-trip support


write-side support for arbitrary user metadata

copy existing metadata

title: Feature request: expose socket fd in Bun.serve fetch handler (and NodeHTTPServerSocket)
excerpt:
What is the problem this feature would solve?
We're building an HTTP proxy that needs to call getsockopt(TCP_INFO) on each connection — to get kernel-reported byte and segment counts rather than relying on socket.bytesRead/bytesWritten, which don't include TCP/IP overhead. The syscall needs a real OS file descriptor. Under Node.js, socket._handle.fd from the connection event gives us that. Under Bun, we can't find any path to it.
We traced this pretty thoroughly:
Bun.serve native HTTP: The fetch handler has server.requestIP(request), which internally calls getpeername(us_poll_fd(&s->p)). The fd is right there in Zig, it just never comes back to JS. The Server class (src/bun.js/api/server.classes.ts, server.zig) has no fd, no socket handle, no connection-level callback.
Node-compat http.createServer: The connection event fires, but the socket is a NodeHTTPServerSocket (src/bun.js/bindings/node/JSNodeHTTPServerSocket.cpp), which has no fd in its prototype table. Meanwhile TCPSocket (Bun.listen) does expose .fd via getFD → us_socket_get_fd - the infrastructure exists, it's just not wired for the HTTP
socket type.
What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?
The preferred fix is something in Bun.serve — either a server.socketFd(request) method alongside requestIP, or a
connection-level callback option (like socket) that fires with something .fd-accessible. That's where most people will
be running HTTP servers.
The easier fix is a .fd getter on NodeHTTPServerSocket. It'd be a small addition to the prototype table pointing at
us_socket_get_fd, same as TCPSocket already does. Not the primary ask, but it'd unblock the Node-compat path on its
own.
The general case this enables is any per-connection low-level TCP operation: getsockopt/setsockopt, TCP_INFO, TCP_CORK,
SO_RCVBUF, etc. Bun.listen already handles this at the TCP layer — it's just not accessible once HTTP is on top.
What alternatives have you considered?
Looked at the bun source code a fair bit but can't find any simple way to access this. There's a potential route via FFI and /proc/self/fd but that feels very messy.

title: Explicit workspace members under symlinked directories install, then fail at runtime with broken package-local node_modules links

install: global virtual store (#29489) breaks bundler resolution & re-materializes on warm installs
excerpt:
Summary
PR #29489 moved the isolated
linker's store from inside the project (<project>/node_modules/.bun/) to
a shared location outside it (~/.bun/install/cache/links/). That change
has two observable regressions on current main (890ef5a3) compared
with the commit immediately before it (bf2e2cec):

Bundlers that canonicalize symlinks (rspack, webpack with the default
resolver) fail to resolve optional-peer-style requires because the
canonicalized path's ancestor chain no longer passes through the
project's top-level node_modules/.
bun install against an already-fully-populated store still
re-materializes ~2000 entries via <entry>.tmp-<suffix> staging dirs
instead of hitting the warm /links/ cache.

Both behaviors disappear when checking out bf2e2cec and rebuilding.
Reproduction
Real-world consumer: 2000+ packages, isolated linker (the default in
1.3.x). debug@4.x is somewhere in the graph, declaring:
"peerDependenciesMeta": { "supports-color": { "optional": true } }
supports-color IS in the consumer's graph (pulled in by chalk or
similar), confirmed by ls ~/.bun/install/cache/links/ | grep ^supports-color returning
multiple versioned entries.
Symptom 1 — bundler can't resolve optional peer
rm -rf node_modules ~/.bun/install/cache
bun install
# run rspack / webpack build
Output:
WARNING in .../.bun/install/cache/links/debug@4.4.3-<hash>/node_modules/debug/src/node.js
  Module not found: Can't resolve 'supports-color'
  in '/Users/<user>/.bun/install/cache/links/debug@4.4.3-<hash>/node_modules/debug/src'

The canonicalized path walks:

.../cache/links/debug@4.4.3-<hash>/node_modules/ (only debug's declared deps)
.../cache/links/debug@4.4.3-<hash>/ (no node_modules)
.../cache/links/ (sibling store entries, no node_modules/supports-color)
.../cache/ → .../ etc.

None of those have node_modules/supports-color, so the resolver gives up.
Under pre-#29489 bun, the canonical path was .bun/debug@<hash>/node_modules/debug/src/node.js
inside the project, and the ancestor walk eventually reached
<project>/node_modules/supports-color.
Postinstall scripts doing require('<optional-peer>') at install time hit
the same wall and exit non-zero — we saw this with @sentry/cli's
postinstall requiring node-fetch, which in turn requires
whatwg-url (declared as peerDependenciesMeta.optional).
Symptom 2 — warm install re-materializes everything
rm -rf node_modules ~/.bun/install/cache
bun install                          # populates /links/
# /links/ now has ~10,000 entries material

title: FormData multipart serializer corrupts adjacent string field value with trailing \r on specific binary payloads
FormData generates non-standard multipart boundary format (`-WebkitFormBoundary{hex}`, 1 leading dash) differing from undici and WebKit
excerpt:
What version of Bun is running?
1.3.13 (also reproduced on 1.3.11).
What platform is your computer?
Linux x86_64. Also seen in production on oven/bun:1.3.13-alpine (arm64).
What steps can reproduce the bug?
Bun's native FormData generates a multipart boundary with only one leading dash (-WebkitFormBoundary...), which produces a 3-dash body-marker (---WebkitFormBoundary...). This differs from both undici and WebKit browsers, which use 4 leading dashes in the declared boundary (→ 6-dash body markers).
Evidence, captured via a Node-hosted HTTPS MITM that dumps the byte-for-byte body Bun emits:
content-type: multipart/form-data; boundary=-WebkitFormBoundary1493ef9033594e1f83f9e85b0e703bf8

---WebkitFormBoundary1493ef9033594e1f83f9e85b0e703bf8<CR><LF>
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="page-17.pdf"<CR><LF>
Content-Type: application/octet-stream<CR><LF>
<CR><LF>
<binary bytes...>
<CR><LF>
---WebkitFormBoundary1493ef9033594e1f83f9e85b0e703bf8<CR><LF>
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="purpose"<CR><LF>
<CR><LF>
user_data<CR><LF>
---WebkitFormBoundary1493ef9033594e1f83f9e85b0e703bf8--<CR><LF>

Compare to undici (lib/web/fetch/body.js:110):
const boundary = `----formdata-undici-0${`${random(1e11)}`.padStart(11, '0')}`
// declared: ----formdata-undici-0XXXXXXXXXXX  (4 dashes)
// body:     ------formdata-undici-0XXXXXXXXXXX  (6 dashes)
And real WebKit browsers use ----WebKitFormBoundary{hex} (4 dashes, capital K).
Bun's format is unique to Bun:

Only 1 leading dash in the declared boundary
Lowercase k in Webkit (vs WebKit browsers which use capital K)
3-dash body markers (vs 6-dash everywhere else)

This format tickles bugs in some downstream multipart parsers. We hit a deterministic, reproducible failure where OpenAI's API returns

Node/undici uploading the identical binary payload succeeds (44/44).
Bun uploading the same bytes to OpenAI fails (43/44, deterministic on one specific payload).
The only wire-level difference between Bun's and undici's requests is the boundary format.

title: z3-solver behavior different from Node
Error: spawn EINVAL
excerpt:
🐛 Root Cause
On Windows, child_process.spawndoes not execute commands through a shell by default. It expects the command argument to be a directly executable binary (e.g. a .exe file).
In this case:

bun is not a real executable on Windows
It is resolved via a shell shim (**bun.cmd**)
When calling:

spawn("bun", ["run", "dev"])

Node tries to execute bunas a binary, not through cmd.exe.
This leads to:
Error: spawn EINVAL

because:

Windows cannot directly execute bun (no .exe)
and spawn does not automatically resolve .cmd files unless a shell is involved


⚠️ Why This Happens Specifically on Windows
On Windows:

Executables must typically be:

.exe, .com, .bat, .cmd


bun resolves to bun.cmd via PATHEXT
BUT spawn()does NOT use **PATHEXT** resolution unless **shell: true** is set

So:



Call
Behavior




spawn("bun", ...)
❌ Fails (EINVAL / ENOENT)


spawn("bun.cmd", ...)
✅ Works


spawn("bun", ..., { shell: true })
✅ Works



Suggested Fix in Bun Codebase
At the referenced line:
👉 
  
    
      bun/packages/bun-debug-adapter-protocol/src/debugger/adapter.ts
    
    
         Line 2265
      in
      dc578b1
    
  
  
    

        
          
           subprocess = spawn(command, args, { 
        
    
  


const isWindows = process.platform === "win32";

spawn(command, args, {
  ...options,
  shell: isWindows, // or map to bun.cmd explicitly
});

Additional information
Root Cause (Two-Part)
Part 1 — GitHub Packages bug: When Bun (or any client) requests a tarball from npm.pkg.github.com,
GitHub Packages issues an HTTP redirect to registry.npmjs.com. The redirect URL drops the @scope/
prefix from the package name:
GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@3dlook-me/camera-rpv-client/-/camera-rpv-client-1.33.0.tgz
→ 302 https://registry.npmjs.com/camera-rpv-client/-/camera-rpv-client-1.33.0.tgz
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ scope prefix missing
The unscoped URL either serves stale CDN content (a different package) or returns 404. Either way,
the content does not match the SHA-512 in the lockfile.
Part 2 — Bun bug (#26341): When the isolated linker receives
a download response that fails its SHA-512 check, it silently deadlocks rather than reporting an
error and exiting. The install process produces no output and must be killed externally.

Reproduction

Add a private npm.pkg.github.com scoped package to a Bun workspace
Run bun install in a clean Linux environment (cold cache)

Zero Extract or Hardlink log entries for those packages (every other package has both)
Hang occurs after the last lifecycle script, with no error output

non-default registries uses / as the scope separator — not +:

title: os.cpus() crashes on Linux with non-contiguous CPU numbering (EPYC 7713)
excerpt:
Bug: os.cpus() crashes with ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR on systems with non-contiguous CPU numbering
Environment

Bun version: 1.3.11
OS: Linux 6.x
CPU: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor (2 sockets, 128 logical CPUs)
CPU numbering: Non-contiguous — /proc/cpuinfo processor fields are 0-63, 128-191

Reproduction
import os from "node:os";
console.log(os.cpus());
Expected: Array of 128 CPU objects with model, speed, times.
Actual: Error [ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR]: os.cpus() failed
Root Cause
The bug is in src/bun.js/node/node_os.zig, function cpusImplLinux. The function performs two separate passes over two different kernel files, and the indexing assumptions break on non-contiguous CPU topologies:
Pass 1 reads /proc/stat to count CPUs and build the return array:

Enumerates cpu0, cpu1, … cpu191 (128 entries due to non-contiguous numbering)
Stores them at sequential array indices 0..127
num_cpus = 128

Pass 2 reads /proc/cpuinfo to populate model names:

Parses processor\t: 128 → cpu_index = 128
Uses cpu_index directly as an array index: values.getIndex(globalThis, cpu_index)
Guard if (cpu_index >= num_cpus) return error.too_may_cpus; triggers: 128 >= 128 → crash

Evidence
$ grep -c \"^processor\" /proc/cpuinfo
128
$ grep \"^processor\" /proc/cpuinfo | head -3
processor	: 0
processor	: 1
processor	: 2
$ grep \"^processor\" /proc/cpuinfo | tail -3
processor	: 190
processor	: 191

/proc/stat shows the same non-contiguous pattern:
$ grep \"^cpu\" /proc/stat | head -3
cpu  ...
cpu0 ...
cpu1 ...
$ grep \"^cpu\" /proc/stat | tail -3
cpu190 ...
cpu191 ...

Sysfs (/sys/devices/system/cpu/) also uses the same non-contiguous naming: cpu0, cpu1, … cpu63, cpu128, … cpu191.
The code even has a self-aware comment acknowledging this uncertainty:
// NOTE: libuv assumes this is fixed on Linux, not sure that's actually the case
Affected Code
File: src/bun.js/node/node_os.zig
Function: cpusImplLinux
Problematic lines:

/proc/cpuinfo parsing (model name):

cpu_index = try std.fmt.parseInt(u32, digits, 10);
if (cpu_index >= num_cpus) return error.too_may_cpus;  // ← CRASH HERE
// ...
const cpu = try values.getIndex(globalThis, cpu_index);  // ← uses raw index

/sysfs frequency loop:

title: SIGILL (libpas) in CloneSerializer under Worker.postMessage with large object payload — reproduces on 1.3.12 and 1.3.13
excerpt:
How can we reproduce the crash?
Summary
Worker.postMessage with a large structured-cloneable object graph (~13 MB of strings in an array) can SIGILL the process with a decoded stack in WebCore::CloneSerializer::serialize hitting pas_allocation_result_crash_on_error / pas_allocation_result_zero inside libpas. Reproduces on Bun 1.3.13 and 1.3.12 with very similar stacks — not specific to the WebKit bump in #29294.
Running with all JIT tiers disabled (BUN_JSC_useJIT=0) did not prevent the crash — the fault is in the structured-clone allocator path called from the LLInt interpreter, not in JIT-generated code. Switching the worker reply to postMessage(JSON.stringify(reply)) (zero-copy string fast-path introduced in 1.2.21) eliminates the crash entirely — the string fast path bypasses CloneSerializer.
Versions

Bun 1.3.13 (bf2e2cecf27e800962b1e7f03d66278f9d5d2e79) on Linux x64 baseline
Bun 1.3.12 (700fc117a2fd01ac0201deaa6fa69c5557acb04f) on Linux x64 baseline
Host: 8 vCPU / 32 GB (AMD EPYC Milan), Linux 6.6, glibc 2.41, COS container

Workload
A long-running HTTP server with several new Worker(entryPath, {env}) threads. One worker builds an in-memory index (~58k records) and, on query, replies via self.postMessage(replyObject). Reply object is roughly:
{ type: 'person.query', __rid: '...', ids: string[] }  // ids.length ≈ 150-300k strings, ~40 chars each, total ≈ 13 MB serialized
Crash fires on the FIRST broad query after prime completes. Peak RSS at the crash is ~14 GB on a 33 GB machine (~42% of capacity — well under host OOM), so this is allocator-internal, not host-OOM.
Interpretation
Both crashes are libpas raising SIGILL via ud2 from a pas_allocation_result_* failure path during CloneSerializer:

On 1.3.13 the allocator fails while growing the structured-clone buffer (WTF::Vector<unsigned char> → FastMalloc::malloc) while writing UTF-16 code units.
On 1.3.12 the allocator fails while rehashing the identifier-dedup HashMap<UniquedStringImpl, unsigned int> inside CloneSerializer::dumpString.

Determinism at the same PC on 1.3.12 (3/3 runs) and the absence of any JIT frames support this being allocator-internal rather than a miscompile. pas_allocation_result_crash_on_error is the documented libpas failure policy — it intentionally emits ud2 to kill the process with a recognizable crash site (see WebKit bug 236164).
