### What is the expected behavior?

`bun-bug` should resolve `vite` to the tarball (`@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core`), the same way:

- **npm** and **pnpm** resolve it to `@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@0.2.1`, and
- **`bun-control`** resolves `vite` to its `vite@5.4.0` tarball.

`bun-control` vs `bun-bug` are identical except for the tarball's internal `name`, so neither the version range nor "it's a URL dependency" is the deciding

title: `Bun.Archive`: support per-entry file modes when creating archives
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`Bun.Archive` hardcodes `0644` for every entry when creating an archive ([Archive.rs](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/runtime/api/Archive.rs): `entry_ref.set_perm(0o644)`). There is no way to mark a file as executable.

This makes it unusable for building npm tarballs that ship precompiled binaries (esbuild-style platform packages): the binary must carry `0755` inside the tarball, since npm only chmods files listed in the manifest's `bin` field. Today we have to keep `node-tar` as a dependency just because it preserves file modes.

Note extraction already preserves modes — creation is the only gap.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

A way to set the mode per entry, e.g.:

```ts
new Bun.Archive({
  "bin/mytool": { data: bytes, mode: 0o755 },
  "README.md": "hello",
});
```

### What alternatives have you considered?

- `node-tar` (works, but defeats the point of a native API)
- chmod after extraction — doesn't help; consumers are npm clients extracting the tarball, not our code

title: prerender writes style count instead of stylesheet string length into index.rsc header
excerpt:
## Summary

In the static `prerender` path, the RSC payload header written to `index.rsc` encodes the wrong value. It should encode the byte length of the joined stylesheet string (matching the live `render()` path), but instead encodes the number of style entries.

## Location

- File: `src/runtime/bake/bun-framework-react/server.tsx`
- Function: `prerender`
- Related (correct) pattern is in `render()`, which does:
  ```ts
  const int = Buffer.allocUnsafe(4);
  const str = meta.styles.join("\n");
  int.writeUInt32LE(str.length, 0);
  ```
- `prerender` currently does:
  ```ts
  const int = new Uint32Array(1);
  int[0] = meta.styles.length;
  let rscChunks: Array<BlobPart> = [int.buffer as ArrayBuffer, meta.styles.join("\n")];
  ```

## Rationale

Client-side navigation reads this header from the RSC payload to determine how many bytes of the response correspond to CSS metadata (the joined stylesheet string), so it can skip past them before parsing the RSC stream. Writing `meta.styles.length` (the count of style URLs) instead of the byte length of the joined string means the header value will mismatch the actual serialized string length whenever styles exist, corrupting the boundary and breaking parsing of the static `index.rsc` payload during client-side navigation.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the `render()` implementation in `prerender`:
```ts
const int = Buffer.allocUnsafe(4);
const styles = meta.styles.join("\n");
int.writeUInt32LE(styles.length, 0);
let rscChunks: Array<BlobPart> = [int, styles];
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `prerender`'s RSC header encodes the byte length of the joined stylesheet string, consistent with `render()`.
- A regression test is added that builds a static route with one or more styles and verifies the `index.rsc` header/CSS-metadata length matches the actual joined stylesheet string length, and that client-side navigation can correctly parse it.

## References

- PR: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/33216
- Discussion: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/33216#discussion_r3509659835
- Reported by: @robobun

title: prerender writes style count instead of stylesheet string length into index.rsc header
excerpt:
## Summary

In the static `prerender` path, the RSC payload header written to `index.rsc` encodes the wrong value. It should encode the byte length of the joined stylesheet string (matching the live `render()` path), but instead encodes the number of style entries.

## Location

- File: `src/runtime/bake/bun-framework-react/server.tsx`
- Function: `prerender`
- Related (correct) pattern is in `render()`, which does:
  ```ts
  const int = Buffer.allocUnsafe(4);
  const str = meta.styles.join("\n");
  int.writeUInt32LE(str.length, 0);
  ```
- `prerender` currently does:
  ```ts
  const int = new Uint32Array(1);
  int[0] = meta.styles.length;
  let rscChunks: Array<BlobPart> = [int.buffer as ArrayBuffer, meta.styles.join("\n")];
  ```

## Rationale

Client-side navigation reads this header from the RSC payload to determine how many bytes of the response correspond to CSS metadata (the joined stylesheet string), so it can skip past them before parsing the RSC stream. Writing `meta.styles.length` (the count of style URLs) instead of the byte length of the joined string means the header value will mismatch the actual serialized string length whenever styles exist, corrupting the boundary and breaking parsing of the static `index.rsc` payload during client-side navigation.

## Suggested fix

Mirror the `render()` implementation in `prerender`:
```ts
const int = Buffer.allocUnsafe(4);
const styles = meta.styles.join("\n");
int.writeUInt32LE(styles.length, 0);
let rscChunks: Array<BlobPart> = [int, styles];
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `prerender`'s RSC header encodes the byte length of the joined stylesheet string, consistent with `render()`.
- A regression test is added that builds a static route with one or more styles and verifies the `index.rsc` header/CSS-metadata length matches the actual joined stylesheet string length, and that client-side navigation can correctly parse it.

Bun Shell: no way to give spawned commands a TTY (stdout/stderr are always pipes) — support `terminal` like Bun.spawn
excerpt:
### What is the problem?

I'm building an interactive shell whose executor is Bun Shell — every line the user types is run through `` $`${{ raw: line }}` ``. It works surprisingly well, except Bun Shell never gives the spawned commands a terminal:

```ts
// run this from a real terminal
await Bun.$`python3 -c "import sys;print(sys.stdin.isatty(),sys.stdout.isatty(),sys.stderr.isatty())"`;
// -> True False False
```

stdin is the parent's tty, but stdout/stderr are always pipes that Bun relays to the parent's stdout. So anything that checks `isatty(1)` degrades: `ls`/`git` turn colors off, pagers behave like `cat`, and full-screen programs (`vim`, `less`, `htop`) can't run. There's also no escape hatch on `ShellPromise`:

```ts
Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(Bun.$`true`))
// constructor cwd env quiet nothrow throws text json lines arrayBuffer bytes blob run then
```

### What did you expect?

Now that `Bun.spawn` supports `terminal: TerminalOptions | Terminal` (PTY on all three fds, `isTTY === true`), it would be great if Bun Shell could attach one too, e.g.

```ts
await using term = new Bun.Terminal({ cols, rows, data: (t, d) => process.stdout.write(d) });
await Bun.$`${{ raw: line }}`.terminal(term);
```

or an option to inherit the parent's stdio for the commands it spawns.

Today the closest workaround is to spawn a whole interpreter per line — `Bun.spawn(["bun", "exec", line], { terminal })` — which does give the commands a real PTY but costs an extra process and loses `$`'s in-process cwd/env handling.

Bun v1.3.14, macOS arm64.

title: Bun Shell: multiple parse errors are concatenated without separators in ShellError.message
Bun.Terminal: spawned child's controlling terminal is not the PTY (no setsid/TIOCSCTTY) — ^C never signals, /dev/tty points at the parent's tty
excerpt:
### What is the problem?

`Bun.spawn({ terminal })` connects the child's stdio to the new PTY, but it doesn't make that PTY the child's *controlling terminal* (no `setsid()` + `TIOCSCTTY` on the slave, the way `forkpty(3)`/node-pty do). Two consequences:

1. The PTY's line discipline has no foreground process group to signal, so writing `^C` (0x03) into the terminal never delivers a `SIGINT` — you can't interrupt anything you spawn on a `Bun.Terminal`.
2. `/dev/tty` inside the child still resolves to the *parent's* terminal (or nothing), so programs that talk to their controlling tty directly (password prompts, `less`, `tput`) reach the wrong one.

Repro (run from a terminal):

```ts
const term = new Bun.Terminal({ cols: 80, rows: 24, data: (_t, d) => process.stdout.write(d) });

const proc = Bun.spawn(["sh", "-c", 'ps -o pid,pgid,sess,tty,command -p "$$"; sleep 500; echo SURVIVED'], {
  terminal: term,
});

setTimeout(() => term.write("\x03"), 500); // ^C into the PTY (slave has ISIG on)

console.log(await Promise.race([
  proc.exited,
  new Promise((r) => setTimeout(() => r("child still alive 3s after ^C"), 3000)),
]));
```

Output on my machine (parent is on `ttys029`):

```
  PID  PGID   SESS TTY      COMMAND
45278 45277      0 ttys029  sh -c ps -o pid,pgid,sess,tty,command -p "$$"; sleep 500; ...
^C
child still alive 3s after ^C
```

The child's `TTY` is the parent's terminal, not the new PTY, and the `^C` is just echoed.

### What did you expect?

The same as `forkpty()`: the child starts a new session with the PTY slave as its controlling terminal, so

- `term.write("\x03")` → `SIGINT` to the PTY's foreground process group (the `sleep` dies, `proc.exited` resolves ~130), and
- `open("/dev/tty")` in the child gives the PTY.

Without this, anything shell- or terminal-emulator-shaped built on `Bun.Terminal` has to reimplement the line discipline's signal generation in userspace (watch for 0x03/0x1c/0x1a in the input stream, check `term.localFlags & ISIG`, signal the process tree manually), which is what I'm doing today.

Ran into this building an interactive shell on Bun Shell + `Bun.Terminal`; related to #33234.

Bun v1.3.14, macOS arm64.

title: event loop: never re-enter from inside a dispatch callback (de-block expect().resolves and HTMLRewriter.transform, then assert)
excerpt:
## Invariant

**The event loop must never be re-entered from inside a poll-dispatch callback.**

`waitForPromise` ("run the event loop until this promise settles") is legitimate only where a synchronous outer context is *inherent* — the module pipeline and top-level drivers, which run when no dispatch is in flight:

- entry-point module-graph evaluation (`bun file.ts`): ES-module evaluation is async by spec, so the synchronous entry must pump until it settles
- macro loading/evaluation inside the transpiler
- the REPL / CLI drivers

Every other caller is a synchronous API signature sitting on an asynchronous operation, reachable from inside I/O completion callbacks. Re-entering the loop there is what makes bugs like the one root-caused in #32233 possible: a nested `epoll_wait`/`kevent` overwrites the shared `ready_polls` batch mid-iteration, and any not-yet-dispatched one-shot entries (subprocess pipe readers, process watchers) are lost forever — the owner hangs.

#32233 contained a correct, minimal, well-tested fix that made the *dispatcher* tolerate re-entry. It was closed deliberately (see the closing comment: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/32233#issuecomment-4867373017) because tolerating the state entrenches it: the right end-state is that the state cannot occur, and CI screams if someone reintroduces it.

## What #32233 established (all of this carries over)

- Plain concurrent `Bun.$` **never** hangs by itself: 0/20 (Linux) and 0/8 (macOS) on unfixed builds. The loss requires a `waitForPromise` caller in a continuation of an I/O completion.
- The nested-tick stack was captured live (`gdb`, `loop->data.tick_depth == 2`), with `HTMLRewriter.transform` (async handler) as a pure-runtime trigger: 20/20 hangs unfixed → 0/20 with the (closed) dispatcher fix.
- `require()` is *not* a trigger: an ordinary graph never pumps the loop, and a top-level-await graph is refused with `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`.
- Three deterministic regression tests exist in that PR's branch (`test/js/bun/spawn/pipe-reader-nested-tick.test.ts`): two trigger via bun:test matchers, one via `HTMLRewriter`; victims cover both `Bun.$` and `Bun.spawn` pipes.

## Caller inventory (from `waitForPromise` / `tickWhilePaused` call sites)

| caller | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| entry-point / module-graph evaluation (`VirtualMachine`) | **keep** (top-level by construction) |
| macro load + eval (transpiler) | **keep** (module pipeline) |
| REPL / CLI drivers | **keep** (top-level) |
| bun:tes

title: `fetch` stalls ~70 s on advertised-but-unroutable IPv6: connect attempts are not family-interleaved (RFC 8305), and `dns.setDefaultResultOrder` has no effect on `fetch`
excerpt:
_Disclosure: Researched and posted by Claude Fable 5_

### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 (macOS, Apple Silicon)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Environment: a network that *advertises* global IPv6 (router announces a prefix, interfaces get `2003:…` addresses) but cannot actually route v6 upstream — common with partial ISP/router misconfiguration. `curl -6 https://oauth2.googleapis.com/` fails; `curl -4` works in 0.1 s.

```js
// bun run repro.js — cold process, first connection
const t = Date.now();
await fetch("https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/", { method: "HEAD" });
console.log(Date.now() - t, "ms");
```

Result: **70 840 ms**. (Second request in the same process: 138 ms — pooled.)

This host matters because it resolves to exactly **four AAAA records before any A records**:

```js
await require("node:dns").promises.lookup("aiplatform.googleapis.com", { all: true })
// [ 4 × family 6, then several × family 4 ]  (RFC 3484 order on macOS)
```

Attempting the documented Node escape hatch has no effect on fetch:

```js
require("node:dns").setDefaultResultOrder("ipv4first");
const t = Date.now();
await fetch("https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/", { method: "HEAD" });
console.log(Date.now() - t, "ms");   // 75 709 ms — unchanged
```

Same machine, same host: `node -e 'fetch(...)'` completes in **1 288 ms** (Happy Eyeballs), `curl` in ~0.1 s.

### What is the expected behavior?

Either of:

1. Connect attempts interleave address families per RFC 8305 (Happy Eyeballs v2 §4 explicitly requires alternating families in the attempt list), so a batch of dead same-family addresses cannot monopolize all attempts; and/or
2. `dns.setDefaultResultOrder("ipv4first")` influences fetch's resolution order.

### What do you see instead?

A cold fetch stalls for the full OS connect timeout (~70 s) before succeeding, on any network with advertised-but-unroutable IPv6.

### Root cause (from source, main @ 1498d7b77a)

Reading the source, this appears to be two independent gaps that combine:

1. **`setDefaultResultOrder` is a JS-shim variable that fetch never consults.** `src/js/node/dns.ts` stores the order in `defaultResultOrder.value` (L89–92) and its only consumer is `dns.lookup()` option defaulting in the same file (L248, applied L314). fetch resolves through the native path (`dns::getaddrinfo` → uSockets), so the setting is structurally invisible to it — same family as #28817 (NODE_OPTIONS flavor).

2

title: Detect unsettled top-level await and exit like Node (exit 13 + warning)
excerpt:
Split out from #14951, which was closed for its CPU-spin half (fixed by #32014: condition-gated drive loops now ref the event loop and park instead of busy-spinning).

The other half remains: when a module's top-level await never settles and nothing else refs the event loop, Node prints a warning and exits 13:

```console
$ node -e 'await new Promise(() => {})'
Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await at [eval]:1
await new Promise(() => {})
^
$ echo $?
13
```

Bun's `wait_for_promise` refs the loop for the duration of the wait, so it waits for any pending unref'd timer and otherwise parks indefinitely rather than exiting. Verified against Node 26.3/26.4.

Implementing this means detecting "the module promise is pending and nothing other than this driver refs the loop", emitting the warning at the awaiting source location, and exiting 13. Two tests in `test/js/web/timers/timers-unref-idle-loop.test.ts` carry `TODO`s pointing here and assert today's divergent behavior (exit 0, no warning); they should be flipped as part of the fix.

Related: #31501 (closed as a duplicate of #14951).

title: VirtualMachine::event_loop_handle is read from producer threads without synchronization (wakeup path)
excerpt:
### What

`VirtualMachine::event_loop_handle` is a plain, non-atomic `Option<*mut PlatformEventLoop>` (src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs:181) that is read from non-JS threads on the cross-thread enqueue path, while the JS thread may concurrently rewrite it.

Read path (POSIX):

```
EventLoop::enqueue_task_concurrent(&self, task)   // called from producer threads
  -> self.wakeup()                                 // src/jsc/event_loop.rs:1003
     -> self.vm_ref().platform_loop_opt()          // src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs:1144
        -> self.event_loop_handle.map(|h| unsafe { &mut *h })   // plain, non-atomic read
```

Write path (JS thread): `ensure_waker()` (event_loop.rs) and the `spawnSync` prepare/cleanup swap (`__bun_spawn_sync_vm_set_event_loop_handle`).

So a producer thread (HTTP client, work pool, waiter thread) can read the field while the JS thread writes it. `platform_loop_opt()`'s own SAFETY comment states "only the owning JS thread reborrows mutably", which that path does not satisfy; it also hands out `&mut PlatformEventLoop` from `&self`, so two producer threads can form aliasing `&mut` to the same loop.

### Impact

Low / practically benign on supported targets, which is why this is filed rather than fixed inline:

- `Option<*mut T>` is niche-optimized to a single machine word, so the read cannot tear.
- `uws::Loop::wakeup()` is a thread-safe eventfd/pipe write.
- Windows does not go through `platform_loop_opt()` in `wakeup()`.

It is still formally UB (unsynchronized read/write of a non-atomic field, plus aliasing `&mut`), and it is the last non-atomic field on a path that was otherwise made atomic (`is_shutting_down` → `AtomicBool`, `event_loop` → `AtomicPtr<EventLoop>`).

### Suggested fix

Make `event_loop_handle` an `AtomicPtr<PlatformEventLoop>` (null = `None`): Release-store in `ensure_waker` / `__bun_spawn_sync_vm_set_event_loop_handle`, Acquire-load in the accessor. Split the accessor in two so the cross-thread `wakeup()` path takes a shared `Option<&PlatformEventLoop>` (it needs no `&mut`), leaving the existing `&mut` accessor for the JS-thread-only `tick`/`run`/`update_counts` call sites.

Credit: spotted in review of #32071, where the neighbouring `event_loop`/`is_shutting_down` fields were made atomic for exactly this reason.

title: Case insensitive FormData header throw an incorrect MIME type/boundary
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Parsing formdata request with `multipart/form-data` as case-insensitive throw an error

```ts
const boundary = '----WebKitFormBoundary7MA4YWxkTrZu0gW'
const body = [
	`--${boundary}`,
	'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="x"',
	'',
	'y',
	`--${boundary}--`,
	''
].join('\r\n')

for (const type of [
	'multipart/form-data',
	'MULTIPART/FORM-DATA',
	'Multipart/Form-Data'
]) {
	const request = new Request('http://localhost/', {
		method: 'POST',
		headers: { 'content-type': `${type}; boundary=${boundary}` },
		body
	})

	try {
		const form = await request.formData()
		console.log(`${type.padEnd(20)} → OK, x =`, form.get('x'))
	} catch (error) {
		console.log(`${type.padEnd(20)} → THREW:`, error.message)
	}
}
```

This code work in Node and browser console but in Bun case, only `multipart/form-data` (all lower case) is supported, the rest are not

As per [RFC 2045 section 5.1](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2045.txt) content-type value should be case-insensitive
```
5.1.  Syntax of the `Content-Type` header field should be case-insensitive

   In the Augmented BNF notation of RFC 822, a Content-Type header field
   value is defined as follows:

     content := "Content-Type" ":" type "/" subtype
                *(";" parameter)
                ; Matching of media type and subtype
                ; is ALWAYS case-insensitive.
```

This means the behavior is incorrect and is different from Node.js

### What is the expected behavior?

It doesn't throw an error
```
multipart/form-data  → OK, x = y
VM79:24 MULTIPART/FORM-DATA  → OK, x = y
VM79:24 Multipart/Form-Data  → OK, x = y
```

### What do you see instead?

```
multipart/form-data  → OK, x = y
MULTIPART/FORM-DATA  → THREW: Can't decode form data from body because of incorrect MIME type/boundary
Multipart/Form-Data  → THREW: Can't decode form data from body because of incorrect MIME type/boundary
```

### Additional information

_No response_

title: Feat: HTTP/URL/CDN imports
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Running portable, ephemeral, single-file scripts in Bun currently requires local setup. 

If a script relies on external npm dependencies, the developer is forced to initialize a `package.json` and run `bun install` (creating a local `node_modules` directory), or globally install packages. This creates friction when sharing simple helper scripts with teammates, pollutes the working directory with lockfiles and module folders, and leaves a permanent footprint on disk. 

Furthermore, in ephemeral environments like CI/CD runners, containerized serverless functions, or secure systems, developers often need to execute a script once and leave absolutely no cached dependencies behind. 

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

I propose adding native support for direct URL imports, piped input execution, and an optional ephemeral flag to bypass caching:

1. **Native URL & `npm:` Imports**: Allow Bun's runtime to directly resolve dependencies from HTTP URLs or the npm registry on-the-fly without needing a local config (e.g., `import chalk from "npm:chalk"` or ESM CDNs).
2. **Stdin/Pipe Execution**: Allow Bun to read and run arbitrary code directly from standard input (e.g., `cat script.js | bun run -`).
3. **An Ephemeral Flag (`--no-cache` / `--ephemeral`)**: Introduce an optional flag that instructs Bun to fetch the targeted CDN/npm dependencies strictly in memory (or to a temporary system folder that is wiped immediately upon process exit) otherwise they're resolved in global bun cache folder. 

This would enable developers to execute highly portable, fast scripts in a single command, like so:
```bash
cat << 'EOF' | bun run --ephemeral -
import chalk from "npm:chalk";

const res = await fetch("https://api.github.com/repos/oven-sh/bun");
const data = await res.json();

console.log(chalk.cyan.bold("Bun Repository Stats:"));
console.log(chalk.green("⭐ Stars: ") + chalk.bold(data.stargazers_count));
console.log(chalk.yellow("🍴 Forks: ") + chalk.bold(data.forks_count));
EOF
```

### What alternatives have you considered?

**Deno**: Deno currently handles this natively using its system-wide global cache combined with the `--node-modules-dir=none` flag.

title: [Windows] require() with forward-slash absolute path and no extension yields wrong __dirname in child module
CSS: lab() colors compile to the wrong sRGB fallback
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0 (reproduces on `main`)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`lab(29.568% 68.287 -112.029)` is sRGB blue, `#0000ff`. Bundling it emits `#002cea` as the sRGB fallback:

```console
$ cat lab.css
a { color: lab(29.568% 68.287 -112.029); }   /* #0000ff */
b { color: lab(54.29% 80.8 69.89); }         /* #ff0000 */

$ bun build lab.css --minify
a{color:#002cea;color:color(display-p3 .00000346541 -.00000245467 .95958);color:lab(29.568% 68.287 -112.029)}
b{color:red;color:color(display-p3 .917461 .200324 .138557);color:lab(54.29% 80.8 69.89)}
```

So a browser that falls back to the hex renders blue as a washed-out `#002cea`. The `display-p3` fallback on the same declaration is correct, which narrows this to the lab → sRGB path specifically.

`Bun.color` goes through the same conversion:

```console
$ bun -e 'console.log(Bun.color("lab(29.568% 68.287 -112.029)", "hex"))'
#002cea
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`#0000ff`, to within rounding.

### What do you see instead?

`#002cea`. Worst channel error across a sweep of 4096 colors is **44/255**; 15 of them are wrong, all saturated blues.

### Additional information

The **forward** direction is exact. `Bun.color(hex, "lab")` matches the CIELAB D50 reference values to four decimal places:

| color | Bun | reference (D50) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#ff0000` | `lab(54.290546% 80.80492 69.89099)` | L 54.29, a 80.80, b 69.89 |
| `#00ff00` | `lab(87.81854% -79.27111 80.994606)` | L 87.82, a -79.27, b 80.99 |
| `#0000ff` | `lab(29.5683% 68.287384 -112.02972)` | L 29.568, a 68.287, b -112.029 |

So sRGB → Lab is right and Lab → sRGB is wrong. Feeding the exactly-correct Lab for blue back in returns `#002cea`, which means the inverse is not the inverse.

Reds and greens round-trip fine, so it looks like something in the inverse transform goes wrong only where the conversion has to clamp or where `b*` is strongly negative.

Found by a round-trip property test added in #33328; there is a `test.failing` in `test/js/bun/css/color.test.ts` pinned to this, which will start reporting once the conversion is fixed.

AVIF encoding fails on Windows 11 with ERR_IMAGE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED despite HEIF and AV1 extensions being installed
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

Bun 1.3.14+0d9b296af

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Environment:

- Bun: 1.3.14+0d9b296af
- Windows: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64 (Windows 11 26H2)
- HEIF Image Extension installed (v1.2.36.0)
- AV1 Video Extension installed (v2.0.7.0)

The following code throws an error:

```ts
import { Image } from "bun";

const thumb = await new Image("photo.png")
  .resize(400, 400, {
    fit: "inside",
    withoutEnlargement: true,
  })
  .avif({ quality: 80 })
  .bytes();

await Bun.write("photo.avif", thumb);
```

Error:

```
Image: format not supported on this machine (HEIC/AVIF/TIFF require the OS codec; AVIF encode needs an AV1 encoder)
code: "ERR_IMAGE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED"
```

Windows Photos can successfully open existing `.avif` images, so AVIF decoding is working.

### What is the expected behavior?

Since the required Windows codecs are installed (HEIF Image Extension and AV1 Video Extension), AVIF encoding should succeed and produce a valid `photo.avif` file.

### What do you see instead?

Bun throws:

```
Image: format not supported on this machine (HEIC/AVIF/TIFF require the OS codec; AVIF encode needs an AV1 encoder)
code: "ERR_IMAGE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED"
```

No AVIF file is produced.

### Additional information

- Bun version: `1.3.14+0d9b296af`
- Windows: `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64`
- HEIF Image Extension: `1.2.36.0`
- AV1 Video Extension: `2.0.7.0`

I verified that:

- Windows Photos can open AVIF images.
- HEIF Image Extension is installed.
- AV1 Video Extension is installed.
- The error occurs consistently.

Is Bun expecting an AV1 encoder that is not provided by the standard Microsoft AV1 Video Extension on Windows, or is this a bug in the Windows image backend?

title: Segfault (null deref, address 0x0) in JSC::MarkedBlock::Handle::sweep during TCPSocket upgradeTLS — Bun v1.4.0, running inside Claude Code
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0 (commit 63bb0ca)

### What platform is your computer?

WSL2 Ubuntu, Windows 11, x86_64. Running as the embedded Bun runtime inside Claude Code (standalone executable), versions 2.1.198 through 2.1.201 — the crash reproduced across all of these.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

I don't have a minimal JS reproduction — this happens inside Claude Code's bundled standalone executable, so I can't isolate the exact call site in user-land code. However, it reproduced **10+ times over a single session**, with no obvious user action correlating to each crash (not tied to any specific command; one instance coincided with `claude --resume <session-id>`, but the other 9 occurred during ordinary use with no `--resume`).

I captured one crash live via `script` to preserve the Bun crash reporter output, which produced this crash report URL:

https://bun.report/1.4.0/B_163bb0camgggkEuhogDs5n/1Egz9r6C6ons6Cui880E8jt80EojkysE8l3xsE4lmpgDk38stDu9zw6Co65qtD_uwwn6Bms3/5Bi3vh2E2uih2E6h0h5Ewpuq7E45i8lD_A2AA

## Crash summary

```
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x0
```

The decoded stack trace shows the fault occurring inside `JSLock.cpp:55` (`RefPtr<JSC::VM>::refIfNotNull` dereferencing a null `VM*`), reached via:

```
JSC::LocalAllocator::allocateSlowCase
  → JSC::MarkedBlock::Handle::sweep
    → (GC sweep triggered during allocation of a new JSTLSSocket cell,
       via JSCellInlines.h / JSC::allocateCell)
    → concurrently, a TCP socket's Rust-side Handlers object is being
      dropped (bun_runtime::socket::Handlers::drop → Bun__JSValue__unprotect)
      as part of TCPSocketPrototype__upgradeTLS
  → RefPtr<JSC::VM>::RefPtr → refIfNotNull → JSLock.cpp:55  [CRASH: null deref]
```

This looks like a race/use-after-free between the JSC garbage collector's mark-and-sweep pass and the Rust-side socket `Handlers::drop` cleanup that happens as part of upgrading a plain TCP socket to TLS (`socket.upgradeTLS()`). The GC sweep, triggered while allocating a new `JSTLSSocket` object for the upgraded connection, appears to encounter a socket handler object whose backing `VM*` has already been invalidated/freed by the concurrent Rust drop, leading to a null pointer dereference.

This may be related to (or share a root cause with) **#24357 "SegFault running Claude Code"**, which shows a very similar crash shape:

title: fs.realpathSync converts backslash to slash on Linux, throws ENOENT for existing paths
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14+0d9b296af — also reproduced on canary 1.4.0-canary.1+d37f52067

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// repro-backslash.js
const fs = require("fs");
const dir = "/tmp/back\\slash";  // one literal backslash in the name
fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
console.log("existsSync:  ", fs.existsSync(dir));
console.log("lstatSync:   ", fs.lstatSync(dir).isDirectory());
console.log("realpathSync:", fs.realpathSync(dir));
```

```console
$ bun repro-backslash.js
existsSync:   true
lstatSync:    true
ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/tmp/back\slash'
```

`fs.realpathSync.native` fails identically. Node v22 prints `/tmp/back\slash`
as expected.

### What is the expected behavior?

On POSIX, `\` is an ordinary filename character. `realpathSync` should resolve
the path exactly as `existsSync`/`lstatSync` already do (both return true for
this directory in the same process).

### What actually happened?

strace shows realpath rewrites the backslash to a forward slash before
touching the filesystem, then opens the wrong path:

```console
$ strace -f -e trace=%file bun repro-backslash.js 2>&1 | grep '/tmp/back'
mkdir("/tmp/back\\slash", 0777)            = -1 EEXIST (File exists)
newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/back\\slash", {st_mode=S_IFDIR|0755, ...}, 0) = 0
access("/tmp/back\\slash", F_OK)           = 0
statx(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/back\\slash", ...)   = 0
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/back/slash", O_RDONLY|O_PATH) = -1 ENOENT
```

Every other fs call passes the backslash through byte-perfect; only realpath's
resolver applies the (Windows-only) `\` → `/` normalization. Two smaller
inaccuracies in the resulting error object: `syscall` is reported as `"lstat"`
(the failing syscall is `openat`), and `path` is the original input, which
makes the error look impossible next to a successful `lstatSync` of the same
string.

`path.normalize` / `path.resolve` / `path.join` are all correct (backslash
preserved), so the stray normalization is specific to the realpath
implementation.

### Real-world impact

Claude Code (a Bun single-file executable) realpath-validates its working
directory at startup, so it cannot launch in any directory whose absolute
path contains a backslash:

```console
$ mkdir 'a\b' && cd 'a\b' && claude
Error: Can't access working directory /home/user/a\b: Path "/home/user/a\b" does not exist
```

title: bun install: applying a patch that adds files in a new (non-existent) directory fails with "EACCES: Permission denied (mkdir())" — still reproduces on 1.4.0
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0-canary.1+4ca9ebc80

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Self-contained repro — any registry package plus a patch that adds a file inside a directory that does **not** exist in the published package:

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro

cat > package.json <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "is-odd": "3.0.1" },
  "patchedDependencies": { "is-odd@3.0.1": "patches/is-odd.patch" }
}
EOF

mkdir patches
cat > patches/is-odd.patch <<'EOF'
diff --git a/android/build/x/results.bin b/android/build/x/results.bin
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/android/build/x/results.bin
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+hi
EOF

bun install
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The patch applies and `node_modules/is-odd/android/build/x/results.bin` exists.

### What do you see instead?

```
bun install v1.4.0-canary.1 (4ca9ebc80)
Resolving dependencies
Resolved, downloaded and extracted [2]
error: failed applying patch file: EACCES: Permission denied (mkdir())
error: failed to apply patchfile (patches/is-odd.patch)
```

### Additional information

I hit this in a real React Native project with 6 patches in `patchedDependencies`. Only some of them failed, which made it possible to isolate the exact trigger. Each patch was then tested in an isolated project with a clean install. Findings:

**The sole trigger is "the patch must create a directory".** Tested variants (each after `rm -rf ~/.bun/install/cache/is-odd* node_modules bun.lock; bun install`):

| Patch does | Result |
|---|---|
| Modify an existing file | ✅ installs OK |
| Add a new file into a directory that already **exists** in the published package (incl. package root) | ✅ installs OK |
| Add a new file into a **new 1-level** directory (`newdir/f.txt`) | ❌ `EACCES: Permission denied (open())` |
| Add a new file into a **new nested** directory (`android/build/x/results.bin`) | ❌ `EACCES: Permission denied (mkdir())` |

Results from the real project's 6 patches, each tested in isolation, match this exactly: 4 patches that only modify existing files or add files into existing directories all pass; the 2 patches that add files under directories absent from the published package (`android/build/**`, `android/.cxx/**`) both fail.

**Ruled out:**

- Not a local filesystem-permission problem: reproduced on a brand-new, clean, user-owned cache (`~/.bun/install/cache`, mode 755) with a writable cwd.
- Di

title: subprocess.channel is an empty Control stub (missing ref/unref/refCounted/unrefCounted) — breaks execa's execaNode()
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (also confirmed against current `main` sources, see below)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

IPC message passing itself works, but the `Control` object exposed as `subprocess.channel` / `process.channel` is missing its methods. No dependencies needed:

```js
// child.mjs
console.log('hello from child');
```

```js
// inspect.mjs
import { fork } from 'node:child_process';
const child = fork('./child.mjs');
console.log('refCounted:', typeof child.channel.refCounted);
console.log('unrefCounted:', typeof child.channel.unrefCounted);
console.log('ref:', typeof child.channel.ref);
console.log('unref:', typeof child.channel.unref);
child.on('exit', () => process.exit(0));
```

```console
$ bun inspect.mjs
refCounted: undefined
unrefCounted: undefined
ref: undefined
unref: undefined

$ node inspect.mjs
refCounted: function
unrefCounted: function
ref: function
unref: function
```

The child side is asymmetric: `process.channel` inside a forked child **does** have `ref`/`unref`, but is still missing `refCounted`/`unrefCounted`:

| method | Node (both sides) | Bun parent `subprocess.channel` | Bun child `process.channel` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ref()` | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| `unref()` | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| `refCounted()` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| `unrefCounted()` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |

This matches the current sources:

- Parent side: [`src/js/node/child_process.ts` defines `class Control extends EventEmitter` with an empty body](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/js/node/child_process.ts#L1818-L1822) — no methods at all.
- Child side: [`src/js/builtins/ProcessObjectInternals.ts` implements only `ref()`/`unref()`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/js/builtins/ProcessObjectInternals.ts#L541-L553).

In Node, `subprocess.channel.ref()`/`.unref()` are documented public API, and `refCounted()`/`unrefCounted()` exist on the internal `Control` class ([lib/internal/child_process.js](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/internal/child_process.js)).

### Real-world impact

execa relies on `channel.refCounted()`/`channel.unrefCounted()` for its IPC modes ([lib/ipc/reference.js](https://github.com/sindresorhus/execa/blob/main/lib/ipc/reference.js)), so **every `execaNode()` call fails under Bun** even though the subprocess itself runs fine:

```js

import { execaNode } from 'execa';
const result = await execaNode('./child.mjs');
console.log('child sai

fetch(): an exception thrown during option conversion is a synchronous throw, not a rejected promise
fetch()/WebSocket: passing a URL object as the whole `proxy` option is silently ignored — the request goes DIRECT with no error
excerpt:
## What version of Bun is running?
Current `main`. Long-standing.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?
```js
const origin = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response("FROM_ORIGIN") });
const prox   = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response("FROM_PROXY") });
const target = `http://127.0.0.1:${origin.port}/`;
console.log(await (await fetch(target, { proxy: `http://127.0.0.1:${prox.port}` })).text());   // string
console.log(await (await fetch(target, { proxy: prox.url })).text());                          // URL object
```
Note `Bun.serve().url` is itself a `URL` — `proxy: server.url` is about the most natural spelling.

## What is the expected behavior?
Both lines print `FROM_PROXY`, or the second one throws.

## What do you see instead?
```
FROM_PROXY
FROM_ORIGIN
```
The `URL` object fails the `is_string()` check on the top-level `proxy` value, falls into the `{url, headers}` object branch (`src/runtime/webcore/fetch.rs`, `'extract_proxy`), has no `.url` own property (`URL` exposes `.href`), and is silently ignored — the request goes **direct, un-proxied, with no error and no signal**. That's a silent proxy bypass: swap a working proxy string for the equivalent `URL` and every request quietly egresses outside the corporate/scanning/anonymizing proxy while returning 200s.

`new WebSocket(url, { proxy: new URL(p) })` has the identical shape and identical silent bypass in `src/jsc/bindings/webcore/JSWebSocket.cpp` (`isString()` → object branch → no `url` prop → no proxy).

## Additional information
This is deliberately **not** folded into the `proxy: { url: URL }` fix (#29103) because a naive "route url-less objects through the URL parser" fix would break a separate, intentional, issue-numbered contract: a *plain* object without a `url` property must be **ignored**, per #25413 and its explicit tests (`test/js/bun/http/proxy.test.ts`, "proxy object without url is ignored"). A correct fix must distinguish "a real `URL` instance" from "an object without `url`" (e.g. a `jsDynamicCast`-style instance check), route the former through the existing `href_from_js` path, and leave the #25413 contract intact — in both `fetch` and `WebSocket`. Given the security-relevant failure mode (silent bypass), failing loud may also be preferable to failing open here.

install: integrity verification keeps only the first digest of the strongest algorithm (ssri any-match)
excerpt:
When a package's `integrity` string carries more than one digest of the same algorithm (legal SSRI, e.g. `sha512-A sha512-B`), `bun install` verifies the tarball against the **first** one only. npm's [`ssri`](https://github.com/npm/ssri) picks the strongest algorithm and then accepts a match on **any** digest of that algorithm (W3C SRI [§3.3.4](https://www.w3.org/TR/SRI/#does-response-match-metadatalist)), so a tarball matching `B` passes npm and hard-fails Bun, and the outcome depends on entry order, which the spec makes irrelevant.

#33072 changed `Integrity::parse` to split a multi-entry SSRI string and keep the strongest algorithm. Before that, a multi-entry string decayed to `Tag::UNKNOWN` and verification was skipped, so #33072 is a strict improvement; it just over-tightens on this one shape. The deviation is noted in that PR's description.

### Why it isn't a one-liner

`Integrity` is a fixed 65-byte value (`tag: u8` + `[u8; 64]`) that lives on disk:

- `src/install/npm.rs` `PackageVersion.integrity` (binary manifest cache)
- `src/install/lockfile/Package/Meta.rs` `Meta.integrity` (lockfile)

All parse sites (`npm.rs`, `bun.lock.rs`, `migration.rs`, `pnpm.rs`, `yarn.rs`) call `Integrity::parse` on the raw string and store the single result; the raw string is discarded. By the time verification runs (`extract_tarball.rs` / `TarballStream.rs` via `integrity::Streaming`), only that single digest is available, so holding a bounded set in `Streaming::init` alone doesn't reach; the extra digests are already gone.

### Scope of a fix

Carry every digest of the strongest algorithm through to verify time. Roughly:

- widen what the manifest cache stores (variable-size, or a small fixed cap) and bump `CacheVersion::CURRENT`
- `Meta.integrity` can stay single-digest for bun.lock (we write the digest that matched), but the migration/package-lock/pnpm/yarn parse paths need the full set until the tarball is verified
- `Streaming`/`verify_by_tag` compare against each
- test: two `sha512-` entries where the tarball matches the second

npm publishes exactly one digest per algorithm, so the trigger is rare (hand-edited lockfiles, third-party registries, or migrated lockfiles that already carry the shape), but the failure mode is a hard integrity error on a tarball npm accepts.

Originated from the `src/install/integrity.rs` review thread on #33072.

### What is the expected behavior?

Either:

1. Bun should preserve the `npm run dev -w app` command and let npm execute the workspace script, producing `workspace-ok`, or
2. Bun should fail clearly if this npm workspace command shape is unsupported.

# ...
# workspace-ok

title: `bun install` misresolves a nested `npm:` alias to a different same-version package (breaks TypeScript 7 / `@typescript/typescript6` coexistence)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.6 (also reproduced on 1.3.14)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (WSL2)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`@typescript/typescript6` is the package Microsoft ships so that tooling needing the TypeScript 6.0 *programmatic* API (e.g. `typescript-eslint`) keeps working while `tsc` is upgraded to the native TypeScript 7 compiler — see the [official TypeScript 7.0 announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/). It is meant to be installed under the name `typescript` via an npm alias. Internally it re-exports the real TS6 through a dependency `@typescript/old` whose spec is `npm:typescript@^6`.

Minimal repro:

```json
// package.json
{
  "name": "alias-of-alias-repro",
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": {
    "typescript": "npm:@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2"
  }
}
```

```sh
bun install
bun -e "const ts=require('typescript'); console.log(ts.version, typeof ts.Extension)"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`require('typescript')` returns the working TS6 API, as it does with npm:

```
$ npm install && node -e "const ts=require('typescript'); console.log(ts.version, typeof ts.Extension)"
6.0.3 object
```

### What do you see instead?

Under bun the module is empty:

```
$ bun install && bun -e "const ts=require('typescript'); console.log(ts.version, typeof ts.Extension)"
undefined undefined
```

### Root cause

`@typescript/typescript6` depends on `@typescript/old` = `npm:typescript@^6` (the real TypeScript 6). bun resolves that dependency to **`@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2` itself** instead of the real `typescript@6`: `@typescript/typescript6` is already hoisted under the name `typescript`, its version `6.0.2` satisfies `^6`, and bun reuses it **despite the package name being different** (`@typescript/typescript6` ≠ `typescript`).

Visible directly in `bun.lock`:

```
"@typescript/old": ["@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2", "", { "dependencies": { "@typescript/old": "npm:typescript@^6" }, "bin": { "tsc6": "bin/tsc6" } }, "sha512-…"],
```

and on disk `node_modules/@typescript/old/package.json` has `"name": "@typescript/typescript6"` (should be `typescript`). So `@typescript/typescript6` ends up `require()`-ing itself through `@typescript/old`, yielding an empty module and a broken TS API. npm resolves `@typescript/old` to the real `typescript@6` and works correctly.

### Additional information

Impact: this blocks the officially-recommended TypeScript 7 coexist

excerpt:
`test/js/web/fetch/fetch-gzip.test.ts` > "followed redirect with a malformed chunked body rejects fetch()" is failing deterministically on every PR build since #33710 landed:

```
error: expect(received).toBe(expected)
Expected: "InvalidHTTPResponse"
Received: "ConnectionRefused"
      at test/js/web/fetch/fetch-gzip.test.ts:521:53
```

The test sets up a server that replies with a 302 redirecting to `http://127.0.0.1:1/unreached` and a malformed chunked body (`ZZ\r\n`, not a valid hex chunk size). It expects `fetch(url, { redirect: "follow" })` to reject with `InvalidHTTPResponse` because the intermediate 302's body is malformed. Instead, the redirect is followed immediately once headers arrive (per #33710's design), so the error is `ConnectionRefused` from port 1. The `redirect: "manual"` branch of the same test is consistent with that behavior.

Repros 5/5 locally on both debug and release builds from current main (65aa83bbaf) with no local changes. Main's own builds are build-only (55 jobs, no test stage), which is why it passed CI there. Hitting every PR build: 71488, 71489, 71490, 71491, 71493 all show it in the error annotations.

Either the test expectation for `redirect:"follow"` needs updating to match the headers-first behavior, or the redirect-follow path needs to consume/validate the intermediate body first.

## Bug

On Windows CI (`windows-latest`, Bun 1.3.14), `Bun.spawnSync(cmd, { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe", timeout })` returned `exitCode: null`, `signalCode` unset, and **empty stdout and stderr**, ~350–450ms after the child process should have started — nowhere near the `timeout` value (20s), for a real `ssh.exe` batch-login child process that authenticates successfully in every other invocation. The equivalent async `Bun.spawn()` + a manual `setTimeout`-based `.kill()` for the exact same command, on the same runner, in the same job, never failed.

## Real-world context (reproduced 3/3, fixed 3/3)

Full write-up with logs: https://github.com/tikoci/quickchr/issues/92

- Failing call (`test/integration/provisioning.test.ts`, before fix):
  ```ts
  const login = Bun.spawnSync(
    ["ssh", "-F", emptyConfig, "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=no",
     "-o", `UserKnownHostsFile=${SSH_NULL_DEVICE}`, "-o", "PasswordAuthentication=no",
     "-o", "IdentitiesOnly=yes", "-o", "BatchMode=yes", "-o", "ConnectTimeout=10",
     "-i", privateKeyPath, `${user}@127.0.0.1`, "-p", String(sshPort),
     ':put "managed-key-login-ok"'],
    { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe", timeout: 20_000 },
  );
  // login.exitCode === null, login.signalCode unset, stdout/stderr both "" — 3/3 runs
  ```

title: TranspilerJob lives inside the VM allocation, so a pool-thread transpile racing worker.terminate() reads freed memory
excerpt:
### What

A `TranspilerJob` that is still on the work pool when its owning worker VM is terminated reads freed memory, because the job itself is stored inside the `VirtualMachine` allocation.

- `RuntimeTranspilerStore.store` is a `HiveArrayFallback<TranspilerJob, 64>` (src/jsc/RuntimeTranspilerStore.rs:394) embedded by value in `VirtualMachine.transpiler_store`; the first 64 slots are an inline array inside the VM allocation (heap-fallback boxes are used only beyond that).
- `TranspilerJob::run()` executes on the work-pool thread and dereferences `(*self.vm)` throughout (generation check, a `ptr::read` of the whole `Transpiler`, `bun_watcher`, `macro_mode`, ...).
- `WebWorker::shutdown()` frees the VM allocation. For an inline-slot job that is `self` itself, so every `self.*` access afterwards is a use-after-free, including the schedule-time `vm_handle` that the checked enqueue in `dispatch_to_main_thread` reads.

Reachable via a worker that performs a dynamic `import()` (the module-load path schedules the transpile on the pool) and is `terminate()`d while the job is in flight.

### Why the checked-enqueue pattern cannot close this one

#32071 routes cross-thread completions through a live-VM registry so producers never touch a freed VM. That works when the producer's own state lives outside the VM allocation. Here the job storage is inside the allocation, so the handle the check needs is itself freed; the registry gate in `dispatch_to_main_thread` (added in #32071) narrows the window for heap-fallback slots and makes a garbage generation overwhelmingly likely to fail the match, but it is not a guarantee, and `run()`'s body reads happen before the gate either way. This is pre-existing behavior; #32071 strictly narrows exposure for this producer.

### Possible fixes (structural)

- Move the job storage out of the VM allocation, e.g. `Box` the `HiveArrayFallback` (or the whole `RuntimeTranspilerStore`) and give it its own lifetime, freed only after the pool quiesces. The schedule-time `vm_handle` then lives in memory that survives VM teardown, and `run()`'s `(*vm)` reads can be gated on the registry check.
- Or have `WebWorker::shutdown()` wait for in-flight transpiler jobs (a per-VM in-flight counter joined before `dealloc(VirtualMachine)`).

Same limitation shape as #33313 (a pre-existing cross-thread access that the registry approach narrows but cannot fully close without structural change). Spotted in review of #32071.

title: new tls.TLSSocket(socket, { isServer: true }) never asks for a client certificate unless ca is also set, even with requestCert: true
excerpt:
### Relationship to #33924

I filed #33924 earlier and it was correctly closed as not planned. That report's central claim - that Bun should auto-close the connection when an untrusted client certificate is presented to a bare `new tls.TLSSocket({ isServer: true })` - was wrong. robobun checked this against real Node.js and showed Node doesn't auto-close there either; that auto-reject logic lives specifically in `tls.createServer()`'s connection listener, not in the `TLSSocket` constructor. I independently confirmed this by reading Node's actual current source (`lib/internal/tls/wrap.js`, `onServerSocketSecure`, wired only by `tlsConnectionListener`) and tracing it back to a 2013 commit, so that part of the discussion is settled and I'm not reopening it.

While verifying that, I found a separate, narrower bug in the same code area that robobun's investigation didn't touch, because their test always included a `ca` option. This report is about that bug specifically. It has nothing to do with auto-closing connections.

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

`new tls.TLSSocket(socket, options)` accepts `requestCert` as a documented option. From Node's own docs (`doc/api/tls.md`, current `main`, under `new tls.TLSSocket(socket[, options])`):

> `requestCert`: Whether to authenticate the remote peer by requesting a certificate. Clients always request a server certificate. Servers (`isServer` is true) may set `requestCert` to true to request a client certificate.

> If set to `true`, the server requests a client certificate.

> Default is `false`.

title: bun test --coverage emits DA records (DA:<line>,0) for comment-only and blank lines
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.13

### What is the problem?

When a source file is loaded but a function is never executed, `bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov` emits `DA:<line>,0` records for lines that are **comment-only or blank**, not just executable lines.

LCOV `DA` records are meant for executable lines. Stamping comment/blank lines makes those lines appear as "uncovered code" in downstream tools — for example, codecov reports them as uncoverable, producing a false-red when several such all-zero coverage chunks are merged (union) into a combined report.

### Minimal reproduction

`mod.ts`:
```ts
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  // this is a comment line that is never executed

  return a + b;
}
```

`load-only.test.ts`:
```ts
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";
import * as mod from "./mod.ts";
test("imports the module but never calls add", () => {
  expect(typeof mod.add).toBe("function");
});
```

Run:
```
bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov --coverage-dir=cov load-only.test.ts
```

`cov/lcov.info` contains:
```
SF:mod.ts
FNF:1
FNH:0
DA:1,0
DA:2,0   <- comment line
DA:3,0   <- blank line
LF:3
LH:0
end_of_record
```

Line 2 (a comment) and line 3 (a blank line) receive `DA` records, while the actual executable `return` (line 4) does not.

### What should happen instead?

Comment-only and blank lines should not receive `DA` records — they are not executable. Only executable lines should appear in `DA` / `LF` / `LH`.

### Related

Possibly related to #12095 (lcov results differ from CLI).

title: bun install leaks package-extraction temp directories (.{16hex}-{8digits}.tmp) into $TMPDIR; filled 25 GB on a long-lived CI container
excerpt:
### What happens

`bun install` leaks its package-extraction temp directories into `$TMPDIR` and never removes them, even when the install exits 0. Each leaked entry is a directory named `.{16 hex chars}-{8 digits}.tmp` (for example `.5dfdff2c5fefbff7-00000006.tmp`) containing the extracted contents of an npm package.

On machines where the OS periodically cleans the temp dir this goes unnoticed. On a long-lived container it is fatal: nothing ever cleans `/tmp`, so the leak grows until the disk fills.

### Impact we measured

- **Linux (Debian-based GitHub Actions runner container, x64):** repeated `bun install` runs in a Bun-workspaces monorepo accumulated ~25 GB of these directories in `/tmp` over ~40 hours, at ~37 MB per directory, and drove the host disk past 90%. All installs succeeded; the leak is not tied to crashes or failed installs.
- **macOS (arm64, Bun 1.3.14):** same pattern in `$TMPDIR`. 22 leaked directories currently present, dated across the last three weeks. Example listing:

```
drwxr-xr-x@  2 marcos staff  64 Jun 22 03:53 .1dba7fff6bf6ffb8-00000002.tmp
drwxr-xr-x@  9 marcos staff 288 Jun 23 03:35 .1dbe8ded7fb73bd2-00000008.tmp
drwxr-xr-x@  9 marcos staff 288 Jul  1 03:35 .3eff58f797b1ad7c-00000002.tmp
drwxr-xr-x@ 15 marcos staff 480 Jul  4 04:13 .5dfdff2c5fefbff7-00000006.tmp
```

`.5dfdff2c5fefbff7-00000006.tmp` contains a complete extracted `react-native` package tree (`Libraries/`, `ReactCommon/`, `ReactAndroid/`, `sdks/`, ...). On macOS `du` reports the trees as taking ~0 blocks (presumably clonefile/hardlink from the cache), but on the Linux container each directory held ~37 MB of real data.

### What I expected

Temp extraction directories are deleted before `bun install` returns, or at minimum on the next install.

### Environment

- Bun 1.3.14 (also observed on earlier 1.3.x)
- macOS arm64 and Linux x64 (Debian-based container, ext4, `/tmp` on the root filesystem)
- Plain `bun install` in a Bun-workspaces monorepo, default cache settings

### Notes

- My best guess at the mechanism, from the documented extract-then-rename-into-global-cache model: some extraction paths skip the cleanup/rename of the temp directory. That is inference, not verified against source.
- Closest existing issue I found is #14793, which is the same class of bug (temp directory left behind, never cleaned) but for `bun upgrade` rather than `bun install`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Every call to `Bun.build()` strands native memory that is never returned. RSS grows

      Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, k) => `  x = (x + ${k}) * 1.0001`).join('\n') +
      `\n  return x + ${i}\n}\n`
  )
}
writeFileSync(

let base = 0

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This file reproduces the bug when bundled with the steps below: https://gist.github.com/theopak/6536127d85204bfc4b1dc7a8dc6890a6#file-bun-symbol-resolution-repro-js

First, run the input directly as a control:

```sh
bun bun-symbol-resolution-repro.js
```

Then bundle and run it:

```sh
bun build bun-symbol-resolution-repro.js --outdir out
bun out/bun-symbol-resolution-repro.js
```

The failure reproduced in three consecutive clean runs.

### What is the expected behavior?

Bundling valid JavaScript should preserve its symbol bindings.

The input contains the equivalent of:

```js
async function J7A(A, B, Q) {
  const result = A3(B.projectId, null);
}
```

`A3` is a global function. The parameter `A` and global `A3` are different symbols.

### What do you see instead?

Bun renames the parameter `A` to `A3`, shadowing the referenced global function:

```js
async function J7A(A3, B, Q) {
  const result = A3(B.projectId, null);
}
```

The bundled output then fails:

```text
TypeError: A3 is not a function.
(In 'A3(g, null)', 'A3' is an instance of Object)
    at J7A
```

Directly running the input does not produce this collision.

This is a severe correctness failure because a successful production build can silently change valid program semantics and ship type-confused runtime crashes in code that worked before bundling.

### Additional information

This requires only one entrypoint and a normal `bun build`. Compilation and bytecode generation are not involved.

The fixture is intentionally large because the failure depends on the scope graph and identifier-renaming order. Removing unrelated scopes can change the assigned names and make the failure disappear. The core problem is that the identifier renamer assigns a function parameter the same name as a referenced global, changing program semantics.

title: ASAN CI: JSC assertion in JSObject::getOwnPropertyDescriptor during worker terminate (test-worker-message-port-transfer-terminate)
excerpt:
On the debian-13 x64-asan test lane, `test/js/node/test/parallel/test-worker-message-port-transfer-terminate.js` intermittently dies with:

```
ASSERTION FAILED: !scope.exception() || !result
vendor/WebKit/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSObject.cpp(3936) : bool JSC::JSObject::getOwnPropertyDescriptor(JSGlobalObject *, PropertyName, PropertyDescriptor &)
main process killed by SIGABRT
```

- Occurs on main as well as feature branches (CI's annotation tagger marks it `[pre-existing]`; observed on builds 72522 and 72563 of PR #32488, which does not touch worker/JSC property machinery).

- Suggested approach: run the worker message-port transfer + terminate suites under `BUN_JSC_validateExceptionChecks=1` on an ASAN/debug build and audit the property-descriptor call sites the trap identifies (likely a missing `RETURN_IF_EXCEPTION` after a user-code-reachable get).

Filing so the failure has a tracker independent of unrelated PRs whose CI it appears on.

Writable.toWeb() breaks when a preload script requires node:stream
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (and current `main`)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`Writable.toWeb()` returns a broken WritableStream when *any* preload script has required `node:stream` (or `node:zlib`).

`preload.js`:
```js
require("node:stream");
```

`repro.js`:
```js
const { Writable } = require("stream");
const w = new Writable({ write(c, e, cb) { cb(); } });
const ws = Writable.toWeb(w);
ws.close().then(
  () => console.log("RESOLVED (wrong)"),
  e => console.log("rejected:", e.code, "(correct)"),
);
w.end();
```

```
bun repro.js                      # rejected: ABORT_ERR (correct)
bun --preload ./preload.js repro.js   # RESOLVED (wrong) + TypeError below
node --require ./preload.js repro.js  # rejected: ABORT_ERR (correct)
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Same as without the preload, and same as Node: ending the underlying `stream.Writable` errors the WritableStream, so `ws.close()` rejects with `ABORT_ERR`.

### What do you see instead?

`ws.close()` resolves instead of rejecting, and the end-of-stream callback then throws:

```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'handleKnownInternalErrors')
      at <anonymous> (internal:webstreams_adapters:204:15)
      at <anonymous> (internal:shared:113:35)
      at onclose (internal:streams/end-of-stream:170:21)
      at emit (node:events:142:22)
      at emitCloseNT (internal:streams/destroy:104:14)
```

`handleKnownInternalErrors` is a plain function declaration in the same builtin module
(`src/js/internal/webstreams_adapters.ts`) as its two call sites, so it should never be
undefined. It only becomes undefined when the module is first pulled in from a preload
script, which suggests the builtin's module-scope bindings are not fully initialized on that
path — `newWritableStreamFromStreamWritable`'s `eos()` callback then faults, and the
`closed` promise settles the wrong way.

### Additional information

Reproduces on released 1.3.14 and on current `main` (i.e. it predates the C++ web-streams
rewrite in #33193). `node:zlib` in the preload triggers it too — `webstreams_adapters.ts`
reads `processBindingConstants.zlib` at module scope.

Found while porting Node's upstream web-streams tests (#32627): it makes
`test/parallel/test-whatwg-webstreams-adapters-to-writablestream.js` fail under the
node-test harness, whose preload requires `node:stream`. That file is left out of the
vendored set until this is fixed.

title: Windows: uv_run's alive-guard wedges teardown states with zero ref'd handles (server.close() waits forever class)
excerpt:
## Mechanism (fully established, A/B-proven on CI agents)

On Windows, Bun drives libuv via `tick_with_timeout` → `uv_run(UV_RUN_ONCE)`. `uv_run`'s alive-guard (`while (r != 0 && ...)`) skips **both timer processing and I/O polling** when the loop has no ref'd handles or active requests. Every uSockets handle (socket polls, asyncs, prepare/check, sweep timer) is `uv_unref`'d by design — socket liveness is tracked by Bun-side KeepAlives that bump uv's `active_handles` counter directly.

Consequence: any state where all Bun KeepAlives drop while a socket still awaits an event wedges completely — no I/O delivery, no JS timer can fire (ref'd or unref'd; the JS-timer bridge `uv_timer` in `timer::All::ensure_uv_timer` is itself unref'd without ref'd JS timers), until an unrelated ref'd uv handle appears. The epoll/kqueue path has no such gap: `us_loop_run_bun_tick` polls unconditionally, bounded by Bun's next-JS-timer deadline (which the Windows path discards entirely).

Canonical repro state: `node:http` server half-closes a connection mid-upload (`res.socket.end()`), response never `end()`ed, client aborts; `server.close()` (graceful stop releases the server's KeepAlive immediately in `stop_listening`) then awaits a teardown event the loop will never deliver. `test-http-should-not-emit-or-throw-error-when-writing-after-socket.end.ts` (quarantined-on-main class) times out exactly here; an identical copy with a ref'd 5s interval passes on the same lane in the same build, while an unref'd 15s watchdog never fires during the stall.

## Fix attempts on PR #32488 (reverted, with reasons)

1. `us_loop_run_bun_tick` for libuv (ref the wakeup async around `uv_run`, scratch `uv_timer` for the deadline): unwedged the blocking branch, but making Windows JS timers punctual globally broke tests depending on the historical lazy-timer timing (proxy-tunnel timeouts, `test-tls-connect-memleak` RSS timing, unconsume/upgrade).
2. Same bypass in `us_loop_pump` (the `tick_without_idle` branch `auto_tick` takes when `is_active()` is false — the branch actually hit in the wedge): unwedged the tests, but delivering I/O during legitimate keepalive-zero *transition* windows (socket handoffs: upgrade, unconsume, proxy CONNECT tunnels) broke those flows.
3. Keep the server's KeepAlive through a graceful stop until `deinit_if_we_can` drains (Node parity — `server.close()` keeps the process alive until connections end): correct in principle, but upgrade-detached connections never decrement

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

The cost of each individual `fs.watch()` call grows super-linearly with the number of watchers already registered in the process. In Node it is flat.

This matters because that is exactly what `chokidar` does: it registers one `fs.watch` per file. Any dev server built on chokidar (Nuxt, Vite plugins, webpack tooling, …) will register thousands of watchers on a medium/large project.

```js

import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'

const runtime = typeof Bun !== 'undefined' ? `bun ${Bun.version}` : `node ${process.version}`

const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'fswatch-bench-'))
const files = []
for (let i = 0; i < 5000; i++) {
  const f = join(dir, `file-${i}.txt`)
  writeFileSync(f, 'x')
  files.push(f)
}

console.log(`[${runtime}] watching ${files.length} files individually (what chokidar does per file)\n`)

const handles = []
let done = 0

for (const mark of [500, 1500, 3000, 5000]) {
  const batch = files.slice(done, mark)
  const t = performance.now()
  for (const f of batch) handles.push(watch(f, () => {}))
  const ms = performance.now() - t
  done = handles.length
  console.log(

for (const h of handles) h.close()
rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })

title: Bun Shell: stdout/stderr are relayed via pipes, not inherited — add explicit `inherit` option or make default truly inherit
excerpt:
## Summary

`Bun.$` is documented as inheriting the parent process's stdout/stderr/stdin, but in practice only `stdin` is a real TTY — `stdout` and `stderr` are pipes that Bun relays to the parent. As a result, spawned commands see `isatty(1) === false` and disable colors / progress bars / pagers.

## Reproduction

```ts
// run from a real terminal
await Bun.$`python3 -c "import sys;print(sys.stdin.isatty(),sys.stdout.isatty(),sys.stderr.isatty())"`;
// -> True False False
```

Same finding as #33234.

## Impact

Any command that checks `isatty(1)` degrades: `ls`/`git` drop colors, `cargo` loses its progress bar, pagers behave like `cat`. The core color issue #11046 (open since 2024-05) traces back to this. Today the only shell-level workaround is `.env({ FORCE_COLOR: "3" })`, which depends on every child supporting `FORCE_COLOR` (tsc, composer, etc. don't).

## What's missing

There's no escape hatch on `ShellPromise` to make stdout/stderr a real inherited fd:

```ts
Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(Bun.$`true`))
// constructor cwd env quiet nothrow throws text json lines arrayBuffer bytes blob run then
```

#10515 requested `.inheritStdio()` and was closed with "by default the shell will use stdout, stderr, and stdin of the bun process" — but the reproduction above shows that's not the case for stdout/stderr; they're pipes, not inherited fds.

## Proposal

Either (or both):

1. **Add an explicit inherit option**, e.g. `.stdout("inherit")` / `.stderr("inherit")` / `.inheritStdio()`, mirroring `Bun.spawn`'s `stdio: "inherit"` and zx's `stdio` API. When set, pass the parent's fd directly to the child so `isatty()` is `true`.

2. **Change the default to truly inherit** stdout/stderr (only piping when `.quiet()` / `.text()` / etc. is used), matching how dax (`@david/shell`) behaves:

```ts
// dax's CommandBuilder default state
#state = {
  stdin: "inherit",
  stdout: { kind: "inherit" },
  stderr: { kind: "inherit" },
  // ...
};
```

In dax, `` await $`cmd` `` keeps colors by default, and only switches to piped when a capture method (`.text()` / `.quiet()`) is called. This is why dax has essentially no "colors lost from subprocess" issues, while Bun shell / zx / execa all do.

## Why this over the PTY route (#33239)

#33239 adds `.terminal(term)` (PTY) and is great for full-screen / interactive programs. But the inherit path is valuable on its own:

- **Cross-platform**: PTY (`Bun.Terminal`) is POSIX-only; fd inheritance works on Windows too.

title: Runaway native recursion in bun 1.3.14 allocates unboundedly until the machine dies (3 concurrent processes; the 2 walkable stacks are identical)

Two of the three had walkable stacks (the third had thrashed its own stack pages out of memory), and **both resolve to the same offsets in the bun binary** — same functions, same call path. That points at a deterministic path rather than a race. I don't have a reproduction; what I have is the macOS panic stackshot, which is unusually complete, and the binary UUID matches a stock release build, so **you should be able to symbolicate the offsets below directly from your dSYM.**

This is **not** #34053 (`Bun.build` mimalloc arena) — no bundler is involved, and the stack shows a native recursion. Growth here was still ongoing at ~330 MB/s when the machine was reset, so I can't say whether it would eventually have plateaued; it did not do so within twenty minutes or 103 GB.

title: macOS: no x64 baseline build — `@oven/bun-darwin-x64-baseline` is byte-identical to the AVX2 default
excerpt:
## Summary

### There is no baseline build for x64 macOS

`@oven/bun-darwin-x64-baseline` ships the **same binary** as `@oven/bun-darwin-x64` — the AVX2 (`-march=haswell`) build.

Linux, by contrast, ships a genuine baseline.

### Why it matters

On a pre-AVX2 Mac (Sandy/Ivy Bridge — no AVX2/FMA) that binary crashes, and there is **no baseline package to fall back to**.

This is the upstream cause of downstream reports like anomalyco/opencode#29039 — opencode's `-baseline` Mac binary SIGILLs on Ivy Bridge.

### Who hits it

Pre-Haswell Intel Macs running a macOS that bun supports. Quoting the reports:

[anomalyco/opencode#24876](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/24876):

> macOS: 13.7.4
> Machine: Macmini6,2 (Intel Ivy Bridge, 2012)
> CPU: x86_64 (supports AVX, but NOT AVX2)

macOS 13.7.4 clears bun's 13.0 deployment target; the CPU has no AVX2. That combination is the gap. Same reporter:

> This makes the tool unusable on: Intel Macs pre-Haswell (≈ 2013 and earlier) / Any x86_64 CPU without AVX2 support. These machines are still relatively common in development environments.

[anomalyco/opencode#29039](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/29039):

> MacBook Pro, Intel Core i7-3520M @ 2.90GHz
> macOS 24.6.0 (Darwin)
> `sysctl -n hw.optional.avx2_0` returns 0 — no AVX2 support

That reporter independently confirmed the packaging bug straight from the Mach-O header:

> `otool -h` shows cpusubtype 3 (CPU_SUBTYPE_X86_64_H — Haswell) for both

For my part, I run OpenCore Legacy Patcher on my mom's 2013 Intel Mac — current macOS, so it clears the deployment target, and the CPU is the only blocker.

## Evidence

Every step is reproducible with `curl` — no bun internals involved.

**1. The two darwin packages ship the same binary.**

Download both npm packages and hash the `bun` binary inside each:

```
ea2f223e94bb2f4bf3050895113c3cf346438f6fa0501c8532284e063f72f7a0  @oven/bun-darwin-x64@1.3.14
ea2f223e94bb2f4bf3050895113c3cf346438f6fa0501c8532284e063f72f7a0  @oven/bun-darwin-x64-baseline@1.3.14
```

Identical hash, identical 69,173,328 bytes — byte-for-byte the same file. The "baseline" package is not a distinct build.

**2. That binary is the AVX2 build.**
Disassembling it (Mach-O, x86_64) finds **248,019 AVX2 (ymm)** + **7,049 AVX-512 (zmm)** instructions — i.e. the modern (`-march=haswell`) build, which a pre-AVX2 CPU can't run.

**3. Linux ships a real baseline; darwin doesn't.**

Same comparison on the linux packages — default and baselin

title: Runtime transpiler cache inlines process.env dot-reads during Worker-thread imports — later processes execute the first process's env values
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 (macOS, Apple Silicon)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

When a sufficiently large module (over the runtime transpiler disk-cache threshold, ~50KB) is **dynamically imported inside a Worker thread**, Bun's transpiler inlines `process.env.X` dot-reads as string literals into the transpiled output — and that output is stored in the shared on-disk runtime transpiler cache (`~/Library/Caches/bun/@t@/*.pile`), keyed by content only. A **second process** (or later run) with **different environment variables** gets a cache hit and executes the *first* process's env values as compile-time constants.

Repro (3 files):

`probe-plugin.ts` (must exceed the disk-cache threshold — pad with ~800 comment lines):

```ts
const k = ["MY", "TEST", "IDENTITY"].join("_")
export const probe = () =>
  console.log("DOT:", process.env.MY_TEST_IDENTITY, "| DYNAMIC:", process.env[k])
// ... ~800 padding comment lines so the file exceeds the runtime transpiler
// disk-cache threshold ...
```

`w.ts`:

```ts
const mod = await import("./probe-plugin.ts")
mod.probe()
```

`main.ts`:

```ts
new Worker(new URL("./w.ts", import.meta.url))
```

Run twice with different env values (file untouched between runs):

```sh
MY_TEST_IDENTITY=FIRST_VALUE bun main.ts
MY_TEST_IDENTITY=SECOND_VALUE bun main.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

```
DOT: FIRST_VALUE | DYNAMIC: FIRST_VALUE
DOT: SECOND_VALUE | DYNAMIC: SECOND_VALUE
```

`process.env` reads should reflect the running process's environment.

### What do you actually see?

```
DOT: FIRST_VALUE | DYNAMIC: FIRST_VALUE
DOT: FIRST_VALUE | DYNAMIC: SECOND_VALUE   <-- dot-read is stale (run 1's value)
```

The second run's dot-read returns the FIRST run's value. Inspecting the cached artifact shows the literal baked into the transpiled code where the source has an env read:

```sh
$ strings ~/Library/Caches/bun/@t@/<hash>.pile | grep MY_TEST
# transpiled output contains:  "FIRST_VALUE"  (a literal), env expression absent
```

Notes:

- Only the **dot-read** (`process.env.MY_TEST_IDENTITY`) is inlined; a computed-key bracket read (`process.env[k]`) stays live.
- Plain `bun main-without-worker.ts` (same import, no Worker thread) does **not** inline — the behavior is specific to the Worker-thread transpile path.
- `BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0` makes both runs correct (workaround).

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

`1.3.14`

### What platform is your computer?

**CI:** GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` (Linux x86_64)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

We run a ~4,400-test / ~450-file Next.js + React Testing Library suite via:

```
bun test --parallel --timeout=20000 <files...>
```

split into 4 shards with `--shard=N/4`. One shard (call it shard A, a fixed set of ~112 files under a deterministic `--shard` split) consistently hangs after all tests finish: every test reports `(pass)`, but the process never prints the final `Ran N tests across M files` summary and never exits. We wrap the run in a watchdog that kills the process after 120s of no new stdout — by that point every individual test has already logged pass with 0 failures, so the hang is strictly a **post-test-completion** hang, not a stuck test.

### Isolating the cause: same file set, only the run mode changes

We bisected shard A's 112 files down to a 28-file slice (`q1`) that reliably reproduces the hang, then ran that exact same 28-file list three different ways:

| Command | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `bun test --parallel --timeout=20000 <q1 files>` | **Hangs** — no final summary, watchdog has to kill it | — |
| `bun test --timeout=20000 <q1 files>` (single process, no `--parallel`) | Completes normally — `Ran 224 tests across 28 files`, 0 fail | 52s |
| `bun test --isolate --timeout=20000 <q1 files>` (single process, per-file isolation) | Completes normally — 224 pass / 0 fail | 337s |

Since the identical test files complete cleanly both without `--parallel` and with `--isolate` (single process), the hang is not caused by a leaked handle/timer/connection in our test code or its dependencies — it only appears when `--parallel` spawns/tears down worker subprocesses.

|---|---|
| `q1` — 28 files | **Hangs** |
| `e1` — first 14 files of `q1` | Clean |
