title: Bun Shell: stdout/stderr are pipes, not inherited — add .stdout("inherit")/.inheritStdio()
excerpt: ## This is not a duplicate of #14967 Issue #34167 was auto-closed by the dedupe bot as "Duplicate of #14967". That closure is incorrect: - #14967 ("bun shell interactive mode") is about **stdin**: interactive commands like `rustup` need a TTY on stdin for prompts / confirmations. - This issue is about **stdout/stderr fd inheritance**: `isatty(1) === false` in children because stdout/stderr are relayed through pipes, which strips colors / progress bars / pagers. Different fds, different symptoms, different fix. The original report was closed for the wrong reason, so this issue restates it. ## Summary `Bun.$` is documented as inheriting the parent process's stdout/stderr/stdin, but in practice only `stdin` is a real TTY — `stdout` and `stderr` are pipes that Bun relays to the parent. As a result, spawned commands see `isatty(1) === false` and disable colors / progress bars / pagers. ## Reproduction ```ts // run from a real terminal await Bun.$`python3 -c "import sys;print(sys.stdin.isatty(),sys.stdout.isatty(),sys.stderr.isatty())"`; // -> True False False ``` ## Impact Any command that checks `isatty(1)` degrades: `ls`/`git` drop colors, `cargo` loses its progress bar, pagers behave like `cat`. The core color issue #11046 (open since 2024-05) traces back to this. Today the only shell-level workaround is `.env({ FORCE_COLOR: "3" })`, which depends on every child supporting `FORCE_COLOR` (tsc, composer, etc. don't). ## What's missing There's no escape hatch on `ShellPromise` to make stdout/stderr a real inherited fd: ```ts Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(Bun.$`true`)) // constructor cwd env quiet nothrow throws text json lines arrayBuffer bytes blob run then ``` #10515 requested `.inheritStdio()` and was closed with "by default the shell will use stdout, stderr, and stdin of the bun process" — but the reproduction above shows that's not the case for stdout/stderr; they're pipes, not inherited fds. ## Proposal Add an explicit inherit option, e.g. `.stdout("inherit")` / `.stderr("inherit")` / `.inheritStdio()`, mirroring `Bun.spawn`'s `stdio: "inherit"` and zx's `stdio` API. When set, pass the parent's fd directly to the child so `isatty()` is `true`. ## Why fd inheritance rather than a PTY (#33234 / #33239) #33234 (open) and PR #33239 propose `.terminal()` / PTY for the same root cause. title: CI: darwin arm64 tart lanes hang at node_modules pre-warm until the 45-minute timeout; sourdough and challah have zero passes since Aug 8
excerpt:
## Symptom

Darwin aarch64 test jobs on the tart fleet boot the guest and docker sidecar, sync the checkout, print

```
[guest] pre-warming node_modules (native bun)
```

and then produce nothing for ~44 minutes until `timeout_in_minutes: 45` kills the job (state `timed_out`, exit 255, no failure annotation). Example: build [90826](https://buildkite.com/bun/bun/builds/90826), job `019fe5ef-f759-470e-8f65-71ff365677bf` on `darwin-sourdough-arm64-tart-26`: last guest output at `t=1786269653698`, next line is the cancellation at `t=1786272303527`, 44m10s later.

Every inspected hang (7 jobs across builds 90826, 90780, 90765, 90755, 90700) stops at exactly that line. On a healthy boot the next output arrives half a second later (`200 packages installed [482.00ms]`, the repo-root install, then `2760 packages installed` for test/), so the wedge starts at the very beginning of the guest-command ssh session and never resolves.

## Two hosts are fully sick

Job outcomes for `:darwin: * aarch64 - test-bun` over builds 90680-90830 (Aug 8-9), grouped by agent:

| host | agent version | passed | timed_out (45 min each) | failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sourdough (tart-15 + tart-26) | 3.87.0 | **0** | 11 | 6 |
| challah (tart-15 + tart-26) | 3.87.0 | **0** | 5 | 7 |
| baguette (both) | 3.127.1 | 17 | 0 | 0 |
| ciabatta (both) | 3.127.1 | 16 | 0 | 16 |
| focaccia (both) | 3.127.1 | 18 | 0 | 2 |

sourdough and challah have not passed a single job in that window. `darwin-sourdough-arm64-tart-26` still passed in build [90500](https://buildkite.com/bun/bun/builds/90500) (Aug 8 ~04:00 UTC), so both hosts went sick during Aug 8 and stayed sick. title: Bytecode cache re-decode: keep JSC's UnlinkedFunctionExecutable at 96 bytes
excerpt:
Follow-up from review of oven-sh/WebKit#397 (that repo has issues disabled, so tracking it here).

The re-decode support keeps `m_cachedRecordOffset` — the offset of a function's record in its bytecode-cache payload, so a jettisoned code block can be re-decoded instead of re-parsed — on `UnlinkedFunctionExecutable`, growing it from 96 to 104 bytes, which the 16-byte atom size rounds to 112: 16 bytes on every function executable, cached or not. The small fields before the first union leave ~3 bytes of padding and both unions are fully occupied once a code block exists, so there is no free slot.

Plan that removes the member entirely: keep the record offset on the decoded `UnlinkedFunctionCodeBlock` (a few bytes on a much larger and rarer object), and when a code block is jettisoned, write the offsets back into the executable's second union and set `m_isCached` again — the executable returns to the ordinary cached representation and the existing cached-decode path performs the re-decode; the record-identity check moves there too.

Kept separate from the PR because it reshapes the re-decode flow rather than fixing it; the current form is correct, just heavier than necessary.

`/^\p{RGI_Emoji}$/v` is roughly **300x slower on Bun than on Node**. Other Unicode property escapes are fine, so it appears specific to `\p{RGI_Emoji}` (a property-of-strings, which requires the `v` flag).

  fn()
  const started = performance.now()
  for (let i = 0; i < iterations; i++) fn()
  console.log(`${label.padEnd(44)} ${((performance.now() - started) / iterations).toFixed(3).padStart(9)} ms`)
}

bench("156x rgi.test() on U+2500 (box drawing)", () => {
  let hits = 0
  for (const c of chars) if (rgi.test(c)) hits++
  return hits
}, 100)

// Control: a similarly-shaped Unicode property regex, fast on both engines.
const control = /^\p{Extended_Pictographic}$/u
bench("156x /^\\p{Extended_Pictographic}$/u", () => {
  let hits = 0
  for (const c of chars) if (control.test(c)) hits++
  return hits
}, 100)

console.log(`\nengine: ${typeof Bun !== "undefined" ? `bun ${Bun.version}` : `node ${process.version}`}`)

Performance roughly comparable to Node/V8, and in the same ballpark as other Unicode property escapes.

Optimize targeted bun update dependency lookup
excerpt:
## Summary

Optimize targeted workspace updates by replacing the repeated workspace-owner scan in `Lockfile::is_update_target_dependency` with a cached `DependencyID` membership lookup.

## Rationale

For `bun update --recursive` and `bun update --filter`, `Lockfile::is_update_target_dependency` currently calls `get_workspace_pkg_if_workspace_dep` for each resolved dependency. That helper scans workspace packages and their dependency slices each time. Large workspaces can incur repeated lockfile-wide scans during dependency resolution.

The current implementation is correct. This issue tracks the deferred performance optimization separately from the workspace-targeted update behavior.

## Affected areas

- `src/install/lockfile.rs`
  - `Lockfile::is_update_target_dependency`
  - `Lockfile::get_workspace_pkg_if_workspace_dep`
  - Lockfile cleanup paths that remap dependency IDs.
- `src/install/PackageManager.rs`
  - State associated with `update_workspace_name_hashes`.
- Workspace update-plan setup in `src/install/PackageManager/updatePackageJSONAndInstall.rs`.

## Required changes

1. Keep `update_workspace_name_hashes` as the durable selected-workspace identity.
2. Build a `DependencyID` membership lookup for dependencies declared by selected workspaces when the workspace update plan is configured.
3. Make `Lockfile::is_update_target_dependency` use the lookup for `--recursive` and `--filter`.
4. Preserve the existing `is_root_dependency` fallback when no workspace target set exists.
5. Rebuild or invalidate and rebuild the lookup after `clean_with_logger` remaps dependency IDs.
6. Add regression coverage for lookup rebuilding across the relevant update lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria

- `is_update_target_dependency` does not scan all workspace packages on each targeted dependency check.
- `bun update --recursive` and `bun update --filter` retain their current update behavior.
- The lookup remains correct after lockfile cleanup remaps dependency IDs.
- The default current-workspace update path retains its existing root-dependency behavior.

## Backlinks

- Pull request: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/33182
- Review discussion: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/33182#discussion_r3749633267
- Requested by: @robobun

title: Startup snapshots: let a Bun.serve() created before the snapshot listen again on restore
excerpt:
Follow-up to the startup snapshot work (#37260 / #37261).

### Today

| | |
|---|---|
| `Bun.serve()` while a snapshot is being taken | Refused under the default (strict) I/O policy; under `local` it is allowed, but the listening socket does not exist in a restored launch (open sockets are gone after restore, like every other descriptor) |
| What a server program does instead | Calls `Bun.serve()` inside `Bun.startupSnapshot.main()` or a `process.on("restore")` listener, so the listen happens in each launch |

That works and is documented, but it means the most common program shape — `Bun.serve()` at module scope — needs a one-line change to be snapshotted in auto mode.

### Proposal

Let a server created before the snapshot come back listening after restore:

| Step | |
|---|---|
| At `Bun.serve()` during a snapshot build | Don't bind; keep the resolved options (handlers, port, hostname, tls, …) on the server object and mark it pending. Under strict this replaces today's refusal, since nothing about this machine is captured |
| At restore | Bind every pending server, in creation order, before `"restore"` listeners run; a bind failure is reported the way it would be at startup |
| `server.port` / `server.url` during the build | Unavailable (throw or `undefined`) — the port is only known per launch. Programs that read them at build time are exactly the ones that should move the call into `main()` |
| `server.stop()` before the snapshot | Drops the pending entry |

`Bun.listen` / `Bun.udpSocket` could follow the same shape later; `Bun.serve` covers the case that matters.

### Not covered

`server.reload()` and `unix:` sockets need no special handling beyond the above; `reusePort` clusters work per launch as they do today.

title: macOS: EMFILE hint recommends `sudo launchctl limit maxfiles 2147483646`; following it makes every new Terminal `login` spin ~5 minutes of CPU, and SIP blocks undoing it until reboot
excerpt:
Bun's fd-exhaustion error hint tells macOS users to raise the system fd limit to `2147483646` (INT32_MAX - 1). Following it verbatim put my machine into a state where every new Terminal window took ~4m40s of 100% CPU in `login` before showing a prompt, and the change could not be reverted because SIP rejects lowering the limit back. The only way out was a reboot. Details and measurements below.

### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14, embedded in the opencode 1.18.15 single-file executable (`bun-darwin-aarch64`). The hint text is unchanged on `main` as of 2026-08-10: [`src/crash_handler/lib.rs` L1296 (SystemFdQuotaExceeded)](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/827475e21b1ffcd7258b6592362c5a35fc88b999/src/crash_handler/lib.rs#L1296), [L1339 (ProcessFdQuotaExceeded)](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/827475e21b1ffcd7258b6592362c5a35fc88b999/src/crash_handler/lib.rs#L1339), [L1404 (fallback)](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/827475e21b1ffcd7258b6592362c5a35fc88b999/src/crash_handler/lib.rs#L1404).

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0), Apple Silicon (arm64)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This report is about the remediation advice printed on `ProcessFdQuotaExceeded` / `SystemFdQuotaExceeded` (and appended to some generic "Unexpected" errors, see #6601), not about the fd exhaustion itself.

1. Exhaust file descriptors in any Bun-built app. In my case: running opencode against an exFAT external volume (AppleDouble `._*` companion files double the entry count there; the exhaustion itself is out of scope here). Bun printed its built-in hint:

   ```
   To fix this, try running:

     ulimit -n 2147483646

   You may also need to run:

     sudo launchctl limit maxfiles 2147483646
   ```

2. Run both commands exactly as printed (both are in my zsh history verbatim, in the printed order).
3. Open a new Terminal window.

Note for anyone reproducing: step 2 degrades every new terminal session on the machine until you reboot.

### What is the expected behavior?

A remediation hint that does not degrade the rest of the OS and that can be undone without rebooting. A bounded suggestion (for example `sudo launchctl limit maxfiles 65536 200000` plus `ulimit -n 65536`) addresses the same class of failures without the side effects below. Ideally the message would also point out that fd exhaustion usually has a findable cause (a leak, or a pathological filesystem); raising the ceiling only hides it.

### What do you see instead?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On Linux, `Bun.dns.lookup`'s default backend — and therefore `node:dns.lookup` — is c-ares, which
reads `/etc/resolv.conf` directly and has no NSS hook. On any host where `/etc/resolv.conf` is not

The common real-world trigger is a corporate split-DNS VPN: on connect, the client replaces
`/etc/resolv.conf` with internal authoritative resolvers that serve internal zones and **refuse
recursion for public names**, while `systemd-resolved` (reached via `nss-resolve`) resolves both
correctly. `nsswitch.conf` is irrelevant to c-ares, so it queries the refusing servers and fails.

```js

    try { const r = await Bun.dns.lookup(host, { backend }); console.log(`backend=${backend} ->`, r[0].address); }
    catch (e) { console.log(`backend=${backend} -> FAIL`, e.code); }
  }
}, 500);

`node:dns.lookup()` resolves the way the platform does, via `getaddrinfo(3)`, honoring NSS — which

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14+0d9b296af

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 26.5.1 arm64 (macOS, Apple Silicon)

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Two files, no dependencies.

`main.ts`:

```ts
Bun.plugin({
  name: "repro",
  setup(build) {
    build.onResolve({ filter: /plain\.ts/ }, (args) => {
      console.log("[plugin] onResolve fired:", args.path)
      return undefined
    })
    build.onLoad({ filter: /plain\.ts/ }, (args) => {
      console.log("[plugin] onLoad fired:", args.path)
      return { contents: "export const source = 'plugin'", loader: "ts" }
    })
  },
})

const mod = await import(process.argv[2]).catch((err) => ({ source: "error: " + err.message }))
console.log("source =", mod.source)
```

`plain.ts`:

```ts
export const source = "disk"
```

Run:

```sh
bun main.ts "$PWD/plain.ts?v=123"
bun main.ts "$PWD/plain.ts?v=123.456"
```

Also reproduces identically in a compiled binary:

```sh
bun build --compile --outfile repro main.ts
./repro "$PWD/plain.ts?v=123"
./repro "$PWD/plain.ts?v=123.456"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Both imports go through the runtime plugin pipeline. Both filters match the specifier in both cases, so the output should be:

```
[plugin] onResolve fired: /.../plain.ts?v=123.456
[plugin] onLoad fired: /.../plain.ts?v=123.456
source = plugin
```

### What do you see instead?

With `?v=123` the plugin works:

```
[plugin] onResolve fired: /.../plain.ts?v=123
[plugin] onResolve fired: /.../plain.ts?v=123
[plugin] onLoad fired: /.../plain.ts?v=123
[plugin] onResolve fired: /.../plain.ts?v=123
source = plugin
```

With `?v=123.456` the plugin pipeline is bypassed entirely — neither `onResolve` nor `onLoad` is invoked, and the module is loaded from disk by Bun's native loader:

```
source = disk
```

The trigger is not "any dot in the query". Empirically, the plugin pipeline is skipped exactly when the text after the **last `.` in the full specifier** starts with a non-letter (digit, another dot, or end of string). Matrix of query strings appended to `plain.ts` (same results under plain `bun` and in a `bun build --compile` binary, Bun 1.3.14):

| query                     | plugin hooks fire? |
| ------------------------- | ------------------ |
| *(none)*                  | yes                |
| `?v=123`                  | yes                |
| `?v.x=1`                  | yes                |
| `?v=1.x`                  | yes                |
| `?v=1.x4`                 | yes

title: 🚀 Feature Request: let CSS `url()` references use the `file` loader
excerpt:
## What is the problem this feature would solve?

`Bun.build` always base64-inlines every `url()` reference in bundled CSS. A stylesheet pulling in a few font weights (e.g. any `@fontsource/*` package) balloons from a few KB to hundreds of KB, and there's no way to opt out:

```ts
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ['app.css'],
  outdir: 'out',
  loader: { '.woff2': 'file' }, // ignored — the font still inlines as a data: URI
  naming: { asset: 'fonts/[name]-[hash].[ext]' },
  publicPath: '/assets/',
});
```

The `file` loader, `naming.asset`, and `publicPath` all work as documented for JS-imported assets, but CSS `url()` ignores them (verified on 1.3.14 and 1.4.0). Plugins can't fill the gap either:

- `onLoad` returning `loader: 'file'` — the returned contents are inlined anyway.
- `onResolve` returning `{ path, external: true }` — stops the inlining, but the printed CSS keeps the *original* specifier; the rewritten path is discarded.

Minimal repro (all three cases, plus a JS control showing the same options working as documented): https://github.com/khromov/bun-css-url-file-loader-repro

## What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Have CSS `url()` references respect the configured loader: with `loader: { '.woff2': 'file' }`, copy the file to `outdir` per `naming.asset` and print `publicPath` + asset name into the CSS — same semantics the JS side already has (and what esbuild does for CSS). Honoring the path returned by `onResolve` for external CSS references would also work as a plugin-level escape hatch.

## What alternatives have you considered?

We currently work around it in [mochi-framework](https://github.com/khromov/mochi) with an `onLoad` plugin that swaps each font's bytes for a tiny unique marker (so the forced data: URI stays small), then post-processes the emitted CSS: extract the markers back out to content-hashed files, rewrite the `url()`s, and re-hash/rename the output file ourselves since Bun's `[hash]` was computed over the pre-rewrite text. It works, but it re-implements asset emission the bundler already has for JS.

title: Per-realm resource ownership: what a ShadowRealm / vm context leaves behind and what closing one would take
excerpt:
### Context

An embedder running one tenant per `ShadowRealm` (or per `node:vm` context) has no way to shut a tenant down: timers, watchers, sockets, servers and child processes created while the tenant's code was running stay alive when the realm is dropped, and there is no realm-level equivalent of `worker.terminate()`. This issue writes down what the runtime does today and what a teardown primitive would take. It is an investigation, not a proposal to implement yet.

### Summary

- Every native handle Bun creates records the global it was created from and roots its own JS wrapper while it is active. Inside a `ShadowRealm` that recorded global is the realm's global (a `ShadowRealm` in Bun is a full `Zig::GlobalObject`, `deriveShadowRealmGlobalObject` in `src/jsc/bindings/ZigGlobalObject.cpp`, and `defaultGlobalObject(lexical)` in `ZigGlobalObject.h` returns it as is). The rooted wrapper keeps the realm's global alive, so a dropped realm with a live handle is a leak of the whole realm, not a use after free: nothing fires into a collected global because a global with live handles cannot be collected. Once the last handle closes on its own (child exits, socket closes, watcher is closed) the realm becomes collectable.
- A `node:vm` context is different: `NodeVMGlobalObject` is not a `Zig::GlobalObject`, so every handle created from inside a context records the host's global. Handles created by a context are indistinguishable from the host's own; per-context teardown cannot be derived from ownership data that exists today and would need an explicit scope API.
- What is per realm is state the event loop only services for the thread's default global (`vm.global`): the nextTick queue (dead inside a realm until #37931), the unhandled rejection list (dead until #35646), and `process` events (`Process__dispatchOnBeforeExit` / `OnExit` in `src/jsc/bindings/BunProcess.cpp` are only ever called with `vm.global()`, `ExitHandler::dispatch_on_exit` in `src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs`, so a realm's `process.on('exit')` never fires). Handles are not in this category; they all work inside a realm.
- Bun has no registry of active native handles: `process.getActiveResourcesInfo` is `Process_stubFunctionReturningArray` (`BunProcess.cpp` property table). The only enumerable sets are (1) each global's `ScriptExecutionContext` (`src/jsc/bindings/ScriptExecutionContext.h`: `m_activeDOMObjects`, `m_destructionObservers`, `prepareForDestruction()`), which a `ShadowRealm` gets its own ins

title: Instantiating a --format=cjs bundle a second time costs ~48 bytes and ~0.1 us per module; no bundler-side deferral is worth doing
excerpt:
### Question

An embedder instantiates the same `bun build --format=cjs` bundle once per tenant in one process (the bundle is one `(function(exports, require, module, __filename, __dirname) {...})` expression, compiled once and called N times). How much does each additional instantiation cost, how much of it is eager module evaluation, and could the bundler defer any of it without changing semantics? This is the write-up of that measurement; the conclusion is that there is nothing worth changing in the bundler, so this issue mostly exists so the numbers are on record.

### How the cjs output is structured (1.4.0 main)

- An ESM file reached only through static `import` is never wrapped: `WrapKind` stays `None` (the default, `src/bundler/bundle_v2.rs` `enum WrapKind`) and the file's top level is emitted flat into the wrapper's scope, so a module that only declares functions contributes hoisted `function` declarations and nothing executes for it at load beyond creating those function objects. Top-level statements with effects run at load, in graph order, which is what ESM semantics require.
- A CommonJS file is always wrapped in `__commonJS(...)` and runs on first `require_x()` (`src/bundler/linker_context/scanImportsAndExports.rs` lines ~259-265, and the `ImportKind::Require` arm at ~225-235). An ESM file that is `require()`d or `import()`ed without splitting gets `WrapKind::Esm`, i.e. an `__esm(...)` init closure (same arms, ~229 and ~241).
- `--format=cjs` adds the outer function expression plus `__toCommonJS(entry_exports)` for the entry. Nothing else is evaluated eagerly on its behalf.

So today's output is already "lazy where the source is lazy, eager where ESM says eager"; there is no bundler-added eager work to remove.

### Measurements

Synthetic bundle: 3000 ESM modules each exporting a function, 100 CJS modules (50 required by the entry at load, 50 only inside a function that is never called), entry re-exporting everything; 200 KB of output containing 3000 hoisted `function` declarations, 100 `__commonJS(` wrappers and no `__esm(`. Release bun 1.4.0 (da3851e57), 3 fresh processes per configuration, N = 8 instantiations each, `bun:jsc` `heapStats()` deltas after `Bun.gc(true)`.

Instantiating the already-compiled wrapper again:

| | first instantiation | each additional one (median of 21) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wall | 11-13 ms (includes compiling the 3163 function bodies) | 0.26-0.5 ms (about 85-160 ns per module) |
| JSFunction cells | +3216 | +3

  TEMP="$ROOT/tmp" \
  BUN_TMPDIR="$ROOT/tmp" \
  BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR="$CACHE" \

title: Add JSON output to `bun pm pack`
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bun pm pack` has no machine-readable output mode. Its help documents `--quiet`, but not `--json`.

More importantly, `--json` is silently accepted and ignored.

Given:

```json
{
  "name": "foo",
  "version": "1.0.0"
}
```

and an `index.js` containing:

```js
export const value = 42;
```

Running:

```console
$ bun --revision
1.4.0-canary.1+b7a043103

$ bun pm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts
bun pack v1.4.0-canary.1 (b7a043103)

packed 42B package.json
packed 25B index.js

foo-1.0.0.tgz

Total files: 2
Unpacked size: 67B
```

The command exits successfully but emits human-oriented text instead of JSON. This is unsafe for automation because the requested output contract is neither honored nor rejected.

By comparison, npm 12.0.2 returns structured package and archive metadata for the same fixture:

```console
$ volta run --npm 12 -- npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts
{
  "foo": {
    "id": "foo@1.0.0",
    "name": "foo",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "size": 185,
    "unpackedSize": 67,
    "shasum": "443b9b8e54c94a2d9bc12514c0f8c91a8e27f69f",
    "integrity": "sha512-j8S69c6CfqxpjGr8puHwqtlRFKsTN3W3PHS8m/ytFnG9r82mouYT1srxRUHeq1eFIwY+WiOInBPp0oq8mxwa2w==",
    "filename": "foo-1.0.0.tgz",
    "files": [
      {
        "path": "index.js",
        "size": 25,
        "mode": 420
      },
      {
        "path": "package.json",
        "size": 42,
        "mode": 420
      }
    ],
    "entryCount": 2,
    "bundled": []
  }
}
```

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Add a documented `--json` flag to `bun pm pack`, usable with normal packing and `--dry-run`.

On success, stdout should contain only valid JSON with a stable, preferably npm-compatible schema containing at least:

- package name, version, and identifier;
- output filename;
- packed and unpacked sizes;
- integrity and checksum values;
- packed file paths, sizes, and modes;
- entry and bundled-dependency counts.

On failure, JSON mode should return a structured error while preserving a nonzero exit status.

If JSON output cannot be supported yet, Bun should reject `--json` instead of silently accepting and ignoring it.

bun test 1.3.13+ SIGTRAP (JSC GC recursive-mark crash) with accumulated React/happy-dom state in shared-global mode — regression from 1.3.12
excerpt:
## Summary

`bun test` (default shared-global mode, no --isolate) crashes with SIGTRAP (exit 133) after the current file's tests all pass — at the file boundary, once enough cross-file state has accumulated in the shared global. Every test passes; the process dies. `--isolate` and `--parallel=N` both avoid it.

Regression window is tight and verified by binary bisect: **bun 1.2.23, 1.3.1, 1.3.4, 1.3.8, 1.3.10, 1.3.12 all green; 1.3.13 and 1.3.14 crash** (macOS arm64, happy-dom 20.11.2, React 19.2.8, @testing-library/react 16).

## Crash signature

- EXC_BREAKPOINT (`brk #0x3910` — WebKit `CRASH()`/WTFCrash), SIGTRAP, termination "Trace/BPT trap: 5".
- Faulting thread: the main thread, inside JSC GC — a run of recursive frames (mark/scan visitor), consistent with the GC parallel-marking family (#34476, open, 1.3.14).
- Deterministic on the repro (3/3 runs), order-independent.

## Repro recipe (deterministic, in a private app — no public repo yet)

Two test files run together in one process (shared-global mode):

- File A (~28 tests): each renders a CodeMirror editor + tooltips under happy-dom/@testing-library/react.
- File B (3 tests): each renders a task panel with a chat event stream.

Each file alone: green, exit 0. The pair together: 3/3 SIGTRAP at the boundary after the last test. Accumulation across files in the shared global is required — no single file, no single component triggers it.

The crash is NOT component-library-specific: it reproduces with all third-party UI components mocked away (plain divs/buttons) as long as the same app-level DOM/stream state accumulates. Pre-migration app code (same test files, fewer mounted component types) is green — the migration simply crossed an accumulation threshold that 1.3.12 and earlier handled fine.

## Impact

Any multi-file suite with per-file React/happy-dom DOM churn in the default shared-global mode crashes on 1.3.13+; the only workarounds are `--isolate`/`--parallel` (per-file globals) or staying on ≤1.3.12. This looks like a JSC GC regression introduced in 1.3.13 (parallel marking), not a JS-level bug — happy to provide more traces or run a repro against a canary.

title: bunfig.toml: support [test] isolate = true — test isolation should be configurable, not CLI-only
excerpt:
## Request

Support `isolate` as a `[test]` key in `bunfig.toml` (e.g. `isolate = true`), so a project can opt into per-file global isolation at the config level instead of passing `--isolate` on every `bun test` invocation.

## Current state

`--isolate` is CLI-only. Setting `isolate = true` in `bunfig.toml` `[test]` is **silently ignored** (verified on bun 1.3.14: the documented `[test]` keys are `preload`, `root`, `smol`, `retry`, `rerunEach`, `coverage*` — `isolate` and `parallel` are absent). Unlike `preload` — which IS configurable — isolation is a suite-wide safety property that currently has to be remembered by every script and every ad-hoc invocation.

## Why it matters

Suites that need isolation (hygiene, or because the default shared-global mode can crash — see #38211: JSC GC SIGTRAP from cross-file accumulation on 1.3.13+) currently depend on the package.json test script carrying the flag. A bare `bun test` in the repo silently runs the unsafe mode. Config-level support makes the safe mode the project default, exactly like `preload` works today.

`--parallel=N` implies `--isolate`, but `parallel` is a per-machine performance knob; the ask here is `isolate` — a correctness/safety property that belongs in project config.

## Expected

```toml
[test]
isolate = true
preload = ["./preload.ts"]
```

`bun test` then runs with per-file isolation without any flag.

title: Harden tool bootstrap in .buildkite/scripts/upload-release.sh
excerpt:
Follow-up to review feedback from @tcely on #28932 (threads there flagged pre-existing code that PR deliberately did not touch).

`.buildkite/scripts/upload-release.sh` bootstraps its own tooling on the release agent, and several aspects deserve hardening:

- `install_gh_linux` downloads a release tarball and installs the binary without verifying a checksum or signature. The gh project publishes checksums alongside releases; pinning a version and verifying would close this.
- `install_aws_linux` extracts and runs the AWS CLI installer from an unverified zip. AWS publishes PGP signatures for the installer.
- `install_sentry_cli_linux` pipes `curl https://sentry.io/get-cli/` straight into `sh`, executing whatever the endpoint returns. At minimum the script should pin a version and verify a checksum rather than executing an arbitrary response.
- `assert_command`'s Linux fallback only knows brew and three hardcoded installers; `apt-get`/`dnf` arms would cover most distributions.
- Shell settings: the script uses `#!/bin/bash` (consider `#!/usr/bin/env bash` so non-/bin installs work) and `set -eo pipefail` without `-u`. Enabling nounset needs an audit first: existing checks like `[ -z "$BUILDKITE_REPO" ]` and `[ -z "$CANARY" ]` become unbound-variable aborts under `-u` and would need `${VAR:-}` defaults.

These run on the production release pipeline, so each change should be reviewed on its own rather than riding along on an unrelated fix.

title: RedisClient: support Redis Sentinel (master discovery + failover following)
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

The [Redis docs page](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/redis) lists Redis Sentinel as unsupported. Self-hosted HA Redis very commonly runs Sentinel — it's the default HA topology outside managed offerings and Cluster (Bitnami charts, spotahome/redis-operator, etc.). A client that can't speak the Sentinel protocol can't be pointed at those deployments at all: there is no stable master address to hand to `new RedisClient(url)` — the master moves between nodes on failover, and only the sentinels know where it is.

This is currently the single blocker keeping us (and, I suspect, many production Kubernetes users) on ioredis. We benchmarked Bun's RedisClient through BullMQ v6's `createBunRedisClient` adapter against ioredis on the same workload (10k jobs, concurrency 32): ~10–12% faster enqueue throughput and ~33% lower peak RSS (~40 MiB less per worker process — significant in 256Mi cgroup pods). We'd switch tomorrow, but production connects via Sentinel, so `Bun.redis` is not an option regardless of how good the client is.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Sentinel mode in `RedisClient`, following the [Sentinel clients spec](https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/reference/sentinel-clients/):

```ts
const client = new RedisClient({
  sentinels: [{ host: "sentinel-0", port: 26379 }, { host: "sentinel-1", port: 26379 }],
  name: "mymaster",           // master group name
  password: "...",            // auth for the master
  sentinelPassword: "...",    // auth for the sentinels
});
```

- On connect: ask a reachable sentinel for the current master (`SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name <name>`), then connect to it.
- On failover: subscribe to the sentinels' `+switch-master` channel and reconnect to the newly announced master promptly, rather than discovering the demotion lazily via failed writes / `READONLY` replies.
- On reconnect: re-run master discovery from the sentinel list (sentinels can also be re-discovered via `SENTINEL sentinels <name>`).

ioredis's Sentinel support is the de-facto reference for the option shape and semantics.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Staying on ioredis (works, but gives up the performance and memory advantages of the native client).
- Sentinel-aware proxies (HAProxy with sentinel health checks, redis-sentinel-proxy) to present a stable endpoint — adds an infra hop and another failover-tracking component to operate.

title: Segfault when terminating Workers that have in-flight fetch() requests (v1.3.14)
Windows x64: segfault in NAPI path after repeated AbortError in msgpackr-extract binding
excerpt:
## Environment

- **Bun**: 1.3.14 (commit `0d9b296a`, baseline build, x64)
- **OS**: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.28120)
- **Arch**: x64 (sse4.2 avx avx2)
- **Host process**: `opencode.exe` v1.18.18 (user-agent `opencode/1.18.18`), PID running ~706s before crash, RSS 1.00 GB, Commit 1.55 GB
- **Native module in use**: `@msgpackr-extract/msgpackr-extract-win32-x64` (loads `node.abi115.node` + `node.napi.node`)

## Crash report

https://bun.report/1.3.14/ea10d9b296m5G+gooc_C8B.bdebb9ffff7f3fec-00000000.d11suwmCC8B.bdebb9ffff7f3fec-00000000.d11qxumC_is33sB__A28N91qy8uB

- `panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0xDED11B6AA2` — non-canonical user-mode address (classic NAPI deref pattern, lower bits `DE`/`DEDE`).

## Repro

1. Install any app that:
   - Runs on Bun 1.3.14 on Windows x64.
   - Loads `@msgpackr-extract/msgpackr-extract-win32-x64` as an optional/native dep (transitively via `msgpackr`).
   - Performs repeated `fetch()` requests with AbortController that get aborted mid-flight (e.g. long-poll auto-sync).
2. In our case: `opencode-omniroute-plugin@0.2.6` performs `autoSync` every 5 min against `http://localhost:20128`. Just before the segfault the stderr shows two identical lines:
   ```
   [omniroute-plugin] auto-sync failed providerId=opencode-omniroute: The operation was aborted.
   [omniroute-plugin] auto-sync failed providerId=opencode-omniroute: The operation was aborted.
   ```
3. Bun crashes. `oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.`

## Expected

Bun should survive repeated AbortError + NAPI serialization round-trips without segfaulting, even when the AbortController fires mid-fetch.

## Actual

Main-thread segfault inside the Bun process running `opencode.exe`. The non-canonical address (all `0xDEDE…` nibbles) strongly suggests a NULL+offset dereference in a NAPI/JSC binding (most likely the `msgpackr-extract` thread-local storage or its internal buffer), triggered shortly after a fetch is aborted.

## Notes

- `bun.report` minidump already includes the crash data; nothing more to attach.
- The trigger is reproducible in production for any Bun-on-Windows user of `opencode-omniroute-plugin`, but the root cause is in Bun, not the plugin — the plugin only calls `fetch()` + `AbortController.abort()`, which is standard.
- Workaround applied on our end: disable the plugin's auto-sync (`autoSyncIntervalMs: 0`).

title: Harden SHASUMS256.txt verification in dockerhub Dockerfiles
excerpt:
Follow-up from review discussion on #28932 (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/28932#discussion_r3785546327).

Two related problems in the `dockerhub/{alpine,debian,debian-slim,distroless}/Dockerfile` manifest verification step:

1. **Separator coupling.** All four Dockerfiles verify with `grep " bun-linux-$build.zip$" SHASUMS256.txt | sha256sum -c -`, which only matches the two-space text-mode line form (`HASH  NAME`). The sha256sum binary-mode form (`HASH *NAME`) is equally valid output that `sha256sum -c` accepts, but the grep rejects it because the character before the name is `*`, not a space. #28932 conformed its manifest producer to the two-space form to avoid breaking these consumers, but the greps should tolerate both separators (e.g. `grep -E "[ *]bun-linux-$build\.zip$"`) so a future producer emitting the binary-mode marker cannot break or bypass verification.

2. **Alpine fails open on an empty grep.** On BusyBox (alpine), `sha256sum -c -` with empty stdin exits 0, so if the grep matches nothing the pipeline succeeds and the image build proceeds **without verifying the archive at all**. GNU coreutils (debian/slim/distroless) exits 1 with "no properly formatted checksum lines found", which at least fails closed. The check should be restructured to fail when the grep finds no line, for example:

   ```sh
   line="$(grep -E "[ *]bun-linux-$build\.zip$" SHASUMS256.txt)" \
     && echo "$line" | sha256sum -c -
   ```

   so an empty match is an error on every base image instead of a silent verification bypass on alpine.

These are published Dockerfiles users build against release artifacts, so each change deserves its own review rather than riding on #28932.

title: Switch SHASUMS256.txt producers to the binary-mode separator once consumers tolerate it
excerpt:
Follow-up from review discussion on #28932 (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/28932#discussion_r3785546327), sequenced after #38595.

The published `SHASUMS256.txt` uses the two-space text-mode separator (`HASH  NAME`) because the dockerhub Dockerfile consumers grep for a space immediately before the filename (see #38595). The binary-mode form (`HASH *NAME`) is the more correct one for zip archives: it tells `sha256sum -c` to open the file in binary mode, which avoids line-ending translation on platforms where O_TEXT and O_BINARY differ (Windows, Cygwin, msys).

Once #38595 lands and the consumers accept both separators, switch both producers to the binary-mode form in one PR:

- `scripts/sign-release-manifest.sh` (the Buildkite inline signer): change the collation `printf '%s  %s\n'` to `printf '%s *%s\n'` and update the format comment plus the pinned assertions in `test/regression/issue/28931.test.ts`.
- `packages/bun-release/scripts/upload-assets.ts` (the daily sign cron): change the `` `${sha256}  ${name}` `` template to `` `${sha256} *${name}` ``.

Both producers must switch together: they write the same published file, and the byte-level identity between `SHASUMS256.txt` and the clearsigned `.asc` body is what end-to-end verification checks. `scripts/validate-digests.ts` already accepts both forms and needs no change.

Ordering constraint: do not switch the producers before #38595 is fixed AND the updated Dockerfiles are what users actually build from, otherwise canary Docker builds fail on GNU sha256sum and silently skip verification on Alpine's BusyBox.

package-lock.json migration fails with InvalidNPMLockfile for npm.pkg.github.com scopes missing resolved+integrity, then silently re-resolves
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0-canary.1+eabb96de728f37a3d2048276a77fd254880fb504

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 (Apple Silicon)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`package-lock.json` migration fails with `InvalidNPMLockfile` when a scope is pointed at **`npm.pkg.github.com`** and that package's lockfile entry has neither `resolved` nor `integrity`.

That entry shape is not contrived: `npm install --package-lock-only` produces it when deriving a lockfile from an already-installed `node_modules`, recording versions read off disk without refetching registry metadata. That is the natural route when moving a repo onto Bun from a package manager whose lockfile Bun can't read (e.g. Yarn Berry).

Three files, no private packages needed — migration never hits the network:

```jsonc
// package.json
{ "name": "repro", "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "@babel/code-frame": "7.27.1" } }
```

```toml
# bunfig.toml
[install.scopes]
"@babel" = { url = "https://npm.pkg.github.com" }
```

```jsonc
// package-lock.json — the entry deliberately has no "resolved" and no "integrity"
{ "name": "repro", "version": "1.0.0", "lockfileVersion": 3, "requires": true,
  "packages": {
    "": { "name": "repro", "version": "1.0.0",
          "dependencies": { "@babel/code-frame": "7.27.1" } },
    "node_modules/@babel/code-frame": { "version": "7.27.1", "license": "MIT" }
  } }
```

```sh
bun pm migrate
# error: Error loading lockfile: InvalidNPMLockfile
```

Now change only the scope URL and rerun — the same lockfile migrates:

| `[install.scopes]` url for `@babel` | `bun pm migrate` |
| --- | --- |
| `https://registry.npmjs.org/` | migrates (0.10 ms) |
| `https://example-registry.invalid/` | migrates (0.09 ms) |
| **`https://npm.pkg.github.com`** | **`InvalidNPMLockfile`** |

Adding either `resolved` or `integrity` back to the entry also makes it migrate. So the failure needs the combination: GitHub Packages scope **and** both fields absent.

I suspect this is about GitHub Packages' non-standard tarball layout — `https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/<name>/<version>/<sha>` rather than `<registry>/<name>/-/<basename>-<version>.tgz` — so the URL can't be synthesized from name and version the way it can for other registries.

### What is the expected behavior?

Migrate the lockfile, deferring URL resolution to install time; or fail with an error naming the offending entry. Entries on other registries already migrate fine without these field

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```ts

Compare with `file.slice(0, size).stream()` instead of `file.stream()`. That path finishes immediately.

### What is the expected behavior?

`S3File.stream()` should emit exactly `stat().size` bytes and close. HTTP/1.1 clients should finish as soon as the object is sent. `slice(0, size).stream()` and unsliced `.stream()` should behave the same for a full object.

### What do you see instead?

Against a 5,643,270-byte MP3 (`HeadObject` `ContentLength`):

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| HTTP/1.1 `GET` (no `Range`) using `.stream()` | `200` in ~160ms, then the body **stalls ~30s** at 5,635,992 bytes. Total ~31.8s. Final size **5,643,291** (+21). |
| HTTP/1.1 `GET` `Range: bytes=0-` (slice stream) | `206` in ~0.26s. Same +21 bytes. |
| HTTP/1.1 `GET` `Range: bytes=0-1` | `206`, `Content-Length: 2`, ~0.25s, exact. |
| HTTP/2 `GET` | Completes in ~0.44s. Still +21 bytes. |

title: Report GitHub API quota usage around release jobs
excerpt:
Follow-up from review discussion on #28932 (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/28932#pullrequestreview-4065511502).

During review of the release-upload path, two API-efficiency goals were discussed:

1. **Cross-asset batching of uploads and verification.** This has since landed via the `upload-release.sh` restructure: `upload_github_assets` is now a single batched `gh release upload <tag> <files...> --clobber` call, and the per-asset verify/retry loop is gone. Nothing further needed here; noted for the record.

2. **GitHub API quota visibility around release jobs (still open).** The release pipeline (Buildkite upload step and the release.yml jobs) should:
   - check the current rate-limit state before starting (`gh api rate_limit`, or the `x-ratelimit-*` response headers), and warn or fail early when the remaining budget is too low to complete the release, rather than dying midway with assets partially clobbered;
   - report actual API usage after the release completes (remaining before vs after), as a running summary of how the optimization effort is doing and to catch regressions that reintroduce per-asset call patterns.

The general goal is to stay comfortably under the API limits on busy days (every push to main re-uploads the full canary asset set, and the new validate job adds a metadata call per run).

title: bunfig.toml [test] should support `parallel` (and `timeout`) like the CLI flags
excerpt:
## Feature request

`bun test` has `--parallel` (files across worker processes, implies `--isolate`) and `--timeout` CLI flags, but the `bunfig.toml` `[test]` section has no config keys for them — the documented keys are only `root`, `preload`, `pathIgnorePatterns`, `smol`, `coverage*`, `rerunEach`, `randomize`, `seed`, `retry`, `onlyFailures`, `reporter`, `ts` (https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig, https://bun.com/docs/test/parallel).

## Why it matters

CLI flags have to live in every package's `package.json` test script (`"test": "bun test --parallel"`) — per-package boilerplate that is easy to miss, and any invocation of `bun test` outside the script (pre-commit hooks, CI steps, ad-hoc runs) silently falls back to the serial default. A config key in `bunfig.toml` would make parallelism the repo's single source of truth, exactly like the other `[test]` options.

## Proposal

```toml
[test]
parallel = true      # or parallel = 8
timeout = 10000      # per-test timeout in ms, mirrors --timeout
```

Expected semantics mirror the flags: `parallel` runs files across N worker processes (default = number of CPU cores, implies per-file isolation), `timeout` sets the default per-test timeout.

title: --compile loads any non-ASCII module as a 16-bit heap copy instead of the mmapped section
excerpt:
### What

In a `bun build --compile` executable, a JavaScript module whose bundled text is pure ASCII is handed to JSC as a zero-copy 8-bit external string over the mmapped section (`StandaloneModuleGraph.rs`: `Encoding::Latin1` is chosen at build time when `first_non_ascii` finds nothing, and `to_wtf_string` wraps the bytes with `create_static_external`). Any other module takes the `clone_utf8` arm, which transcodes the whole module into a 16-bit heap string at startup. The mmapped bytes stay mapped as well, so such an executable holds roughly three bytes of source per character instead of one; on a bundle with a single non-ASCII preserved comment this measures at about twice the bundle size of extra RSS.

Today this is triggered by a non-ASCII `/*! */` comment, `--banner` / `--footer` text, or a client-side chunk. Once #33866 lands, regex literals and tagged template raw text are no longer escaped to ASCII either, so any bundle containing a non-ASCII regex or raw template also takes the slow arm. That PR does not change how often the copy happens for text that was already verbatim, but it makes the condition much more common, which is why this is worth fixing separately.

### Suggested fix

Store each compiled module in the width it will be loaded in, the same way the runtime transpiler cache does after #33866 (`LATIN1` / `UTF16` tags):

- at build time, if the module text is not ASCII, convert it once: to Latin-1 bytes when every character is at or below U+00FF, otherwise to UTF-16 code units (the section needs 2-byte alignment for that case);
- record the width in the graph's per-file `Encoding` and, at runtime, wrap the section with an 8-bit or 16-bit static external string instead of calling `clone_utf8`;
- generate `--bytecode` from the stored form so the SourceCodeKey matches; the generators in `ZigSourceProvider.cpp` take a `Latin1` / `Utf16` input after #33866, so only the call site in `bundle_v2.rs` needs to pass the stored width.

Non-JavaScript-like files and client chunks can keep the current `Binary` handling.

Noted during review of #33866.

### What platform is your computer?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

I have connection pinning via an undici Agent whose connect.lookup hook returns the pre-resolved IP — this prevents a second DNS lookup at connect time and defeats DNS rebinding (TOCTOU).

Bun resolves undici to its own built-in compatibility shim, whose Agent is an inert stub: the dispatcher option passed to undiciFetch is ignored outright, so the request goes through Bun's ordinary fetch and the OS resolver runs again at connect time — exactly the second lookup the pin exists to prevent.

The protection is genuine under Node, but not under node.

ref: https://github.com/workglow-dev/libs/issues/789

Reproducer
Pin connect.lookup at a black-hole address. If the dispatcher were honored the request could not reach 127.0.0.1.

title: bun patch silently applies hunks at stale + offsets, corrupting patched files
bun update and bun dedupe undo each other forever
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0-canary.1+39fb3c103

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "cookie": "^1.1.1",
    "@types/cookie": "^1.0.0"
  }
}
```

```sh
bun install
bun dedupe   # removes cookie@2.0.1
bun update   # adds it back
bun dedupe   # removes it again
bun update   # adds it back ... forever
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun update` and `bun dedupe` should agree on a stable lockfile. Running them in sequence should reach a fixed point.

### What do you see instead?

They undo each other indefinitely:

```
after install:  cookie@1.1.1  cookie@2.0.1
after dedupe:   cookie@1.1.1
after update:   cookie@1.1.1  cookie@2.0.1
after dedupe:   cookie@1.1.1
after update:   cookie@1.1.1  cookie@2.0.1
```

`@types/cookie` declares `"cookie": "*"`.

- `bun update` moves every edge to the newest version its own range allows, so the `*` edge goes to `2.0.1` and a second copy is added.
- `bun dedupe` collapses onto the fewest versions that satisfy everyone, and `1.1.1` also satisfies `*`, so it removes `2.0.1`.

Neither is wrong on its own, but together they never settle. This happens whenever a wide range (`*`) sits alongside a narrower one for the same package.

Minor, possibly related: the `bun update` row for this reads

```
↑ cookie 1.1.1 → 2.0.1
```

which looks like the top-level `cookie` was bumped to a new major. It wasn't — the top-level stays at `1.1.1` and a nested copy is added. Labelling nested/transitive rows would make this clearer.

1.4.0-canary.1+39fb3c103

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A workspace root with a catalog, and two members — only `api` uses the catalog entry:

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "mono",
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"],
  "catalog": {
    "is-odd": "^2.0.0"

`packages/web/package.json`:

```

`packages/api/package.json`:

```json

  "name": "api",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": {
    "is-odd": "catalog:"
  }
}
```

```sh
bun install
# api resolves is-odd@2.0.0

bun add is-odd@3.0.1 --catalog --filter web
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`--filter web` should only affect `web`. Since `3.0.1` does not satisfy the existing catalog range `^2.0.0`, overwriting the shared catalog entry silently changes every other workspace that references it. I would expect either a warning, an error, or a separate catalog entry.

### What do you see instead?

```

2 packages installed
```

```diff

-  "is-odd": "^2.0.0"
+  "is-odd": "3.0.1"
 }
```

And `api` — which was not named in `--filter` and whose `package.json` is unchanged — is silently moved across a major version:

```

after:   is-odd@3.0.1
```

`packages/api/package.json` still just says `"is-odd": "catalog:"`, so nothing in the diff of that workspace hints that its dependency changed major version.

title: Switching from isolated to hoisted linker leaves the whole store behind and bun prune refuses to clean it
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0-canary.1+39fb3c103

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Install with the isolated linker, then switch the project to the hoisted linker.

```sh
bun install --linker=isolated

printf '[install]\nlinker = "hoisted"\n' > bunfig.toml
bun install

bun prune
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Switching linkers should leave `node_modules` containing only the new layout, or `bun prune` should be able to clean up the old one.

### What do you see instead?

The isolated store is left behind in full. On a Next.js app with 519 packages:

```
isolated install:         755 MB, node_modules/.bun has 522 entries
after switch to hoisted: 1113 MB, node_modules/.bun still has 522 entries
after bun install --force: 1570 MB
```

The hoisted layout is correct and working — the old store is just never removed, and re-running install keeps growing the directory.

`bun prune` then refuses to clean it:

```
error: node_modules was installed with the isolated linker, but bun prune would use the hoisted linker
note: run 'bun prune --linker isolated' to prune it as-is, or 'bun install' to reinstall with the hoisted linker
```

Two problems with that message:

1. `node_modules` was **not** installed with the isolated linker — it was just reinstalled with the hoisted one. The detection appears to key off the leftover `.bun` directory, which is exactly the garbage that needs removing.
2. The suggested remedy, `bun install` to reinstall with the hoisted linker, is the step that was already run and is what produced this state.

`bun prune --production` fails the same way. `bun install --force` does not clean it either. The only fix I found is `rm -rf node_modules`.

title: SIGTRAP (EXC_BREAKPOINT) at exit after bun test passes — cancelling a ReadableStream whose start() is still awaiting
excerpt:
## What happens

`bun test` on a 35-file React/happy-dom suite **exits 133 (SIGTRAP) after every test has passed and the summary has printed.** The run reports `310 pass, 0 fail`, then the process dies.

macOS writes a crash report for each one, and the signature is identical across **8 of 8** collected:

```
exception   EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
codes       0x0000000000000001, 0x0000000104b37160
thread      com.apple.main-thread
frames      bun +30339424
            bun +3920848
            bun +18764416
            bun +4980980
            <jit>
            bun +53004380
            ...
```

`EXC_BREAKPOINT` on the main thread is why this is filed as a bug rather than as a question: userland JavaScript should not be able to reach a release assertion. Note also that **bun's own crash handler never fires** — there is no panic message, no `bun.report` URL, nothing on stdout or stderr. The process simply exits 133. That may be worth looking at independently of the crash itself.

```
bun     1.3.14+0d9b296af
os      macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Darwin 25.5.0
arch    arm64
```

## What triggers it

Reduced to a single line in a single test. The app under test has a `ReadableStream` whose `start()` awaits an in-flight `fetch` and reads its SSE body; the test clicks a "Stop" button, which aborts the fetch **and cancels the outer stream while its `start()` is still awaiting**.

Deleting that one click is the difference between a crash and a clean run:

| variant | full-suite exit codes |
|---|---|
| as written | `133 133 133 133` |
| test's `fetch` stub replaced with a bare promise — no `Response`, no `ReadableStream`, rejects with `AbortError` on the signal | `133 133 133 133` |
| stub replaced with a promise that **never settles and ignores the signal entirely** | `133 133 133 133` |
| same never-settling stub, **`fireEvent.click(stop)` removed** | `0 0 0 0` |

The third and fourth rows are the informative pair. With no stream, no rejection and no abort anywhere in the fake `fetch`, it still crashes — and removing the click makes it clean. So the crash is not in the mocked network at all; it is the application's own teardown path: cancelling a JS `ReadableStream` whose `start()` has not returned.

## It is probabilistic, and it scales with what runs afterwards

This is the part that makes it easy to misdiagnose:

| scope | crash rate |
|---|---|
| that test file alone | 0% |
| paired with one other file | ~60% |
| all 35 files | 100% (3/3, then 2/2, then 4/4) |

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.6.127-android15-8-g74246892e200-ab15480978-4k aarch64 unknown, Native Termux on Android 16 (API level 36), aarch64, running on an ASUS ROG Phone 9 Pro Edition with a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite (`ASUSAI2501C`, device code `ASUSAI2501`). asus/TJAI2501/ASUSAI2501:16/BQ2A.250525.001/36.0810.1810.86:user/release-keys. This occurs when Bun runs directly in Termux, rather than inside a PRoot Linux distribution.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Run a normal package installation in native Termux without the workaround:

```sh
mkdir bun-install-sigsys-repro
cd bun-install-sigsys-repro
bun init -y
bun add fast-deep-equal
```

On the affected Android environment, the process is terminated by `SIGSYS` when the Android seccomp policy blocks a newer syscall instead of returning `ENOSYS` or `EPERM`.

Testing with a temporary aarch64 `SIGSYS` shim identified two syscalls reached during installation:

- `openat2`
- `fchmodat2`

The shim changes the interrupted syscall return register to `-ENOSYS`. With both syscalls handled this way, the same installation completes successfully. This suggests that the crash is caused by Bun issuing these syscalls directly under an Android seccomp policy that reports the denial using `SIGSYS`.

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun install` should not be terminated when the Android kernel/seccomp policy does not permit `openat2` or `fchmodat2`.

Bun should detect that these syscalls are unavailable and use an Android-compatible fallback while preserving the relevant path-containment and symlink-safety properties.

### What do you see instead?

Without the workaround, `bun install` is killed by `SIGSYS`.

The existing errno-based fallbacks cannot run because the seccomp denial delivers a signal rather than returning `ENOSYS` or `EPERM` to the syscall caller.

With the workaround below, the syscall appears to Bun as returning `ENOSYS`, and installation succeeds.

Output from the exact reproduction above:

```console
$ bun add fast-deep-equal
bun add v1.4.0-canary.1 (88a639883)
fish: Job 1, 'bun add fast-deep-equal' terminated by signal SIGSYS (Bad system call)
$ echo $status
159

Repeating the same command with the shim succeeds:

```console
$ env LD_PRELOAD="$LD_PRELOAD:$HOME/test/preload_openat2_sigsys.so" bun add fast-deep-equal

feat(pm): support package-name wildcards in bun rm and bun update
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Migrating an application away from a meta-framework or switching design systems often requires removing or updating an entire family of direct dependencies. Today, `bun remove` and `bun update` require every package name to be listed explicitly. The existing `--filter` option selects workspaces; it does not select dependency names.

For example, migrating an application may require touching every installed `@lucide-react/*` or `@next/*` dependency. Maintaining a manual list is error-prone and makes automated migration scripts brittle as packages are added or removed.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Allow quoted wildcard patterns in package arguments for `bun remove` and `bun update`. A wildcard should be expanded against the direct dependency names in the current package.json before the command runs.

```sh
# Remove every matching direct dependency from the current project
bun rm "@lucide-react/*"

# Update every matching direct dependency
bun update -d "@next/*"
```

Suggested behavior:

- Match package names, not workspace names and not transitive dependencies.
- Apply the command to every matching direct dependency, regardless of the dependency section it is declared in (while retaining the command's existing flags/semantics).
- Keep `--filter` exclusively for workspace selection, so the two mechanisms can be combined in monorepos.
- Report a clear non-zero error when no direct dependency matches.
- Require quoting glob patterns so the shell does not expand them first.

This would make migration and cleanup workflows concise, repeatable, and auditable without requiring a custom jq/xargs script.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Enumerating every package explicitly: works, but is tedious and easy to miss packages.
- Reading package.json with jq and passing its matching keys to `bun remove`/`bun update`: workable, but platform/shell-specific and not as discoverable or portable as CLI support.
- Using `--filter`: this selects workspaces, whereas this proposal needs to select dependency names within a manifest.

Related: #27897 added workspace filtering for `bun remove`; this proposal is intentionally about dependency-name matching instead.

title: bun dedupe: --check and --dry-run print identical output, and prune has no CI gate at all
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0-canary.1+39fb3c103

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On a project whose `bun.lock` has duplicate versions (7 here, in a Next.js app with 633 packages):

```sh
bun dedupe --check           ; echo "exit=$?"
bun dedupe --dry-run         ; echo "exit=$?"
bun dedupe --frozen-lockfile ; echo "exit=$?"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Three flags that all decline to write should be distinguishable from their output, and the flag set should be consistent between `dedupe` and `prune`.

### What do you see instead?

**`--check` and `--dry-run` produce byte-identical output.** Diffing the two captures gives only the timing figure:

```diff
-7 duplicate versions can be removed (checked 633 packages) [6.00ms]
+7 duplicate versions can be removed (checked 633 packages) [4.00ms]
```

Both print the seven rows, the summary, and the `bun dedupe` remedy line. The only real difference is the exit code — `--check` exits 1, `--dry-run` exits 0.

That split is reasonable in itself (one informs, one gates), but the help text implies a different split:

```
--check      Exit with code 1 if the lockfile has duplicate versions that can be removed, without changing anything
--dry-run    Print the duplicate versions that would be removed without changing anything
```

Reading that, `--check` sounds like the quiet gate and `--dry-run` like the verbose preview. In practice both are verbose, so nothing on screen tells you which one you ran, and in CI logs the two are indistinguishable.

**`--frozen-lockfile` is `--check` with different framing.** Same rows, same exit code 1, same refusal to write — only the last lines differ:

```
7 duplicate versions can be removed (checked 633 packages) [4.00ms]
error: 7 duplicate versions can be removed, but --frozen-lockfile was passed
note: run 'bun dedupe' to remove them, or 'bun dedupe --check' in CI
```

The note recommends `bun dedupe --check`, which is the flag that already does this. `--frozen-lockfile` earns its place when it is inherited from config or CI environment rather than typed, but as something you would reach for deliberately it is dominated by `--check`.

**`prune` has neither.** `bun prune --help` offers `--dry-run` only, and `bun prune --production --dry-run` exits 0 even when it would remove 264 packages. So there is no way to gate `prune` in CI the way `dedupe --check` gates dedupe, even though the two commands were introduced together and are otherwise parallel.

### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bun dedupe` tells you what moved but never who wanted it:

```
↳ @types/node 25.9.1 → 22.19.19
↳ @types/unist 2.0.11 → 3.0.3
↳ hasown 2.0.3 → 2.0.4

Two rows here need context the output does not give:

- `@types/node 25.9.1 → 22.19.19` is a three-major downgrade, rendered exactly like the patch bumps around it. Whether that is fine depends entirely on who pinned `^22`.
- `undici-types 7.24.6` has no arrow at all, because it is dropped rather than moved. In a column of arrows it reads like truncated output.

Answering either question today means running `bun why` afterwards, once per package.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Add **one level** of dependents under each row — the packages that requested it, grouped by the range they asked for:

```

    wanted ^2.0.2   by es-abstract, es-set-tostringtag, es-shim-unscopables +7 more
    wanted ^2.0.4   by form-data

↳ @types/node 25.9.1 → 22.19.19
    wanted *          by @types/jsonwebtoken, sharp
    wanted ^22.10.10  by alistair

↳ undici-types 7.24.6 → (removed)
    wanted >=7.24.0 <7.24.7  by @types/node@25.9.1

title: fetch: NO_PROXY CIDR entries (e.g. 127.0.0.0/8) are not matched — loopback requests routed through HTTP_PROXY
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (Linux x64, also reproduced via the Bun runtime embedded in opencode 1.18.18)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-29-generic)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```bash
# terminal 1: any local HTTP server on loopback
python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1

# terminal 2: a LAN/HTTP proxy in env, NO_PROXY using CIDR notation
export HTTP_PROXY=http://10.0.0.2:8080
export NO_PROXY="127.0.0.0/8"
bun -e 'const r = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:8080/"); console.log(r.status)'
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`NO_PROXY` CIDR entries should match, so `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` is fetched **directly**. CIDR notation in `NO_PROXY` is widely deployed (distro defaults, corporate proxy configs, `gsettings`/`systemd` generators) and is supported by curl, Go (`golang.org/x/net/http/httpproxy`), wget, etc.

### What do you see instead?

The request is sent to the proxy (in my environment the proxy answers `502 Bad Gateway` because it cannot reach my machine's loopback; with an unreachable proxy the fetch fails with a proxy-connection error).

Verified matrix (Bun 1.3.14, same server, only `NO_PROXY` changed):

| `NO_PROXY` | Result |
|---|---|
| `127.0.0.0/8` (CIDR) | **proxied — bug** |
| `127.0.0.1` (literal) | direct ✅ |
| `localhost` | direct ✅ |
| `*` | direct ✅ |

Letter case (`NO_PROXY` vs `no_proxy`) makes no difference — both are honored for literal entries.

### Additional information

From reading the current matching implementation (e.g. `isNoProxy()` added in #26608 and the ongoing work in #37429 / #35145), supported forms are `*`, exact host, `host:port`, domain suffix, and bracketed IPv6 — CIDR ranges are not matched anywhere.

Related: #32045 (`NO_PROXY` honored inconsistently across subsystems), #6339 (`NO_PROXY` whitespace parsing), #1440 (original proxy env support).

Real-world impact: this breaks [opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) (which embeds Bun) — in-process plugin SDK calls to its own loopback server (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) get routed through the system proxy and fail, e.g. anomalyco/opencode#37043.

title: Feature request: Allow selective dependency externalization when using --compile
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bun build` already supports external dependencies through `--external` / `external`, as well as externalizing all package dependencies with `--packages external`.

However, when using `bun build --compile`, dependencies are bundled into the resulting executable.

It would be useful to support **selectively externalizing dependencies from compiled executables**, so that the executable can resolve those packages externally at runtime instead of embedding their contents into the binary.

There are several use cases for this:

* Applications containing dependencies which should remain separately distributed
* Native or platform-specific dependencies that are preferable to load from disk
* Plugins or replaceable runtime components
* Reducing the amount of third-party code embedded into an executable
* Software distribution policies based on dependency licenses
* Avoiding bundling dependencies whose licenses are incompatible with an application's distribution requirements

The last case is particularly useful for commercial applications. A project may have a large transitive dependency graph where most dependencies can safely be embedded, while a small number need to remain external according to the project's licensing policy.


### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?


Allow dependencies to be externalized during `--compile` based on either:

1. Package name
2. Package license

For example, configuration could look something like:

```toml
[compile]
externalize-dependencies = ["some-dep", "another-dep"]
allowed-licenses = ["*", "!GPL-*", "!AGPL-*"]
```

The exact naming/syntax isn't important; this is just an example.

`externalize-dependencies` would prevent matching packages from being embedded into the executable.

`allowed-licenses` would provide a policy for deciding which dependencies may be embedded. Dependencies with licenses that do not match the allow policy would automatically be externalized.

For example:

```toml
[compile]
allowed-licenses = ["MIT", "BSD-*", "Apache-2.0"]
```

would bundle packages with those licenses while leaving other packages external.

Conversely:

```toml
[compile]
allowed-licenses = ["*", "!GPL-*", "!AGPL-*"]
```

would bundle everything except packages matching those license expressions.

### CLI equivalents

It would also be useful to expose the same functionality through `bun build`:

```bash
bun build ./src/index.ts \
  --compile \
  --external

title: bun build --compile converts SIGBUS termination to SIGILL
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

  Create a minimal long-running TypeScript program:

  ```ts
  // repro.ts
  setInterval(() => undefined, 60_000);
  ```

  Compile it as a standalone executable and send it `SIGBUS`:

  ```sh
  bun build --compile repro.ts --outfile repro

  ulimit -c 0
  ./repro 2>stderr.txt &
  repro_pid=$!

  sleep 0.2
  kill -BUS "$repro_pid"

  wait "$repro_pid"
  printf 'exit status: %s\n' "$?"

  cat stderr.txt
  ```

  On Linux, `SIGBUS` is signal 7, so Bash should report a wait status of
  135 (`128 + 7`). Instead, the compiled Bun executable terminates as if it
  received `SIGILL`, and Bash reports status 132.

  The standard error output also contains Bun's internal crash banner,
  including:

  ```text
  panic(main thread): Bus error
  oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.
  ```

  This reproduces without application signal handlers or third-party
  dependencies.


### What is the expected behavior?

  The standalone executable should retain the default POSIX disposition for
  `SIGBUS`.

  After `kill -BUS`, the parent should observe that the process terminated from
  `SIGBUS`. On Linux, Bash should therefore report status 135 (`128 + 7`), or a
  `waitpid()` caller should observe `WIFSIGNALED(status)` with
  `WTERMSIG(status) == SIGBUS`.

  Bun should not translate the termination into `SIGILL`, report status 132, or
  print an internal Bun crash diagnostic for an externally delivered signal.


### What do you see instead?

  The process is reported as terminating from `SIGILL` instead of `SIGBUS`.
  Bash reports exit status 132 rather than 135:

  ```text
  Illegal instruction (core dumped)
  exit status: 132

  At the same time, Bun writes an internal crash report to standard error:

  panic(main thread): Bus error
  oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.

  Therefore, Bun recognizes the original SIGBUS while handling it, but the
  compiled process ultimately terminates with SIGILL and exposes the wrong
  wait status to its parent.


### Additional information

  This was discovered during POSIX asynchronous-signal testing and
  then reduced to the standalone reproduction above.

title: fs.writeFile with flag "a+" overwrites from offset 0 instead of appending on Windows
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (also reproduces on current `main`)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64 (Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26100.0 x64). Not reproducible on macOS/Linux.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const fs = require("fs");
fs.writeFileSync("t.txt", "0123456789");
fs.writeFileSync("t.txt", "AB", { flag: "a+" });
console.log(JSON.stringify(fs.readFileSync("t.txt", "utf8")));
```

`fs.promises.writeFile("t.txt", "AB", { flag: "a+" })` behaves the same way.

### What is the expected behavior?

`"0123456789AB"` — `a+` opens for reading and appending, so the write should land at the end of the file. That is what Node prints.

### What do you see instead?

`"AB23456789"` — the write lands at offset 0 and silently overwrites the start of the file. No error is thrown.

### Additional information

Only the path-based `writeFile`/`writeFileSync` with `a+` is affected. These work correctly:

- `writeFileSync(p, data, { flag: "a" })`
- `appendFileSync(p, data, { flag: "a+" })`
- `openSync(p, "a+")` + `writeSync` (goes through libuv)
- flags `w`, `w+`, `wx`, `ax`

Root cause: in `openat_windows_impl` (`src/sys/lib.rs`, the POSIX-flag → `NtCreateFile` translation) the desired-access mask is built with an if/else chain that checks `O_RDWR` before `O_APPEND`. `a+` is `O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_APPEND`, so the `O_APPEND` arm is unreachable and the handle never gets `FILE_APPEND_DATA`. Windows append is emulated by a post-open `SetFilePointerEx(..., FILE_END)` that only runs when `FILE_APPEND_DATA` is present in the mask, so without the bit there is no seek and the write starts at 0. Plain `a` is `O_WRONLY|O_APPEND`, which does reach the append arm — hence only `a+` breaks.

Fix in https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/39355.

1.3.14+0d9b296af

Empirically reproduced on 1.3.14+0d9b296af (latest stable), on **1.4.0-canary.1+30fa51970 (current `main`)**, and earlier on 1.3.8, all Windows x64. The bug carried over into the Rust codebase on `main` — permalinks below point at the current tip (`c3995e43d5`). The same three pieces existed verbatim in the 1.3.x line where the measurements below were first taken.

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

Nothing in the mechanism is Windows-specific — on POSIX `bunx` is a symlink to `bun`, so `argv[0]` still ends in `bunx` and the same dispatch runs.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
export BUN_OPTIONS=--smol     # any value works; --smol is just what we had
bunx -y cowsay@latest hello   # any package; @latest forces the cache-bust install path
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`bunx` installs the package and runs it. (`BUN_OPTIONS` applying to the process is fine; it should not change which *command* bun thinks it is running.)

### What do you see instead?

`bunx` never completes. The process tree grows one level at a time, each level blocked in `spawnSync` waiting on the next:

```
bunx -y cowsay@latest hello
└─ bunx add cowsay@latest --no-summary --no-cache --force
   └─ bunx add add@latest --no-summary --no-cache --force
      └─ bunx add add@latest --no-summary --no-cache --force
         └─ ... (unbounded; ~44 MB per level)
```

Measured on 1.3.14+0d9b296af with the exact repro above: the bunx process count grew **0 → 4 → 14 → 21 → 26 → 37 → 44 → 51 → 57 in ~4 s** (~15 processes/s, strictly monotonic) until the tree was force-killed. On current `main` (1.4.0-canary.1+30fa51970) the same repro grew **0 → 34 in ~3 s** with the identical chain. Observed parent chain (`Win32_Process`):

```
ProcessId  ParentProcessId  CommandLine
76636      7944             ...\.bun\bin\bunx.exe -y cowsay@latest hello
33420      76636            ...\.bun\bin\bunx.exe add cowsay@latest --no-summary --no-cache --force
95428      33420            ...\.bun\bin\bunx.exe add add@latest --no-summary --no-cache --force
105824     95428            ...\.bun\bin\bunx.exe add add@latest --no-summary --no-cache --force
```

The npm package literally named `add` gets installed into `$TMPDIR/bunx-<uid>-add@latest/` (its `package.json` is the `{}` bunx writes). In an earlier uncontrolled occurrence (1.3.8), chains reached depth 40–75 before an external supervisor killed them.
