title: bun-plugin-svelte derives Svelte's `preserveWhitespace` from the bundler's minify flag, so dev and production compile differently
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14+0d9b296af

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-90-generic x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun-plugin-svelte` derives the Svelte **compiler** option `preserveWhitespace` from the **bundler's** minify flag, in `packages/bun-plugin-svelte/src/options.ts`:

```ts
preserveWhitespace: !minifyWhitespace,
```

`preserveWhitespace` is semantic, not cosmetic — it changes which nodes a component receives, not just how output is formatted. Deciding it from a minifier flag means a purely cosmetic bundler setting silently changes rendering.

Separately, the dev server hands plugins a stub bundler config and never sets `minify` — the existing FIXME in `packages/bun-plugin-svelte/src/index.ts`:

```ts
// FIXME: the dev server does not currently respect bundler configs; it
// just passes a fake one to plugins and then never uses it.
```

Combined: under `bun --hot`, `minify` is unset, so `preserveWhitespace` is always `true`; a production `Bun.build` with `minify: true` gets `false`. Same source, two different compilations — and dev gets the unusual one, since Svelte's own default is `false`.

Minimal reproduction, no Svelte app needed:

```ts
import { getBaseCompileOptions } from "bun-plugin-svelte/src/options";

console.log(getBaseCompileOptions({}, {}).preserveWhitespace);                      // true
console.log(getBaseCompileOptions({}, { minify: true }).preserveWhitespace);        // false
console.log(getBaseCompileOptions({}, { minify: { syntax: true } }).preserveWhitespace);      // true
console.log(getBaseCompileOptions({}, { minify: { identifiers: true } }).preserveWhitespace); // true
console.log(getBaseCompileOptions({}, { minify: { whitespace: true } }).preserveWhitespace);  // false
```

Only `whitespace` moves it. `syntax` and `identifiers` — the minify options that could plausibly affect semantics — leave it alone, while the purely cosmetic one flips it.

End to end, the way it was actually hit: a `bits-ui` `Popover` renders nothing under `bun --hot`, and renders correctly from a `Bun.build` with `minify: true`. Same source, same server.

| `Bun.build` minify | resulting `preserveWhitespace` | Popover renders? |
|---|---|---|
| `{ whitespace: true }` | `false` | ✅ |
| `{ syntax: true }` | `true` | ❌ |
| `{ identifiers: true }` | `true` | ❌ |
| `true` (all) | `false` | ✅ |
| `false` | `true` | ❌ |
| dev server, any config | `true` | ❌ |

There is also no supported way to override

ws shim loads node:http eagerly, which is ~95% of the cost of require("ws")
excerpt:
### What

`require("ws")` resolves to the built-in shim `src/js/thirdparty/ws.js`, which does `const http = require("node:http")` at module scope (line 12). Almost all of the cost of loading `ws` is that line, and the client API does not need `node:http` at all.

Measured on a release build of current main (linux-x64, `bun -e` with `performance.now()` around the `require`):

| | cold `require()` |
|---|---|
| `node:events` | ~12.5ms |
| `node:http` | ~27ms |
| `ws` | ~28ms |
| `ws` when `node:http` is already loaded | ~1ms |

On a debug build the same eager load is what makes `bun-debug -e "require('ws')"` take ~1.87s (`-e 1`: 0.26s, `node:http` alone: 1.76s); that is why the echo client fixture in `test/js/bun/websocket/` was moved off `ws` in #39370, and `test/js/first_party/ws/ws.test.ts` still pays it once per test through `test/js/web/websocket/websocket-server-echo.mjs` (~2s per spawned echo server on debug, ~69s for that file).

### Where `http` is actually used in the shim

- `makeHandshakeResponse` (around line 99): `new http.IncomingMessage(...)` for the client `upgrade` / `unexpected-response` events, only when such a listener is registered and a handshake response arrives.
- `abortHandshake` (around line 931): `http.STATUS_CODES[code]`.
- `WebSocketServer` constructor (around lines 1350-1351): `http.createServer(...)` and `http.STATUS_CODES[426]`, only on the `port` option path (not for `server` / `noServer`).

All three are inside functions, so the `require` could move to those sites (or to a small lazy getter). The paths are already covered by `test/js/first_party/ws/ws-upgrade-events.test.ts` and the `WebSocketServer({ port })` tests in `test/js/first_party/ws/ws.test.ts`.

Noting it here rather than folding it into #39370, which is test-only.

title: `bunx`: allow multiple packages in a single temporary execution environment
excerpt:
## What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bunx` supports `--package` for selecting a package to install and use when running a command. This functionality was addressed by #7034, which added support for specifying a package separately from the executable name.

This request is related to that functionality, but addresses a different use case: **making multiple temporary packages available in the same `bunx` execution environment**.

For example, `npx` allows multiple `--package` options:

```bash
npx \
  --package semantic-release@25 \
  --package @semantic-release/exec@6.0.3 \
  --package conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits@9 \
  --package typescript@5.9.3 \
  semantic-release
```

In this case, all four packages are installed into the same temporary environment and are available to the executed command.

With `bunx`, `--package` currently covers the case of selecting a single package, but there is no equivalent way to provide several temporary packages to the same execution.

## Proposed solution

Allow `--package` to be specified multiple times:

```bash
bunx \
  --package semantic-release@25 \
  --package @semantic-release/exec@6.0.3 \
  --package conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits@9 \
  --package typescript@5.9.3 \
  semantic-release
```

Each specified package should be installed temporarily and made available within the same execution environment.

The temporary installation should not modify the project's:

* `package.json`
* lockfile
* `node_modules`

The existing `-p` shorthand could also support multiple occurrences if it is intended to remain an alias for `--package`.

## Why is this useful?

This is particularly useful for CI/CD workflows and other cases where a command depends on a temporary collection of tools, plugins, or configuration packages.

For example, a release workflow may need a specific version of `semantic-release` together with several plugins and configuration dependencies, without wanting those packages to become part of the project's dependency graph:

```bash
bunx \
  --package semantic-release@25 \
  --package @semantic-release/exec@6.0.3 \
  --package conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits@9 \
  --package typescript@5.9.3 \
  semantic-release
```

This allows the versions of the temporary toolchain to be pinned independently while keeping the project's dependencies focused on packages that are actually required by the project itself.

title: `SQL`: `prepare: false` changes parameter encoding — `Date` and plain objects stop binding
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (0d9b296a) — reproduced on macOS arm64 and on `oven/bun:1.3-alpine`.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 15 arm64 (Darwin 25.5.0); also Linux x86_64 (alpine container).

### What is the problem?

`prepare` is documented as a switch for *"automatic creation of prepared statements"*, i.e. statement caching. In practice it also changes how parameters are encoded: with `prepare: false`, a `Date` is sent via `toString()` and a plain object is not JSON-serialized, so both are rejected by PostgreSQL. The same code works with the default `prepare: true`.

This makes `prepare: false` unusable as a workaround for statement-cache issues: turning off caching silently breaks typed parameters that worked a line earlier.

### Reproduction

```ts
import { SQL } from "bun";

const URL = "postgres://user:passwd@localhost:5432/test";

for (const prepare of [true, false]) {
  const sql = new SQL({ url: URL, prepare });
  await sql.unsafe("drop table if exists repro1");
  await sql.unsafe("create table repro1 (ts timestamptz, j jsonb)");

  const date = await sql
    .unsafe("insert into repro1 (ts) values ($1)", [new Date("2026-08-17T13:06:14.904Z")])
    .then(() => "ok")
    .catch((e: Error) => `FAIL: ${e.message}`);

  const json = await sql
    .unsafe("insert into repro1 (j) values ($1)", [{ a: 1 }])
    .then(() => "ok")
    .catch((e: Error) => `FAIL: ${e.message}`);

  console.log(`prepare: ${prepare}\n  Date   -> ${date}\n  object -> ${json}`);
  await sql.end();
}
```

### What do you see?

```
prepare: true
  Date   -> ok
  object -> ok
prepare: false
  Date   -> FAIL: time zone "gmt+0300" not recognized
  object -> FAIL: invalid input syntax for type json
```

Under `TZ=UTC` the `Date` failure persists with a different message (`invalid input syntax for type timestamp with time zone: "Mon Aug 17 2026 13:06:14 GMT+0000 (Coordinated Universal Time)"`), so it is not about the host timezone — the value is simply stringified with `toString()` instead of being encoded as a timestamp.

### What should happen?

Parameter encoding should not depend on `prepare`. Toggling statement caching should be transparent to the values a query binds.

### Notes

Found while looking for a workaround to a prepared-statement name collision in a production service (separate issue). Worth flagging because ORMs that build raw SQL fragments — drizzle's `sql` template, for one — pass `Date` objects straight through, so `prepare: false` brea

title: Fully self-sufficient binary trust chain with bun upgrade
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Currently, `bun upgrade` is insufficiently strict about requiring checksums. It only uses the checksum that GitHub provided.

Relying on external tools or manually verifying signatures and checksums is too much of a burden to place on users.

Encouraging users to run `bun upgrade` with elevated privileges should also be avoided.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

1. Allow `bun upgrade` to handle signature checking of `SHASUMS256.txt.asc`
2. Parse the checksums from the signed content
3. Download the appropriate asset to a new directory in `TMPDIR` without any elevated privileges
4. Verify that the checksum matches the downloaded file
5. Provide the user with the location of the verified download for extraction/installation

For signatures, it would be a good idea to embed all previously used signing keys, the current key, and a "next" key in the binary itself. Providing a known web location for key revocation checks would also be a good practice. In the future a key could be revoked by placing it's revocation at that location for immediate effect.

### What alternatives have you considered?

An alternative would be to publish a separate rust binary for all supported platforms that would be more general purpose. It could eliminate dependence on OS provided checksum verification tools and accept a key fingerprint to serve as a root of trust along with a file to retrieve pgp keys from.

Bun.markdown: hardSoftBreaks and collapseWhitespace options are documented but do nothing
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running? 1.4.0 (also current main) ### What steps will reproduce the bug? ```ts console.log(JSON.stringify(Bun.markdown.html("a\nb\n", { hardSoftBreaks: true }))); console.log(JSON.stringify(Bun.markdown.html("a b\n", { collapseWhitespace: true }))); ``` ### What is the expected behavior? Both options are listed in the options table of docs/runtime/markdown.mdx and in `Bun.markdown.Options` (packages/bun-types/bun.d.ts): - `hardSoftBreaks`: "Treat soft line breaks as hard breaks", so the first call should print `"

a
\nb

\n"`. md4c's test file for this flag is already checked in as `test/js/bun/md/spec-hard-soft-breaks.txt` (it also expects trailing whitespace before the forced break to be dropped), but it is not in the `specFiles` list of `test/js/bun/md/md-spec.test.ts`. - `collapseWhitespace`: "Collapse whitespace in text", so the second call should print `"

a b

\n"` (md4c's `MD_FLAG_COLLAPSEWHITESPACE` collapses non-trivial whitespace runs in normal text into a single space). ### What do you see instead? ``` "

a\nb

\n" "

a b

\n" ``` Both options are accepted and ignored: - `hard_soft_breaks` is parsed into `Options` (src/md/root.rs) but `Options::to_flags()` drops it; `Flags` in src/md/types.rs has no such field, and the newline handling in `process_inline_content` (src/md/inlines.rs) always emits `TextType::Softbr` unless the line itself ends in a hard break. - `collapse_whitespace` reaches `Flags` and `build_mark_char_map` (src/md/parser.rs) marks space, tab and CR for it, but `process_inline_content` has no branch for those characters, so they fall through as text. Related: the same situation for `latexMath` and `underline` is fixed by the PR referenced below; those two were left out of it because they are text-level options rather than span types the renderers already support. If they are not going to be implemented, the docs and types should stop listing them.

title: Bun.markdown: emphasis delimiters inside a wiki link target pair with delimiters outside it, producing unbalanced HTML
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running? 1.4.0 (also current main) ### What steps will reproduce the bug? ```ts const o = { wikiLinks: true }; console.log(JSON.stringify(Bun.markdown.html("*a [[b*|c]] d\n", o))); console.log(JSON.stringify(Bun.markdown.html("[[a *b|c]] d* e\n", o))); console.log(JSON.stringify(Bun.markdown.html("**a [[b**|c]]\n", o))); ``` ### What is the expected behavior? The emphasis delimiters inside the wiki link target should not pair with delimiters outside the link (md4c resolves bracket constructs before emphasis, so the asterisks here are all literal text): ``` "

*a c d

\n" "

c d* e

\n" "

**a c

\n" ``` ### What do you see instead? Unbalanced HTML: an `` / `` that is never closed, or a `` with no opener. ``` "

a c d

\n" "

c d e

\n" "

a c

\n" ``` Cause: `collect_emphasis_delimiters` in src/md/inlines.rs skips over regular links and images (`try_match_bracket_link`) but not over `[[...]]` wiki links, so delimiters inside the target are collected and resolved against delimiters outside it. The emit walk then renders the wiki link as a unit, so one half of each resolved pair is never emitted. The fix is to skip wiki link constructs in that first phase the same way regular links are skipped; any other delimiter kind collected in that phase (strikethrough, and math spans once the PR referenced below lands) is covered by the same change.

excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`docs/pm/global-store.mdx` documents the tradeoff already:

> With the global store, packages realpath into `<cache>/links/`, so that layer is no longer on the resolution path from inside a package.
> In practice this only affects **true phantom dependencies** […] If you hit this, add the helper to the consuming package's dependencies (the right fix) or set `globalStore = false`.

The gap is in the remedy, not the description. **The consuming package is usually not one you control.** Adding the helper to *your* `package.json` does nothing, because the walk from inside the store never re-enters the project — so for a phantom import inside a third-party package the only documented option left is `globalStore = false`.

This is not rare. Three of our dependencies do it, and each one takes down a whole tool:

| package | imports, never declares | symptom |
|---|---|---|
| `bun-types` | `undici-types` | ~260 `TS2339` on `Response` / `Request` / `Headers` |
| `@sentry/bun` | `@sentry/node-core` | `TS2353` on a valid `Sentry.init` option |
| `@darraghor/eslint-plugin-nestjs-typed` | `typescript` | eslint won't load the plugin |

None is a bun bug — each store entry contains exactly what its `package.json` declares. But collectively they make `globalStore` unusable for us, and the payoff is large: our CI install step goes **19s → 2s** with the store on.

The failures also don't point at the store. Nothing in `TS2339: Property 'status' does not exist on type 'Response'` suggests a linker setting.

Three files, two public packages, no workspace:

excerpt:
### Decision needed: should the terminal preset turn on `underline`?

`Options::TERMINAL` in src/md/root.rs (used by `Bun.markdown.ansi()` and by `bun ./file.md`) has listed `underline: true` since the markdown parser landed, and the `ansi()` JSDoc said the preset enables underline. The option was a no-op until #39493, so terminal output has always rendered `_text_` as italic and `__text__` as bold, the same as `*text*` / `**text**`.

#39493 implements the option with md4c's `MD_FLAG_UNDERLINE` semantics (every matched underscore becomes a `<u>` span, so both `_x_` and `__x__` underline) but leaves it off in the terminal preset, because turning it on there would change the output of every README that uses `_emphasis_`: underscores would render underlined while asterisks stay italic/bold in the same document, and `ansi()` has no parser options, so there would be no opt-out.

If the terminal is meant to underline underscores, the change is one line (`underline: true` in `Options::TERMINAL`) plus the `ansi()` JSDoc and the two terminal-path tests (`ansi() keeps underscores as emphasis` in test/js/bun/md/md-edge-cases.test.ts and `renders math spans; underscores stay emphasis` in test/cli/run/markdown-entrypoint.test.ts). Two things to settle at the same time:

- whether the intended terminal semantic is md4c's (all underscores) or only `__x__`, which is what the old docs table described; the option itself implements md4c's, backed by the checked-in `test/js/bun/md/spec-underline.txt`
- the ANSI renderer's `U` arm, which has never been exercised: its off code (`\x1b[24m`) also switches off an enclosing link's underline, and `SPAN_U` is a single flag, so the tail of `_a _b_ c_` or of `[_a_ b](url)` loses its underline. That needs fixing before the preset enables the option.

### What version of Bun is running?

Verified **fixed** on `1.4.0-canary.1+4c689909e`.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 (also seen on Vercel's Linux build image)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No dependencies, no network:

```sh

echo '{ "name": "root", "private": true, "workspaces": ["*"] }'                              > package.json

echo '{ "name": "aa",  "version": "1.0.0", "dependencies": { "@x/lib": "workspace:*" } }'    > aa/package.json
echo '{ "name": "aaa", "version": "1.0.0", "dependencies": { "@x/lib": "workspace:*" } }'    > aaa/package.json

(cd aa  && bun install)   # fails
(cd aaa && bun install)   # succeeds
```

`aa` fails, `aaa` succeeds. The two directories are identical apart from one letter in the name.

### What is the expected behavior?

Both succeed. A workspace member's directory name length should not affect whether `bun install`
run from inside it can find the workspace root.

### What do you see instead?

error: @x/lib@workspace:* failed to resolve
```

#### The rule

It is the length of the member's path **relative to the workspace root**, and only when the member
is matched by a **glob** entry. Threshold is 3.

| `["*"]` | `a/` | `a` | 1 | fail |

while `["*"]` + `aa` (path 2, pattern 1) fails.

error that cites the same `package.json` twice:

title: node:test: running a test file directly throws "Cannot use test outside of the test runner"
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14+0d9b296af (also reproduces on `main`, built as 1.4.0-debug+4c689909e)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 (10.0.26200) x64. The throw is not platform-gated, so this is unlikely to be Windows-specific — I only verified it here.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`node:test` files run standalone under Node: `node file.mjs` executes the tests and exits 0. Under Bun the same file throws.

```js
// repro.mjs
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert';
test('runs standalone', () => { assert.strictEqual(1, 1); });
```

```
$ node repro.mjs
✔ runs standalone (1.5045ms)
ℹ tests 1
ℹ pass 1
ℹ fail 0
$ echo $?
0
```

```
$ bun repro.mjs
1 | import { test } from 'node:test';
2 | import assert from 'node:assert';
3 | test('runs standalone', () => { assert.strictEqual(1, 1); });
    ^
error: Cannot use test outside of the test runner. Run "bun test" to run tests.
      at test (node:test:149:10)
```

`describe` fails the same way.

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun file.mjs` runs the tests declared with `node:test` and exits nonzero if any fail, matching `node file.mjs`. Running a test file directly is the documented entry point for `node:test` — Node's docs describe `node --test` as a way to run *many* such files, not as a requirement for running one.

### What do you see instead?

The file throws on the first `test()` or `describe()` call, before any test body runs.

### Additional information

The throw comes from `get_test_root` in `src/runtime/test_runner/bun_test.rs`, which errors when `Jest::runner()` is `None` — that is, whenever the process was not started by `bun test`. There is no platform gate on that path.

This also affects Bun's own vendored Node compatibility suite. 113 files under `test/js/node/test/{parallel,sequential}` import `node:test`, and `test/js/node/test/parallel/CLAUDE.md` states these tests are meant to be run directly (`bun bd <file-path>`, "the tests pass by exiting with code 0"). I ran a 313-file slice of that suite (buffer, zlib, timers, url, querystring, util, path, os, events, assert, punycode, readline, tty, v8, domain) against a debug build of `main`: 292 passed, and 17 of the 21 failures were this error and nothing else.

Related: #5090 (`node:test` support) was closed on 2026-08-07. This looks like a remaining gap in that support rather than a regression — `bun test` runs these files fine.

title: Windows build requires Developer Mode to extract two zstd test symlinks it never uses
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

On Windows, `bun bd` fails unless Developer Mode is on or the shell is elevated, because extracting a dependency archive tries to create symbolic links:

```
[zstd] error: tar extraction failed (exit 1): tests/cli-tests/bin/unzstd: Can't create '\?\C:\...\vendor\zstd\tests\cli-tests\bin\unzstd': Invalid argument
ninja: build stopped: subcommand failed.
```

The two entries that fail are `tests/cli-tests/bin/unzstd` and `tests/cli-tests/bin/zstdcat` in the zstd source archive. Both are symlinks to `zstd`, and the zstd build never reads them — `scripts/build/deps/zstd.ts` compiles a fixed list of `lib/*.c` sources. bsdtar extracts every other entry successfully and only returns exit 1 at the end, so the build stops on two files it does not use.

Of the nine dependency tarballs my build downloaded (brotli, libarchive, libdeflate, libjpeg-turbo, lolhtml, picohttpparser, tinycc, zlib, zstd), zstd is the only one containing symlinks:

```
$ tar -tvzf zstd-e010993a24072468.tar.gz | grep '^l'
lrwxrwxrwx  0 root root 0 Feb 19  2025 .../tests/cli-tests/bin/unzstd -> zstd
lrwxrwxrwx  0 root root 0 Feb 19  2025 .../tests/cli-tests/bin/zstdcat -> zstd
```

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Make `extractTarGz` in `scripts/build/download.ts` not depend on symlink-creation privilege for entries the build does not need.

One shape that avoids adding cost to the working path: leave the current `tar` invocation alone, and only on Windows, only after a failure, list the archive for symlink entries. If there are any, re-run the extraction with `--exclude` for each and log which entries were skipped; if there are none, rethrow the original error. That keeps the happy path unchanged, avoids parsing tar's stderr, and does not silently drop anything.

I am not confident this is the shape you want, which is why this is an issue rather than a PR:

- Excluding symlinks is only obviously safe for entries nothing reads. It may be wrong for an archive whose symlinks matter — the prebuilt WebKit tarball also goes through `extractTarGz`, and I have not checked whether it contains any.
- Copying the target file in place of the link would preserve read semantics on Windows, but costs more complexity than the two zstd fixtures justify on their own.

title: gitattributes: per-extension eol=lf list misses 1106 files, which a default Windows clone checks out as CRLF
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`.gitattributes` pins `eol=lf` extension by extension. The Git for Windows installer sets `core.autocrlf=true` at the system level, so anything the list misses is rewritten to CRLF on checkout. On a default Windows clone, 1106 tracked files are LF in the index and CRLF in the working tree:

```
$ git config --system --get core.autocrlf
true
$ git ls-files --eol | awk '$1=="i/lf" && $2=="w/crlf"' | wc -l
1106
```

By extension:

```
139 .pem     93 .txt      52 .gitignore   45 (none)   29 .cnf    17 .env
108 .svelte  62 .snap     51 .idl         44 .yaml    18 .svg    15 .cts
 98 .cjs     60 .gyp      45 .snapshot    44 .sh      18 .html   13 .reg2
```

By area:

```
309 test/js/node/test          29 src/jsc/bindings/webcrypto
 97 test/integration/vite-build/the-test-app    26 test/js/node/crypto
 61 test/napi/node-napi-tests/test              22 src/jsc/bindings/webcore
 45 test/cli/install/migration                  21 test/js/node/tls
```

Three of these stand out:

- **`.cjs` (98) and `.cts` (15)** sit directly beside `*.js`, `*.mjs`, `*.ts`, `*.mts`, which are all covered. This looks like an oversight rather than a decision.
- **`.sh` (44)** — a CRLF shell script fails to run on Linux, so these break if a Windows checkout ever feeds them to a container or CI image.
- **`.snap` and `.snapshot` (107)** — snapshot tests compare exact bytes.

This is not theoretical. I ran a 1310-file slice of `test/js/node/test/parallel` (http, http2, https, stream, fs) against a debug build of `main` on Windows 11: 1285 passed, and ten failures were caused only by CRLF fixtures. `fixtures/x.txt` is `xyz\n` in the index and `xyz\r\n` on disk, so `test-fs-read-optional-params.js` reports `actual: 5, expected: 4`. #39675 fixes that subtree and lists the ten files; all ten pass with the rule and fail without it, under the same git config.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Replace the per-extension list with a catch-all so new file types are covered by default:

```
* text=auto eol=lf
```

Git still auto-detects binary content and leaves it alone, and the existing `-text` entries keep overriding it for files that must not be touched at all.

I did not open this as a PR because I cannot verify it. The change moves 1106 files across areas I have no way to exercise on one machine — the vite-build integration app, the napi suite, the webcrypto and webcore binding inputs. A `text=auto` misdetection

> First of all, thank you for making a great package manager like Bun and providing this example repository! It has been a game-changer for my workflow.
> 
> 
> I would like to request an official reference `Dockerfile` for this template that correctly handles the Next.js build and runtime using Bun.
> 
> As a developer, I have successfully containerized pure backend applications with Bun without issues. However, getting Next.js to play well with the Bun runtime inside Docker has been a significant struggle.
> 
> I have attempted various configurations across different infrastructure providers (VPS, standard Docker runners), but I consistently run into friction between:
> 
> 1. **The Vercel/Next.js build output:** Which is heavily optimized for Node.js.
> 2. **The Bun Runtime:** Trying to run the Next.js `standalone` output or standard build artifacts often leads to obscure errors regarding missing dependencies, sharp/image optimization glibc issues, or entry point mismatches (`server.js` vs `bun start`).
> 
> 
> I am looking for a "Golden Path" Dockerfile added to this repo that demonstrates the Bun team's recommended way to:
> 
> 1. Install dependencies using `bun install`.
> 2. Build the Next.js app (`bun run build`) specifically for a containerized environment.
> 3. **Crucially:** Serve the application in production using the `bun` runtime (not falling back to `node`), ensuring `next.config.ts` and environment variables are respected.
> 
> 
> Currently, most community resources or Vercel documentation assume a Node.js runtime for the final container. Having an official example here would solve a lot of headaches for developers trying to move their full-stack Next.js stack entirely to Bun.

title: HTMLRewriter: expose source location (byte offset) on handlers/attributes
excerpt:
Bun's `HTMLRewriter` handlers (`element`, `text`, `comments`, `doctype`) and the `Element`/`Attribute` objects passed to them don't expose any source-location info for the node/attribute being visited — not even a byte offset. That makes it impossible to build a useful error message pointing at *where* in the input a problem was found when validating or transforming a template with `HTMLRewriter`.

Upstream, `lol-html` (which `HTMLRewriter` wraps) exposes this as a byte-offset range (`SourceLocation { start, end }`, not line/column):
- Tag/token-level locations since [v2.5.0](https://github.com/cloudflare/lol-html/releases/tag/v2.5.0), exposed to the C/JS APIs in [v2.6.0](https://github.com/cloudflare/lol-html/releases/tag/v2.6.0).
- `Attribute::name_source_location()` / `value_source_location()` since [v2.9.0](https://github.com/cloudflare/lol-html/releases/tag/v2.9.0) ([lol-html#313](https://github.com/cloudflare/lol-html/pull/313)).

Bun currently vendors `lol_html` 2.7.2, which already has the tag-level data — it's just not wired up in Bun's binding — but predates attribute-level locations. The same ask has been open against Cloudflare's own WASM binding since 2023: [cloudflare/html-rewriter-wasm#5](https://github.com/cloudflare/html-rewriter-wasm/issues/5).

Would it be possible to:
1. Expose tag/element-level source location on `HTMLRewriter` handlers now, using the data already available in the vendored 2.7.2?
2. Merge the open, unmerged bump PR [#29474](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/29474) (targets [v3.0.1](https://github.com/cloudflare/lol-html/releases/tag/v3.0.1), the current latest release) to pick up attribute-level locations and the v3.0.0 `Comment::set_text` security fix (rejects `--!>`/leading `>`/`->`, closing a comment-injection vector), then expose attribute-level locations too?

Caveat: `value_source_location()` currently has a known bug for valueless attributes — [cloudflare/lol-html#333](https://github.com/cloudflare/lol-html/issues/333) — worth tracking as a blocker for the attribute-level part specifically.

title: Config dependencies: supply catalog, overrides and trustedDependencies from an installed package
excerpt:
## What I want

One place that decides dependency versions for every project I maintain, and a
single version bump that carries the new versions into all of them.

Concretely: publish `@myorg/versions` containing a catalog, depend on it, and
have `bun update @myorg/versions` be the whole update. No copying, no codegen
step.

## Why this is not possible today

Catalogs are the right primitive and already exist — they just cannot cross a
repository boundary:

- `catalog:` resolves only from the workspace root `package.json`. A catalog
  declared in any other package fails the install with `failed to resolve`.
- `package.json` has no `extends`, so the root cannot inherit a list from
  anywhere.

So the list has to physically live in each root, and keeping N repositories in
step means copying it N times.

I want to note the obvious objection myself, because it is the reason a naive
`extends` would not work: a version list inside `package.json` would have to be
fetched *before* dependencies resolve, but fetching it **is** resolving a
dependency. There is no ordering that works if it is an ordinary dependency.

## Prior art: pnpm solves the ordering with a separate phase

pnpm's [config dependencies](https://pnpm.io/config-dependencies) install
**before** `dependencies`, `devDependencies` and `optionalDependencies`, in their
own phase. Two constraints stop that phase from recursing into a full graph:

- a config dependency **cannot declare regular `dependencies`** — only
  `optionalDependencies`, one level deep, exact versions
- a config dependency **cannot define lifecycle scripts**

Integrity is tracked in a separate lockfile document. The catalog then arrives
through a hook in the published package:

```js
// @org/pnpm-plugin-versions/pnpmfile.mjs
export const hooks = {
  updateConfig(config) {
    config.catalogs.default ??= {}
    config.catalogs.default['hono'] = '4.12.27'
    return config
  },
}
```

```yaml
# pnpm-workspace.yaml, in the consuming project
configDependencies:
  '@org/pnpm-plugin-versions': '1.0.0'
```

`pnpm add hono@catalog:` then resolves. Those two constraints are the interesting
part: they are what make a pre-resolution install phase safe rather than a
bootstrapping problem.

## Bun already has most of the machinery

`bun install` reads `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and writes its `catalog` / `catalogs` /
`overrides` / `patchedDependencies` into the root `package.json` before
resolution — most recently extended in #38754 to run without a migr

title: fs.rmSync throws EFAULT (bad address in system call argument) on Windows during recursive temp-dir removal
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### What platform is your computer?

windows-latest GitHub Actions runner (`windows-latest`)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No local reproduction. Observed once under CI load.

In [oh-my-openagent CI run 32243430643](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/actions/runs/32243430643), job `senpi-compatibility (windows-latest)`, Bun 1.3.14 threw during test teardown while recursively removing a unique temp directory:

```
EFAULT: bad address in system call argument, rm C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local\Temp\omo-memory-footer-wiring-xxI3Ny
```

The test ("once-only footer gate") had already passed its assertions. The failure was in `afterEach` teardown via `fs.rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 10, retryDelay: 200 })`.

`fs.rm`/`rmSync` retry `EBUSY`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE`, `ENOTEMPTY`, and `EPERM`. `EFAULT` is not in that set, so it throws immediately.

### What is the expected behavior?

Recursive `fs.rmSync` / `fs.rm` of a temp directory on Windows should not surface `EFAULT` ("bad address in system call argument"). If the path is gone, `force: true` should succeed. If the call is retried, `EFAULT` is not a documented filesystem condition for this API.

### What do you see instead?

```
EFAULT: bad address in system call argument, rm C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local\Temp\omo-memory-footer-wiring-xxI3Ny
```

Occurred once on a loaded Windows CI runner. No local reproduction on macOS (0/10).

### Additional information

Related (different reproduction): https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/36984 — concurrent `fs.rm(..., { recursive: true, force: true })` on the same directory on macOS also surfaces `EFAULT`. This report is a single recursive removal of a unique temp directory on Windows.

title: install (hardlink backend): parallel extraction races on creating a shared @scope parent directory, causing "Fail extracting tarball"
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (0d9b296a)

### What platform is your computer?

Alpine Linux 3.20.6 (linux/x64). Reproduced identically on: the real CI job (Forgejo Actions self-hosted runner, host executor, not docker-per-job), a fresh `git clone` of the repo, and an isolated `bun add next@16.2.2` in an empty directory with no other files — not runner-specific.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro
echo '{}' > package.json
bun add next@16.2.2
# error: Fail extracting tarball for "next"
# error: Fail extracting tarball from next

# Works:
rm -rf node_modules bun.lock*
bun add next@16.2.2 --backend=copyfile
# installed next@16.2.2 with binaries: - next
```

Deterministic in this environment on a cold global cache + empty `node_modules`. `npm install next@16.2.2` on the same machine/tarball succeeds, ruling out tarball corruption.

`next` pulls in several sibling packages under the same npm scope (`@next/env`, `@next/swc-linux-x64-gnu`, `@swc/helpers`, etc.), extracted/linked in parallel across worker threads by the default `hardlink` backend. `strace -f` on the failing run shows the actual failure happens during linking, after decompression:

```
openat(12, "@next/swc-linux-x64-gnu@16.2.2@@@1", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = 18
openat(16, "@next/swc-linux-x64-gnu", O_RDONLY|O_LARGEFILE|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
mkdirat(16, "@next/swc-linux-x64-gnu", 0755) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
```

`mkdirat` fails with `ENOENT` — not because `@next/swc-linux-x64-gnu` doesn't exist, but because its parent (`node_modules/@next`) doesn't exist yet at that instant. Each worker thread owns a different `@next/*` sibling and assumes the shared scope directory either already exists or that its own `mkdirat` call will create it — there's no synchronization ensuring the shared parent directory exists before the first sibling tries to create a child inside it. Whichever thread loses the race gets `ENOENT` and that package's tarball is reported as "failed to extract."

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun add next@16.2.2` installs successfully with the default `hardlink` backend.

### What do you see instead?

```
error: Fail extracting tarball for "next"
error: Fail extracting tarball from next
```

### Additional information

- `--backend=copyfile` avoids this entirely — evidently a different code path for directory creation that isn't exposed to the same race (not nec

Importing a `node:` builtin Bun does not implement reports it as an unresolved package and suggests installing it:

```js
import 'node:definitely-not-real';
```

```
error: Could not resolve: "node:definitely-not-real". Maybe you need to "bun install"?
```

`require()` of the same specifier gets it right:

```
$ bun -e "require('node:definitely-not-real')"
error: No such built-in module: node:definitely-not-real
```

Same split for every specifier I tried, so it is the ESM path rather than anything specific to one module:

| specifier | `import` | `require` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node:definitely-not-real` | Could not resolve … Maybe you need to "bun install"? | No such built-in module |
| `node:sqlite-xyz` | Could not resolve … Maybe you need to "bun install"? | No such built-in module |
| `node:stream/iter` | Could not resolve … Maybe you need to "bun install"? | No such built-in module |

### What is the expected behavior?

The `import` path reports an unknown builtin the way the `require` path already does. Node uses `ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE` for both.

### What do you see instead?

An unknown `node:` builtin is reported as a missing package, with a remedy that cannot work: the `node:` prefix is reserved for builtins, so no `bun install` will ever resolve it. There is no package on npm named `node:stream/iter` to install.

### Additional information

This cost me real time, which is why I am filing it. I hit it on `test/js/node/test/parallel/test-quic-stream-idle-timeout.mjs`, whose first failure line is:

```
error: Could not resolve: "node:stream/iter". Maybe you need to "bun install"?
```

I went looking for a missing dependency before checking whether the module existed at all. The `require` wording would have told me in one step.

Separately, and not what this issue is about: `node:stream/iter` genuinely is not implemented, while `process.versions.node` reports `26.3.0`, a version that has it. Two vendored tests (`test-quic-stream-idle-timeout.mjs`, `test-quic-h3-stream-idle-timeout.mjs`) fail only for that reason. I am happy to open that separately if it is worth tracking.

title: test-net-pingpong: the PONG answering the final PING before end() is never delivered
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

Debug build of `main` (1.4.0-debug+4c689909e) and 1.3.14+0d9b296af. Both fail.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 (10.0.26200) x64. I could not test other platforms.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`test/js/node/test/parallel/test-net-pingpong.js` fails deterministically — 3/3 runs on the debug build, and also on 1.3.14. Node v24.11.0 passes it.

```
$ bun-debug test/js/node/test/parallel/test-net-pingpong.js
AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal:

1000 !== 1001

    at <anonymous> (test/js/node/test/parallel/test-net-pingpong.js:119:14)
```

The assertion is on the client's `close` handler:

```js
client.on('close', common.mustCall(function() {
  assert.strictEqual(count, N + 1);      // <- 1000, expected 1001
  assert.strictEqual(sentPongs, N + 1);
  assert.strictEqual(sent_final_ping, true);
}));
```

`count` counts `'data'` events on the client. The last exchange is a final `PING` written immediately before `client.end()`, and the client is expected to still receive the server's `PONG` for it. One `'data'` event never arrives.

Note the earlier `assert.strictEqual(data, 'PONG')` inside the data handler does **not** fire, so the missing event is not two `PONG`s coalescing into one — that would have failed on the string first.

### What is the expected behavior?

1001 `'data'` events on the client, as in Node.

### What do you see instead?

1000. The `PONG` answering the final `PING` is not delivered before `close`.

I could not reduce this to a standalone script, and the negative results are probably more useful than another repro attempt would be. None of the following reproduce it on `main` — each printed the expected count:

- Half-close on its own: write, `end()`, expect one inbound message afterwards. `readable` stays `true` and the message arrives.

- The same loop with `net.createServer({ allowHalfOpen: true })` and the server calling `socket.end()` from its `'end'` handler.
- The same again over `::1` instead of `127.0.0.1`.

title: Async file I/O promise never resolves — thread-pool dispatch appears lost (Bun 1.3.5, macOS arm64)
excerpt:
## Environment

- Bun: **1.3.5** (`bun --version`)
- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83), Darwin 25.6.0, kernel 12377.161.14
- Arch: arm64 (Apple Silicon, native — not Rosetta)
- Disk: local SSD (internal + external Thunderbolt volumes tested, both affected)
- Reproduced in: a sequential batch CLI doing file I/O in a plain `for`/`while` loop (not a server, no concurrent load)

## Symptom

An `await` on an async file-read call never resolves. No error, no rejection, no exception — the promise simply never settles. The process sits alive indefinitely: 0% CPU, no growth in RSS, no open file descriptor on the target volume, no pending syscall on the main thread beyond the event loop's own `kevent64` wait.

We saw this with two different call shapes on two separate incidents:
1. `Bun.file(path).stream()` consumed via `for await` — hung 2h43m before we killed it (see "Scale" below).
2. `Bun.file(path).slice(0, N).arrayBuffer()` — same signature, different call site (EXIF header read), diagnosed during a later, related sweep.

We did not test plain `node:fs/promises` reads in isolation on this exact workload, but our fs-walk code also switched off `fs/promises`' `readdir`/`stat` proactively (same hazard class, not independently reproduced hanging) — see "Scope" below.

## Scale / frequency observed

This surfaced in a photo-archive ingest CLI processing tens of thousands of files sequentially (JPEGs on local disk, ordinary file sizes, one in the 10-20MB range at each hang point). Over one extended session:

- **2 confirmed indefinite hangs** on the same async-read call site, both on ordinary JPEG files, both under sequential (non-concurrent) I/O.
- Hang #1: silent for **2h43m** before we noticed and killed it (no watchdog yet).
- Hang #2: reproduced on the very same call site **2 minutes** after resuming with a heartbeat/watchdog added — different file, same failure signature.
- Total files processed across the session before/around these hangs: on the order of 10,000+ (walking + hashing + uploading), so the failure rate is low but not a one-off — it recurred on the same code path within the same day, at similar low single-digit-thousands-of-files intervals.
- We could not correlate the hang to any particular file's size, extension, or filesystem attributes — the two hung files were ordinary JPEGs with nothing distinguishing them from thousands of others processed without incident immediately before and after.

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```bash
echo 'console.log("hello-from-compiled")' > hello.ts

bun-1.4.0 build --compile ./hello.ts --outfile hello-140
codesign -v ./hello-140
./hello-140; echo exit:$?
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A trivial `bun build --compile` binary should launch and print `hello-from-compiled`, the same way it does with Bun 1.3.14.

### What do you see instead?

On **1.3.14**, `codesign -v` already reports an invalid signature, but the binary **still runs**:

```
hello-1314: invalid signature (code or signature have been modified)
In architecture: arm64
hello-from-compiled
exit:0
```

`codesign -dvvv` on the 1.3.14 artifact:

```
Identifier=a.out
Format=Mach-O thin (arm64)
CodeDirectory v=20400 size=491934 flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed) hashes=15370+0 location=embedded
Signature=adhoc
```

On **1.4.0**, `codesign -v` reports the same error, but the process is **SIGKILL'd before any user code runs** (no stdout/stderr):

```
hello-140: invalid signature (code or signature have been modified)
In architecture: arm64
exit:137
```

`codesign -dvvv` on the 1.4.0 artifact:

```
Identifier=a.out
Format=Mach-O thin (arm64)
CodeDirectory v=20400 size=495550 flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed) hashes=15483+0 location=embedded
Signature=adhoc
```

`BUN_NO_CODESIGN_MACHO_BINARY=1` and `codesign --remove-signature` also SIGKILL on 1.4.0. Replacing the signature works:

```bash
codesign --force --sign - ./hello-140
codesign -v ./hello-140   # valid on disk
./hello-140               # hello-from-compiled
```

### Additional information

This is **not** the 1.3.12 truncated-`LC_CODE_SIGNATURE` bug (#29120 / #29270 / #29306, fixed in 1.3.13). 1.3.14 is the last Zig release and its compile artifacts still execute on this macOS 27 host.

1.4.0 is the Zig→Rust rewrite. The in-process signer now lives in `src/exe_format/macho.rs`. Something in that port made the kernel actually reject the binary. Both versions fail `codesign -v` the same way; only 1.4.0 is kill

bun install 1.4.0: scoped-registry credentials dropped on tarball /download/ URLs (GitHub Packages 401; 1.3.14 works)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

`1.4.0+34cbb9a40` (broken)

Compared against `1.3.14+0d9b296af` (works), same workflow, same lockfile, same credentials.

### What platform is your computer?

GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest` — Ubuntu 24.04 x64, runner image `ubuntu24/20260816.277`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Install a private package from a scoped registry that serves tarballs from a different path on the same host. GitHub Packages does exactly this: metadata lives at `https://npm.pkg.github.com/@scope/package`, tarballs at `https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@scope/package/<version>/<sha>`.

```bash
# package.json depends on a private @scope/* package published to GitHub Packages
echo '@scope:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com/'        > .npmrc
echo '//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=<TOKEN>'          >> .npmrc
echo '//npm.pkg.github.com/:always-auth=true'            >> .npmrc

bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The install completes, as it does on 1.3.14 with byte-identical config — 581 packages installed in 4.58s.

### What do you see instead?

Resolution succeeds, then every tarball fetch 401s:

```
bun install v1.4.0 (34cbb9a40)
error: GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@scope/a/0.1.19/<sha> - 401
error: GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@scope/b/0.5.2/<sha>  - 401
error: GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@scope/c/0.1.0/<sha>  - 401
... (6 of 6 private packages)
```

**The telling part: no 401 is on metadata — all six are on `/download/`.** Bun resolved every package to an exact version and content SHA first, which requires an authenticated metadata read against the same host. So the credential is being sent for `https://npm.pkg.github.com/@scope/...` and dropped for `https://npm.pkg.github.com/download/@scope/...`.

### What I ruled out

Five runs, one variable:

| bun | registry config | credential | Result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1.3.14 | hand-written `.npmrc` | PAT | installs |
| 1.4.0 | hand-written `.npmrc` | PAT | 401 × 6 |
| 1.4.0 | hand-written `.npmrc` | Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` | 401 × 6 |
| 1.4.0 | `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2` `registry-url` + `scope`, no `.npmrc` | PAT | 401 × 6 |
| 1.3.14 | hand-written `.npmrc` | PAT | installs |

So it is not the credential, not which file declares the registry, and not a stale token — the two 1.3.14 runs bracket the failures in time, 90 minutes apart, using the same secret.

### Possible cause

The 1.4 announcement says registry credential

title: bun:test recursively snapshots JSDOM internals, causing massive memory usage
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

Reproduced with both:

- Bun 1.4.0 (`34cbb9a40`)
- Bun 1.3.14 (`0d9b296a`)

This does not appear to be a 1.4 regression.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.2 on Apple Silicon (M2 Pro).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Install JSDOM 26.1.0 and create this test:

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";

test("snapshots a tiny JSDOM DocumentFragment", () => {
  const dom = new JSDOM("<!doctype html><html><body></body></html>");
  const fragment = dom.window.document.createDocumentFragment();
  const button = dom.window.document.createElement("button");

  button.textContent = "Follow Auctioneer";
  fragment.append(button);

  expect(fragment).toMatchSnapshot();
  dom.window.close();
});
```

Minimal `package.json`:

```json
{
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "devDependencies": {
    "jsdom": "26.1.0"
  }
}
```

Run:

```sh
bun install
bun test
wc -l __snapshots__/repro.test.ts.snap
du -h __snapshots__/repro.test.ts.snap
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The snapshot should contain a few lines of DOM markup:

```text
<DocumentFragment>
  <button>
    Follow Auctioneer
  </button>
</DocumentFragment>
```

Jest 30.3.0 produces exactly this: a 9-line snapshot (4 KB on disk) in about
0.46 seconds for the equivalent test.

### What do you see instead?

Bun recursively snapshots JSDOM implementation details, internal symbols,
circular object graphs, and related `Window`/`Document` state instead of
formatting the value as DOM.

Measured output for the single button above:

| Runner | Snapshot lines | Snapshot size |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Bun 1.4.0 | 146,955 | 7.5 MB |
| Bun 1.3.14 | 154,095 | 7.7 MB |
| Jest 30.3.0 | 9 | 4 KB on disk |

This causes a large transient memory spike even for the minimal test. In a
React suite containing several DOM snapshots, Bun grew beyond 40 GB and made
the desktop unresponsive. The test appeared stuck on the first snapshot.

### Additional information

The issue does not require React, React Testing Library, a custom preload, or
parallel test workers. A bare JSDOM `DocumentFragment` and one
`toMatchSnapshot()` call are sufficient.

title: bun test: persistent worker-level test environments for isolated DOM/React suites
excerpt:
## What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bun test --isolate` correctly gives every test file a fresh global and module registry, but environment infrastructure loaded from `preload` is also loaded and evaluated inside every fresh test global.

For DOM/React suites, a typical preload imports `jsdom`, constructs a `JSDOM`, installs its globals, imports environment helpers, and registers cleanup. Bun's VM-level `SourceProvider`/JSC `CodeCache` avoids retranspiling and reparsing ordinary JavaScript for every file, but each isolated file still has to:

- resolve/link the environment graph into its new module registry;
- evaluate the top level of jsdom and its dependencies;
- recreate all module-level functions, classes, exports, and mutable initialization state;
- evaluate any React/testing environment helpers imported by the preload.

This differs from Jest's worker model. A Jest worker loads `jest-environment-jsdom` and the `jsdom` implementation through the worker's outer Node module registry once. For each test file it constructs a new `JSDOM`, creates a fresh environment/runtime/module registry, runs setup files, and tears that file's environment down. The environment implementation is persistent worker infrastructure; user modules remain isolated.

Rstest recently introduced a related optimization in commit `f5c4ade73b3407c53e1eb63ef033b28e291476d3`: it optionally prebundles jsdom/happy-dom once per run and caches the loaded environment module once per worker, while still constructing and tearing down an environment per file.

Observed on a large React + jsdom + React Testing Library suite (one CI shard out of five):

- Jest: approximately 40 seconds
- Bun with `--parallel=3` and per-file isolation: approximately 296 seconds
- Bun peak RSS: approximately 15 GB across three workers

Two independent memory/correctness problems need to be separated from this proposal:

- #31771/#31772 tracks retired isolated module graphs being retained across files.
- #39768 (fix open in #35712) tracks Bun's snapshot serializer recursively walking jsdom internals through `Symbol(impl)`. A tiny seven-line DOM snapshot becomes roughly 147,000 lines/7.6 MB, and DOM snapshot suites can exceed 40 GB RSS.

Those fixes should land independently and are prerequisites for clean end-to-end measurements. This proposal concerns repeated environment loading/evaluation after retired module graphs are reclaimed and DOM values serialize normally. It should not weaken test-file is

title: import()/import.meta.resolve reject single-slash file: URLs that new URL() and Node accept
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.x x86_64 (also reproduces on the same version via the prebuilt `bun-linux-x64` release archive)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Bun rejects the single-slash `file:` URL form. Per WHATWG URL, `file:/abs/path` is
valid and normalizes to `file:///abs/path` — `new URL('file:/tmp/x').href` returns
`file:///tmp/x` in Bun itself. But passing that same string to `import()` or
`import.meta.resolve()` makes Bun parse it as a *bare specifier* whose package
name is `file:`.

```js
// mod.mjs
export default { ok: true };
```

```js
// probe.mjs
import path from 'node:path';

const abs = new URL('./mod.mjs', import.meta.url).pathname;

console.log(new URL('file:/tmp/x').href);          // file:///tmp/x  (Bun agrees with the spec here)

await import('file://' + abs);                     // OK in Bun
await import('file:/' + abs.replace(/^\//, ''));   // throws in Bun, works in Node
await import(path.join('file://' + abs));          // same: path.join collapses // to /
```

```
bun probe.mjs
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Both forms resolve, as they do in Node.js 24.19.0:

```
OK  import.meta.resolve file://  (two slashes) -> file:///tmp/fileurl3/mod.mjs
OK  import()           file://  (two slashes)
OK  import.meta.resolve file:/   (one slash)   -> file:///tmp/fileurl3/mod.mjs
OK  import()           file:/   (one slash)
OK  import.meta.resolve path.join collapses it  -> file:///tmp/fileurl3/mod.mjs
OK  import()           path.join collapses it
```

### What do you see instead?

```
OK  import.meta.resolve file://  (two slashes) -> file:///tmp/fileurl3/mod.mjs
OK  import()           file://  (two slashes)
ERR import.meta.resolve file:/   (one slash)   -> Cannot find package 'file:' imported from /tmp/fileurl3/probe.mjs
ERR import()           file:/   (one slash)    -> Cannot find package 'file:' imported from /tmp/fileurl3/probe.mjs
ERR import.meta.resolve path.join collapses it -> Cannot find package 'file:' imported from /tmp/fileurl3/probe.mjs
ERR import()           path.join collapses it  -> Cannot find package 'file:' imported from /tmp/fileurl3/probe.mjs
```

Note Bun's own `new URL()` normalizes the same string correctly, so the URL parser
and the module resolver disagree.

### Additional information

This is not a synthetic case. It is what currently stops Storybook from running
under Bun, which matters for `bun --bun vitest` against a Storybook confi

title: "is not in the catalog" after bumping a catalog entry to a version published the same day
excerpt:
Bun 1.4.0 (34cbb9a40), macOS arm64. Monorepo with a root `catalog` and a few workspaces depending on `"@aws-sdk/client-s3": "catalog:"`.

I bumped the catalog entry from 3.1114.0 to 3.1115.0 (published to npm about an hour earlier) and ran `bun install`:

```
error: @aws-sdk/client-s3@catalog: is not in the catalog
  bun add --catalog @aws-sdk/client-s3
```

The error repeats once per workspace referencing the entry, and the suggested `bun add --catalog @aws-sdk/client-s3@3.1115.0` fails the same way. The entry was in the catalog the whole time, and `bun info @aws-sdk/client-s3 version` printed 3.1115.0 at the same moment.

Deleting the package's resolved entry from bun.lock unblocked it (install refetched and resolved 3.1115.0 fine), and so did simply retrying a while later — recreating the exact same package.json/bun.lock state then installs cleanly. So it looks like resolution used a cached manifest that predated 3.1115.0 without revalidating it, and the failure surfaced as a catalog problem. Bumping the same catalog entry to an already-cached version does not trigger it.

title: bun install writes uninitialized memory into package.json `overrides` while migrating pnpm-workspace.yaml (silently drops version pins; can feed `git clone`)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

### What platform is your computer?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun install` in a large pnpm monorepo.

> **Note on redaction:** this is a closed-source repo, so every package name below
> is replaced with a placeholder (`@scope/pkg-a`, `pkg-b`, …) and versions are
> stand-ins. **All non-printable byte sequences are verbatim**, and the structure,
> counts and timings are unmodified. I can build a sanitized reproduction bundle
> if that would help — see the end.

The repo has `pnpm-workspace.yaml` + `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so Bun runs its migration:

```
moved pnpm-workspace.yaml to workspaces, pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides to overrides,
pnpm-workspace.yaml patchedDependencies to patchedDependencies in package.json
[13.88s] migrated lockfile from pnpm-lock.yaml
```

Scale of the repo that reproduces it:

| | |
|---|---|
| workspace packages | 78, across 5 glob roots |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | 35,717 lines |
| packages installed | 2,935 |
| `overrides:` entries in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | 52 |

```sh
rm -rf node_modules bun.lock
bun install
```

**Nondeterministic — 3 of 5 runs.** The tell is how long the migration step takes: every run where `migrated lockfile from pnpm-lock.yaml` reported **~14s** was corrupt, and every run where it reported **under 2s** was clean.

| run | migration step | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `[13.88s]` | **corrupt** — 16 of 52 entries |
| 2 | `[1.60s]` | clean |

title: `Bun.plugin()` cannot safely instrument JavaScript: `onLoad()` breaks CommonJS
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a CommonJS module named `target.js`:

```js
module.exports.greet = function greet(name) {
  return `hello ${name}`
}
```

Create `app.js`:

```js
const { greet } = require('./target.js')

console.log(greet('world'))
```

Without a plugin, the application works:

```bash
bun ./app.js
```

Output:

```text
hello world
```

Now create `preload.js` with an `onLoad()` hook that returns the file unchanged:

```js
const { readFileSync } = require('node:fs')

Bun.plugin({
  name: 'pass-through-source-hook',

  setup(build) {
    build.onLoad(
      {
        filter: /target\.js$/,
        namespace: 'file'
      },
      args => {
        console.log('onLoad keys:', Object.keys(args).sort())

        return {
          loader: 'js',
          contents: readFileSync(args.path, 'utf8')
        }
      }
    )
  }
})
```

Run the same application with the plugin:

```bash
bun --preload ./preload.js ./app.js
```

Bun 1.4 prints:

```text
onLoad keys: [ "path" ]

TypeError: greet is not a function.
```

The plugin did not modify the source, but returning the CommonJS source through `onLoad()` changed its behavior and caused `require('./target.js')` to return an object without the expected exports.

The logged arguments also show that the callback only receives:

```js
{
  path: '/absolute/path/to/target.js'
}
```

It does not receive the module format, import kind, importer, namespace, loader, or source contents.

### What is the expected behavior?

Returning a JavaScript file unchanged from `Bun.plugin().onLoad()` should preserve its original module semantics. A CommonJS file using `module.exports` should remain CommonJS and continue to work through `require()`.

The callback also needs enough information to transform the source safely. At minimum, it should expose:

- Whether the module is being loaded through `require()` or `import`.
- Whether Bun will evaluate it as CommonJS or ESM.
- The importer.
- The namespace.
- The selected loader or module format.
- Optionally, the source contents Bun has already loaded.

The same `.js` file can be interpreted differently depending on the importing package, its nearest `package.json`, and whether it was reached through `require()` or `import`. A source-transforming plugin cannot reliably infer that information from the filename.

### What do you see instead?

A pass

title: Windows: a rejecting Bun.file() read does not keep the event loop alive — process exits 0 mid-await with no output (regression in 1.4.0)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40 (regression — 1.3.14 is fine)

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

Linux (Ubuntu/WSL2, bun 1.4.0) is **not** affected — see the platform matrix below.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On Windows, a rejecting `Bun.file(...)` read (missing file) does not keep the event loop referenced. If that read is the only pending work, the process exits 0 _before the promise settles_ — the `await` never returns, the `catch` never runs, and nothing after it executes.

`floating.ts`:

```ts
async function main() {
  try {
    await Bun.file("definitely-missing-file.txt").text();
  } catch {}
  console.log("DONE");
}
main();
```

```
bun run floating.ts
```

The trigger is that `main()` is _not_ top-level awaited, so once the module finishes evaluating there is nothing else holding the loop open. This is the ordinary shape of a CLI entrypoint (`main().catch(handler)`).

### What is the expected behavior?

Prints `DONE` and exits 0. This is what Bun 1.3.14 does on Windows, and what Bun 1.4.0 does on Linux.

A pending `Bun.file().text()` should keep the event loop alive until it settles, whether it resolves or rejects with ENOENT.

### What do you see instead?

No output at all. Exit code 0.

There is no error, no unhandled rejection, and no non-zero exit — the process reports success while having silently skipped the rest of the program. That combination is what makes this nasty in practice: it looks like a command that ran fine and produced nothing.

### Additional information

**Platform / version matrix** (20 runs each of the snippet above, counting silent exits):

|                                | result                      |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| Windows, bun 1.3.14            | 0/20 silent — prints `DONE` |
| Windows, bun 1.4.0             | **20/20 silent**            |
| Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu), bun 1.4.0 | 0/20 silent — prints `DONE` |

Deterministic on Windows 1.4.0, not intermittent.

title: node:http2 client stops processing inbound frames for ~28s under load (regression 1.3.14 → 1.4.0)
excerpt:
On bun 1.4.0 a `node:http2` client stops processing inbound frames entirely for about 28 seconds, then resumes on its own. During the stall the client answers nothing — not even HTTP/2 PING, which is handled below the application. The same workload on bun 1.3.14 is clean.

Platform: darwin-aarch64, macOS 26.2 (arm64). Reproduced against a Rust `tonic`-based gRPC server running in Docker with a published port.

Versions tested:

| Runtime | Result |
|---|---|
| bun 1.4.0 (`34cbb9a40`) | fails |
| bun 1.4.0-canary.1 (`01c4e2fd6`) | fails |
| bun 1.3.14 (`0d9b296a`) | passes |
| node 22.22.2 | passes |

Evidence, captured with a passthrough TCP proxy that decodes HTTP/2 frames without reframing. Same server, same workload, only the runtime differs:

```
bun 1.4.0                                bun 1.3.14
 1065ms S->C PING                         1167ms S->C PING
 1065ms C->S PING ACK   (0ms)             1168ms C->S PING ACK  (1ms)
 3088ms S->C PING                         3194ms S->C PING
 3088ms C->S PING ACK   (0ms)             3195ms C->S PING ACK  (1ms)
13164ms S->C PING
        (never ACKed)                     workload completes: 2.28s
31063ms C->S PING       <- client's own 30s keepalive timer fires; it wakes up
```

The client ACKs PINGs normally at 1065ms and 3088ms, then stops. Client outbound is completely silent from **3161ms to 31063ms**. The proxy kept delivering inbound DATA to the client's socket during that window (6069ms, 11067ms, 16070ms) and the application never saw any of it. Timers keep firing throughout — the 30s keepalive fires on schedule and appears to be what kicks the session back to life.

The stall begins immediately after a burst of concurrent streams (ids 37/41/43 at ~3.15s).

Consequence against a real gRPC server: the server's keepalive goes unanswered, so it resets the long-lived streams with `RST_STREAM` (code 0) ~3s later, dropping server-side handler registrations. Application-level heartbeats then time out and the channel is declared dead, surfacing as `UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped` cascades in `@grpc/grpc-js`.

Two further constraints, both reproducible:

- It only occurs under `bun test`. The identical code under `bun run` passes every time.
- Ruled out as causes: HTTP/2 flow-control window sizes and SETTINGS (matched exactly to the server's `initialWindowSize: 65535`), TLS, IPv6 vs IPv4, Docker port-mapping NAT, TCP segmentation, and PING handling in isolation (all fine standalone on 1.4.0).

title: Prisma relation query fails inside Next.js server when executed by Bun 1.4.0
excerpt:
## Summary

Prisma relation queries fail only when the Next.js server is executed by Bun. The same Next.js production artifact, database, generated Prisma client, and request succeed when the server is executed by Node.js.

The failure is exposed by Better Auth's authenticated session lookup, but it also reproduces with a direct `prisma.session.findFirst()` call in a server-rendered Next.js path.

## Environment

- Bun 1.4.0 stable
- Next.js 16.3.1
- Prisma 7.9.1
- `@prisma/adapter-pg` 7.9.1
- `pg` 8.x
- Better Auth 1.7.1
- PostgreSQL
- Next.js App Router with Turbopack
- Prisma generator: `prisma-client`, `engineType = "client"`, `runtime = "bun"`

The application uses the Prisma-recommended `@prisma/adapter-pg` driver adapter and a normal `pg.Pool`.

## Reproduction

With a schema containing this relation:

```prisma
model User {
  id       String    @id
  email    String    @unique
  sessions Session[]
}

model Session {
  id        String   @id
  token     String   @unique
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  userId    String
  user      User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
}
```

Create a server-rendered Next.js path that runs:

```ts
const session = await prisma.session.findFirst({
  orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
  select: { id: true, user: true },
});
```

Then build and run the standalone artifact:

```sh
bun prisma generate
bun next build
bun .next/standalone/server.js
```

Request the server-rendered path with a valid database/session.

## Actual behavior

Bun logs:

```text
prisma:error null is not an object (evaluating 'e.constructor')
```

The request fails. In the real application, the HTTP response is misleadingly `200`, but the React Server Components payload contains Better Auth's `Failed to get session` error and the authenticated merchant home page cannot render.

The scalar equivalent succeeds in the same Bun-hosted Next server:

```ts
await prisma.session.findFirst({
  orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
  select: { id: true },
});
```

The same relation query also succeeds in a standalone Bun script importing the identical generated client, so this is specific to the Next.js server bundle/runtime combination rather than the PostgreSQL schema or credentials.

## Control result

The identical Next.js standalone artifact passes authenticated sign-in and the authenticated page when started with:

```sh
node .next/standalone/server.js
```

Node emits the expected SQL for the session query and the related user query. Start

title: node:inspector: Profiler.takePreciseCoverage emits zero-width ranges, hanging the @bcoe/v8-coverage merge
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`Profiler.takePreciseCoverage` emits **zero-width ranges** (`startOffset === endOffset`). V8 never does, and every consumer of the protocol treats a range as a half-open interval, so a zero-width entry is not a valid range-tree node.

The whole repro is self-contained — no dependencies, writes and removes its own fixture, and exits non-zero when the bug is present:

```js
import { Session } from 'node:inspector/promises'
import { writeFileSync, unlinkSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'

const file = join(tmpdir(), `cov-fixture-${process.pid}.mjs`)
writeFileSync(file, 'export function f(x){return x}\n')

const session = new Session()
session.connect()
await session.post('Profiler.enable')
await session.post('Profiler.startPreciseCoverage', { callCount: true, detailed: true })

const { f } = await import(pathToFileURL(file).href)
f(1)

const { result } = await session.post('Profiler.takePreciseCoverage')
unlinkSync(file)

const runtime = typeof Bun === 'undefined' ? `node ${process.version}` : `bun ${Bun.version}`
const script = result.find((s) => s.url.includes('cov-fixture-'))
const ranges = script ? script.functions.flatMap((fn) => fn.ranges) : []
const zeroWidth = ranges.filter((r) => r.startOffset === r.endOffset)

console.log(`${runtime}  |  source is 31 bytes  |  ${ranges.length} ranges emitted`)
console.log(`zero-width ranges: ${zeroWidth.length}`, JSON.stringify(zeroWidth))
console.log(zeroWidth.length === 0 ? 'PASS — no zero-width ranges' : 'FAIL — V8 never emits startOffset === endOffset')
process.exit(zeroWidth.length === 0 ? 0 : 1)
```

title: Recursive import reference continuously imports while maintaining high CPU usage
1.4.0 regression: `s3.write(key, Bun.file(path))` hangs forever when the file is ≥ 5 × partSize — worked in 1.3.14
excerpt:
## What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0

## What platform is your computer?

Reproduced on both:
- macOS arm64 (Darwin 24.6.0)
- Linux x64 (official `oven/bun` Docker image, Debian)

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

Upload a file to any S3-compatible endpoint (observed against Cloudflare R2) using a `Bun.file` input:

```ts
import { S3Client } from 'bun';

const s3 = new S3Client(); // S3_* env vars, R2 endpoint
await Bun.write('payload.bin', new Uint8Array(25 * 1024 * 1024));
await s3.write('repro/payload.bin', Bun.file('payload.bin')); // never resolves, never rejects
console.log('done'); // never reached
```

## What is the expected behavior?

The upload completes (Bun 1.3.14 completes all the cases below in a few seconds).

## What do you see instead?

`s3.write` neither resolves nor rejects — it hangs forever. No error, no timeout.

The boundary is exact and tracks `partSize`:

| partSize | file size | parts | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 MiB (default) | 24 MiB | 5 (4 full + partial) | OK |
| 5 MiB (default) | 25 MiB | 5 full | **hangs** |
| 5 MiB (default) | 26–74 MiB | ≥5 | **hangs** |
| 10 MiB | 26 MiB | 3 | OK |
| 10 MiB | 50 MiB | 5 full | **hangs** |
| 10 MiB | 51 MiB | 6 | **hangs** |

So the hang starts precisely when the file reaches **5 × partSize** — i.e. once the first 5 parts fill the in-flight window, the file reader is never resumed. Notes:

- Buffer input is NOT affected: `s3.write(key, uint8array)` works at every size tested (up to 74 MiB), only the `Bun.file` streaming path hangs.
- `queueSize` appears to be ignored: with `{ partSize: 10 MiB, queueSize: 2 }`, 21 MiB and 26 MiB still succeed (they would exceed a 2-slot window) and the threshold stays at 5 parts.
- Bun 1.3.14 passes every case above, same machine, same bucket — this regressed in 1.4.0.

Real-world impact: our hourly production ingest archives a ~74 MiB CSV to R2 via `s3.write(key, Bun.file(path))`; after the `oven/bun:1` image advanced to 1.4.0 the call hung indefinitely on every run on two independent servers, wedging the whole pipeline (there is no timeout to hit — the promise just never settles).

Workarounds we found: pin Bun ≤ 1.3.14, buffer the file into memory first, or set `partSize > size / 5`.

---

*Investigation, bisection, and repro by Claude (Fable 5) via Claude Code, working from our production incident.*

title: Heap peaks 1.4x to 2.6x above Node under sustained allocation before collecting
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.1.8-1-cachyos x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

I put the repro here: https://github.com/jlucaso1/js-runtime-memory-probe

```sh
git clone https://github.com/jlucaso1/js-runtime-memory-probe
cd js-runtime-memory-probe
node run.mjs
```

It runs four allocation shapes under both runtimes and reports `Private_Dirty` growth above each run's own baseline, so the size of the runtime at startup never enters the numbers. Linux only, since it reads `/proc/self/smaps_rollup`.

The smallest case on its own is `module-load`, which generates an ESM tree at run time and imports it, so both runtimes parse identical bytes:

```sh
MODULE_FILES=800 node --expose-gc scenarios/module-load.mjs
MODULE_FILES=800 bun scenarios/module-load.mjs
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Peak heap in the same range as Node for the same work, or a collection triggered before the heap climbs that far.

### What do you see instead?

Bun's heap grows well past Node's before it collects. Medians of 3 runs, MiB of `Private_Dirty` growth:

| scenario | runtime | peak | settled |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| allocation-rate | node | 6.3 | 6.1 |
| allocation-rate | bun | **16.5** | 5.2 |
| module-load | node | 39.0 | 39.6 |
| module-load | bun | **53.4** | 34.7 |
| request-loop | node | 11.1 | 11.1 |
| request-loop | bun | **18.0** | 10.4 |
| retention | node | 148.8 | 148.8 |
| retention | bun | 69.1 | 69.1 |

I want to be clear that this is not a "Bun uses more memory" report. Bun settles at or below Node in every scenario, and when nothing is garbage it wins outright: in `retention` it holds the same live records in half the memory, 364 bytes per record against 778. Node peaks lower but then never hands the pages back.

The only problem is the peak. On `module-load` with 800 files Bun reaches 69.1 MiB against Node's 40.1, and five seconds later it is back down to 40.3 without any manual collection, so the memory does come back, just late. `--smol` helps a little, lowering the peak by roughly 14% across four runs, from about 53 MiB to about 46, which still leaves it above Node.

That gap matters because container limits, memory quotas and the OOM killer all watch the peak rather than the settled value. A process sized against Node's footprint can die on Bun while ending up smaller once it has collected.

I ran into this while benchmarking a What

title: os.userInfo().username returns $USER env value (or "unknown" when unset) instead of the passwd entry — Node compat
excerpt:
## What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

## What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.1 arm64 (Apple Silicon)

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
# Bun: username tracks the $USER env var
env -u USER bun -e 'console.log(require("os").userInfo().username)'
# → unknown

USER=zzz bun -e 'console.log(require("os").userInfo().username)'
# → zzz

# Node (v26.7.0) on the same machine: username comes from the passwd entry
env -u USER node -e 'console.log(require("os").userInfo().username)'
# → <real username>

USER=zzz node -e 'console.log(require("os").userInfo().username)'
# → <real username>
```

## What is the expected behavior?

Node-compat: `os.userInfo()` documents that it returns the effective user from the password database (libuv `uv_os_get_passwd`, i.e. `getpwuid(geteuid())`). The env should not influence `username`, and an unset `$USER` should not degrade it to `"unknown"`.

## What do you see instead?

`userInfo().username` mirrors `$USER` verbatim — any spoofed value is returned as-is, and when the variable is absent it returns the string `"unknown"` even though the uid has a perfectly good passwd entry.

## Additional information

This bites in minimal-environment spawn contexts (launchd, cron, containers, agent frameworks that construct child envs from scratch): code that restores identity with `userInfo().username` works under Node but silently propagates a wrong/absent `$USER` under Bun. In our case it re-broke a keychain-credential lookup that the call was specifically added to fix; `execFileSync('/usr/bin/id', ['-un'])` was the workaround.
