docs: `timestamp without time zone` decoding as UTC isn't documented in the PostgreSQL section
excerpt:
### What is the type of issue?

Documentation is missing, Documentation is confusing

### What is the issue?

`Bun.SQL`'s postgres adapter decodes `timestamp` (i.e. `timestamp without time zone`, OID 1114) by treating the wire text as **UTC**. `node-postgres` and `postgres.js` — and PGlite, which follows `pg` — decode the same value as **local time**. This is a real, user-visible divergence from the two most widely used JS Postgres drivers.

Bun's behavior is deliberate and self-consistent, so this is a docs request, not a bug report. From `src/sql_jsc/postgres/types/date.rs:39-46`:

> Decode a Postgres `timestamp` (WITHOUT TIME ZONE) text value as UTC, so the text/simple-query path agrees with the binary path (which is already UTC). ... without this they'd go through JS `Date.parse` and be read as local time on non-UTC hosts.

I confirmed the choice is coherent: a `Date` bound into a `timestamp` column round-trips exactly, at both `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=Etc/GMT+7`, because Bun writes UTC components and reads them back the same way.

The problem is purely discoverability. The behavior is documented in **one sentence, in the MySQL section** (`docs/runtime/sql.mdx:1370`), as a trailing clause:

> `DATETIME` and `TIMESTAMP` values have no timezone on the wire, so Bun reads them back as **UTC**. ... The same applies to PostgreSQL's `timestamp` (without time zone); `timestamptz` carries an explicit offset and is unaffected.

A developer using PostgreSQL has no reason to read the MySQL section. The PostgreSQL type-mapping table says nothing about it, and nothing anywhere mentions that this differs from `pg` / `postgres.js`.


### Where did you find it?

<https://bun.com/docs/runtime/sql> — `docs/runtime/sql.mdx:1370` (the existing note, inside the MySQL section). The gap is in the PostgreSQL type-mapping section of the same page.

### Suggested change

1. Add a `timestamp` / `timestamptz` row to the **PostgreSQL** type-mapping table noting `timestamp` decodes as UTC.
2. Add a short callout in the PostgreSQL section stating explicitly that this differs from `node-postgres` and `postgres.js`, which decode OID 1114 as local time, and that code migrating from those drivers on a non-UTC host will see values shift by the local offset.
3. Optionally note the rationale (text and binary paths agree; bound `Date`s round-trip) so the choice doesn't read as an oversight.

title: `formData()` ignores the multipart part's `Content-Type` header and infers `File.type` from the filename extension
excerpt:
## What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0 (also reproduced on 1.3.5)

## What platform is your computer?

Darwin arm64 (macOS 15 / Apple Silicon)

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// repro.js
const boundary = "----reproBoundary123";
const body = [
  `--${boundary}`,
  `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="a.bin"`,
  `Content-Type: image/png`,
  ``,
  `fakepngbytes`,
  `--${boundary}--`,
  ``,
].join("\r\n");

const req = new Request("http://localhost/upload", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": `multipart/form-data; boundary=${boundary}` },
  body,
});
const fd = await req.formData();
console.log(fd.get("file").type);
```

```
$ bun repro.js
application/octet-stream
```

The part header explicitly says `Content-Type: image/png`, but the parsed `File.type` is `application/octet-stream`.

Two observations that narrow down the cause:

1. **Rename `a.bin` to `a.png` in the same repro and the output flips to `image/png`.** The part header is unchanged, so the parser is deriving `File.type` from the filename extension and ignoring the part's `Content-Type` header entirely. The extension-based guess masks the bug whenever the extension happens to agree with the header.
2. `Response.formData()` behaves the same way (same repro via `new Response(body, { headers })`).

Per the Fetch spec's multipart/form-data parsing (and RFC 7578 §4.4), the resulting `File`'s type comes from the part's `Content-Type` header. Node 22.22 returns `image/png` for the exact same bytes:

```
$ node repro.mjs   # same body, via new Request(...).formData()
image/png
```

## What is the expected behavior?

`File.type` is `"image/png"` — the value of the part's `Content-Type` header, regardless of the filename.

## What do you see instead?

`File.type` is `"application/octet-stream"` (or whatever the filename extension implies).

## Additional information

The same thing happens over real HTTP into a `Bun.serve` handler — this is not specific to hand-constructed `Request` objects. With a handler that just echoes `(await req.formData()).get("file").type`:

```
$ curl -F 'file=@a.bin;type=image/png' http://127.0.0.1:55696/
{"bun":"1.4.0","type":"application/octet-stream"}

$ curl -F 'file=@a.bin;filename=a.png;type=image/png' http://127.0.0.1:55696/
{"bun":"1.4.0","type":"image/png"}
```

Same bytes, same declared `Content-Type`, only the filename differs — and the filename wins. So every multipart parsing path is affected, and the bug stays invisible

YAML.stringify() emits an unnecessary trailing space after `:` on parent-mapping keys
excerpt: ## Description When a key's value is itself a nested mapping (i.e. the key has no scalar value directly after it), `Bun.YAML.stringify()` emits a **trailing space** after the colon, even though that space carries no meaning and isn't required by the YAML spec for an empty/parent node (YAML 1.2 §7.1.3). This is wasted output — extra bytes on every parent-mapping line with zero functional purpose — and it causes **noisy git diffs** any time a file is rewritten, since every parent-mapping line shows trailing-whitespace churn even when nothing semantically changed. ## Actual behavior Open `bun repl` & paste this: ```ts import { YAML } from "bun"; console.log(YAML.stringify({ models: { openai: { name: "gpt" } } }, null, 2)); ``` Then open it in a text editor like Zed to see: Output (trailing space after `models:` and `openai:` — invisible but present): ``` models: openai: name: gpt ``` ## Expected behavior No trailing space after a colon when the key has no inline scalar value: ``` models: openai: name: gpt ``` ## Why this matters The trailing space serves no purpose — it's pure wasted output on every parent-mapping key in every stringified document. For YAML files tracked in git (config files, prompt templates, fixtures), this also means unnecessary whitespace-only diff noise on every rewrite.

title: Support Vite / Rolldown plugin compatibility layer in Bun.build
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

The JavaScript ecosystem has an enormous collection of battle-tested Vite and Rollup plugins (such as `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, SVGR, MDX, PWA, and specialized asset/CSS transformers). 

Currently, migrating an existing frontend project or complex build pipeline to `Bun.build` / `Bun.serve` requires rewriting these plugins into Bun's native plugin format (`BunPlugin` with `setup`, `onResolve`, and `onLoad`). For teams relying on third-party, niche, or unmaintained Vite plugins, this lack of compatibility is a major blocker to adopting Bun as their primary bundler and dev server.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Provide an adapter layer (either built directly into `Bun.build`'s `plugins` array or via a utility like `bun:plugins`) to consume standard Vite/Rollup plugin hooks.

### Example API
```ts
import { build } from "bun";
import vue from "@vitejs/plugin-vue";
import { fromVitePlugin } from "bun:plugins"; // or native support directly in plugins array

await build({
  entrypoints: ["./src/main.ts"],
  outdir: "./dist",
  plugins: [
    fromVitePlugin(vue()),
  ],
});

### What alternatives have you considered?

Proposed Hook Mapping
resolveId -> onResolve
load -> onLoad
transform -> onLoad (post-read transform pipe)
buildStart / configResolved -> setup initialization
Alternatives considered
Running Vite via bunx --bun vite, which works but sacrifices the native speed and simplicity of Bun.build and Bun.serve.
Manually rewriting plugins for Bun, which creates duplicate maintenance overhead and fragments the ecosystem.

## What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0 (stable release), macOS arm64; also observed on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest

## What happened?

Follow-up to #36235 (closed as fixed on the 1.4 line, and locked to author-reopen). The `bun test --parallel` worker deadlock still occurs on v1.4.0 stable, at a reduced rate.

Data from migrating our suite (~1100 Bun test files) from 1.3.14 to 1.4.0 stable:

- 30-run randomized soak (`--parallel=4 --randomize`): the stall occurred twice, absorbed by our 120s no-output watchdog and passing on identical retry; zero test failures otherwise.
- One additional occurrence on a GitHub Actions ubuntu runner during the same migration (job overran its budget while absorbing a stall).
- Rate comparison on the same suite: roughly 10% per run on 1.3.14, roughly 7% (2/30) on 1.4.0.

Signature is unchanged from #36235 when captured live: exactly one `--test-worker` process remains, every thread parked in `__ulock_wait2` / `__psynch_cvwait`, no children, no external sockets, no common in-flight test file, and the parent buffers output while waiting, so the log freezes.

## Steps to reproduce

Same as #36235: needs a large suite; reproduces for us within a few dozen `--parallel=4 --randomize` runs. We are happy to run instrumented or patched builds against our suite and can share full `sample`/`lsof` captures.

## What did you expect to happen?

The run completes or fails instead of hanging.

bun-types 1.4.0 memoryPressure overrides break process.removeListener/off with @types/node@24
excerpt:
> **Note: this issue was opened by an AI agent** on behalf of its user, after verifying the reproduction in a real project.

### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```bash
bun init -y
bun add -d @types/node@24
printf 'process.removeListener("SIGINT", () => {});\n' > index.ts
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit
```

### What is the expected behavior?

No errors — `process.removeListener("SIGINT", fn)` is valid Bun/Node code.

### What do you see instead?

```
error TS2345: Argument of type '"SIGINT"' is not assignable to parameter of type '"memoryPressure"'.
```

Same failure for `process.off("unhandledRejection", fn)` and any other event name passed to `removeListener`/`off`.

### Additional information

This is the same bug as #39807, which was closed as unreproducible — but the triage repro resolved `@types/node@26.2.0` and only tested `process.on("SIGINT")`, both of which mask the bug (see https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/39807#issuecomment-5375609896 for the full analysis). Filing fresh since that issue can't be reopened by non-maintainers.

Root cause:

- `bun-types@1.4.0` `overrides.d.ts` declares `removeListener(event: "memoryPressure", …)` and `off(event: "memoryPressure", …)` on `NodeJS.Process`.
- In `@types/node@24` (current LTS typings), `Process` has **no** direct `removeListener`/`off` declarations — they are only inherited from `EventEmitter`. A derived interface's re-declared method **hides** inherited overloads instead of merging, so `memoryPressure` becomes the only visible overload.
- `@types/node@26` declares generic `removeListener(eventName: string | symbol, …)`/`off` directly on `Process` (process.d.ts:2176, 2206), so declaration merging keeps them visible — that's why the triage matrix passed.
- `process.on("SIGINT")` typechecks on both versions because `on` has Signals-specific overloads on `Process` itself.

Suggested fix: re-declare the generic `(eventName: string | symbol, listener: (...args: any[]) => void): this` overload for `removeListener`/`off` (and the other overridden methods) alongside the `memoryPressure` overloads in `overrides.d.ts`.

title: bun test hangs at 100% CPU when mock.module factory is async and suspends, and the specifier is also statically imported
excerpt:
## What version of Bun is running?

1.3.13 (bf2e2cec), Linux x64.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

Two files, no dependencies.

`helper.ts`:
```ts
export const x = 1;
```

`hang.test.ts`:
```ts
import { test, expect, mock } from "bun:test";
mock.module("./helper.ts", async () => { await Promise.resolve(); return { x: 2 }; });
import { x } from "./helper.ts";
test("t", () => { expect(x).toBe(2); });
```

Run:
```
bun test hang.test.ts
```

## What is the expected behavior?

The test runs and passes, as it does when the factory is synchronous.

## What do you see instead?

The process never terminates. It prints the `bun test v1.3.13` banner and nothing else, then spins at ~100% CPU indefinitely. It has to be SIGKILLed. In one real-world case it ran 13m31s wall with 13m11s of CPU time before being killed.

The hang is at module load, not in a test body and not at teardown: passing `-t "zzzznomatchzzz"` so that no test matches still hangs.

## Minimal trigger

Three conditions together:

1. `mock.module()` factory is `async` **and actually suspends** (contains an `await` that yields).
2. The mocked specifier is also **statically imported** in the module graph being loaded.
3. Both occur in the same file.

Remove any one and it works.

## Variants tested

Hangs:
- The reproducer above.
- Same shape via `vi.mock` (vitest API shim) instead of `mock.module`.
- Same shape mocking a builtin (`fs`, `fs/promises`) instead of a user module.

Passes:
- Synchronous factory: `mock.module("./helper.ts", () => ({ x: 2 }))`.
- Async but non-suspending factory: `async () => ({ x: 2 })`.
- Async suspending factory **without** the static import of the mocked specifier.

So it is not specific to vitest, not specific to builtins, and not specific to any package. The `await` inside the factory combined with the static import is the trigger.

## Process forensics

Main thread state `R`, `wchan=0` (pure userspace, no syscall). Thread count drops from 18 to 8 on entering the spin. `utime` grows 1s per second. Output stops permanently. Looks like an unbounded busy-loop in the module loader waiting on a promise that cannot settle.

Also worth noting: a full `bun test` run in this state survived SIGTERM and needed SIGKILL, though the minimal reproducer above does die on SIGTERM.

## Impact

A single test file with this shape hangs an entire `bun test` run forever. In our repo, 600 of 601 test files run together in ~61s; the one file with this pattern makes the whole suite unrunna

title: Bun 1.4.0 fresh install keeps a globally deduplicable transitive TypeScript 7 copy
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

Regression comparison:

- Bun 1.3.14 (`0d9b296a`)
- Bun 1.4.0 (`34cbb9a40`)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64. The downstream failure also reproduces in GitHub Actions on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a fresh directory with this `package.json`:

```json
{
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "dts-bundle-generator": "9.5.1",
    "typescript": "^5.9.3"
  }
}
```

Then run:

```sh
rm -rf node_modules bun.lock
bun install
bun -e 'const { createRequire } = require("node:module"); const r = createRequire(require.resolve("dts-bundle-generator/package.json")); const ts = r("typescript"); console.log(ts.version, typeof ts.sys)'
bun dedupe --check
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Bun 1.3.14 resolves one TypeScript instance, `5.9.3`. That version satisfies both the root range `^5.9.3` and `dts-bundle-generator@9.5.1`'s dependency range `>=5.0.2`. npm 11 and pnpm 11 also resolve only TypeScript 5.9.3 for the same fresh manifest.

I expected Bun 1.4.0 either to preserve that fresh-install behavior or to document the new duplication policy explicitly.

### What do you see instead?

Bun 1.4.0 installs two versions:

```text
typescript@5.9.3
dts-bundle-generator/typescript@7.0.2
```

The probe prints:

```text
7.0.2 undefined
```

Bun 1.3.14 prints:

```text
5.9.3 object
```

Bun 1.4.0's own dedupe planner reports that the nested copy is removable:

```text
$ bun dedupe --check
~ typescript 7.0.2 -> 5.9.3

1 duplicate version can be removed
```

Applying `bun dedupe` removes the nested TypeScript 7 copy without changing `package.json`, and the downstream declaration bundle succeeds.

### Additional information

This is not a claim that `typescript@7.0.2` violates the transitive `>=5.0.2` range. The regression/design gap is that a fresh Bun 1.4 install keeps a second version which `bun dedupe` immediately identifies as globally removable, whereas Bun 1.3.14, npm 11, and pnpm 11 converge to one version.

- #38919: keeps a deduped state stable under `bun update`; it explicitly leaves fresh-install behavior unchanged.
- #38333: introduced `bun dedupe`.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.12.101+deb13-amd64 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

## Description

With `minimumReleaseAge` enabled, I want to be able to explicitly approve a specific newly-released package version, commit that resolution to `bun.lock`, and then have `bun ci` reproduce the committed lockfile.

On Bun 1.4.0, `bun ci` appears to re-resolve the dependency and re-apply `minimumReleaseAge`, even though the exact version is already present in the committed lockfile.

This seems inconsistent with the documented behaviour that `minimumReleaseAge` only affects new resolution and that packages already present in `bun.lock` remain unchanged.

## Configuration

```toml
[install]
minimumReleaseAge = 1209600 # 14 days
```

`package.json` uses a catalog containing:

```json
{
  "catalog": {
    "@types/bun": "1.4.0"
  }
}
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Explicitly allow the new release when adding/updating it:

```bash
bun add @types/bun@1.4.0 --minimum-release-age 0
```

2. Commit `package.json` and `bun.lock`.

The committed lockfile contains exact resolutions for:

```text
@types/bun@1.4.0

excerpt:
### What

`test/js/bun/jsc/heapStats-mimalloc.test.ts` > `arena memory is tagged as application memory, not IOAccelerator` fails on **macOS 27.0 developer beta (build 26A5416b)**, and passes on macOS 26.6.2 / 15 / 14. First seen on the new opportunistic `darwin 27 aarch64` CI lane (#40019), build [103104](https://buildkite.com/bun/bun/builds/103104), bun `1.4.1-canary.1+246a83ff0`. Deterministic: fails in the parallel batch and when rerun alone.

```
test/js/bun/jsc/heapStats-mimalloc.test.ts:90:20
expect(appTag).toBeGreaterThan(64)
Expected: > 64
Received: 0
```

`ioaccelerator` is also 0 (that assertion passes), so the 96 MB of arena memory the child allocates shows up under **neither** `IOAccelerator` nor `Memory Tag 24x/25x` in `vmmap --summary` on 27.

### Likely causes, in order

1. `vmmap --summary` on 27 changed how it labels app-reserved VM tags (240-255): the test matches lines starting with `Memory Tag 24` / `Memory Tag 25`, so a rename (or a different column layout) reads as 0. Parser issue, not a tagging regression.
2. The kernel/libmalloc on 27 no longer honors the `VM_MAKE_TAG(…)` passed by mimalloc's mmap, and the memory is reported under a different bucket (e.g. `MALLOC_*` or untagged). That would be a real regression in how profilers see Bun's heap.

### To confirm

On a macOS 27 machine:

```sh
bun -e 'const keep=[];for(let i=0;i<96;i++)keep.push(Buffer.alloc(1<<20,i).toString("latin1"));console.log(Bun.spawnSync({cmd:["vmmap","--summary",String(process.pid)]}).stdout.toString())'
```

and look for where the ~96 MB lands. If the label changed, widen the test's matcher. If the memory is untagged, it is the mimalloc arena tag path (`src/allocators/mimalloc_arena.zig`, the `VM_MAKE_TAG` mmap flag) on 27.

### Environment

- Host: M2 Mac mini, macOS 27.0 beta (26A5416b), bare-metal agent `darwin-aarch64-27.0-1`, queue `test-darwin-beta`
- Lane is `soft_fail`, so this does not block merges; it is an early warning for 27.

title: Bun.serve: server.stop(true) never resolves while a fetch handler promise is pending (graceful stop() works)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26220, x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`server.stop(true)` never resolves while a `fetch` handler promise is still pending. The graceful `server.stop()` resolves fine in the same situations, which is the opposite of what the two modes are for — `closeActiveConnections: true` is meant to be the one that tears down in-flight work immediately.

Plain `Bun.serve`, no WebSocket, no framework:

```ts
const server = Bun.serve({ fetch: () => new Promise<Response>(() => {}), port: 0 });
void fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${server.port}`).catch(() => {});
await Bun.sleep(100);

console.log('calling server.stop(true)');
await server.stop(true);
console.log('this line is never reached');
```

Prints `calling server.stop(true)`, then hangs indefinitely.

### What is the expected behavior?

`server.stop(true)` resolves, closing the active connection and abandoning the pending handler.

### What do you see instead?

It never resolves. Each cell below is a separate run (force = `stop(true)`, graceful = `stop()`):

| pending handler? | how the request ended | `stop(true)` | `stop()` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no request at all | — | returns 6ms | returns 6ms |
| yes | left in flight | **hangs** | returns 12006ms (after the 10s idleTimeout) |
| yes | client `AbortController.abort()` | **hangs** | returns 1004ms |
| yes | client `AbortSignal.timeout(50)` | **hangs** | returns 1004ms |

So it is the outstanding handler promise that wedges it, not the disconnect path — the client going away cleanly, aborting, or never leaving all behave the same. In the "left in flight" row Bun logs `Bun.serve() timed out a request after 10 seconds`, and `stop(true)` still does not return afterwards.

A handler that settles when the request aborts (`request.signal`) stops cleanly in 103ms, which is the workaround.

### Additional information

This appears to be new in 1.4.0: the affected test suite ran this exact shape in 279ms on 1.3.14 and hangs indefinitely on 1.4.0.

It is easy to misdiagnose downstream. Every assertion in the affected test passes; the hang happens afterwards in a `finally` doing `await server.stop(true)`. A test runner then reports it as `this test timed out after <N>ms`, which reads like a slow test rather than a stuck teardown — so the instinct is to raise the per-test timeout, which just moves the identical hang to a larger number.

title: Standalone executables leak a fresh TMPDIR copy of every dlopen'd embedded native library on each launch
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14

### Which platform(s) does your issue occur on?

Linux x64 (WSL2, kernel 6.6). Likely affects every platform where `bun build --compile` output dlopens embedded native libraries.

### What build steps are needed to reproduce?

```console
$ cc -shared -fPIC -o lib.so lib.c   # int marker(void) { return 42; }
```

`entry.ts`:

```ts
import lib from "./lib.so" with { type: "file" }

const { dlopen } = await import("bun:ffi")
dlopen(lib, { marker: { args: [], returns: "int" } })
console.log("dlopened:", lib)
```

Build and run the standalone executable twice:

```console
$ bun build --compile --target=bun-linux-x64 ./entry.ts --outfile app
$ ./app && ./app
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The temporary extraction of an embedded native library should be cleaned up after `dlopen` (or reused across launches), so running a compiled binary does not grow `$TMPDIR`.

### What do you see instead?

Every launch extracts a **fresh copy** of the embedded library to `$TMPDIR/.<hash>-<index>.so` and never deletes it — not even on clean exit. After the two runs above:

```
$ ls -la /tmp/.59ee* 
-rw-r--r-- 1 thomas thomas 15112 Aug 22 11:20 /tmp/.59ee776dfc9ebfd7-00000000.so
-rw-r--r-- 1 thomas thomas 15112 Aug 22 11:20 /tmp/.59ee776dfddbfeff-00000000.so
-rw-r--r-- 1 thomas thomas 15112 Aug 22 11:16 /tmp/.59ee77edf4bfbfbf-00000000.so
-rw-r--r-- 1 thomas thomas 15112 Aug 22 11:16 /tmp/.59ee77edf7b2bf97-00000000.so
```

One leaked file per process launch (the two 11:16 files are from earlier runs of the same binary).

### Real-world impact

[opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) ships a ~14 MB `libopentui.so` inside its compiled binary; it gets extracted to a fresh temp file on every launch and never unlinked. A user accumulated 44 orphaned copies (~533 MB), which filled `/tmp` completely — after which opencode failed to start at all with a misleading "Failed to open library ... No such file or directory" (the extraction write hits ENOSPC, so the path doesn't exist by the time `dlopen` runs).

### Notes for a fix

- Unlinking the temp file right after `dlopen` returns is safe on Linux/macOS: the inode survives for the existing mapping, and typical consumers (e.g. OpenTUI) never re-open the path. On Windows the unlink of a loaded DLL will fail, which can be ignored or deferred.
- Alternatively, reuse one cached extraction per embedded library across launches (keyed by content hash) instead of extracting per launch.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Here are three ready-to-post GitHub issues for `oven-sh/bun`, plus one comment for an existing thread. Copy each fenced block as-is into a new issue.

**Environment line for all of them:** `Bun 1.4.0 (34cbb9a40)` · Windows 11 · found migrating ~1,600 tests across 15 apps from Vitest to `bun:test`.

---

## Issue 1 — `toMatchSnapshot()` on a live DOM node OOMs instead of erroring

```markdown
**Bun version:** 1.4.0 (34cbb9a40)
**OS:** Windows 11

### Description
Calling `expect(element).toMatchSnapshot()` where `element` is a live DOM node
(e.g. a React Testing Library render result, `happy-dom`) does not serialize
the node — it walks/copies the underlying object graph and attempts a
multi-gigabyte allocation, crashing the process (OOM) instead of either
serializing correctly or throwing a normal "cannot serialize" error.

### Reproduction
```ts
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";
import { render } from "@testing-library/react";
import { MyComponent } from "./MyComponent";

test("snapshot", () => {
  const { container } = render(<MyComponent />);
  expect(container).toMatchSnapshot(); // OOMs
});
```

### Expected
Either a correct serialized snapshot (matching Vitest/Jest behavior, which
serialize via the node's own string representation) or a clean thrown error.

### Actual
The process attempts a ~30GB allocation and crashes. No catchable error —
just OOM.

### Workaround (that we shipped)
Snapshot `element.outerHTML` (a string) instead of the node itself:
```ts
expect(container.outerHTML).toMatchSnapshot();
```
This works correctly and is what we standardized on across our test suite,
but it means `toMatchSnapshot()` is unsafe on any DOM/live-object value by
default — worth either a guard that throws instead of OOMing, or a built-in
DOM-aware serializer.
```

<html>
  <head>

3. Write `styles.css` = `body { color: green; }`. Fetch `/`.

A browser then requests `/styles.css`, which the HTML route answers with the HTML fallback (status 200, `text/html`), so the browser logs a MIME type error for that stylesheet. patchedDependencies: a stale version key silently drops the patch, and --frozen-lockfile does not catch it
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A patch is keyed by exact version in `patchedDependencies`. When the package moves to a new version, the key matches nothing installed and Bun stops applying the patch — with no warning, no error, and a zero exit code.

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro && bun init -y
bun add is-odd --exact  # v3

bun patch is-odd
# edit node_modules/is-odd/index.js, e.g. make it always return true
bun patch --commit node_modules/is-odd

bun run -e "console.log(require('is-odd')(2))"   # true  <- patch applied

# now bump the package, as any routine dependency update would
bun add is-odd --exact  # now pin a different version

bun install --frozen-lockfile ; echo "exit=$?"
bun run -e "console.log(require('is-odd')(2))"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Some signal that a declared patch is no longer being applied. At minimum a warning on install; ideally an error under `--frozen-lockfile`.

### What do you see instead?

`bun install --frozen-lockfile` exits **0**. The package is reinstalled without the patch and the patched behaviour is gone. `package.json` still lists the patch, so nothing in the repo looks wrong.

`bun pm` offers nothing that surfaces it, and the patch docs do not mention version-key mismatch.

### Additional information

The failure is silent by construction, which is what makes it costly: a patch exists to change behaviour that tests do not cover — that is usually why it was a patch rather than a code change. So a full test suite, typecheck and build can all pass with the patch gone.

It is worse for transitive dependencies. A patched package can move because a *different* direct dependency bumped its range, so nothing in the changed dependency list names it and there is no prompt to re-key.

**Detection looks cheap.** Bun writes only the patches it actually applied into `bun.lock`, so a stale key survives in `package.json` and disappears from the lockfile. Comparing those two sets is sufficient — no resolution, no `node_modules` inspection, no store-layout knowledge. I wrote ~40 lines of CI doing exactly that and it catches both directions reliably.

Suggested shape, smallest first:

1. Warn on install for any `patchedDependencies` key that was not applied. Pure upside; nothing relies on the current silence.
2. Error under `--frozen-lockfile`. A patch that stopped applying *is* a manifest/lockfile divergence, which is what that flag exists to reject.

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

I found this in a native aarch64 macOS source build of Bun from commit
34cbb9a40b4bd1bd767d134a7065e66c2432a676.

The exact build can be reproduced with Nix:

```sh

__TEXT
__DATA_CONST
__DATA
__BUN
__DATA_DIRTY
__LINKEDIT

Inspect the segment order with:

```sh
otool -l "$BUN" |

PY

The official `bun-darwin-aarch64` binary from the same Bun commit compiles

The command should create a standalone executable.

The native source build fails with:

title: Bun 1.4.0: `bun build --compile` fails with EACCES on ftruncate when cwd is on WSL2 DrvFS (/mnt/c)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 x86_64  |  Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS  |  WSL 2.7.12.0  |  Windows 10.0.19045.6456

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Run the following from any writable directory under /mnt/c in WSL2:

  mkdir -p bun-ftruncate-repro
  cd bun-ftruncate-repro

  printf 'console.log("hello");\n' > index.ts

  bun build ./index.ts \
    --compile \
    --target=bun-linux-x64 \
    --outfile /tmp/bun-ftruncate-repro-output

  The output path is intentionally placed on native WSL ext4 and does not exist before the command.

  The build consistently fails:

    [24ms]  bundle  1 modules
  Error truncating ELF file: EACCES: Permission denied (ftruncate())
  failed to write compiled executable /tmp/bun-ftruncate-repro-output

  The error depends on the current working directory, not on the source or output path.

  The same entrypoint compiles successfully if Bun is launched with /tmp as its current working directory:

  REPRO_DIR="$PWD"

  cd /tmp

  bun build "$REPRO_DIR/index.ts" \
    --compile \
    --target=bun-linux-x64 \
    --outfile /tmp/bun-ftruncate-repro-output-ok

  Output:

    [20ms]  bundle  1 modules
   [241ms] compile  /tmp/bun-ftruncate-repro-output-ok

  The entrypoint is still located on /mnt/c; only the current working directory has changed.

### What is the expected behavior?

bun build --compile should create the standalone executable when the source directory and output path are writable.

  The temporary build file should be created with permissions that allow Bun to call ftruncate() on filesystems commonly used by WSL, containers, network mounts, and shared folders.

### What do you see instead?

Bundling completes successfully, but creation of the standalone ELF executable fails during ftruncate() of an internal temporary .bun-build file.

  Changing the permissions or name of the requested --outfile does not help because the failure occurs before Bun opens the requested output file.

### Additional information

A filtered strace shows the exact failure:

  openat(
    AT_FDCWD,
    ".61c15956fb097872-00000000.bun-build",
    O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_LARGEFILE|O_CLOEXEC,
    000
  ) = 7

  openat(AT_FDCWD, "/root/.bun/bin/bun", O_RDONLY|O_LARGEFILE|O_CLOEXEC) = 8
  close(8) = 0

  openat(AT_FDCWD, "/proc/self/exe", O_RDONLY|O_LARGEFILE) = 8

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.0 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create `repro.ts`:

```ts
const decoder = new TextDecoder("windows-1251");
console.log(
  decoder.decode(Uint8Array.from([0xcf, 0xf0, 0xe8, 0xe2, 0xe5, 0xf2])),
);
```

With `typescript` and `@types/bun@1.4.0` installed, compare runtime execution and type checking:

```console
$ bun repro.ts
Привет

$ bun x tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --strict --skipLibCheck --types bun --lib esnext repro.ts
repro.ts(1,33): error TS2345: Argument of type '"windows-1251"' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Encoding | undefined'.
```

The same narrow declaration is still present on Bun `main` as of commit `abe2ad4f0064334ebe83427ee689eb3e8d713a2e`:

```ts
type Encoding = "utf-8" | "windows-1252" | "utf-16";
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The global `TextDecoder` constructor type should accept every encoding label that Bun's implementation accepts at runtime, including `"windows-1251"` (and its supported aliases, if the type intentionally models labels rather than just canonical names).

### What do you see instead?

Bun 1.4 decodes `windows-1251` correctly at runtime, but `bun-types` rejects the same constructor call with TS2345. This forces TypeScript code to switch to `node:util.TextDecoder`, add a cast, or locally augment the declaration despite using a working Bun runtime API.

### Additional information

- #6084 tracked runtime support for `windows-1251` and is closed as completed.
- #18747 tracked the broader type signature while those encodings were not implemented and was closed as not planned. The premise has changed for `windows-1251`: runtime support now exists, but the published and current-source type has not caught up.
- Current declaration: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/abe2ad4f0064334ebe83427ee689eb3e8d713a2e/packages/bun-types/bun.d.ts

Implement Promise.allKeyed and Promise.allSettledKeyed (TC39 await dictionary proposal)
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun 1.4 does not implement Promise.allKeyed / Promise.allSettledKeyed (TC39 proposal-await-dictionary, reached Stage 3 July 2026). Users must manually await values and reconstruct the result object, which is verbose and error-prone. Firefox 155 is already shipping this; Bun lacks parity.

https://github.com/tc39/proposal-await-dictionary

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Add Promise.allKeyed(promises) and Promise.allSettledKeyed(promises) to the global Promise constructor, following the TC39 await dictionary spec and matching Firefox/core-js behavior. It should accept an object/dictionary of promises and resolve/reject with an object preserving the same keys. 

https://github.com/tc39/proposal-await-dictionary

### What alternatives have you considered?

Manual workaround: await Promise.all(Object.values(obj)) then remap keys by hand. 2) Use a polyfill (e.g. core-js/proposals/promise-all-keyed). 3) Wait for TC39 Stage 4 before implementing; but it is already Stage 3 and Firefox is shipping it.

title: Messages posted to a Worker before its top-level await completes are silently dropped (1.4.0 regression)
excerpt:
## What happens

`worker.postMessage()` calls made while a module Worker is still inside its
top-level-await startup phase are silently lost on Bun 1.4.0. The messages
are neither delivered once the worker installs `onmessage`, nor is any
error raised. On 1.4.0-canary.1 (and Node, and browsers) the same messages
are buffered and delivered as soon as the handler exists.

The drop happens the moment the worker's event loop turns before a message
handler is installed. If the worker installs `onmessage` synchronously
before its first `await`, nothing is lost.

## Minimal repro

`worker.ts`:

```ts
// Any async pre-handler phase: the event loop turns before onmessage exists.
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500))
self.onmessage = (e: MessageEvent) => {
  postMessage(e.data)
}
postMessage("ready")
```

`repro-min.ts`:

```ts
const worker = new Worker(new URL("./worker.ts", import.meta.url).href)
const got: any[] = []
worker.onmessage = (e) => got.push(e.data)
for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) worker.postMessage(i)
setTimeout(() => {
  console.log(`RESULT got=[${got.join(",")}] lost=${7 - got.filter((x) => typeof x === "number").length}`)
  process.exit(got.filter((x) => typeof x === "number").length === 7 ? 0 : 1)
}, 4000)
```

Run: `bun run repro-min.ts`

## Results

| bun | result |
|---|---|
| `1.4.0-canary.1+8f1a9540f` (2026-07-13) | `RESULT got=[ready,0,1,2,3,4,5,6] lost=0` (correct) |
| `1.4.0+34cbb9a40` (release, 2026-08-20) | `RESULT got=[ready] lost=7` |
| `1.4.1-canary.1+abe2ad4f0` (today) | `RESULT got=[ready] lost=7` |

So the regression landed between the July 13 canary and the 1.4.0 release,
and is still present at HEAD.

Control experiments:

- Worker that installs `onmessage` synchronously before its first `await`:
  `lost=0` on all versions. The loss requires the worker's loop to turn
  while no handler exists.
- Worker that busy-spins (blocking loop, no await) before installing the
  handler: `lost=0` on all versions. A blocked loop never turns, so the
  queue survives.
- The main-thread side does not matter: timers, microtasks, MessageChannel,
  and later `postMessage` calls to the same worker all work; only the
  messages that were queued during the pre-handler window vanish.

## Expected behavior

Per the HTML spec, a dedicated worker's implicit port message queue is
enabled only after the worker script's initial evaluation completes, and
for module workers that includes settling top-level awaits. Messages posted
before or during evaluation

title: bun install fails on Android SDCARD in Bun 1.4.0: symlinkat for .bin/ entries not covered by #36853
excerpt:
## bun install still fails on Android SDCARD in Bun 1.4.0 — symlinkat for .bin/ entries not covered by #36853

**Environment:** Android aarch64, Termux, Bun 1.4.0 (34cbb9a40)

**Error:**
```
error: Failed to link typescript: EACCES
```

Reproducible on SDCARD (`/storage/emulated/0`). Works correctly on internal storage (`~/`).

---

## Relationship to #36853

PR #36853 fixed `linkat` returning `EACCES` by falling back to `copyfile`. However, `bun install` still fails on SDCARD in Bun 1.4.0, even with `--backend=copyfile`.

Investigation with an LD_PRELOAD syscall tracer (tnode/thook) revealed the actual failing operation is `symlinkat`, not `linkat`. When installing packages on SDCARD, Bun calls `symlinkat` to create `.bin/` entries (e.g. `node_modules/.bin/tsc -> ../typescript/bin/tsc`). SDCARD (FUSE-backed) rejects `symlinkat` with `EACCES`/`EPERM`, and Bun does not have a fallback for this case.

The tracer log shows the exact call sequence:

```
[symlinkat] Attempting: '/sdcard/.../node_modules/.bin/tsc' -> '../typescript/bin/tsc'
[symlinkat] EACCES (errno 13) on storage path — no fallback, install aborts
error: Failed to link typescript: EACCES
```

When the tracer intercepts `symlinkat` and falls back to a file copy wrapper, `bun install` completes successfully:

```
[symlinkat] WARN: EACCES detected. Engaging fake symlink wrapper.
[symlinkat] SUCCESS: Fake symlink wrapper created for binary.
+ typescript@5.9.3
5 packages installed
```

---

## Expected Fix

In the `.bin/` entry creation path, when `symlinkat` fails with `EACCES` or `EPERM`, fall back to copying the target file directly — consistent with the approach taken for `linkat` in #36853.

Alternatively, treat `EACCES`/`EPERM` from `symlinkat` the same as `EXDEV`, so the existing fallback paths are reused.

title: fetch always dials AAAA first; --dns-result-order, setDefaultResultOrder and node:https family are all ignored
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (linux x64)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8 x86_64 (Ubuntu-based, systemd-resolved at 127.0.0.53)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On a host with **no usable public IPv6 route** (only a global-scope Tailscale ULA `fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48`; `curl -6` fails instantly with exit 7), fetch a dual-stack hostname that publishes AAAA records:

```sh
cat > once.ts <<'T'
const r = await fetch("https://api.example-dualstack.test/health", { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) });
console.log(r.status);
T
for i in $(seq 1 50); do bun run once.ts; done
```

~2% of fresh processes fail with `TimeoutError: The operation timed out`. In-process loops are always clean (warm DNS + socket reuse), which makes this hard to catch in simple repros.

**strace ground truth** (`strace -f -e trace=connect`): Bun dials `AF_INET6` **first on every run**, regardless of resolver ordering:

```
connect(14, {sa_family=AF_INET6, sin6_port=htons(443), sin6_addr="2606:4700:3037::6815:19ae"}, ...) = -1 ENETUNREACH
connect(14, {sa_family=AF_INET, sin_port=htons(443), sin_addr="104.21.25.174"}, ...) = 0
```

When the kernel rejects v6 immediately (`ENETUNREACH`), the v4 fallback succeeds and the request is fine. But if any covering route exists that accepts-then-blackholes v6 packets (e.g. transient tunnel/route states), the AAAA-first attempt hangs and the whole request times out — that is the production failure mode we hit.

### What is the expected behavior?

One or more of:

1. Bun's fetch should implement happy-eyeballs-style racing/fallback so a stalled first-family attempt cannot kill the request while the other family connects in <500ms.
2. The documented DNS-ordering controls should affect fetch's dial order. All three of these are currently ignored by `fetch` on this platform/version:
   - CLI flag: `bun --dns-result-order=ipv4first` / `ipv6first` — forcing `ipv6first` still yields 12/12 successful v4 connections (proving the flag never reaches fetch)
   - Programmatic: `import { setDefaultResultOrder } from "node:dns"` (honored by `node:dns.lookup`, not by fetch)
   - `node:https.request({ family: 6 })` under Bun connects successfully over IPv4 anyway (`family` option appears to be dropped)
3. Alternatively, honoring RFC 6724/getaddrinfo sorting (which correctly deprioritizes the ULA here — libc returns A-first in 40/40 samples) would avoid the AAAA attempts entirely.

title: Add a bun --hot flag that runs the React Fast Refresh transform
excerpt:
**Use case**

Native desktop apps with React HMR. Not a browser. Not `Bun.serve`.

[GPUIX](https://github.com/remorses/gpuix) renders React through Zed's GPUI (Metal / DirectX / Vulkan). The window, GPU device, and `.node` addon stay loaded. `bun --hot app.tsx` remounts the React tree on that same window. Fast Refresh would keep `useState` across saves.

```bash
bun --hot --react-fast-refresh examples/chat.tsx
```

**Ask**

Do **not** turn this on for every `bun --hot`. Most `--hot` scripts are not React. Add an opt-in flag:

```bash
bun --hot --react-fast-refresh app.tsx
```

Same `$RefreshReg$` / `$RefreshSig$` contract as `bun build --react-fast-refresh`. The host can install `react-refresh/runtime` before the first render.

**Today**

`bun build --react-fast-refresh` injects those globals. `bun --hot file.tsx` does not. Checked on Bun 1.4.0: the running module has no `$RefreshReg$`, and `import.meta.hot` is `undefined`.

The only way to get the transform is `Bun.build({ reactFastRefresh: true })`. Calling `Bun.build()` from a `bun --hot` entry has also been reported to break `--hot` itself (#30436).

Related: `reactFastRefresh` on `Bun.build` (#25716), `Bun.Transpiler` still does not expose it (#32919 / #30295).

title: Add --macos-icon and --linux-icon to bun build --compile
excerpt:
`--windows-icon` lets a compiled `.exe` show a custom icon. There is no equivalent for macOS or Linux, so a GUI app built with `--compile` always looks like a generic binary in Finder, Dock, and the desktop launcher.

Windows can stamp an `.ico` into one PE file. macOS and Linux cannot do that for a Dock / launcher icon. A raw Mach-O or ELF has no place for one. So these flags should keep the same *shape* as the Windows API, but they have to change the *artifact*:

- **Windows** (already exists): `myapp.exe` with the icon inside
- **macOS**: `MyApp.app/` with `Contents/MacOS/myapp`, `Contents/Resources/AppIcon.icns`, and `Info.plist`
- **Linux**: `myapp` plus `myapp.desktop` plus `myapp.png` beside it

CLI would look like the existing Windows flags:

```bash
bun build --compile --macos-icon=icon.png --macos-identifier=com.example.myapp \
  ./app.ts --outfile "My App"

bun build --compile --linux-icon=icon.png --linux-name="My App" \
  ./app.ts --outfile myapp
```

JS API next to `compile.windows`:

```ts
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./app.ts"],
  compile: {
    outfile: "./My App",
    macos: {
      icon: "./icon.png",
      identifier: "com.example.myapp",
      name: "My App",
    },
    linux: {
      icon: "./icon.png",
      name: "My App",
    },
    windows: {
      icon: "./icon.ico",
      hideConsole: true,
      title: "My App",
    },
  },
});
```

Suggested rules:

- Accept **PNG** (and `.icns` / `.ico` if that is what you pass). Convert inside bun so the user does not need `iconutil` or ImageMagick.
- If `--macos-icon` is set, write an `.app`. If `--outfile` has no `.app` suffix, append it.
- If `--linux-icon` is set, write the binary plus a [freedesktop `.desktop`](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/) and the PNG next to it.
- If no macos / linux icon block is set, keep today's single-file binary. CLI tools stay one file.
- These should work when **cross-compiling**. `--windows-icon` currently errors off Windows. Please do not copy that.

Not asking for AppImage, DMG, or notarization here. Just the icon-shaped package each OS actually shows in the UI.

Related: #10823 #13686 (Windows icon, done). No existing issue covers macOS / Linux.

## Bug: SIGSEGV (null deref) in `tokio-rt-worker` thread when a Rust napi addon starts a Tokio runtime — Android build only

### Environment
- Bun: `1.4.0+34cbb9a40` — official `bun-linux-aarch64-android.zip` build (also reproduced with the tur-packages Android build, same crash)
- OS: Android 14 (Termux), aarch64, Kernel 5.15.153, bionic libc
- Reproduced on: Xiaomi 13

### Summary
Loading a Rust napi addon that contains a Tokio async runtime (e.g. `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`'s `pi_natives.linux-arm64.node`, v18.0.3) and calling a function that starts the Tokio runtime (`executeShell`) reliably crashes Bun with `Segmentation fault at address 0x0`. The crash happens on a `tokio-rt-worker` thread **inside bionic libc code**, not in the addon itself. The exact same addon + Bun 1.4.0 (Linux build, glibc) in a Debian chroot does **not** crash — this is specific to the Android build.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install any Rust napi addon that embeds a Tokio runtime (I used `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent` v18.0.3 — its `pi_natives.linux-arm64.node`).
2. Run with bun:

```js
// test.js
const n = require('/path/to/pi_natives.linux-arm64.node');
console.log('calling executeShell...');
try {
  const r = n.executeShell({ command: 'echo hi' });
  console.log('executeShell returned:', JSON.stringify(r));
} catch (e) {
  console.log('executeShell error:', e.message);
}
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5000));
console.log('still alive after 5s');
```

3. `bun run test.js` — crashes within ~1s, always reproducible.

### Actual behavior
```
panic: Segmentation fault at address 0x0
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.
bun.report: https://bun.report/1.4.0/Lr134cbb9aggEggggCuiloGurkp6B2kE+vv8wI+zj8wImhl8wIm5n8wIusph+G2i42mIu2uglImo9m6H2y+15Huw1y6Huqp64H2w5ovIu0xovIuhjpvImz3kvI2k7ovIA2AA
```

### gdb analysis
```
Thread 9 "tokio-rt-worker" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
x0 = 0x0                          ← null deref
crash instruction: ldp x2, x3, [x0]
```

Crash address `0x7fec8f59d0` falls **inside the bionic libc mapping** (`/apex/com.android.runtime/lib64/bionic/libc.so`, r-xp segment `0x7fec89a000-0x7fec974000`), not in the addon or bun. All 6-7 `tokio-rt-worker` threads sit in the same libc code region (`0x7fec8f8090`).

### Control experiment (same kernel, same addon, different bun build)
| Bun | libc | executeShell | Result |
|-----|------|--------------|--------|
| bun 1.4.0 Android (`bun-linux-aarch64-android.zip`) | bionic

title: install.globalStore: bun postinstall moves @oven platform binary out of the shared store
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0 (`34cbb9a40`)

### What platform is your computer?

Reproduced with the official `oven/bun:1.4.0` Linux x64 image. The shared-store mutation also reproduces on macOS ARM64.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a project that depends on the npm `bun` wrapper, trusts its postinstall, and enables the global virtual store:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "bun": "1.4.0"
  },
  "name": "global-store-repro",
  "private": true,
  "trustedDependencies": ["bun"]
}
```

```toml
[install]
globalStore = true
linker = "isolated"
```

Put those files in `project/`, create an empty `cache/` sibling, then run the project and cache as separate mounts:

```sh
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 \
  -e BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/cache \
  -v "$PWD/project:/work" \
  -v "$PWD/cache:/cache" \
  -w /work \
  oven/bun:1.4.0 \
  bun install
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun install` succeeds. A trusted package's lifecycle script should not move files out of an immutable shared global-store entry.

### What do you see instead?

The `bun` wrapper's postinstall resolves its executable through the global-store link for `@oven/bun-linux-x64` and calls `renameSync()` to move it into the project-local trusted `bun` package. Because the store and project are separate mounts, that move fails and the install exits 1:

```text
bun install v1.4.0 (34cbb9a40)

error: Your package manager doesn't seem to support bun. To use bun, install using the following command: curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash
      at optimizeBun (/work/node_modules/.bun/bun@1.4.0/node_modules/bun/install.js:526:13)

error: postinstall script from "bun" exited with 1
```

When the cache and project are on the same filesystem, the rename succeeds but removes `bin/bun` from the shared `@oven/bun-*` store entry. A fresh project sharing that cache has to re-materialize the platform package, after which the wrapper moves the executable out again. This mutates the supposedly shared entry and defeats warm reuse.

Adding the selected platform package to `trustedDependencies` keeps it project-local and makes the same Docker reproduction pass:

```json
"trustedDependencies": ["bun", "@oven/bun-linux-x64"]
```

### Additional information

The npm wrapper's move behavior also causes a related pnpm failure in #25031, but that issue predates Bun's global virtual store and does not cover `install.globalStore`.

title: install.globalStore: @hookform/resolvers cannot resolve an explicitly installed Zod adapter dependency
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0 (`34cbb9a40`)

### What platform is your computer?

macOS ARM64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a minimal workspace with `globalStore` enabled:

```json
// package.json
{
  "name": "bun-global-store-hookform-repro",
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["app"]
}
```

```toml
# bunfig.toml
[install]
globalStore = true
linker = "isolated"
```

```json
// app/package.json
{
  "name": "app",
  "private": true,
  "dependencies": {
    "@hookform/resolvers": "5.2.2",
    "react": "19.2.5",
    "react-hook-form": "7.82.0",
    "zod": "4.3.6"
  }
}
```

```ts
// app/index.ts
import { zodResolver } from "@hookform/resolvers/zod";
import { z } from "zod";

const resolve = zodResolver(z.object({ name: z.string() }));
console.log(typeof resolve);
```

Then run:

```sh
bun install
bun run app/index.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The script prints `function`. The consuming workspace explicitly installs `zod`, which is the validator selected through the `@hookform/resolvers/zod` adapter.

This package intentionally ships adapters for many validators rather than declaring every validator as a dependency. That package pattern works when the virtual store is project-local.

### What do you see instead?

The script fails at runtime:

```text
error: Cannot find module 'zod/v4/core' from '<cache>/links/@hookform+resolvers@5.2.2+.../node_modules/@hookform/resolvers/zod/dist/zod.mjs'
```

The `@hookform/resolvers` package is realpathed into the global link store. Its lookup for the consumer-provided `zod` package never reaches the workspace's project-local virtual-store fallback, even though `zod` is explicitly declared in `app/package.json`.

### What platform is your computer?

Two modules import each other. The second module reads the import at the top level, while the first module still evaluates.   return "entry";
}

console.log(describe());

**b.js**

```js

  return "b sees " + name();

bun-types lag runtime: Bun.dns.resolve* family not declared (1.4.0)
excerpt:
### Runtime vs types mismatch

On Bun 1.4.0 the runtime exposes the full `Bun.dns` resolver family, but
`bun-types` (1.4.0) does not declare them:

```ts
// runtime keys (probed on 1.4.0):
//   lookup, resolve, resolveSrv, resolveTxt, resolveSoa, resolveNaptr,
//   resolveMx, resolveCaa, resolveNs, resolvePtr, resolveCname, resolveAny,
//   getServers, setServers, reverse, lookupService, prefetch, getCacheStats,
//   ADDRCONFIG, ALL, V4MAPPED

await Bun.dns.resolveCname("www.github.com");
// TS2339: Property 'resolveCname' does not exist on type 'typeof dns'.
```

Only `lookup`, `prefetch`, `getCacheStats` are usable from `bun-types` 1.4.0
without a cast.

### Repro

```ts
await Bun.dns.resolveNs("github.com");   // TS2339
await Bun.dns.resolveTxt("github.com");  // TS2339
await Bun.dns.resolveMx("github.com");   // TS2339
```

### Expected

Declare the `resolve*` family (plus `reverse`, `getServers`/`setServers`,
`lookupService`) in `bun-types` with the runtime shapes (probed):

- `resolveCname` / `resolveNs` / `resolvePtr` -> `Promise<string[]>`
- `resolveTxt` -> `Promise<string[][]>` (each record is a chunk array)
- `resolveMx` -> `Promise<Array<{ priority: number; exchange: string }>>`
- `resolveSrv` / `resolveSoa` / `resolveNaptr` / `resolveCaa` / `resolveAny`
  -> structured records (observed at runtime)

Same class as the `test options timeout` typing lag (which the Bun docs work
around with `@ts-expect-error`).

### Version

- bun: 1.4.0 (34cbb9a40)
- bun-types: ^1.4.0

title: node:worker_threads: new Worker() reads the mutable global MessagePort, so replacing it (happy-dom) throws `port.on is not a function` on 1.4.0
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0 (34cbb9a40)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin arm64 (macOS, Apple Silicon)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`new Worker()` from `node:worker_threads` reads `MessagePort` from the **mutable global** instead of the intrinsic, so any code that replaces `globalThis.MessagePort` before constructing a Worker makes construction throw from Bun's own internals.

No dependencies needed:

```ts
// repro.ts
class FakePort extends EventTarget {} // a DOM-shaped MessagePort: no .on()
globalThis.MessagePort = FakePort as any;

const { Worker } = await import("node:worker_threads");
const w = new Worker("", { eval: true });
await w.terminate();
console.log("ok");
```

```sh
bun repro.ts
```

- **1.3.14**: prints `ok`
- **1.4.0**: throws

The same thing happens with a real-world replacement, which is how we hit it. `@happy-dom/global-registrator` replaces the DOM globals, and every Bun test suite that registers happy-dom in a preload now fails the moment anything constructs a Worker:

```sh
mkdir bun-worker-messageport && cd bun-worker-messageport
bun add @happy-dom/global-registrator@20.11.2

cat > preload.ts <<'TS'
import { GlobalRegistrator } from "@happy-dom/global-registrator";
GlobalRegistrator.register();
TS

cat > worker.test.ts <<'TS'
import { test } from "bun:test";
import { Worker } from "node:worker_threads";

test("new Worker", async () => {
  const w = new Worker("", { eval: true });
  await w.terminate();
});
TS

bun test --preload ./preload.ts ./worker.test.ts
```

- **1.3.14**: 1 pass
- **1.4.0**: 1 fail

It is not specific to the test runner (the first repro is a plain `bun run`), and it is not `--isolate` (fails identically with `--no-isolate`).

### What is the expected behavior?

Worker construction uses the intrinsic `MessagePort`, so it is unaffected by user code replacing the global, and keeps working as it did on 1.3.14.

### What do you see instead?

```
TypeError: port.on is not a function. (In 'port.on("message", handleMessageFromThread)', 'port.on' is undefined)
      at handleMessageFromThread (internal:worker/messaging:15:48)
      at registerMainThreadPort (internal:worker/messaging:83:28)

`internal:worker/messaging` treats the port as a Node-style `EventEmitter` and calls `port.on(...)`, but the object it got is the replaced global's instance, which only has `addEventListener`.

title: auto-install: prebuilt native addons can't reach their sibling shared library in the global cache
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-137-generic x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Running a script from a directory with no `node_modules` forces bun to auto-install into its global cache, where packages get flat, version-suffixed directory names (e.g. `@img/sharp-linux-x64@0.35.3@@@1`). 

Prebuilt native addons (e.g. `sharp`) that ship a sibling shared library locate it with `$ORIGIN`-relative RPATH entries that assume a `node_modules`-shaped layout, so every candidate misses and `dlopen` fails (even though the library is literally one directory away in the same cache folder)

`test.js` (make sure to run this in a folder with NO `node_modules` in order to get bun to auto-install)

```javascript
console.log("sharp resolved from:", require.resolve("sharp"));
const sharp = require("sharp");
console.log("emscripten:", sharp.versions.emscripten ?? "none (native binding)");
try { require("@img/sharp-linux-x64/sharp.node"); console.log("native binding: OK"); }
catch (e) { console.log("native binding FAILED:", e.message); }
```

```bash
BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/repro-cache bun test.js
```

(using `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` to point at a throwaway global cache folder just for simplicity's sake)

### What is the expected behavior?

The native binding loads as it would from a real `node_modules`:

```
sharp resolved from: /tmp/repro-cache/sharp@0.35.3@@@1/dist/index.cjs
emscripten: none (native binding)
native binding: OK
```

### What do you see instead?

```
sharp resolved from: /tmp/repro-cache/sharp@0.35.3@@@1/dist/index.cjs
emscripten: 6.0.1                     <-- silently fell back to wasm
native binding FAILED: libvips-cpp.so.8.18.3: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

No error is actually visible to users. In this particular instance, `sharp` catches the `dlopen` fail and substitutes its wasm binding. Coincidentally, that wasm binding then deadlocks under bun on any real work, due to a separate worker_threads globals bug. I've researched and confirmed (built locally and tested) that PR #35655 fixes that.

Every RPATH candidate misses, while the library sits one directory over:

title: Bun.write(path, response) never resolves when the fetch Response is GC'd mid-download; fetch finalizer ignores the pending write waiter
excerpt:
## TL;DR for maintainers

The `Locked`-body arm of `Bun.write(dest, response)` registers `locked.on_receive_value = WriteFileWaitFromLockedValueTask::then_wrap` but never sets `locked.promise` and creates no GC root for the Response ([Blob.rs:5149-5174](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/runtime/webcore/Blob.rs#L5149-L5174), key lines 5164-5166). `FetchTasklet::on_response_finalize` classifies the body from `locked.promise` and `response_stream_source` only ([FetchTasklet.rs:2705-2741](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/runtime/webcore/fetch/FetchTasklet.rs#L2705-L2741)), so a write-locked body falls into "Scenario 3" and `ignore_remaining_response_body()` ([FetchTasklet.rs:1913-1946](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/runtime/webcore/fetch/FetchTasklet.rs#L1913-L1946)).

Once receive mode is `Ignore` and the native response is unref'd, the terminal `BodyValue::resolve` ([FetchTasklet.rs:890-925](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/runtime/webcore/fetch/FetchTasklet.rs#L890-L925) → [Body.rs:1093-1096](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/runtime/webcore/Body.rs#L1093-L1096)) never runs, `on_receive_value` never fires, and the `Bun.write` promise pends forever. The task box, its `JSPromiseStrong`, and the destination blob leak. An `AbortSignal` on the fetch does not rescue it (verified empirically below).

JSC's liveness-based GC collects `response` as soon as its last syntactic use is behind it. In the documented pattern

```ts
const response = await fetch(url);
await Bun.write(path, response); // last use of `response`
```

that point is mid-download, so any collection during the body transfer triggers the hang.

`response.arrayBuffer()` / `.text()` / `.blob()` are immune because `set_promise` stores **and `protect()`s** the promise ([Body.rs:420-432](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/runtime/webcore/Body.rs#L420-L432)) — which is exactly what the finalizer checks. Fix options:

1. `on_response_finalize`: treat `locked.on_receive_value.is_some()` as "keep loading" (same as Scenario 2b), or
2. the `Bun.write` locked arm roots the Response/promise the way `set_promise` does.

Reproduced with forced GC on `1.3.14+0d9b296af`, `1.4.0+34cbb9a40`, and `1.4.1-canary.1+9dd73746c`, so this is latent in all current lines — but 1.4.0's GC timing makes it fire *naturally and frequently* (matrix below). This is not the ReadableStream-pump case of #13237 / #15796: the repro use

title: Bun 1.4 REPL hangs while completing properties of a large Buffer
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

```text
1.4.0+34cbb9a40
```

This works correctly in `1.3.14+0d9b296af`.

### What platform is your computer?

```text
Linux 7.0.0-108029-tuxedo x86_64 x86_64
```

I can also reproduce it in a Windows 11 VM.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Warning: this allocates a 1 GiB Buffer and may require terminating the REPL from another process.

Start the REPL:

```console
bun repl
```

Enter:

```js
globalThis.data = Buffer.allocUnsafe(1 << 30);
```

Then type the following without pressing Enter or Tab:

```js
data.
```

Typing the period triggers the problem.

### What is the expected behavior?

The REPL should remain responsive and display the period. Property completion should avoid enumerating every byte index of a Buffer.

Bun 1.3.14 remains responsive with the same input.

### What do you see instead?

The period is not displayed and the REPL hangs. On Linux it also stops responding to Ctrl+C. The process remains active; I observed approximately 1.33 GiB RSS before terminating it with SIGTERM.

The hang also occurs in a Windows 11 VM.

### Additional information

This appears to be caused by inline property completion in the new REPL.

The character handler calls `update_suggestion()` before redrawing the input, which explains why the period is not displayed:

https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/runtime/cli/repl.rs#L2370-L2374

Completion then calls `getPropertyNames()` on the target before filtering the results:

https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.0/src/jsc/bindings/bindings.cpp#L6994-L7015

Buffer indices are exposed as own property names, so with an empty prefix this attempts to collect names for all `1 << 30` indices. Numeric names are rejected by the Rust completion code later, after the names have already been collected.

In 1.3.14, typing a character only inserted it and redrew the line; completion was not run after every keystroke:

https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.3.14/src/cli/repl.zig#L1787-L1790

Disclosure: this report was drafted with LLM assistance. The reproduction was observed directly, and the source references were checked against the Bun v1.4.0 tag.

1.4.0

### What platform is your computer?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Any JPEG whose colorspace is CMYK fails to decode. Every terminal method fails the same way. The constructor is lazy and does not throw.

await new Bun.Image(bytes).webp({ quality: 82 }).bytes();

```sh
sips -s format jpeg input.png --out rgb.jpg
sips --matchTo '/System/Library/ColorSync/Profiles/Generic CMYK Profile.icc' rgb.jpg --out cmyk-fixture.jpg

| input | `png()` | `webp(q82)` | `resize(100).png()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rgb-control.jpg` (same pixels, RGB) | OK | OK | OK |
| `cmyk-fixture.jpg` (plain CMYK, no APP14) | `Image: decode failed` | `Image: decode failed` | `Image: decode failed` |

The JPEG decodes and converts to RGB, matching every browser, macOS ImageIO (`sips`), Skia/CanvasKit, Sharp/libvips, and ImageMagick, all of which decode both fixtures fine. (Verified the exact same fixture bytes decode in CanvasKit.)

`Error: Image: decode failed` from the first terminal method, for every pipeline (`png()`, `webp()`, `avif()`, with or without `resize()`).

title: Bun.Terminal (PTY): exit lifecycle callback never fires spontaneously after a voluntary child exit on Linux, though it does on macOS; host-initiated close() triggers it promptly on both
excerpt:
### Proposed issue title

`Bun.Terminal (PTY): exit lifecycle callback never fires spontaneously after a voluntary child exit on Linux, though it does on macOS; host-initiated close() triggers it promptly on both`

### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (`Bun.version`, verified via `bun --version` on both hosts)

### What platform is your computer?

- macOS 26.6.2 arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0)
- Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 native container, kernel 6.8.0-117-generic

(The same behavioral split was independently observed with Bun 1.3.14 on
GitHub Actions `ubuntu-24.04` x86_64.)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Standalone script below; run `bun bun-terminal-exit-repro.mjs --arm interleaved --iterations 8`.

Each iteration creates a fresh `Bun.Terminal` and spawns
`/bin/sh -c 'echo MARK_<n>; exit 7'` into it **with `detached: true`** (setsid —
the child becomes a session leader, which is how PTY hosts normally spawn
shells). It then:

- accumulates output through the `data` callback across chunks (split-safe,
  streaming decode) and classifies each byte-delivery phase relative to child
  exit and terminal closure;
- waits for `Subprocess.exited`, asserting the child's actual exit code is 7;
- **voluntary mode:** waits up to 3000 ms for the Terminal `exit` lifecycle
  callback WITHOUT closing the terminal;
- **control mode:** calls `terminal.close()` immediately after `child.exited`
  (timestamp captured before the call) and classifies whether the callback was
  already delivered pre-close or only fired after close.

All callback timestamps are recorded exactly (no polling proxies); latencies
are computed from those timestamps; every result field is snapshotted only
after the complete observation window.

### What is the expected behavior?

When a session-leader child exits voluntarily, its controlling terminal is torn
down, so the PTY master reaches EOF/EIO. The documented `exit` callback
("invoked when the PTY stream closes (EOF or read error)") should fire within
ordinary scheduling latency — as it does on macOS — so consumers can correlate
child death with terminal closure without an arbitrary timeout.

### What do you see instead?

**Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, arm64, Bun 1.3.14):** across 400 iterations (200
voluntary-mode + 200 control-mode) the `exit` callback NEVER fired
spontaneously — 0/400 before any close. Every single callback arrived only
after the host called `terminal.close()` (median 58 µs voluntary / 5 µs
control after the pre-close timestamp). Waiting w

A long-lived Windows x64 standalone executable (opencode's TUI client, `opencode2.exe`, built with `bun build --compile` on Bun 1.4.0) segfaults recurrently while executing JIT-compiled JS. We have 5 crash instances across 2 machines with an identical signature.

Crash report URL from the most recent instance: https://bun.report/1.4.0/wa134cbb9amQuhogC______os1+5C________A2gVx///nzB

Decoded (instance 1, 2026-08-24, after ~4.7 h uptime):

```text
Bun v1.4.0 (34cbb9a) on windows x86_64 [StandaloneExecutable]

Segmentation fault at address 0x150CCC00008

- 6 unknown/js code
- vmEntryToJavaScript

Features: spawn, standalone_executable, workers_spawned, Bun.stderr(2), Bun.stdin(2), Bun.stdout(2), abort_signal(2), fetch(640), jsc
Builtins: "bun:ffi" "bun:main" "bun:sqlite" "node:assert" "node:buffer" "node:child_process" "node:console" "node:crypto" "node:events" "node:fs" "node:fs/promises" "node:http" "node:inspector" "node:module" "node:net" "node:os" "node:path" "node:perf_hooks" "node:process" "node:readline" "node:stream" "node:stream/promises" "node:string_decoder" "node:timers/promises" "node:tty" "node:url" "node:util" "node:worker_threads" "node:zlib" "ws"
Elapsed: 16856905ms | User: 224593ms | Sys: 81390ms
RSS: 0.28GB | Peak: 0.44GB | Commit: 0.71GB | Faults: 3463700
CPU: sse42 avx avx2
OS: Windows 10.0.26200
```

Decoded (instance 2, 2026-08-23, different machine, 4 crashes in one session at 10:01:33Z, 10:02:04Z, 10:03:16Z, 10:30:31Z — so uptime is not a prerequisite):

```text
Bun v1.4.0 (34cbb9a) on windows x86_64 [StandaloneExecutable]

Segmentation fault at address 0x1E014680008

- 6 unknown/js code
- vmEntryToJavaScript

Features: standalone_executable, Bun.stderr, Bun.stdin, Bun.stdout, fetch, jsc
```

Second instance environment: Windows 11 x64 build 10.0.26200.9168, Windows Terminal, PowerShell 7.6.5. Tracked downstream in anomalyco/opencode#43591.

## Signature analysis

bun add follows a deprecated latest dist-tag that npm skips, installing a bin-less placeholder
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.1

### What platform is your computer?

macOS arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0). Also reproduces on Fedora Linux x86_64.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

When a package's `latest` dist-tag points at a **deprecated** version, `bun add <pkg>` still installs that version, while `npm i <pkg>` skips it. The published package `omo-ai` is a live example — `latest` is a 415-byte bootstrap placeholder, the real distribution ships under the `beta` tag, and the placeholder is deprecated:

```console
$ npm view omo-ai dist-tags
{ latest: '0.0.0-beta.0', beta: '5.0.0-0.beta.18' }

$ npm view omo-ai@0.0.0-beta.0 deprecated
Bootstrap placeholder so trusted publishing (OIDC) could be configured.
The omo-ai product ships ONLY on the beta channel: npm install -g omo-ai@beta
```

```console
$ mkdir /tmp/t && cd /tmp/t && echo '{"name":"t","version":"1.0.0"}' > package.json

$ npm i omo-ai
npm error code ETARGET
npm error notarget No matching version found for omo-ai@*.

$ bun add omo-ai
installed omo-ai@0.0.0-beta.0
1 package installed [206.00ms]
```

npm's `omo-ai@*` in the error is the *fallback* after it skipped the deprecated `latest`. The remaining published versions are all prereleases (`5.0.0-0.beta.x`), so `*` matches nothing and npm fails loudly. Bun never takes that path: it follows `latest` even when that version is deprecated.

The installed placeholder has no `bin` and no dependencies:

```console
$ npm view omo-ai@0.0.0-beta.0 bin dependencies dist.unpackedSize description
bin: undefined
dependencies: undefined
415
'Bootstrap placeholder for the omo-ai package. Real distribution ships via trusted publishing from github.com/...'
```

**Correction (2026-08-24):** the original report attributed npm's refusal to the placeholder being a prerelease. That was wrong. A Bun maintainer identified the actual fork — deprecated `latest` — and I confirmed it. The repro is unchanged.

### What is the expected behavior?

Match npm on the deprecated-`latest` case: skip that version rather than installing it.

Independently of how resolution is decided, print the deprecation notice. npm surfaces `npm WARN deprecated …` (and this placeholder's notice names the correct install command). Bun currently prints nothing:

```console
$ bun add omo-ai 2>&1 | grep -i 'deprecat\|warn'
(no output)
```

### What do you see instead?

`bun add` reports success and installs the deprecated placeholder. With `-g` the consequence is worse than a version mismatch

title: NODE_OPTIONS is ignored, breaking `react-router dev` on React Router 8.3+ under the Bun runtime
excerpt:
## What happens

Bun 1.4.0 does not apply flags from `NODE_OPTIONS`. One consequence is that `react-router dev` now crashes outright on the Bun runtime, starting with React Router 8.3.0.

React Router 8.3.0 ([#15291](https://github.com/remix-run/react-router/pull/15291)) made its dev command relaunch itself with `--conditions=development` when that condition isn't already active. It passes the flag through `NODE_OPTIONS` and marks the child with `REACT_ROUTER_DEV_RESTARTED=true`. Under Bun the child doesn't get the condition, so it tries to restart a second time and hits its own guard:

```
[restart] Relaunching with NODE_OPTIONS: --conditions=development
error: restartWithMergedOptions() was called, but the process has already been restarted. This is likely a bug in @react-router/dev.
```

Reproduce with the stock template:

```sh
bunx create-react-router@latest rr-bun-repro --yes --no-git-init
cd rr-bun-repro
bun --bun react-router dev
```

`bun run dev` is fine because the bin shim starts Node. It only breaks when the CLI itself runs on Bun, which is what `--bun` is for. Pinning React Router to 8.2.0 also works, so it's specific to the 8.3.0 change.

## Minimal repro, no framework

```sh
mkdir cond && cd cond
echo '{"name":"cond","type":"module","imports":{"#c":{"development":"./true.mjs","default":"./false.mjs"}}}' > package.json
echo 'export default true'  > true.mjs
echo 'export default false' > false.mjs
echo 'import v from "#c"; console.log(v)' > probe.mjs
```

| command | result | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_OPTIONS=--conditions=development node probe.mjs` | `true` | `true` |
| `NODE_OPTIONS=--conditions=development bun --bun probe.mjs` | `false` | `true` |
| `bun --bun --conditions=development probe.mjs` | `true` | `true` |

So Bun implements `--conditions`, it just doesn't pick it up from the environment.

## It's the whole variable, not just `--conditions`

Checked on 1.4.0:

```console
$ NODE_OPTIONS=--import=file:///abs/pre.mjs bun --bun probe.mjs     # pre.mjs never runs (Node runs it)
$ NODE_OPTIONS=--title=hello bun --bun -e 'console.log(process.title)'   # unchanged
$ NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first bun --bun -e 'import dns from "node:dns"; console.log(dns.getDefaultResultOrder())'
verbatim
$ NODE_OPTIONS=--not-a-real-flag bun --bun probe.mjs                # runs; Node exits with an error here
```

The last one is worth noting on its own: because the variable is ignored wholesale rather than validated, nothing points
