title: bundler: split require() of a re-wrapped lifted module returns the chunk namespace (regression on main)
excerpt:
### What is the problem?

On main, a split `require()` can return the module namespace of its chunk, `{ default: module.exports }`, and not `module.exports`. The target is a file whose `module.exports = require()` #41188 lifts, and that the linker then wraps again. Bun 1.4.1-canary.1 (a6c4cc276) returns `module.exports`, so no release has this bug.

The trigger needs all of these:

- `--splitting` and `--target=bun` (split `require()` is on by default for bun).
- A `require()` that stays a call. A `require()` into the unwrap list (react, react-dom, ...) stays a call only inside `try`.
- A target that the linker wraps again, because the target of its lifted `module.exports = require()` is CommonJS.

Repro in an empty directory:

```sh
mkdir -p node_modules/react-dom
printf "console.log('side effect');\nmodule.exports = require('./impl');\n" > node_modules/react-dom/index.js
printf 'module.exports = function render() { return "rendered"; };\nmodule.exports.version = "19.0.0";\n' > node_modules/react-dom/impl.js
printf 'let m;\ntry {\n  m = require("react-dom");\n} catch {}\nconsole.log(m.version);\n' > entry.js
bun build ./entry.js --splitting --target=bun --outdir=out && bun out/entry.js
```

Bun 1.4.1-canary.1 prints `side effect` and `19.0.0`. Main (e8c8d8150a) prints `side effect` and `undefined`. The entry chunk has `m = import.meta.require("./index-<hash>.js")`. That chunk ends with `export default require_react_dom();`.

With npm react-dom 18.3.1, `NODE_ENV=development bun build --splitting --minify --target=bun` of `try { rd = require("react-dom") } catch {}` gives `rd.createPortal === undefined` on main. Production builds do not show it, because there the target of `react-dom/index.js` is lifted and the file is not wrapped again.

### Cause

- `ReachableFileVisitor` splits a `require()` when its target is `ExportsKind::Esm` at parse time (`src/bundler/bundle_v2.rs:1998`).
- Since #41188, the parser turns `module.exports = require("./impl")` after a side effect into `export * from "./impl"`. The file is ESM at parse time, so the `require()` splits.
- The linker then wraps the file again, because `./impl` is CommonJS (`src/bundler/linker_context/scanImportsAndExports.rs:422`). Its chunk is `export default require_x()`.
- `import.meta.require()` of an ES module returns its namespace.

### Possible fixes

- Do not split a `require()` of a lifted file with an export star. That is the behavior before #41188.
- Or read `.default` of a split `require()` who

title: Bun.SQL: `sql.array()` binds `json[]`, so a `text[]` column silently stores JSON-quoted elements
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-30-generic x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Server is Postgres 17.11.

`sql.array()` binds its parameter as `json[]`. That reads back correctly when nothing
casts it, but writing it into a real `text[]` column stores each element's **JSON
representation**, so a string arrives wrapped in literal `"` characters. No error is
raised on either side.

```ts
// bun repro.ts
const sql = new Bun.SQL('postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres');

await sql.unsafe('DROP TABLE IF EXISTS probe');
await sql.unsafe('CREATE TABLE probe (tags text[])');
await sql`INSERT INTO probe (tags) VALUES (${sql.array(['a', 'b'])})`;

const [row] = await sql.unsafe('SELECT tags FROM probe');
console.log('stored :', row.tags);
console.log('lengths:', row.tags.map((s: string) => s.length));

await sql.unsafe('DROP TABLE probe');
await sql.close();
```

### What is the expected behavior?

```
stored : [ "a", "b" ]
lengths: [ 1, 1 ]
```

### What do you see instead?

```
stored : [ "\"a\"", "\"b\"" ]
lengths: [ 3, 3 ]
```

The quote characters are in the stored value, not in the display. The same row read
by `psql` shows `{"\"a\"","\"b\""}`.

### Additional information

`pg_typeof` confirms the binding:

```ts
await sql`SELECT pg_typeof(${sql.array(['a', 'b'])})`;   // -> json[]
```

Three consequences follow from that one fact:

```ts
sql`SELECT ${sql.array(['a','b'])}`             // -> [ "a", "b" ]      ok, nothing casts it
sql`SELECT ${sql.array([1,2])}::int[]`          // -> error: cannot cast type json[] to integer[]
sql`SELECT ${sql.array(['a','b'])}::text[]`     // -> [ "\"a\"", "\"b\"" ]
```

The `::text[]` case and the column write above are the ones worth prioritising: they
are silent. The `::int[]` case at least fails loudly.

This matters for any library that writes its own `$n::type` casts rather than relying
on inference - which is the normal shape for a library written against `node-postgres`.
I hit it porting pg-boss onto `Bun.SQL`.

For completeness, a raw JS array (no `sql.array()`) still fails on this version too:

```ts
sql.unsafe('SELECT $1::text[]', [['a','b']])    // -> malformed array literal: "a,b"
sql.unsafe('SELECT $1::int[]',  [[1,2]])        // -> insufficient data left in message
```

I believe `sql.array()` was what #16840, #17798, #18775 and #22165 shipped, and those
are all closed - so this is a follow-up on the cast path rather

title: Native `bun login` / `bun logout`
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun is the only major package manager with no way to authenticate to a registry from the CLI.

- `npm login` — yes (web + legacy)
- `pnpm login` — yes (web login with QR, stores to its own `config.yaml`/`auth.ini`)
- `yarn npm login` — yes
- `bun login` — `Uh-oh. bun login is a subcommand reserved for future use by Bun.`

Today the only path is to hand-write a token into `.npmrc` or `bunfig.toml`, or shell out to `bunx npm login` — which installs npm just to obtain a credential Bun already knows how to read. Bun's own error text on an unauthenticated publish points at `bunx npm login`.

This is a recurring source of friction, and the existing issues are all downstream of the same missing primitive:

- #17531 (open) — `bun publish` doesn't support token-based login (Azure DevOps)
- #16523 / #14824 (closed on the `NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN` workaround) — no easy way to use an npm token; `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` still doesn't work because Bun doesn't read `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`, which is what open PR #38047 fixes
- #22423 (open) — `bun publish` doesn't support npm OIDC in GitHub Actions
- #24124 (closed 2026-08 by #36289) — auth failure despite a valid `.npmrc`; the fix was one more special case in the `.npmrc` lookup path
- #14444 / #14867 (closed) — Bun printed `.npmrc` credentials in warnings, because credential handling is spread across ad-hoc paths

The only prior ask for the command itself is #1176 (2022): titled `bun login --registry`, but filed through the bug template with just `Script not found "login"` in the body, and closed in two days. There is no open issue, PR, or discussion for it.

This is about to get more pressing. Since December 2025 `npm login` hands out a **two-hour session token** instead of a long-lived one, classic tokens are revoked, new granular tokens default to a 7-day lifetime (90-day cap), and bypass-2FA tokens are slated to lose direct publish (npm is targeting January 2027) in favour of staged publishing — #34306 is already asking Bun for an `npm stage publish` equivalent. The direction is unambiguous: publishing as a human means an interactive, 2FA-backed login session, re-established every couple of hours. Today the only way to get one is `bunx npm login`.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

`bun login` and `bun logout`, matching npm's surface:

```bash
bun login                                  # web login against the default registry
bun login --registry ht

title: Native workspace release management: `bun pm change`, `bun pm version --recursive`, `bun publish --recursive`
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun can install a monorepo, filter across it (`--filter`), catalog its versions, and publish a single package — but it cannot **release** one. Cutting a release from a Bun workspace today means bolting on Changesets, which is where it falls apart:

- #24687 — `bun changeset publish` ships `workspace:*` verbatim, so the published packages are uninstallable outside the repo. `bun publish` itself does rewrite the protocol; Changesets shells out to `npm publish` (its publish-tool picker only knows npm, pnpm and yarn), and npm doesn't. Tracked on their side as changesets#1468, and already closed as not-planned once on Bun's side (#16074)
- #18906 — `bun.lock` workspace versions aren't updated after bumping a workspace `package.json`
- #20477 — `bun pm pack` uses the `bun.lock` version rather than the package's own `package.json`
- #40789 — no `bun publish --recursive`, so publishing N packages means N invocations in dependency order, by hand

Each of those is filed as a separate bug, but they're one hole: **nothing in Bun owns the version-bump → propagate → changelog → tag → publish sequence**, so every tool layered on top hits the same seams.

For comparison, pnpm shipped this natively in 11.13.0 (2026-07-13, pnpm#12952): `pnpm change` records changeset-compatible intents, `pnpm version -r` consumes them (bumping across the workspace, propagating through `workspace:` ranges, writing changelogs), `pnpm publish -r` publishes whatever isn't on the registry yet. npm has none of it; this is a real chance for Bun to be the better tool rather than the catching-up one.

What Bun has today is `bun pm version` — bumps one `package.json`, commits, tags (`pm_version_command.rs`). It has no workspace awareness at all: no recursion, no dependent propagation, no changelog, and it doesn't refresh `bun.lock` (#28935, folded into #18906).

There is **no existing issue or discussion** requesting this. The four above are the symptoms, filed individually; the closest thing to a workflow ask is #34306, which wants an `npm stage publish` equivalent.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Three pieces, all under names that are already Bun's:

```bash
bun pm change                  # record a change intent (interactive; --package/--bump/--message for CI)
bun pm version --recursive     # consume intents: bump, propagate, changelog, one commit + tags
bun publish --recursive        # publish every workspace pac

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0+34cbb9a40 (Windows 11 x64). Same output on canary `1.4.1-canary.1+6c0619572` (`bun-windows-x64.zip` from the canary release, run directly).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`main.mjs`, with an empty `sub/` directory next to it:

```js
const parent = new URL("./sub/mod.mjs", import.meta.url);

for (const [label, value] of [
  ["string", parent.href],
  ["URL", parent],
  ["number", 42],
]) {
  try {
    console.log(label.padEnd(7), import.meta.resolve("./sibling.mjs", value));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(label.padEnd(7), "throws:", error.message);
  }
}
```

```
bun main.mjs
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Node documents `parent` as `<string> | <URL>` (under `--experimental-import-meta-resolve`), so the `URL` row should resolve the same as the string row, and a value of any other type should be rejected. Node v26.7.0, `node --experimental-import-meta-resolve main.mjs`:

```
string  file:///…/probe/sub/sibling.mjs
URL     file:///…/probe/sub/sibling.mjs
number  throws: The "parentURL" argument must be of type string or an instance of URL. Received type number (42)
```

### What do you see instead?

```
string  file:///…/probe/sub/sibling.mjs
URL     file:///…/probe/sibling.mjs
number  file:///…/probe/sibling.mjs
```

A `URL` instance is treated the same as a nonsense value: the argument is dropped and resolution falls back to the calling module's own location. No error for either, just a plausible-looking path from the wrong directory, where Node honours the `URL` and throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` for the number. That is how it stayed hidden in my probes for #40931, where the object form looked like it "worked".

### Where it comes from

`functionImportMeta__resolve` in `src/jsc/bindings/ImportMetaObject.cpp` accepts the second argument only when it is a string or an object with a `paths` array; anything else falls through to `import.meta.path`. Reading `href` off a `URL` instance there, and throwing Node's `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` for other non-`undefined` types instead of silently falling through, would close both halves.

Related: #40931 / #40933 (string `file://` parent mishandled in the resolver). This is a separate layer: argument validation before the resolver is reached, so #40933 does not touch it.

title: 1.4.1 regression: bundler emits `var X = X` shadowing a block-scoped `let X`, breaking any Elysia build
excerpt:
### What happens

Bundling an Elysia app with Bun 1.4.1 produces invalid JavaScript. The build
succeeds, but the output fails to parse at run time:

```
SyntaxError: Cannot declare a var variable that shadows a let/const/class variable: 'Check2'.
```

Bun 1.4.0 builds the same input correctly. This makes 1.4.1 unusable for any
project that bundles or compiles an Elysia server.

### Reproduction

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
bun init -y
bun add elysia@1.4.29
echo "import { Elysia } from 'elysia'; export default new Elysia().get('/', () => 'ok')" > app.ts
bun build app.ts --target=bun --compile --outfile=app-bin
./app-bin
```

- Bun 1.4.0: starts, exit 0
- Bun 1.4.1: `SyntaxError: Cannot declare a var variable that shadows a let/const/class variable: 'Check2'.`

`--compile` is not required; `bun build app.ts --target=bun` shows the same bad
output.

### Cause

Elysia's `dist/schema.mjs` already contains the shape a bundler emits when it
lowers a block-scoped function declaration: a block-scoped `let` holding the
function, plus a `var` alias under the original name.

Input (`elysia/dist/schema.mjs`, lines 253-283):

```js
let Check2 = function (value, validated = !1) { /* ... */ },
    runCheckers2 = function (/* ... */) { /* ... */ },
    mergeValues2 = function (/* ... */) { /* ... */ };
var Check = Check2, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues = mergeValues2;
```

That is valid: `let Check2` and `var Check` are different names.

Bun 1.4.1 renames `Check` to `Check2` to resolve a collision with another
`Check` in the bundle, without accounting for the `let Check2` already in that
scope. Output:

```js
let Check2 = function(value, validated = false) { /* ... */ },
    runCheckers2 = function(/* ... */) { /* ... */ },
    mergeValues2 = function(/* ... */) { /* ... */ };
var Check2 = Check2, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues = mergeValues2;
//  ^^^^^^ shadows the `let Check2` above
```

Bun 1.4.0 picks non-colliding names for the same input:

```js
var Check3 = Check22, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues2 = mergeValues22;
```

So the renamer no longer treats block-scoped `let` bindings as taken when it
picks a replacement name.

### Environment

- Bun 1.4.1, reproduced on macOS arm64 and Linux arm64
- Elysia 1.4.29 and 1.4.30 both affected
- Last good version: 1.4.0

### Possibly related

#41269 (bundler: keep the CommonJS wrapper when a var has the name of a
top-level function) landed shortly before 1.4.1 and touches var/function name
collision

title: Add native UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 segment validation
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Currently there is just literally no way to do this with native JavaScript, except to hand-roll your own byte validation according to RFC 3629 https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3629.

When you're working on lower level protocols and bitarray patterns, this is a highly useful feature to validate incoming inputs.


### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

There are a few ways this API could be implemented: in Buffer / U8intArray or a dedicated UTF API on Bun.
We then would need functions similar to `utf8SegmentSize` that return -1, 8, 16, 24, or 32 in bits. Utf16 and Utf32 would also need a isBigEndian parameter. All of these functions ideally could also take an offset parameter.

### What alternatives have you considered?

There is the TextDecoder API where you can set the `{ fatal: true }` option, but that doesn't actually tell you the size of the UTF-8 segment (can be 1-4 bytes long).
There is also isUtf8 for buffers in nodejs I think, but this again doesn't tell us anything about the length.

## Summary

On a KVM guest using QEMU's **default, CPUID-masked CPU model** (shows as "Common KVM processor"; flags limited to SSE2 + SSE3/`pni` — no SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2, AVX), `bun <large-entry-file>` never progresses past early runtime init:

- bun 1.4.0: process burns ~100% userspace CPU **forever** (confirmed 11+ minutes), RSS flat at ~11 MB, no output, and the **entry file is never even `open()`ed**. `bun --version` and trivial `bun -e` scripts work fine.
- bun 1.3.14 (same CPU): does not hang, but shows **pathological memory behavior** — OOM-killed climbing past 3.8 GB RSS for a workload that peaks at **~730 MB** on a full-feature CPU.

title: `HTMLBundle` cannot returned as `Response` in `Bun.serve()` even though directly it works
Support mixed static/dynamic route segments like `/@:username`
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun's built-in router supports named parameters and wildcard routes, but I need to match a parameter with a static prefix inside the same path segment.

For example:
```
routes: {
  "/@:username": handleProfile,
  "/*": handleSPA,
}
```

`/@alice` should match the profile route, while everything else should fall through to the SPA catch-all for example.

This pattern is useful for user/profile URLs such as `/@username` without reserving an entire top-level path like `/users/:username`.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Support mixed static/dynamic route segments (prefixed named parameters), such as:

```
/@:username
/file-:id
/:name.json
```

The more specific route should take precedence over a general `/*` catch-all.

### What alternatives have you considered?

Currently I'm handling it through a catch-all route and do the logic manually and if it doesn't match I internally `fetch()` by parsing URL.pathname. It works, adds a bit of overhead (fetch) and a direct implementation would be much cleaner.

title: bun install applies an `overrides` entry to versions outside its range when the selector has a prerelease bound
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.1+4661e494f

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-31-generic x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

An `overrides` key whose version selector contains a **prerelease bound** matches versions that are outside the range, and the override is applied to them.

`ts-node@10.9.2` depends on `diff@^4.0.1`, which resolves to `4.0.4`. `4.0.4` is not in `>=5.0.0-alpha.0 <8.0.0`, so the override below must not apply to it.

```json
{
  "name": "repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "ts-node": "10.9.2" },
  "overrides": { "diff@>=5.0.0-alpha.0 <8.0.0": "8.0.4" }
}
```

```bash
bun install
node -p "require('./node_modules/diff/package.json').version"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`4.0.4` — the installed version is outside the selector's range, so the override should not apply.

That is what both other package managers do with the same `package.json`:

| package manager | resolved |
| --- | --- |
| npm 11.16.0 | `4.0.4` |
| pnpm 9.15.9 (key under `pnpm.overrides`) | `4.0.4` |

Bun's own semver API agrees with them:

```js
Bun.semver.satisfies("4.0.4", ">=5.0.0-alpha.0 <8.0.0"); // false
```

So the range evaluation used while resolving `overrides` disagrees with `Bun.semver`.

### What do you see instead?

`8.0.4` — the override is applied to a version the selector does not match.

### Additional information

The trigger is specifically a prerelease tag in the selector. Same repro, varying only the key:

| `overrides` key | resolved | correct? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *(no overrides)* | `4.0.4` | baseline |
| `diff@>=5.0.0 <8.0.0` | `4.0.4` | yes |
| `diff@>=5.0.0-alpha.0 <8.0.0` | `8.0.4` | **no** |

Dropping `-alpha.0` from the lower bound is enough to make it behave correctly, so the selector is being parsed and evaluated (it is not simply ignored). Two further checks confirm the range is normally respected:

- `diff@>=99.0.0` → `4.0.4` (correctly does not match)
- `diff@zzz` (invalid range) → `4.0.4` (correctly ignored)

#### How this surfaced

While migrating a test repository from pnpm to Bun. The key was a security override carried over verbatim:

```json
"ajv@>=7.0.0-alpha.0 <8.18.0": ">=8.18.0"
```

`eslint` declares `ajv@^6.14.0`, which resolves to `6.14.0`/`6.15.0` — outside that range. Under Bun the override rewrote it to `ajv@8.x`, which no longer ships `lib/refs/json-schema-draft-04.json`, so eslint crashed on startup:

```
Cannot find module 'ajv/lib/refs/json-schema-draft-0

Bun.serve({unix}) accepts connections but never responds (1.4.0, macOS arm64) — also node:http .listen(socketPath) and raw Bun.listen({unix})
excerpt:
## Summary

On Bun 1.4.0 (macOS arm64) a server bound to a **Unix domain socket** accepts the connection and then never responds. Three independent APIs all reproduce it, and a Node↔Node control over the same socket path on the same machine works — so it is not the platform, the path, or permissions.

## Reproductions

**1. `Bun.serve({ unix })`**

```js
const p = '/tmp/uds-probe.sock'
try { require('fs').unlinkSync(p) } catch {}
Bun.serve({ unix: p, fetch: () => new Response('hello-from-uds') })
await Bun.sleep(300)
// curl -sv --max-time 3 --unix-socket /tmp/uds-probe.sock http://localhost/x
```

curl output — the request is fully sent, nothing comes back, exit 28 (timeout):

```
*   Trying /tmp/uds-probe.sock:0...
* Connected to localhost (/tmp/uds-probe.sock) port 0
> GET /x HTTP/1.1
> Host: localhost
> User-Agent: curl/8.7.1
> Accept: */*
>
* Request completely sent off
```

**2. `node:http` listening on a socket path (under Bun)**

```js
import http from 'node:http'
http.createServer((req, res) => { res.writeHead(200); res.end('ok') }).listen('/tmp/uds-probe3.sock')
```
Same result: connects, no response, curl exit 28.

**3. Raw `Bun.listen({ unix })` with a Node client**

```js
Bun.listen({ unix: '/tmp/uds-probe4.sock', socket: { data(sock, d) { sock.write('pong\n') } } })
```
Node client via `net.createConnection(path)` writes and receives nothing (3s timeout).

**Control — Node server + Node client, same machine, same socket API:**

```js
net.createServer(s => s.on('data', d => s.write('pong:' + d))).listen('/tmp/uds-control.sock')
// client receives: pong:ping
```
Works immediately. This is what makes it attributable to Bun's listener rather than the environment.

## Environment

- Bun **1.4.0** (`34cbb9a40`)
- macOS 25.5.0, arm64
- Socket created successfully in every case (file exists, `srw-------` after chmod)

## Impact / why we care

We wanted machine-scope endpoints on a channel a browser cannot address — a Unix socket is ideal because it has no origin, no port, and no URL `fetch()` can name. Having verified the failure three ways we backed the code out (rather than ship a socket that is created, announced in the log, and answers nothing) and used the parent process's stdio instead. The stdio channel is fine on its own merits, so this is not blocking us — filing because the diagnosis is done and the next person should not have to repeat the three-way bisection.

Happy to test a patch.

title: Bun 1.4.1 bundler renames two identifiers to the same name, emitting illegal "var Check2 = Check2" that Bun's own runtime rejects
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.1 (also reproduced with the exact `oven/bun:1.4.1-alpine` image)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (Alpine, docker `oven/bun:1.4.1-alpine`)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Minimal repro repo: **https://github.com/vlrdimir/bun-1.4.1-var-shadow-repro**

`repro.js`:

```js
import { t } from "elysia";
const schema = t.Object({ name: t.String() });
console.log("bundle parsed and ran, schema:", typeof schema);
```

Bundle and run with bun 1.4.1:

```sh
bun install
bun build repro.js --outdir=dist --target=bun
bun dist/repro.js
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The bundle produced by `bun build` should be parseable and runnable — as it is with bun 1.4.0, which outputs `bundle parsed and ran, schema: object` for the same input.

### What do you see instead?

Bun 1.4.1's runtime rejects the bundle Bun 1.4.1's bundler just produced:

```
SyntaxError: Cannot declare a var variable that shadows a let/const/class variable: 'Check2'.

Bun v1.4.1 (Linux x64)
```

### Additional information

The 1.4.1 bundler renames **two distinct identifiers to the same name**. Source is `elysia@1.4.29` `dist/schema.mjs:283`, which legitimately aliases:

```js
let Check = function(value, validated = false) { ... };
// ...
var Check2 = Check, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues = mergeValues2;
```

Bun 1.4.1's bundle output collapses both `Check` and `Check2` into `Check2`, emitting an illegal same-scope `let`/`var` collision (and TDZ self-reference):

```js
let Check2 = function(value, validated = false) { ... };
// ...
var Check2 = Check2, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues = mergeValues2;
```

Bun 1.4.0 bundling the identical input renames correctly (`Check` -> `Check22`):

```js
var Check2 = Check22, runCheckers = runCheckers2, mergeValues = mergeValues2;
```

and that 1.4.0 output runs fine on **both** the 1.4.0 and 1.4.1 runtimes — so this looks like a regression in the 1.4.1 bundler's identifier renaming, not in the parser (the parser is right to reject it).

Real-world impact: any app bundling `elysia` (we're on elysia 1.4.29, zod 4.4.3, `--target=bun`) fails at startup after deploying a 1.4.1-built bundle. We hit this in production because our Dockerfiles use the floating `oven/bun:1.4` tag, which moved from 1.4.0 to 1.4.1 today; we've pinned back to 1.4.0 as a workaround.

Repro repo with bundle excerpts for both versions: https://github.com/vlrdimir/bun-1.4.1-var-shadow-repro

bun add: unbounded tarball extraction allows disk-exhaustion DoS via malicious package
excerpt:
A malicious (or compromised) registry package can exhaust the victim's disk during `bun add` / `bun install`: neither extraction path caps total output bytes, per-file size, entry count, or disk usage.

## Where

- Streaming path: `src/install/TarballStream.rs` — `entry_count` is incremented (`on_entry`, ~L888) but never limited; `content_length` is stored but only logged (~L1141); data lands via `pwrite`+`ftruncate` (~L921+) with `preallocate_file` for sizes >1MB (~L893).
- Buffered path: `src/install/extract_tarball.rs` + `src/libarchive/lib.rs` — the sub-64MB branch (~L308 in extract_tarball.rs) only selects the gunzip backend, not a limit; sparse holes via `pwrite`+`ftruncate` (~L261-350 in lib.rs).

Traversal/hardlink/symlink handling in the same code is solid (absolute paths stripped, `..` clamped, symlinks skipped in npm mode, no mknod/hardlink sinks, setuid masked) — this report is only about the missing resource caps.

## Attack sketch (not executed to completion — static finding)

```bash
mkdir -p poc/package && head -c 200000000 /dev/urandom > poc/package/blob.bin
tar -czf evil.tgz -C poc package   # small compressed, large on disk
# serve evil.tgz as dist.tarball, then: bun add evil-pkg
```

A modest compressed payload expands to GBs under the temp dir and then the package cache, with no error until ENOSPC. Repeated entries multiply it.

## Expected

Abort extraction past sane thresholds (total bytes, entry count) with a clean error and temp-dir cleanup, similar in spirit to #28162 (size limit for `Bun.zstdDecompress`).

## Severity notes

Honestly assessed as DoS hardening, not RCE: it needs the victim to install an untrusted package, and registries + lockfiles already assume some trust. Still, a cap + clear error is cheap and protects CI runners and shared hosts.

title: Bun.RedisClient exposes no url or options, so a client cannot be rebuilt for the same server
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.1+4661e494f052c83c80dade1318e5710238340be6 (also on 1.4.0, 1.3.14)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-31-generic x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`Bun.RedisClient` keeps no reference to the url it was constructed with, and an
instance has no own properties at all. Any library that is handed a client and
needs to build a second one aimed at the same server has nothing to read.

```ts
const url = 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379/3';
const client = new Bun.RedisClient(url);
await client.connect();

console.log('constructed with :', url);
console.log('client.url       :', (client as { url?: string }).url);
console.log('own properties   :', Object.getOwnPropertyNames(client));
console.log('"url" in client  :', 'url' in client);

// What a library reconstructing from it actually gets.
const Ctor = client.constructor as new (u?: string) => Bun.RedisClient;
const rebuilt = new Ctor((client as { url?: string }).url);
await rebuilt.connect();
const info = String(await rebuilt.send('CLIENT', ['INFO']));
console.log('rebuilt connects to db:', /\bdb=(\d+)/.exec(info)?.[1]);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A constructed client exposes the target it was constructed with, so a
replacement can be aimed at the same server. `redis.createClient()` exposes
`options`, and `ioredis` exposes `options.host` / `options.port` / `options.db`,
which is what libraries written against those clients read.

### What do you see instead?

```
constructed with : redis://127.0.0.1:6379/3
client.url       : undefined
own properties   : []
"url" in client  : false
rebuilt connects to db: 0 (expected 3)

The replacement silently connects to Bun's default target rather than failing,
so nothing rejects and nothing is logged. The same happens for any non-default
host, port or password, not just a non-zero database index.

connection with `new (this.raw.constructor)(this.raw.url)`. A Worker against a

there as taskforcesh/bullmq#4582 and worked around by switching to
`duplicate()`, which preserves the target.

title: UB: `assume_init()` on never-written `[u8; N]` in `PathBuffer`, `WPathBuffer`, and resolver `Bufs`
excerpt:
**Source tree:** `c01965ff72` (on `main`). Platform-independent — the two
buggy constructions are not `cfg`-gated.

Not filed via the bug-report template: this is a source-level soundness bug
with no user-visible symptom, so the template's version/repro fields don't
apply. Per `SECURITY.md` this is deliberately a public issue and not a
`security@bun.com` report — see "Severity" for why it is not a vulnerability.

## Summary

Three sites construct a value from uninitialized memory where the target type
has a no-uninit validity invariant. Two are UB.

`src/paths/path_buffer_pool.rs` **already fixes this exact bug correctly** for
the same two types. These three sites are the siblings that were never updated
to match.

## Repro

`bun_sys` is not in `MIRI_CRATES` (`scripts/rust-miri.ts:39`), so
`bun run rust:miri` does not currently cover it. Running it the way that
script does — `-Zmiri-tree-borrows`, per #30876 — surfaces this immediately:

```
MIRIFLAGS=-Zmiri-tree-borrows cargo miri test -p bun_sys \
  dir::tests::borrow_does_not_close
```

```
error: Undefined Behavior: constructing invalid value of type
bun_core::PathBuffer: at .0[0], encountered uninitialized memory,
but expected an integer
```

Miri cannot reach every crate: `bun_core`'s tests stop at
`simdutf__convert_utf8_to_utf16le_with_errors` (vendored C is not callable
under Miri) and `bun_parsers` fails its build script, which also takes out
`bun_runtime`. Those need skips, not shims — consistent with the green-list
being described as the FFI-free crate set.

## The established, correct pattern

`src/paths/path_buffer_pool.rs:44-53`:

```rust
fn new_boxed() -> Box<Self> {
    // SAFETY: `PathBuffer` is `#[repr(transparent)]` over `[u8; N]`;
    // `new_zeroed` writes every byte to `0`, which is a valid `u8`, so the
    // value is fully initialized before `assume_init`. We use `new_zeroed`

    // were never written is UB even for integer arrays. This path runs only
    // on pool cache miss (<= once per slot per thread); `alloc_zeroed` for a
    // 64 KB heap block is typically satisfied by fresh OS-zeroed pages, so
    // there is no hot-path memset cost.
    unsafe { Box::<Self>::new_zeroed().assume_init() }
}
```

raised at the buggy sites. The module header adds the other half of the
rationale: the pool exists because "on Windows, each path bu

Add blur (Gaussian) filter support to Bun.Image pipeline
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`Bun.Image` currently supports resizing, rotation, flipping, and modulation (`.resize()`, `.rotate()`, `.flip()`, `.flop()`, `.modulate()`), plus encoding to various formats. However, there is no way to apply a blur effect (e.g. Gaussian blur) to an image within the pipeline.

Blur is a very common image operation — used for thumbnails/placeholders, privacy redaction, background effects, and general image processing pipelines. Right now users have to either:
- pull in Sharp or another native dependency alongside Bun.Image, or
- implement pixel-level blur manually, which defeats the purpose of using Bun's native, dependency-free image pipeline.


### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Add a `.blur(sigma)` (or similarly named) chainable method to the `Bun.Image` pipeline that applies a Gaussian blur to the image, similar to Sharp's `blur(sigma)` API:

```ts
await Bun.file("photo.jpg")
  .image()
  .blur(5) // sigma value
  .webp({ quality: 80 })
  .write("blurred.webp");


### What alternatives have you considered?

Using Sharp or another npm package alongside Bun - works, but reintroduces the native dependency overhead that Bun. Image is meant to avoid.

title: Every `new WebAssembly.Memory` leaks ~4 KB of RSS that GC never returns (1.4.0 through 1.4.3-canary; 1.3.14 is flat)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84. Also reproduced on 1.4.0 and 1.4.3-canary.1+76e9dcc6a. Not reproducible on 1.3.14.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.12.101 (Debian 13) x86_64, 16 cores.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Allocate `WebAssembly.Memory` objects in a loop, drop each one, and watch process RSS. No module compile or instantiate is involved.

```sh
bun wasm-memory-leak.mjs 20000
```

`wasm-memory-leak.mjs`:

```js
// Allocate WebAssembly.Memory objects in a loop, drop them, and print RSS.
const N = Number(process.argv[2] ?? 20000);
const rt = process.versions.bun ? `bun ${process.versions.bun}` : `node ${process.versions.node}`;
const gc = globalThis.gc ?? (globalThis.Bun ? () => Bun.gc(true) : () => {});
const mb = (b) => (b / 1048576).toFixed(1);
const base = process.memoryUsage().rss;
console.log(`${rt}: base rss ${mb(base)} MB`);
for (let i = 1; i <= N; i++) {
  const m = new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 65 }); // 65 pages = 4 MiB + 64 KiB
  new Uint8Array(m.buffer).fill(1, 0, 4096 * 1024);
  if (i % 5000 === 0) { gc(); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200)); console.log(`after ${i}: +${mb(process.memoryUsage().rss - base)} MB rss`); }
}
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 3000)); gc();
console.log(`after 3 s idle + gc: +${mb(process.memoryUsage().rss - base)} MB rss`);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

RSS plateaus once the collector starts reclaiming dropped memories, as it does on Bun 1.3.14 and Node 24:

```
bun 1.3.14: base rss 33.6 MB
after 5000: +20.8 MB rss
after 10000: +21.2 MB rss
after 15000: +21.0 MB rss
after 20000: +24.0 MB rss
after 3 s idle + gc: +11.9 MB rss
```

```
node 24.19.0: base rss 44.8 MB
after 5000: +9.6 MB rss
after 10000: +10.2 MB rss
after 15000: +10.2 MB rss
after 20000: +10.2 MB rss

### What version of Bun is running?

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun run` rewrites `npm run` to `bun run` inside a script body. Because `bun run` does not support `--workspace`, the rewritten command re-runs the **root** script instead of the workspace one — and when both define the same script name, that recurses without bound.

`package.json`

  "name": "root",
  "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["ui"],
  "scripts": {
    "build": "npm run build --workspace ui"
  }
}
```

`ui/package.json`
```json
{
  "name": "ui",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "echo RAN_UI_BUILD"
  }
}
```

Then `bun run build`.

### What is the expected behavior?

`npm run build` prints `RAN_UI_BUILD` — it runs the `ui` workspace's `build`.

Unbounded recursion, silently. With a depth counter added to the root script so it terminates:

title: Add a flag for `bun update` to only update direct dependencies and keep transitive ones at their locked versions
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Since 1.4, `bun update` re-resolves transitive dependencies as well as direct ones (that's what #24523 asked for, and it's a reasonable default). The problem is there's no way to opt out of it: a bare `bun update` bumps everything in the tree with a loose range to the newest in-range version at once, including packages you never asked to touch.

Two things this has caused me on a Bun app I maintain:

- Build tooling drifting: the esbuild copy under vite (plus a couple of other build-chain transitive deps) got bumped, and I ended up with multiple versions of them in the tree with no direct dependency changing. Took a while to even figure out why the build behaved differently.
- The app segfaulted at startup right after a bare update. Restoring the previous `bun.lock` from git brought it back. When the lockfile diff is a few hundred unrelated lines, "what changed?" has no good answer.

Right now `bun update` is all-or-nothing: either review a giant diff of packages you didn't intend to update, or update packages one by one with `bun update <pkg>`.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

An opt-in flag that makes `bun update` only move direct dependencies and reuse the resolutions already recorded in the lockfile for everything else (unless the new resolution invalidates them):

- `--depth 0`, matching what `npm update --depth 0` does, or
- `--prefer-locked`, like the Yarn Berry flag of the same name.

Not asking to change the default. A bunfig setting alongside `minimumReleaseAge` would also work.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- `bun update <pkg>` one at a time — works, but there's no way to say "all my direct deps, nothing else" without listing every one.
- Pinning the offenders with `overrides` — whack-a-mole, and you have to remember to clean them up.
- Committing `bun.lock` and reverting when things break — that's my current workflow, but it means finding out after the damage.
- `minimumReleaseAge` — helps against brand-new releases, not with the general problem.

Related but different: #25305 (`--latest` and `minimumReleaseAge` for transitive deps), #30407 (update the lockfile without saving to package.json), #25969 (keeping locked versions on `bun add`/`bun install`, which already works).

title: Bun.spawn IPC on Windows: child never receives NODE_CHANNEL_FD ("Unable to start IPC pipe")
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (also reproduces on 1.4.0)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 x64, build 10.0.26200.9267 (chocolatey install at
`C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\lib\bun\tools\bun-windows-x64\bun.exe`,
upgraded to 1.4.2 via `bun upgrade`)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

parent.mjs:

```js
const p = Bun.spawn({
  cmd: ["bun", "child.mjs"],
  ipc: (m) => console.log("GOT:", JSON.stringify(m)),
  onExit: (p, code) => console.log("EXIT:", code),
});
setTimeout(() => p.kill(), 6000);
```

child.mjs:

```js
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
writeFileSync("env.out", "NODE_CHANNEL_FD=" + JSON.stringify(process.env.NODE_CHANNEL_FD));
process.send?.({ status: "boot" });
setInterval(() => {}, 1000);
```

Run `bun parent.mjs`. Variants tried, all identical: parent launched from
`cmd.exe` as well as from a dev-harness shell, `serialization: "json"`,
`stdio: "inherit"`, `bun` binary directly instead of `bun run`.

### What is the expected behavior?

`GOT: {"status":"boot"}` and `process.env.NODE_CHANNEL_FD` set in the child.

### What do you see instead?

```text
warn: Unable to start IPC pipe 'Fd(9223372036854775811)'
```

No message ever arrives, in either direction. `env.out` shows
`NODE_CHANNEL_FD=undefined` — the parent never injects it. Per #40847 the
number is the raw tagged `u64`: `9223372036854775811 - 2^63 = 3`, i.e. fd 3
that cannot be opened as a libuv pipe. `process.send` exists in the child
and never throws; messages are silently lost.

Side symptoms on the same box: after `p.kill()` the parent sometimes stays
alive past its own timers (had to be force-terminated), and `onExit`
reported `null`.

### Additional information

- Same-machine control: `node:child_process.fork` with identical
  `process.send` / `process.on("message")` code delivers both directions
  immediately, so OS pipes are fine — only `Bun.spawn`'s native channel is
  affected. Our workaround is `fork`.
- Related: #33020 (Windows teardown hang, different trigger), #40847
  (documents this exact warning; your Windows CI passes, so this may be
  specific to newer Windows builds or to the `NODE_CHANNEL_FD` injection
  step rather than the pipe itself).

bun test: stderr report loses its head (the `(fail)` lines) when stderr is a pipe and a test prints a ~100 KB expect diff; sizes cap under 64 KiB multiples; a file redirect never loses (1.3.14, macOS)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (macOS 15 / Darwin 25.6.0, Apple Silicon, 18 cores)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun test` writes its report to **stderr**. When stderr is a **pipe** (a parent process capturing it) and one failing test prints a **large expect diff (~100 KB, one line)**, the **head of the stream is lost**: the per-test `(fail) …` line(s) and the beginning of the diff never reach the reader, while the diff's tail and the final summary (` 21 pass`, ` 2 fail`, `Ran 23 tests across 1 file.`) arrive intact and the exit code is 1 as expected. The captured size caps just under 64 KiB multiples (65,267 · 130,220 · 150,7xx bytes; the complete output is 171,625 bytes). It is intermittent unloaded and near-certain under CPU load (six concurrent `bun test` processes). Redirecting stderr to a regular **file** instead of a pipe never loses anything.

Minimal reproduction:

```ts
// big-diff.test.ts
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";
const big = "You are a pricing expert with hyperlocal market knowledge. ".repeat(1800); // ~100 KB
test("INV-20 the needle line", () => { expect(big).toContain("THIS STRING IS NOT THERE"); });
test("passes", () => { expect(1).toBe(1); });
```

```python
# probe.py — run: python3 probe.py
import subprocess, re, os
def run_pipe():
    p = subprocess.Popen(["bun", "test", "big-diff.test.ts"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    so, se = p.communicate(); out = so + se
    return p.returncode, len(out), len(re.findall(r"^\s*\(fail\)", out, re.M)), "INV-20 the needle line" in out
loaders = [subprocess.Popen(["bun", "test", "big-diff.test.ts"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL) for _ in range(6)]
for i in range(5):
    print("pipe under load:", run_pipe())   # rc=1, bytes≈130-151k, fail_lines=0 (expected 1), needle may be missing
for l in loaders: l.kill()
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The complete report: every `(fail) <name>` line and the whole diff, regardless of whether stderr is a pipe or a file, and regardless of load — the same bytes the file redirect produces (171,625 in our measurement, 2 `(fail)` lines).

### What do you see instead?

Measured over 5 runs per condition (the same spec, the same machine):

| condition | runs with lost `(fail)` lines | bytes captured |
|---|---|---|
| stderr → pipe, unloaded | 0/5 | 171,625 |
| stderr → file, unloaded | 0/5 | 171,625 |
| stderr → pipe, 6 concurrent bun test | **5/5** | 130,396–150,935 |
| s

title: Windows: pending Bun.stdin.text() no longer keeps the event loop alive after module evaluation (regression in 1.4.0, worked in 1.3.11–1.3.14)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (also reproduced on 1.4.0 and 1.4.1)

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 (Windows 11 Pro)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`repro.ts`:

```ts
process.on("exit", (code) =>
  console.error("exit", code, "bun", Bun.version, process.platform)
);

async function main() {
  const text = await Bun.stdin.text();
  console.log("read:", JSON.stringify(text));
}

main();
```

```
printf 'hello\n' | bun run repro.ts
```

The same happens with a file redirect (`bun run repro.ts < in.txt`) and with a parent that spawns the script with `stdin: "pipe"` and writes to it two seconds later — the child exits before the data arrives.

### What is the expected behavior?

```
read: "hello\n"
exit 0 bun 1.4.2 win32
```

This is what Linux prints on 1.4.0, and what Windows prints on 1.3.11 through 1.3.14.

### What do you see instead?

```
exit 0 bun 1.4.2 win32
```

The process exits 0 without the `read:` line: the pending `Bun.stdin.text()` read does not keep the event loop alive once module evaluation has finished, so the promise never settles.

### Additional information

Bisect on Windows x64 (same script, `printf 'hello\n' | bun run repro.ts`, 3–5 runs each, fully deterministic):

| Bun                    | result               |
| ---------------------- | -------------------- |
| 1.3.9, 1.3.10          | exits before reading |
| 1.3.11, 1.3.13, 1.3.14 | reads correctly      |
| 1.4.0, 1.4.1, 1.4.2    | exits before reading |

The v1.3.11 release notes list "Fixed: `Bun.file().text()` and similar async read methods not keeping event loop alive", which matches the window in which it worked; 1.4.0 appears to have regressed that fix on Windows. Linux 1.4.0 is unaffected.

Two details that narrow it down:

- A top-level `await Bun.stdin.text()` works on every version. Only a read awaited after module evaluation has completed (a floating `main()`, a Commander action, a `.then()` chain) is affected.
- Adding any other ref'd handle — a `setInterval`, a `process.on("beforeExit")` listener, or reading through `process.stdin` async iteration instead — makes the read complete, so the data path is fine; only the keep-alive accounting is missing.

Real-world impact: a git credential helper written in Bun (`git` spawns it with the request on a pipe and waits for stdout) silently answers nothing, so every authenticated clone fails with `could not read Username`. That is how we found it: https://github

title: Windows: stable install-scoped aliases for --bun and run.bun
excerpt:
# Windows: stable install-scoped aliases for --bun and run.bun

A proposed fix is already available in my [draft PR #41853](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/41853). Related: [oven-sh/bun#25321](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/25321), which reports different installed and temporary Bun executables during upgrades.

## Problem

On Windows, Bun 1.4.2's `--bun` / `[run] bun = true` uses `%TEMP%\bun-node-<build SHA>\node.exe`. The installed Bun path remains stable, but the alias path changes with the Bun build. Executable-specific antivirus exceptions therefore cannot reliably follow that alias across upgrades.

The request is a stable alias per Bun installation, not a global shared alias that can switch runtimes underneath concurrent installations.

## Reproduce the path difference

Create a package with:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "runtime": "node -p \"process.execPath\""
  }
}
```

Compare `bun -e 'console.log(process.execPath)'` with `bun --bun run runtime` on Windows. The first identifies the installed Bun executable; the second uses its build-specific temporary alias. Repeat after updating Bun at the same installed path to observe the alias change. We verified released Bun's path selection and SHA-based implementation. For the proposed fix, we built two binaries with different embedded Git revisions and verified that replacing one installation changed the child revision while retaining the same alias path.

## Why it matters

On one Windows 11 machine with Bun 1.4.2, Vitest 5.0.0 and Bitdefender Antivirus Plus 28.0.9.198, a controlled A/B/B/A comparison of the same project test command produced:

| Condition                                      | Durations        | Worker-shutdown warnings | Tests passed per run |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------- |
| Normal ATD protection                          | 43.70 s, 43.55 s | 99, 97                   | 1,918                |
| ATD exception for the temporary node.exe alias | 8.16 s, 7.98 s   | 0, 0                     | 1,918                |

This is evidence of an ATD interaction on this machine, not proof of a Bun shutdown defect. No standalone reproduction of the antivirus slowdown has been isolated. The path churn itself is independently observable.

## Proposed fix in draft PR #41853

1. Use an alias directory tied to the stable installed executable path, rather than the build SHA. Keep separate installations sep

title: `--bun` silently falls back to `node` when `/tmp/bun-node-<sha>` is owned by another user
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 5.14.0-741.el9.x86_64 x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On a server where several Unix accounts share one Bun binary, with no Node.js installed:

```sh
# as user A
sudo -u usera bun --bun run build      # works, creates /tmp/bun-node-<sha>/ owned by usera, mode 700

# as user B, same machine, same bun binary
sudo -u userb bun --bun run build
```

Where the `build` script is any script that invokes a bin with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang, for example `vite build`.

### What is the expected behavior?

User B's script runs under Bun, the same as user A's.

### What do you see instead?

```
$ vite build && vite build --ssr
/usr/bin/env: 'node': No such file or directory
error: script "build" exited with code 127
```

No warning from Bun. `ls -la /tmp | grep bun-node` shows the directory owned by user A with mode `drwx------`, which user B cannot enter:

```
drwx------   2 usera  usera  29 Sep  8 13:02 bun-node-744846f84
```

### Additional information

The cause is in `create_fake_temporary_node_executable` in `src/install/lib.rs`. `BUN_NODE_DIR` is `/tmp/bun-node-<GIT_SHA_SHORT>`, so every user of the same Bun build computes the same path. The directory is created with mode 0700, and on `EEXIST` the code refuses to use it unless `st_uid == getuid()`, then returns `Ok(())` without modifying `PATH`. That refusal is sensible for a shared temp directory, but the result is that `--bun` only works for the first account to run a given Bun version on a multi-user host.

`bunx --bun`, `bun --bun run <script>`, and `bun --bun <bin>` are all affected, since they share this code path. Setting `TMPDIR` does not help because the path is a compile-time constant.

Suggested fixes, either of which would resolve this:

1. Include the uid in the directory name, for example `/tmp/bun-node-<sha>-<uid>`, so accounts never collide.
2. Fall back to a per-user location such as `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bun-node-<sha>` or `~/.cache/bun/node-<sha>` when the shared directory is unusable.


Related: #4690 fixed the stale-symlink case for a directory the user owns, but does not cover a directory owned by someone else.

### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Running `bun run` without a script name lists the available `package.json` scripts, but it immediately exits. I cannot navigate the displayed scripts with the arrow keys, type to filter them, or press Enter to run a selection. I have to read the list and then type a second command with the full script name.

This adds friction in projects with many similarly named scripts, such as `build:dev`, `build:test`, `build:release`, and `preview`. An interactive script picker would make scripts easier to discover and run directly from Bun.

When `bun run` is invoked without a script name in an interactive terminal and the package has scripts, show a searchable script picker:

title: Support omitting application source from bytecode-compiled executables
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

We're evaluating switching a packaged application from `pkg` to Bun. With `pkg`, we use bytecode packaging to avoid distributing directly readable application JavaScript. We'd like a comparable option for Bun's standalone executables.

With `bun build --compile --bytecode --minify`, bundled application source is still included in the executable, even without source maps. Minification makes it less readable, but the JavaScript can still be extracted.

I understand this is the documented behavior:

- [Bytecode documentation: Source code still required](https://bun.com/docs/bundler/bytecode#source-code-still-required)
- [Bytecode documentation: Bytecode is not obfuscation](https://bun.com/docs/bundler/bytecode#bytecode-is-not-obfuscation)
- [Discussion #14422: Question re --bytecode compilation](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/discussions/14422), where Jarred explains that JavaScriptCore's bytecode implementation requires source and suggests minification.
- Related report: #19498, whose discussion also covers extra source included with the Bun runtime.

The goal is to make casual recovery of proprietary application logic harder, accepting that bytecode can still be reverse engineered.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

An opt-in mode for `bun build --compile --bytecode` that produces a standalone executable without embedding the bundled application JavaScript source.

Ideally:

- The executable runs from the embedded bytecode without requiring application source files.
- Any limitations affecting source-dependent runtime behavior, debugging, or supported JavaScript features are documented.
- If a build cannot meet the source-omission guarantee, it reports that explicitly instead of silently retaining the source.

This would preserve the current default behavior. The request concerns the application's source; removing unrelated built-in Bun assets is a separate concern.

Given the JavaScriptCore requirement described in #14422, is such a mode feasible with changes to Bun or its JavaScriptCore integration? It would be useful to track the necessary work or the remaining blockers.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- **Minification and omitting source maps:** useful, but still leave extractable application JavaScript in the executable.
- **A separate JavaScript obfuscation step:** adds build complexity and compatibility/performance tradeoffs while still shipping JavaScript.

1.3.14 and 1.4.0 (both reproduce)

## What platform is your computer?
Linux x86_64, containerized (GitLab CI Kubernetes executor, `oven/bun:1.4-debian` / Debian-based images). Does not reproduce on macOS with the same Bun version.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?
We run a React + jsdom test suite (~1500 tests, ~34% of files) via Vitest, invoked through the `bun` binary as the JS runtime (`bun run test:coverage`, i.e. `vitest run --coverage`, **not** `bun:test`):

- vitest 4.1.8, `@vitest/coverage-istanbul` 4.1.8, jsdom 29.1.1
- React 19, `@testing-library/react` 16.3.2

```bash
# package.json
"test:coverage": "vitest run --coverage"

# invoked as
bun run test:coverage
```

Sampling pod RSS while the suite runs:

- **Bun 1.3.14**, `--maxWorkers=1` (i.e. vitest's fork pool runs *serially*, one worker, no concurrency at all): RSS still climbs ~0.5 GiB per test file, unbounded, and the pod is OOM-killed (exit 137) after ~6 files. Raising the pod's memory limit to 3 GiB did not help — it just took longer to hit the ceiling.
- **Bun 1.4.0**, `--maxWorkers=2`: same shape, OOM-killed even sooner — after completing a single test file.
- **Node 22** running the *identical* suite via `npx vitest run --coverage` (no Bun involved at all): peak RSS ~0.7–0.8 GiB, stays flat across all files, exits 0.
- **macOS**, Bun 1.3.14/1.4.0, same suite: RSS is reclaimed between files as expected, no leak.

So: same vitest version, same test files, same worker-pool code path — the only variable that produces unbounded growth is "JS runtime = Bun" + "OS = Linux".

When a vitest worker (fork/thread) finishes a test file and vitest recycles or tears it down, the runtime's freed heap pages should be returned to the OS (or at least become reclaimable), the same way they are under Node on Linux and under Bun on macOS. RSS grows monotonically and roughly linearly with files processed, ~0.5 GiB/file, regardless of `--maxWorkers` (reproduces at `--maxWorkers=1`, i.e. no concurrency), and is never reclaimed — even under memory pressure, even between GC-eligible teardowns. title: Response.clone() after accessing .body leaves the original stream empty
install: cache lifecycle-script output so postinstall payloads aren't re-materialized per project
excerpt:
## What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun's package cache already does its job well — this is not a report that it is broken. An ordinary package costs **zero** additional disk in a second project, because bun clones it out of `~/.bun/install/cache`.

The gap is narrower: **output produced by a lifecycle script is not cached.** For a package whose `postinstall` materializes a large payload into its own directory, every project pays the full disk and CPU cost again, even though the result is byte-identical.

### Measurements

macOS 26.6.2, APFS, arm64, **bun 1.4.2**. "Real disk" is `df` before/after — `du` massively overcounts CoW clones and would report these numbers wrong. Every run is with an already-warm cache and a freshly deleted `node_modules`.

| Package | apparent size | real disk, warm install |
|---|---|---|
| `@next/swc-darwin-arm64@16.1.6` (ordinary package) | 101 MiB | **0 MiB** |
| `electron@33.4.11` (postinstall payload) | 242 MiB | **242 MiB** |

The first row is the control: the cache and clonefile path work exactly as intended. The second row is the gap.

### Reproduction

```sh
mkdir /tmp/e && cd /tmp/e
cat > package.json <<'J'
{"name":"e","dependencies":{"electron":"33.4.11"},"trustedDependencies":["electron"]}
J

bun install                 # warm the cache
rm -rf node_modules

df -k ~ | tail -1           # note available blocks
bun install
df -k ~ | tail -1           # ~242 MiB less available
```

### Where the 242 MiB comes from

1. The npm package is ~1 MiB; it ships essentially only `"postinstall": "node install.js"`.
2. `install.js` downloads `electron-v33.4.11-darwin-arm64.zip` — **95 MiB compressed** — and caches it by SHA-256 under `~/Library/Caches/electron/`.
3. It unzips into `node_modules` → **242 MiB**, of which a single `Electron Framework` binary (compiled Chromium) is 149 MiB.

So the *download* is already cached, by Electron itself. What is not cached is the **extraction**. Each project spends the CPU to unzip 95 MiB into 242 MiB of blocks bit-identical to those the project next door already has.

### Why it matters

The cost scales with the number of checkouts, not repo size. We run parallel git worktrees of one monorepo, and each worktree pays the full 242 MiB and the full unzip.

This also interacts with `trustedDependencies`: Electron's script *must* run for the package to work at all, so the packages most affected here are exactly the ones users have already had to trust.

title: Bun.spawn({ terminal }): process hangs forever in __wait4_nocancel when a process-group signal races the child's own exit (macOS)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (aarch64-apple-darwin), also seen on 1.3.13

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 15.1, arm64 (M-series). Also reproduces on GitHub's `macos-14` runners.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Spawn a PTY child via `Bun.spawn(..., { terminal })` that exits on its own, and race a process-group `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL` against that exit. Within a few thousand iterations the process stops making progress entirely.

```js
// bun repro.mjs
const ITERATIONS = Number(process.argv[2] ?? 20000)
const CONCURRENCY = Number(process.argv[3] ?? 8)
let done = 0

async function once() {
  const proc = Bun.spawn(["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo dying-now; exit 7"], {
    terminal: { cols: 80, rows: 24, name: "xterm-256color", data: () => {} },
  })
  const { pid } = proc
  setTimeout(() => { try { process.kill(-pid, "SIGTERM") } catch {} }, 0)
  setTimeout(() => { try { process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL") } catch {} }, 1)
  await proc.exited
  try { proc.terminal?.close() } catch {}
  if (++done % 200 === 0) console.log(`${done}/${ITERATIONS} pid=${process.pid}`)
}

await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: CONCURRENCY }, async () => {
  while (done < ITERATIONS) await once()
}))
console.log(`completed ${done} — no wedge`)
```

```
$ bun repro.mjs
200/20000 pid=65130
...
2400/20000 pid=65130
   ← stops here permanently
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The loop runs to completion. Racing a signal against a child's own exit should at worst lose the race; it should not stop the runtime.

### What do you see instead?

The process hangs forever at 0% CPU.

**Main thread is blocked in a synchronous `wait4`** (`sample <pid>`):

```
1789 Thread_2951758   DispatchQueue_1: com.apple.main-thread  (serial)
  ...
    1789 ???  (in bun)  load address 0x1009b0000 + 0x13d2a64
      1789 __wait4_nocancel  (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) + 8  [0x18c76e2d8]
```

**Every child is stuck part-way through exit** and does not respond to `SIGKILL`:

```
  PID  PPID STAT COMMAND
72148 65130 ?NEs (bash)
72157 65130 ?NEs (bash)
   ... 8 of them, all ?NEs
```

`kill -9 <child>` leaves the state unchanged; so does `SIGCONT`. The children are only reaped when the *parent* bun process is killed. In longer-running cases a mix of `<defunct>` zombies and `?NEs` children accumulates.

Note this is a `Bun.spawn` with `{ terminal }` — no `stdout`/`stderr` option — so all three fds are the PTY.

title: Segfault (macOS) / undefined symbol v8::Function::GetScriptOrigin (Linux) when a N-API addon calls it: @newrelic/fn-inspect funcInfo()
excerpt:
### How can we reproduce the crash?

`@newrelic/fn-inspect` is a small N-API addon that the New Relic Node.js agent uses for "code-level metrics". Its `funcInfo(fn)` calls `v8::Function::GetScriptOrigin()` and friends. Calling it once is enough:

```sh
mkdir fn-inspect-bun-repro && cd fn-inspect-bun-repro
bun init -y
bun add @newrelic/fn-inspect@5.1.0
cat > repro.cjs <<'JS'
const { funcInfo } = require("@newrelic/fn-inspect");
function hello() { return 1; }
console.log("calling funcInfo");
console.log(funcInfo(hello));
JS
bun repro.cjs
```

Node prints `{ lineNumber: 1, method: 'hello', file: '/.../repro.cjs', column: 14, type: 'Function' }`.

Bun:

- macOS 26.3.1 arm64, Bun 1.4.2+744846f84: `panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x0`
- Linux arm64 glibc, `oven/bun:1.4.2` and `oven/bun:canary` (1.4.3): the process aborts with `bun: symbol lookup error: .../@newrelic+fn-inspect.abi147.uv1.armv8.glibc.node: undefined symbol: _ZNK2v88Function15GetScriptOriginEv` (exit 127)

Real-world impact: any app that runs the New Relic agent (`newrelic` 14.x) under Bun with code-level metrics on (the default) crashes as soon as the agent records a segment, because `lib/util/code-level-metrics.js` calls `funcInfo`. Setting `NEW_RELIC_CODE_LEVEL_METRICS_ENABLED=false` avoids the call and is the workaround we use. Probably part of the broader V8 C++ API story in #4290, filing separately since this is a hard crash from a single, widely used function.

### Relevant log output

```text
calling funcInfo
Features: bunfig jsc transpiler_cache(46) tsconfig process_dlopen
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x0
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.
```

Linux:

```text
calling funcInfo
bun: symbol lookup error: /w/node_modules/@newrelic/fn-inspect/prebuilds/linux-arm64/@newrelic+fn-inspect.abi147.uv1.armv8.glibc.node: undefined symbol: _ZNK2v88Function15GetScriptOriginEv
```

Bun.serve: reused keep-alive socket reset (ECONNRESET / socket hang up) on immediate back-to-back requests to small/fast responses (linux-x64)
excerpt:
## Environment
- Bun **1.4.0** and **1.4.2** (stable), **linux-x64** (GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`).
- NOT reproduced on darwin-arm64 at 1.3.14 / 1.4.0 / 1.4.2 (0 resets in 2000–4000 requests) — appears **linux-x64 timing-specific**.
- Client: `node-fetch@2.6.7` over Node ≥19's keep-alive `http.Agent` (also affects undici / any spec-honoring client that reuses keep-alive sockets).

## Summary
A `Bun.serve` server returning a tiny, instant response **resets a reused keep-alive socket** when the next request arrives immediately after the previous response completed. The client sees `ECONNRESET` → `FetchError: … socket hang up`. There is **no HTTP response** and **nothing in the server log** — the `fetch` handler never runs for the reset request; the reset is at Bun's HTTP/TCP layer, ~1 ms. Single requests, and reuse delayed ≥~50 ms, succeed — so only small/fast responses lose the reuse race.

This looks like the **`Bun.serve` sibling** of the `node:http`-under-Bun keep-alive reuse reset that was addressed around Bun 1.4.0 — the `Bun.serve` transport still exhibits it at 1.4.2.

## Minimal reproduction (no framework)
`server.mjs`:
```js
Bun.serve({
  port: Number(process.env.PORT || 3000),
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  fetch() { return new Response('ok'); }, // tiny, instant
});
```
Client: fire ~2000 back-to-back requests over a Node keep-alive agent (or `node-fetch@2` with `new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true })`) and count `socket hang up`. On linux-x64 a fraction reset; on darwin none do. (Because it is reuse-timing-specific, a tight back-to-back loop over a single keep-alive agent is needed to observe it.)

## Evidence it is socket reuse
Serving a real app through `Bun.serve` (Next.js via nitro's bun preset), ~79 fixtures of the official Next.js e2e suite fail with exactly this `socket hang up` across unrelated features. Stamping `Connection: close` on every response — so clients never reuse the socket — makes **59 of them pass** on the same linux-x64 Bun 1.4.0 CI, with zero other changes. The mitigation's only effect is to stop socket reuse, which isolates the cause to the keep-alive reuse path.

## Ask
Treat the `Bun.serve` keep-alive socket-reuse path the same as the `node:http` fix — do not reset a reused idle keep-alive socket on an immediately-following request. Happy to provide the packaged repro harness (server + node-fetch keep-alive driver) if useful.

title: install: minimumReleaseAgeExcludes matches by name only, so an exemption never expires and `name@version` silently matches nothing
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (macOS, Apple Silicon).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`minimumReleaseAgeExcludes` matches by package NAME, so an entry exempts that
package at every future version. There is no way to exempt one version, and the
`name@version` spelling is accepted into the array and silently matches nothing.

`vite@8.3.0` was published about 7 hours before this run, so a 24-hour window
blocks it.

```toml
# bunfig.toml
[install]
minimumReleaseAge = 86400
minimumReleaseAgeExcludes = []   # then ["vite"], then ["vite@8.3.0"]
```

```json
{ "name": "mra", "private": true, "dependencies": { "vite": "8.3.0" } }
```

```
$ bun install --dry-run     # excludes = []
error: No version matching "vite" found for specifier "8.3.0" (blocked by minimum-release-age: 86400 seconds)

$ bun install --dry-run     # excludes = ["vite"]
 nanoid@3.3.18
 picocolors@1.1.1
 source-map-js@1.2.1
[745.00ms] done

$ bun install --dry-run     # excludes = ["vite@8.3.0"]
error: No version matching "vite" found for specifier "8.3.0" (blocked by minimum-release-age: 86400 seconds)
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Two things, and the first is the one that matters:

1. **An exemption should be able to name a version**, so it expires on its own
   when the dependency moves past it. pnpm's `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` takes
   `name@version` alongside a bare name, which is what makes an entry there a
   temporary waiver rather than a permanent hole.
2. **`"vite@8.3.0"` should not be silently inert.** If the field only takes
   names, an entry carrying `@` is a mistake worth a warning; today it neither
   matches nor complains.

### What do you see instead?

An entry is permanent and total. `["vite"]` exempts vite from the release-age
policy forever, at every version, including versions published minutes ago in
some future incident. The policy exists precisely for the window in which a
compromised release is most dangerous and least likely to have been noticed, so
a name-only exemption disables the check exactly where it was meant to apply.

The failure is quiet in the direction that matters. Nothing errors, nothing
warns, and the entry keeps looking like a note about one bump long after that
bump landed. In our repository the list once held 22 entries, and every one of
them had outlived the release it was added for; the list was not stale, it was a
set of permanently disabled checks

title: Date: an offset change that reverts within 19 days can be skipped by the local time offset cache (America/Recife, October 2000)
excerpt:
### What happens

In a zone whose UTC offset changes and then changes back within 19 days, `Date` can return the surrounding offset for the whole short period. Which instants are wrong depends on the lookups the process made before.

America/Recife had DST from 2000-10-08 to 2000-10-15 only. On bun 1.4.3 and on main:

```sh
TZ=America/Recife bun -e "
new Date('2000-10-07T12:00Z').getTimezoneOffset();
new Date('2000-10-20T12:00Z').getTimezoneOffset();
console.log(new Date('2000-10-10T12:00Z').getTimezoneOffset())"
# 180

TZ=America/Recife bun -e "console.log(new Date('2000-10-10T12:00Z').getTimezoneOffset())"
# 120
```

`Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the same process says `GMT-02:00` (120) both times. No special priming is needed. A daily forward walk that starts on 2000-09-08 returns 180 for all seven DST days:

```sh
TZ=America/Recife bun -e "
for (let t = Date.parse('2000-09-08T12:00Z'); t <= Date.parse('2000-10-14T12:00Z'); t += 864e5)
  if (new Date(t).getTimezoneOffset() !== 180) console.log('DST seen on', new Date(t).toISOString())"
# prints nothing
```

26 of the 40 start days before 2000-10-08 give a wrong walk for Recife, 16 of 40 for America/Argentina/Tucuman (2004-06-01), 12 of 40 for America/Fortaleza (2000-10-08).

Node 26 prints the same wrong values. V8's `DSTOffsetCache` makes the same assumption.

### Cause

`DateCache::DSTCache::localTimeOffset()` in JSC (`Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSDateMath.cpp`, a port of V8's cache) takes the offset to be constant between two instants that have the same offset and are at most 19 days apart (`defaultDSTDeltaInMilliseconds`). Two places do that:

- the merge of `m_before` and `m_after` when their offsets are equal
- the branch of `extendTheAfterCache()` that moves `m_after->start` back by up to 19 days

The comment in `JSDateMath.h` names Egypt 2010 (20 days of DST) as the shortest period. tzdata has shorter ones.

### Periods shorter than 19 days in tzdata 2026b

Compared as `(offset, isDST)`, which is what JSC caches:

| Zone | Period |
| --- | --- |
| America/Recife, America/Noronha, America/Boa_Vista | 7 days of DST, 2000-10-08 to 2000-10-15 |
| America/Fortaleza, America/Maceio | 14 days of DST, 2000-10-08 to 2000-10-22 |
| America/Argentina/Tucuman | 12 days at -04, 2004-06-01 to 2004-06-13 |
| Asia/Gaza, Asia/Hebron | predicted 7 and 14 day periods in 2040, 2053, 2054, 2072, 2073, 2086 |
| Africa/Freetown 1939, Africa/Tunis 1943, Europe/Tirane 1943, Europe/Vienna 1945 | 4 to 12 days |

excerpt:
# SIGTRAP on M3 Pro: WebKit StringImpl assertion failure in Worker thread

## Environment
- **Bun**: 1.4.0 and 1.4.2 (both affected)
- **OS**: macOS 26.0 (Sequoia), Apple M3 Pro (Mac15,7)
- **Binary**: opencode.exe (Bun-based CLI app, ad-hoc signed)

## Description

Bun crashes with SIGTRAP (exit 133) on M3 Pro when running a long-lived CLI application. The crash occurs in the Worker thread at a fixed offset in the binary, triggered by a WebKit `StringImpl` assertion failure.

## Crash Signature

All 30+ crashes share identical characteristics:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Exception | `EXC_BREAKPOINT` / `SIGTRAP` |
| ESR | `0xF200C471` — `(Breakpoint) pointer authentication trap IB` |
| Faulting thread | `Worker` (JSC GC/JS execution) |
| Faulting instruction | `brk #0xc471` at binary offset `0x1CDA3D8` |
| Source | WebKit `vendor/WebKit/Source/WTF/wtf/text/StringImpl.h` line 894 |
| Assertion | `RELEASE_ASSERT(m_length <= MaxLength)` where `MaxLength = int32_t::max()` (2GB) |
| Crash pattern | Fixed offset across all crashes (ASLR slide varies) |

## Reproduction

1. Run a Bun-based CLI app (opencode) with TUI
2. Use it for an extended session (15+ hours, multiple restarts reusing same session ID)
3. After session completes, send new input
4. → SIGTRAP crash

The crash is **intermittent but frequent** — happens roughly every 30-60 minutes of active use.

## Key Observations

1. **Same offset every time**: All 30+ crashes at binary offset `0x1CDA3D8` (instruction `brk #0xc471`)
2. **Not data-size dependent**: Database is only 6MB, session data is 3MB — nowhere near 2GB limit
3. **Not plugin-related**: Crashes with all plugins disabled
4. **Not compaction-related**: Crashes with auto-compaction disabled
5. **Not Orca-related**: Crashes with Orca hooks disabled
6. **Bun 1.4.0 and 1.4.2 both affected**
7. **M3 Pro specific**: Same binary runs fine on M4 Max

## Hypothesis

The crash is likely caused by:
- WebKit's `StringImpl` constructor receiving a length value that exceeds `int32_t::max()`
- This could happen during string concatenation/serialization in the Worker thread
- The `brk #0xc471` is a deliberate assertion failure (not a PAC issue despite macOS reporting it as "pointer authentication trap IB")
- M3 Pro may have a specific code path in WebKit's string handling that produces incorrect length values

## Related

- Similar to Bun issue #37284 (SIGSEGV in JSC GC on 1.4.0-canary, macOS arm64)
- The `brk #0xc471` instruction is WebKit's `RELEA

title: completions: fix --cwd support, Bash 3.2 compatibility, and optimize package.json parsing
excerpt:
### Description

The current shell completion scripts across Bash, Zsh, and Fish have several bugs and limitations:

1. **Bash 3.2 Compatibility (macOS):** `completions/bun.bash` uses associative arrays (`declare -A`), which break on macOS default Bash 3.2.
2. **Unsafe regex evaluation:** `_read_scripts_in_package_json` evaluates empty regular expressions when variables are unset and causes unnecessary subshell execution.
3. **Missing \`--cwd\` awareness:** Completions only inspect `$PWD` for scripts, packages, and binaries, completely ignoring `--cwd <dir>` and `--cwd=<dir>`.
4. **Hard dependency on \`jq\` in Zsh:** `_bun_remove_param_package_completion` fails silently if `jq` is not installed on the system.
5. **Missing CLI commands & Directory UX:** Completions are missing for `test`, `build`, `repl`, and `bunx`. Directory completions incorrectly append trailing spaces.

### Proposed Solution

- Replace associative arrays in `bun.bash` with flat option lists for Bash 3.2 compatibility.
- Stream `package.json` line-by-line to prevent empty regex matching bugs.
- Support `--cwd` flags across Bash, Zsh, and Fish.
- Use native Zsh pattern matching instead of external `jq`.
- Add completions for `test`, `build`, `repl`, and `bunx`, and suppress trailing spaces on directory completions.

title: node:tls autoSelectFamily adds a duplicate end listener per address attempt
excerpt:
### Bun version

Reproduced with:

- Bun `1.4.2+744846f84`
- Bun `1.3.14+0d9b296af`
- Bun 1.4.0

The relevant repeated listener registration is also present on current `main` at `6b394bfeb0ce69d6668a8aecb648b5c5b2fc6cbf`.

### Platform

- macOS 27.0 (26A5425a)
- arm64

### What happened?

`tls.connect()` with `autoSelectFamily` adds another `end` listener to the same `TLSSocket` for each address attempt. Nine attempts are enough to cross the default listener limit: two listeners exist initially, then each attempt adds one more.

This emits `MaxListenersExceededWarning` even though only one socket and one logical connection are involved. The duplicate listeners remain attached until the socket is destroyed.

### Reproduction

This is deterministic and performs no external network requests:

```js
import { getEventListeners } from 'node:events'
import tls from 'node:tls'

const addresses = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, index) => ({
  address: `127.0.0.${index + 2}`,
  family: 4,
}))
let attempts = 0

process.on('warning', (warning) => {
  console.error(
    `warning=${warning.name} type=${warning.type} count=${warning.count}`,
  )
})

const socket = tls.connect({
  host: 'many-addresses.invalid',
  port: 443,
  servername: 'many-addresses.invalid',
  autoSelectFamily: true,
  autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout: 10,
  lookup: (_hostname, options, callback) => {
    if (!options.all) throw new Error('expected lookup({ all: true })')
    queueMicrotask(() => callback(null, addresses))
  },
})

socket.on('connectionAttempt', () => {
  attempts += 1
  console.log(
    `attempt=${attempts} endListeners=${getEventListeners(socket, 'end').length}`,
  )
})
socket.on('error', () => {})
setTimeout(() => {
  console.log(
    `totalAttempts=${attempts} finalEndListeners=${getEventListeners(socket, 'end').length}`,
  )
  socket.destroy()
}, 500)
```

Run with:

```sh
bun repro.mjs
```

Relevant output:

```text
attempt=1 endListeners=3
attempt=8 endListeners=10
attempt=9 endListeners=11
attempt=12 endListeners=14
totalAttempts=12 finalEndListeners=14
MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 end listeners added to [TLSSocket].
warning=MaxListenersExceededWarning type=end count=11
```

As a control, Node.js 22.23.1 runs all 12 attempts with `endListeners=2` throughout and emits no warning.
