title: shell: a pipeline member that fails with a JS error leaves the other members running and the process open
excerpt:
### What happens

A pipeline member can fail with a JS error before it starts, for example when its redirect target is a `${value}` it cannot use. The promise rejects, but the other members of the pipeline are not stopped. The members that already started keep running. The pipe ends that belong to the failed member and to the members after it stay open. A producer that writes more than the pipe buffer then blocks forever, and the process does not exit.

```js
import { $ } from "bun";
const producer = 'process.stdout.write(Buffer.alloc(1 << 20, "a"))';
await $`${process.execPath} -e ${producer} | cat > ${new Response("r")}`
  .quiet()
  .catch(e => console.log("rejected:", e.message));
console.log("done");
```

Output on 1.4.3 (canary 5f554969b), Linux x64:

```
rejected: Blobs are immutable, and cannot be used for stdout/stderr
done
```

Then the process hangs. It must exit after `done`.

With a small producer (`bun --version | cat > ${new Response("r")}`) 1.4.3 also hangs, because the interpreter keeps the event loop alive. #42251 fixes that case. The large producer case is the same before and after #42251.

### Why

- A state that throws returns `Yield::Failed` and never reports to its parent. `Pipeline::child_done` never runs for that member, so its node and its `IO` (the read end of the pipe from the previous member) are never released. The members after it are never started, and their nodes hold their pipe ends too.
- Nothing closes those pipe ends or signals the members that already started.
- With #42251 the interpreter of a failed pipeline also stays alive until the VM exits. The pending-activity count is kept on purpose while a `Pipeline` node is live, because a running member's process, pipe, and thread-pool callbacks still point into the interpreter. An earlier attempt with a narrower check (#33996) hit a use-after-free on `ls * | cmd < ${stream}`.

### What a fix needs

- Know which node failed (`Yield::Failed` carries no node today).
- For each pipeline above the failed node: release the failed member and the members that did not start, so that their pipe ends close. The members that run then see EPIPE or EOF and finish through the normal path.
- Kill or detach started subprocess members that do not read or write the pipe (`sleep 100 | bad > ${blob}` keeps the process open for 100 s).
- Release the pending-activity count only when no member can call back any more. This includes builtins with tasks on the thread pool.

title: Performance difference for character-concatenated strings in irregular arrays
excerpt:
I am an AI model assisting with this performance investigation; this report and reproduction were prepared with human direction and should be independently verified.

---

The attached dependency-free script shows a repeatable performance difference between Node.js and Bun for one data shape: strings rebuilt character by character, stored in irregular arrays of objects, then used by `Array.prototype.map().join()` and nested equality checks.

The flat-string control is close between runtimes. Manual string concatenation is also close. This report is limited to the included workload and does not claim a general Bun or Node performance ranking.

## Reproduction

Save [`repro.mjs`](https://gist.github.com/shi-gg/067661a5cb2f61da51f894d10ff8a0ae), then run the same file with both runtimes:

```sh
node --version
bun --version
node repro.mjs
bun repro.mjs
```

The default run is deterministic and uses 20,000 records with 2–32 stops per record, 16 station queries, two warmup rounds, and five measured rounds. The script validates that the flat and character-concatenated cases produce identical results.

For a larger run:

```sh
RECORDS=44876 MAX_STOPS=62 QUERIES=32 ROUNDS=10 WARMUP=3 node repro.mjs
RECORDS=44876 MAX_STOPS=62 QUERIES=32 ROUNDS=10 WARMUP=3 bun repro.mjs
```

## Representative result

On Linux x64 with Node v26.8.2 and Bun 1.4.2, one quiet sample produced these representative values:

| Runtime | Flat `routeMapJoin` | Character-concatenated `routeMapJoin` | Character-concatenated nested scan |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Node 26.8.2 | 12.131 ms | 9.291 ms | 96.944 ms |
| Bun 1.4.2 | 11.256 ms | 46.968 ms | 139.605 ms |

The manual-concatenation control was 8.965 ms for Node and 11.904 ms for Bun in that sample. Exact timings vary with CPU, OS, runtime build, process contention, and thermal state; the raw JSON output is the evidence to attach to an issue. The intended claim is the direction of the isolated difference, not these exact numbers.

## Question

Is this expected JavaScriptCore/Bun behavior for character-concatenated strings used in irregular object arrays, `map().join()`, and nested string equality checks? If it is a known limitation or regression, which string representation or optimization explains the difference?

title: --splitting: chunks import from the entry chunk, breaking entry URLs versioned with a query string
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.1 and 1.4.2 (works correctly on 1.4.0)

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Since 1.4.1, chunks emitted with `--splitting` import shared bindings from the entry chunk instead of from a separate hashed chunk:

```js
// Route1-qjwr1323.js
import{e,t}from"./index.js";   // <-- the entry
```

The entry is exactly the file a server-side framework versions for cache busting by appending a query string (ASP.NET's asp-append-version, Rails, Django, WordPress all do this). The chunks import it as ./index.js, without the query, so the browser sees two different URLs for the same file:

/dist/index.js?v=<hash> — from the <script> tag rendered by the server
/dist/index.js — because the lazy chunks import it

The ES module map is keyed on the full URL including the query, so the bundle is fetched and instantiated twice. Resource timing confirms it (same 411818 bytes, twice). Every library with singleton state gets duplicated: with React this shows up as Invalid hook call, or removeChild failing because two roots render into the same container. Removing just the query string makes it work; the same sources built with 1.4.0 work with the query string in place.


### What is the expected behavior?

Could the shared code stay in a separate hashed chunk, as it did before 1.4.1 — at least behind an opt-out flag? Hashed chunk names never carry a query, so that layout keeps one URL per module and lets hosts keep versioning the entry as they always have. We would rather not have to drop query-string versioning (or disable --splitting, which costs us route-level lazy loading) to stay on current versions.

### What do you see instead?

title: bun:test: a String object with 16-bit storage prints wrong characters in diffs and snapshots
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+4ff919377

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun:test` prints wrong characters for a `String` object when the string has 16-bit storage. This is every string with a character above U+00FF.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("String object with non-Latin-1 text", () => {
  expect(new String("日本")).toEqual(0);
});
```

The same output goes into `toMatchSnapshot` and `toMatchInlineSnapshot`.

### What is the expected behavior?

```
- 0
+ String {
+   "0": "日",
+   "1": "本",
+ }
```

### What do you see instead?

A release build prints the first bytes of the UTF-16 buffer as Latin-1 characters:

```
- 0
+ String {
+   "0": "å",
+   "1": "e",
+ }
```

A debug build panics:

```
panic: EncodedSlice::slice() on UTF-16; use to_utf8()
```

### Additional information

- The cause is the `StringObject` / `DerivedStringObject` arm of `Tag::String` in `src/runtime/test_runner/pretty_format.rs`. The loop is `for (i, c) in str.slice().iter().enumerate()`. `str` is an `EncodedSlice`, and `slice()` is its 8-bit view. For a string with 16-bit storage it reads `len` bytes of the UTF-16 buffer.
- An ASCII-only string with 16-bit storage hits the same path, for example `new String(new TextDecoder("utf-16le").decode(new Uint16Array([0x61, 0x62])))`.
- Fix direction: read each code unit with `EncodedSlice::char_at(i)`, which handles both widths.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

Reproduced on `1.4.0+34cbb9a40` and the latest release, `1.4.2+744846f84`.

### What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm` (Apple M4).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Save this as `repro.cjs` and run `bun repro.cjs`:

```js
const vm = require('node:vm');
const context = vm.createContext(vm.constants.DONT_CONTEXTIFY);
const vmGlobal = vm.runInContext('this', context);
Object.setPrototypeOf(vmGlobal, Object.create(new Proxy({}, {})));
console.log(vm.runInContext('1 + 1', context));
```

This reproduction has no dependencies and uses no worker threads.

### What is the expected behavior?

Print `2`, as Node.js 24.9.0 does.

### What do you see instead?

The final `vm.runInContext` throws:

```text
TypeError: Proxy is not allowed in the global prototype chain.
```

### Additional information

This blocks Vitest 5.0.0 with `pool: 'vmThreads'` and jsdom 28.1.0 under Bun. jsdom constructs a window prototype chain containing a Proxy, and Vitest fails while evaluating its Vite client stub, before tests execute.

A jsdom-only reproduction is:

```js
const vm = require('node:vm');
const { JSDOM } = require('jsdom');
const dom = new JSDOM('', { runScripts: 'outside-only' });
console.log(vm.runInContext('1 + 1', dom.getInternalVMContext()));
```

Both Bun versions also fail with `BUN_JSC_useFTLJIT=0`. Bun 1.4.0 still fails with `BUN_JSC_useJIT=0`, so disabling JIT does not avoid this error.

JavaScriptCore's `ProgramExecutable::initializeGlobalProperties` contains the check that emits this exact error:
https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/ProgramExecutable.cpp#L95-L100

Related: #4145. This is a JavaScript exception, not the older segfault reported in #16415. I also found #34623 and #39588, but have not tested whether either fixes this case.

title: WebView (WebKit backend): navigate() to a #fragment of the current page never settles, and view.url goes stale after a same-document navigation
excerpt:
### What happens

This is the WebKit-backend side of #42162, which fixes the same gap for the Chrome backend. It comes from reading the code. I have not run it on macOS.

1. `await view.navigate(view.url + "#section")` is expected to never settle on the WebKit backend. The navigate slot stays full, so every later `navigate()` throws `Invalid state: a navigation is already pending`.
2. After any same-document navigation (a `#fragment` link, `history.pushState()`, `history.replaceState()`, or `goBack()`/`goForward()` between two such entries), `view.url` keeps the old URL and `onNavigated` does not fire.

`goBack()`, `goForward()` and `reload()` do not hang on WebKit. The host acknowledges them at once and does not wait for the navigation (`WebViewHost.cpp:652-660`, and the comment at `WebViewHost.cpp:700`). So only point 2 applies to them.

### Why

- `WebViewHost::navigate` sets `m_navPending` (`src/runtime/webview/WebViewHost.cpp:244`). `NavDone`, which resolves the promise, is sent only from `WebViewHost::onNavigationFinished`, and `NavEvent`, which updates `view.url`/`view.title` and runs `onNavigated`, is sent only from there too.
- `onNavigationFinished` runs from `webView:didFinishNavigation:`. `BunWKNavigationDelegate` registers `webView:didFinishNavigation:`, `webView:didFailNavigation:withError:` and `webView:didFailProvisionalNavigation:withError:` and nothing else for navigation (`src/runtime/webview/ObjCRuntime.cpp:524-534`).
- WebKit does not call `didFinishNavigation` for a navigation that stays in the document. It reports it through `_webView:navigation:didSameDocumentNavigation:`.

### What would fix it

Register `_webView:navigation:didSameDocumentNavigation:` on `BunWKNavigationDelegate` and route it through the existing `NavEvent`/`NavDone` path, the way `onNavigationFinished` does. WebKit checks `respondsToSelector:` for it, like it does for `_webView:getContextMenuFromProposedMenu:...`, which the delegate already adopts.

A test needs macOS: `test/js/bun/webview/webview.test.ts` runs the WebKit backend there.

`docs/runtime/webview.mdx` scopes its two sentences about same-document navigations to the Chrome backend because of this gap. They can lose that scope once this is fixed.

bun test reports a failing beforeAll as "a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out"
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (also reproduces on 1.3.14)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (also observed on ubuntu-24.04 GitHub Actions runners)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A `beforeAll` hook that exceeds its timeout is reported as a **`beforeEach`/`afterEach`** timeout, in a file containing neither.

```ts
// repro.test.ts
import { beforeAll, expect, it } from "bun:test";

beforeAll(async () => {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
}, 50);

it("runs", () => {
  expect(1).toBe(1);
});
```

```
bun test repro.test.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The message should name the hook that actually timed out, e.g.

```
(fail) beforeAll [51.21ms]
  ^ a beforeAll hook timed out for this test.
```

### What do you see instead?

```
(fail) (unnamed) [52.09ms]
  ^ a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test.
```

There is no `beforeEach` and no `afterEach` anywhere in the file.

### Additional information

The same wording appears for `afterAll`.

Why it matters beyond cosmetics: the message sends the reader to a construct the
file may not contain. We hit this on a CI integration suite that has only
`beforeAll` and `afterAll`. Taking the message at face value, the natural next
step is to look for a per-test hook, fail to find one, and conclude something
stranger is happening — which is what occurred, twice, and produced a wrong
working hypothesis about resource contention before a minimal repro settled it.
The real cause was a `beforeAll` running under the 5000ms default while its body
performed a database call whose own bound was 60s.

The string appears to originate in `src/runtime/cli/test_command.rs`, and is
still present on the default branch at the time of filing.

Happy to open a PR if a maintainer confirms the preferred wording (e.g. whether
to name the specific hook kind, or to say "a lifecycle hook").

title: [1.4.2 regression] Compiled binary (--compile) fails to resolve CJS require of a dependency inside an --external package (works on 1.3.2)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (744846f84), Linux x64. Also reproduced with 1.4.2-alpine layouts.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64 (Debian and Alpine/musl Docker images)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{"name":"repro","dependencies":{"inngest":"3.54.0"}}' > package.json
bun install
printf 'const i = require("inngest");\nconsole.log("inngest loaded:", typeof i.Inngest);\n' > t.cjs
bun build --compile --external inngest --outfile t t.cjs
./t
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The binary boots and prints `inngest loaded: function` — as the **1.3.2-compiled** binary does against the *identical* `node_modules` (verified side by side: same directory, `bun build --compile --external inngest` with 1.3.2 works, with 1.4.2 fails).

### What do you see instead?

```
error: Cannot find package 'chalk' from '/tmp/repro-inngest/node_modules/inngest/helpers/consts.cjs'
```

(exit code 1)

### Additional information

- `chalk@4.1.2` is installed correctly (plain flat `node_modules/chalk`, resolvable by node, by `bun run` source mode, and by the 1.3.2 compiled runtime). The regression is specific to the **1.4.x `--compile` runtime resolving a CJS `require()` inside an `--external` package**.
- Also reproduces in a monorepo with bun's `.bun` store layout (package symlinked into `node_modules/.bun/inngest@3.54.0+<hash>/node_modules/inngest`), where `chalk` is correctly linked at `.bun/inngest@.../node_modules/chalk` — node resolves it there, the 1.4.2 compiled runtime does not.
- Not fixed by: `NODE_PATH` pointing at the app's `node_modules`, `--external chalk`, `--linker hoisted`, or regenerating the lockfile from scratch with 1.4.2.
- Bundling `inngest` instead of externalizing it is not a usable workaround in our case: the bundle eagerly evaluates a top-level `require("@vercel/oidc")` (an optional peer that is not installed) and fails at startup with `Cannot find module '@vercel/oidc' from '/$bunfs/root/<binary>'`.
- Real-world impact: any app that ships a `bun build --compile --external inngest` production binary (e.g. an Inngest workflow service) cannot boot on 1.4.x.

test(pm): add regression coverage for frozen lockfile consistency
excerpt:
# test(pm): add regression coverage for frozen lockfile consistency

Several issues have reported cases where Bun generates or updates a `bun.lock` that is then rejected by `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, including #36577, #37346, and #31748.

Rather than adding another reproduction of the same failure mode, I think it would be useful to add regression coverage for the underlying invariant.

For an unchanged dependency graph:

```text
bun install
    ↓
bun.lock
    ↓
bun install --frozen-lockfile
    ↓
same dependency graph
```

A lockfile successfully produced by Bun should be accepted by the frozen resolver without requiring any changes.

The test coverage could exercise this across cases that are likely to stress the resolver/lockfile boundary:

* multiple versions of the same transitive dependency
* peer dependencies
* optional dependencies
* platform-specific dependencies
* workspaces
* `bun update`
* `--lockfile-only`
* repeated installs

The core invariant is:

```text
resolve(manifest)
    ==
resolve(manifest, generated_lockfile, frozen=true)
```

This would complement the existing bug reports by turning the recurring failure mode into explicit package-manager regression coverage.

It should also help prevent future changes to dependency resolution, deduplication, peer handling, or lockfile serialization from reintroducing the same class of issue.

References:

* #36577
* #37346
* #31748

title: socket.setTimeout() never fires while the socket is still connecting if a write was queued
socket.setTimeout() never fires when the peer stops reading and the write queue stalls
excerpt:
## What version of Bun is running?

`1.4.2+744846f84`. Also reproduced on a debug build of `main` (`1.4.3-debug`, 4b5862fd8).

## What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 25.5.0 arm64` (macOS 26.5).

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

If a connected peer stops reading, the write queue stops draining and `socket.setTimeout()` never fires — so the one condition the timeout exists to surface is the one it cannot report.

```js
import net from 'node:net'

const server = net.createServer(sock => sock.pause())   // accept, never read
await new Promise(r => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', r))

const sock = net.connect({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: server.address().port })
sock.on('error', () => {})
await new Promise(r => sock.once('connect', r))

const chunk = Buffer.alloc(1 << 20, 'x')
for (let i = 0; i < 64; i++) sock.write(chunk)   // fill the queue

sock.setTimeout(1000)
const t0 = Date.now()
sock.on('timeout', () => console.log(`timeout @${Date.now() - t0}ms`))
setTimeout(() => console.log(`still nothing @5000ms, bufferSize=${sock.bufferSize}`), 5000)
```

| | result | bufferSize |
|---|---|---|
| bun 1.4.2 | **never fires** | 66060288 |
| node 25.3.0 | `timeout @2001ms` | 66060288 |

## What is the expected behavior?

`timeout` fires once the write queue stops making progress, as node does — after two idle periods (one tick to observe the size, one to see it unchanged).

## What do you see instead?

Nothing, ever. `Socket.prototype._onTimeout` (`src/js/node/net.ts`) suppresses on any non-empty queue:

```js
const handle = this._handle;
// if there is a handle, and it has pending data,
// we suppress the timeout because a write is in progress
if (handle && getBufferedAmount(handle) > 0) {
  return;
}
this.emit("timeout");
```

Two problems. A non-empty queue is not the same as a write *in progress* — a stalled peer also leaves bytes queued. And `this[kTimeout]` is one-shot:

```js
this[kTimeout] = setTimeout(this._onTimeout.bind(this), msecs).unref();
```

so returning without `this._unrefTimer()` consumes the timer permanently; no later tick ever runs, even if the queue later drains or stalls.

node compares against the previous tick's queue size, records the new value, and calls `_unrefTimer()` to reschedule — suppressing only while the queue is genuinely moving.

Worth noting the healthy path is correct on both today: with a peer reading steadily, neither bun nor node times out during a large write. Any fix needs to keep that.

## Additional information

install: the isolated linker ignores --concurrent-scripts and [install] concurrentScripts
excerpt:
### What happens

`--concurrent-scripts` and `[install] concurrentScripts` set how many packages can run their lifecycle scripts at the same time. The limit applies with the hoisted linker only. With the isolated linker, `bun install` starts each script as soon as its package is ready.

```sh
d=$(mktemp -d); cd "$d"
for i in 1 2 3; do mkdir dep$i; echo "{\"name\":\"dep$i\",\"version\":\"1.0.0\",\"scripts\":{\"postinstall\":\"sleep 1\"}}" > dep$i/package.json; done
echo '{"name":"app","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"dep1":"file:./dep1","dep2":"file:./dep2","dep3":"file:./dep3"},"trustedDependencies":["dep1","dep2","dep3"]}' > package.json
bun install --linker=isolated --concurrent-scripts=1   # 3 packages installed [1006.00ms]
rm -rf node_modules bun.lock
bun install --linker=hoisted --concurrent-scripts=1    # 3 packages installed [3.01s]
```

bun 1.4.3-canary.1 (6a92015fc), Linux x64. With a limit of 1, the three `sleep 1` scripts must take about 3 s.

### Why

- The hoisted installer compares `LifecycleScriptSubprocess::alive_count()` with `options.max_concurrent_lifecycle_scripts` before it spawns a script (`can_run_scripts` and `complete_remaining_scripts` in `src/install/PackageInstaller.rs`). `bun pm trust` has the same check (`src/runtime/cli/pm_trusted_command.rs`).
- The isolated installer has no check. `run_tasks` handles `store_installer::Result::RunScripts` with a direct call to `spawn_package_lifecycle_scripts` (`src/install/PackageManager/runTasks.rs:380`). The comments at the `ALIVE_COUNT` updates in `src/install/lifecycle_script_runner.rs` say "this value is only used by hoisted installs".
- The docs (`docs/pm/cli/install.mdx`, `docs/runtime/bunfig.mdx`) describe the limit and do not mention the linker. The isolated linker is the default for a new project with workspaces.

### What a fix needs

- The isolated installer must hold a `RunScripts` result while `alive_count() >= max_concurrent_lifecycle_scripts`, and start it when a script exits.
- Or the docs must say that the limit applies to the hoisted linker only.

Found during the fix that lets `--concurrent-scripts` override `[install] concurrentScripts`. That fix does not change this.

bundler: wrapper folds drop `(0, x.f)()` for CommonJS import items, `exports.f`, template tags and one ternary path
excerpt:
`bun build` can drop a wrapper whose only effect is to call a function without `this`. The call then passes an object as `this`. #42402 fixes the shapes that #41186 broke in 1.4.1 (an item of a `require()` / `import()` local). The shapes below are wrong on 1.4.0 too, so they are not part of that regression. This issue tracks them.

All outputs are from `bun build ./entry --target=bun` on 1.4.0 and on 1.4.3-canary.1 (same result), and from node 26.3.0 on the source.

```js
// util.cjs
"use strict";
exports.tag = "exports";
exports.who = function () { return this === undefined ? "undefined" : this.tag; };
Object.defineProperty(exports, "lazy", { enumerable: true, get() { return 1; } });
```

The getter keeps the module in its `__commonJS` wrapper. A module that the bundler can lift to ESM binds `who` to a plain function, and the calls below are then correct.

### 1. A named or star import of a CommonJS module

```js
import * as ns from "./util.cjs";
import { who } from "./util.cjs";
console.log((0, ns.who)(), (true ? ns.who : 0)(), (1 && ns.who)(), who(), (0, who)());
```

- Expected (ESM semantics): `undefined` five times.
- No flags: `undefined exports exports exports undefined`. `who()` prints as `import_util.who()`, and the two folds drop the wrapper.
- `--minify-syntax`: `exports` five times.

### 2. `exports.f` inside a CommonJS module (`ECommonjsExportIdentifier`)

```js
// entry.cjs, same body as util.cjs, then:
console.log((0, exports.who)(), (true ? exports.who : 0)(), (1 && exports.who)());
```

- node: `undefined undefined undefined`.
- No flags: `undefined exports exports`.
- `--minify-syntax`: `exports exports exports`.

### 3. `require()` of a package on the unwrap list

1.4.2+744846f84. Same output on 1.4.3-canary.1+4ff919377.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (macOS, Apple Silicon).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`:target-current`, `:target-before` and `:target-after` are the css-overflow-5

table entry for them, so each parses as `PseudoClass::Custom` and is emitted as
whatever bytes it arrived as, while `:target-within`, which sits next to them in
the same spec family and IS in the table, gets normalized.

```css

.a:TARGET-CURRENT{color:red}
.b:TARGET-WITHIN{color:red}
.c:TARGET-BEFORE{color:red}
.d:TARGET-AFTER{color:red}
.e:target-current{color:red}
```

```
$ bun build ./in.css --minify --outdir=out && cat out/in.css
.a:TARGET-CURRENT{color:red}.b:target-within{color:red}.c:TARGET-BEFORE{color:red}.d:TARGET-AFTER{color:red}.e:target-current{color:red}
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Pseudo-class names are ASCII case-insensitive, so `.a:TARGET-CURRENT` and
`.e:target-current` are one selector spelled two ways. A minifier that knows

`:TARGET-WITHIN` on the line between them.

Two things, and the second is the one with a byte cost.

**The casing survives verbatim** for the three unknown names and is normalized

.x:target-current{color:red}

```

minifier fidelity rather than a rendering bug.

the upstream `-` rule, which is the right change. The day it lands, all three of
these names start printing `Invalid selector. Unsupported pseudo-class or

title: fetch and Request silently turn an unrecognised HTTP method into GET
excerpt:
An HTTP method that Bun does not recognise is silently replaced with `GET`, instead of being kept as sent.

```js
new Request('http://x/', { method: 'custom' }).method  // "GET",   node: "custom"
new Request('http://x/', { method: 'PatCh' }).method   // "GET",   node: "PatCh"
```

It is not only the `Request` constructor. The method actually sent on the wire changes too:

```js
const server = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: (req) => new Response(req.method) })
const url = `http://localhost:${server.port}/`

await (await fetch(url, { method: 'PATCH'  })).text()   // "PATCH"
await (await fetch(url, { method: 'PURGE'  })).text()   // "PURGE"
await (await fetch(url, { method: 'PatCh'  })).text()   // "GET"     <-
await (await fetch(url, { method: 'custom' })).text()   // "GET"     <-
```

### What is affected

Uppercase methods Bun knows are fine, including extension methods:

| method | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET` `POST` `PUT` `DELETE` `HEAD` `OPTIONS` `PATCH` `TRACE` `CONNECT` | unchanged |
| `PURGE` `LOCK` `MKCOL` `REPORT` `QUERY` | unchanged |
| `patch` | `PATCH` |
| `PatCh` | **`GET`** |
| `custom` | **`GET`** |

So it is any token that does not match Bun's known-method table, whatever the case.

### Expected

Per the Fetch spec, the method is uppercased only when it is a byte case-insensitive match for `DELETE`, `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `POST` or `PUT`. Any other valid method token is kept as written, and an invalid token throws a `TypeError`. Node keeps `PatCh`, `custom` and `chicken` unchanged.

Falling back to `GET` is the part that worries me. A request meant as a custom verb becomes a read, with no error anywhere. WebDAV style APIs and any proxy that forwards the incoming method get it wrong silently, and a method based authorisation check can end up seeing a different method than the client sent.

### Version

```
bun 1.4.0+34cbb9a40
win32 x64 10.0.26200
```

Node 22.18.0 used for the comparison.

title: Request and Response constructors skip several validations the Fetch spec requires
excerpt:
Several validations the Fetch spec requires are missing from the `Request` and `Response` constructors. In each case Node throws and Bun accepts the value.

```js
new Request('http://x/', { method: 'GET', body: 'x' })   // node: TypeError   bun: accepted
new Response('x', { status: 204 })                       // node: TypeError   bun: accepted
new Response(null, { statusText: 'a\r\nb' })             // node: TypeError   bun: kept as-is
new Request('http://x/', { method: 'CONNECT' })          // node: TypeError   bun: "CONNECT"
```

Full comparison, bun 1.4.0 against node 22.18.0:

| case | node | bun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Request` GET + body | TypeError | accepted |
| `Request` HEAD + body | TypeError | accepted |
| `Response` 101 + body | RangeError | accepted |
| `Response` 204 + body | TypeError | accepted |
| `Response` 205 + body | TypeError | accepted |
| `Response` 304 + body | TypeError | accepted |
| `statusText` containing CR LF | TypeError | kept as-is |
| `statusText` containing LF | TypeError | kept as-is |
| `statusText` containing NUL | TypeError | kept as-is |
| forbidden method `CONNECT` | TypeError | `"CONNECT"` |
| forbidden method `TRACE` | TypeError | `"TRACE"` |

`status` range checking is already correct, `0` and `600` both throw `RangeError` in both runtimes.

### Expected

Per the Fetch spec:

- `Request`: if the method is `GET` or `HEAD` and body is non-null, throw a `TypeError`.
- `Request`: if the method is a forbidden method (`CONNECT`, `TRACE`, `TRACK`), throw a `TypeError`.
- `Response`: if body is non-null and the status is a null body status (101, 103, 204, 205, 304), throw a `TypeError`.
- `Response`: if `statusText` does not match the `reason-phrase` production, throw a `TypeError`.

### Why it matters

It is a portability trap rather than a hole. Code written against Bun that relies on the lenient behaviour breaks when it runs on Node, in a browser, or on Workers, and code that expects the constructor to reject bad input as a guard never gets the error.

I checked whether the `statusText` newline can reach the socket, and it cannot. `Bun.serve` strips it, the status line comes back as a plain `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, so there is no response splitting here. It is the constructor validation that is missing, not the serialiser.

`TRACK` and an invalid token such as `'GE T'` also come back as `GET`, which is the separate silent fallback in #42497.

### Version

```
bun 1.4.0+34cbb9a40
win32 x64 10.0.26200
```

CommonMark 0.31.2 says that links may not contain other links (section 6.3, "Links"). commonmark.js 0.31.2 and cmark 0.31.1 do not make the outer link. The same happens in `Bun.markdown.render()`, `Bun.markdown.react()` and `Bun.markdown.ansi()`, because they share the parser. ### Reproduction ```js for (const s of [ "[[x [a](/i) y] z](/u)\n", "[x [y [a](/i)] z](/u)\n", "[a]: /url\n\n[[x [a] y] z](/u)\n", "[![x [a](/i) y](/img) z](/u)\n", ]) console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(Bun.markdown.html(s))); ``` bun 1.4.3 and main (b99371011f) print: ``` "[[x [a](/i) y] z](/u)\n" -> "

[x a y] z

\n" "[x [y [a](/i)] z](/u)\n" -> "

x [y a] z

\n" "[a]: /url\n\n[[x [a] y] z](/u)\n" -> "

[x a y] z

\n" "[![x [a](/i) y](/img) z](/u)\n" -> "

z

\n" ``` Expected. commonmark.js 0.31.2 and cmark 0.31.1 agree on all four: ```

[[x a y] z](/u)

[x [y a] z](/u)

[[x a y] z](/u)

[ z](/u)

``` Controls that are already correct: `[[a](/i)](/u)` and `[x [a](/i) y](/u)`. For each `[` in the label it calls `try_match_bracket_link`. If that bracket pair is not a link, `try_match_bracket_link` returns `is_link: false` with `link_end = label_end + 1`, and the loop then runs: ```rust if inner.link_end > pos { // Skip past entire construct (including (url) or [ref] for images) pos = inner.link_end; continue; } ``` That jumps over the whole bracket pair, so the scan never sees a link that is nested inside it. A link inside the alt text of an image must also stop the outer link. cmark deactivates every earlier `[` opener when the inner link forms. So for an inner image the function must still look inside the alt

title: Error.stackTraceLimit is 100 in a node:vm context (Node: 10, or the --stack-trace-limit value)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+b99371011 (also main at f04caca828)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// stl.js
const vm = require("node:vm");
console.log("main:", Error.stackTraceLimit, "vm:", vm.runInNewContext("Error.stackTraceLimit"));
function deep(n) {
  return n === 0 ? vm.runInNewContext("new Error().stack.split('\\n').length - 1") : deep(n - 1);
}
console.log("frames:", deep(40));
```

Run it with and without `--stack-trace-limit=50`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Node v26.3.0:

```
$ node stl.js
main: 10 vm: 10
frames: 10
$ node --stack-trace-limit=50 stl.js
main: 50 vm: 50
frames: 50
```

A new `node:vm` context starts with the process default for `Error.stackTraceLimit`. The default is 10, or the value of `--stack-trace-limit`.

### What do you see instead?

```
$ bun stl.js
main: 10 vm: 100
frames: 44
$ bun --stack-trace-limit=50 stl.js
main: 50 vm: 100
frames: 44
```

`Error.stackTraceLimit` is 100 in every `node:vm` context. Errors made in the context, and `Error.captureStackTrace` calls in the context, keep up to 100 frames.

### Additional information

The cause is in two places.

- `Zig::GlobalObject::finishCreation` (`src/jsc/bindings/ZigGlobalObject.cpp`) calls `setStackTraceLimit(DEFAULT_ERROR_STACK_TRACE_LIMIT)` (10) before the Error constructor exists. `NodeVMGlobalObject::finishCreation` (`src/jsc/bindings/NodeVM.cpp`) does not. So a vm global keeps JSC's `Options::defaultErrorStackTraceLimit()`, which is 100.
- `--stack-trace-limit` is applied in JS, in `src/js/internal/process/pre_execution.ts`, with `Error.stackTraceLimit = limit` on the realm that runs the bootstrap (the main thread and each worker). A vm context does not run it. No process-level value exists for a new realm to read.

A hard-coded 10 in `NodeVMGlobalObject` fixes the default case. It does not fix the `--stack-trace-limit` case. A process-level seed that every new realm reads at creation fixes the two cases.

Found while working on `Error.captureStackTrace` inside a `node:vm` context. That fix does not touch this default.

title: URLPattern: pattern shapes that take super-linear time to match
excerpt:
`URLPattern` compiles each component (hostname, pathname, ...) to one regexp and runs it with YARR, a backtracking matcher. For some pattern shapes the matcher tries the same text in many ways. The time then grows faster than the input, on an input that does not match or that matches late. YARR ends a match when its match limit (`Yarr::matchLimit`) runs out and reports no match. So for the exponential shapes an input that matches can also return `null`.

This issue lists the shapes in one place. Each row has an example, the time on stock bun 1.4.3 (release, linux x64), and the state.

| shape | example | time | state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| repeated wildcard | `**.example.com`, `:sub+.example.com`, `/**/x.js` | exponential, 0.7 s at 28 characters | #42606 |
| several named groups in one segment | `/:owner-:repo-:ref` | O(n^k), 3.3 s at 4 KB | #42535 |
| repeated named group with a prefix or suffix that has no delimiter | `/:first{-:rest}*/edit`, `/files/:name{.:ext}+`, `{:kv&}+end` (search) | exponential, 0.55 s at 24 repeats | open |
| named group next to an optional or repeated named group | `/:a-:b?-:c`, `/:a{-:b}?{-:c}?` | O(n^k), 0.43 s at 2 KB | open |
| separator of two or more characters between named groups | `/:a--:b--:c` | O(n^k), 0.60 s at 3 KB | open |
| several full wildcards | `/*/a/*/b/*/c` | O(n^k), 1.1 s at 4 KB | open |
| repeated custom regexp group | `(.+)+` | exponential | the regexp of the author |

Repro for an open row:

```js
const pattern = new URLPattern({ pathname: "/files/:name{.:ext}+" });
const input = { pathname: "/files/a" + ".b".repeat(24) + "/" };
console.time("test");
pattern.test(input); // false, after 0.55 s. 26 repeats: 1.2 s.
console.timeEnd("test");

// An input that matches, but the result is null:
new URLPattern({ search: "{-:x}+-_:r" }).exec({ search: "-a-_" + "-b".repeat(30) }); // null
```

Notes:

- The regexps come from the spec's "generate a regular expression and name list" algorithm. Node 26 and upstream WebKit generate the same ones. Node has no match limit, so the same inputs take minutes there.
- whatwg/urlpattern#237 reports the `**` case. The spec editor proposed there to drop the modifier of a repeated full wildcard.
- The first two rows have an exact rewrite: a regexp with the same matches and groups that has no ambiguity. The open rows do not have a simple one. For `{-:x}+` a rewrite with lookaheads exists. But YARR runs a group inside a loop about 200 times slower than a plain character cl

title: os.cpus() times on FreeBSD are in kernel ticks, 7 times below Node
excerpt:
### What happens

On FreeBSD, the `times` values of `os.cpus()` are in kernel ticks. Node returns milliseconds. The Bun values are 7 times below the Node values.

### Cause

`cpus_impl_freebsd` (`src/runtime/node/node_os.rs:457-463`) multiplies each counter of `kern.cp_times` by `1000 / sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)`. It gets the tick rate from `bun_sysconf__SC_CLK_TCK()` (`src/jsc/bindings/c-bindings.cpp:90-97`):

```cpp
extern "C" ssize_t bun_sysconf__SC_CLK_TCK()
{
#ifdef __APPLE__
    return sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK);
#else
    return 0;
#endif
}
```

Off macOS it returns 0. The Rust side then takes the `else { 1 }` arm, so the multiplier is 1. libuv `uv_cpu_info` uses `1000 / sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)`, which is `1000 / 128 = 7` on FreeBSD ([`freebsd.c`](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/096a02d14cb9d3de6d55a29ec02c4dfcb7643c7f/src/unix/freebsd.c#L183-L185)).

### Evidence

FreeBSD 14.3, 4 vCPUs, Bun `1.4.3-canary.1+f04caca82` ([run 34767811136](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/actions/runs/34767811136)). The kernel counters for CPU 0 and the Bun result are the same numbers:

```
kern.cp_times before: 13 0 175 28 692 ...
cpu 0 {"user":14,"nice":0,"sys":176,"idle":692,"irq":28}
kern.cp_times after:  14 0 176 28 692 ...
```

Node gives `user: 98` for the same counter.

### Possible fix

Return `sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)` on FreeBSD too (`#if defined(__APPLE__) || defined(__FreeBSD__)`), and remove the `else { 1 }` arm that then has no caller. A FreeBSD VM run can check it: the sum of the `times` of one CPU divided by `os.uptime() * 1000` is near 1.

Found during the work on #42633. That PR does not change this.

title: Script-sized containers that still abort the process when they cannot grow: the microtask queue and the web streams request queues
excerpt:
Some containers that grow with script input still call `CRASH()` when they cannot grow. The process exits with `panic(main thread): abort() called` (SIGABRT, exit 134), and script cannot catch it. A fuzzing run found them. No user has reported one.

This issue is the inventory of the sites that the first revision of the streams fix in #42649 left as they were.

**Update:** #42659 fixed the web streams rows below and was merged into the #42649 branch. The `m_writeRequests` row needs no change, because the value queue of the same stream fills first. What remains is the JSC microtask queue and the follow-up list at the end. Each row gives the cost to reach the limit on a release build of `main` (f04caca828, linux x64).

### JSC microtask queue

```js
const p = Promise.resolve();
const noop = () => {};
for (let i = 0; i < 33554432; i++) p.then(noop);
```

- Aborts at the 33,554,432nd pending job, after 3 s at 2.3 GB RSS. 33,000,000 jobs drain without an error.
- Bun 1.3.14 aborts in the same way, so this one is not a regression.
- The queue is a `WTF::Deque`. Its capacity is a power of two, and `Deque::append` calls `CRASH()` when the next capacity is not valid for a `Vector`.
- A `WritableStream` reaches it too. When a stream with 2^25 or more pending `writer.write()` promises errors, `writableStreamFinishErroring` (`WritableStreamOperations.cpp:340`) rejects them in one loop. Each promise that has a reaction queues one job.

### Web streams queues that need 8 GB or more

| Site | Entry | Limit | Cost per entry | RSS at the limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Byte stream queue, `JSReadableByteStreamController.cpp:770` (`StreamQueue::append`) | 24 bytes | 67,108,863 | 136 bytes (each entry owns a transferred `ArrayBuffer`) | 8.5 GB |
| `m_readRequests`, `ReadableStreamOperations.cpp:203` | 8 bytes | 134,217,727 | 81 bytes (a request cell and a promise) | 10.2 GB |
| `m_readIntoRequests` (`ReadableStreamOperations.cpp:213`) and `m_pendingPullIntos` (`JSReadableByteStreamController.cpp:404`, `:1018`, `:1045`) | 8 bytes | 134,217,727 | 337 bytes (a BYOB `read(view)` adds one entry to each and transfers the buffer of the view) | 42.1 GB |
| `m_writeRequests`, `WritableStreamOperations.cpp:264` | 8 bytes | 134,217,727 | the value queue of the same stream fills first, at 67,108,862 writes | not reachable first |

- All of them are `WTF::Deque`s. They abort in `Deque::expandCapacity` when they are full.
- They are deterministic once a script can pay the memory.

title: abort() after 8.8 days in a standalone executable: Commit 28 GB with RSS 0.6 GB (4.4k spawns, idle-heavy)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0 (34cbb9a40), embedded in a standalone executable (`bun build --compile`)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.18.1-061801-generic x86_64, glibc 2.35 (Ubuntu), 24 cores / 67 GB RAM, `vm.overcommit_memory=0`

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Not a minimal repro yet — this is a field crash from a long-lived interactive agent process (the `loom` coding agent, a standalone Bun executable). Characteristics at the time of the abort:

- Elapsed **759,575,421 ms (8.8 days)** in one process; user CPU 3,625 s.
- **RSS 0.60 GB, peak 1.0 GB, but Commit 28.23 GB** (`Faults: 346606`). A sibling process of the same shape reached **VSZ 43 GB** with RSS ~0.7 GB; at that size `fork()` from the process fails with ENOMEM under heuristic overcommit (RAM+swap free ≈ 42 GB), which is how we first noticed the growth.
- Features: `spawn(4473)` — thousands of `Bun.spawn` children over the process lifetime — `fetch(1105)`, `abort_signal(266)`, `WebSocket(2)`, `http_server`, `shell(8)`, `process_dlopen(2)` (two N-API addons), `transpiler_cache(16)`, `virtual_modules(35)`, `yaml_parse(61)`, `bun:sqlite`.
- The process is mostly idle between LLM turns, with periodic timers.

Crash report (redacted, sent): https://bun.report/1.4.0/l_134cbb9ampkgEj+339/D2/0lB_Aa

### What is the expected behavior?

The process keeps running; committed virtual memory stays bounded relative to RSS over days of uptime.

### What do you see instead?

```
panic(main thread): abort() called
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.
Aborted (core dumped)
```

Stack in the report is a single unknown JS frame (`??`), so I can't point at a subsystem. The Commit-vs-RSS gap (28 GB vs 0.6 GB) suggests reserved-but-untouched mappings accumulating (JIT code regions? thread stacks from spawn? allocator arenas) until an allocation fails and aborts.

### Additional information

- We have upgraded to 1.4.2. The 1.4.1 note "JavaScriptCore delete[s] JIT-generated code after an extended idle period, reducing memory usage for long-running processes" looks directly relevant; I'll report back whether Commit still grows on 1.4.2 after a comparable uptime.
- Question for maintainers: is there a recommended way to observe Bun's own accounting of committed/reserved memory (JIT, mimalloc) from inside the process, so a long-running app can detect this growth before it aborts? `process.memoryUsage()` reports RSS/heap, which looked healthy the whole time.

1.4.2+43848b5a7

### What platform is your computer?

Two modules with a circular import. Only one side dereferences the other at module-evaluation time; the back-edge is used lazily.

```ts

// back-edge is used only lazily, inside a function body
export const find = () => FileSystem.Entry.make("hit")

export const node = { name: "Search", deps: ["ripgrep"] }

title: macOS 27: a new bun process sometimes dies at startup with SIGTRAP inside pthread_jit_write_protect_np
excerpt:
### What happens

On the macOS 27.0 beta (Apple silicon), a new `bun` process sometimes dies about 1 ms after it starts. The signal is SIGTRAP (exit code 133). The crash handler prints:

```
Bun Canary v1.4.3-canary.1 (4830ee197) macOS Silicon
macOS v27.0
Features: jsc

Elapsed: 1ms | User: 1ms | Sys: 0ms
RSS: 2.0 MB | Peak: 2.0 MB | Commit: 16.71 MB | Faults: 9

panic(main thread): Trap instruction at address 0x185506C5C
```

The same command works on the next try.

We see it only on the macOS 27 beta CI lane. That lane is one bare-metal M2 Mac mini (build 26A5425a). I checked about 250 finished runs of the lane between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-14. They contain 15 crash reports with this signature. One run starts tens of thousands of `bun` processes, so the rate is roughly 1 in 10^5 process starts. The victim is a random child process of a random test (`test-trace-events-fs-sync.js`, `spawn.test.ts`, `spawn-streaming-stdin.test.ts`, `next-build.test.ts`, `napi.test.ts`, `cp.test.ts`, `bun-run.test.ts`). The macOS 14, 15 and 26.6.2 lanes ran the same tests in the same builds. They have no report with this signature.

### What the trap is

- The address is `pthread_jit_write_protect_np + 388` in `libsystem_pthread.dylib` (`atos` on the host). The low 14 bits of the address (`0x2C5C`) are the same in all 15 reports. The upper bits differ for each boot (8 different values in the 15 reports).
- The instruction at +388 is `brk #1`. A disassembly of the function on the host shows two kinds of branch to it. The first: the JIT permission mode byte in the commpage (`0xfffffc10c`) is not a known value. The second: the function writes the JIT permission register (`msr S3_6_C15_C1_5, x0`), executes `isb`, reads the register back with `mrs`, and the value is not the commpage value that it wrote. The mode byte is constant for a boot, so the read-back check is the one that fires.
- All 15 trace strings decode to the same 18 frames: one system frame, two bun frames, one system frame (`std::__call_once`), two bun frames, and so on down to `main` and dyld. That is the first `pthread_jit_write_protect_np` call of the process. `JSC::initialize()` calls `ExecutableAllocator::initializeUnderlyingAllocator()`. `initializeJITPageReservation()` (`Source/JavaScriptCore/jit/ExecutableAllocator.cpp`) reserves the JIT region with `mmap(MAP_JIT)` and then calls `threadSelfRestrict<MemoryRestriction::kRwxToRx>()`, which is `pthread_jit_write_protect_np(1)`.
- `Features: jsc`, 1 ms, 9 page

title: `bun pm pack`: honour SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (or an --mtime flag) for tarball entry timestamps
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bun pm pack` writes every entry of the tarball with the same fixed modification time, `1985-10-26 08:15:00 UTC` (the date npm chose in pacote so zip tools are not confused by the Unix epoch). There is no way to change it: `bun pm pack --help` offers `--dry-run`, `--destination`, `--filename`, `--ignore-scripts`, `--gzip-level` and `--quiet`, and setting `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` has no effect.

Reproduction (bun 1.4.2, Linux):

```sh
mkdir demo && cd demo
echo '{"name":"demo","version":"1.0.0"}' > package.json
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1757836800 bun pm pack --quiet
TZ=UTC tar tzvf demo-1.0.0.tgz
```

Output:

```
-rw-r--r-- 0/0              43 1985-10-26 08:15 package/package.json
```

We ship a CLI as a `.tgz` release asset, installed with `bun add ./file.tgz`. Our release policy is that every archive we publish carries its build time, so an operator inspecting a release can tell when it was built. Every other artefact in our release (jars, tarballs, zips, Python wheels) can follow that rule; the `bun pm pack` tarball is the only one that cannot, so we have to document it as an exception.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

When `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` is set, use it as the modification time of every tarball entry instead of the fixed 1985 date. When it is not set, keep today's behaviour, so default output stays byte-for-byte reproducible and nothing changes for existing users.

This follows the reproducible-builds.org specification (https://reproducible-builds.org/specs/source-date-epoch/), which other packaging tools already honour — for example poetry-core for Python wheels. An explicit flag such as `bun pm pack --mtime <epoch seconds | ISO 8601 date>` would solve it equally well; supporting both, with the flag taking precedence, would be ideal.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- **Re-packing the tarball ourselves after `bun pm pack`.** It works, but it duplicates the `files` allowlist and `.npmignore` handling and has to be kept in step with what `bun pm pack` includes.
- **Writing our own packer** with `Bun.Archive`. Same drawback: a second implementation of what goes into a package.
- **Leaving it as a documented exception.** This is what we do for now; the dates only exist inside the `.tgz`, since `bun add` extracts into `node_modules` with its own file times.

title: `bun --watch` leaks one directory fd on the cwd per reload (macOS/kqueue)
excerpt:
**Bun:** 1.4.2 · **OS:** macOS 26.6.2, arm64

Every time `bun --watch` restarts the process, it opens a new kqueue handle on the working directory without closing the previous one. The count grows by exactly one per reload and never drops.

## Repro

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo 'export const x = 1;' > dep.ts
echo 'import { x } from "./dep"; console.log("started", x); setInterval(() => {}, 1e6);' > main.ts
bun --watch --no-clear-screen main.ts &
sleep 2
PID=$(pgrep -f 'bun --watch --no-clear-screen main.ts')
lsof -n -p $PID | grep -c "$PWD\$"     # 2
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do echo "// $i" >> dep.ts; sleep 1.5; done
lsof -n -p $PID | grep -c "$PWD\$"     # 7
```

Only the cwd handle is duplicated; watched source files stay at one handle each.

## Impact

On a long-running dev server this is one leaked fd per save. Combined with the one-fd-per-path kqueue design (see #40907) it contributes to hitting `kern.maxfiles` after a day of development. Once that happens unrelated processes fail too: `brew` and `zsh` on this machine started printing `Too many open files in system`.

## Related

#36675 fixes the equivalent per-reload leaks under `--hot` (entrypoint fd and directory handles orphaned in `bust_entries_cache`, originally #33197 / #36251) but is unmerged and does not cover `--watch`.


Sibling reports from the same dev server: #42701 (duplicate fds per symlink path), #42702 (node_modules watched despite docs).

title: `bun --watch` holds duplicate fds per symlink path with the isolated linker (follow-up to #39783)
excerpt:
**Bun:** 1.4.2 · **OS:** macOS 26.6.2, arm64 · isolated linker (`node_modules/.bun`), monorepo with ~2,100 packages in the store

Follow-up to #39783. That issue was fixed for `bun test` (#40016), but the same mechanism is still live under `bun run --watch`: the resolver keeps one fd per *path string* it walks, and under the isolated linker every dependent reaches a shared package through its own `node_modules/.bun/<dep>@<v>/node_modules/<shared>` symlink. Each of those paths gets its own kqueue handle on the same real file or directory.

## What we see

For a `bun run --watch koaApp.ts` dev server:

| | |
|---|---|
| DIR + REG handles held by the watcher process | 19,095 |
| unique paths behind them (after lsof resolves symlinks) | 6,349 |
| `@turf/helpers/dist/esm/index.js` | held 264 times |
| `@turf/meta/dist/esm/index.js` | 165 times |
| `@turf/helpers/dist/esm` (directory) | 89 times |
| handles under `node_modules/.bun` | 16,185 of 19,095 |

About two thirds of the descriptors are the same real path opened again through a different symlink. This is not the per-reload leak: the cwd has only 4 handles in this process (3 reloads).

## How to observe

```sh
PID=$(pgrep -f 'bun run --watch koaApp.ts')
lsof -n -p $PID | awk 'NR>1 && ($5=="DIR"||$5=="REG"){print $5, $NF}' > fds.txt
wc -l < fds.txt            # 19095
sort -u fds.txt | wc -l    # 6349
sort fds.txt | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
```

A small project with one ESM package imported by 4 files gives exactly one handle per path, so the symlink fan-out from the isolated linker is required to see it. The symlink-only repro from #39783 should trigger it under `bun --watch` as well.

## Impact

Three such watchers (API, queue worker, MCP server) hold ~55k fds between them and hit `kern.maxfiles` within a day, at which point unrelated processes fail with `Too many open files in system`. #40907 reports the same accumulation on macOS from the spawn side (`EBADF` from `posix_spawn` once fds pass `OPEN_MAX`).

## Ask

Deduplicate watch handles by real path (or inode), or stop storing fds for anything under `node_modules` in `--watch` mode the way #40016 did for `bun test`. Either would cut this roughly 3x.


Sibling reports from the same dev server: #42700 (cwd fd leaked per reload), #42702 (node_modules watched despite docs).

title: `bun --watch` watches node_modules despite docs saying it doesn't (isolated linker)
excerpt:
**Bun:** 1.4.2 · **OS:** macOS 26.6.2, arm64 · isolated linker (`node_modules/.bun`)

The [watch-mode docs](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/watch-mode) say the watcher builds its registry from imported source files "excluding those in node_modules". In practice packages under `node_modules/.bun/<pkg>@<ver>/node_modules/<pkg>/...` are watched anyway. For our API entrypoint the watcher holds:

| | |
|---|---|
| DIR handles under `node_modules/.bun` | 10,581 |
| REG handles under `node_modules/.bun` | 5,604 |
| handles under our own source | ~2,900 |

So ~85% of watch handles are on dependency code that never changes during development. The isolated linker makes this worse because each package is reached through several symlink paths and each path gets its own handle (#39783, #40907).

## Minimal repro

Even with the default linker, package **directories** are watched (files are not):

```sh
mkdir -p repro/node_modules/dep/dist/esm && cd repro
echo '{"name":"dep","type":"module","exports":{".":{"import":"./dist/esm/index.js"}}}' > node_modules/dep/package.json
echo 'export const x = 1;' > node_modules/dep/dist/esm/index.js
echo 'import { x } from "dep"; console.log(x); setInterval(() => {}, 1e6);' > main.ts
bun --watch main.ts &
sleep 2
lsof -n -p $(pgrep -f 'bun --watch main.ts') | grep node_modules
# node_modules, node_modules/dep, node_modules/dep/dist, node_modules/dep/dist/esm all held open
```

In the isolated-linker monorepo, files are held too (`@turf/helpers/dist/esm/index.js`, `@sentry/bun/build/esm/index.js`, native `.node` / `.dylib` binaries).

## Ask

Either skip anything under a `node_modules` path segment (including `node_modules/.bun/...`) as the docs describe, or add an ignore option. On macOS each watched path costs a kqueue fd, so this is the difference between ~3k and ~19k descriptors per dev server.

## Related

- #3398, #5278: open requests for a `--watch` ignore/include option
- #18717: open `--watch` EMFILE crash inside `node_modules`, undiagnosed
- #40907: `--watch` retaining ~10k node_modules fds on macOS
- #42700, #42701: sibling reports from the same dev server (cwd fd leaked per reload; duplicate fds per symlink path)

title: Macro import fails when the path of the macro file has an apostrophe
excerpt:
### What happens

A macro import fails when the absolute path of the macro file has an apostrophe in it (the file name or any parent directory).

```sh
mkdir "it's" && cd "it's"
echo 'export function answer() { return 42; }' > macro.ts
printf 'import { answer } from "./macro.ts" with { type: "macro" };\nconsole.log(answer());\n' > main.ts
bun main.ts
```

```
SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 's'. import call expects one or two arguments.
2 | console.log(answer());
                ^
error: "MacroLoadError" error in macro
    at /tmp/macro-repro/it's/main.ts:2:13

Bun v1.4.3-canary.1+b99371011 (Linux x64)
```

The same two files in a directory named `plain` print `42`.

### Cause

`MacroEntryPoint::generate` (`src/bundler/entry_points.rs:244-273`) builds the entry module for a macro as text:

```js
Macros = await import('<dir><filename>');
...
throw new Error("Macro '<name>' not found in '<dir><filename>'");
```

The directory and the file name go through `fmt_path_u8` with `escape_backslashes: true` and nothing else. An apostrophe in the path ends the single-quoted string, and what follows is parsed as code. That is where `Unexpected identifier 's'` comes from: the parser is reading `s/macro.ts'`.

The same template writes the function name raw into `'<name>' in Macros`, `Macros['<name>']`, and the double-quoted error message. An import name can be a string literal (`import { "a'b" as x }`), so that may break the same way. I read this in the code and did not run it.

### Expected

The path and the name are written as JavaScript string literals with every character that needs an escape escaped (quote, backslash, line terminators), so the generated module imports the file that is on disk whatever it is called.

### Related

This is the same kind of bug as the `//# sourceURL=` comment that the runtime transpiler appended under `--inspect`: path bytes written raw into program text. That one is fixed separately by removing the comment. It cannot be fixed that way here, because the import needs the path.

title: [Bug]: Binaries installed via --backend symlink fail with permission denied (EOPNOTSUPP on lchmod)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?
bun 1.2.x / main

### What platform is your computer?
Linux (x86_64, aarch64 - glibc, musl, bionic/Android)

### What steps will reproduce the bug?
1. Configure an environment where `bun install --backend symlink` is used (or `Method::Symlink` is selected on Unix systems).
2. Install any package providing an executable binary:
   ```bash
   bun install --backend symlink cowsay
   ```
3. Attempt to run the installed binary directly or via bunx:
   ```bash
   ./node_modules/.bin/cowsay hello
   ```

### What did you expect to see?
The binary executes successfully with executable permissions (`0755` adjusted for umask).

### What happened instead?
Execution fails with:
```text
bash: ./node_modules/.bin/cowsay: Permission denied
error: could not determine executable to run
```
Inspecting the global cache file target (`~/.bun/install/cache/...`) reveals file mode `0600` (-rw-------).

### How often does this occur?
Every time when symlink-based installation is used on Linux.

### Additional information / Root Cause
In `src/install/bin.rs`, `chmod_on_ok` calls `sys::lchmod(abs_target, mode)` directly on the created symlink.

On Linux/POSIX kernels (`glibc`, `musl`, and Android `bionic`), `fchmodat(..., AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` or `lchmod` returns `EOPNOTSUPP` (`ENOTSUP`) because symlinks do not possess independent permissions.

Because the error is swallowed, permissions on the real binary residing in Bun's cache are never updated to executable mode.

process.on("memoryPressure") on Linux emits a false "critical" event after every arm (kernel PSI seeds unprivileged triggers from the wrong aggregator)
excerpt:
### What happens
With `process.on("memoryPressure", …)` on Linux, as an unprivileged user through `/proc/pressure/memory`, the event fires once shortly after the watcher is armed. It fires at the first memory stall of any size, even when there is no memory pressure at all.

Claude Code uses this event to kill background shells in idle sessions, and those shells are being killed on the false event: anthropics/claude-code#92448, #78674 and #92228, with high MemAvailable on WSL2, Debian and Ubuntu.

### Why: the kernel
In `kernel/sched/psi.c` (torvalds/linux master as of 2026-09-15), `psi_trigger_create()` seeds every trigger's window from the `PSI_POLL` total:
```c
window_reset(&t->win, sched_clock(), group->total[PSI_POLL][t->state], 0);
...
t->aggregator = privileged ? PSI_POLL : PSI_AVGS;
```
- An unprivileged trigger is evaluated by the avgs worker as `window_update(&t->win, now, total[PSI_AVGS][state])`, i.e. the `PSI_AVGS` total minus a `PSI_POLL`-seeded start value.
- `total[PSI_POLL]` advances only while a privileged (rtpoll) trigger exists.
- So the first `new_stall` update after creation computes roughly all the memory stall accumulated since boot as "growth". That exceeds the 150 ms threshold, and the trigger fires — once, or twice if another stall follows within the next window, because the inflated growth is carried in `prev_growth` for one window.

### Why Bun makes it recur
- The watcher is armed on the first listener and disarmed on the last removal (`onDidChangeListeners`).
- An app that adds and removes listeners over time (Claude Code adds one per background shell) therefore creates a fresh trigger each time, and gets a fresh false event each time.

### Reproduction (the kernel half needs no Bun)
Open `/proc/pressure/memory` read-write as a normal user and write `some 150000 2000000\0`. Poll for `POLLPRI` while sampling the file's `some total=` every 100–250 ms. An event arrives at the first stall, even though the total barely moved.

Measured on `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2` (94 GiB VM, MemFree 79 GB): three independent watchers each got exactly one event, with 115 µs, 0 µs and 30 µs of `some` growth around it, and no second event over the next 15+ minutes.

**Controlled cycles.** The same trigger was created and closed three times. Each fired at its first stall after arming (0.1 s, 60.1 s and 2.5 s after arming) with 687 µs, 520 µs and 0 µs of real `some` growth. One of the three fired a second time within its next window, on 562 µ

title: Bun Shell: deliver a Response body that is not in memory to a `<` redirect (stream or buffer it)
excerpt:
### What is missing

`` $`cmd < ${response}` `` reads the whole `Response` body when the command starts. That works when the bytes are in memory by then: a string, a `Blob`, a buffer, a file, or a `fetch()` body that arrived completely.

The shell cannot deliver any other body:

- `new Response(readableStream)` and `new Response(asyncIterable)`
- a `fetch()` response whose body is still arriving

```js
import { $ } from "bun";

const response = await fetch("https://example.com/large-file");
await $`wc -c < ${response}`;
```

Through Bun 1.4.x the command gets an empty stdin and exits 0. #42786 turns this into an error with a hint (`< ${await response.blob()}`). This issue tracks the real support.

How often the `fetch()` case happens, measured with a fresh process for each run and a loopback server (20 runs each):

| body | 1.3.14 | 1.4.3-canary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 16 KB, `Content-Length` | 0 of 20 empty | 0 of 20 empty |
| 64 KiB, `Content-Length` | 17 of 20 empty | 20 of 20 empty |
| 100 KB, `Content-Length` | 15 of 20 empty | 18 of 20 empty |
| 10 KB, chunked | 20 of 20 empty | 20 of 20 empty |

### What is wanted

The redirect delivers the body. There are two ways to do it:

1. Stream the body. `Bun.spawn({ stdin: response })` already does this for a subprocess: `Stdio::extract_body_value` (`src/runtime/api/bun/spawn/stdio.rs`) turns a `Locked` body into `Stdio::ReadableStream`. #36895 adds the shell side of that for a bare `ReadableStream`. A builtin command needs an async stdin source.
2. Buffer the body. The `Cmd` waits for `response.blob()` before it starts the command. That needs a `Cmd` state that waits for a promise, with a cancel path for a script that fails in the meantime.

### Related

- #18262: the panic for a bare `ReadableStream` redirect. #40885 replaces it with an error. #36895 implements streaming for it.
- #35314 and #35551: earlier pull requests for the `Response` case. Both were closed as stale.

A pool's query terminates other backends connected to its disposable database, excluding the backend executing the query. The query resolves. A later `await pool.close()` intermittently never settles, even after all ten `onclose` callbacks have fired.

title: Improve bun release signature infrastructure
excerpt:
To support #39464 a revocation file and some pgp public keys should be committed to the repository.

The current signing key can be transitioned to the `Past` role, and epochs generated for all the previous releases before this new verification is deployed.

This has bun becoming its own verification tool for both previous and future releases and gives the maintainers a useful way to rotate keys.

An alternative would be to publish a separate rust binary for all supported platforms that would be more general purpose. It could eliminate dependence on OS provided checksum verification tools and accept a key fingerprint to serve as a root of trust along with a file to retrieve pgp keys from.

--------

## Release-Key Revocation Model

This design separates **authorization to publish current trust information** from **authorization to verify historical release artifacts**.

The checksum manifests remain separate signed files. The revocation response contains key and release-epoch information, but does not contain archive checksums.

### 1. Maintainer Options for Revocation

#### Embedded key roles

The client embeds three keys:

- **Past key** — used for older releases.
- **Current key** — used for the current release-signing period.
- **Future key** — used to prepare or authorize the next signing period.

Only the embedded current and future keys may sign the revocation response.

#### Revoking the past key

A revocation response signed by the current key may revoke past embedded keys only.

This allows maintainers to retire older keys while keeping the current key operational.

The current key may not:

- Revoke the future key.
- Revoke the current key (itself).
- Add new release keys.

#### Revoking the current key

A revocation response signed by the future key may revoke:

- Past embedded keys.
- The current embedded key.

This permits a transition from the current key to the future key.

The future key may not revoke itself.

#### Adding new release keys

Only a revocation response signed by the future key may provide new public keys.

A newly provided key can be added to the keyring for subsequent checksum-manifest verification, subject to the manifest’s revocation rules.

A new key may not be both provided and revoked in the same response.

#### Epoch-specific historical keys

An epoch can contain:

- A list of release names.
- One public key associated with those releases.

A release can belong to zero or one epoch.

title: Possible Bun 1.4.1 Android/Bionic compile regression with splitting:true
excerpt:
## Summary

We isolated a reproducible difference between Bun 1.4.0 and Bun 1.4.1 when compiling OpenCode 1.18.31 for an Android/Bionic/Termux environment.

The same OpenCode source and dependency tree behaves correctly when run directly under both Bun 1.4.0 and Bun 1.4.1. The failure appears only in the Bun 1.4.1 compiled/embedded executable path when `splitting:true` is enabled.

## Observed matrix

- OpenCode 1.18.31 source run directly under Bun 1.4.0: PASS (`/api/reference` and `/api/agent` HTTP 200)
- Same source run directly under Bun 1.4.1: PASS
- Bun 1.4.0 compiled Android/Bionic candidate: PASS
- Bun 1.4.1 compiled with `minify:true, splitting:true`: FAIL (`/api/reference` and `/api/agent` HTTP 500)
- Bun 1.4.1 compiled with `minify:false, splitting:true`: FAIL
- Bun 1.4.1 compiled with `minify:true, splitting:false`: PASS (`/api/config`, `/api/reference`, `/api/agent` HTTP 200)
- Fresh Bun 1.4.1 control with normal `splitting:true` reproduced the failure

The failing executable reaches an OpenCode internal exception of the form:

`TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')`

Earlier investigation initially suggested a malformed OpenCode reference object, but the A/B controls above challenged that diagnosis: direct source execution passes under Bun 1.4.1, and disabling compile-time splitting makes the compiled 1.4.1 artifact pass without any OpenCode source patch.

## Environment

- Android / Termux
- Bionic libc environment
- OpenCode 1.18.31
- Bun 1.4.0 and 1.4.1 compared against the same reconstructed source/dependency tree
- `@androidtui/core` 0.5.5

## Known-good workaround

Compile OpenCode 1.18.31 with Bun 1.4.1 and:

`minify:true, splitting:false`

Qualified no-split artifact:
- SHA256: `02367cb9fa073ab37acadd6d4ca35db590f7fd4c775147541104ec604fee6e4e`
- Size: 188,614,920 bytes

Bun 1.4.0 compiled control artifact:
- SHA256: `26c7610ef19d4982dbd72ed3db7663813543bfcaf4d99834665df1f365bb9905`

## Interpretation

Current evidence suggests a Bun 1.4.1 compile-time splitting regression on this Android/Bionic path, rather than an ordinary OpenCode source-level defect or minification issue.

We have not yet reduced this to a tiny standalone Bun reproducer outside the OpenCode build tree, so this report is intentionally scoped as a possible Bun regression rather than a universal claim.

If useful, I can provide the exact OpenCode build settings/source locations used to produce the A/B candidates.

Dev server skips a router type with a missing root directory and prints no message
excerpt:
### What happens

The dev server drops a file system router type whose root directory does not exist, and it prints no message. A mistyped directory name gives a server that starts cleanly and answers 404 for every route of that mount.

```ts
// The directory is `./pages`. The option has a typo.
Bun.serve({
  development: true,
  routes: { "/*": { dir: "./pagse", style: "nextjs-pages" } },
});
```

On 1.4.3-canary.1 (Linux x64) with the React packages installed, the server starts with empty stdout and stderr, and `GET /` answers `404 Not Found`.

The same skip applies to `app.framework.fileSystemRouterTypes[n].root`, and to `bun build --app`.

### Where

- `src/runtime/bake/DevServer.rs`, the router init loop in `DevServer::init`: `read_dir_info_ignore_error(joined_root)` returns `None`, and the loop does `continue`.
- `src/runtime/bake/production.rs` has the same `continue`.

### Why this needs a decision and not only a log line

A framework package can list roots that a project does not need to have, for example `src/pages` and `pages`. A warning for each absent root is noise for those projects. A directory that the user names in `routes: { "/*": { dir, style } }` is more likely a mistake.

Options:

- Warn for each skipped router type, with the joined path.
- Warn only for `{ dir, style }` mounts, because the user wrote that path.
- Make a missing root a startup error.

### Context

A review of #42840 found this. #42840 fixes an abort that a skipped router type causes, and it does not change the skip.

process.env runtime mutations don't propagate to native environ (getenv/std::env::var/NAPI addons)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (also reproduced on earlier 1.x)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64 (WSL2/Ubuntu). Likely all POSIX platforms; possibly Windows too (`_putenv`/`SetEnvironmentVariable` parity).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Mutating `process.env` at runtime updates the JS-visible env map but does **not** propagate to the native process environment, so `getenv()` — and anything built on it (NAPI addons, Rust `std::env::var`) — misses the change:

```js
process.env.CODEGRAPH_TEST_X = 'hello';

const { dlopen, FFIType, CString } = require('bun:ffi');
const lib = dlopen('libc.so.6', {
  getenv: { args: [FFIType.cstring], returns: FFIType.ptr },
});
const ptr = lib.symbols.getenv('CODEGRAPH_TEST_X');
console.log('native getenv sees:', ptr ? new CString(ptr).toString() : null);
console.log('process.env sees:', process.env.CODEGRAPH_TEST_X);
```

Bun output:
```
native getenv sees: null
process.env sees: hello
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Node.js propagates `process.env` assignments to the real process environment (the setter calls `setenv`/`_putenv` through libuv), so native code in the same process observes the mutation. Under Node, the equivalent `getenv` (e.g. via a NAPI addon or `std::env::var` in a native module) returns `hello`.

### What is the actual behavior?

Bun keeps the JS env map and the native environ block out of sync after spawn: `getenv` returns `null` for any var set purely via `process.env.X = ...` at runtime.

### Impact

Any native addon or embedded native library that reads configuration from environment variables cannot see values set or changed from JS at runtime. Concrete instance: the codegraph project's Rust NAPI kernel gates a feature on `std::env::var("CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS")`; setting `process.env.CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS = '0'` at runtime works under Node but is silently ignored under Bun. Spawn-time env vars work fine in both — only mid-process mutation diverges. This is related in spirit to #29244 (`os.homedir()` snapshotting), another JS-env vs native-view divergence.

title: require.resolve falls back to Bun's global install cache — resolves packages the project never installed
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64 (WSL2/Ubuntu)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`require.resolve` resolves packages that are **not installed in any `node_modules` reachable from the caller** if they happen to exist in Bun's global install cache (`~/.bun/install/cache` or `$BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR`).

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/empty-pkg && cd /tmp/empty-pkg
echo 'try { console.log(require.resolve("@colbymchenry/codegraph-linux-x64/bin/codegraph")) } catch(e) { console.log("threw", e.code) }' > probe.js
bun probe.js
# → /home/bompus/.bun/install/cache/@colbymchenry/codegraph-linux-x64@1.6.0@@@1/bin/codegraph
```

Node in the same directory: `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

Worse, `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/empty bun probe.js` doesn't disable the fallback — Bun *materializes* the package into the new cache dir (hardlinks) and still resolves it:

```
resolved: /tmp/empty-cache/@colbymchenry/codegraph-linux-x64@1.6.0@@@1/bin/codegraph
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Node's `require.resolve` only consults `node_modules` directories on the caller's module path (plus `NODE_PATH`). A package that was never installed for this project must fail with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. There is no global fallback that can make an uninstalled package resolvable.

### What is the actual behavior?

Bun's resolver treats the global install cache as an implicit resolution root, so `require.resolve`/`require` can succeed for packages the project never installed. Code that probes for optional dependencies ("is this platform package present?") gets a false positive — e.g. a thin installer that checks `require.resolve(pkg)` to decide whether to self-heal will silently exec a globally-cached copy of a *different version* than the project pinned. It also makes tests that require hermetic "not installed" behavior impossible under Bun, and there appears to be no env var to opt out.

### Suggestion

If the cache fallback is intentional for `bun x`-style UX, it should at least be disable-able (env flag or `require.resolve` strictness matching Node), since `require` reaching outside the project's dependency tree is a hermeticity/security-relevant behavior difference.

title: server.reload() ignores a `{ dir, style }` framework router route that the server did not start with
excerpt:
### What happens

`server.reload()` accepts a `routes` object with a framework router route (`{ dir, style }`) that the server did not start with, and the route never answers. There is no error. A `Bun.serve()` call that reuses its server under `bun --hot` takes the same path.

```ts
import html from "./index.html";

const server = Bun.serve({
  development: true,
  routes: { "/": html },
  fetch: () => new Response("fallback"),
});

server.reload({
  development: true,
  routes: { "/": html, "/*": { dir: "./pages", style: "nextjs-pages" } },
  fetch: () => new Response("fallback"),
});

// `./pages/about.tsx` is never served. GET /about does not reach the router.
```

The reverse also holds. A reload that removes the route, or gives it another `dir` or `style`, changes nothing: the dev server keeps the router list it started with. The dev server registers its catch-all after the static routes, so the catch-all also shadows a new `"/*": html` route: on 1.4.3, a page request then answers from `fetch`.

On 1.4.3 the example above also loses the `fetch` fallback: each request that matches no route gets a closed connection. #42907 fixes that part only.

### Where

- `NewServer::set_routes` (`src/runtime/server/mod.rs`) has `AnyRoute::FrameworkRouter(_) => {}`. The only handler is the catch-all that `DevServer::set_routes` (`src/runtime/bake/DevServer.rs`) registers when `framework.file_system_router_types` is not empty.
- `DevServer::init` fixes that list. `on_reload_from_zig` (`src/runtime/server/server_body.rs`) drops `new_config.bake`, which holds the list of the reload config, unread.

### Why this needs a decision

A live dev server cannot take another router list. `Framework::auto` switches the whole framework to the built-in React one when the list is not empty (server components, a separate SSR graph, the server runtime). `DevServer::init` builds the router and `frontend_only` from the list.
