title: codegraph index ~4% slower than Node on a 71k-file corpus (parse-loop +5%, parse-index-rebuild +21.5%)
excerpt:
## Summary

Running CodeGraph's full index (`codegraph index --force`) on a ~71k-file corpus (Linux kernel source tree) is ~3.8% slower under Bun 1.4.2 than Node v26.8.2, with byte-identical output. Phase timings show the loss is concentrated in the parse loop (JS tree-sitter walkers + NAPI kernel calls) and the SQLite index rebuild (`node:sqlite` bulk inserts).

## Reproduction

```bash
# corpus: a linux kernel source checkout, codegraph initialized
CODEGRAPH_SYNTH_TIMINGS=1 /usr/bin/time -v nice -n 10 bun  dist/bin/codegraph.js index --force
CODEGRAPH_SYNTH_TIMINGS=1 /usr/bin/time -v nice -n 10 node dist/bin/codegraph.js index --force
```

Sequential arms, same corpus/flags/`nice` level, idle host, swap cleared, no other load during either run.

## Results

| phase | bun 1.4.2 | node v26.8.2 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| wall clock | 365.7s | 351.8s | +3.8% |
| scan (71120 files) | 1,409ms | 1,310ms | +7.6% |
| parse-loop | 148,300ms | 141,183ms | +5.0% |
| parse-index-rebuild | 29,049ms | 23,901ms | +21.5% |
| ref-index-recreate | 6,119ms | 5,273ms | +16.0% |
| edge-index-recreate | 13,228ms | 12,951ms | +2.1% |
| callback-synthesis | 50,037ms | 59,479ms | −15.8% |
| resolution | 170,247ms | 170,489ms | −0.1% |
| maintenance | 6,450ms | 1,595ms | +304% |
| MaxRSS | 15.04 GB | 17.58 GB | −14% |

Output identical under both runtimes: 2,082,872 nodes / 6,412,714 edges.

Bun uses 14% less peak RAM and wins the callback-synthesis phase; it loses the parse loop (JS tree-sitter walkers over a serialized AST + NAPI addon calls) and the SQLite index rebuild phases enough to net ~4% slower overall.

## Environment

Bun 1.4.2, Node v26.8.2, WSL2 Ubuntu on Windows 11, x86_64.

`Bun.sliceAnsi` still calls `CRASH()` on the five inputs below. The process exits with `panic(main thread): abort() called` (SIGABRT, exit 134), and script cannot catch it. A fuzzing run and the review of #42929 found them. No user has reported one.

#42929 makes the two `Vector`s of `Bun.sliceAnsi` throw. These five sites are not a `Vector`, so that PR leaves them as they are. Each row gives the peak RSS on a release build (Linux x64) that includes #42929.

### The result fits, and a `StringBuilder` doubles its capacity past the longest 16-bit string

| Call | Site | Result | Peak RSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Bun.sliceAnsi("\u3042".repeat(2 ** 30), 0, 4)` | `result.reserveCapacity(input.size())`, `src/jsc/bindings/sliceAnsi.cpp:876` | 2 characters | 2.2 GB |

- The first two rows start at an input of 1,073,741,818 code units. The reserve is the whole input length, also for a slice of a few columns.

title: Windows watcher: a ReadDirectoryChangesW buffer overflow drops the changes and nothing reloads
excerpt:
### What happens

On Windows, `--hot`, `--watch`, `bun build --watch` and the dev server read file changes with `ReadDirectoryChangesW` into a 64 KiB buffer. Between two reads, Windows records the changes for the directory handle in a buffer of the same size. When more changes arrive than that buffer holds, Windows completes the next read with zero bytes (`ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR`). The documented meaning is that changes were lost and the caller must enumerate the directory.

`WindowsWatcher::next` (`src/watcher/WindowsWatcher.rs`, the `nbytes == 0` branch) logs the overflow, issues a new read and continues. It does not tell the reloader. If a dropped record named a watched file, nothing reloads until that file changes again.

### Expected

The watcher reports the overflow to its context. The context then acts as if every watched file changed: `--watch` restarts, `--hot` reloads, `bun build --watch` rebuilds, and the dev server invalidates its graph.

### Notes

- I do not have a repro. A burst of 12,000 file writes around one write of the entry point still reloaded, on a debug build and on 1.4.3-canary (Windows Server 2019, 16 vCPUs). With a short watchlist the watcher thread drains the buffer fast. The watcher matches each record against the whole watchlist, so a project with many watched files is the likely victim.
- #39820 saw the end of a deep change burst go missing on a debug build and attributes it to this path.
- The inotify backend has the same gap for `IN_Q_OVERFLOW`. #36416 proposes a recovery for it.

title: MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=1000 flips codegraph index from +3.8% slower to 7-16% faster than Node (gain is the small-alloc insert path)

Follow-up to #42924 carrying the full-corpus `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=1000` data requested there — refiled so the new numbers get a fresh triage; the earlier issue is closed as superseded.

title: `bun run --filter` leaves workspace child process alive after Ctrl+C on Windows
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+f5649a7ed

The same reproduction also fails with Bun 1.4.0+34cbb9a40.

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Minimal reproduction repository:

https://github.com/rubenferreira97/bun-filter-ctrl-c-repro

The repository contains one Bun workspace package, no dependencies, and no lockfile. The workspace package's only start script is:

```json
"start": "bun src/index.ts"
```

From the repository root, run:

```powershell
$env:PORT = '3011'
bun run --filter @bun-filter-ctrl-c-repro/server start
```

After the server reports that it is listening, press `Ctrl+C` once. Check the port from another PowerShell terminal:

```powershell
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 3011 -State Listen -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Select-Object LocalAddress,LocalPort,State,OwningProcess
```

For comparison, run the same entry point directly:

```powershell
Push-Location packages/server
$env:PORT = '3011'
bun src/index.ts
Pop-Location
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The filtered command should terminate the workspace script and release port `3011` after `Ctrl+C`. The server should receive `SIGINT` and print:

```text
[server] SIGINT received; stopping.
```

### What do you see instead?

With `bun run --filter`, after pressing `Ctrl+C`, the descendant `bun src/index.ts` process remains alive and keeps port `3011` occupied. The server does not print its `SIGINT` shutdown message.

Running `bun src/index.ts` directly receives `SIGINT`, prints the shutdown message, and releases the port as expected.

### Additional information

This reproduces with a dependency-free workspace and is independent of Elysia, Node-based tooling, or the original application.

This appears related to the closed issues [#20319](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/20319), [#10649](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/10649), [#18605](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/18605), and [#24360](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/24360), which were associated with [#36291](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/36291). The reproduction still fails with the versions above, so this may be an uncovered `bun run --filter` path or a regression after the existing fix.

NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS from a .env file shows in process.env but the TLS loader ignores it
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+c6b7fcb5b. Also main at b8eacead4d.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir extra-ca-dotenv && cd extra-ca-dotenv
echo 'NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt' > .env

# The variable comes from .env only.
env -u NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS bun -e 'console.log(process.env.NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, require("tls").getCACertificates("extra").length)'

# The variable comes from the real environment.
NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt bun -e 'console.log(process.env.NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, require("tls").getCACertificates("extra").length)'
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Both commands print the same certificate count, or the documentation says that `.env` cannot set this variable.

### What do you see instead?

```
/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt 0
/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt 151
```

`process.env` shows the value from `.env`, but TLS does not use the file. A handshake shows the same result. With a server certificate that `ca1-cert.pem` issued, `fetch()` fails with `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE` when `.env` sets `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=ca1-cert.pem`. The chain verifies when the real environment sets it. `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` in the same `.env` does take effect.

### Additional information

`us_get_root_extra_cert_instances()` (`packages/bun-usockets/src/crypto/root_certs.cpp:178`) reads `getenv("NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS")`, which is the C environment. `us_should_use_system_ca()` in the same file does the same for `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA`. Bun loads `.env` into the map behind `process.env`, not into the C environment.

`cacheDefaultCACertificates()` in `src/js/node/tls.ts` reads `process.env.NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and `process.env.NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA`. The native store reads the C environment for both, so the two can disagree:

- With `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` in `.env`, `tls.getCACertificates("default")` lists 273 certificates in place of 121 on this machine. `us_should_use_system_ca()` does not see the variable.
- After `delete process.env.NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` at run time, `tls.getCACertificates("default")` drops the extra certificates, and the native store still trusts them.

Node reads `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` once at startup. Later changes to `process.env` have no effect there.

title: Native warnings written on a JS thread stay in the Output buffer until exit, and a Worker drops them
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+c6b7fcb5b. Also main at b8eacead4d.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// idle-warn.js
const server = Bun.serve({
  port: 0,
  development: true,
  fetch: () => new Promise(() => {}),
});
fetch(server.url).catch(e => console.log("client error:", e.code));

Run `bun idle-warn.js` and wait 15 seconds.

When the idle timeout closes the request, this line appears on stderr:

```

```

### What do you see instead?

Only `client error: ECONNRESET` appears. The warning appears when the process exits in the usual way (for example `setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 17000)` in place of the `setInterval`). A process that is killed never shows it. So a server does not show the warning while it runs, which is when the warning is useful.

A Worker thread loses such a line completely:

title: `bun run <script>` prints "Script not found" and hides the error when package.json does not parse
excerpt:
### What happens

`package.json` has a syntax error. `bun run <script>` prints only `error: Script not found "<script>"`. It does not print the JSON error. `bun run <file>` prints the JSON error, then runs the file and exits 0.

### Reproduction

Bun 1.4.3-canary.1+c6b7fcb5b, linux x64.

```sh
mkdir t && cd t
printf '{"scripts":{"hello":"echo ran"},,}' > package.json
echo 'console.log("ran-file")' > index.js

bun run hello
# error: Script not found "hello"
# exit 1

bun run index.js
# 1 | {"scripts":{"hello":"echo ran"},,}
#                                     ^
# error: Expected string but found ","
#     at /tmp/t/package.json:1:33
# ran-file
# exit 0

bun install
# 1 | {"scripts":{"hello":"echo ran"},,}
#                                     ^
# error: Expected string but found ","
#     at /tmp/t/package.json:1:33
# ParserError: failed to parse '/tmp/t/package.json'
# exit 1
```

### Expected

`bun run hello` prints the JSON error from `package.json`, as `bun install` does. For the same file, `npm run hello` (npm 11.16.0) fails with `npm error code EJSONPARSE`.

### Cause

`RunCommand::exec_with_cfg` reads the working directory through `configure_env_for_run_without_linker` (`src/runtime/cli/run_command.rs`). The resolver adds the JSON error to `ctx.log` and returns a directory entry with no `package.json`. The "Script not found" exit path prints its own message and never prints `ctx.log`.

  secretAccessKey: 'B',
  bucket: 'bkt',

await s3.write('b.html', 'x', { contentEncoding: 'identity' })

`content-type` is sent on every request, so it should appear in `SignedHeaders` — just like `content-encoding` (added in #26149) and `content-disposition` already do.

title: node:net: a socket adopted from an fd (cluster worker connections) emits 'error' twice when a buffered write fails
fs.watchFile: no change event when the stat error code changes while the file is missing
excerpt:
### What happens

`fs.watchFile` emits one `change` event when a watched path starts to fail `stat()`. Node emits one more `change` event each time the error code of the failed `stat()` changes, for example `ENOENT` to `ENOTDIR`. The arguments are the same each time: a zeroed `current` and the last real stat as `previous`.

The mechanism is in libuv's `poll_cb`, which calls back when `busy_polling != req->result`:
https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/5152db2cbfeb5582e9c27c5ea1dba2cd9e10759b/src/fs-poll.c#L200-L208

Bun treats every failed `stat()` the same (`src/runtime/node/node_fs_stat_watcher.rs`, `restat()`).

### Repro

Watch `d/f.txt`. Remove `d` (stat fails with `ENOENT`). Create a regular file named `d` (`ENOTDIR`). Remove it (`ENOENT`). Restore `d/f.txt`.

```
node v26.3.0: 4 callbacks (gone, gone, gone, back)
bun 1.4.3:    2 callbacks (gone, back)
```

Found while working on #43050, which does not change this.

title: Shell: a command substitution in a pipeline reads the stdin of the process, not the pipe
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+c6b7fcb5b. `main` at 5c26a6cca5 has the same behavior.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64. The code path is not specific to a platform.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```ts
// repro.ts
import { $ } from "bun";
const r = await $`echo hi | echo "[$(cat)]"`.quiet();
console.log(r.stdout.toString());
```

Run it with data on the stdin of the process:

```sh
echo FROM_PROCESS_STDIN | bun repro.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`[hi]`. bash and dash print this:

```sh
echo FROM_PROCESS_STDIN | bash -c 'echo hi | echo "[$(cat)]"'
# [hi]
```

The substitution runs in the second pipeline member. Its stdin is the pipe.

### What do you see instead?

`[FROM_PROCESS_STDIN]`. The `cat` inside `$(...)` reads the stdin of the bun process, not the pipe. On a terminal the script blocks, because `cat` waits for terminal input.

### Additional information

- `echo hi | (echo "[$(cat)]")` has the same defect.
- `echo hi | (cat)` and `echo hi | if true; then cat; fi` print `hi`. Only a command substitution reads the wrong stdin.
- The cause is in `Expansion::next` (`src/runtime/shell/states/Expansion.rs:204`). It builds the IO of the substitution from the root IO: `stdin: interp.root_io().stdin.clone()`. An `Expansion` node does not receive the IO of the command that contains it, so it cannot use the stdin of that command.

title: crypto.pbkdf2: ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE says ">= 1 and <= 2147483647", Node says ">= 1 && <= 2147483647"
excerpt:
`crypto.pbkdf2` and `crypto.pbkdf2Sync` word the range of `iterations` and `keylen` differently from Node. A differential run against Node v26.3.0 found it. No user reported it.

```js
const crypto = require("crypto");
for (const args of [["a", "b", 0, 1, "sha1"], ["a", "b", 1, -1, "sha1"]]) {
  try { crypto.pbkdf2Sync(...args); } catch (e) { console.log(e.code, "|", e.message); }
}
```

| | message |
|---|---|
| Node v26.3.0 | `The value of "iterations" is out of range. It must be >= 1 && <= 2147483647. Received 0` |
| Bun 1.4.3-canary (main b64b63069c) | `The value of "iterations" is out of range. It must be >= 1 and <= 2147483647. Received 0` |
| Node v26.3.0 | `The value of "keylen" is out of range. It must be >= 0 && <= 2147483647. Received -1` |
| Bun 1.4.3-canary | `The value of "keylen" is out of range. It must be >= 0 and <= 2147483647. Received -1` |

Node validates both arguments with `validateInt32`, which writes `>= ${min} && <= ${max}`. The `and` form is the wording of Node's Buffer and zlib bounds errors.

The cause is in `src/runtime/crypto/PBKDF2.rs`. Both checks call `throw_range_error` with `RangeErrorOptions { min, max }`, and the shared Rust formatter writes `>= min and <= max` for that form. `fd_jsc.rs` and `node_crypto_binding.rs` pass the range as `msg` (`>= a && <= b`) where Node uses a validator, and #40737 does the same for `validators.rs`. #40737 does not touch `PBKDF2.rs`.

`test/js/node/crypto/pbkdf2.test.ts` (lines 132 and 215) pins the `and` form for `keylen`, so a fix has to update those two expectations.

title: tsconfig.json `extends` array (TS 5.0 form) is silently ignored by the bundler
excerpt:
## What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84

## What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (macOS 27.0)

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

TypeScript 5.0 allows `extends` to be an array of config paths. Bun's tsconfig parser only accepts a string, so when `extends` is an array the whole `extends` field is dropped — no warning is emitted and every option inherited from the base config(s) is lost. The relative-path *string* form of `extends` works fine, so this is distinct from #6326 (package specifiers not resolved through `node_modules`).

Self-contained repro (no dependencies):

```sh
mkdir bun-extends-array && cd bun-extends-array

cat > base.json <<'EOF'
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "experimentalDecorators": true,
    "useDefineForClassFields": false
  }
}
EOF

cat > dec.ts <<'EOF'
function deco(_target: unknown, _key: string) {}
export class A {
  @deco x = 1;
}
EOF

# 1) string extends — works
echo '{ "extends": "./base.json" }' > tsconfig.json
bun build ./dec.ts | head -1

# 2) array extends with the same single entry — ignored
echo '{ "extends": ["./base.json"] }' > tsconfig.json
bun build ./dec.ts | head -1

# tsc resolves the array form correctly
bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --showConfig | grep -E 'experimentalDecorators|useDefineForClassFields'
```

## What is the expected behavior?

Both builds should emit the legacy TypeScript decorator helper, because `experimentalDecorators: true` is inherited from `base.json` in both cases:

```

```

Per TypeScript semantics, `{ "extends": ["a", "b"] }` is equivalent to `b` extending `a`; later entries override earlier ones.

## What do you see instead?

Case 1 (string) emits the legacy helper as expected. Case 2 (array) emits the TC39 standard-decorator runtime instead, i.e. `experimentalDecorators`/`useDefineForClassFields` from `base.json` were never applied:

```
== string extends
var __legacyDecorateClassTS = function(decorators, target, key, desc) {
== array extends
var __create = Object.create;
```

`tsc --showConfig` on the array form shows both options set, so the config itself is valid:

```
"experimentalDecorators": true,
"useDefineForClassFields": false
```

No warning or debug log is produced for the array case — the field is just skipped.

bun:sqlite: DDL on an FTS5 table fails SQLITE_LOCKED while query-cache statements are open — heap-layout dependent, clearQueryCache() avoids it
excerpt:
### What happens

On bun 1.4.2 (stable, `744846f84`) and today's 1.4.3 canary, after using cached `db.query()` statements on a connection, later **DDL on an FTS5 virtual table on the same connection** fails with:

```
SQLiteError: database table is locked
errno: 6, code: "SQLITE_LOCKED"
```

Three failure modes were observed in the same app (an FTS5 shadow-table index rebuild that drops/renames an fts5 table pair on one connection):

1. `DROP TABLE` / `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME` on an FTS5 table inside a transaction that follows cached-DML use → `SQLITE_LOCKED database table is locked`
2. explicit `COMMIT` after cached DML → `SQLITE_BUSY cannot commit transaction - SQL statements in progress`
3. the connection pins the write lock against other connections: a second connection's DDL waits out `busy_timeout` (5 s) then fails `SQLITE_BUSY database is locked`

`db.clearQueryCache()` before the DDL deterministically prevents all three. `Bun.gc(true)`, event-loop yields, one-shot `db.prepare(...)` + `.finalize()`, and swapping `.get()` for `.all()` do **not**.

### Conditions (bisected)

- The DDL target being an **FTS5 virtual table** is required: the identical flow with plain tables never fails (100+ runs).
- The cached statements can be plain `INSERT ... SELECT` / `SELECT COUNT(*)` against **plain, unrelated tables** — the fts5 table itself never has to be read by user code.
- The failure is **heap/module-graph dependent**: the same SQL in a standalone file passes; in the failing app, adding or removing *unrelated code after the failing call in the same test function* flips the outcome. This is the most concerning part — correct lock behavior should not depend on JS heap layout.

### Repro harness

The standalone file below reproduces the exact shape (migrations, WAL+pragmas, cached chunk writers, cached count read, DDL-only swap txn) but **passes standalone** on my machine — it needs the larger app's module graph to fail. Bun.Archive#extract() writes into an existing file instead of replacing it
excerpt:
### What happens

`Bun.Archive#extract()` opens each regular file with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC`. When the destination already holds a file with that name, the extractor writes into the existing inode. GNU tar removes the existing file first and creates a new one.

Three sites share this open: `extract_to_dir` (`src/libarchive/lib.rs`), `extract_to_disk_filtered` (`src/runtime/api/Archive.rs`) and `open_output_file` (`src/install/TarballStream.rs`).

Results on 1.4.3-canary, Linux x64, as a non-root user, umask 022:

| the destination already holds | archive member | `extract(dir)` | `extract(dir, { glob: "**" })` | GNU tar 1.35 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `secret.txt`, mode 0644 | `secret.txt`, mode 0600 | new content, mode stays 0644 | new content, mode stays 0644 | new content, mode 0600 |
| `a.txt`, mode 0444 | `a.txt`, mode 0644 | rejects with `ReadError` | resolves with count 0, the old content stays | new content |
| `a.txt`, a hard link to `store/a.txt` | `a.txt` | `store/a.txt` is overwritten too | `store/a.txt` is overwritten too | `store/a.txt` does not change |

The first row matters after an upgrade. Released versions create a 0600 member as 0644 when no glob is given. A later extraction into the same directory keeps that 0644.

### Repro

Run this as a non-root user.

```js
import { chmodSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

mkdirSync("out", { recursive: true });
writeFileSync("out/secret.txt", "old");
chmodSync("out/secret.txt", 0o444);
// Rejects with ReadError. `tar -xf` replaces the file.
await new Bun.Archive({ "secret.txt": "new" }).extract("out");
```

### Suggested direction

#41228 fixed the same problem in the copy backend of `bun install` (`src/install/PackageInstall.rs`): open with `O_EXCL`, and on `EEXIST` call `unlinkat` and open again. The three sites above can use the same open. An `unlinkat` on a path with more than one component can follow a symlink in a parent directory. So this is safe only when the extractor opens each entry as a single name in a verified parent directory. #41750 does that.

With that open in place, `bun_libarchive::file_mode` can give `Bun.Archive#extract()` the exact bits of the entry. The write bits that #43135 adds (for the owner always, for the group and others where the entry lets them read) exist only so that the `O_TRUNC` reopen of a file from an earlier extraction succeeds.

### Other differences between the two extractors

`extract()` runs `extract_to_dir` without a glob

title: S3File.writer() drops an upload failure that arrives with no pending flush() or end() promise: end() resolves 0
s3: a failed multipart upload sends AbortMultipartUpload while parts are still in flight, and does not abort again
excerpt:
### What happens

When a multipart upload fails, `MultiPartUpload::fail` (`src/runtime/webcore/s3/multipart.rs`) sends `AbortMultipartUpload` at once, while `UploadPart` requests can still be in flight. The abort and those parts race. A part that S3 stores after it processed the abort stays in the bucket as storage of an upload that nothing aborts again.

The S3 documentation for `AbortMultipartUpload` describes this case: if part uploads are in progress, they might or might not succeed, and it can be necessary to abort the upload again to free all storage.

### Where

`fail()` calls `cancel()` on every part that is not `NotAssigned`. `UploadPart::cancel` only sets the state to `Canceled` (and frees the buffer of a part that has not started). The HTTP request of a `Started` part keeps going. `fail()` then runs the completion callback and calls `rollback_multi_part_request()` in the same call. `on_part_response` later sees `Canceled`, frees the buffer, and drops its ref. Nothing sends a second abort after the last in-flight part has reported back.

Every caller of `fail()` has this: a part that fails while other parts are in flight (`on_part_response` with no retry left), a failed source stream of `s3.write(key, stream)`, and `writer().end(error)` in #43134. With the default `queueSize` of 5, up to 5 parts can be in flight.

### Possible fix

Send the rollback after every `Started` part has reported back: count the parts in flight in `fail()`, and send the abort from the `Canceled` branch of `on_part_response` when the count reaches zero. An alternative is to send the abort at once and send it one more time after the last in-flight part has reported back.

### Notes

There is no wrong object under the key in this case. The cost is storage of parts that only a bucket lifecycle rule removes.

Related: #43099 (the 204 answer of `AbortMultipartUpload` counts as a failure), #41688 (an upload id that arrives after `fail()` is not aborted).

title: bun install applies a ranged `overrides` key to a dependency pinned at a prerelease that the range does not admit
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+c6b7fcb5b (the semver code on main is the same)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64. The code path has no platform branch.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A dependency that pins an exact prerelease, and a ranged `overrides` key whose range holds that prerelease by semver order but names no prerelease of that major.minor.patch.

```json
{
  "name": "repro",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "uuid": "9.0.0-beta.0" },
  "overrides": { "uuid@<9.0.0": "8.3.2" }
}
```

```bash
bun install
node -p "require('./node_modules/uuid/package.json').version"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`9.0.0-beta.0`. A prerelease satisfies a range only when a comparator of that range names a prerelease of the same major.minor.patch. `<9.0.0` names none, so `9.0.0-beta.0` is outside the selector and the rule must not apply.

- npm 11.16.0 installs `9.0.0-beta.0` from the same `package.json`. It matches a ranged key with `semver.intersects(edgeSpec, keySpec)` (`@npmcli/arborist/lib/override-set.js:112`), and `semver.intersects("9.0.0-beta.0", "<9.0.0")` is `false`.
- Bun's own API agrees: `Bun.semver.satisfies("9.0.0-beta.0", "<9.0.0")` is `false`.

### What do you see instead?

`8.3.2`. Bun applies the rule.

### Additional information

- Cause: a ranged key is matched against the range the edge declares with `Group::intersects` (`src/install/lockfile/OverrideMap.rs:217`). `Group::intersects` (`src/semver/intersects.rs`) compares the bounds by semver order only. `9.0.0-beta.0 < 9.0.0`, so it reports an intersection. It does not apply the prerelease rule.
- The same happens in the local test registry: `"no-deps-tags": "1.0.0-rc.1"` with the key `no-deps-tags@<1.0.0` or `no-deps-tags@>=0.0.0`. Bun installs the override target, npm 11.16.0 keeps `1.0.0-rc.1`.
- This is a sibling of #41371, where the selector has the prerelease bound. #43102 fixes #41371 at the bound that `^`, `~` and x-ranges derive. It does not change this case: a build of that branch also installs `8.3.2`.
- #41377 (closed in favor of #43102) covered this case with one rule inside `intersects` (`Interval::has_version`). That rule also rejects pairs that npm accepts, for example `>=4.0.1 <5.0.0` with `>=5.0.0-alpha.0 <8.0.0`, so it is not the right shape for this fix.

excerpt:
I compared what `bun build` prints for `@scope` with what Chrome 153 does with the source, and with css-cascade-6 and css-nesting-1. #43146 fixes the scope-end selector (`to (...)`). The seven defects below remain. Each one reproduces on 1.4.3-canary.1+c6b7fcb5b and on main 0d3492e353.

Terms: "compiled" means that the targets have no CSS nesting, which is the `bun build` default. "Kept" means that the targets have CSS nesting, or that there are no targets (`--target=bun`). The outputs below are minified.

### 1. The scope-start selector of an `@scope` in a style rule loses the parent rule

```css
.p { @scope (.a) { span { color: red } } }
```

- Compiled output: `@scope(.a){:scope span{color:red}}`. It also styles a `.a` that is not in `.p`.
- Expected: `@scope (.p .a)`. The scope-start selector is relative to the nesting context (css-cascade-6, "Scope Nesting"). Chrome styles only the `.a` in `.p`.
- The kept output is correct.

```css
.p { @scope (> .a) { span { color: red } } }
```

- Both outputs have `@scope(:scope>.a)`, which matches nothing. Chrome reads the source as `.p > .a`.

### 2. A rule in the block of an `@scope` in a style rule gets a `& ` prefix, also when it has `:scope`

```css
.p { @scope (.a) { :scope > .c { color: red } } }
```

- Kept output: `.p{@scope(.a){& :scope>.c{color:red}}}`. Compiled output: `@scope(.a){:scope :scope>.c{color:red}}`.
- Both match nothing, because the scoping root is not its own descendant. Chrome styles the `.c` children of the scoping root.
- Expected: `:scope > .c`, as written. The same rule in a top-level `@scope` prints correctly.

### 3. `&` in the block compiles to `:scope`, which adds specificity

```css
div.c { color: blue }
@scope (.a) { & .c { color: red } }
```

- Compiled output: `@scope(.a){:scope .c{color:red}}`, with specificity (0,2,0). It wins over `div.c` (0,1,1).
- Expected: `:where(:scope) .c`. css-cascade-6: "The `&` selector is defined to behave as `:where(:scope)`", so it adds no specificity. In Chrome the source loses to `div.c`, and the compiled output wins.
- The `& ` prefix of defect 2 compiles the same way: `.p { @scope (.a) { .c {} } }` compiles to `:scope .c`.

### 4. A relative selector in the block of a top-level `@scope` does not parse

```css
@scope (.a) { > .c { color: red } }
```

- Result: `Invalid selector. Empty selector is not allowed`. The build fails. `+ .c` and `~ .c` fail the same way.
- Expected: accepted. A scoped style rule takes a relative selector list (css-c

title: `bun install` links no bin when one value of a `bin` object is not a string
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+c6b7fcb5b. The code on main (0d3492e353) is the same.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64. The code path has no platform branch.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A dependency whose `bin` object has two or more entries, and one value that is not a string.

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/r/mixed && cd /tmp/r
echo '{"name":"foo","dependencies":{"mixed":"./mixed"}}' > package.json
echo '{"name":"mixed","version":"1.0.0","bin":{"mixed-a":"a.js","mixed-b":5}}' > mixed/package.json
printf '#!/usr/bin/env node\nconsole.log("a")\n' > mixed/a.js
bun install --save-text-lockfile
ls node_modules/.bin
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`node_modules/.bin/mixed-a` exists. npm 11.16.0 on the same tree links `mixed-a` and skips `mixed-b`.

### What do you see instead?

The install exits with code 0 and prints no warning. `node_modules/.bin` does not exist, and `bun.lock` records no bin for the package:

```
"mixed": ["mixed@file:mixed", {}],
```

### Additional information

- Cause: the build pass for a `bin` object with two or more entries stops at the first value that is not a string, before it sets the bin of the package (`break 'bin` at `src/install/lockfile/Package.rs:2699` on main). The entries before that value are dropped with it.
- The registry manifest parser has the same early exit for the same shape (`src/install/npm.rs:2495` on main). I read that code. I did not run that path.
- That arm also grows `lockfile.buffers.extern_strings` by two slots for each entry before the loop, and the early exit leaves them in place. I did not find them on disk: `bun.lockb` is 1193 bytes for this package, the same as for a package with no `bin`, and 1258 bytes when both values are strings.
- A `bin` object with one entry whose value is not a string links nothing. That matches npm, because no entry is valid.
- Found in the review of #43145. That PR does not change this arm.

title: ws: frames that arrive before a deferred handleUpgrade() are dropped
`http.ServerResponse.end(cb)`/`write(cb)` fire before the response is flushed
node:http: a WebSocket upgrade from a request body handler stops the parser for the next request on another connection
excerpt:
### What happens

A `node:http` server upgrades a request to a WebSocket from the request's body handler, for example `wss.handleUpgrade()` inside `req.on("end")` for an upgrade request that carries a body. After that, the next request on any other connection of the same server stops the parser after its first request. Requests pipelined behind it in the same read get no answer, and the connection stays open.

| | Node v26.3.0 + ws 8.18.3 | Bun 1.4.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control (no upgrade before) | `["/one","/two"] (connection closed)` | `["/one","/two"] (connection closed)` |
| after the upgrade | `["/one","/two"] (connection closed)` | `["/one"] (no answer to /two after 3 s)` |

The same happens on main at 8f8e16c577.

### Cause

`HttpResponse::upgrade()` (`packages/bun-uws/src/HttpResponse.h`) sets `httpContextData->upgradedWebSocket` when it runs while `HttpContext::onData` parses. Only the request handler in `onData` looks at that field (`if (httpContextData->upgradedWebSocket) return nullptr;` after `route()`). The data handler does not. So after an upgrade from a body handler:

1. The data handler continues with `httpResponseData`, which the upgrade has destroyed. The socket ext now holds the `WebSocketData`. `if (fin) httpResponseData->inStream = nullptr;` writes into it, and the parser that called the data handler (also part of the destroyed `HttpResponseData`) updates `remainingStreamingBytes` after the handler returns.
2. The data handler returns the socket, `onData` takes its normal return path, and nothing resets `upgradedWebSocket`.
3. The next request on another connection runs `route()`, sees the stale field in the request handler and returns `nullptr`. The parser stops, and the tail of `onData` uncorks and returns the WebSocket of the first connection as if this read had upgraded it.

I saw step 3 in an instrumented build: the request handler of connection B read `upgradedWebSocket == <WebSocket of connection A>` with `s == <socket of connection B>`.

`Bun.serve` does not reach this path through `server.upgrade()`: for a request with a body, `server.upgrade(req)` after `await req.text()` returns `false`.

### Repro

`bun repro.cjs` and `bun repro.cjs control`. It needs only `ws`.

```js
// bun upgrade-from-body-handler.cjs [control]
// Connection A: an upgrade request with a body. The server upgrades it when the body has ended.
// Connection B, afterwards: two plain requests in one write. Both must get a response.
const http = require

title: `bun patch <pkg>` leaves a partial package in node_modules when the copy from the cache fails part-way
excerpt:
### What happens

`bun patch <pkg>` deletes `node_modules/<pkg>` and then copies the package from the cache into it (`overwrite_package_in_node_modules_folder` in `src/install/PackageManager/patchPackage.rs`). If the copy fails part-way, the command exits with

```
error: error overwriting folder in node_modules: <errno>
```

and `node_modules/<pkg>` is empty or partial. The installed package is lost.

The copy can fail on a full disk (`ENOSPC`), on an I/O error, on a cache file the user cannot read (`EACCES`), or through the `Global::exit(1)` in `FileCopier::copy` when a destination file cannot be created.

A later `bun install` can accept the partial folder, because it verifies only the name and version in `package.json`. `bun install --force` repairs it.

### Possible fix

Copy the package into a temporary folder in the root `node_modules` first. When the copy is complete, detach and delete the old folder and rename the copy into place (`renameat_concurrently` already handles a destination that exists). A failure in the copy then leaves the installed package as it was.

### Context

Found in the review of #43160. That PR covers the failures before the copy (a missing cache entry) and the failures of `bun patch --commit` around `git diff`. It does not change the copy step. I did not find a way to make the copy fail part-way in a test: `FileCopier` skips symlinks and special files, and the CI containers run as root, so a permission error does not occur.

title: `bun patch <pkg>` removes the bundled dependencies of `<pkg>`, and `--commit` records them as deleted
excerpt:
### What happens

`bun patch <pkg>` breaks a package that bundles dependencies, and `bun patch --commit` makes the damage permanent.

```sh
bun add aws-cdk-lib@2.150.0 constructs
ls node_modules/aws-cdk-lib/node_modules        # 30+ bundled packages (semver, fs-extra, minimatch, ...)

bun patch aws-cdk-lib
ls node_modules/aws-cdk-lib/node_modules        # No such file or directory
bun -e 'const cdk = require("aws-cdk-lib"); new cdk.Stack(new cdk.App(), "S")'
# error: Cannot find package 'semver' from '.../node_modules/aws-cdk-lib/cloud-assembly-schema/lib/manifest.js'

bun install                                     # "no changes", the bundled packages do not come back

echo "// edit" >> node_modules/aws-cdk-lib/index.js
bun patch --commit node_modules/aws-cdk-lib
grep -c '^deleted file mode' patches/aws-cdk-lib@2.150.0.patch    # 933
```

The committed patch is 327 KB. It deletes every file of the bundled packages, so each later install applies those deletions and the package stays broken (`Cannot find package 'semver'`). The deletion headers also carry the absolute path of the local cache (`b/tmp/.../.bun-cache/aws-cdk-lib@2.150.0@@@1/node_modules/...`).

Seen on 1.4.3-canary.1 (c6b7fcb5b). The code is the same on main.

### Cause

All in `src/install/PackageManager/patchPackage.rs`:

- `overwrite_package_in_node_modules_folder` deletes the whole package folder and copies the cache entry back with a skip list of `node_modules`, `.git` and `CMakeFiles`. The skip list matches a directory of that name at any depth. The bundled dependencies live in `<pkg>/node_modules` of the cache entry, so they are not copied back. A nested fixture folder such as `test/fixtures/node_modules` is dropped the same way.
- `do_patch_commit` hides the package's top-level `node_modules` from `git diff` by renaming it away, but only on the `node_modules` side. The cache entry still has the bundled files, so the diff reports all of them as deleted.
- The same `delete_tree` also removes the nested dependencies that bun installed under the package (hoisted linker, version conflict). Those come back on the next install, but the package is broken between `bun patch` and `bun patch --commit`, which is when the user tests the change.

### Expected

- `bun patch <pkg>` keeps everything the package's tarball ships, and keeps the nested dependencies bun installed.
- The committed patch contains only the user's changes.

title: Runtime-Conditional Dependencies for Published Packages
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

JavaScript packages can already select different code paths for different runtimes. Bun supports the `bun` conditional export alongside conditions such as `node`, `import`, `require`, and custom conditions. This lets a single published package expose a Bun-native implementation when executed by Bun and a portable fallback when executed by Node.js.

The dependency graph, however, cannot express the same distinction.

A package may need **no third-party dependency under Bun** because Bun provides a capability natively, while its Node.js fallback may require an additional package. Today the package author must usually choose between two undesirable outcomes:

1. declare the fallback package as a normal dependency, causing Bun consumers to install code they never use; or
2. make the fallback dependency optional/peer-based and force Node.js consumers to perform additional installation steps or discover a missing dependency at runtime.

The desired behavior is straightforward:

* a Bun consumer should install the package once and receive the minimal dependency graph required by the Bun implementation;
* a Node.js consumer should install the same package once and automatically receive the dependencies required by the Node.js implementation;
* consumers should not need runtime-specific package names or manual secondary install commands;
* package managers that do not understand any new Bun-specific metadata must remain correct, even if their install is less optimized.

This is not primarily an “optional dependency” problem. It is a mismatch between **conditional module resolution** and an **unconditional installation graph**.

Consider a library that provides one public API but has two internal implementations:

* **Bun:** uses a capability already built into Bun;
* **Node.js:** uses a third-party fallback package to provide equivalent behavior.

The library can already express the runtime-specific code selection through conditional exports. Bun explicitly documents the `bun` export condition and supports custom conditions as part of module resolution.

What the package cannot express is that the fallback dependency is required only by the Node.js branch.

    P[Published package] --> E[package.json exports]
    P --> D[package.json dependencies]

    E --> C{Runtime condition}
    C -->|Bun| B[Bun-native implementation]
    C -->|Node.js| N[Node-compatible fallback]

    B --> BN[Uses Bun-

title: node:dns Resolver missing resolve4/resolve6 when test runs under `bun test --inspect-wait` with a debugger attached
Segfault when a Bun process receives SIGPWR on Linux (process.kill(pid, 30), kill -PWR <pid>)
excerpt:
### What happens

On Linux, a SIGPWR that the runtime did not send to itself crashes the process.

```js
// repro.mjs
process.kill(process.pid, 30); // SIGPWR. The same from a shell: kill -PWR <pid>
setTimeout(() => console.log("survived"), 150);
```

```
$ bun repro.mjs
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x60
oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code.
$ echo $?
139
```

- Reproduces 3 of 3 on 1.4.3-canary.1+c6b7fcb5b and on a debug build of main b64b63069c. 1.4.0-canary.1+1498d7b77 crashed the same way at address `0x58` in July, so this is not a recent regression.
- An ASAN build reports `SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000060` in `WTF::Thread::signalHandlerSuspendResume` (`wtf/posix/ThreadingPOSIX.cpp`).
- Other ways to reach it: `subprocess.kill("SIGPWR")` on a Bun child, `raise(SIGPWR)` from native code, and `kill -PWR <pid>` from any other process. Container managers send SIGPWR to PID 1 when they stop a container (LXC's default halt signal), so a Bun server that runs as PID 1 crashes on shutdown.
- Node.js v26 terminates with the default action (exit 158), or runs a `process.on("SIGPWR")` listener.

### Cause

JSC suspends and resumes threads (for the GC and the sampling profiler) with a signal, and Bun's WebKit fork uses SIGPWR for it on Linux. The handler treats every delivery as a request from `Thread::suspend()` or `Thread::resume()` and dereferences `targetThread`, which only those two set.

There is a second failure with the same cause. A SIGPWR that lands while a thread is suspended ends the handler's `sigsuspend()` early. `resume()` then returns before its own signal arrives, the handler reads that signal as a new suspend request, and the thread never leaves `sigsuspend()`.

### Fix

oven-sh/WebKit#693 makes the handler act only on a request that `suspend()` or `resume()` published for its own thread. A Bun PR that bumps `WEBKIT_VERSION` and adds tests follows when that change is merged.

A fix on the Bun side only (#33777, closed unmerged) cannot work. It has to tell JSC's own `pthread_kill` from other senders by `siginfo`, and the kernel delivers both as `SI_USER` from pid 0 once `RLIMIT_SIGPENDING` is exhausted. With `ulimit -i 0` such a build hangs in the first GC.

title: `bun patch` reads the `file:` dependency of a registry package from the project root
excerpt:
### What happens

A registry package `outer` declares `"inner": "file:vendor/inner"` and ships `vendor/inner` in its tarball. The hoisted linker links `node_modules/outer/node_modules/inner` to `node_modules/outer/vendor/inner`. `bun patch inner` (and `bun patch node_modules/outer/node_modules/inner`) opens `<project>/vendor/inner` instead:

- If the project has no folder at that path: `error: error overwriting folder in node_modules: ENOENT`. On main the command deletes `node_modules/outer/node_modules/inner` before it fails. #43160 stops the delete.
- If the project has a folder at that path: that unrelated folder is copied into `node_modules/outer/node_modules/inner`, exit 0.

The test registry has a fixture for it: `bundled-file@2.0.0` (`"bundled-file-dep": "file:vendor/bundled-file-dep"`, not bundled).

### Cause

`compute_cache_dir_and_subpath` (`src/install/PackageManager/PackageManagerDirectories.rs`) uses the project root plus the folder path for every `Folder` resolution. That base is right for a path that the root, a workspace, or a local `file:` package declares, because `Package::parse` stores those relative to the project root. A registry manifest's path is stored as written (`Package::from_npm`), relative to the declaring package. The hoisted installer handles that case in `src/install/PackageInstaller.rs` ("One declared by an npm manifest ... is verbatim").

### Notes for a fix

- "The declaring package is a registry package" is not the right test by itself. A root `overrides` entry with a `file:` path is relative to the project root even when the dependency row belongs to a registry package (`Lockfile::is_trusted_folder_dependency` has that exception). A check that missed this refused `bun patch` for an overridden dependency that works today.
- The base directory rule for these folders is changing in #38856, #38994 and #38816. `bun patch` should use the same predicate as the installer, not a copy of it.
- A refusal may be the better shape than a second base directory. `bun install` never applies a patch to a folder dependency (`patched_package_missing_from_cache` finds the folder and marks the package done), and `bun patch --commit` fails for every folder dependency with `ENOENT: failed to read from cache (readlink)`. So a prepared copy of a folder dependency can never become an applied patch.

title: Bun Shell: an external command that never stops writing hangs when its `> ${buf}` target is full
excerpt:
### What happens

An external command that never stops writing never finishes when its stdout goes to a JS buffer. The promise does not settle, and the shell reads and drops the output at pipe speed.

```ts
import { $ } from "bun";
await $`/usr/bin/yes > ${Buffer.alloc(16)}`; // never settles
```

Reproduced on 1.4.3 and on main (Linux x64). `cat /dev/zero > ${buf}` does the same. The `yes` builtin is not affected: it stops when the buffer is full and exits 1.

### Why

`PipeReader::on_read_chunk` (`src/runtime/shell/subproc.rs`) copies each chunk into the buffer with `BufferedOutput::append` and reads until EOF. When the buffer is full, `append` drops the bytes. The child never gets a write error. So a child that never stops writing never reaches EOF, and `Cmd::has_finished` waits for that EOF.

Under bash the writer stops: it gets `ENOSPC` from a full device, or `SIGPIPE` when the reader goes away (`yes | head -c 16`).

### Possible fix

The pipe reader already has a byte budget for the `maxBuffer` option of `Bun.spawn` (`src/io/MaxBuf.rs`). When the budget is gone, the reader stops and the owner signals the child. The shell can give the reader of a `> ${buf}` redirect a budget equal to the length of the buffer.

#43196 makes a command that ends report the overflow and exit 1. It does not change this hang.

title: bun install ignores a failed lifecycle script of a required package when an optional dependency on it comes first
bun install with the isolated linker exits 1 when an optional dependency's tarball cannot be downloaded
bun install: whether a failed download of a peer dependency's package is an error depends on the name order of its parents
bun install deletes a workspace folder when its lifecycle script fails and only an optional dependency links it (isolated linker)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+b52d51348, and main at 663508d6d6

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Workspace `y` lists workspace `x` in `optionalDependencies`. `x` has a `postinstall` script that fails. Run `bun install --filter y` with the isolated linker.

```sh
mkdir -p repro/packages/x repro/packages/y && cd repro
echo '{"name":"root","workspaces":["packages/*"]}' > package.json
echo '{"name":"x","version":"1.0.0","scripts":{"postinstall":"exit 1"}}' > packages/x/package.json
echo 'keep me' > packages/x/src.txt
echo '{"name":"y","version":"1.0.0","optionalDependencies":{"x":"workspace:*"}}' > packages/y/package.json
printf '[install]\nlinker = "isolated"\n' > bunfig.toml
bun install --filter y
ls packages
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`packages/x` still exists. A failed script of an optional dependency removes the installed copy of that dependency. A workspace has no installed copy, its files are the user's source.

### What do you see instead?

```
bun install v1.4.3-canary.1 (b52d51348)
Saved lockfile

Done! Checked 3 packages (no changes) [4.00ms]
y
```

`packages/x` is gone. `bun install --filter y --verbose` prints `warn: deleting optional dependency 'x' due to failed 'postinstall' script`.

### Additional information

`LifecycleScriptSubprocess::deinit_and_delete_package` (`src/install/lifecycle_script_runner.rs`) runs `delete_tree` on the script's `cwd`. For a workspace entry in the isolated store that `cwd` is the workspace folder itself. The hoisted linker does not delete the folder in this case.

The `--filter` matters because then the only linked edge to `x` is the optional one from `y`. Without the filter the root's workspace edge is required, and the install exits 1 with the script error.

title: `bun run --filter`, `--parallel` and `--sequential` ignore `--shell` and bunfig `[run] shell`
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+b52d51348 (also main at fd8422ce4)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (the code path is the same on macOS)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
printf '{"name":"app","version":"1.0.0","scripts":{"which":"echo $0"}}' > package.json
bun run --shell=bun which                 # which            (Bun shell: $0 is the script name)
bun run --shell=system which              # /usr/bin/bash    (system shell)
bun run --shell=bun --filter '*' which    # app which: /usr/bin/bash
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`--shell=bun` (and bunfig `[run] shell = "bun"`) selects Bun's shell for `--filter`, `--parallel`, `--sequential` and `--workspaces` runs, as it does for a plain `bun run <script>`. `docs/runtime/bunfig.mdx` says `shell = "bun"` is the way "to always use Bun's shell instead of the system shell".

### What do you see instead?

The system shell runs the script. On an image without a system shell (`FROM scratch`, `oven/bun:distroless`), `bun run --shell=bun --filter '*' start` and `bun run --shell=bun --parallel start` exit 1 with `error: MissingShell`.

### Additional information

`src/runtime/cli/filter_run.rs` (near line 937) and `src/runtime/cli/multi_run.rs` (near line 910) pick the interpreter by platform only and never read `ctx.debug.use_system_shell`. POSIX always runs `<sh> -c <script>` with the result of `find_shell`. Windows always runs `bun exec <script>`, so `--shell=system` is ignored there.

#43231 fixes the plain `bun run <script>` path (`run_command.rs`) and does not touch these two runners. To honor the flag here changes which shell runs existing `--filter` scripts, so it needs its own change and tests. `echo $0` tells the two shells apart without a special image.

title: Bun.SQL: a query created on a transaction or reserved handle still runs when it is first awaited after the handle closed
Bun.SQL: reserved.release() during a running reserved.begin() lets the nested transaction commit inside the next caller's transaction

bun install: an aborted install leaves a partially-extracted package that later installs never repair (workspaces/isolated linker)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-31-generic x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

When `bun install` aborts because a lifecycle script fails, a package that was mid-extraction is left **partially written** — and **no subsequent `bun install` ever repairs it**. Later installs report `no changes` and exit 0, so the tree looks healthy while a dependency is missing most of its files.

This only reproduces in a **workspace** (isolated linker). The same abort in a single-package (hoisted) project leaves the tree complete.

The abort here is caused by a package that ships `binding.gyp` with **no** install script (`better-sqlite3@13.0.3`, which ships prebuilds). Listing it in `trustedDependencies` makes bun run the implicit `node-gyp rebuild`, which fails on a machine without `node-gyp`. Any failing lifecycle script should do.

```bash
mkdir -p repro/packages/a repro/packages/b && cd repro

cat > package.json <<'JSON'
{ "name": "repro-root", "private": true,
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"],
  "trustedDependencies": ["better-sqlite3"] }
JSON

cat > packages/a/package.json <<'JSON'
{ "name": "pkg-a", "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "better-sqlite3": "13.0.3", "kysely": "0.29.5", "react-aria": "3.50.0" } }
JSON

cat > packages/b/package.json <<'JSON'
{ "name": "pkg-b", "version": "1.0.0",
  "dependencies": { "kysely": "0.29.5", "react-aria": "3.50.0" } }
JSON

# 1. aborts: `node-gyp: command not found` (ensure node-gyp is NOT on PATH)
bun install

# 2. remove the trust so the abort cannot recur, then install again — exits 0
sed -i 's/.*trustedDependencies.*//' package.json
bun install

# 3. inspect
D=$(readlink packages/a/node_modules/react-aria)
find "packages/a/node_modules/react-aria/" -type f | wc -l     # 1079
npm pack react-aria@3.50.0 >/dev/null 2>&1
tar tzf react-aria-3.50.0.tgz | grep -vc '/$'                  # 6960
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The second `bun install` — which succeeds — should repair the incomplete package, or at minimum detect that it is incomplete rather than reporting `no changes`.

### What do you see instead?

`react-aria@3.50.0` is left with **1079 of its 6960 files (15.5%)**. The directory structure is there (all the `useXxx` entry folders), but `dist/` holds **1 of 6706** entries.

Every later `bun install` says:

```
Done! Checked 20 packages (no changes) [2.00ms]
```

title: react-compiler: codegen uses memory quadratic in the number of blocks of a component
excerpt: ### What happens `bun build --react-compiler` uses memory that grows with the square of the number of branches in one component. 4000 sequential `if`/`else` statements take 2.3 GB and 12 s of CPU time. A plain build of the same file takes 26 MB. ### How to reproduce ```js // gen.js import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs"; const N = Number(process.argv[2]); const head = "import {useState} from 'react';\nexport default function App({a}) { const [n] = useState(0); let deep = n; "; const body = Array.from({ length: N }, (_, i) => `if (a > ${i}) { deep = ${i}; } else { deep = ${N + i}; } `).join(""); writeFileSync(`ifelse-${N}.jsx`, head + body + " return {deep}{n}; }\n"); ``` ```sh bun gen.js 4000 bun build --react-compiler --target=browser --external react --outdir=out ifelse-4000.jsx ``` Peak RSS and user CPU time on 1.4.3-canary.1+b52d51348, Linux x64: | input | peak RSS | CPU | | --- | --- | --- | | 1000 `if`/`else` | 223 MB | 0.7 s | | 2000 | 672 MB | 3.0 s | | 4000 | 2347 MB | 12.5 s | | 4000, without `--react-compiler` | 26 MB | 0.01 s | | 4000 statements `deep += a * i;` (no branches) | 169 MB | 0.3 s | The memory follows the number of blocks, not the number of statements. ### Likely cause I did not confirm this with a profiler. It comes from a read of the code, and the size estimate fits. `codegen_block` in `src/react_compiler/codegen.rs` clones the map of temporaries before each block and restores it after: ```rust let temp_snapshot: Temporaries = cx.temp.clone(); let result = codegen_block_no_reset(cx, block)?; cx.temp = temp_snapshot; ``` - `Temporaries` is an `IdMap` in the per-file AST arena. The arena does not free, so each clone stays resident until the file is done. - In the top-level block the map holds every temporary declared so far. The k-th `if` copies about 3k entries for each of its two blocks. For 4000 `if`s at about 50 bytes per entry that is 2.4 GB. - The same clone is made for each reactive scope (`ReactiveStatement::Scope`) and for each nested function (`inner_cx.temp.clone_from(&cx.temp)`). Upstream does the same (`new Map(cx.temp)`), with a garbage collector behind it. ### Possible fix `IdMap` keeps insertion order. A block only adds temporaries, so the restore can truncate the map to its length at block entry. A log of overwritten entries covers the case where a block replaces an existing one. Found while working on #43259, which does not change this.

title: JIT miscompiles String.prototype.codePointAt at end of string: css-tokenizer endOfFile() never true, bun test OOMs
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.13, 1.3.14 (0d9b296a) and 1.4.2, linux x64. Also 1.3.6.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.18.8 x86_64 (Fedora 43), and WSL2.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Under `bun test`, a React 19 + jsdom 28 + `@testing-library/react` suite that runs several `getByRole` queries against rendered DOM makes the process allocate without bound (past 5GB in seconds) and get OOM-killed. Which test dies depends on what ran earlier in the process, and it is nondeterministic (5 of 7 runs in our case).

The runaway loop is `tokenize()` in `@csstools/css-tokenizer@4.0.0` (`dist/index.mjs`), reached through jsdom `getComputedStyle` -> cssstyle border colour setter -> the css colour package cssstyle depends on, `splitValue("rgb(0, 0, 0) rgb(0, 0, 0) rgb(0, 0, 0) rgb(0, 0, 0)")`:

```js
function tokenize(e,n){const t=tokenizer(e,n),o=[];for(;!t.endOfFile();)o.push(t.nextToken());return o.push(t.nextToken()),o}
// inside tokenizer():
//   nextToken(){ ... const n=d.source.codePointAt(d.cursor); if(void 0===n) return [c.EOF,"",-1,-1,void 0]; ... }
//   endOfFile(){ return void 0===d.source.codePointAt(d.cursor) }
```

Once JIT-tiered, `nextToken()` sees `undefined` for `codePointAt(cursor)` at the end of the string and returns an EOF token, while `endOfFile()` (inlined into `tokenize`, which is inlined into `splitValue`) sees a number for the same receiver and index, so the loop never exits.

Standalone loops calling `codePointAt(length)` on trimmed substrings (millions of iterations, both directly and through `@csstools/css-tokenizer`'s `tokenizer()` API) do not reproduce it. Any JS-level instrumentation of `String.prototype.codePointAt` or of the `tokenize` loop makes it disappear (0 of 6 runs), so it depends on what the DFG/FTL inlined.

I cannot share the app, but I can run any diagnostic you suggest against the reproducing suite.

### What is the expected behaviour?

`endOfFile()` returns `true` when `cursor === source.length`, the same answer `nextToken()` gets one call earlier.

### What do you see instead?

The token array grows until the kernel kills the process. Captured with gdb on `bun-linux-x64-profile` at 1.4GB RSS, by walking the `$rbp` CallFrame chain and reading `CodeBlock->m_ownerExecutable`:

```
JS #0 nextToken (node_modules/@csstools/css-tokenizer/dist/index.mjs)
JS #1 splitValue (the css colour package, dist/cjs/index.cjs)   <- tokenize() inlined here
JS #2 prepareBorderStringValue (node_modules/csssty

title: `bun why <workspace>@<version>` finds nothing: the version part is compared with `workspace:<path>`
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+b52d51348 (also main at 511ddb3a27)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (the code path is the same on every platform)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir -p why-ws/packages/pkg-a && cd why-ws
printf '{"name":"ws-root","version":"1.0.0","workspaces":["packages/*"]}' > package.json
printf '{"name":"pkg-a","version":"1.2.3"}' > packages/pkg-a/package.json
bun install
bun why 'pkg-*'          # pkg-a@workspace:packages/pkg-a
bun why 'pkg-*@1.2.3'    # error: No packages matching 'pkg-*@1.2.3' found in lockfile
bun why 'pkg-*@^1'       # error: No packages matching 'pkg-*@^1' found in lockfile
bun why 'pkg-*@*'        # error: No packages matching 'pkg-*@*' found in lockfile
```

The steps use a glob because, on 1.4.3, an exact name with a version matches nothing at all. #43284 fixes that. With #43284, `bun why pkg-a@1.2.3` and `bun why 'pkg-a@*'` fail in the same way as the glob.

### What is the expected behavior?

The version part of the query is compared with the version of the workspace package (`1.2.3`, from its `package.json`). `*` matches every package. npm 11.16.0 does this: `npm explain pkg-a@1.2.3` and `npm explain 'pkg-a@*'` print the workspace package, and `npm explain 'pkg-a@^2'` prints `No dependencies found matching pkg-a@^2`.

### What do you see instead?

`error: No packages matching '<query>' found in lockfile`, exit 1. Only the resolution string matches: `bun why 'pkg-*@workspace:packages/pkg-a'` and `bun why 'pkg-*@workspace'` print the package.

### Additional information

`WhyCommand::exec_with_manager` in `src/runtime/cli/why_command.rs` builds the version string from the resolution (`pkg_resolution[pkg_idx].fmt(..)`). For a workspace package that string is `workspace:<path>`. `GlobPattern::matches_version` cannot parse it as a semver version, so it falls back to a string compare with the query, and `1.2.3`, `^1` and `*` all fail.

The lockfile has the real version: `bun.lock` stores `"version": "1.2.3"` for the workspace, and `Lockfile::workspace_versions` holds it after the load.

The same fallback applies to every resolution that is not a semver version. For example, with a dependency resolved to `github:user/repo#abc1234`, `bun why 'fo*@*'` finds nothing. Those packages have no version to compare a range with, but `*` can still match them.

docs: `Subprocess.resourceUsage().maxRSS` on Linux is never lower than the spawner's peak RSS
excerpt:
### What is missing

The documentation and the JSDoc of `Subprocess.resourceUsage()` (`packages/bun-types/bun.d.ts`, `docs/runtime/child-process.mdx`) describe `maxRSS` as the peak memory of the child. On Linux that is not the whole story.

`maxRSS` is `ru_maxrss` from `wait4`. On Linux that value survives exec: the kernel folds the peak of the address space that the child leaves at exec into the child (`exec_mmap` calls `setmax_mm_hiwater_rss`). `Bun.spawn` uses vfork semantics, so that address space is the one of the process that calls `Bun.spawn`. The reported value is max(peak RSS of the spawner, peak RSS of the child).

### Reproduction

```js
const big = process.argv[2] === "big" ? Buffer.alloc(700 * 1024 * 1024, 1) : null;
const proc = Bun.spawn({ cmd: [process.execPath, "-e", "0"], stdout: "ignore", stderr: "ignore" });
await proc.exited;
console.log(Math.round(proc.resourceUsage().maxRSS / 1048576), "MB", big?.length ?? "");
```

Linux x64, bun 1.4.3-canary: 31 MB without `big`, 731 MB with it. The child is the same in both runs. macOS and Windows do not do this.

### Suggested change

Add one sentence to the JSDoc of `maxRSS` and to the docs page: on Linux the value is never lower than the peak RSS of the process that spawned the child. A caller that needs the peak of the child alone must spawn it from a small process.

Found while working on #43192. The test harness now has `runCommandMaxRSS` for this reason.

title: A syntax error in bunfig.toml or .npmrc can print part of a secret when the line is longer than 120 bytes
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+b52d51348

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir leak && cd leak && echo '{}' > package.json
node -e 'require("fs").writeFileSync("bunfig.toml", "[install]\ntoken = \"" + "SECRET".repeat(12) + "\" ] # " + "x".repeat(120) + "\n")'
NO_COLOR=1 bun install
```

The second line of `bunfig.toml` is 207 bytes long. The stray `]` at byte 83 is a syntax error.

### What is the expected behavior?

The printed source line masks the value of `token`, as it does for a shorter line:

```
2 | token = "************************************************************************" ] # xxxx
```

### What do you see instead?

The last 38 bytes of the token are printed. `FORCE_COLOR=1` prints the same bytes.

```
2 | ETSECRETSECRETSECRETSECRETSECRETSECRET" ] # xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
                                                                                       ^
error: Expected a newline or end of file after a key/value pair
    at /tmp/leak/bunfig.toml:2:84
```

### Additional information

The cut comes before the redaction.

- `Location::init_or_null_impl` (`src/ast/lib.rs:808`) keeps only about 120 bytes of a long line when more than 80 bytes follow the error: 40 bytes before the error and 80 after it. It does this when the diagnostic is created.
- The redaction runs later, in the printer (`fmt_javascript` with `redact_sensitive_information`, `src/bun_core/fmt.rs:1802`, and `starts_with_secret`, `src/bun_core/lib.rs:2094`). It knows a secret by the key in front of it: `token`, `_authToken`, `_auth`, `password`, `_password`, `email`.
- When the key is more than 40 bytes to the left of the error, the cut drops the key. The printer then sees a plain string and prints it.

The same applies to `.npmrc`, which uses the same flag (`src/ini/lib.rs`). A cut can also split a UUID or an `npm_` token, which the redaction only matches whole.

`Log::add_formatted_msg` and `Log::add_error_opts` have `redact_sensitive_information` in hand when they build the `Location`. One possible fix is to keep the whole line for such a message.

Found while bounding the excerpt that the printer writes for a long line. That change leaves a redacted line whole for this reason. It does not change the cut described here.

title: `bun test --rerun-each --coverage`: a test file that runs again reports only its last run, and an ES module test file loses its row
excerpt:
### What happens

`bun test --coverage --rerun-each=N` reports wrong coverage for a test file that bun evaluates again. This needs `coverageSkipTestFiles = false`, because the default leaves test files out of the report. Files that the test file imports are not evaluated again, so their rows are correct.

- An ES module test file has no row when N is 2 or more. `All files` shows `0.00 | 0.00`, and the lcov file is empty.
- A CommonJS test file shows only its last evaluation. A line that ran only in an earlier run shows as not covered, so a `coverageThreshold` can fail. Today this needs #43317, because 1.4.3 evaluates a CommonJS test file only once under `--rerun-each`.
- With `--isolate` both cases report `100.00 | 100.00`.

### Repro (ES module test file, 1.4.3-canary.1+b52d51348)

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
printf '[test]\ncoverageSkipTestFiles = false\n' > bunfig.toml
cat > b.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";
test("t", () => { expect(1).toBe(1); });
EOF
bun test --coverage --rerun-each=1 ./b.test.ts
bun test --coverage --rerun-each=2 ./b.test.ts
```

`--rerun-each=1`:

```
All files  |  100.00 |  100.00 |
 b.test.ts |  100.00 |  100.00 |
```

`--rerun-each=2`:

```
All files  |    0.00 |    0.00 |
```

### Repro (CommonJS test file, with #43317)

In the same directory:

```sh
cat > a.test.cjs <<'EOF'
const { test, expect } = require("bun:test");
globalThis.evaluations = (globalThis.evaluations ?? 0) + 1;
function onlyInRun1() {
  return "run1";
}
if (globalThis.evaluations === 1) onlyInRun1();
test("t", () => { expect(1).toBe(1); });
EOF
bun test --coverage --rerun-each=3 ./a.test.cjs
```

The row for `a.test.cjs` shows line 3 as not covered. With `--rerun-each=1` it is `100.00 | 100.00`.

### Cause, as far as I found it

- Coverage keeps one `ByteRangeMapping` for each path. `ByteRangeMapping__generate` (`src/sourcemap_jsc/CodeCoverage.rs`) runs for every new `SourceProvider` and overwrites the `source_id` of that entry.
- The report asks JSC for the basic blocks of that one source ID (`CodeCoverage__withBlocksAndFunctions` in `src/jsc/bindings/CodeCoverage.cpp`). Every rerun transpiles the test file again and gets a new source ID, so the report sees the last evaluation only.
- Under `--isolate`, the source provider cache gives every rerun the same `SourceProvider`, so the counts add up.
- I did not find why the last source ID of an ES module test file has no basic blocks at all.

title: `bun test --rerun-each`: a rerun that registers no tests is silent
excerpt:
### What happens

The `--rerun-each` loop in `TestCommand::run` (`src/runtime/cli/test_command.rs`) does not compare a rerun with run 1. When a rerun registers no tests, bun prints the file header and nothing else. The summary counts only run 1, and the exit code is 0. So a bug in the loop stays silent.

Known cases:

- #13493: the second iteration was skipped.
- A CommonJS test file ran only once (#43317). Output on 1.4.3:

```
c.test.cjs: (run #1)
(pass) cjs test [0.03ms]

c.test.cjs: (run #2)

c.test.cjs: (run #3)

 1 pass
 0 fail
Ran 1 test across 1 file.
```

### Proposal

After each rerun, compare the number of tests that the file registered with the number from run 1. Report the file when a rerun registers 0 tests and another run of the same file registered more than 0. This narrow condition matches the known cases. A check for any difference would also fire on a file that registers tests conditionally.

These points are open for a maintainer:

- The report is an error for the file, or a warning.
- The check also applies under `--isolate`, or only without it.
- The check counts tests only, or hooks too.

#43184 changes the same block of the loop. This change fits best after that PR lands.

### Related behaviour in the same loop

When the load of a file fails on rerun k (for example a throw at the top level), `run` returns from the `Status::Rejected` arm. The reruns k+1..N of that file do not happen. The failure itself is reported (`1 fail`, exit code 1).

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)"
cat > b.test.mjs <<'EOF'
import { test } from "bun:test";
globalThis.evaluations = (globalThis.evaluations ?? 0) + 1;
if (globalThis.evaluations === 2) throw new Error("boom on evaluation 2");
test("t", () => {});
EOF
bun test --rerun-each=3 ./b.test.mjs
```

1.4.3-canary.1+b52d51348 prints run #1 and run #2, then `1 pass`, `1 fail`, `Ran 2 tests across 1 file.` There is no run #3.

title: Bun.SQL (postgres): an array with explicit bounds (`[0:2]={1,2,3}`, `indkey::int2[]`) fails with ERR_POSTGRES_UNSUPPORTED_ARRAY_FORMAT
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+b52d51348 (the code on main is the same)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64. The code path has no platform branch.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Select a PostgreSQL array whose lower bound is not 1. The server prints such an array with its bounds in front: `[0:2]={1,2,3}`. The system catalogs have these arrays: `int2vector` and `oidvector` start at 0, so `pg_index.indkey::int2[]` and `pg_proc.proargtypes::oid[]` arrive in this form. A slice assignment such as `update t set a[0:1] = '{1,2}'` makes one in a user table.

```ts
import { SQL } from "bun";

const sql = new SQL({ url: process.env.DATABASE_URL, max: 1 });
const show = (p: Promise<any>) =>
  p.then(
    r => JSON.stringify([...r]),
    e => "REJECTED " + e.code,
  );

console.log(await show(sql`select '[0:2]={1,2,3}'::text[] as v`));
console.log(await show(sql`select '[0:2]={1.5,2,3}'::float8[] as v`));
console.log(await show(sql`select indkey::int2[] as v from pg_index where indexrelid = 'pg_class_oid_index'::regclass`));
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The elements, with the bounds dropped. node-postgres 8.11.1 returns this for the three queries:

```
["1","2","3"]
[1.5,2,3]
[1]
```

### What do you see instead?

Each query rejects:

```
REJECTED ERR_POSTGRES_UNSUPPORTED_ARRAY_FORMAT
REJECTED ERR_POSTGRES_UNSUPPORTED_ARRAY_FORMAT
REJECTED ERR_POSTGRES_UNSUPPORTED_ARRAY_FORMAT
```

The error message is `Failed to read data`. The queries that wait behind the failed one on that connection reject with the same error (#43187 changes that part).

### Additional information

`parse_array` in `src/sql_jsc/postgres/DataCell.rs` requires the text to start with `{`:

```rust
if bytes.len() < 2 || bytes[0] != opening_brace {
    return Err(AnyPostgresError::UnsupportedArrayFormat);
}
```

`array_out` (`src/backend/utils/adt/arrayfuncs.c`) writes the decoration `[l1:u1][l2:u2]...=` before the first `{` when a lower bound is not 1. The decoder has no case for it. node-postgres (`postgres-array`) skips the text up to the `=`.

The binary path does not have the problem: `select '[0:2]={1,2,3}'::int4[] as v where ${1} = 1` returns `Int32Array [1, 2, 3]`, because the binary decoder ignores the lower bound.

title: A triple-quoted secret in bunfig.toml is printed in the clear by a config diagnostic
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir leak && cd leak && echo '{}' > package.json
printf '[install]\ntoken = """SECRETVALUE""" ]\n' > bunfig.toml
NO_COLOR=1 bun install
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The printed source line masks the value, as it does for `token = "SECRETVALUE" ]`:

```
2 | token = "***********" ]
```

### What do you see instead?

```
2 | token = """SECRETVALUE""" ]
                              ^
error: Expected a newline or end of file after a key/value pair
    at /tmp/leak/bunfig.toml:2:30
```

`FORCE_COLOR=1` prints the same value.

### Additional information

TOML allows a multi-line basic string (`"""..."""`) or literal string (`'''...'''`) on one line, and the parser accepts both (`src/parsers/toml.rs`).

The redaction reads the value after a sensitive key with a quote scanner that stops at the first matching quote. In `starts_with_redacted_item` (`src/bun_core/lib.rs:2058`), `""` is an empty value, so the scanner masks nothing and the rest of the line prints as is. The color highlighter in `src/bun_core/fmt.rs` stops at the same place.

Found while reviewing #43316. That PR does not change this case.
