title: Bun Shell: the output of a command substitution is not split on a tab
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9 (also main at 6d504dd983)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (the code path is platform independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
import { $ } from "bun";
await $`echo $(printf 'a\tb\tc')`;
```

### What is the expected behavior?

bash and dash print `a b c`. The output of an unquoted command substitution is split into fields on the default `IFS`: space, tab and newline. `echo` gets three arguments.

### What do you see instead?

```
a	b	c
```

`echo` gets one argument that contains the two tabs. Tab-separated output from tools like `cut`, `awk` or `git` does not split into words.

### Additional information

- `post_subshell_expansion` (`src/runtime/shell/states/Expansion.rs:548`) turns each newline into a space and then splits on runs of `b' '` only (lines 579 and 585). A tab is never a separator there.
- Do not add the tab to that loop before the operands of `[[ ]]` stop being split. `CondExpr` expands each operand with the same splitting expansion (`src/runtime/shell/states/CondExpr.rs:69`). `[[ -f $(echo 'my file') ]]` is false in Bun today and true in bash, because the operand is split on the space. `[[ -f $(printf 'my\tfile') ]]` is true today only because a tab does not split. A tab split alone makes that case false too.
- #33552 was an earlier attempt. It made the split follow `IFS`. It was closed as stale, with no review from a maintainer.
- The lexer has the same gap for a tab in the script text. That part has its own fix and does not touch this layer.

title: Bun Shell: `for`, `while` and other unsupported reserved words run as commands, and the loop body runs once
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9 (also main at 6d504dd983)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (the code path is platform independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
import { $ } from "bun";

const f = await $`for f in one two three; do
  echo "f=[$f]"
done`.nothrow().quiet();
console.log(JSON.stringify(f.stdout.toString()), f.exitCode);

const w = await $`while false; do
  echo BODY
done
echo tail`.nothrow().quiet();
console.log(JSON.stringify(w.stdout.toString()), w.exitCode);
```

The same happens in a `.sh` file that `bun run` executes. A one-line loop (`for f in a b; do echo $f; done`) does not run its body, because `do echo $f` is one command named `do`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Bun Shell does not support `for`, `while`, `until`, `case`, `select` or `function`. A script that uses one of them must fail before it runs a command, the way `echo hi &` fails today with `Background commands "&" are not supported yet.`

### What do you see instead?

```
"f=[]\n" 1
"BODY\ntail\n" 0
```

stderr has `bun: command not found: for`, `bun: command not found: do` and `bun: command not found: done`. The shell looks up each reserved word as a command, reports that it does not exist, and continues with the next statement. So each line of the loop body runs once as a plain command, with the loop variable empty. The body of `while false` runs, and the script exits 0.

This can lose data. `for f in a b c; do rm -rf "$dir/$f"; done` runs `rm -rf "$dir/"` once.

### Additional information

- `parse_compound_cmd` (`src/shell_parser/parse.rs:969`) special-cases only `(`, `if` and `[[`. Every other word goes to `parse_simple_cmd`, which takes `for`, `do` and `done` as command names.
- #36196 was an earlier fix: a parse error for these words in command position, with quoted and interpolated words left alone. It was closed as stale, with no review from a maintainer.
- Today a tab-indented loop body does not run, because the lexer does not split words on a tab and each body line fails with `command not found: \trm`. When the lexer splits on a tab, a tab-indented body behaves like a space-indented body, and this bug reaches it too.

### What

On Bun 1.4.2 (Linux x64), `JSON.stringify` on an object with a circular reference is pathologically slow, and the indented (`null, 2`) path is ~15x slower than the compact path. Node.js 22 throws the same `TypeError` essentially instantly.

### Repro

```js
const circular = { name: "x", items: Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, i) => ({ i, text: "y".repeat(50) })) };
circular.self = circular;
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) { try { JSON.stringify(circular, null, 2); } catch {} }
```

### Measurements (20 iterations each, ms/op, same machine)

| call                              | bun 1.4.2 | node 22.16 |
|-----------------------------------|-----------|------------|
| `JSON.stringify(plain)`           | 0.01      | 0.01       |
| `JSON.stringify(plain, null, 2)`  | 0.01      | 0.01       |
| `JSON.stringify(circular)`        | ~120      | 0.05       |
| `JSON.stringify(circular, null, 2)` | ~1750   | 0.09       |

### Expected

Throw `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON` at roughly plain-input speed (Node: < 0.1 ms).

### Impact

Any code that stringifies user-provided or deeply nested data (with or without indentation) pays up to seconds of CPU before the exception fires. We hit this in a payload-display helper; our current workaround is to probe with a compact stringify first, which still costs ~120 ms per call on cyclic input.

### Environment

- Bun 1.4.2, Linux x64 (Fedora 44)
- Node v22.16.0 for comparison

excerpt:
### Environment

- Bun: `1.4.2`
- OS: Fedora Linux 44, x86_64
- Command: `bun test <large-suite> --parallel=6` — the stalled process was a worker started with `--test-worker --isolate --timeout=5000 --max-concurrency=20`. The suite in question: ~177 files / ~3,100 tests.

### What happened

After a sufficiently long run of a large test suite with parallelism enabled, one isolated worker entered a state in which **timer-driven macro tasks no longer appeared to advance**.

The affected code is an application-level polling wait whose normal progress depends on real time plus a timer-backed sleep/timeout. In the affected worker the wait did not converge: the worker repeatedly executed the polling path, consumed approximately 99% CPU, and did **not** honor its timer-based timeout.

This is an observation, not a confirmed root cause: the behavior is consistent with macro-task/timer scheduling being starved or otherwise no longer progressing in that worker. We could not isolate a minimal JavaScript-only reproducer.

Impact:

- A test worker can stay hot instead of timing out or completing.
- The enclosing `bun test` invocation can stall indefinitely (until externally killed).
- This is particularly disruptive for long-running, isolated, parallel test suites, because a single worker prevents the whole suite from completing.

### Reproduction

What we have is the full-suite recipe:

```sh
bun test <large-suite> --parallel=6
```

Let it run long enough; in the affected runs, one isolated worker stopped making progress in a timer-based wait and remained at ~99% CPU.

Minimization attempts (time-boxed, unsuccessful): full suite vs. smaller slices (including single files that complete normally on their own, e.g. a TUI test file completes 190 tests in ~30s), repeated isolated/parallel runs, and ablation runs. Even under `--isolate` and parallel load, a pending timer (`setTimeout`-based sleep/timeout) should eventually run, or the test worker should enforce the configured per-test timeout and terminate the test. A timer-based wait should not degrade into an unbounded high-CPU polling loop.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{"name":"repro","gypfile":false}' > package.json
echo "{'targets':[{'target_name':'x','sources':['missing.cc']}]}" > binding.gyp

```

...
gyp ERR! not ok
error: install script from "repro" exited with 1
```

It also happens for dependencies. `better-sqlite3@13.0.3` sets `"gypfile": false`, has no install script and ships prebuilds, but `bun add better-sqlite3@13.0.3` still runs `node-gyp rebuild`. That fetches `node-gyp@latest` and the Node headers and runs gyp and make, and it builds nothing, because the prebuild is what gets loaded. So the install needs Python, make and network access for no reason. When node-gyp can't write its cache folder (in a sandboxed install, for example), the install fails with exit code 1 even though the package works.

### What is the expected behavior?

No default `node-gyp rebuild` when `gypfile` is `false`, same as npm. `@npmcli/run-script` only adds it when:

```js
!scripts.install && !scripts.preinstall && gypfile !== false && await isNodeGypPackage(path)
```

### What do you see instead?

`node-gyp rebuild` runs, and the install fails if node-gyp does.

### Additional information

The places that add the default script only check for an empty `install` / `preinstall` and an existing `binding.gyp`: `src/install/lockfile/Package/Scripts.rs` (twice) and `load_root_lifecycle_scripts` in `src/install/PackageManager/PackageManagerLifecycle.rs`.

For a local `file:` dependency it only shows up if the package has some other lifecycle script, such as a `postinstall`. better-sqlite3 from the registry hits it without one.

title: bun build: a CSS url() gets part of the file path appended when a directory or file name has a literal # or ?
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (the change that causes it is in the 1.4.0, 1.4.1 and 1.4.2 tags, and main at 73df7bb270 has it too)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir -p "C#" && head -c 200000 /dev/zero > "C#/logo.png"
printf 'body { background: url("./C#/logo.png"); }\n' > style.css
bun build ./style.css --outdir=out
grep -o 'url([^)]*)' out/*.css
```

### What is the expected behavior?

```
url("./logo-68tr27nb.png")
```

Bun 1.3.5 prints this. esbuild 0.18.6 prints `url(./logo-DFVMILRG.png)` for the same input.

### What do you see instead?

```
url("./logo-68tr27nb.png#/logo.png")
```

The text after the first `#` or `?` of the specifier is appended to the rewritten URL, although it is part of the file path.

Other shapes of the same bug:

- A small asset is inlined: `url("data:image/png;base64,...#/logo.png")`.
- A `?` in a name: `url("./what?/logo.svg")` becomes `url("./logo-<hash>.svg?/logo.svg")`.
- The dev server prints `url("/_bun/asset/<hash>.png#/logo.png")`.
- An absolute specifier under a `C#` directory, `url("/home/me/C#/proj/img/logo.svg")`, becomes `url("./logo-<hash>.svg#/proj/img/logo.svg")`. Local path segments go into the output CSS, and the bytes and the hash of the CSS chunk depend on where the project is checked out.

### Additional information

I found this when I read the code for #43854. No user reported it, and I did not find a public stylesheet that hits it. In the directory-name case the asset still loads, because a browser ignores an unknown fragment on an image. An SVG consumer that reads the fragment (`#svgView`, a `mask` or `clip-path` id) gets a fragment that the author did not write.

It is a regression from #33685, first released in 1.4.0. Before that change the CSS printer appended nothing. Since that change, `Printer::get_import_record_url` (`src/css/printer.rs`) takes the suffix from the text of the specifier: everything from the first `?` or `#`. The resolver tries the specifier as written first and removes the `?query#fragment` only when that fails (`src/resolver/resolver.rs`, the retry for `kind.is_from_css()`). For `./C#/logo.png` the first try finds the file and nothing is removed, but the printer still appends `#/logo.png`.

### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (1.3.5 does the same)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
head -c 200000 /dev/zero > "icon#1.png"
printf '.a { background: url("./icon#1.png"); }\n' > style.css
bun build ./style.css --outdir=out
ls out && grep -o 'url([^)]*)' out/*.css
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A URL that a browser resolves to the copied file `out/icon#1-68tr27nb.png`, for example `url("./icon%231-68tr27nb.png")`.

### What do you see instead?

```
url("./icon#1-68tr27nb.png")
```

A browser ends the path at the `#` and requests `./icon`, which does not exist. (1.4.0 to 1.4.2 also append `#1.png`. That part is #43907.)

The same happens for a `?` or a `%` in the file name. It also happens for a directory name when the asset naming has `[dir]`:

```sh
mkdir -p "C#" && head -c 200000 /dev/zero > "C#/logo.png"
printf '.a { background: url("./C#/logo.png"); }\n' > style.css
bun build ./style.css --outdir=out --asset-naming="[dir]/[name]-[hash].[ext]"
# url("./C#/logo-68tr27nb.png")  -> a browser requests ./C
```

### Additional information

I found this when I worked on #43907. No user reported it. esbuild 0.18.6 prints the same kind of URL (`url(./icon#1-55H3Y73Q.png)`).

The output path of a copied asset replaces a placeholder in the printed chunk, as raw bytes (`IntermediateOutput::code_with_source_map_shifts`, `src/bundler/Chunk.rs`). #41793 percent-encodes that path for HTML chunks (`src` and `href`). CSS chunks go through the same join and are not covered by it.

1.4.2+744846f84 (1.3.5 does the same)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir -p "C#" && head -c 200000 /dev/zero > "C#/logo.png"
printf '.a { background: url("./C#/logo.png?v=2"); }\n' > style.css
bun build ./style.css --outdir=out
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The build finds `C#/logo.png` and prints `url("./logo-68tr27nb.png?v=2")`.

### What do you see instead?

```
error: Could not resolve: "./C#/logo.png?v=2"
```

`url("./C#/logo.png")` resolves, and `url("./logo.png?v=2")` resolves. The two together do not.

### Additional information

I found this when I worked on #43907. No user reported it. esbuild 0.18.6 fails the same way (`Could not resolve "./C#/logo.png?v=2"`).

For an import from CSS or HTML, the resolver tries the specifier as written. When that fails, it tries one more time without the text from the first `?` or `#` (`src/resolver/resolver.rs`, the retry for `kind.is_from_css()`). Here the first `#` is part of the directory name, so the retry looks for `./C` and gives up. A retry at each later `?` or `#` would find `./C#/logo.png` with the suffix `?v=2`.

The CSS printer puts the removed suffix back on the rewritten URL. With #43911 it reads one flag on the import record and takes the suffix from the first `?` or `#` of the specifier. A retry at a later position needs the record to carry the position of the cut, not only the flag.

fs.watch on macOS: three differences from libuv in how FSEvents events are filtered
excerpt:
### What happens

On macOS, `FSEventsLoop::events_cb` in `src/runtime/node/fs_events.rs` decides which FSEvents events a watcher reports. It differs from libuv's `uv__fsevents_event_cb` in three cases:

1. An event with a system flag is reported as a `change` of the watched directory. libuv reports nothing.
2. The removal of the watched directory is not reported. libuv 1.49.0 and later reports `rename`.
3. A non-recursive watcher on `/` reports nothing. libuv reports a direct child as `/name`.

Found during the work on #43923. That PR does not change these.

**These are not observed at runtime.** I have no macOS machine. They come from reading the code next to libuv, and from a copy of both filters that I ran over 1680 combinations of watched path, event path, recursion and flags.

### Cause

1. libuv drops every event that carries `UserDropped`, `KernelDropped`, `EventIdsWrapped`, `HistoryDone`, `Mount`, `Unmount` or `RootChanged` ([fsevents.c#L249-L251](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/v1.52.0/src/unix/fsevents.c#L249-L251)). `events_cb` has no such check. An event of this kind names the watched path and has no `ItemIsDir` flag. So `is_file` is true ([fs_events.rs#L551](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/4227e466c489/src/runtime/node/fs_events.rs#L551)), the empty remainder takes the basename branch, and the watcher reports `change` with the name of the watched directory.
2. An event whose path equals the watched directory is dropped ([fs_events.rs#L557-L560](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/4227e466c489/src/runtime/node/fs_events.rs#L557-L560)). libuv removed the same check in 1.49.0 ("fsevents: detect watched directory removal").
3. The path of a root watcher keeps its leading `/`. The subdirectory filter drops each path that contains a `/` ([fs_events.rs#L577-L583](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/4227e466c489/src/runtime/node/fs_events.rs#L577-L583)). libuv starts that search after the first byte ([fsevents.c#L296-L301](https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/v1.52.0/src/unix/fsevents.c#L296-L301)).

### How to check on a Mac

Item 2 has a short script. By libuv's code, a Node version with libuv 1.49.0 or later prints `rename` with the directory name. By the code above, Bun prints nothing.

```js
const fs = require("fs");
const os = require("os");
const path = require("path");

const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "watched-"));
fs.watch(dir, (event, filename) => console.log(event, filename));
setTimeout(() => fs.rmdirSync(dir), 500

title: `Bun.inspect()` prints `0.0 ZB` for a Request or Response whose file body is a slice or has no known size
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84. Also main at 4227e466c.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const header = value => Bun.inspect(value).split("\n")[0];

const slice = Bun.file(import.meta.path).slice(0, 7);
console.log(slice.size); // 7
console.log(header(new Response(slice))); // Response (0.0 ZB) {, expected Response (7 bytes) {

const missing = Bun.file("/path/that/does/not/exist");
console.log(header(new Request("http://example.com/", { method: "POST", body: missing }))); // Request (0.0 ZB) {
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The header shows the size of the body: `Response (7 bytes) {` for the slice. For a file with no known size it shows no number that looks like a size.

### What do you see instead?

The header shows `0.0 ZB` for a slice of a file, for a missing file, and for a file that is not seekable (`/dev/zero`, `Bun.stdin`). Reads are correct: `.bytes()` on the slice gives 7 bytes.

### Additional information

`Body::Value::size` (`src/runtime/webcore/Body.rs`) takes the number from `Blob::get_size_for_bindings` (`src/runtime/webcore/Blob.rs`). That function returns `u64::MAX` when `seekable` of the file store is not `Some(true)`. A slice already has a size, so nothing stats the file and `seekable` stays `None`. The size formatter prints `u64::MAX` as `0.0 ZB`.

#6584 reported this header for a whole file (`4.50 PB` at that time). #20933 corrected it for a whole file.

#36296 edits the same line of `Body::Value::size`.

title: prompt() returns null on a bare Enter when no default is given, so it cannot be told apart from end of input
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (744846f84), macOS arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
bun -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(prompt("Q?")))'
```

Press Enter without typing anything.

### What is the expected behavior?

`""`, the empty string the person responded with.

The HTML standard declares `prompt(optional DOMString message = "", optional DOMString default = "")`, so an omitted default is the empty string, and step 8 ("Let result be null if the user aborts, or otherwise the string that the user responded with") returns it. Browsers return `""` here.

`null`, the same value as pressing Ctrl-D or closing standard input.

### Additional information

A script that asks "Press Enter to continue, or Ctrl-D to stop" cannot use `prompt` to tell the two answers apart. Passing a default works around it, but prints the default in brackets after the question. We read one line from `console` instead.

bun update <name> keeps the old lockfile row for URL/local tarball deps (stale integrity and dependency list)
excerpt:
### What happens

For a dependency resolved from a URL or local tarball, `bun update <name>` re-downloads the tarball and re-extracts the cache, and `node_modules` receives the new files. But the lockfile keeps the **old** package row: the old integrity hash, and the old dependency list. Any new dependencies or `bin` entries declared by the new tarball's `package.json` are never installed or linked.

A later clean `bun install --frozen-lockfile` then fails with `Integrity check failed`, because the pinned hash is the old one while the URL now serves the new bytes.

### Repro

Serve a tarball at a fixed URL. v1 has no dependencies. v2 adds `"dependencies": {"is-number": "7.0.0"}` and `"bin": {"mybin": "./cli.js"}`, at the same URL.

```console
$ bun install                    # v1 served
$ # switch the server to v2
$ bun update my-url-pkg
$ cat node_modules/my-url-pkg/index.js     # new file content: refreshed
$ ls node_modules/is-number                # missing
$ ls node_modules/.bin/mybin               # missing
$ grep sha512 bun.lock                     # still v1's hash
```

Verified on main at `73ab3ddc7` (1.4.0-canary) with no other changes applied.

### Cause

The resolve phase re-downloads the tarball and `process_extracted_tarball_package` calls `Lockfile::append_package`, which always appends a **new** package row (with the recomputed integrity and the freshly parsed dependency list). The root dependency's resolution is never repointed from the old row to the new one, so the differ prunes the new row as an orphan and the old row is what gets saved.

The same root cause limits the `--force` and `bun i <url>` refresh added in #31868: those re-fetch and re-extract the tarball and persist the new integrity, but do not re-resolve the tarball's `package.json`, so new transitive dependencies and bins are not picked up until that re-resolution exists.

### Related

- #31864 (the `--force` refresh that surfaced this)
- #31868 (fix for #31864; documents this as a known limitation)

title: `bun test` exits 0 and silently skips a nonexistent `./`-prefixed path when another path matches
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.13

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (baseline)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

In an empty directory containing a single test file:

```ts
// a.test.ts
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";
test("a", () => { expect(1).toBe(1); });
```

run:

```sh
bun test ./a.test.ts ./missing.test.ts
echo "exit=$?"
```

`missing.test.ts` does not exist.

### What is the expected behavior?

A non-zero exit (or at minimum a warning) reporting that `./missing.test.ts` does not exist.

Bun's own diagnostic describes the `./` prefix as the way to pass an argument as a **path** rather than a filter. Running `bun test ./missing.test.ts` on its own exits 1 and prints:

```
note: To treat the "missing.test.ts" filter as a path, run "bun test ./missing.test.ts"
```

So a `./`-prefixed argument that names a file which doesn't exist should be an error in the mixed case too.

### What do you see instead?

```
 1 pass
 0 fail
 1 expect() calls
Ran 1 test across 1 file. [10.00ms]
exit=0
```

The nonexistent path is dropped silently and the run exits 0. The same happens without the `./` prefix whenever at least one other argument matches a file. If *every* argument matches nothing, `bun test` does exit 1, so the silent case is specifically a mix of present and missing paths.

### Additional information

This produces false greens in CI. A command that lists specific test files keeps passing after one of those files is renamed or deleted, and nothing reports that the named suite never ran. Scripts that pass an explicit file list are relying on each listed file actually running, so a silent skip hides lost coverage.

title: An `exit` listener that throws replaces the exit code with 1
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9. Also main at 973016372d.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// a.cjs
process.exitCode = 4;
process.on("exit", code => {
  console.log("exit", code, process.exitCode);
  throw new Error("cleanup failed");
});
```

```sh
bun a.cjs; echo $?
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Node v26.3.0 prints `exit 4 4`, prints the error, and exits with 4.

### What do you see instead?

Bun prints `exit 4 4`, prints the error, and exits with 1.

### Additional information

Two more programs have the same result:

| program | node v26.3.0 | bun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `process.on("exit", () => { throw new Error("x") }); process.exit(7);` | 7 | 1 |
| `process.on("exit", () => { process.exitCode = 98; throw new Error("x") }); Promise.reject(new Error("oops"));` | 98 | 1 |

Node uses 1 only when no exit code is set. Bun stores 1 over the code that is set. The error is thrown after `beforeExit` was dispatched, so `VirtualMachine::uncaught_exception` (`src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs`) prints it and calls the exit function with 1, and `Bun__Process__exit` (`src/runtime/node/node_process.rs`) stores that code.

#42032 changes the `process.exit(7)` row to 7. It does not change the other two rows. #38116 does not change this path.

title: A default-mode unhandled rejection does not reach an `uncaughtException` listener
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9. Also main at 973016372d.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// r.cjs
process.on("uncaughtException", (err, origin) => console.log("uncaughtException", err.message, origin));
process.on("exit", code => console.log("exit", code, process.exitCode));
Promise.reject(new Error("oops"));
```

```sh
bun r.cjs; echo $?
```

There is no `unhandledRejection` listener and no `--unhandled-rejections` flag.

### What is the expected behavior?

Node v26.3.0 raises the rejection as an uncaught exception. The listener receives it and the process lives:

```
uncaughtException oops unhandledRejection
exit 0 undefined
```

The exit status is 0.

### What do you see instead?

Bun does not call the listener. It prints the error to stderr, prints `exit 0 undefined`, and exits with 1.

### Additional information

`process.setUncaughtExceptionCaptureCallback(fn)` has the same result: node calls `fn` and exits with 0, bun does not call it and exits with 1.

With `--unhandled-rejections=throw` bun does call the listener. The default mode of `VirtualMachine::unhandled_rejection` (`src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs`) calls the `unhandledRejection` listeners and then the default error printer. It does not try the `uncaughtException` path.

Found during the work on #38116. With #38116 the `exit` listener of this program is told `1 1` and not `0 undefined`, because the run fails. The `uncaughtException` listener is still not called.

title: `process.exit()` with no argument after an unhandled rejection exits with 0
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9. Also main at 973016372d.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// c.mjs
process.on("exit", code => console.log("exit", code, process.exitCode));
setTimeout(() => { Promise.reject(new Error("boom")); }, 5);
await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 50));
process.exit();
```

```sh
bun c.mjs; echo $?
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Node v26.3.0 prints the error, prints `exit 1 1`, and exits with 1. It exits at the rejection.

### What do you see instead?

Bun prints the error and continues, because the top-level await is pending. `process.exit()` then prints `exit 0 undefined` and exits with 0. A run that printed an uncaught error exits with 0.

### Additional information

With `throw new Error("boom")` in the timer, the same program prints `exit 1 1` and exits with 1 on bun. `VirtualMachine::uncaught_exception` stores exit code 1 when it reports the error. The default mode of `VirtualMachine::unhandled_rejection` does not store it. `bun run` stores the code only at the natural end of the run (`Run::start` in `src/runtime/cli/run_command.rs`), and `process.exit()` does not reach that code.

#42032 stores the code when the rejection is reported. With it this program exits with 1. #38116 does not change this program.

Bun.SQL MySQL: the docs say that queries are pipelined, the adapter writes one command at a time since v1.2.22
excerpt:
### What is the problem?

The documentation says that the MySQL adapter of `Bun.SQL` pipelines queries. The adapter does not. Since v1.2.22 it writes a command only after the reply to the command before it is complete.

The two places in `docs/runtime/sql.mdx`, both from #22094:

- Line 141, in the list of MySQL features: "**Query pipelining**: Execute multiple prepared statements without waiting for responses"
- Line 1314, in an example: "Query pipelining - multiple statements sent without waiting"

No maintainer has said which of the two is intended. This issue asks that question.

### Measurements

**What the client writes behind a command that has no reply.** One connection (`max: 1`), one cached statement, three queries started together, flag `BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_SQL_AUTO_PIPELINING` not set. The server is a mock that never answers the first of the three `COM_STMT_EXECUTE` commands.

| Client | Commands on the wire after the warm-up |
|---|---|
| 1.2.21 | `EXECUTE b`, `EXECUTE c`, `EXECUTE d` in one write |
| 1.2.22 | `EXECUTE b` |
| 1.3.0 | `EXECUTE b` |
| main (29d9638da3) | `EXECUTE b` |

**Results of a mixed batch.** MariaDB 11.8.6. Statement A is cached. The batch is the first use of statement B between two executes of A, all started together:

```js
import { SQL } from "bun";
const sql = new SQL({ url: "mysql://root@127.0.0.1:3306/bun_sql_test", max: 1 });
const a = v => sql`SELECT ${v} AS a`;
const b = v => sql`SELECT ${v} AS b, 1 AS n`;
await a("warm");
const settle = p => p.then(rows => JSON.stringify(Array.from(rows)), e => "rejected " + e.code);
console.log(await Promise.all([settle(a("a1")), settle(b("b1")), settle(a("a2")), settle(b("b2"))]));
```

| Client | Flag | Result, the same in 3 of 3 runs |
|---|---|---|
| 1.2.21 | not set | 1 of 4 correct. 3 queries reject with `ERR_MYSQL_UNEXPECTED_PACKET` |
| 1.2.21 | set | 2 of 4 correct. `b1` resolves with the row of `a2`, and `a2` resolves with the row of `b1` |
| 1.2.22 | not set | 4 of 4 correct |
| main (29d9638da3) | not set | 4 of 4 correct |

So the pipelining of 1.2.21 gave wrong results, and the change to one command at a time is what made them correct. A revert of that change is not a way back to pipelining.

### History

- #21968 (v1.2.21) added the adapter. Its `canPipeline` did not read `is_ready_for_query`.
- #22094 added the two documentation lines.
- #22619 (v1.2.22) added `is_ready_for_query` to `canPipeline`. Each write clears that field and only a complete reply sets

title: Windows: a failed read of a child's stdout or stderr leaves the pipe open
excerpt:
### What happens

On Windows, when a read of a child's stdout or stderr fails, `WindowsBufferedReader::on_error` (`src/io/PipeReader.rs`) marks the reader done and reports the error to its parent. It does not close the pipe. These parents only record that the pipe is finished, so the pipe stays open until they are torn down:

- `bun run --filter` (`src/runtime/cli/filter_run.rs`)
- `bun run --parallel` and `--sequential` (`src/runtime/cli/multi_run.rs`)
- `bun install`: lifecycle scripts, git, the security scanner (`src/install/`)
- `Bun.cron` (`src/runtime/api/cron.rs`)

Nothing reads the pipe after the error. A child that still writes blocks when the pipe is full, and the command waits for an exit that does not come.

### Status

This comes from the code. It is not reproduced on Windows: the test suite cannot make the read of a Windows pipe fail for these commands.

On POSIX the same sequence is reproduced with an injected read error. `bun run --filter` with a script that writes 8 MB never returns, because the child blocks in its write.

### What to do

Release the source in the error path of the Windows reader before the parent hears of the error, as EOF does. Two points differ from POSIX:

- #42819 replaces the Windows reader. A change to `WindowsBufferedReader` made now conflicts with it, so this belongs after it.
- On POSIX the `CLOSE_HANDLE` flag says who owns the fd. On Windows the shell `IOReader` keeps the flag set, so the rule must come from the kind of source: release a pipe or a tty, leave a file to its parent.

The change needs a test that fails without it. `subprocessInternals.injectStdioReadError` reaches the Windows error path today. Its parent, the pipe reader of `Bun.spawn`, releases the pipe itself in `on_reader_error`, so that test passes with or without a release in the reader.

### Related

- #41456 released the pipe for `Bun.spawn` on both platforms, in the parent.
- #42819

Bun.Image: decode HEIC/HEIF on Linux (dlopen system libheif)
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`Bun.Image` decodes HEIC/HEIF only through the system backends (ImageIO on macOS, WIC on Windows). On Linux there is no system backend (`HAS_SYSTEM_BACKEND` is false, per `src/runtime/image/README.md`), so HEIC input fails:

```ts
// Bun 1.4.2, oven/bun:1.4.2-slim (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64)
const bytes = await Bun.file("photo.heic").bytes(); // straight from an iPhone
await new Bun.Image(bytes).metadata();
// error: ERR_IMAGE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED
```

The same code works on macOS. Most servers run Linux, and HEIC is the default photo format on iPhones, so apps that accept user photo uploads work in development and break in production. Today the only option on Linux is to shell out to `heif-dec` (libheif) before `Bun.Image`, or to pull in sharp.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Decode HEIC/HEIF on Linux by `dlopen`-ing the system libheif when it is installed, the same approach #30204 proposes for AVIF via libavif. Decode-only is enough for the upload use case; if libheif isn't present, keep returning `ERR_IMAGE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`. Since the library is provided by the user's system (e.g. `apt install libheif1`), Bun doesn't have to bundle an HEVC decoder.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Shelling out to `heif-dec` from `libheif-examples`, then feeding the PNG to `Bun.Image` (what we do now).
- sharp with its prebuilt libvips.

Related: #30199 (AVIF on Linux), #35300 (TIFF on Linux), #30235 (HEIC rotation).

bun build --compile: an --external package is resolved from process.cwd(), not from the executable's directory
excerpt:
### What happens

A compiled executable that leaves a package external (`--external dep`) finds that package only when the **current working directory** has it (or `NODE_PATH` points at it). Placing `node_modules/dep` next to the executable does nothing; running the binary from any other directory fails:

```
error: Cannot find package 'dep' from '/$bunfs/root/app'
```

`import.meta.resolve("dep")` from inside the binary reports the same, and `import.meta.dir` is `/$bunfs/root`, so the resolver walks up from the virtual path and then falls back to the cwd.

### Minimal repro (Bun 1.4.2, macOS arm64)

```
mkdir -p ext/node_modules/dep && cd ext
cat > node_modules/dep/package.json <<'EOF'
{ "name": "dep", "version": "1.0.0", "type": "module", "exports": "./index.js" }
EOF
echo 'export default "dep-loaded";' > node_modules/dep/index.js
cat > main.js <<'EOF'
import dep from "dep";
console.log("static:", dep);
EOF
bun build --compile --external dep ./main.js --outfile ./app
```

| where the binary runs | result |
|---|---|
| `./app` in `ext/` (cwd has `node_modules`) | `static: dep-loaded` |
| copy `app` **and** `node_modules` to `/somewhere/`, run `cd / && /somewhere/app` | `Cannot find package 'dep' from '/$bunfs/root/app'` |
| binary in a dir **without** `node_modules`, run with cwd = `ext/` | `static: dep-loaded` |
| any cwd, `NODE_PATH=/somewhere/node_modules` | `static: dep-loaded` |

Same result for a dynamic `await import(name)`, and with `--bytecode --format=esm --minify`. `--compile-autoload-package-json` does not change it.

The executables docs say that a relative path to a file that was not included is loaded "relative to the process's current working directory"; bare package specifiers evidently follow the same rule, and nothing in the search order looks at the executable's own directory.

### Why it matters

The natural way to ship a compiled app with optional native or heavy dependencies is `app` + `node_modules/` in one directory, started by a service manager or a container `ENTRYPOINT` whose cwd is elsewhere. Today that layout only works with `NODE_PATH` or a `cd`. The same applies to plugin systems that load packages by name at runtime, and to bundles produced by other tools that emit `createRequire(import.meta.url)("pkg")`.

### Proposal

For modules that live inside `$bunfs`, resolve bare specifiers in this order: the bundled graph → `dirname(process.execPath)/node_modules` (and its parents) → `NODE_PATH` → cwd. That is what `bun run` would

title: Bun.serve sends an empty body for a file on procfs or cgroupfs (st_size 0)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (and main at 36cd1514ec)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const path = "/proc/version";
const server = Bun.serve({
  port: 0,
  routes: {
    "/route": new Response(Bun.file(path)),
    "/dir/*": { dir: "/proc" },
  },
  fetch: () => new Response(Bun.file(path)),
});
for (const url of ["/handler", "/route", "/dir/version"]) {
  const res = await fetch(new URL(url, server.url));
  const body = await res.text();
  console.log(url, res.status, "content-length:", res.headers.get("content-length"), "body bytes:", body.length);
}
console.log("Bun.file(path).text() bytes:", (await Bun.file(path).text()).length);
server.stop(true);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Each response has the 219 bytes of the file, the same bytes that `Bun.file(path).text()` returns.

### What do you see instead?

```
/handler 200 content-length: 0 body bytes: 0
/route 200 content-length: 0 body bytes: 0
/dir/version 200 content-length: 0 body bytes: 0
Bun.file(path).text() bytes: 219
```

### Additional information

A regular file on procfs or cgroupfs reports `st_size` 0. The kernel makes the content at `read`. Three places in `Bun.serve` take `st_size` as the length of the body:

- `RequestContext::do_sendfile` in `src/runtime/server/RequestContext.rs`: a `BunFile` body from a `fetch` handler.
- `FileRoute::serve` in `src/runtime/server/FileRoute.rs`: a static route.
- `DirectoryRoute::on` in `src/runtime/server/DirectoryRoute.rs`: a `{ dir }` route.

The report comes from a read of the code. No user reported it before. `new Response(await Bun.file(path).bytes())` sends the bytes today.

This issue tracks the parts:

- [ ] A `BunFile` body from a `fetch` handler and from a static route, for a body of each size: #43974. It tests the file for content with one `pread`, sends a file with content through `FileResponseStream`, as a pipe, and it is stacked on #37082.
- [ ] A `BunFile` that holds a size of 0 already, after `file.size`, `await file.exists()` or a read of `response.body`. The cause is in `Blob::resolve_size`: #43910, #41593.
- [ ] `HEAD`: #43974 too, for the `fetch` handler and the static route. #41585 changes the same lines of the `fetch` handler: it sends `HEAD` for each file through the code of `GET`.
- [ ] A `{ dir }` route. There the client names the file. A maintainer must decide if such a route reads these files.
- [ ] `Bun.file(fd)`

title: bun build --compile: __dirname/__filename in an included CommonJS entrypoint are inlined as the build directory, not the $bunfs path
excerpt:
### What happens

When a CommonJS file is included in a `bun build --compile` binary as an extra entrypoint, `__dirname` and `__filename` in that module are replaced at build time with string literals of the **build machine's** directory (`var __dirname = "/private/tmp/.../chunks";` is visible in the embedded source). Code that loads siblings via `require(path.join(__dirname, "x.cjs"))` therefore fails once the binary runs anywhere the build directory doesn't exist. `require("./x.cjs")` and `require.resolve("./x.cjs")` (→ `/$bunfs/root/chunks/x.js`) work.

### Repro (Bun 1.4.2, macOS arm64)

`app.js`
```js
const name = "loader";
require("./chunks/" + name + ".js").load("n1");
```
`chunks/loader.js`
```js
const path = require("path");
console.log("__dirname:", __dirname);
exports.load = (name) => {
  try { console.log("relative:", require("./" + name + ".cjs")); } catch (e) { console.log("relative FAIL:", e.message); }
  try { console.log("join(__dirname):", require(path.join(__dirname, name + ".cjs"))); } catch (e) { console.log("join FAIL:", e.message); }
  console.log("require.resolve:", require.resolve("./" + name + ".cjs"));
};
```
`chunks/n1.cjs`
```js
module.exports = "n1 loaded";
```
`build.js`
```js
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["app.js", "chunks/loader.js", "chunks/n1.cjs"],
  compile: { outfile: "out" },
  root: ".", naming: "[dir]/[name].[ext]", format: "cjs",
});
```
```sh
bun build.js
mv "$PWD" "$PWD.moved"      # simulate another machine: build dir no longer exists
cp "$PWD.moved/out" /tmp/empty/ && cd / && /tmp/empty/out
```
Output:
```
__dirname: /private/tmp/bun-repros/dirname-inlined/chunks
relative: n1 loaded
join FAIL: Cannot find module '/private/tmp/bun-repros/dirname-inlined/chunks/n1.cjs'
Require stack:
- /$bunfs/root/chunks/loader.js
require.resolve: /$bunfs/root/chunks/n1.js
```
Same with `format: "esm"` (`__dirname` still inlined to the build dir). Note `eval("__dirname")` in the module sees the same inlined value, since it is a module-scope variable.

| Expression inside the included CJS module | Result in the relocated binary |
|---|---|
| `__dirname` / `__filename` | build directory (wrong) |
| `require("./n1.cjs")` | works |
| `require.resolve("./n1.cjs")` | `/$bunfs/root/chunks/n1.js` (right) |
| `require(path.join(__dirname, "n1.cjs"))` | fails: build path not found |

Also noticed: `.cjs`/`.mjs` entrypoints are embedded as `.js` and the resolver maps `x.cjs` → `x.js`.

### Expected

`__dirname`/`__filename` for a modul

Windows: stable install-scoped aliases for --bun and run.bun
excerpt:
# Windows: stable install-scoped aliases for --bun and run.bun

Related: [oven-sh/bun#25321](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/25321), which reports different installed and temporary Bun executables during upgrades.

## Problem

On Windows, Bun 1.4.2's `--bun` / `[run] bun = true` uses `%TEMP%\bun-node-<build SHA>\node.exe`. The installed Bun path remains stable, but the alias path changes with the Bun build. Executable-specific antivirus exceptions therefore cannot reliably follow that alias across upgrades.

The request is a stable alias per Bun installation, not a global shared alias that can switch runtimes underneath concurrent installations.

## Reproduce the path difference

Create a package with:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "runtime": "node -p \"process.execPath\""
  }
}
```

Compare `bun -e 'console.log(process.execPath)'` with `bun --bun run runtime` on Windows. The first identifies the installed Bun executable; the second uses its build-specific temporary alias. Repeat after updating Bun at the same installed path to observe the alias change. We verified released Bun's path selection and SHA-based implementation.

## Why it matters

On one Windows 11 machine with Bun 1.4.2, Vitest 5.0.0 and Bitdefender Antivirus Plus 28.0.9.198, a controlled A/B/B/A comparison of the same project test command produced:

| Condition                                      | Durations        | Worker-shutdown warnings | Tests passed per run |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------- |
| Normal ATD protection                          | 43.70 s, 43.55 s | 99, 97                   | 1,918                |
| ATD exception for the temporary node.exe alias | 8.16 s, 7.98 s   | 0, 0                     | 1,918                |

This is evidence of an ATD interaction on this machine, not proof of a Bun shutdown defect. No standalone reproduction of the antivirus slowdown has been isolated. The path churn itself is independently observable.

## Proposed fix

1. Use an alias directory tied to the stable installed executable path, rather than the build SHA. Keep separate installations separate, including concurrent versions.
2. Refresh stale Windows hard links when the installed executable is replaced. A stable directory must not retain an old runtime.
3. Share alias-path computation between creation, `NODE`/`npm_node_execpath`, and child PATH setup; preserve the original installation identity th

title: test(sql): the fixture of "process should exit when idle" does not set allowPublicKeyRetrieval
excerpt:
### What is the problem?

`test/js/sql/sql-idle-exit-fixture.ts` connects to the MySQL containers of `test/js/sql/sql-mysql.test.ts` without `allowPublicKeyRetrieval`. Each other connection of that suite sets the option through `getOptions()`.

The connection to the `mysql:9` container is plain TCP with a password. The first connection of an account needs the full authentication of `caching_sha2_password`. Without the option the client refuses it (`src/sql_jsc/mysql/MySQLConnection.rs:831`) and the connection fails with `ERR_MYSQL_PUBLIC_KEY_RETRIEVAL_NOT_ALLOWED`. `test/js/sql/sql-mysql.auth.test.ts` has a test for that refusal.

So, by the code, the test "process should exit when idle" passes only if another connection did the full authentication before its child connects. In a run of the whole file the other tests of the suite do that, and the server answers the child from its cache.

### History

- #23873 added the fixture.
- #31129 made the client refuse public key retrieval by default. It added the option to `getOptions()` and not to the fixture.

### Not verified

I did not run the test alone against a new MySQL 9 server. The machine that I used has no MySQL 9 server.

### Possible change

Add `allowPublicKeyRetrieval: true` to the options in the fixture. #44022 makes the same change to the fixture that it adds, after a review found this there.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (also reproduces on linux-x64)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// build.mjs
const r = await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./main.cjs", "./assets.mjs"],
  root: ".",
  target: "bun",
  format: "cjs",
  naming: { entry: "[dir]/[name].[ext]", asset: "[dir]/[name].[ext]" },
  compile: { outfile: "./app" },
});
if (!r.success) { for (const l of r.logs) console.error(String(l)); process.exit(1); }
```

```js
// assets.mjs
import m from "./data/m.json" with { type: "file" };
export default m;
```

```js
// main.cjs
const p = require("node:path").join(require("node:path").dirname(process.argv[1]), "data/m.json");
console.log("readFileSync:", require("node:fs").readFileSync(p, "utf8"));
console.log("require:", JSON.stringify(require(p)));
```

```json
// data/m.json
{"a":1}
```

```sh
bun build.mjs && ./app
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`require(p)` returns the parsed object `{ a: 1 }`, the same as Node's `require()` of a `.json` file on
disk, and the same as `require("node:fs").readFileSync(p, "utf8")` reads the same embedded path
successfully.

### What do you see instead?

`readFileSync` succeeds and prints the raw bytes (`{"a":1}`), but `require(p)` on the exact same
embedded path throws:

```
SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'
```

The embedded JSON asset's contents are being parsed as a JavaScript module body instead of going
through the `.json` loader that a disk-based `require()` uses.

### Additional information

Only shows up for the compiled executable's embedded asset path (`/$bunfs/root/...`), and only when
`require()` gets the path at runtime rather than a static `import`. A static `import ... from
"./x.json"` is fine since the bundler inlines it at build time. `fs.readFileSync` and `require()`
should return the same thing for the same embedded path.

## Bug: sharp file I/O crashes Bun with `mprotect failed: 487` / "Illegal instruction" on Windows

### Description

Calling any `sharp` operation that reads a file from disk (e.g. `.metadata()`, `.extract().toFile()`) causes Bun to crash with:

```
mprotect failed: 487
```

This manifests as an **"Illegal instruction"** CPU exception and terminates the process with exit code 9.

In-memory operations (e.g. `sharp({ create: { ... } }).png().toBuffer()`) work fine.

### Reproduction

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro
npm init -y
npm install sharp
# Create any PNG file
bun -e "
  const sharp = require('sharp');
  sharp('test.png').metadata().then(console.log).catch(console.error)
"
```

**Expected:** Metadata printed or graceful error.
**Actual:** Bun crashes with `mprotect failed: 487` / "Illegal instruction".

### Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Bun version | 1.3.14 (revision: `0d9b296af`) |
| Node.js (works) | v24.15.0 |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro, build 26200 |
| CPU | 13th Gen Intel Core i7-13700H |
| sharp version | 0.35.3 |
| sharp runtime | WASM (Windows x64) |

### Notes

- Error `mprotect failed: 487` = Windows `ERROR_INVALID_ADDRESS` — Bun's WASM runtime cannot allocate executable memory for libvips file I/O.
- Crash report: `https://bun.report/1.3.14/wa10d9b296ghkgEugggCg0j2uB+r74vC+h/6vCo924vCww04vC+z9mnDutx17Ci0l27Cypn27C0k6plDgxg7zC+69gyCgzpuxCg9/mqCys5rkCmqwqxDCYKERNEL32.DLLu4mLCSntdll.dll4ulrBA3s//Bg0jyykB`

title: bun test --isolate: two import() calls of one module in the same tick abort a build with assertions
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3 (debug build with assertions, main at a4f1429148)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`dep.ts`:

```ts
export const value = 1;
```

`two-imports.test.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

// Two import() calls of the same module that is not loaded yet, in the same tick.
const first = import("./dep.ts");
const second = import("./dep.ts");

test("both imports resolve to the same module", async () => {
  expect((await first).value).toBe(1);
  expect(await second).toBe(await first);
});
```

Run `bun-debug test --isolate two-imports.test.ts`.

### What is the expected behavior?

The test passes. It passes without `--isolate`, and it passes with `--isolate` on a release build.

### What do you see instead?

```
ASSERTION FAILED: IsolatedModuleCache::insert for already-cached key
result.isNewEntry
src/jsc/bindings/IsolatedModuleCache.cpp(37) : static void Bun::IsolatedModuleCache::insert(JSC::VM &, const WTF::String &, Zig::SourceProvider &)
```

The process ends with SIGABRT. With `--parallel`, which uses the same cache, the worker crashes and the runner aborts the other files of the bucket.

### Additional information

- The mechanism: each of the two `import()` calls gets its own fetch (the comment in `src/jsc/bindings/ModuleLoader.cpp:486` describes this). Each fetch ends in `IsolatedModuleCache::insert` (`ModuleLoader.cpp:518`). The second call finds the key of the first, and the assertion in `IsolatedModuleCache.cpp:37` fails. A release build has no assertion: `HashMap::add` keeps the first entry.
- Where the test suite reaches it: `describeWithContainer` in `test/harness.ts:1273` calls `import("./docker/index.ts")` one time for each block, when the block is defined. A test file with two or more `describeWithContainer` blocks aborts a build with assertions under `--isolate`. `test/js/sql/sql-statement-cache-hash-collision.test.ts` is an example.
- `scripts/runner.node.ts` keeps a test file out of the `--parallel` buckets only when its path matches a key of `test/docker/prestart-map.mjs`. A file with two blocks and no key in that map can abort the ASAN lane.

### What platform is your computer?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

const sql = new SQL({ url: "postgres://bun_sql_test@127.0.0.1:5432/bun_sql_test", max: 1 });
console.log("before:", JSON.stringify(await sql`SELECT 1 AS one`));

new ShadowRealm().evaluate("typeof Bun.SQL");

console.log("after: ", JSON.stringify(await sql`SELECT 1 AS one`));
const failed = await sql`SELECT * FROM no_such_table`.catch(e => e);
console.log("instanceof SQL.PostgresError:", failed instanceof SQL.PostgresError);
process.exit(0);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

```
before: [{"one":1}]
after:  [{"one":1}]
instanceof SQL.PostgresError: true
```

### What do you see instead?

```
before: [{"one":1}]
uncaughtException: TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'is_last')
after:  undefined
instanceof SQL.PostgresError: false
```

### Additional information

- `init()` of each adapter (`src/sql_jsc/postgres/PostgresSQLContext.rs`, `src/sql_jsc/mysql/MySQLContext.rs`) stores the two query callbacks in a slot of the VM. Each realm that loads `Bun.SQL` calls `init()` with its own callbacks (`src/js/internal/sql/postgres.ts`, `mysql.ts`), and the last call wins.
- `src/js/bun/sql.ts` loads the two adapters when `Bun.SQL` is read, so `typeof Bun.SQL` in a `ShadowRealm` is sufficient.
- After that, native code calls the callbacks of the `ShadowRealm` for a query of the first realm. Those callbacks read the query with the private symbols of their own realm and make errors from the classes of their own realm.
- A callback slot for each global object, or callbacks that the connection holds, keep the realms apart.

(`bun --revision`.) Also reproduced on 1.2.21, and in a `bun build --compile` binary.

### What platform is your computer?

(`uname -mprs`.) Android 16, Pixel 8 Pro (Tensor G3), inside Termux with proot-distro. The host only matters because `/proc` is bind-mounted over — the code path in question is Bun's own Linux `os.cpus()`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

const c = os.cpus()
console.log(c.length)     // 9
console.log(c[0].model)   // throws: Failed to get CPU information
```

The trigger is `/proc/stat` reporting fewer per-CPU lines than `/proc/cpuinfo` reports `processor` blocks. That is not a corrupt system — `/proc/stat` is bind-mounted over by anything that substitutes it. The case here is a userspace proot/chroot on Android: the real `/proc/stat` is unreadable, so a static copy is bound in its place, while `/proc/cpuinfo` is left live and correct.

To reproduce on an otherwise normal machine, mask one per-CPU line:

```sh

sudo unshare -m --propagation private -- \

title: bun test --changed skips tests that import through package.json "imports" (#subpath) or a workspace package
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (744846f84)

### What platform is your computer?

macOS arm64 and Linux x64 (GitHub Actions)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun test --changed` doesn't follow two kinds of bare specifier when it works out which test files a change affects:

- **package.json `imports` subpaths**, e.g. `#src/own.ts` with `"imports": { "#src/*": "./src/*" }`
- **workspace packages**, e.g. `@repro/lib/lib`, which resolves through the workspace's `exports`

A test that reaches a changed file only through one of these is skipped, while the same import written as a relative path is picked up. This looks like the same short-circuit as #29590: the specifier is treated as external before it is resolved. That fix (#29591) exempted tsconfig `paths` only.

Run this in an empty directory:

```sh
set -e
mkdir bun-changed-repro && cd bun-changed-repro
git init -q

cat > package.json <<'EOF'
{ "name": "root", "private": true, "workspaces": ["packages/*"] }
EOF

# A workspace package, imported by name through its `exports`.
mkdir -p packages/lib/src
cat > packages/lib/package.json <<'EOF'
{ "name": "@repro/lib", "type": "module", "exports": { "./*": "./src/*.ts" } }
EOF
echo 'export const lib = () => 1;' > packages/lib/src/lib.ts

# The package under test, which imports its own files through `imports`.
mkdir -p packages/app/src
cat > packages/app/package.json <<'EOF'
{
  "name": "@repro/app",
  "type": "module",
  "imports": { "#src/*": "./src/*" },
  "dependencies": { "@repro/lib": "workspace:*" }
}
EOF
echo 'export const own = () => 2;' > packages/app/src/own.ts
cat > packages/app/src/relative.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { own } from "./own.ts";
test("relative import", () => expect(own()).toBe(2));
EOF
cat > packages/app/src/subpath.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { own } from "#src/own.ts";
test("package.json imports (#src/*)", () => expect(own()).toBe(2));
EOF
cat > packages/app/src/workspace.test.ts <<'EOF'
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";
import { lib } from "@repro/lib/lib";
test("workspace package", () => expect(lib()).toBe(1));
EOF

bun install
echo node_modules > .gitignore
git add -A && git -c user.name=r -c user.email=r@r commit -qm init
cd packages/app

echo "--- change own.ts (relative.test.ts and subpath.test.ts import it)"
echo '// change' >> src/own.ts
bun test --changed

echo "--- change the workspace package (workspace.test.ts imports it)"
git c

title: Bun.PLIST: parse/stringify Apple property lists (XML, binary, OpenStep) + .plist loader
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

I'm building tooling that reads metadata out of iOS app builds. The starting point is an `.ipa`: unzip it, find `Payload/<App>.app/Info.plist`, and read values like `CFBundleIdentifier`, `CFBundleShortVersionString` and `CFBundleVersion`.
  
  The zip part is the easy bit. The plist part pulled in more than expected:
  
  - The `Info.plist` inside a built app is either a **binary** plist (`bplist00`) or an XML one in the source tree, so an XML parser alone isn't enough.
  - I ended up on `simple-plist`, which wraps separate packages for XML (`plist`) and binary (`bplist-parser` / `bplist-creator`) etc
  - Source-side files have the same problem in other formats: Capacitor/React Native projects keep an XML `Info.plist`, and Xcode projects (`project.pbxproj`) and `.strings` files use the OpenStep text format.
  
  Property lists are everywhere in Apple tooling (Info.plist, entitlements, provisioning profiles, `.pbxproj`, `.strings`, macOS preferences). Bun already parses TOML, YAML, JSON5 and now XML (`Bun.XML`, #37048) natively, and plists feel like a
  natural extension: the XML format is a small vocabulary on top of XML, and the other two formats are compact.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

 A `Bun.PLIST` namespace and a `.plist` loader, following the shape of `Bun.TOML` / `Bun.XML`.

  ## API

  ```ts
  // Format detected from the input: XML, binary (bplist00) or OpenStep
  const info = Bun.PLIST.parse(await Bun.file("Payload/App.app/Info.plist").bytes());
  info.CFBundleShortVersionString; // "5.22.0"

  Bun.PLIST.stringify(info);                         // XML string, in Xcode's layout
  Bun.PLIST.stringify(info, { format: "binary" });   // Uint8Array

  import info from "./ios/App/App/Info.plist";
  import strings from "./en.lproj/Localizable.strings" with { type: "plist" };
  ```

  Type mapping: `<dict>` → object, `<array>` → array, `<string>` → string, `<integer>` → number (`bigint` outside ±2^53−1), `<real>` → number, `<true/>`/`<false/>` → boolean, `<date>` → `Date`, `<data>` → `Uint8Array`. A binary UID becomes `{
  CF$UID: n }`, which is how `plutil` writes it in XML, so it round-trips.

  The goal is to reuse what Bun already has rather than add a parallel stack:

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9. Also main at a4f1429148.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// k.cjs
process.on("exit", code => { console.log("first", code); throw new Error("cleanup failed"); });
process.on("exit", code => { console.log("second", code); });
process.exit(7);
```

```sh
bun k.cjs; echo $?
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Node v26.3.0 prints `first 7`, prints the error, and exits with 7. The second listener does not run.

### What do you see instead?

Bun prints `first 7` and `second 7`, prints the error, and exits with 1. The exit code is #44018. This issue is about `second 7`.

### Additional information

**A later listener can hide the failure.** This program prints the error and exits with 0 on Bun. Node exits with 7.

```js
process.on("exit", () => { throw new Error("cleanup failed"); });
process.on("exit", () => { process.exitCode = 0; });
process.exit(7);
```

**The same happens for other events.** In each program the first listener prints `first` and throws, and the second listener prints `second`. An `uncaughtException` listener handles the error where the table says "handled".

| program | Node v26.3.0 | Bun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| two `exit` listeners, `process.exit(7)` | `first` | `first`, `second` |
| two `exit` listeners, loop is empty, handled | `first` | `first`, `second` |
| two `SIGUSR2` listeners, `process.kill(process.pid, "SIGUSR2")`, handled | `first` | `first`, `second` |
| two `warning` listeners, `process.emitWarning()`, handled | `first` | `first`, `second` |
| two `message` listeners in a forked child, handled | `first` | `first`, `second` |
| two `unhandledRejection` listeners | `first` | `first`, `second` |
| `try { process.emit("custom") } catch {}` | `first`, the `catch` block runs | `first`, `second`, the error is reported as uncaught, exit code 1 |

**Where Bun already stops.** With two `exit` listeners, an empty loop, and nothing that handles the error, Bun prints `first 0` and exits with 1, as Node does. The same is true after a fatal error. The test `a throw from an exit listener after a fatal throw still stops subsequent exit listeners` in `test/js/node/process/process.test.js` covers that path.

**Cause.** `process` uses a native emitter. `EventEmitter::innerInvokeEventListeners` (`src/jsc/bindings/webcore/EventEmitter.cpp`) calls each listener with the catching form of `JSC::call`, reports the exception through `Bun__reportUnhandledError`, and continues

### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (also reproduces on 1.3.14)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 (macOS 26.3.1)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// repro.mjs
import { mkdtempSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";

const dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "bun-dircache-"));
writeFileSync(join(dir, "a.mjs"), "export const v = 'a';");
console.log("a:", (await import(join(dir, "a.mjs"))).v);

writeFileSync(join(dir, "b.mjs"), "export const v = 'b';");
console.log("b:", (await import(join(dir, "b.mjs"))).v);
```

```sh
bun repro.mjs
```

It fails the same way under `bun test`.

### What is the expected behavior?

```
a: a
b: b
```

This is what Node 24.21.0 prints.

### What do you see instead?

```
a: a
error: Cannot find module '/private/var/folders/…/T/bun-dircache-XXXX/b.mjs' from ''
```

`b.mjs` exists when it is imported. It looks like the directory's entries are cached on the first import from that directory, so a file written into it later is never found through a plain absolute path.

### Additional information

Same setup (import `a.mjs`, then write `b.mjs` into the same directory), varying only how `b.mjs` is imported:

| import specifier for `b.mjs` | Bun 1.4.2 | Node 24.21.0 |
|---|---|---|
| plain absolute path | ❌ Cannot find module | ✅ |
| `pathToFileURL(path).href` | ✅ | ✅ |
| absolute path + `?v=1` | ✅ | ✅ |
| plain path, after `readdirSync(dir)` | ✅ | ✅ |
| control: `b.mjs` written *before* the first import from the dir | ✅ | ✅ |

We hit this in a test suite that bundles code, writes each bundle into a shared temp directory, and imports it. Running the file alone failed; the full suite happened to mask it. Our workaround is one fresh `mkdtemp` directory per written module.

Symbol reachable only as a property key is garbage-collected: WeakMap entries removed, WeakRef cleared
bun build --compile: embedded native libraries (.so) are extracted to hidden  paths on every run and never unlinked (.node addons are)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (as embedded in opencode 1.18.33's `bun build --compile` binary — this is where we observed it)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.17 x86_64 (Ubuntu 25.04-ish, tmpfs /tmp)

### What you did

A standalone binary built with `bun build --compile` that embeds **native shared libraries** (`.so` napi addons) extracts them to a *hidden, randomized* path in `$TMPDIR` on every process start and **never unlinks them**:

```
$TMPDIR/.{content-derived hex stem}-{8-digit index}.{so,node}
e.g. /tmp/.9adbdafff7edfd87-00000000.so   (13.7 MB @opentui/core)
     /tmp/.bcd9d71ebc8fba3c-00000001.so  (5.6 MB fff-core)
     /tmp/.5effd61ebdd3ff6b-00000002.node (small addon)
```

We caught this on a machine where `/tmp` (tmpfs) filled to 99%: ~670 files / ~6.1 GB accumulated over ~4 days, minted in bursts that match app launches. Every copy within a family is byte-identical — a fresh extraction per launch, never reused, never removed.

### What you expected to happen

The extraction is a dlopen-then-clean dance: after `dlopen`, the temp file should be unlinked (the mapping survives via the fd/inode), so no files accumulate.

### What actually happens

`strace -f` of the opencode TUI shows all three embedded natives being written via a dirfd-relative `openat(..., O_WRONLY|O_CREAT)` and then reopened by path (the dlopen), but only the **`.node`** addon gets cleaned up:

```strace
1439838 openat(13, ".9adbd9bfeaedfdd7-00000000.so", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_CLOEXEC, 0644) = 14
1439838 openat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/.9adbd9bfeaedfdd7-00000000.so", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 14
1439888 openat(32, ".bcd9d59eb69fb63c-00000001.so", O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_CLOEXEC, 0644) = 33
1439888 openat(AT_FDCWD, "/tmp/.bcd9d59eb69fb63c-00000001.so", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 33
1439888 unlink("/tmp/.5effd796bdbbdf5b-00000002.node") = 0    <-- the .node IS unlinked
```

The two `.so` files are never unlinked — not on graceful exit, not on SIGKILL, not on the next launch. The asymmetry (`.node` unlinked, `.so` left behind) suggests the cleanup path exists but only covers the napi `.node` loader route.

Additional observations that may help whoever picks this up:

- The extraction honors `TMPDIR` (redirecting it moves the files), which lets embedders scope the leak, but doesn't fix it.
- The stem looks content-derived (stable prefix per file across days/versions) plus a randomized tail and a constant `-00000000`-style index.
- The leaked `.so` stays mmap'd by the live process

Standalone executables: no build-time switch to disable cwd bunfig.toml loading (preload runs arbitrary code inside compiled binaries)
excerpt:
**What version of Bun?** 1.4.2
**What platform?** Linux x64

## Summary

Bun standalone executables automatically load `bunfig.toml` from the **current working directory** when they start. The `.env` part of this behavior can be disabled at build time via `--no-compile-autoload-dotenv` / `CompileBuildOptions.autoloadDotenv`, but there is **no equivalent build-time switch for `bunfig.toml`**.

This means `preload` entries from a cwd-local `bunfig.toml` execute arbitrary code inside a compiled binary that never opted into project-local configuration.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `bun build --compile --no-compile-autoload-dotenv entry.ts --outfile app`
2. In an unrelated directory, create:

```toml
# bunfig.toml
preload = ["./evil.ts"]
```

```ts
// evil.ts
console.error("PRELOAD-EXECUTED-IN-SERVICE-PROCESS");
```

3. `cd` into that directory and run `./app`.
4. `PRELOAD-EXECUTED-IN-SERVICE-PROCESS` appears on the compiled binary's stderr — the preload script ran inside the standalone process.

## Observed details

- Only the **cwd-level** `bunfig.toml` is read; ancestor directories are not (verified).
- No build-time option exists in 1.4.2 to disable this for compiled executables.
- The executables documentation notes this default and that "In a future version of Bun, `.env` and `bunfig.toml` may also be disabled by default" — the `.env` half now has a switch; `bunfig.toml` does not.

## Why it matters

Compiled CLIs and long-running servers are routinely launched with a cwd the tool does not control (user project directories). A project-local `bunfig.toml` then becomes an arbitrary-code-execution vector injected into the standalone binary's process — including high-privilege services — even though the binary author never opted into loading project-local Bun configuration.

## Suggested fix

Add a build-time option parallel to `autoloadDotenv`, e.g. `--no-compile-autoload-bunfig` / `CompileBuildOptions.autoloadBunfig: boolean`, and/or exclude `preload` from applying to compiled executables unless explicitly enabled. A runtime-equivalent escape hatch (env var) would not fully solve it, since the injection happens before user code runs.

## Workaround we currently use

Always launching the compiled binary from a tool-controlled working directory (project directories are passed as arguments only). Documenting a build-time switch would remove the need for this discipline.

title: Error printer matches Symbol-keyed properties of an Error by their description
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1 (a build of main a4f1429148). bun 1.4.2 prints the same.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const e = new Error("x");
e[Symbol("message")] = "a symbol-keyed value";
e[Symbol("stack")] = 2;
e[Symbol("name")] = 3;
e[Symbol("foo")] = 4;
e.bar = 5;
console.log(e);

const f = new Error("top", { cause: new Error("real") });
f[Symbol.for("cause")] = new Error("sym");
console.log(f);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Each Symbol-keyed property prints, with a key that reads as a Symbol. `f` prints its real cause.

node v26.3.0 prints `Symbol(message): 'a symbol-keyed value'`, `Symbol(stack): 2`, `Symbol(name): 3` and `Symbol(foo): 4` for `e`. For `f` it prints both `Symbol(cause): Error: sym` and `[cause]: Error: real`.

### What do you see instead?

Source previews and stack frames removed:

```
error: x
     bar: 5,
     foo: 4,

error: top

error: sym
```

- The properties with the keys `Symbol("message")`, `Symbol("stack")` and `Symbol("name")` do not print.
- `Symbol("foo")` prints as `foo`, like a string key.
- For `f`, `error: sym` prints in the position of the cause. `error: real` never prints.

### Additional information

The cause is in `print_error_instance_body` (`src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs`). It iterates the own properties with `include_symbols: true`. The iterator yields a Symbol key as its description (see the comment above `PropertyNameArrayBuilder` in `src/jsc/bindings/JSPropertyIterator.cpp`). The loop then compares that name with `message`, `name`, `stack`, `code` and `cause`, so a Symbol key with one of those descriptions is treated as the string key.

Found during the review of #44174. That PR does not fix this. With it, a nested error treats a Symbol key described `cause` the same way the outermost error already does on main.

title: Error printer drops a `cause` from the constructor option when it is not an Error
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1 (a build of main a4f1429148). bun 1.4.2 prints the same.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const cases = {
  string: new Error("outer", { cause: "a string cause" }),
  number: new Error("outer", { cause: 404 }),
  object: new Error("outer", { cause: { code: "E_PLAIN", detail: 42 } }),
  assigned: Object.assign(new Error("outer"), { cause: "assigned string" }),
};
for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(cases)) {
  console.log("--- " + name);
  console.log(Bun.inspect(value));
}
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Each error prints its cause. node v26.3.0 prints `[cause]: 'a string cause'`, `[cause]: 404`, `[cause]: { code: 'E_PLAIN', detail: 42 }` and `cause: 'assigned string'`.

### What do you see instead?

Source previews and stack frames removed:

```
--- string
error: outer

--- number
error: outer

--- object
error: outer

--- assigned
error: outer
 cause: "assigned string",
```

Only the assigned cause prints. A cause from the constructor option that is not an Error prints nothing. The same happens for an uncaught `throw`, for `console.log(err)` and for `console.error(err)`.

### Additional information

The cause is in `print_error_instance_body` (`src/jsc/VirtualMachine.rs`). The constructor option makes `cause` a non-enumerable own property, so the loop over the enumerable own properties does not see it. The fallback after the loop (comment: `"cause" is not enumerable, so the above loop won't see it.`) reads the own `cause` and queues it only when it is an `ErrorInstance`. Any other value is dropped.

Found during the review of #44174. That PR does not change this.

title: Linux x64 1.4.2 segfault in generateNativeModule on import "node:events"
excerpt:
### How can we reproduce the crash?

Official Bun **1.4.2** (`744846f84`), Linux x64, glibc 2.39, kernel 7.0.0. CPU flags reported by the crash banner: sse42 popcnt avx avx2.

```sh
bun -e 'import "node:events"'
```

That exits 139 in about 4ms:

```
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0xFFFFFFFFC24036E4
```

The same address, same `generateNativeModule` frame, on this binary:

```sh
bun -e 'import { stripVTControlCharacters } from "node:util"'
```

These exit 0 on the same 1.4.2 binary:

```sh
bun -e 'import "node:path"'   # prints path-ok
bun -e 'import "node:os"'     # prints os-ok
bun --version                 # prints 1.4.2
```

Bun **1.4.0** runs `bun -e 'import "node:events"'` and prints `events-ok`.

`commander` 14 and 15 hit this on startup because `lib/command.js` begins with `import { EventEmitter } from 'node:events'`. A named ESM import of `commander` is enough. The crash is inside Bun's builtin initializer, before user code runs.

bun install spins when node_modules is a dangling symlink with isolated linker
excerpt:
### Bun version and platform

Bun `1.4.2+744846f84`, Linux x86_64 (`7.2.5-3-omarchy`).

### Reproduction

This script creates a standalone package. It first installs with a link to an existing directory, which also warms the package cache. It then replaces `node_modules` with a dangling symlink and repeats the install.

```sh
set -eu
d=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
mkdir "$d/tmp" "$d/existing"
printf '%s\n' '{"name":"bun-dangling-link-repro","private":true,"devDependencies":{"typescript":"5.9.3"}}' > "$d/package.json"
cat > "$d/bun.lock" <<'EOF'
{
  "lockfileVersion": 1,
  "configVersion": 1,
  "workspaces": {
    "": {
      "name": "bun-dangling-link-repro",
      "devDependencies": { "typescript": "5.9.3" }
    }
  },
  "packages": {
    "typescript": ["typescript@5.9.3", "", { "bin": { "tsc": "bin/tsc", "tsserver": "bin/tsserver" } }, "sha512-jl1vZzPDinLr9eUt3J/t7V6FgNEw9QjvBPdysz9KfQDD41fQrC2Y4vKQdiaUpFT4bXlb1RHhLpp8wtm6M5TgSw=="]
  }
}
EOF
printf '%s\n' '[install]' 'linker = "isolated"' 'globalStore = true' 'publicHoistPattern = ["*"]' > "$d/bunfig.toml"
ln -s "$d/existing" "$d/node_modules"
BUN_TMPDIR="$d/tmp" timeout 120s bun install --cwd "$d" --frozen-lockfile
mv "$d/node_modules" "$d/working_node_modules"
ln -s "$d/missing" "$d/node_modules"
BUN_TMPDIR="$d/tmp" timeout 5s bun install --cwd "$d" --frozen-lockfile
```

### Expected

Bun reports the invalid `node_modules` link or replaces it, then exits promptly.

### Actual

The second install consumes a CPU core and does not exit before the five-second timeout (status 124). The working-link install completes. The hang also reproduced with an absolute or relative dangling link and with or without `--frozen-lockfile`.

A dangling `node_modules` link can arise when a project is moved or mounted without the directory that the link targets. A dependency install should fail or repair the link instead of spinning indefinitely.
