title: A new dependency follows an `npm:` alias that package.json dropped, with bun.lockb and package-lock.json and not with bun.lock
excerpt:
### What happens

One install removes an `npm:` alias and adds a package that depends on the same name. The package that the new dependency gets depends on the lockfile format. `bun install` exits 0 and prints no warning.

```
# package.json at the first install
{ "name": "app", "version": "1.0.0", "dependencies": { "kept": "npm:short@1.0.0" } }

# package.json at the second install
{ "name": "app", "version": "1.0.0", "dependencies": { "new-dependency": "1.0.0" } }
```

The registry has `kept@1.0.0`, `short@1.0.0` and `new-dependency@1.0.0`. `new-dependency` depends on `kept@^1.0.0`.

| Lockfile from the first install | `node_modules/kept` after the second install | Manifests that the second install requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bun.lock` | `kept@1.0.0` | `/kept`, `/new-dependency` |
| `bun.lockb` | `short@1.0.0` | `/new-dependency`, `/short` |
| `package-lock.json` (npm 11.16 wrote it, bun migrates it) | `short@1.0.0` | `/new-dependency`, `/short` |
| none | `kept@1.0.0` | `/kept`, `/new-dependency` |

- The results are the same when a registry package holds the alias (`has-alias@1.0.0` depends on `"kept": "npm:short@1.0.0"`) and the second install replaces `has-alias` with `new-dependency`.
- bun saves the result. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` then reports no changes.
- npm 11.16 with its own `package-lock.json` keeps `short@1.0.0` in `node_modules/kept` in both cases. It requests only `/new-dependency`.
- `yarn.lock` is not in the table. `bun install` fails for a `yarn.lock` that has no entry for a dependency of package.json (`error: new-dependency@1.0.0 failed to resolve`), with or without an alias.

Seen on bun 1.4.3-canary.1 (367d939d9) and on main at a4f1429148. #44294 does not change these results.

### Cause

`PackageManager::known_npm_aliases` maps a dependency name to the last `npm:` alias that bun read under that name. `enqueue_dependency_with_main_and_success_fn` (`src/install/PackageManager/PackageManagerEnqueue.rs`) sends a plain dependency of that name to the alias target when the alias version is in the range of the dependency.

- The loader of `bun.lockb` (`buffers::load` in `src/install/lockfile/Buffers.rs`) and the migration of `package-lock.json` register the alias of each dependency row. The loader of `bun.lock` registers no dependency row.
- Nothing removes an entry when the install drops the row that held the alias. The new dependency resolves while the entry is still there.
- #44294 moves the registration out of the loaders

title: `bun update <alias>` right after a yarn.lock migration requests a wrong package name when the alias target is over 8 bytes
excerpt:
### What happens

A command that resolves a dependency row again, right after bun migrated yarn.lock, can request a wrong package name. The row is an `npm:` alias that a package of yarn.lock declares, and the target name is over 8 bytes.

```
# package.json
{ "name": "app", "dependencies": { "has-aliases": "1.0.0" } }

# yarn.lock (yarn v1)
"dependency-of-some-other-package@npm:some-other-package@1.0.0":
  version "1.0.0"
  resolved "<registry>/some-other-package/-/some-other-package-1.0.0.tgz#<sha1>"
  integrity <sha512>

has-aliases@1.0.0:
  version "1.0.0"
  resolved "<registry>/has-aliases/-/has-aliases-1.0.0.tgz#<sha1>"
  integrity <sha512>
  dependencies:
    dependency-of-some-other-package "npm:some-other-package@1.0.0"
```

```
$ bun update dependency-of-some-other-package
migrated lockfile from yarn.lock
error: GET <registry>/:%2f%2flocalhost:PORT - 404
error: dependency-of-some-other-package@npm:some-other-package@1.0.0 failed to resolve
```

- With a target name of 8 bytes or less (`npm:short@1.0.0`), the same command exits 0.
- `bun install` and `bun update` with no name exit 0 in this project. They keep the package that yarn.lock binds to the row.
- With the alias in the root package.json, the command exits 0. bun reads that row from package.json.

Seen on bun 1.4.3-canary.1 (367d939d9) and on main at a4f1429148. #44294 does not change this result.

### Cause

The yarn.lock migration parses a dependency row with the version literal as its own string buffer: `SlicedString::init(literal, literal)` in `src/install/yarn.rs` (lines 1635, 1707, 1759, 1811 and 1863 on main, and line 573 in `process_deps`).

`Dependency::parse` stores a string over 8 bytes as an offset into the buffer it gets (`sliced.sub(...)` in `src/install/dependency.rs`). The offset is then relative to the literal, and not to `lockfile.buffers.string_bytes`. The migration sets `version.literal` again after the parse, so the literal is right and the name of the alias target is not. A reader slices that name from `string_bytes` and gets other bytes. In the output above they are a part of the registry URL.

Other rows parse against the lockfile buffer: `version_string.sliced(this.buffers.string_bytes.as_slice())` at `yarn.rs:1175`, and `npm_lock.rs:679` for package-lock.json.

From a read of `Dependency::parse`, the same holds for each string that it slices from such a row: a git or GitHub reference, a tarball URL, a folder path, a dist-tag over 8 bytes. I ran only the alias case.

title: The yarn.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml migrations read the lockfile through `manager.lockfile` while they hold `&mut Lockfile`
excerpt:
### What happens

The migrations of yarn.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml end with `Lockfile::fetch_necessary_package_metadata_after_yarn_or_pnpm_migration(&mut self, manager)` (`src/install/lockfile.rs:1485`, called from `yarn.rs:1920` and `pnpm.rs:1623`). Its first step is `populate_manifest_cache(manager, Packages::All)`. For `Packages::All` that function walks the packages of `manager.lockfile`, through a shared reference that it makes from a raw pointer to the manager (`src/install/PackageManager/PopulateManifestCache.rs:144`).

At the call sites that load the lockfile in place, `manager.lockfile` is the same allocation as `self`:

- `install_with_manager` (`src/install/PackageManager/install_with_manager.rs:86`)
- `PackageManager::load_lockfile_from_cwd` (`src/install/PackageManager.rs:838`)
- `bun pm migrate` (`src/runtime/cli/package_manager_command.rs:733`)
- `bun outdated` (`outdated_command.rs:116`) and `bun pm scan` (`scan_command.rs:46`)

So the migration reads the lockfile through a `&Lockfile` while the `&mut Lockfile` that it got from the caller is live. I know of no wrong result from this.

Two more facts, from a read of the code:

- The comments at those call sites said that the load "never re-projects `manager.lockfile`". #44294 removes that sentence. It does not change the code.
- `bun why` (`why_command.rs:351`) and `bun pm diff` (`pm_diff_command.rs:387`) take the lockfile out of the manager before the load. `populate_manifest_cache` then sees an empty lockfile and requests no manifest. The step that fills `bin`, `os` and `cpu` after it has only the manifests of the disk cache.

The line numbers are those of main at 2722608f47.

### Possible change

Give `populate_manifest_cache` the lockfile (or the slices that it reads) as an argument, and do not read `manager.lockfile` there. The migration then passes `self`, and the two kinds of caller behave the same.

### What happens

`bun update --latest` moves a package past the version of its catalog entry when only an override refers to that entry. The catalog entry keeps the old version in package.json and in bun.lock.

  "name": "app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "workspaces": { "packages": [], "catalog": { "kept": "1.0.0" } },
  "dependencies": { "parent": "1.0.0" },

The registry has `kept@1.0.0`, `kept@1.1.0` and `parent@1.0.0`. `parent` depends on `kept@^1.0.0`.

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile` reports no changes.

`docs/pm/overrides.mdx` says that `catalog:` "keeps the overridden version in sync with a workspace catalog".

When a dependency also refers to the entry (`"dependencies": { "kept": "catalog:" }`), the same command writes `1.1.0` to the catalog entry in package.json and in bun.lock. The entry and the row then agree.

Worker global scope has no close() (DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope.close)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```ts
// worker.ts
postMessage({ hasClose: "close" in self, type: typeof (self as any).close })
```

```ts
// main.ts
const w = new Worker(new URL("./worker.ts", import.meta.url).href)
w.onmessage = (e) => { console.log(JSON.stringify(e.data)); w.terminate() }
```

`bun main.ts`

### What is the expected behavior?

`{"hasClose":true,"type":"function"}`. The HTML spec defines `close()` on `DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`, which discards the worker's pending tasks and stops the worker ([spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#dom-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-close)). Browsers and Deno implement it.

### What do you see instead?

`{"hasClose":false,"type":"undefined"}`

Libraries that treat the worker global as a `MessagePort` and call `close()` on shutdown throw `TypeError: ... close is not a function` under Bun. `@effect/platform-browser`'s `BrowserWorkerRunner` is one example: Effect-TS/effect#8635.

### Additional information

`process.exit()` works inside the worker, but code written for the web platform expects `self.close()`.

title: process.title is still not visible to ps / pgrep on macOS and Linux (#14255 was closed but not fixed)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.0-canary.1+da08a6b8d. Also reproduced on 1.4.2 (latest stable) and 1.4.2-canary.20260930.1.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

#14255 was closed as "Already Fixed" in February. The bot that closed it only checked that `process.title` reads back its new value in JS. As @Jarred-Sumner said on that issue, the purpose of `process.title` is to change how the process appears in `ps`, `top`, `htop` and to other programs. That part still does not work, so this issue tracks it.

```js
// repro.js
process.title = "my-renamed-proc";
console.log(`pid ${process.pid}, process.title = ${process.title}`);
setInterval(() => {}, 1000);
```

```sh
bun "$PWD/repro.js" &
ps -o command= -p $!
pgrep -f my-renamed-proc
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`pgrep -f my-renamed-proc` finds the process, and `ps` shows the new title, as in Node. The Node docs say: "Assigning a new value to `process.title` modifies the current value of `ps`."

Node on the same machine (v20.18.0) with the same script:

```
pid 56760, process.title = my-renamed-proc
pgrep -f my-renamed-proc -> 56760
```

### What do you see instead?

```
pid 56750, process.title = my-renamed-proc
ps -o command= -p 56750  -> bun /…/repro.js
pgrep -f my-renamed-proc -> (no output)
```

The value reads back correctly in JS, but the OS never sees it. I got the same result under `bun --watch`. This matters for any tooling that finds or cleans up processes by title (`pgrep -f`/`pkill -f`, process monitors).

### Additional information

Cause: on POSIX, `Bun__Process__setTitle` in `src/runtime/node/node_process.rs` only stores the string for the getter. There is still a `TODO` pointing at libuv's `darwin-proctitle.c`. The `--title` CLI flag works the same way. Windows already calls `uv_set_process_title`. I tested on macOS; Linux uses the same POSIX setter path.

Earlier fix attempts were all closed without merging: #26697, #28051, and #34618 (Linux only, closed as stale).

A fix for macOS and Linux is in #44318.

title: bun patch --commit records the .bun-tag cache marker when re-patching an already patched package
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64 (reproduced with both the hoisted and isolated linkers)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{"name":"repro","private":true,"dependencies":{"ms":"2.1.3"}}' > package.json
bun install

# First patch: fine
bun patch ms
# edit node_modules/ms/index.js
bun patch --commit ms

# Patch the already-patched package again
bun patch ms
# edit node_modules/ms/index.js again
bun patch --commit ms

head -3 patches/ms@2.1.3.patch
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The second patch contains only changes to package files.

### What do you see instead?

After the second `bun patch ms`, `node_modules/ms` contains the cache marker `.bun-tag-3ba6e16088f1e643`, and `--commit` records it as a new file with a malformed header:

```diff
diff --git a/node_modules/ms/.bun-tag-3ba6e16088f1e643 b/.bun-tag-3ba6e16088f1e643
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391
diff --git a/index.js b/index.js
```

The `a/` side keeps the `node_modules/ms/` prefix while the `b/` side does not, and `git apply` rejects the patch:

```text
error: git diff header lacks filename information when removing 1 leading pathname component at patches/ms@2.1.3.patch:4
```

### Additional information

The first `bun patch` / `--commit` cycle is clean. The marker appears only when `bun patch` runs on a package that is already patched (its folder comes from the `_patch_hash=` cache entry, which holds the tag). Excluding `.bun-tag-*` from the diff, or not copying it into `node_modules/<pkg>` for `bun patch`, would avoid it.

Related, but separate: #33520 (a patched cache folder without its tag gets reused unpatched) and #41733 (hunks applied without context checks).

title: `bun test --coverage` takes about 512 MB for each covered file that has a source map from `bun build`
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1 (main at 2722608f47). The files named below are the same at 5a183c1ebc.

### What happens

`bun test --coverage` makes the line sets of a report for 2^31 lines when the covered file has a JSON source map. Each such file adds about 512 MB to the peak RSS and about 0.55 s to the run. Output of `bun build --target=bun` with `--sourcemap=external`, `linked` or `inline` is such a file.

I found this while I worked on #44295. That PR does not change it.

| Run | Peak RSS | Time |
|---|---|---|
| the repro below | 794 MB | 0.6 s |
| `--sourcemap=linked` | 794 MB | 0.6 s |
| `--sourcemap=inline` | 793 MB | 0.65 s |
| `--sourcemap=none` | 26 MB | 0.01 s |
| the test imports `./lib.ts` | 26 MB | 0.01 s |
| 2 built files, the test calls a function of each | 1,305 MB | 1.1 s |
| 4 built files, the test calls a function of each | 2,330 MB | 2.3 s |

Linux x64, release build. Peak RSS is `ru_maxrss` of the `bun test` process.

### Where

1. `parse_json` passes `i32::MAX` as the line count of the original source (`src/sourcemap/lib.rs:947`). `mapping::parse` stores it in `ParsedSourceMap::input_line_count` (`src/sourcemap/Mapping.rs:728`).
2. The coverage report takes `input_line_count + 1` as its line count (`src/sourcemap_jsc/CodeCoverage.rs:843`). It makes two bit sets and one `Vec<u32>` of that length (`:844` to `:846`). Two bit sets of 2^31 bits are 512 MB.

The source map that bun makes when it transpiles a file stores a line count of its own (`src/sourcemap/InternalSourceMap.rs:66`). So a `.ts` file that the test imports directly does not show this.

### How to reproduce

```sh
printf 'export function first() {\n  return 1;\n}\nexport function second() {\n  return 2;\n}\n' > lib.ts
bun build --target=bun --sourcemap=external lib.ts --outdir=dist
printf 'import { expect, test } from "bun:test";\nimport { first } from "./dist/lib.js";\ntest("a", () => { expect(first()).toBe(1); });\n' > a.test.ts
bun test --coverage
```

The run passes and prints the table. It takes about 0.5 s and 794 MB for a file of 6 lines.

title: `bun test --parallel`: a worker that panics after its last test file does not fail the run
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1 (main at 2722608f47). The files named below are the same at 5a183c1ebc.

### What happens

Under `--parallel`, a worker that panics after its last test file does not change the exit code of the run. With `--coverage`, the run then has no coverage from that worker, and `coverageThreshold` does not fail the run.

| Run of the repro below | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun test --coverage` | `panic: range start index 4294967295 out of range for slice of length 5`, exit code 134 |
| `bun test --coverage --parallel` | the panic text of the worker on stderr, `2 pass`, no coverage table, exit code 0 |
| the same with `coverageThreshold = { lines = 0.9, functions = 0.9 }` | no coverage table, exit code 0 |
| the same, and both tests also import a second file that sorts first | a table with that file alone, exit code 0 |

I found this while I worked on #44295. The panic of this repro is the bug that #44295 fixes, so the repro needs a build without that PR. #44295 does not change the coordinator.

### Where

`Coordinator::reap_worker` (`src/runtime/cli/test/parallel/Coordinator.rs:584`) reads `is_panic_status(status)` in two cases only: a file is in flight (`w.inflight`), or the worker died before it was ready (`startup_failure`). A worker that sent its test results and then dies is in neither case. Here the worker dies in `worker_flush_aggregates` (`src/runtime/cli/test/parallel/runner.rs:701`), which makes the coverage reports of the worker and sends them (`:723`).

The comment in `reap_worker` says that a fatal signal from Bun's own panic handler "must not be masked by the rest of the suite passing". `docs/test/parallel.mdx:62` says: "A crash from a fatal signal aborts the whole run, so later passing files can't mask it."

### How to reproduce

```sh
printf '// @bun\nexport function first() {\n  return 1;\n}\nexport const second = () => 2;' > prebuilt.js
printf 'import { expect, test } from "bun:test";\nimport { first } from "./prebuilt.js";\ntest("a", () => { expect(first()).toBe(1); });\n' > a.test.ts
printf 'import { test } from "bun:test";\ntest("b", () => {});\n' > b.test.ts
bun test --coverage --parallel; echo "exit code $?"
```

`prebuilt.js` has no newline at the end. The second test file is necessary: with one test file, `--parallel` runs the file in the main process.

### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Currently, developers using Bun for full-stack and frontend development often still have to rely on Vite (`vite`, `@vitejs/*`, `rollup`, `esbuild`) to get a standard developer experience (HTML entry-point serving, robust HMR/Fast Refresh, asset processing, and production chunking).

This introduces heavy `node_modules` overhead, duplicate tooling, and process-management friction when Bun already possesses native bundling primitives (`Bun.build`) and a high-performance HTTP server (`Bun.serve`).

Reference package/concept:
[https://www.npmjs.com/package/bun-as-vite](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bun-as-vite)

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Provide built-in, first-class CLI commands and configuration presets that make Bun a direct, drop-in alternative to Vite for frontend applications:

1. **Native HTML Dev Server (`bun dev`):** Serve `index.html` natively, automatic on-the-fly transpilation for `.tsx`/`.jsx`/`.ts`, CSS bundling, and zero-config asset serving without external wrapper scripts.
2. **Built-in Fast Refresh & HMR:** Out-of-the-box HMR protocol compatible with standard web workflows, preserving component state during rapid iteration.
3. **Unified Single-Binary Build (`bun build --target browser`):** Streamline standard production outputs (asset hashing, chunk splitting, HTML injection) directly via the C++/Zig core engine without needing Vite/Rollup in `devDependencies`.
4. **Vite Plugin Shim / API Compatibility:** An adapter or standard loader format allowing common Vite plugins (or a simplified Bun equivalent) to integrate seamlessly into `bun.config.ts`.

### What alternatives have you considered?

_No response_

title: fetch: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS doesn't trust a self-signed CA:FALSE leaf cert (Node does)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (Linux arm64)

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, aarch64 (devcontainer)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`fetch()` rejects a self-signed certificate that has `basicConstraints: CA:FALSE` even when that exact certificate is pinned via `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. Node.js trusts the identical certificate/env-var combination without issue.

This certificate shape is what ASP.NET Core's `dotnet dev-certs` / .NET Aspire generate for local HTTPS development, and Aspire's documented way to let Node.js/Bun apps trust it is exactly `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` (see [Aspire certificate configuration docs](https://aspire.dev/app-host/certificate-configuration/)). Minimal repro:

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro

# Self-signed cert shaped like dotnet dev-certs: CA:FALSE, EKU=serverAuth
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 365 -nodes \
  -subj "/CN=localhost" \
  -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:FALSE" \
  -addext "keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature,keyEncipherment" \
  -addext "extendedKeyUsage=critical,serverAuth" \
  -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"
```

```ts

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
const cert = readFileSync("./cert.pem", "utf8");
const key = readFileSync("./key.pem", "utf8");

# Node client — SUCCEEDS (control, same cert, same env var)

  'fetch("https://localhost:8443/").then(async r => console.log(r.status, await r.text()))'

Both runtimes should trust the pinned certificate and return `200 ok`, matching Node's behavior.

title: bun-types: SQL `database` is documented to default to the username, but the mysql/mariadb adapters default to "mysql"/"mariadb"
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+5f554969b (bun-types 1.4.2)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-31-generic x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun-types/sql.d.ts` documents the `database` option of `PostgresOrMySQLOptions` (shared by the `postgres`, `mysql` and `mariadb` adapters) as:

```ts
/**
 * Name of the database to connect to
 * @default The username value
 */
database?: string | undefined;
```

(the deprecated `db` alias says the same). That holds for `postgres`, but the `mysql` and `mariadb` adapters default it to the adapter's name instead:

```ts
import { SQL } from "bun";

const user = "someuser";
for (const url of [
  `postgres://${user}:pw@127.0.0.1:1/`,
  `mysql://${user}:pw@127.0.0.1:1/`,
  `mariadb://${user}:pw@127.0.0.1:1/`,
]) {
  const sql = new SQL(url); // no connection is made
  console.log(url.split(":")[0], (sql as any).options.database);
}
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Either the documented default (the username) for all three adapters, or JSDoc that states the per-adapter default:

```

mysql someuser
mariadb someuser
```

### What do you see instead?

```
postgres someuser
mysql mysql
mariadb mariadb
```

Connecting to a MariaDB/MySQL server with a URL that has no database path (e.g. `mariadb://root:secret@127.0.0.1:3306/`, a common shape for admin connections) then fails with `Unknown database 'mariadb'` (or `'mysql'`), which the types give no hint of.

### Additional information

The behaviour looks deliberate (the adapter defaults are set in `src/js/internal/sql/shared.ts`), so this may be a documentation fix in `packages/bun-types/sql.d.ts` rather than a runtime change.

title: `process.env.TZ` reads `undefined` when `TZ` is set to an empty string
excerpt:
### What happens

`process.env.TZ`, `process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` and `process.env.BUN_CONFIG_VERBOSE_FETCH` read `undefined` when the environment sets them to an empty string. `Object.keys(process.env)` still lists them. Every other variable reads `""`. Node reads `""` for all of them.

```sh
$ S='console.log(process.env.TZ, process.env.NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, process.env.BUN_CONFIG_VERBOSE_FETCH, JSON.stringify(process.env.OTHER), "TZ" in process.env)'
$ TZ= NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED= BUN_CONFIG_VERBOSE_FETCH= OTHER= bun -e "$S"
undefined undefined undefined "" true
$ TZ= NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED= BUN_CONFIG_VERBOSE_FETCH= OTHER= node -e "$S"
   "" true
```

Bun 1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9 on Linux x64. Node v26.3.0.

### What follows from it

Each row runs with `TZ=` in the environment. `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=` gives the same results.

| | Node | Bun |
|---|---|---|
| `process.env.TZ` | `""` | `undefined` |
| `{ ...process.env }.TZ` | `""` | `undefined` |
| `JSON.stringify(process.env)` | has `"TZ":""` | has no `TZ` |
| `process.env.TZ` in a `node:worker_threads` Worker | `""` | the string `"undefined"` |
| `process.loadEnvFile()`, the file has `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` | keeps `""` | sets `"Asia/Tokyo"` |
| `process.execve("/usr/bin/env", ["env"])` | the new image has `TZ=` | the new image has no `TZ` |

### Cause

The three variables are `CustomAccessor` properties on `process.env`. Each getter in `src/jsc/bindings/JSEnvironmentVariableMap.cpp` treats an empty value as a variable that is not set:

```cpp
if (!Bun__getEnvValue(globalObject, &name, &value) || value.len == 0) {
    return JSValue::encode(jsUndefined());
}
```

The getters are `jsTimeZoneEnvironmentVariableGetter`, `jsNodeTLSRejectUnauthorizedGetter` and `jsBunConfigVerboseFetchGetter`.

One caller works around the `undefined`. The env loop of `Process_functionExecve` in `src/jsc/bindings/BunProcess.cpp` skips an `undefined` value ("The accessor-backed keys ... read back undefined for an unset / empty value"). The test "inherits process.env when env is omitted with an empty TZ in the OS env" in `test/js/node/process/process-execve.test.ts` pins that skip. Because of the skip, `process.execve(path, args, { A: undefined })` does not throw. Node throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`.

The review of #44356 found this. That PR does not change it.

Intl.Segments.containing() includes the preceding grapheme at a leading surrogate
excerpt:
### Bun versions

Reproduced on Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.18.44) with:

- Bun 1.3.14+0d9b296af
- Bun 1.4.2+744846f84

### Minimal reproduction

Save as `repro.mjs` and run `bun repro.mjs`. No dependencies or terminal UI library are needed.

```js
const text = 'a\u{1F600}'; // a😀, three UTF-16 code units
const segments = new Intl.Segmenter('en', {
  granularity: 'grapheme',
}).segment(text);
const summarize = ({ index, segment }) => ({ index, segment });

console.log(JSON.stringify({
  iteration: [...segments].map(summarize),
  atLeadingSurrogate: summarize(segments.containing(1)),
  atTrailingSurrogate: summarize(segments.containing(2)),
}));
```

### Expected behavior

Iteration identifies two graphemes, `a` at index 0 and `😀` at index 1. Both UTF-16 offsets 1 and 2 are inside that same emoji grapheme, so both containing calls should return `{ "index": 1, "segment": "😀" }`.

Node v24.19.0 and Deno 2.9.0 produce:

```json
{"iteration":[{"index":0,"segment":"a"},{"index":1,"segment":"😀"}],"atLeadingSurrogate":{"index":1,"segment":"😀"},"atTrailingSurrogate":{"index":1,"segment":"😀"}}
```

### Actual behavior

Both tested Bun versions produce:

```json
{"iteration":[{"index":0,"segment":"a"},{"index":1,"segment":"😀"}],"atLeadingSurrogate":{"index":0,"segment":"a😀"},"atTrailingSurrogate":{"index":1,"segment":"😀"}}
```

The result at the leading surrogate includes the preceding grapheme, contradicting the segmentation iterator. The trailing-surrogate lookup is correct. This also reproduces with `ab😀cd` at offset 2 and `a👩‍💻` at offset 1.

### Impact

This was found while qualifying a terminal editor: normalizing a caret already at an emoji's starting boundary moves it backward into the preceding grapheme. The standalone reproduction above isolates the issue from terminal decoding and application code.

I have not established the underlying implementation cause or tested other operating systems.

title: Bun.write(Bun.stdout, data) pads an appended file with NUL bytes when data is over 1024 bytes (fallocate on an O_APPEND fd)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.7 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
printf 'abc\n' > out.log
bun -e 'await Bun.write(Bun.stdout, "x".repeat(1999) + "\n")' >> out.log
wc -c < out.log                 # 4000
tr -cd '\0' < out.log | wc -c   # 1996
```

It needs stdout opened with `O_APPEND` (`>>`), more than 1024 bytes written, and a file shorter than the data. With 1024 bytes, or with a file already longer than the data, the output is correct.

### What is the expected behavior?

`out.log` is `abc\n` followed by the 2000 bytes, 2004 bytes in total, as with `process.stdout.write` or `fs.writeFileSync(1, …)`.

### What do you see instead?

4000 bytes: `abc\n`, then 1996 NUL bytes, then the data.

`strace` shows

```
fallocate(1, 0, 0, 2000) = 0
write(1, "xxxx"..., 2000) = 2000
```

`fallocate` with mode 0 grows the file to 2000 bytes, and the `O_APPEND` write then lands after the new end.

### Additional information

The preallocation is in [`WriteFile`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/4b02e1031d6195d96fc0446dfbff49297f89f2d6/src/runtime/webcore/blob/write_file.rs#L452-L467): for more than 1024 bytes on Linux it calls `preallocate_file(fd, 0, len)`, which is `fallocate(fd, 0, 0, len)`, without checking how the fd was opened. The equivalent preallocation in `node:fs` [already skips preallocation for `O_APPEND` fds](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/4b02e1031d6195d96fc0446dfbff49297f89f2d6/src/runtime/node/node_fs.rs#L7407-L7441) and uses the current offset from `lseek`; doing the same here, or passing `FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE`, would fix it.

We hit it in a merge script: the JSON output of a Bun script, appended to a log with `>>`, was preceded by 211,016 NUL bytes.

title: A failed directory read is taken as the end of the directory in 16 loops outside pack and publish
excerpt:
### What happens

`bun_sys::dir_iterator` `next()` returns an entry, the end of the directory, or the error of the read. Many callers fold the error into the end of the directory: `iter.next().unwrap_or(None)`, `while let Ok(Some(entry)) = iter.next()`, `Err(_) => break`. When one read of a directory fails (`EIO` from NFS, sshfs or FUSE, or `EINTR` on Linux), the caller continues with the entries it has. It prints nothing and the command exits 0.

#44400 fixes this for the eight loops of `bun pm pack` and `bun publish`. This issue tracks the other loops. Each needs its own decision: fail the command, or stay best-effort on purpose and say so in the code.

No user reported these. A fault-injection run found them: one `getdents64` of one directory fails with `EIO`. The results below are from that run on 1.4.2 and on main. Rows that say "from the source" were read and not run.

excerpt:
### What happens

Some numeric options accept NaN and silently use a placeholder. No error is thrown. #39682 fixes this for `uid` and `gid` of `Bun.spawn`, where the placeholder was id 0. The inputs below have the same shape and are not changed by that pull request.

No user reported these. They came up in the review of #39682.

#### 1. `maxBuffer` of `Bun.spawn` and `Bun.spawnSync`

```js
const big = ["sh", "-c", "head -c 200000 /dev/zero"];
for (const maxBuffer of [10, NaN, "10", -1]) {
  const r = Bun.spawnSync(big, { maxBuffer });
  console.log(String(maxBuffer), r.stdout.length, r.exitedDueToMaxBuffer, r.signalCode);
}
```

bun 1.4.3-canary (Linux x64) prints:

```
10 65546 true SIGTERM
NaN 200000 undefined undefined
10 200000 undefined undefined
-1 200000 undefined undefined
```

NaN, a negative number and a string remove the limit. The caller believes that the output is bounded.

`child_process.spawnSync` with the same three values throws in bun and in node 26.3.0, because `node:child_process` validates `maxBuffer` in JavaScript. So only a direct caller of `Bun.spawn` or `Bun.spawnSync` is affected.

Cause: the `maxBuffer` branch of `spawn_maybe_sync` (`src/runtime/api/bun/js_bun_spawn_bindings.rs:769`) sets the limit only for a finite number above 0. Every other value leaves the limit unset. `Infinity` means "no limit" on purpose, and a comment there says so.

#### 2. Callers of `validate_integer_range`

`JSGlobalObject::validate_integer_range` (`src/jsc/JSGlobalObject.rs:1252`) returns the caller's `default` argument for NaN. These inputs take that default today:

excerpt:

### What platform is your computer?

Windows, any version. I found this by reading the source and have not run it on a Windows machine.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun init` writes `.cursor/rules/use-bun-instead-of-node-vite-npm-pnpm.mdc` when it detects Cursor. On Windows, unless `CURSOR_TRACE_ID` is set, it detects Cursor by building a path from the `USER` environment variable:

                ...

title: docs: bun test "AI Agent Integration" omits how AGENT and RUNNER_DEBUG turn failures-only output off
excerpt:
### What is the type of issue?

Documentation is missing

### What is the issue?

The "AI Agent Integration" section of the test runner docs lists `CLAUDECODE=1`, `REPL_ID=1`, and `AGENT=1` as ways to enable failures-only output, but says nothing about how detection is turned off or which variable wins. Inside an agent session (for example Claude Code, which sets `CLAUDECODE`), the docs give no way to see passing test files again, and an exported `AGENT` with any value other than `1` silently disables the documented `CLAUDECODE=1` behavior.

What the runtime does (`is_ai_agent` in `src/bun_core/output.rs`, unchanged between `bun-v1.4.2` and current `main`):

- If `AGENT` is set at all, it decides: only the exact value `1` enables agent mode; any other value (`0`, `true`, an empty string) disables it, even when `CLAUDECODE` or `REPL_ID` is set. https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99/src/bun_core/output.rs#L870-L897
- Otherwise, if `is_verbose()` is true, agent mode is off; `is_verbose()` is true when `RUNNER_DEBUG` is truthy (GitHub Actions debug logging). https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99/src/bun_core/output.rs#L903-L906
- Otherwise `CLAUDECODE` or `REPL_ID` enables it, and both accept any value except empty, `0`, `false`, `no`, or `off` (not only `1`). https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99/src/bun_core/env_var.rs#L410-L416
- Same code on main: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/faac63e6d4b4d90807f13308785d9ced3104681f/src/bun_core/output.rs#L853-L880 and https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/faac63e6d4b4d90807f13308785d9ced3104681f/src/bun_core/output.rs#L886-L889

Reproduction with Bun `1.4.2+744846f84` (official release binary) on macOS arm64: a directory with `alpha.test.ts` (2 passing), `beta.test.ts` (1 passing), and `gamma.test.ts` (1 passing, 1 failing), run with `CLAUDECODE`, `AGENT`, `REPL_ID`, `RUNNER_DEBUG`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, and `CI` unset except as listed:

| Environment / flags | File headers printed | `(pass)` lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | alpha, beta, gamma | 4 |
| `CLAUDECODE=1` | gamma only | 0 |
| `CLAUDECODE=1 AGENT=0` | alpha, beta, gamma | 4 |

title: fetch: four `Content-Encoding: deflate` bodies where Bun differs from Node or curl
excerpt:
#33711 changed how `fetch()` tells a zlib stream from raw deflate. Its tests pin the four results below. Each one differs from Node v26.3.0 or from curl 8.14.1. Only the first one is new in that PR. This issue tracks them, so that the test rows have a reference.

Results on main faac63e6d4, Linux x64. A row name is a row of the matrix in `test/js/web/fetch/fetch-gzip.test.ts`, in the `describe` block "Content-Encoding: deflate, zlib-wrapped or raw".

| | body | Bun | Node v26.3.0 | curl 8.14.1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | raw deflate that starts with a valid zlib header (`rawPassing1950`) | `ZlibError` | error | decodes |
| 2 | a zlib stream whose header declares a smaller window than its data uses (`lyingWindow`) | `ZlibError` | decodes | decodes |
| 3 | a raw deflate stream with 287 literal/length codes (no row) | decodes when whole, `ZlibError` when split | error | error |
| 4 | a body that ends after one byte, `78` (`oneByte`) | `ZlibError` | empty body | empty body |

### 1. Raw deflate that starts with a valid zlib header

- `has_zlib_header` (`src/http/Decompressor.rs`) accepts the first two bytes. zlib-ng then rejects the stream, and nothing tries raw deflate.

- Such a body needs a stored first block with a padding bit set. No deflater that I tested writes one: Node's zlib, zlib-ng, libdeflate and CPython's zlib.
- curl, Chromium and Firefox inflate the body as zlib. When that fails early, they start again as raw deflate (`lib/content_encoding.c`, `net/filter/gzip_source_stream.cc`, `netwerk/streamconv/converters/nsHTTPCompressConv.cpp`).
- If Bun adds the retry, its rule must depend on the body bytes only, not on the read boundaries. Decide on a bounded prefix, and reopen as raw when the zlib reading fails before the first output byte. `process_body_buffer` already presents unconsumed bytes again, so the decoder does not have to keep a copy.

title: node:http2 client: maxReservedRemoteStreams counts a pushed stream until it closes, node until its response HEADERS arrive
excerpt:
### What happens

A `node:http2` client counts a pushed stream against `maxReservedRemoteStreams` until that stream closes. node counts it only while it is reserved, which ends when the pushed response HEADERS arrive. So Bun refuses a PUSH_PROMISE that node accepts.

With `http2.connect(url, { maxReservedRemoteStreams: 1 })` a raw server sends, on request stream 1: PUSH_PROMISE for stream 2, the response HEADERS of stream 2 (no END_STREAM), then PUSH_PROMISE for stream 4.

```
node v26.3.0:                    'stream' events for 2 and 4, no RST_STREAM
bun 1.4.2 and 1.4.3-canary.1:    'stream' event for 2 only, RST_STREAM(4, CANCEL)
```

Without the HEADERS on stream 2 both refuse stream 4, which is correct.

### Why

nghttp2 keeps `num_incoming_reserved_streams`. It adds one when a reserved (remote) stream opens, and subtracts one when the pushed response HEADERS arrive (`nghttp2_session_on_push_response_headers_received`) or when a stream that is still reserved closes ([nghttp2_session.c](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.3.0/deps/nghttp2/lib/nghttp2_session.c#L3991-L3995)).

Bun keeps the count in JS: `ClientHttp2Session.#reservedStreamsCount` in `src/js/node/http2.ts`. The `streamPush` handler adds one, and a `'close'` listener on the pushed stream subtracts one.

### A second effect, once #37588 lands

The inbound engine (`Connection::handle_push_promise` in `src/runtime/api/bun/h2/connection.rs`) reserves every promised stream, and JS refuses the one over the limit afterwards. nghttp2 refuses before it counts the promised stream as processed ([the check](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.3.0/deps/nghttp2/lib/nghttp2_session.c#L4612-L4627) returns before `last_proc_stream_id` is set). Measured with PUSH_PROMISE for 2 and for 4 and a limit of 1:

```
node v26.3.0:  lastProcStreamID 2, the GOAWAY of session.close() names 2
bun today:     lastProcStreamID 1, GOAWAY names 0   (the mark is wrong for other reasons, #37588 fixes that)
bun + #37588:  lastProcStreamID 4, GOAWAY names 4   (not measured by me, the number comes from the work on #37588)
```

So after #37588 a refused promise is named as the last processed stream.

### Suggested shape

Keep the count in the parser or the engine, where the state of the promised stream is known (it leaves `ReservedRemote` when its HEADERS arrive), and refuse when the PUSH_PROMISE frame arrives. #43465 adds `Sink::can_accept_push(parent_id)` for exactly that point: the engine sends RST_STREAM(CANCEL) and de

title: TC39 decorators fail in the HMR runtime: missing bun:wrap helpers (source patch included)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

Reproduced with Bun 1.4.2 on Linux x86_64. The proposed source patch was built and tested against commit `bc7a813b10b6ef8accc00c931b9a501331ac8c5c` (Bun 1.4.3 development sources).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Serve an HTML entry point containing a TypeScript module with a standard TC39 decorator, using `development: { hmr: true }`.

`server.ts`:
```ts
import index from "./index.html";

Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  routes: { "/": index },
  development: { hmr: true },
});
```

`index.html`:
```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <body>
    <script type="module" src="./main.ts"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

`main.ts`:
```ts
function DEBUG(value: Function, context: ClassDecoratorContext) {
  console.log(typeof value, context.kind, context.name);
}

@DEBUG
class Example {}

console.log(new Example());
```

`tsconfig.json`:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "experimentalDecorators": false,
    "emitDecoratorMetadata": false
  }
}
```

Run `bun server.ts` and open `http://localhost:3000`.

### Expected behavior

The decorator receives the class constructor and a TC39 class context, and the module executes. Decorated modules also continue to work after HMR updates.

### Actual behavior

The browser bundle fails before the decorator executes:

```text
TypeError: import_bun_wrap.__decoratorStart is not a function
```

### Root cause and proposed fix

`src/runtime/bake/hmr-module.ts` supplies the synthetic `bun:wrap` module for both client and server HMR. Its registered exports include the legacy decorator helpers but omit the TC39 helpers emitted by the transpiler.

The patch imports the existing implementations from `runtime.bun` and registers:

- `__decorateElement`, `__decoratorMetadata`, `__decoratorStart`, `__runInitializers`.
- `__privateAdd`, `__privateGet`, `__privateIn`, `__privateMethod`, `__privateSet`, `__publicField`, which are also needed for lowering decorated private members and auto-accessors.

It also updates the internal `bun:wrap` declarations. It does not copy or replace the decorator implementations.

[Patch file](https://github.com/TiedWithType/bun-tc39-decorators/blob/72304f8f6f1d85d4d2631e43f3d55339eb41c492/patches/bun-hmr-tc39.patch) · [Raw download](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TiedWithType/bun-tc39-decorators/72304f8f6f1d85d4d2631e43f3d55339eb41c492/patches/bun-hmr-tc39.patch)

title: Bun.WebView (chrome backend): first navigate() on a fresh Chrome sometimes never settles on Windows, with no readiness signal
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Windows (GitHub Actions `windows-latest`); not observed on `ubuntu-latest` or `macos-latest` in the same runs.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Intermittent. A test process creates Chrome-backed views (`new Bun.WebView({ backend: "chrome" })`) on the main thread, sequentially, with `WebView.closeAll()` plus killing the browser tree between tests, then calls `await view.navigate(url)` on a local HTTP page.

We traced every launch on CI (10 full runs of our suite on `windows-latest`, about 130 first navigations):

- The constructor always returns in about 10 ms.
- Healthy first navigations settle in p50 2.0 s, p95 3.4 s, max 18 s (the first Chrome of a cold runner).
- In some runs the first `navigate()` on a freshly launched Chrome never settles: it was still pending after 60 s, and the local page server never received a request. The browser and its helpers stay alive until killed.
- On `ubuntu-latest` the same suite (140 first navigations) never stalled (max 1.2 s).

### What is the expected behavior?

The first navigation either settles, or rejects with an error that says which internal step did not complete (`Target.createTarget`, `Target.attachToTarget`, `Page.enable`, `Page.navigate`, load event), so the caller can tell a stuck launch from a slow page.

### What do you see instead?

`navigate()` stays pending with no event and no rejection. Before the first navigation there is no CDP session either (`cdp()` throws "no session - await navigate() first"), so the caller has no way to observe whether the target ever attached.

### Additional information

Feature request that would make this diagnosable and recoverable on the caller side: a readiness signal for Chrome-backed views (for example a promise or event when the target's CDP session is attached), or a per-step error/timeout inside the first navigation. Our current workaround is to navigate each new view to `about:blank` under a bound before handing it out, close a view that is still pending at the bound, end that browser, and launch once more.

`bun:test`'s test reporter ignores a user-assigned `Error.stack` and

lives inside a wrapper the test author intended to be invisible. This

```ts

function wrapper() {
  throw new Error('boom')
}

test('modified stack via captureStackTrace', () => {
  try {
    wrapper()
  } catch (err) {
    const e = err as Error
    // Filter `wrapper` out of the captured frames.
    Error.captureStackTrace(e, wrapper)
    // Inject a synthetic frame pointing to a user-code location.
    e.stack += '\n    at userCode (fake-user/src/thing.ts:42:5)'
    throw e
  }
})
```

## What is the expected behavior?

Bun's test reporter should render the modified stack — exactly the
way Node / Jest / Vitest do. In Jest, the canonical
[`Error.captureStackTrace(err, wrapper)`](https://kentcdodds.com/blog/improve-test-error-messages-of-your-abstractions)
pattern lets assertion-library authors hide their wrapper functions
and surface the caller's frame. Bun:test should respect the same
trick.

and shows that throw site — not the synthetic frame we appended, and
not the `wrapper()` call site either. The `e.stack +=` we did in the
catch is silently discarded.

### What happens

The per-encoding methods of `Buffer.prototype` (`hexSlice`, `utf8Slice`, `hexWrite`, `utf8Write` and the others) throw `TypeError: Expected ArrayBufferView` when the receiver is not an ArrayBufferView. The error has no `code`. Node throws `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: argument must be a buffer`.

The class of the error is the same. The `code` and the message differ. A receiver that is an ArrayBufferView and not a Buffer (a `DataView`, a `Uint8Array`) works in Node and in Bun.

### Reproduction

```js
const t = (n, f) => { try { console.log(n, "=>", JSON.stringify(f())); } catch (e) { console.log(n, "=> throws", e.name, e.code, JSON.stringify(e.message)); } };
const P = Buffer.prototype;
const dataView = () => new DataView(new Uint8Array([104, 105, 33, 33]).buffer);
for (const m of ["hexSlice", "utf8Slice", "hexWrite", "utf8Write"]) {
  const arg = m.endsWith("Write") ? ["ab"] : [];
  t(`${m}.call({})`, () => P[m].call({}, ...arg));
  t(`${m}.call(new ArrayBuffer(4))`, () => P[m].call(new ArrayBuffer(4), ...arg));
  t(`${m}.call(dataView())`, () => P[m].call(dataView(), ...arg));
}
```

Node v26.3.0 prints:

```
hexSlice.call({}) => throws TypeError ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE "argument must be a buffer"

node:http2 client: a PUSH_PROMISE before its enablePush=false SETTINGS is ACKed ends the session
excerpt:
### What happens

A `node:http2` client that called `session.settings({ enablePush: false })` fails the whole session when a PUSH_PROMISE arrives before the server ACKed that SETTINGS frame. node refuses only the promised stream and keeps the session.

RFC 9113 section 6.6: "An endpoint that has both set this parameter to 0 and had it acknowledged MUST treat the receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE frame as a connection error". Before the ACK the server can still have a push in flight.

A raw server completes the first SETTINGS exchange. The client has one open request (stream 1) and calls `client.settings({ enablePush: false })`. The server reads that SETTINGS frame and then writes PUSH_PROMISE (parent 1, promised 2) and a PING.

```
not ACKed before the PUSH_PROMISE
  node v26.3.0:                 RST_STREAM(2, CANCEL), the PING is ACKed, no 'stream' event, no session error
  bun 1.4.2, 1.4.3-canary.1:    GOAWAY(PROTOCOL_ERROR), then GOAWAY(INTERNAL_ERROR), session error ERR_HTTP2_ERROR, session closes

ACKed before the PUSH_PROMISE (both fail the session, which is correct)
  node v26.3.0:                 session error ERR_HTTP2_ERROR, GOAWAY(INTERNAL_ERROR)
  bun 1.4.2, 1.4.3-canary.1:    session error ERR_HTTP2_ERROR, GOAWAY(PROTOCOL_ERROR), then GOAWAY(INTERNAL_ERROR)
```

### Why

[`nghttp2_session_on_push_promise_received`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.3.0/deps/nghttp2/lib/nghttp2_session.c#L4572-L4627) makes it a connection error only when `local_settings.enable_push == 0`. nghttp2 updates `local_settings` when the ACK arrives. While the change is pending (`!session->pending_enable_push`) it cancels the promised stream with RST_STREAM(CANCEL) and ignores the header block.

`Connection::handle_push_promise` in `src/runtime/api/bun/h2/connection.rs` tests `self.local_settings.enable_push == 0`. The parser copies the submitted settings into `local_settings` on every read, so the test uses the submitted value and not the acknowledged one.

### Suggested shape

The engine already keeps acknowledged values for two settings: `acked_local_initial_window` and `enforced_max_header_list_size` take their value from `pending_local_settings_acks` when a SETTINGS ACK arrives. An `acked_local_enable_push` (1 until an ACK says otherwise) fits next to them. Then:

- the connection error uses the acknowledged value,
- a submitted value of 0 that is not acknowledged yet cancels the promise: RST_STREAM(CANCEL) on the promised stream, the block decoded for HPACK sync on

node:http2 server ends the session at the 100th malformed request, node keeps it
excerpt:
### What happens

A `node:http2` server in Bun ends the session with GOAWAY(ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM) at the 100th request that it rejects, for every kind of rejection. Node keeps the session in the cases below.

Bun has one counter, `rejected_streams`, that never goes back to 0, and it compares with `max <= count`. Four places add to it: a request refused for `maxSessionMemory`, a malformed header block, a header list over `maxHeaderListSize`, and `request()` over the memory limit. Node:

- counts with `rejected_stream_count_++ > max` and sets the count to 0 for each stream that it admits ([node_http2.cc:1038](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.3.0/src/node_http2.cc#L1035-L1050)). Only the memory refusal uses this counter.
- charges a malformed block to `maxSessionInvalidFrames` (default 1000), not to `maxSessionRejectedStreams` ([node_http2.cc:1128](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.3.0/src/node_http2.cc#L1128-L1143)).

### Repro

A raw client sends the preface, SETTINGS and 150 requests in one write, then a PING. Each request block has a `connection: close` field, which makes it malformed (RFC 9113 8.2.2). The server is `http2.createServer()` with default options.

| | RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR) | session |
|---|---|---|
| node v26.3.0 | 150 | open, PING answered |
| Bun 1.4.3 | 100 | GOAWAY(last stream 199, ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM), `ERR_HTTP2_SESSION_ERROR` |

### Notes

- `test/js/node/http2/node-http2.test.js` has tests that pin the current count (a GOAWAY at the first rejection with `maxSessionRejectedStreams: 0`). Node keeps the session for that first rejection.
- #44337 moves the refusal for SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS to `maxSessionInvalidFrames`, as in node. It does not change the four writers above.

title: node:http2: session.settings({ enableConnectProtocol }) inside a handler applies from the next read
excerpt:
### What happens

A `node:http2` server calls `session.settings({ enableConnectProtocol: false })` inside a `'stream'` handler. A request with `:protocol` that arrives later in the same read still reaches the handler. Node rejects it with RST_STREAM(PROTOCOL_ERROR), because nghttp2 applies the submitted value at once (`pending_enable_connect_protocol`).

### Repro

The server starts with `settings: { enableConnectProtocol: true }`. The handler of stream 1 turns it off. A raw client sends, in one write: a GET on stream 1 and an extended CONNECT (`:method CONNECT`, `:protocol websocket`) on stream 3. In a later write it sends the same extended CONNECT on stream 5.

| | handlers | RST_STREAM |
|---|---|---|
| node v26.3.0 | 1 | 3 and 5, PROTOCOL_ERROR |
| Bun 1.4.3 | 1 and 3 (with `:protocol: websocket`) | 5, PROTOCOL_ERROR |

### Where

The h2 engine (`src/runtime/api/bun/h2/connection.rs`) reads `self.local_settings.enable_connect_protocol` in `finish_header_block`. `H2FrameParser::rewrite_read` copies the local settings into the engine once, at the start of a read (`engine.local_settings = self.rewrite_local_settings()`), so a change that a handler makes during the read is not seen until the next read.

#44337 adds a `Sink` query for one setting, `max_concurrent_streams`, for this reason. The same holds for the other local settings that the engine reads.

A TypeScript extension file (~68 KB, many CJK strings) loaded through a host app's package-discovery pipeline crashes Bun **deterministically at startup**:

panic(main thread): index out of bounds: index 87852, len 49147

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`repro.js`:

```js
const fs = require("node:fs");

for (const p of [".", ".."]) {
  try {
    console.log(`mkdirSync(${JSON.stringify(p)})`, fs.mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true }));
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(`mkdirSync(${JSON.stringify(p)}) threw`, e.code, e.errno);
  }
}

fs.mkdir(".", { recursive: true }, (err) => console.log("mkdir(\".\") callback", err ? err.code : "ok"));
fs.promises.mkdir(".", { recursive: true }).then(
  () => console.log("promises.mkdir(\".\") ok"),
  (e) => console.log("promises.mkdir(\".\") rejected", e.code),
);
```

Run `bun repro.js`, then `node repro.js`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Recursive mkdir of an existing directory is a no-op. Node v26.10.0:

```
mkdirSync(".") undefined
mkdirSync("..") undefined
mkdir(".") callback ok
promises.mkdir(".") ok
```

### What do you see instead?

All three APIs throw `EEXIST` for `.` and `..`:

```
mkdirSync(".") threw EEXIST -4075
mkdirSync("..") threw EEXIST -4075
mkdir(".") callback EEXIST
promises.mkdir(".") rejected EEXIST
```

An absolute path to the same directory (`fs.mkdirSync(process.cwd(), { recursive: true })`) works.

### What do you see instead?

This is the same case as #21901, which was closed as fixed by #26634. That PR fixed `.` normalization for `exists`/`stat` only, and recursive mkdir still fails on current canary, without needing `Promise.all`.

Real-world impact: any `mkdirp(path.dirname(file))` where `file` is a bare relative filename ends up calling `mkdir(".", { recursive: true })`. For example, fs-extra's `move(src, "out.json")` fails with `EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '.'`. In our case this broke an rspack plugin that writes a stats file, which failed every dev compile and left webpack-dev-middleware requests hanging.

title: [FEATURE] TCP User Timeout for FetchSession and Sockets
excerpt:
The following is AI generated, but I proofread it and adjusted it where necessary and it makes sense to me. It is based on a real problem that I have with Claude Code ( https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/99524 ).

### What is the problem this feature would solve?

## Problem

Claude Code runs as a Bun standalone executable and sends its model API requests through a
`Bun.FetchSession`, which keeps a pool of keep-alive connections. After a network change, e.g. a
network change (e.g. wifi switch) on Linux (anthropics/claude-code#99524), a pooled connection keeps the old source IP
address. The kernel does not close the socket when that address disappears, and no RST arrives. A
request sent over this connection is retransmitted without ever being acknowledged. With default
settings, Linux gives up only after about 15 minutes (`net.ipv4.tcp_retries2 = 15`). Until then,
the `fetch` call neither resolves nor rejects, so the application has to rely on its own timeout.
In Claude Code that timeout is 180 s.

The operating systems already have a per-socket option for this case. It aborts a connection
when sent data stays unacknowledged for a given time:

| OS      | Option                 | Unit                                 |
| ------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Linux   | `TCP_USER_TIMEOUT`     | milliseconds                         |
| macOS   | `TCP_RXT_CONNDROPTIME` | seconds                              |
| Windows | `TCP_MAXRTMS`          | milliseconds (`TCP_MAXRT`: seconds)  |

Bun offers no way to set any of these options. `FetchSessionInit` has only `keepAlive`, `proxy`,
`tls` and `unix`, and the Node-compatible `net` API has no such option either. JavaScript code
cannot set the option with `bun:ffi`, because `fetch` does not expose its sockets.

## Proposal

### 1. A user timeout option for FetchSession

- A new `FetchSessionInit` field: `new Bun.FetchSession({ tcp: { userTimeout: ms } })`.
- Bun sets the option on every TCP connection of the session when it opens it. Plain `fetch()`
  calls get the option by passing such a session in the `session` option.
- The option does not apply to HTTP/3 connections, in line with the `keepAlive` limits, which also
  exclude HTTP/3.

### 2. The same option on the socket APIs

- `net.connect({ ..., userTimeout: ms })`, `tls.connect({ ..., userTimeout: ms })` and
  `Bun.connect({ ..., userTimeout: ms })`.
- `socket.setUserTimeout(ms)` on `net.Socket` and on the soc

Each number is the median of five fresh-process runs' mean batch latencies. A batch calls `set()` 2,100 times with a capacity of 1,000. Lower is better. Units are microseconds, **not nanoseconds**.

Lifecycle scripts have no equivalent for `run.bun`
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Bun with `run.bun = true` enabled in the `bunfig.toml` correctly shims `node` to point to `bun`. But this does not apply for lifecycle scripts, like `prepare`. This results in some lifecycle commands failing if you happen to use Bun-specific features and don't explicitly declare them to run with Bun. For example, SvelteKit's `svelte-kit sync` command will run your project under Node to re-generate `.svelte-kit` output—in my case, this results in my `uno.config.js` script running, which contains `Bun` namespace function calls, which causes `svelte-kit sync` to fail under Node.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Add a new config value and command line option to add the same Node shim for lifecycle scripts.

### What alternatives have you considered?

Adding `bun run --bun` to every lifecycle script that might possibly call Node. It works, but it's annoying and shouldn't be necessary.

Uninstalling Node/removing Node from `$PATH` also works, but again, this shouldn't be necessary.

title: fs.realpathSync.native resolves ".." before following a symlink, unlike node
excerpt:
## What breaks

`fs.realpathSync.native` disagrees with node when a `..` follows a symlink segment. Bun collapses `link/..` lexically, so the result is a sibling of the link, not of its target.

```text
$ bun repro.mjs /tmp/repro/base
input          : /tmp/repro/base/link/../x
realpath.native: /tmp/repro/base/x
realpath (js)  : /tmp/repro/base/x
```

```text
$ node repro.mjs /tmp/repro/base
input          : /tmp/repro/base/link/../x
realpath.native: /tmp/repro/base/real/x
realpath (js)  : /tmp/repro/base/x
```

Node's JS `fs.realpathSync` also collapses lexically, and bun matches it there. The divergence is only in `.native`, which node implements with libc `realpath(3)`. The shell's `realpath(1)` and Python's `os.path.realpath` both return `base/real/x` for the same input, like node's `.native`.

## Repro

1. `mkdir -p /tmp/repro/base/real/inner && touch /tmp/repro/base/real/x /tmp/repro/base/x && ln -s real/inner /tmp/repro/base/link`
2. `bun repro.mjs /tmp/repro/base` and `node repro.mjs /tmp/repro/base`

```js
import fs from "node:fs";

// Concatenate: path.join() would collapse the ".." lexically before either runtime sees it.
const input = process.argv[2] + "/link/../x";
console.log("input          :", input);
console.log("realpath.native:", fs.realpathSync.native(input));
console.log("realpath (js)  :", fs.realpathSync(input));
```

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** `realpathSync.native` follows `base/link` to `base/real/inner`, then applies `..`, giving `/tmp/repro/base/real/x` as node does.
- **Actual:** bun collapses `base/link/..` to `base` lexically first and returns `/tmp/repro/base/x`.

Versions: bun 1.4.2+744846f84, node v26.9.0, macOS (`Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`).

title: fs.rm with force fails with ENOTDIR on a missing path with a trailing slash (gVisor)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (`oven/bun:1`)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64, inside a gVisor (runsc release-20260928.0) sandbox

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`fs.rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })` on a path that doesn't exist, written with a trailing slash, on a filesystem where `unlink()` of that path returns `ENOTDIR` instead of `ENOENT`:

```js
await require("fs/promises").rm("/src/.output/", { recursive: true, force: true })
```

Under gVisor, `unlink("/src/.output/")` returns `ENOTDIR` for a missing path (gVisor bug, reported at google/gvisor#15303), while `lstat` of the same path correctly returns `ENOENT`.

This is exactly what Nitro does before every build (`prepareDir` → `fs.rm('.output/', { recursive: true, force: true })`), so Nuxt, TanStack Start and other Nitro-based builds fail under Bun in gVisor-sandboxed CI and build services.

### What is the expected behavior?

`force: true` means a missing path is not an error, so the call resolves.

Node's `rm` lstat()s the path first (`ENOENT` → done with `force`), so it doesn't depend on which errno `unlink` reports for a missing path with a trailing slash.

### What do you see instead?

```
Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory, rm '/src/.output/'
  code: 'ENOTDIR', path: '/src/.output/', syscall: 'rm', errno: -20
```

Probe of the same paths in the sandbox:

```
/src/.missing/  lstat=ENOENT rmdir=ENOENT unlink=ENOTDIR  rmSync({recursive,force})=ENOTDIR
/src/.missing   lstat=ENOENT rmdir=ENOENT unlink=ENOENT   rmSync({recursive,force})=ok
```

### Additional information

The root cause is gVisor's errno, but `rm` with `force` could be robust to it: on `ENOTDIR` from `unlink`, check `lstat` and treat `ENOENT` as missing (or lstat first, as Node does). Found while running user builds in gVisor for [homeport](https://homeport.sh).

title: RealAudio/RealVideo MIME types incorrect
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.18.54-0-lts x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```
Bun.file("file.ra").type
Bun.file("file.rv").type
```

### What is the expected behavior?

According to [archived RealNetworks documentation](https://web.archive.org/web/20110705135130/http://service.real.com/help/faq/rp8/configrp8win.html), the MIME types for RealAudio and RealVideo file extensions (they both share the RMF container format so this is really only for describing the extension/contained data) should respectively be:

```
audio/vnd.rn-realaudio
video/vnd.rn-realvideo
```

### What do you see instead?

Bun uses `audio/x-realaudio` for RealAudio and has nothing for RealVideo.

```
audio/x-realaudio
application/octet-stream
```

### Additional information

Not sure where this usage originated from, but it looks like [NGINX uses it](https://github.com/nginx/nginx/blob/2b5c2b605b5df669da5dec6749dcc76c07d1315d/conf/mime.types#L85). Some Apache HTTPD configs are floating around that `AddType` it for `.ra`/`.ram`, but current HTTPD specifies [`audio/x-pn-realaudio`](https://github.com/apache/httpd/blob/trunk/docs/conf/mime.types) for RealAudio (technically incorrect as this is for the streaming metadata format `.ram`) and nothing for RealVideo...

It's a tossup on whether to use the most commonly supported type, whatever that may be, or the officially documented one. I'd go for the latter, though it seems it was not so widely adopted by third party clients and webservers.

Ultimately none of this really matters because the RealPlayer formats are long obsolete, and is low priority enough it could break the Earth's crust goung down :)

title: FreeBSD: process hangs on exit after a successful conversation (JSC thread-suspend signal sent but never handled)
excerpt:
## Summary

After a **successful** conversation, the OpenCode (bun `--compile`) process **hangs on exit** on FreeBSD. This is a **separate** bug from the compiled-binary freeze in #44572 (that one is the aarch64 Wasm instruction-cache publication and is fixed by the `membarrier` patch). This exit hang is architecture-independent — it reproduces on **amd64 as well as aarch64** — and it is in the WTF/JSC **thread-suspension handshake**.

## Environment

- FreeBSD 15.1-RELEASE aarch64 and FreeBSD 14.4-RELEASE amd64
- bun 1.4.2 (built from source; also with the official FreeBSD binary)
- OpenCode 2.0.22, TUI run as `opencode --standalone`

## Reproduction

Start the TUI, complete one or more turns, then exit (Ctrl-C twice). The process never exits; the main thread is parked in native code. It hangs with or without heap snapshots (SIGUSR1) — it is the exit path.

## What it is

Symbolized `lldb` capture (all threads) at the hang:

- **main**: `JSC::MachineThreads::tryCopyOtherThreadStacks` → parked (wants the thread-suspend machinery)
- **Worker**: `JSC::Heap::runTaskInParallel` → `WTF::Condition::waitUntilUnchecked` (parked)
- **VMTraps SignalSender**: `JSC::VMTraps::SignalSender::work` → `WTF::sendMessageScoped` → `WTF::Thread::suspend` → `sem_wait`

So a `VMTraps::SignalSender` is trying to stop the VM owner thread and never completes.

## Pinpointed with an instrumented build

With temporary logging in `Thread::suspend` / `Thread::resume` / `signalHandlerSuspendResume` (the handler logging via async-signal-safe `write(2)`) and `VMTraps::SignalSender::work`:

```
[VMTRAPS] suspend owner uid=13
[SUSP] enter target uid=13 cnt=0 handle=0x... name=[Worker] curUid=21 sig=30
[SUSP] killed uid=13 result=0
```

- the target is the **`Worker`** thread (the owner of the Worker VM),
- the signal number is **30 (SIGPWR)**,
- `pthread_kill` **succeeds** (`result=0`),
- but the signal handler **never runs** — `[HANDLER]` count is **0** for the whole run, and `[SUSP] woken` is never printed (the `globalSemaphoreForSuspendResume->wait()` never returns).

The Worker thread is blocked in an **interruptible** `__umtx_op_wait_uint_private` (`sleepq_wait_sig`) at the time, so the signal should be deliverable. `procstat sigfastblock` shows a `sigfastblock` pointer for every thread, so this looks like the suspend signal is **blocked or deferred** on that thread (or its disposition differs), i.e. the signal is sent but never dispatched to `signalHandlerSuspendResume`.

title: Performance drops due to Windows Defender scanning `.pile` cache files
excerpt:
For some time now, I've been noticing that a command like `bun eslint` would sometimes (every several hours) take many times longer than usually.

I managed to debug (with AI help) that this was mainly due to Windows Defender scanning Bun's runtime cache folder during imports. For example, this:

```sh
bun -e "console.time('vue'); require('eslint-plugin-vue'); console.timeEnd('vue')"
```

would normally print around 400 ms, but sometimes 10x more - and in the second case, Defender's performance recorder would show something like:

```
1442 scans
3412 ms total scan duration
```

with most of the scanned files matching `C:\Users\<user>\.bun\install\cache\@t@\*.pile`.

I fixed it with `Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "$env:USERPROFILE\.bun\install\cache\@t@"`. Another possible fix is to just disable the cache with `BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0`, although some performance (~30%) is then lost in the fastest case.

Some ideas for a possible solution in Bun:
* Document this behavior, especially how it's different than in Node.js.
* Warn users about this, like e.g. [IntelliJ products do](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61288179/windows-defender-on-pycharm).
* Disable the runtime cache by default - because if it only makes things faster by ~30% in the best case, but can degrade performance 10x in the worst case, it seems counterproductive.

node:dgram: socket.setMulticastTTL(0) throws EINVAL on Windows (Node accepts 0)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (also 1.3.13)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26100, x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// repro.mjs
import dgram from "node:dgram";
const s = dgram.createSocket("udp4");
s.bind(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
  for (const [name, fn] of [
    ["setMulticastTTL(0)", () => s.setMulticastTTL(0)],
    ["setMulticastTTL(1)", () => s.setMulticastTTL(1)],
    ["setMulticastTTL(255)", () => s.setMulticastTTL(255)],
    ["setTTL(0)", () => s.setTTL(0)],
    ["setTTL(1)", () => s.setTTL(1)],
  ]) {
    try { fn(); console.log(`${name}: ok`); }
    catch (e) { console.log(`${name}: ${e.code} ${e.message}`); }
  }
  s.close();
});
```

```
bun repro.mjs
node repro.mjs
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`setMulticastTTL(0)` succeeds. The Node docs say that for `setMulticastTTL`, "the `ttl` argument may be between 0 and 255". TTL 0 is the standard way to keep multicast on the local host.

Node v24.14.1, same machine:

```
setMulticastTTL(0): ok
setMulticastTTL(1): ok
setMulticastTTL(255): ok
setTTL(0): EINVAL setTTL EINVAL
setTTL(1): ok
```

### What do you see instead?

Bun 1.4.2:

```
setMulticastTTL(0): EINVAL setMulticastTTL EINVAL
setMulticastTTL(1): ok
setMulticastTTL(255): ok
setTTL(0): EINVAL setTTL EINVAL
setTTL(1): ok
```

Bun 1.3.13 gives the same results, with the message `EINVAL: invalid argument, setsockopt`.

### Additional information

`setTTL(0)` throwing is correct: Node does the same, and the docs give 1–255 for unicast TTL. Only `setMulticastTTL(0)` differs from Node. That suggests Bun applies the unicast range check to the multicast setter. This is a guess: I have not read Bun's source.

Impact: Unreal Engine's Python Remote Execution uses a multicast TTL of 0 by default. A Node library for that protocol calls `setMulticastTTL(0)` inside a `"listening"` handler. Under Bun the exception stops the handler before setup finishes, so the library's `start()` promise never settles. The app works under Node and hangs when compiled with `bun build --compile`.

I tested only on Windows. I do not know whether Linux or macOS are affected.

title: Bun.YAML.parse: a merged key replaces an own key when the two are different YAML types with the same property name
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

main 3f1765a6de. 1.4.3 gives the same result.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
Bun.YAML.parse('x: &x {1: a}\ny:\n  "1": z\n  <<: *x').y;        // { "1": "a" }
Bun.YAML.parse('x: &x {~: a}\ny:\n  "null": z\n  <<: *x').y;     // { null: "a" }
Bun.YAML.parse('x: &x {true: a}\ny:\n  "true": z\n  <<: *x').y;  // { true: "a" }
Bun.YAML.parse('x: &x {"1": a}\ny:\n  1: z\n  <<: *x').y;        // { "1": "a" }
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`"z"` in all four cases. A key that the mapping has itself wins over a key that `<<` merges in. js-yaml 4.3.2 and `yaml` 2.9.1 give `"z"`. Bun also gives `"z"` when both keys have the same YAML type (`k: z` and a merged `k: a`).

### What do you see instead?

The merged value replaces the own value when the two keys are different YAML nodes that become the same JS property name: the string `"1"` and the number `1`, the string `"null"` and `~`, the string `"true"` and `true`.

### Additional information

`MappingProps::merge` in `src/parsers/yaml.rs` decides if the mapping already has a key with `yaml_merge_key_expr_eql`. That function compares the YAML nodes by type, so the string `"1"` and the number `1` are not equal and the merged key is appended after the own key. Both become the property `"1"` when the mapping becomes a JS object, and the later write wins.

Found in the review of #44629, which does not change this.
