title: Windows: closing a ServerWebSocket inside open() drops the 101; clients see 1006 without open (Bun 1.4.2)
bun install zero-fills one path buffer of lockfile string space for each workspace (98 KB each on Windows)
excerpt:
### What happens

`bun install` writes zeros to one full path buffer of lockfile string space for each workspace. The bytes are reserved as slack and most of them are never used.

- `builder.cap += MAX_PATH_BYTES` runs once for each workspace in `src/install/lockfile/Package/WorkspaceMap.rs:387` and `:583`. `string_builder.cap += MAX_PATH_BYTES` runs in `src/install/lockfile/Package.rs:2467`.
- `StringBuilder::allocate` (`src/install/lockfile.rs:2700`) then calls `string_bytes.resize(prev_len + self.cap, 0)`. It writes every reserved byte, so every reserved page becomes resident.
- `MAX_PATH_BYTES` is 4,096 on Linux, 1,024 on macOS and 98,302 on Windows (`src/bun_core/util.rs:676`).

bun 1.3.14 reserved the same capacity (`ensureUnusedCapacity` and a length bump in `lockfile.zig`) and did not write it. The zero fill came with the Rust rewrite.

### Cost

| platform | reserved and zeroed for each workspace | 1,000 workspaces | 65,000 workspaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linux | 4,096 bytes | 3.9 MiB | 254 MiB |
| macOS | 1,024 bytes | 1.0 MiB | 63 MiB |
| Windows | 98,302 bytes | 93.7 MiB | 5.95 GiB |

Measured:

- Linux x64, release builds, a repo of workspaces whose package.json has only `name` and `version`, peak RSS of `bun install` for each workspace (slope from 1,000 to 3,000 workspaces): 9.2 KB with #44610, 5.8 KB on 1.3.14. The difference is 3.4 KB.
- Windows, CI build 123460 of #44610: an install of 1,000 workspaces grew the peak working set by 121 to 122 MiB (x64 and aarch64). The same install grows by 30 MiB on Linux x64. The difference is about 1,000 x 98,302 bytes. Nobody ran this on a Windows machine outside CI, so the Windows attribution is arithmetic.

### Reproduce

`bench/install/workspaces.sh` in #44610 generates the repos and prints peak RSS (Linux, GNU time):

```sh
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun KINDS=two-key SIZES="1000 3000" bench/install/workspaces.sh /abs/path/to/bun-1.3.14
```

### Possible fixes (not built)

- In `StringBuilder::allocate`, grow the buffer through a zeroed allocation and copy the live prefix. The reservation stays zero and untouched, and no caller changes.
- Or count the exact bytes that the build pass appends at the three sites, in place of `MAX_PATH_BYTES`. An under-count panics in `append` (`lockfile.rs:2725`), so the count and the append must share one helper.

title: install: three mimalloc heaps are created and destroyed for each package.json
excerpt:
### What happens

After #44610 the package manager keeps no mimalloc heap for a cached package.json, but it still creates a heap and destroys it at once in three places. Each `bun_alloc::Arena::new()` is one `mi_heap_new()`.

| place | when | what the arena is for |
|---|---|---|
| `process_workspace_name`, `src/install/lockfile/Package/WorkspaceMap.rs:177` | once for each workspace | copies of `name`, `version` and `installConfig.hoistingLimits` that are boxed again at once |
| `Package::parse_with_json_impl`, `src/install/lockfile/Package.rs:2175` | once for each package.json that becomes a lockfile package | UTF-16 transcoding that a parsed package.json never needs, and the keys of optional peers |
| `print_json`, `src/js_printer/lib.rs:7920` | once for each package.json that `bun add`, `remove` or `update` prints | the printer takes an arena and a JSON tree allocates nothing from it |

`mi_heap_new` / `mi_heap_destroy` calls (gdb breakpoints, release build of #44610, N workspaces): `bun install` 2N+5 / 2N+3, `bun update -r` 5N+10 / 5N+8. Two heaps are live at exit in both.

### Cost

Small since #44560 made heap creation cheaper. It is CPU only, peak RSS does not change.

- Linux x64, 3,000 workspaces with a two-key package.json, user plus system CPU of `bun install`, 24 interleaved rounds: 0.140 s with the two scratch heaps, 0.128 s without them. The median paired difference is 9.8 ms (95% CI 4.7 to 15.6 ms).
- With a 975-byte package.json the difference is not separable from the noise (2.9 ms, 95% CI -22 to 12 ms).

### A change that exists

Branch `robobun/709e1a2d/package-json-scratch-heaps` (commit d686e476801) removes the first two. Both functions read the strings in place with `Expr::as_utf8_string_literal()`, which is correct because every string of a parsed package.json is UTF-8. `bun.lock` is byte-identical on the fixtures of #44610 and the install suites pass on a build with ASAN. It was part of #44610 and was moved out because it does not change memory.

`print_json` has about twenty callers, among them the `Bun.serve` info handler (`src/runtime/server/server_body.rs:2700`), so it needs a caller-owned arena or a printer that takes none.

title: CSS: oklch() inside filter and backdrop-filter drop-shadow() is never lowered
CSS: gamut mapping returns at the first chroma under the JND, so sRGB fallbacks come out desaturated
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+9bd19c98e (npm `1.4.2-canary.20261005.1`)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.2.0 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```css
/* in.css */
.a { color: lab(98.2504% -7.697 88.7581) }
.b { color: color(prophoto-rgb .9784 .9925 .3037) }
.c { color: lch(94.4698% 111.9227 117.6737deg) }
```

```sh
bun build in.css --minify --outdir out
bun -e 'console.log(Bun.color("lab(98.2504% -7.697 88.7581)", "hex"))'
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The sRGB fallback follows the CSS Color 4 binary search ([§14.2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-color-4/#pseudo-binsearch)), which converges on the largest chroma whose clip is still within the 0.02 JND:

| input | expected |
|---|---|
| `lab(98.2504% -7.697 88.7581)` | `#fffc44` |
| `color(prophoto-rgb .9784 .9925 .3037)` | `#ffff6d` |
| `lch(94.4698% 111.9227 117.6737deg)` | `#b0ff00` |

These expected values are colorjs.io 0.7.1 with `method: "css"`, as reported in parcel-bundler/lightningcss#1298. I took them from that issue and didn't rerun colorjs myself.

### What do you see instead?

```css
.a{color:#fffbac;...}.b{color:#fffea7;...}.c{color:#bcff61;...}
```

`Bun.color(..., "hex")` returns the same `#fffbac`. All three come out less saturated than the spec, and all three match lightningcss 1.33.0 byte for byte.

### Additional information

`map_gamut` is a port of lightningcss's, and it kept the loop that parcel-bundler/lightningcss#1298 describes. Inside the search ([`src/css/values/color.rs:1304`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bbdc5a519e0a06d1b3133b564f91096b9ba10a31/src/css/values/color.rs#L1304)), the first chroma whose clip lands under the JND returns immediately. The spec returns there only when `JND - E < ε`; otherwise it sets `min_inGamut = false`, raises `min`, and keeps searching upward. The `min_inGamut` flag has no counterpart in bun's loop.

#33333 already fixed the other half of this function: it added the pre-loop "clip is within the JND, use it" check ([`color.rs:1281`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bbdc5a519e0a06d1b3133b564f91096b9ba10a31/src/css/values/color.rs#L1281)) that lightningcss still lacks. So on `oklch(50% .1 200)` bun prints the spec's `#00747a` where lightningcss prints `#007277`. This issue is the remaining in-loop half.

title: bun test: per-file test environment (preload and isolate selected by glob), so DOM and server tests can share one run
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

A repository with both server-side tests and DOM component tests cannot run them in one `bun test` invocation. Registering a DOM (`@happy-dom/global-registrator`, the setup Bun's own docs recommend) replaces process-wide globals: `fetch`, `URL`, `Request`, `Response`, `Headers`, `Blob`, `FormData`, timers, `window`, `document`. Server tests (route handlers, PGlite, tRPC callers, React server rendering) need Bun's real versions of those.

Jest solves this per file with the `@jest-environment` docblock or `testEnvironment` + `testMatch` projects; Vitest with `environmentMatchGlobs` / `// @vitest-environment`. `bun test` has only one process-wide `preload` list, so the environment is decided per run.

What we ended up with to work around it, in a ~100-workspace monorepo:

- a naming convention (`*.dom.test.tsx`) so each file can be assigned to a run,
- a second config file `bunfig.dom.toml` with its own `preload` (because `--preload` on the command line merges with the bunfig list rather than replacing it, the server preload would otherwise also run in every DOM file),
- `pathIgnorePatterns = ["**/*.dom.test.tsx"]` in the main config,
- a second package script per workspace: `bun --config=.../bunfig.dom.toml test --isolate .dom.test.tsx`,
- a second task in the task runner and CI.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Let a preload (and ideally `isolate`) apply to a subset of files, selected by glob, so one `bun test` run can host both environments. For example:

```toml
[test]
preload = ["./test/server-preload.ts"]

[[test.environments]]
files = ["**/*.dom.test.tsx"]
preload = ["./test/dom-preload.ts"]
isolate = true
```

or, closer to Jest, a per-file docblock (`// @bun-test-preload ./test/dom-preload.ts`) honored at file load.

Files matching an environment would load its preload instead of (or in addition to) the top-level one, in a fresh global when `isolate` is set, so the DOM registration never leaks into the server files.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- `--isolate` for every file so each file can register its own environment in a `beforeAll`: measured 6–9x slower in packages whose preload sets up PGlite.
- A second runner (Vitest browser mode, Playwright component testing) for the DOM files: rejected to stay on one runner.
- The two-run setup described above, which works but duplicates config and scripts per workspace.

Bun 1.4.2, macOS 15.

title: bunfig.toml: add `test.isolate` and a test file `include` pattern
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Two `bun test` options can only be given on the command line, so a project that needs them in a config file has to repeat them in every package script:

1. `--isolate` has no `[test]` key in `bunfig.toml`.
2. There is no key to *include* test files by pattern. `test.root` narrows to one directory and `test.pathIgnorePatterns` excludes, but selecting "only `**/*.dom.test.tsx`" is only possible with a positional filter argument.

Concretely, in a monorepo where DOM component tests run from a dedicated `bunfig.dom.toml`, every workspace's script has to be:

```json
"test:dom": "bun --config=\"$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/bunfig.dom.toml\" test --isolate .dom.test.tsx"
```

when the config file itself is the natural home for both settings.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

```toml
[test]
isolate = true
include = ["**/*.dom.test.tsx"]   # same glob syntax as pathIgnorePatterns; positional filters still narrow further
```

`include` would replace the default `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`/`_test_` discovery patterns when set, and positional arguments would keep working as an additional filter.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Expressing the include as an exclude: `pathIgnorePatterns` cannot say "every `.test.tsx` that is not `.dom.test.tsx`" without extglob negation.
- A shared shell script wrapping `bun test`: works, but moves configuration out of `bunfig.toml`, which is where `preload`, `pathIgnorePatterns` and the reporter already live.

title: `new Response(s3file)`: a static route and some copies answer a URL that S3 refuses
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1 (main at 13a98b0dbd)

### What happens

`new Response(s3file)` is a 302. Its `Location` is a presigned URL. The constructor signs that URL one time: for GET, for 15 minutes, before a request exists (`src/runtime/webcore/Response.rs:1076`). S3 checks the method and the date of a presigned URL. So these forms of a `Bun.serve` route answer a URL that S3 refuses. The script below runs each of them against an origin that checks the URL as S3 does. No user report exists for them.

| # | Form | Request | Result after the redirect | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A handler returns `new Response(s3file)`, `response.clone()` or `new Response(null, response)` | HEAD | 403 `SignatureDoesNotMatch` | #44645 |
| 2 | A static route, `routes: { "/f": new Response(s3file) }` | HEAD | 403 `SignatureDoesNotMatch` | needs a decision |
| 3 | The same static route, later than 15 minutes after `Bun.serve()` | GET | 403 `Request has expired` | needs a decision |
| 4 | A handler returns `kept.clone()` of one Response, later than 15 minutes after `new Response()` | GET | 403 `Request has expired` | open |
| 5 | A handler returns a Response that code built again from `response.status` and `response.headers` | HEAD | 403 `SignatureDoesNotMatch` | open |

Two more defects of the same constructor have their own numbers: #43930 (a slice redirects to the whole object) and #44311 (the URL has no `x-amz-request-payer`).

Linux 7.0.0-31-generic x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On a case-sensitive file system (reproduced on tmpfs and ZFS), a directory holding two files whose names differ only in case and extension — `fooBar.ts` and `FooBar.tsx` — makes an extensionless import of one resolve to the other.

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
printf 'export const value = "from fooBar.ts";\n' > fooBar.ts
printf 'import { value } from "./fooBar";\nexport const shown = value;\n' > FooBar.tsx
printf 'import { shown } from "./FooBar";\nconsole.log(shown);\n' > main.ts
bun main.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

```
from fooBar.ts
```

`./fooBar` names `fooBar.ts`, the only file whose name is `fooBar` plus an extension. `tsc` resolves it that way.

### What do you see instead?

```
SyntaxError: Export named 'value' not found in module '/…/repro/FooBar.tsx'.
```

`./fooBar` resolved to `FooBar.tsx`, the importing file itself.

Importing `./fooBar` directly from another file fails differently, as though the name was matched case-insensitively and then read with the requested case:

```sh
printf 'import { value } from "./fooBar";\nconsole.log(value);\n' > m2.ts
bun m2.ts
# error: ENOENT reading "/…/repro/fooBar.tsx"
```

### Additional information

- With both files `.ts` (`fooBar.ts` and `FooBar.ts`), `./fooBar` imported from `FooBar.ts` resolves to `FooBar.ts` the same way.
- Writing the extension (`import { value } from "./fooBar.ts"`) works.
- Workaround: give the two files names that differ by more than case.

title: bun check: "A is not assignable to A" for a contextually typed generic arrow that returns Promise#then inside a generic call (tsc 7 accepts)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+bbdc5a519

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.4.0 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No dependencies.

`repro.ts`:

```ts
interface Box<A, R> { readonly a: A; readonly r: R }

declare function run<A, R>(box: Box<A, R>): Promise<A[]>

declare function make<R>(
  runner: <A>(box: Box<A, R>) => Promise<A[]>,
  tag: R,
): void

make((box) => Promise.resolve(0).then(() => run(box)), "tag")
```

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": { "strict": true, "target": "ES2022", "lib": ["ES2022"], "noEmit": true, "types": [] },
  "files": ["repro.ts"]
}
```

Run `bun check`.

### What is the expected behavior?

No errors. `tsc` 5.7.3 and `tsgo` 7.0.0-dev.20260707.2 both accept the file.

### What do you see instead?

```
repro.ts(10,15): error TS2322: Type 'Promise<A[] | A[]>' is not assignable to type 'Promise<A[]>'.
  Type 'A[] | A[]' is not assignable to type 'A[]'.
    Type 'A[]' is not assignable to type 'A[]'. Two different types with this name exist, but they are unrelated.
      Type 'A' is not assignable to type 'A'. Two different types with this name exist, but they are unrelated.
        'A' could be instantiated with an arbitrary type which could be unrelated to 'A'.
Found 1 error in 1 file
```

### Additional information

The error needs all three parts:

| Change | `bun check` |
|---|---|
| As above | error |
| `make` is not generic (`R` replaced by `"tag"`) | no error |
| No `.then`: `make((box) => run(box), "tag")` | no error |
| A user-defined generic `map` method in place of `Promise#then` | no error |

It looks like the arrow function's type parameter `A`, which comes from the contextual signature `<A>(box: Box<A, R>) => ...` after `R` is inferred, is not the same `A` that `run(box)` infers inside the `.then` callback. The result is a union of two different `A[]` types.

Real-world case: an object literal `{ runPromiseExit: (program) => ctx().then(() => runtime.runPromiseExit(program)) }` passed to a generic function whose parameter type is `{ runPromiseExit: <A, E>(program: Effect<A, E, R>) => Promise<Exit<A, E>> }` (`effect@4.0.0`). `bun check` reports `Type 'Failure<A, E>' is not assignable to type 'Failure<A, E>'`.

In a 3,691-file project, this is the only difference between `bun check` and `tsgo` 7: the other 32 errors are the same in both.

`bun prune` and `bun update` remove packages behind a workspace `node_modules` that is a symlink
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 and main (1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9). `src/install/prune.rs` is the same in both.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```sh
mkdir -p repro/packages/w && cd repro
printf '[install]\nlinker = "hoisted"\n' > bunfig.toml
echo '{"name":"root","workspaces":["packages/*"],"dependencies":{"is-number":"7.0.0"}}' > package.json
echo '{"name":"w","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"is-odd":"3.0.1"}}' > packages/w/package.json
bun install
ln -s ../../node_modules packages/w/node_modules
bun update   # or: bun prune
ls node_modules
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The root `node_modules` still holds `is-number`, `is-odd` and `w`.

### What do you see instead?

Only `w` is left. `bun update` prints `(no changes)`. `bun prune` prints `- is-number@7.0.0 (packages/w/node_modules)`. Both exit 0.

The same happens in these cases:

- With the isolated linker, `bun prune` removes the root's link to its own dependency through the linked workspace folder.
- When the link leads to a folder that is not part of the project, `bun prune` removes the directories in that folder, with both linkers.
- `bun dedupe` and `bun audit fix` run the same pass as `bun update` with the hoisted linker.

### Additional information

`bun prune` and the pass after a hoisted `bun update` (`remove_collapsed_copies` in `src/install/prune.rs`) open each workspace's `node_modules` with `Dir::open`, which follows a link. The entries behind the link then look like leftovers of the workspace: the root provides each of them, so they are removed as copies that hide the root's.

#44484 makes both refuse a workspace `node_modules` that is a symlink and print a warning.

title: hoisted: `bun prune` and `bun update` remove packages `bun.lock` places when a self-contained workspace depends on a sibling
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

main (1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9). `src/install/prune.rs` is the same in 1.4.2.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`c` is a self-contained workspace and depends on its sibling `b`.

```sh
mkdir -p repro/packages/b repro/packages/c && cd repro
printf '[install]\nlinker = "hoisted"\n' > bunfig.toml
echo '{"name":"root","workspaces":{"packages":["packages/*"],"selfContained":["packages/c"]},"dependencies":{"is-number":"7.0.0"}}' > package.json
echo '{"name":"b","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"is-number":"6.0.0","ms":"2.0.0"}}' > packages/b/package.json
echo '{"name":"c","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"b":"workspace:*","is-number":"6.0.0","ms":"2.1.3"}}' > packages/c/package.json
bun install
ls packages/b/node_modules   # is-number (6.0.0) and ms (2.0.0)
bun prune
ls packages/b/node_modules
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun prune` prints `(nothing to prune)`. The install was clean, and `bun.lock` places both packages in `packages/b/node_modules`.

### What do you see instead?

```
- is-number@6.0.0 (node_modules/c/node_modules/b/node_modules)
- ms@2.0.0 (node_modules/b/node_modules)
2 packages removed (checked 11 installed packages)
```

`packages/b/node_modules` is empty and the exit code is 0. `b` then loads `is-number@7.0.0` from the root.

`bun update` has the same fault. After `bun install` puts the two packages back, `bun update` prints `(no changes)` and `packages/b/node_modules/ms` is gone.

### Additional information

`b` has two trees in the lockfile: one below the root (for `is-number@6.0.0`, which the root does not provide) and one below `c` (for `ms@2.0.0`, which cannot hoist into `c`'s folder). The installer writes both trees into `packages/b/node_modules`.

`src/install/prune.rs` keys a folder by its tree path. `plan_hoisted` visits `packages/b/node_modules` once per tree with the rows of that tree only, so the rows of the other tree look like leftovers. The pass after `bun update` (`plan_and_remove_collapsed_copies`) reads only the tree at `node_modules/b/node_modules` for that folder.

title: `bun prune` follows a root `node_modules` or `node_modules/.bun` that is a symlink
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

main (1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9). `src/install/prune.rs` is the same in 1.4.2.

### What is the problem?

`bun prune` opens the root `node_modules` and `node_modules/.bun` with `Dir::open`, which follows a symlink. What is behind the link is pruned as if it were the project's own folder. #44484 adds a guard for a workspace's `node_modules` only. This issue is for the cases it leaves open, so that one rule can be chosen for `bun install` and `bun prune` (#42039 changes what the installer does with such links).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A root `node_modules` that is a link to a folder with other content:

```sh
mkdir -p proj shared/first shared/second && cd proj
printf '[install]\nlinker = "hoisted"\n' > bunfig.toml
echo '{"name":"root","dependencies":{"is-number":"7.0.0"}}' > package.json
ln -s ../shared node_modules
bun install
bun prune
ls ../shared   # only is-number is left
```

`bun prune` prints `- first`, `- second`, `2 packages removed` and exits 0.

The same with the isolated linker and `node_modules/.bun` as a link to a folder that holds other entries: `bun prune` removes every entry there that is not a store entry of this project.

A root `node_modules` that is a link into a workspace's real `node_modules` (`node_modules -> packages/a/node_modules`), hoisted linker: `bun prune` scans that directory once as the root's folder and once as the workspace's folder, and removes the root's packages as leftovers of the workspace.

### What is the expected behavior?

One documented rule. The options seen so far: follow the link (today), refuse it and warn (what #44484 does for a workspace folder), or replace the link with a folder (what #42039 does in the installer). For the case of one directory under two paths, a check of the directory identity (device and inode) before anything is removed.

title: hoisted: the pass that removes nested copies after `bun update` runs before a failed run exits and reports nothing
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

main (1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9). The code is the same in 1.4.2.

### What is the problem?

With the hoisted linker, `bun update`, `bun dedupe` and `bun audit fix` run a pass that removes nested and workspace copies that a folder above now provides (`remove_collapsed_copies` in `src/install/prune.rs`, called from `src/install/PackageManager/install_with_manager.rs`). Two things are wrong with when it runs and what it reports.

1. The pass runs before the run is known to succeed. It is called inside the linker arm, above the exit for a run that logged errors (`Global::crash()`) and above the save of `bun.lock`. A `bun update` that resolves a new tree, removes the copies that tree no longer places, and then fails (a tarball that returns 404) exits 1 with the old `bun.lock` on disk. That `bun.lock` still places the copies the pass removed.
2. The pass reports nothing. `plan_and_remove_collapsed_copies` calls `execute(&plan, true)` and drops its result. A run that removed copies prints `(no changes)`. When a removal fails, `execute` prints `error: failed to remove ...` and the count it returns is not used, so the exit code does not change. `bun prune` uses the same count to exit 1.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

For 1: a root that depends on `baz@0.0.5`, a workspace `pkg-a` that depends on `baz@0.0.3` (so `packages/pkg-a/node_modules/baz` exists), then `pkg-a` changes its range to `~0.0.3` and the root adds a dependency whose tarball returns 404. `bun update` exits 1 and `packages/pkg-a/node_modules/baz` is gone, while `bun.lock` is unchanged. The branch of #44406 has this as a test: `test/cli/install/bun-update.test.ts`, "keeps the nested copy whose row it collapsed when the run fails". It fails on main.

For 2: the repro of #44670 ends with a `bun update` that removes a package and prints `(no changes)`.

### What is the expected behavior?

The pass runs after the run is known to succeed and `bun.lock` is saved. The summary counts what the pass removed, and a failed removal makes the command exit 1.

title: Bun shell mv: a cross-device move that fails midway leaves the tree split between source and destination
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1 (main at bbdc5a519e). The copy path is the same since 1.4.0.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64. The copy path is shared by all platforms.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The Bun shell `mv` builtin calls `renameat`. When `renameat` returns `EXDEV`, `move_across_devices` in `src/runtime/shell/builtin/mv.rs` copies the source tree. It removes each source entry directly after the copy of that entry. When a later entry fails, the entries done so far are at the destination and the others are still at the source.

Any failure in the middle of the tree shows it. A FIFO is the shortest one, because the copy refuses it. `/tmp` and `/dev/shm` must be two file systems:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/mvtree && for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do echo $i > /tmp/mvtree/f$i; done && mkfifo /tmp/mvtree/pipe
bun -e 'import {$} from "bun"; $.nothrow(); const r = await $`mv /tmp/mvtree /dev/shm/`; console.log("exit", r.exitCode)'
echo "source:      $(ls /tmp/mvtree | tr '\n' ' ')"
echo "destination: $(ls /dev/shm/mvtree | tr '\n' ' ')"
```

A destination that runs out of space does the same. This one needs a mount, so run it as `unshare -Urm sh split.sh`:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/split/src/tree /tmp/split/dst
mount -t tmpfs -o size=12k tmpfs /tmp/split/dst
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do head -c 4096 /dev/zero > /tmp/split/src/tree/f$i; done
cd /tmp/split
bun -e 'import {$} from "bun"; $.nothrow(); const r = await $`mv src/tree dst/`; console.log("exit", r.exitCode)'
echo "source:      $(ls src/tree | tr '\n' ' ')"
echo "destination: $(ls dst/tree | tr '\n' ' ')"
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The source stays complete when the move fails. POSIX `mv` duplicates the whole hierarchy first, and removes the source hierarchy only after the duplication finished. GNU coreutils 9.7 on the second script:

```
mv: error writing 'dst/tree/f8': No space left on device
source:      f1 f2 f3 f4 f5 f6 f7 f8
```

### What do you see instead?

The first script (the order of the directory listing decides which files move before the failure):

```
mv: /dev/shm/mvtree: Operation not supported
exit 95
source:      pipe
destination: f1 f2 f3 f4 f5 f6 f7 f8
```

The second script:

```
mv: dst/tree: No space left on device
exit 28
source:      f1 f4 f5 f6 f8
destination: f2 f3 f7
```

No byte is lost, because an entry is removed only after its own copy. But the tree is split between two places, and a second `mv` cannot continue from that s

title: bun check: NodeJS.BuiltinIteratorReturn evaluates to unknown when @types/bun is loaded (false TS2322 on URL; tsc 7 accepts)
excerpt:
`bun check` reports false TS2322 errors when `@types/bun` is loaded next to `@types/node`: `NodeJS.BuiltinIteratorReturn` evaluates to `unknown` instead of `undefined`, so `import("url").URL` is no longer assignable to the global `URL`. tsc 5.7.3 and tsc 7.0.2 report no errors on the same input.

## Versions

- Bun: 1.4.3-canary.1+bd599f5af (newest canary on 2026-10-07; also 1.4.3-canary.1+bbdc5a519), macOS 26 arm64
- Reference: `typescript@5.7.3` (tsc) and `typescript@7.0.2` (tsc, native): 0 errors
- Packages: `@types/node@22.19.19`, `@types/bun@1.3.14`

## Repro — `NodeJS.BuiltinIteratorReturn` evaluates wrong when @types/bun is loaded

`package.json` devDependencies: `@types/node@22.19.19`, `@types/bun@1.3.14`.

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{ "compilerOptions": { "strict": true, "noEmit": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "target": "ES6", "lib": ["dom", "dom.iterable", "esnext"], "module": "esnext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "types": ["node", "bun"] }, "files": ["a.ts"] }
```

`a.ts`:

```ts
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"

// Under strict, the @types/node polyfill evaluates to the intrinsic BuiltinIteratorReturn = undefined.
export const probe: [NodeJS.BuiltinIteratorReturn] extends [undefined] ? true : false = true

// Fails only because the line above evaluates differently.
export const url: URL = pathToFileURL("/tmp/x")
```

`NodeJS.BuiltinIteratorReturn` comes from `@types/node/compatibility/iterators.d.ts`:

```ts
type BuiltinIteratorReturn = ReturnType<any[][typeof Symbol.iterator]> extends
    globalThis.Iterator<any, infer TReturn> ? TReturn : any;
```

Expected (tsc 5.7.3, tsc 7.0.2): no errors.

Actual (`bun check --no-pretty`):

```
a.ts(4,14): error TS2322: Type 'true' is not assignable to type 'false'.
a.ts(7,14): error TS2322: Type 'import("url").URL' is not assignable to type 'URL'.
  The types of 'searchParams[Symbol.iterator]().next(...)' are incompatible between these types.
    Type 'IteratorResult<[string, string], unknown>' is not assignable to type 'IteratorResult<[string, string], undefined>'.
      ...
          Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'undefined'.
```

Notes: with `"types": ["node"]` only, `bun check` agrees with tsc. A `/// <reference path>` to any one of `bun-types/{fetch,extensions,ffi,overrides,bun.ns}.d.ts` is enough to flip the probe; `globals.d.ts`, `bun.d.ts`, `test.d.ts` and others alone do not. The result is the same with `--threads=1`. It is deterministic.


## Impact

On a real Effect v4 + Bun

title: node:dns resolveTxt returns each character string of a TXT record as a separate record
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.18.48 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A DNS TXT record can consist of several character strings (RFC 1035, section 3.3.14). `node:dns` returns each record as an array of its character strings, so `resolveTxt` resolves to `string[][]` with one inner array per record. Bun instead returns each character string as its own record, so a single multi-string record looks like several records.

```js
import dns from "node:dns"

// s1._domainkey.github.com has one TXT record made of two character strings.
const records = await dns.promises.resolveTxt("s1._domainkey.github.com")
console.log(records.length, records.map((chunks) => chunks.length))
```

The same happens with `dns.promises.Resolver#resolveTxt`, `resolve(name, "TXT")`, and against a local name server serving `example.test. IN TXT "v=spf1 " "-all"`.

### What is the expected behavior?

One record with two chunks, as in Node.js (v26.8.1):

```
1 [ 2 ]
```

For the local record: `[["v=spf1 ","-all"]]`.

### What do you see instead?

Two records with one chunk each:

```
2 [ 1, 1 ]
```

For the local record: `[["v=spf1 "],["-all"]]`.

### Additional information

Splitting the chunks loses information: callers can no longer tell which strings belong to the same record, so long values such as DKIM keys or SPF policies that span several strings cannot be reassembled correctly when a name has more than one TXT record.

title: Windows: Bun switches the console code page to 65001 at startup, which garbles output and breaks other processes in the same console (root cause of #43660)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 (also reproduced on 1.4.3-canary.1+bbdc5a519)

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

At startup Bun saves the console's input/output code pages and sets both to 65001; at exit it restores the saved values ([`init()`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/3f1765a6de030d00a98c33ff0c776c7a7e4b23e9/src/bun_core/output.rs#L561-L567), [`restore()`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/3f1765a6de030d00a98c33ff0c776c7a7e4b23e9/src/bun_core/output.rs#L517-L524)). The code page belongs to the console and is shared by every process attached to it, so two Bun processes in one console overwrite each other's saved value. This is the root cause of #43660.

Open a **new `cmd.exe` window** (any code page other than 65001; 437 on English Windows, 932 on Japanese Windows) and run:

```bat
bun -e "console.log('abc \u6771\u4eac\u5927\u962a xyz'); setTimeout(() => {}, 2000)" | (ping -n 2 127.0.0.1 >nul & bun -e "let d = ''; process.stdin.on('data', c => d += c); process.stdin.on('end', () => setTimeout(() => process.stdout.write(d), 800))")
chcp
```

The `ping` and the timers only fix the order: the writer starts first, the reader starts about 1 s later, and the writer exits while the reader is still running. This reproduced every time (3 out of 3 at code page 437, 3 out of 3 at 932, on both builds).

### What is the expected behavior?

The text is printed correctly and the console keeps its code page. This is what Node.js prints when both `bun -e` are replaced with `node -e`, and Deno prints the same with `deno eval`:

```
abc 東京大阪 xyz
Active code page: 437
```

### What do you see instead?

At code page 437:

```
abc µ¥▒Σ║¼σñºΘÿ¬ xyz
Active code page: 65001
```

At code page 932 (Japanese Windows):

```
abc 譚ｱ莠ｬ螟ｧ髦ｪ xyz
Active code page: 65001
```

What happens:

1. The writer starts, saves 437 and sets 65001
2. The reader starts and saves 65001 as its "original" value
3. The writer exits and restores 437
4. The reader writes raw UTF-8 bytes to a console that is now at 437, so they are garbled
5. The reader exits and restores 65001, which stays on the console after both are gone

### Additional information

**Request: please don't change the console code page at all.** Write console output with `WriteConsoleW` (UTF-8 → UTF-16), write bytes unchanged to pipes and files, and read console input with `ReadConsoleW`. None of these depend on the code page.

title: Reading RegExp.lastMatch or RegExp.$1 after a long search segfaults at address 0x4
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84 and 1.4.3-canary.1+367d939d9, Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const re = new RegExp("^" + "(z)?".repeat(8) + "(?:[ab]{0,699}?(?:a|b)+c|(?:a|b)+$)");
console.log(re.test(Buffer.alloc(100000, "a").toString())); // true, after about 0.5 s
console.log(RegExp.lastMatch.length);
```

A faster one, with a small backtracking pool:

```sh
BUN_JSC_maxRegExpStackSize=65536 bun -e '
  const re = new RegExp("^" + "(z)?".repeat(8) + "(?:a|b)+$");
  console.log(re.test(Buffer.alloc(100000, "a").toString()));
  console.log(RegExp.lastMatch.length);'
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`true`, then `100000`. Node v26.3.0 prints that. An error is also acceptable. A crash is not.

### What do you see instead?

```
true
panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x4
```

The same happens for `RegExp.$1` to `RegExp.$9`, `RegExp["$&"]` and `RegExp.lastParen`.

### Additional information

- `RegExp.lastMatch` does not keep the match. `RegExpCachedResult::lastResult` runs the last search again to build the array that the legacy statics read.
- The two runs are not the same. `test()` runs match-only code. The second run keeps the subpatterns. In JIT code that makes each context of a repeating group 8 bytes larger for each subpattern, and the contexts are on the machine stack. A search that fits the first time can need the interpreter the second time, and the interpreter can run out of its step limit or of its pool.
- The engine reports that as "no match". `createRegExpMatchesArray` then returns no array and no exception, `lastResult` stores it, and `RegExpGlobalData::getBackref` (`RegExpGlobalData.cpp:50`) reads `array->length()` through a null pointer.
- oven-sh/WebKit#343 has the fix: the second run throws a `RangeError`, and `lastResult` throws when that run has no match for any other reason.

title: Runtime plugin onLoad: CommonJS contents are never executed (module comes back empty)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (744846f84)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.8-200.fc44.x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A runtime plugin's `onLoad` returns `{ contents, loader: 'js' }`. If `contents` is ESM, it runs. If it is CommonJS (`module.exports = …`, no ESM syntax), the callback is called but the contents are never executed, and the importer gets an empty module — with `require` and with `import` alike.

`a.foo`:
```js
console.log('original file ran')
```

`p.ts` (preload):
```ts
import { plugin } from 'bun'
plugin({
  name: 'r',
  setup(b) {
    b.onLoad({ filter: /[\\/]a\.foo$/ }, () => ({
      contents: "console.log('contents ran'); module.exports = 42",
      loader: 'js',
    }))
  },
})
```

`e.cjs`:
```js
const m = require('./a.foo')
console.log('got', m)
```

`e.mjs`:
```js
const m = await import('./a.foo')
console.log('got', m.default)
```

```sh
bun --preload ./p.ts e.cjs
bun --preload ./p.ts e.mjs
```

Swapping the contents for `console.log('contents ran'); export default 42` is the only change between the rows below:

| contents | `import` | `require` |
|---|---|---|
| ESM (`export default 42`) | `contents ran` / `got 42` | `contents ran` / `got Module { default: 42 }` |
| CJS (`module.exports = 42`) | `got undefined` | `got Module {}` |

The same happens for a `.js` file, for an `async` `onLoad`, and with the plugin registered through `Bun.plugin` in the entry rather than a preload.

### What is the expected behavior?

`contents ran`, then `got 42`, for both entry points — the same as `require('./disk.js')` gives when `disk.js` holds that source and no plugin is involved (verified: `contents ran`, `got 42`).

### What do you see instead?

The `onLoad` callback runs, but nothing in `contents` executes and the module is empty.

### Additional information

This blocks the workaround suggested in #4754 for `vue-tsc`. It patches TypeScript by swapping `fs.readFileSync` around `require(tscPath)`, which Bun's module loader does not read through, so under Bun every `.vue` file goes unchecked and the run still exits 0. A loader that returns the patched `typescript/lib/tsc.js` source would fix that, but that source is CommonJS, so it is dropped in exactly this way: `onLoad` is called with the patched 6.2 MB source and its first line never runs.

bun build --compile: a require whose path is computed from __dirname keeps the build machine's absolute path instead of embedding the file
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (latest release)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin arm64. We first hit it with a binary cross-compiled with `--target bun-linux-x64` and run in `debian:bookworm-slim`, where the build path does not exist.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A package that loads its own `package.json` by a computed path:

```js
// node_modules/fakepkg/lib/index.js
const path = require("path");
const packageRoot = path.join(__dirname, "..");
module.exports = require(path.join(packageRoot, "package.json"));
```

```js
// main.js
console.log("version", require("fakepkg").version);
```

```sh
bun build --compile main.js --outfile app
./app                     # version 1.0.0
mv node_modules node_modules.hidden
./app                     # fails
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`app` prints `version 1.0.0` without `node_modules`, because the file is part of the build input. Failing that, the build should report that it left a file outside the binary.

### What do you see instead?

```
error: Cannot find module '<build directory>/node_modules/fakepkg/package.json' from '/$bunfs/root/app'
```

The build resolves `__dirname` to the build machine's absolute directory, which is why the full path appears in the error. It then keeps a runtime `require` of that path instead of embedding the file. The binary works only where it was built, so a check on the build machine passes while the same binary fails in a container.

### Additional information

Rewriting the call as `require("../package.json")` makes the binary print `version 1.0.0` without `node_modules`. The resolved path is known at build time in both cases.

We hit this with `playwright-core` 1.63.0, which reads `package.json` and `browsers.json` this way in four places (microsoft/playwright#43140). Its maintainer considers it something for Bun to support. We patch those four `require` calls into literal specifiers today.

bun-types: global `Blob` and `File` declare no `slice()` without lib.dom
excerpt:
With `@types/bun` 1.4.2 and no `DOM` lib, the global `Blob` interface in `bun-types/globals.d.ts` declares `size`, `type`, `json`, `image`, `formData`, `text`, `arrayBuffer`, `bytes` and `stream`, but no `slice`. `File extends Blob`, so it has none either. The runtime has it: `new File(["abcdef"], "a").slice(0, 2).text()` resolves to `"ab"` on Bun 1.4.2.

Reproduction, with TypeScript 7.0.2:

```ts
// repro.ts
declare const file: File;
export const start = file.slice(0, 4);
export const blob = new Blob(["a"]).slice(0, 1);
```

```sh
tsc --noEmit --strict --lib esnext --types bun --module esnext --moduleResolution bundler repro.ts
```

repro.ts(2,27): error TS2339: Property 'slice' does not exist on type 'File'.
repro.ts(3,37): error TS2339: Property 'slice' does not exist on type 'Blob'.
```

Expected: `slice(start?: number, end?: number, contentType?: string): Blob`, as lib.dom and `@types/node`'s `buffer.Blob` declare it.

`bun-types@1.4.3-canary.20261007T141441` still declares no `slice` on `Blob`.

title: bun check: false TS18046 when an array literal combines values of a named union (tsc 7 accepts)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+bd599f5af

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`src/repro.ts`:

```ts
type Base = { name: string };
type WithState = { name: string; state: { id: string } };
type Item = Base | WithState;

export function ids(a: Item, b: Item) {
  return [a, b].map((item) => ("state" in item ? item.state.id : null));
}
```

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true, "noEmit": true, "target": "ES2022", "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler", "skipLibCheck": true, "types": []
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*.ts"]
}
```

Run `bun check` in that directory.

### What is the expected behavior?

No errors. With TypeScript 7.0.2, `tsc -p tsconfig.json` prints nothing and exits 0. TypeScript 6.0.3 does the same.

### What do you see instead?

```
src/repro.ts(6,50): error TS18046: 'item.state' is of type 'unknown'.
Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 1 file [17.62ms]
```

`bun check` exits 1.

### Additional information

The element type of `[a, b]` loses `WithState`. With `const list = [a, b]` and `type HasState<T> = T extends WithState ? 1 : 0`, tsc accepts `const check: HasState<(typeof list)[number]> = 1`, while bun check reports `Type '1' is not assignable to type '0'`.

It only happens with a named union. If the parameters are written as `a: Base | WithState, b: Base | WithState`, tsc reports the same TS18046, because `WithState` is a subtype of `Base` and subtype reduction leaves only `Base`. With `type Item`, tsc returns `Item` unchanged. That looks like the named-union shortcut in typescript-go's `getUnionTypeWorker` ([checker.go#L25829-L25839](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go/blob/89d5d5b2849a0db0957065889ca58536fa6d2e4a/internal/checker/checker.go#L25829-L25839)): when every member left after reduction belongs to a single named union, it returns that union.

Each case below was checked as its own project with the tsconfig above (`a, b: Item`; `xs, ys: Item[]`):

| Code | bun check | tsc 7.0.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[a, b]` | TS18046 | no errors |
| `[...xs, ...ys]` | TS18046 | no errors |
| `[...xs, b]` | TS18046 | no errors |
| `for (const item of [a, b])` | TS18046 | no errors |
| `type Item = Base \| (Base & { state: { id: string } })` | TS18046 | no errors |
| `a, b: Base \| WithState` (no alias) | TS18046 | TS18046 |
| `[a]` | no errors | no errors |
| `const list: Item[] = [a, b]` | no errors | no error

title: A lowered top-level `using` drops `export default` function and class declarations
excerpt:
### What happens

A module with a top-level `using` loses its default export when the default export is a function declaration or a class declaration. This happens where `using` is lowered: every target except `bun`. `export default <expression>` keeps the export.

Found by a review of the `export default` arm of the parser. I know of no user report.

```js
// mod.js
function dec(value, ctx) {}
using resource = { [Symbol.dispose]() {} };
export default class Df {}
export const other = 1;
```

`bun build --target=node` on Bun 1.4.2 and on `main` (bd599f5af9), with three importers of `mod.js`:

| Default export in `mod.js` | `import Df from "./mod.js"` | `import * as ns from "./mod.js"` | `mod.js` as the entry point |
|---|---|---|---|
| `export default class Df {}` | `error: No matching export in "mod.js" for import "default"` | builds. `default` is not in `ns` | builds. The module has no `default` export |
| `export default function f() {}` | the same error | `default` is not in `ns` | no `default` export |
| `export default function () {}` | the same error | `default` is not in `ns` | no `default` export |
| `@dec export default class Df {}` | the same error | builds. The bundle throws `ReferenceError: Df is not defined` | builds. The module throws `ReferenceError: Df is not defined` |
| `export default (class Df {})` | builds and runs | `default,other` | `default,other` |

`new Bun.Transpiler({ loader: "js", target: "node" }).transformSync(source)` prints the module with no default export for the first four rows.

### Where

- `s_export_default` (`src/js_parser/visit/visit_stmt.rs`) rewrites only the expression form to a `var` plus an export clause when the module is wrapped for `using`.
- `LowerUsingDeclarationsContext::finalize` (`src/js_parser/p.rs`) then drops every `S::ExportDefault` statement.
- For a class with decorators, the statements that decorator lowering puts after the class (`Df = _Df`, `__runInitializers(...)`) stay in the `try` block. They refer to a class that is gone.

#38287 fixes the function arm and the class arm.

title: The generated `<file>_default` binding of an anonymous default export has no collision guard without a bundle
excerpt:
### What happens

For an anonymous default export the parser makes a symbol with the name `<file>_default`. Some lowerings print that symbol as a binding of the module. Without a bundle no renamer runs, so the name is printed as it is. A module that uses the same name then fails to load, or reads the wrong value.

Found by a review of the `export default` arm of the parser. I know of no user report.

```js
// fn.js
const fn_default = 1;
export default function () {}
console.log(fn_default);
```

`bun fn.js` on Bun 1.4.2 and on `main` (bd599f5af9) prints `SyntaxError: Cannot declare a const variable twice: 'fn_default'.` Node prints `1`.

Each row is a module `x.js` that holds the two statements:

| User binding | Default export | Result on `main` |
|---|---|---|
| `const x_default = 1` | `export default function () {}` | `SyntaxError: Cannot declare a const variable twice: 'x_default'.` |
| `var x_default = 1` | `export default function () {}` | `SyntaxError: Cannot declare a var variable that shadows a let/const/class variable: 'x_default'.` |
| `const x_default = 1` | `@dec export default class {}` | `SyntaxError: Cannot declare a class twice: 'x_default'.` |
| `const x_default = 1` | `export default class { @dec m() {} }` | `SyntaxError: Cannot declare a class twice: 'x_default'.` |
| `var x_default = 1` | `@dec export default class {}` | loads. `typeof x_default` is `"function"` |
| `globalThis.x_default = 1` | `@dec export default class {}` | loads. A free `x_default` reads the class |
| `const x_default = 1` | `export default class {}` | runs |

Node runs the two function rows. The output of tsc 6.0.2 and of esbuild 0.21.5 runs the first class row (esbuild always renames).

### Where

- `create_default_name` (`src/js_parser/p.rs`) builds `<file>_default` with `new_symbol` and no suffix.
- `s_export_default` (`src/js_parser/visit/visit_stmt.rs`) makes that symbol the name of an anonymous default function. It also makes it the name of an anonymous default class that decorator lowering must assign to.
- `NoOpRenamer` (`src/js_printer/renamer.rs`) prints `original_name` as it is. The other generated names on this path have a guard: `generate_temp_var` prints `name$N`.

#34932 removes the function row by keeping the function anonymous. A decorated anonymous class needs a binding, so it needs a name that cannot collide.

title: Inspector precise coverage marks an unexecuted nullish-coalescing RHS as covered
excerpt:
Bun: 1.4.2+744846f84. OS: Linux ARM64. Comparison: Node v24.18.0.

This reproduces with the built-in inspector API, without Vitest or dependencies.

`fallback.mjs`:

```js
export function fallback(value, missing) {
  return value ?? missing()
}
```

`inspect.mjs`:

```js
import inspector from 'node:inspector/promises'
import { fallback } from './fallback.mjs'
const session = new inspector.Session()
session.connect()
await session.post('Profiler.enable')
await session.post('Profiler.startPreciseCoverage', { callCount: true, detailed: true })
let fallbackCalls = 0
const result = fallback('present', () => { fallbackCalls++; return 'fallback' })
const { result: coverage } = await session.post('Profiler.takePreciseCoverage')
console.log(JSON.stringify({result, fallbackCalls, coverage: coverage.filter(entry => entry.url.endsWith('/fallback.mjs'))}, null, 2))
await session.post('Profiler.stopPreciseCoverage')
session.disconnect()
```

Run `node inspect.mjs`, then `bun inspect.mjs`.

Both return `present` and `fallbackCalls: 0`, proving the RHS is skipped. Node reports an uncovered subrange (offsets 58–70, count 0). Bun does not report that subrange; its encompassing range (24–70) has count 1. Bun does report a zero-count range at 71–72, which is outside the skipped expression.

Expected: detailed coverage should distinguish the skipped RHS from the executed LHS, without requiring exact offset parity with Node.

Actual: a consumer of this output treats the skipped RHS as executed. With Vitest 5.0.3 and @vitest/coverage-v8 5.0.3, a test that asserts the fallback mock was never called reports branch coverage 50% on Node versus 100% on Bun. The same problem inflated our application's branch coverage from 587/634 to 592/634 without added test execution.

The direct inspector reproduction above needs no install. It isolates the discrepancy before any Vitest coverage conversion.

Node reports `fallback` ranges `[{startOffset:7,endOffset:72,count:1},{startOffset:58,endOffset:70,count:0}]`. Bun reports ranges `[{startOffset:0,endOffset:74,count:1},{startOffset:24,endOffset:70,count:1},{startOffset:71,endOffset:72,count:0}]`, with an empty function name. All ranges have `isBlockCoverage: true`.

Impact: coverage gates can pass despite untested short-circuit branches. Test execution and assertions themselves behave correctly in this reproduction.

title: Bun.plugin: registering onResolve with a namespace from several Workers at once crashes the process
`--setenv` / `--setenv-force`: set env vars from flags, so compiled binaries can carry them
excerpt:
## The problem

Much of Bun's behavior is configured only through environment variables, read
from somewhere deep inside the runtime. For a compiled binary there is no
supported way to set any of them: whatever the binary needs, the user's
environment has to supply.

The case that hit us: a compiled binary uses a `Bun.plugin` `onResolve` hook to
map `#token/...` imports to a directory taken from an env var. The runtime
transpiler caches its output keyed by file contents, so an identical file in a
second git worktree got the cached output of the first one, with the first
tree's resolved paths baked in. The fix on our side was to disable the cache with
`BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0`, and that is where we got stuck:

- `process.env.X = ...` doesn't reach the variable: it is read from the C
  environment.
- A libc `setenv` via `bun:ffi` works if it runs before the first transpile,
  but making that portable is a mountain of work for what should be a
  molehill.
- `--env-file` fills only the JS-side `process.env`, not the C environment —
  and it requires a file next to the binary anyway.
- `--compile-exec-argv` can embed flags, but there is no flag for this.
- What remains is a launcher script or a re-exec, which defeats the point of a
  single binary.

This particular problem looks fixed for the next release by #44473
(transpiler cache version 34), but it is one of many possible problems with the
same shape: any behavior configured only through an env var.

## The request

This follows existing practice for wrapping executables — nixpkgs
`makeWrapper` (`--set` vs `--set-default`) and Cargo's `[env]` table
(`force = true`): a value is a default that the user's environment can
override, and overriding it takes the explicit, louder form.

Two runtime flags that set variables in the real process environment, applied
before anything reads it:

```sh
bun --setenv=FOO=bar app.ts         # set FOO unless it is already set
bun --setenv-force=FOO=bar app.ts   # set FOO, overriding the environment
```

Being plain flags, they work with `bun` directly and in `BUN_OPTIONS`, and
`--compile-exec-argv` embeds them in a compiled binary with no new mechanism:

```sh
bun build --compile \
  --compile-exec-argv="--setenv=BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0" \
  app.ts --outfile app
```

The one hard requirement is timing: the flags must be applied to the C
environment before any of Bun's own env var reads, since those values are read
once and kept.

title: bun check: duplicate type alias declared in a .d.ts resolves differently than tsc (tsc 5.9 / 7 accept, skipLibCheck)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+5749c3129

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A `.d.ts` that declares the same type alias name twice (one of them self-referential through a same-named `const`), consumed with `skipLibCheck: true`. Generated declaration files sometimes end up like this.

`node_modules/lib/package.json`
```json
{ "name": "lib", "version": "1.0.0", "types": "index.d.ts" }
```

`node_modules/lib/index.d.ts`
```ts
export type Method = typeof Method;
export declare const Method: { a: number };
export type Method = "get" | "post";
export type Fn = (method: Method) => void;
```

`index.ts`
```ts
import type { Fn } from "lib";

export const f: Fn = (method: number) => {};
```

`tsconfig.json`
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler"
  },
  "include": ["index.ts"]
}
```

```sh
tsc -p .        # exit 0, no errors (TypeScript 5.9.3 and 7.0.2)
bun check       # exit 1
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun check` reports the same result as `tsc --noEmit`: no errors. With the duplicate declaration, `tsc` treats `Method` as an unresolved/circular type (effectively `any`), so `(method: number) => void` is assignable to `Fn`.

### What do you see instead?

```
index.ts(3,14): error TS2322: Type '(method: number) => void' is not assignable to type 'Fn'.
  Types of parameters 'method' and 'method' are incompatible.
    Type '{ a: number; }' is not assignable to type 'number'.
Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 1 file
```

`bun check` resolves `Method` to the type of the `const`, so it reports errors in user code that `tsc` does not.

### Additional information

Whether `tsc`'s lenient result is "correct" is debatable (the declaration is invalid and only tolerated because of `skipLibCheck`), but `bun check` is documented as reporting the same errors as `tsc`. In a real project this surfaced as two false-positive TS2322/TS2769 errors on a library's generated `Fetcher` type, while `tsc` reported none.

Without the `typeof Method` self-reference, both agree (both error), so the divergence is in how the circular alias is resolved when the name is declared twice.

title: `bun check`: loading time grows with the number of project references; each referenced project re-reads the libs and node_modules declarations
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3-canary.1+620b50f6a

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm (macOS 27.0, Apple M3 Pro, 12 cores)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

When the project being checked has `references`, `bun check` loads every referenced project as its own program, re-reading the default libs and every `node_modules` declaration file once per referenced project. The loading phase then grows with the number of references, while the number of distinct files does not change. On a real monorepo this makes `bun check -p <app>` about 25x slower than the same check with the `references` array deleted, and slower than tsgo 7.0.2 with the Effect plugin.

Generator for a minimal workspace: one app that imports `N` workspace modules through `paths` and lists them in `references`; each module imports `effect` (any package with a few hundred `.d.ts` files shows it).

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: make-repro.sh <dir> <modules> <files-per-module> <linker: isolated|hoisted>
set -e
R=$1; N=$2; F=$3; LINKER=$4
rm -rf "$R"; mkdir -p "$R/modules" "$R/apps/api/src"
echo '{"name":"repro","private":true,"workspaces":["modules/*","apps/*"]}' > "$R/package.json"
printf '[install]\nlinker = "%s"\n' "$LINKER" > "$R/bunfig.toml"
refs=""; paths=""; imports=""; rootrefs='{"path":"./apps/api"},'
for i in $(seq 1 $N); do
  m="$R/modules/m$i"; mkdir -p "$m/src"
  echo "{\"name\":\"@repro/m$i\",\"version\":\"0.0.0\",\"private\":true,\"dependencies\":{\"effect\":\"4.0.0-rc.109\"}}" > "$m/package.json"
  echo '{"compilerOptions":{"lib":["ESNext"],"target":"ESNext","module":"Preserve","moduleResolution":"bundler","strict":true,"skipLibCheck":true,"types":[],"composite":true,"declaration":true,"emitDeclarationOnly":true,"rootDir":"./src","outDir":"./dist","tsBuildInfoFile":"./dist/.tsbuildinfo"},"include":["src/**/*.ts"]}' > "$m/tsconfig.json"
  for j in $(seq 1 $F); do
    printf 'import { Effect } from "effect"\nexport const f%d_%d = Effect.succeed(%d)\n' $i $j $j > "$m/src/f$j.ts"
  done

  refs="$refs{\"path\":\"../../modules/m$i\"},"
  rootrefs="$rootrefs{\"path\":\"./modules/m$i\"},"

  imports="$imports""import * as m$i from \"@repro/m$i\"\n"

title: bun check: optional persistent incremental type-check caching
excerpt:
`bun check` currently checks the whole project on every invocation and does not write `.tsbuildinfo`, even with `incremental` enabled. This is documented as intentional: https://bun.com/docs/runtime/check#differences-from-tsc

Would an opt-in persistent cache be considered, allowing unchanged project-reference dependencies to reuse prior type-check work across separate `bun check` processes? A Bun-native cache would be fine; compatibility with TypeScript's `.tsbuildinfo` format or declaration emission is not required for this request.

In an existing monorepo task graph, each workspace has its own type-check command and dependent workspaces run first. Replacing every TypeScript command with native `bun check --build`, while retaining the same project configurations and Turbo dependency graph, can cause shared sources to be checked repeatedly by independent processes. An optional cache could also help subsequent local checks after small edits.

For context, three clean runs of a graph containing 67 compiler tasks had a median elapsed time of 45.08s under Bun canary `1.4.3-canary.1+620b50f6a` versus 35.89s under TypeScript 7.0.2. The final type-heavy task itself was faster under Bun: 5.09s versus 15.24s. Both variants passed with zero diagnostics. Every run started without prior build outputs or metadata, Turbo local/remote caching was disabled, and normal task concurrency was retained. TypeScript could consume newly emitted dependency declarations/metadata during that same run. These measurements motivate investigating reuse; they do not isolate the benefit of a persistent cache or predict performance after implementing one.

Related but separate: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/44763 concerns repeated loading within a single Bun invocation. A dependency-free synthetic generator is posted here: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/44763#issuecomment-6060167817. This request concerns reusing work across independent checker invocations. Both improvements may be useful.

The requested behavior is opt-in reuse with correct invalidation when source files, resolved dependencies, compiler configuration, or the Bun/compiler version change. Cached runs must retain complete diagnostics. Keeping the default check free of generated files would be fine.

Is this already planned, or is there a technical reason persistent incremental checking is intentionally excluded?

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`index.ts`
```ts
type Ref<T, S extends "root" | "plugin" = "root" | "plugin"> = { scope: S; t?: T };
declare function create<T>(o: { service: Ref<T, "root">; deps: { dep: Ref<unknown, "root"> } }): void;
declare function create<T>(o: { service: Ref<T, "plugin">; deps: { dep: Ref<unknown> } }): void;

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64, WSL2, kernel 7.2.9-locietta-WSL2-xanmod1

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Save as repro.mjs. No dependencies are needed.

```js
import { createHmac, getHashes } from 'node:crypto';
const results = [];
for (const algorithm of ['sha3-512', 'RSA-SHA3-512']) {
  try {
    results.push({ algorithm, digest: createHmac(algorithm, 'key').update('message').digest('hex') });
  } catch (error) {
    results.push({ algorithm, errorName: error.name, errorMessage: error.message });
  }
}
console.log(JSON.stringify({ node: process.versions.node, bun: process.versions.bun ?? null,
  bunRevision: globalThis.Bun?.revision ?? null, aliasEnumerated: getHashes().includes('RSA-SHA3-512'), results }));
```

```sh
node repro.mjs
bun --no-env-file --no-install repro.mjs
```

Verified on Node 26.11.1 and Bun 1.4.2 on 2026-10-08. This checks digest-name compatibility, with no performance claim.

### What is the expected behavior?

Node 26.11.1 accepts both sha3-512 and RSA-SHA3-512 in createHmac. Both produce the same digest:

```text
4b733ae1713d83ed27e49527a1e4ce032ecad6657e82403b42c31f901f00bdc306fdc5d1e4b664530e9c691a01070d85e6479be0b9c43b28e0ed7740f90628cf
```

Node also enumerates RSA-SHA3-512 in getHashes().

### What do you see instead?

Bun 1.4.2 produces the same expected digest with sha3-512, but RSA-SHA3-512 throws:

```text
TypeError: Invalid digest: RSA-SHA3-512
```

Bun does not enumerate this alias in getHashes(). The script catches the exception, so exit 0 is not evidence of alias support.

### Additional information

Canonical sha3-512 is a working workaround in this reproduction. The failure concerns createHmac digest-name compatibility, not an incorrect SHA-3 digest or RSA signing operation.

- #24075 is closed and reported missing canonical sha3-256 support. This report concerns a failing alias with a working canonical digest.
- #21812 was merged and concerned lowercase RSA algorithm handling. That does not establish support for this SHA-3 al

A file with no module syntax that uses `delete x` or a strict-mode reserved word as a name does not load
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

main at 5749c31290 (1.4.3-canary)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Each file has no `import`, `export`, `require`, `module` or `exports`. There is no package.json `"type"`.

```js
// delete.js
var x = 1;
console.log(delete x);
```

```js
// package.js
var package = 1;
console.log(package);
```

The second file fails in the same way for each of these names: `implements`, `interface`, `let`, `package`, `private`, `protected`, `public`, `static`, `yield`, `eval`, `arguments`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Node.js v26.3.0 runs each file as CommonJS.

```
$ node delete.js
false
$ node package.js
1
```

### What do you see instead?

```
$ bun delete.js
SyntaxError: Cannot delete unqualified property 'x' in strict mode.
$ bun package.js
SyntaxError: Cannot use the reserved word 'package' as a variable name in strict mode.
```

### Additional information

Bun runs a file that has no CommonJS marker as an ES module, so JavaScriptCore parses it as strict code. Strict code rejects these forms, so such a file cannot be an ES module.

Each file runs when it is named `.cjs`, and when `module.exports = 1;` is added at the end. The CommonJS kind alone is enough.

Two forms of this group already make a file CommonJS: a `with` statement (#7167) and a top-level `"use strict"` (#15868). A top-level `return` is #8908. A function declaration as the body of a label or of `if` is part of #25737.

bun check: opt-in safety checks beyond TypeScript compatibility
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

TypeScript intentionally accepts some code that can fail at runtime, even with strict enabled. Could bun check offer opt-in safety checks beyond TypeScript compatibility?

Known areas include:
- Mutable array and object variance: widened references can write values that violate the original type.
- Refinements retained across calls that may mutate the narrowed object.
- Bivariant method parameters, even with strictFunctionTypes.
- Unchecked type assertions and unsafe propagation of any: explicit escape hatches that projects may want to restrict.

Existing options such as noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes help, but do not address all these areas. This is a feature proposal for the announced checker, not a bug report against a released version.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Add an opt-in mode, for example `bun check --extra-strict` (illustrative name), with individually configurable safety checks beyond what TypeScript currently provides.

Candidate checks:
- Reject unsafe widening of mutable containers while allowing safe read-only conversions.
- Detect or conservatively invalidate refinements across calls that may mutate the relevant value, with documented false-positive tradeoffs.
- Check method parameter compatibility more strictly than TypeScript’s bivariant behavior.
- Report unsafe flows of any and unchecked assertions, with exceptions for external boundaries.

These are examples, not a requirement to implement every check at once. The broader request is a supported path for Bun to improve static safety beyond TypeScript, rather than limit all checking to parity.

Requirements:
- Preserve TypeScript compatibility by default; all additional restrictions must be opt-in.
- Allow incremental adoption through per-rule settings and targeted suppressions.
- Provide clear diagnostics with safer alternatives.
- Document limitations and compatibility costs; do not claim full soundness.
- Prioritize gaps that existing compiler options and lint rules cannot already cover well.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Existing TypeScript strictness flags: useful, but leave known safety gaps.
- Type-aware ESLint rules: already address many unsafe any/assertion uses; deeper assignability and mutation analysis may fit better in a checker.
- Readonly types and coding conventions: reduce risk but require consistent manual use.

title: fs.realpathSync throws EOPNOTSUPP on a Unix domain socket on macOS (lstat and stat succeed; works on Linux and in Node)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (also reproduced on 1.3.14)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create a Unix domain socket and call `fs.realpathSync` on its path:

```js
// repro.js
const fs = require("fs"), net = require("net"), os = require("os"), path = require("path");
const sock = path.join(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "sock-")), "s.sock");
net.createServer().listen(sock, () => {
  console.log("lstat isSocket:", fs.lstatSync(sock).isSocket());
  for (const [name, fn] of [
    ["realpathSync", () => fs.realpathSync(sock)],
    ["realpathSync.native", () => fs.realpathSync.native(sock)],
  ]) {
    try { console.log(name, "->", fn()); } catch (e) { console.log(name, "FAIL", e.code, e.syscall, e.message); }
  }
  process.exit(0);
});
```

```sh
bun repro.js
```

A real-world instance is the Docker socket:

```sh
bun -e 'console.log(require("fs").realpathSync("/var/run/docker.sock"))'
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`realpathSync` and `realpathSync.native` return the canonical path of the socket, as Node.js does and as the libc `realpath(3)` does on macOS. The socket exists, is readable by `lstat`/`stat`, and lives in an ordinary directory.

Node.js output of the same script:

```
lstat isSocket: true
realpathSync -> /private/var/folders/.../sock-XXXX/s.sock
realpathSync.native -> /private/var/folders/.../sock-XXXX/s.sock
```

### What do you see instead?

Both calls throw `EOPNOTSUPP`. The `realpathSync` error is reported against `lstat`, which is misleading because `lstat` on the same path succeeds.

```
lstat isSocket: true
realpathSync FAIL EOPNOTSUPP lstat EOPNOTSUPP: unknown error, lstat '/var/folders/cb/.../sock-8Egu91/s.sock'
realpathSync.native FAIL EOPNOTSUPP realpath EOPNOTSUPP: unknown error, realpath '/var/folders/cb/.../sock-8Egu91/s.sock'
```

`fs.promises.realpath` fails the same way.

### Additional information

- **Platform specific.** The same script succeeds with Bun 1.3.14 on Linux (`oven/bun:1.3.14-alpine`), including through a symlink to the socket. It fails on macOS with 1.3.14 and 1.4.2.
- **Likely cause.** On macOS Bun resolves `realpath` by opening the file and asking the kernel for its path (`fcntl(F_GETPATH)`). `open(2)` on a Unix domain socket is not allowed, so the open fails with `EOPNOTSUPP` and that errno is surfaced as the `realpath` result. title: `Bun.CryptoHasher` with a key throws an unrelated error left behind by a failed `crypto.subtle.importKey`
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm (also reproduced in the oven/bun:1.4 image: Linux 6.8.0-117-generic aarch64 unknown)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A failed `crypto.subtle.importKey` leaves its error in BoringSSL's error queue. The next `update()` on a keyed `Bun.CryptoHasher` (HMAC) throws that error, although the HMAC itself is fine. Only once: the throw clears the queue.

`repro.mjs`, no dependencies:

```js
const hmac = () => new Bun.CryptoHasher("sha256", "key").update("data").digest("hex");

console.log("1. HMAC before:", hmac());

// Any failed key import works; a 3 byte buffer is not PKCS#8 DER.
await crypto.subtle
  .importKey("pkcs8", new Uint8Array([0, 0, 0]), { name: "RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5", hash: "SHA-256" }, false, ["sign"])
  .catch((error) => console.log("2. importKey rejected, as expected:", error.name));

try {
  console.log("3. HMAC after:", hmac());
} catch (error) {
  console.log("3. HMAC after THROWS:", error.code, "-", error.message);
}
console.log("4. HMAC again:", hmac());
```

```sh
bun repro.mjs
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Step 3 prints the same HMAC as steps 1 and 4. The failed import has nothing to do with the HMAC.

```
1. HMAC before: 5031fe3d989c6d1537a013fa6e739da23463fdaec3b70137d828e36ace221bd0
2. importKey rejected, as expected: DataError
3. HMAC after: 5031fe3d989c6d1537a013fa6e739da23463fdaec3b70137d828e36ace221bd0
4. HMAC again: 5031fe3d989c6d1537a013fa6e739da23463fdaec3b70137d828e36ace221bd0
```

### What do you see instead?

```
1. HMAC before: 5031fe3d989c6d1537a013fa6e739da23463fdaec3b70137d828e36ace221bd0
2. importKey rejected, as expected: DataError
3. HMAC after THROWS: ERR_OSSL_ASN1_DECODE_ERROR - error:0c00006d:ASN.1 encoding routines:OPENSSL_internal:DECODE_ERROR
4. HMAC again: 5031fe3d989c6d1537a013fa6e739da23463fdaec3b70137d828e36ace221bd0
```

The same output on macOS arm64 and in the `oven/bun:1.4` container with no network.

title: process.hrtime counts from process start, so readings from separate processes can't be compared as in Node
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.9-locietta-WSL2-xanmod1 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`process.hrtime.bigint()` (and `process.hrtime()`) in Bun starts near zero when the process starts. In Node it reads the system monotonic clock (`uv_hrtime`, `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), which counts from boot and is the same clock in every process. So an hrtime reading from a Bun process can't be compared with one from another process, a Node process, or a tool that reads `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` directly.

`hrtime.mjs`:

```js
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
const hrtime = Number(process.hrtime.bigint()) / 1e9;
const uptime = Number(readFileSync("/proc/uptime", "utf8").split(" ")[0]);
console.log(`hrtime ${hrtime.toFixed(3)} s, /proc/uptime ${uptime.toFixed(2)} s`);
```

```
$ node hrtime.mjs   # v26.11.1
hrtime 10477.449 s, /proc/uptime 10477.44 s
$ bun hrtime.mjs
hrtime 0.004 s, /proc/uptime 10477.45 s
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`process.hrtime` reads the same clock as Node: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux, so the value tracks `/proc/uptime` (until the machine suspends) and two processes started at different times return comparable values.

### What do you see instead?

The value is the time since this Bun process started, so it differs from every other process's reading by that process's start time.

### Additional information

Node documents the hrtime origin as "an arbitrary time in the past", and #13387 was closed after a reply quoting that. In practice Node's origin is shared by every process on the machine, and code that coordinates timing across processes depends on that. I hit this in a benchmark where a Bun child process and an external observer process stamp the same events, and the audit compares their timestamps directly. With Bun as the child, every run would fail those checks.

Workaround: read the clock through FFI.

```js
import { dlopen, FFIType, ptr } from "bun:ffi";
const { symbols } = dlopen("libc.so.6", { clock_gettime: { args: [FFIType.i32, FFIType.ptr], returns: FFIType.i32 } });
const ts = new BigInt64Array(2);
symbols.clock_gettime(1 /* CLOCK_MONOTONIC */, ptr(ts));
console.log(Number(ts[0]) + Number(ts[1]) / 1e9); // matches /proc/uptime
```

title: Windows AppContainer: extend the #33119 VOLUME_NAME_NT fallback to fs.realpath (EPERM makes chokidar loop forever)
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

(Written using Claude Opus 5.5)

-----

Inside a Windows AppContainer, `fs.realpath`, `fs.realpathSync` and `fs.promises.realpath` fail with `EPERM` for every path, including folders the container can fully read and write. #33119 lists this as a known limitation, at Node.js parity.

Measured with Bun 1.4.3 (embedded in Claude Code's `claude.exe`), Windows 11 10.0.26200, in a folder the AppContainer may read and write:

    statSync(cwd)                ok    directory
    realpathSync(cwd)            FAIL  EPERM: operation not permitted, lstat 'C:\'
    realpathSync.native(cwd)     FAIL  EPERM: operation not permitted, realpath 'C:\ccrepro\work'
    promises.realpath(cwd)       FAIL  EPERM: operation not permitted, lstat 'C:\ccrepro\work'

(Reproduce with `acrun.c` + `realpath-probe.js` from https://github.com/electrotype/issue-claude-code-appcontainer-cpu-loop, section "The realpath failure on its own".)

The impact goes beyond a failed call. Libraries treat a realpath error as "try the parent", and in a container every parent fails too. chokidar, a very common file watcher, then loops forever at the drive root: its `add()` re-adds `dirname()` with no root check, and `dirname("C:/") === "C:/"`. In Claude Code (a Bun-compiled binary), every directory watcher does this, and an idle session burns one or two CPU cores indefinitely, about 6,000 `stat`/`realpath` calls per second on `C:/`. Reported to Claude Code as anthropics/claude-code#100831.

Two separate causes:
1. **Native path:** `GetFinalPathNameByHandleW(VOLUME_NAME_DOS)` is denied, because the DOS-name translation opens `\\.\MountPointManager` (DACL `WD/SY/BA/RC`, no AppContainer access). `VOLUME_NAME_NT` and `VOLUME_NAME_NONE` work. `QueryDosDeviceW` is denied too, so the #43540 approach doesn't help inside a container.
2. **Non-native path:** the walk `lstat`s the drive root first, and an AppContainer cannot read `C:\`.

Bun already solves cause 1 internally: #33119's AppContainer fallback rebuilds the DOS name as `<system-drive>:` + the `VOLUME_NAME_NT` tail for its own resolver and `bun install`. It just isn't applied to user-facing `fs.realpath`.

Make `fs.realpath*` work inside an AppContainer, gated on `is_app_container()` like the rest of #33119, so nothing changes outside a container:
