excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2+744846f84. Also reproduces on 1.4.3-canary.1+5749c3129.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.6 x86_64. Also seen on GitHub Actions `ubuntu-22.04` runners.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is the full `packages/ai` suite (483 test files) of [oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi), at a commit on our public fork [RigelBuild/oh-my-pi](https://github.com/RigelBuild/oh-my-pi). I don't have a small repro. The hang depends on how many files run in one process, and no single file triggers it.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/RigelBuild/oh-my-pi && cd oh-my-pi
git checkout a68b5a34c91c
bun install
# copy pi_natives.linux-x64-*.node from @oh-my-pi/pi-natives-linux-x64@18.6.1 on npm (or a local build) into packages/natives/native/
cd packages/ai
bun test --parallel=1 --timeout=120000
```

`--parallel` implies `--isolate`. With `--parallel=1` the files run in-process, through `run_as_coordinator` -> `run_all_tests`.

A normal run takes about 160s. In about 1 run of 3, the process stops making progress and sits at 100% CPU on the main thread:

| Bun | Runs | Hung |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1.4.2 | 23 | 8 |
| 1.4.3-canary.1+5749c3129 | 10 | 4 |
| 1.4.2, files split into 4 separate `bun test` processes | 32 processes | 0 |

Upstream oh-my-pi CI (`--parallel=4`) shows what looks like the same stall: a test that runs far past its own timeout. For example, [this run](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/actions/runs/37714060288) has `(fail) Snowflake browser OAuth > cancellation after-auth prevents token exchange [320365.47ms]` followed by `^ this test timed out after 120000ms.`


### What is the expected behavior?

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?
1.4.3+c6da4a4d3 (same result on 1.4.3-canary.1+e555359cc)

### What platform is your computer?
Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`repro.c`
```c
int echo_int(int v) { return v; }
```

`repro.ts`
```ts
import { cc } from "bun:ffi";

const { echo_int } = cc({
  source: new URL("./repro.c", import.meta.url).pathname,
  symbols: { echo_int: { returns: "int", args: ["int"] } },
}).symbols;

const heap = new Float64Array([7, 3, 0, -5, 1e6]);
for (const v of heap) {
  console.log(`value=${v} direct=${echo_int(v)} coerced=${echo_int(v | 0)}`);
}
```

`bun repro.ts`

### What is the expected behavior?
`echo_int(7)` returns 7 no matter how the number is stored.

### What do you see instead?
```
value=7 direct=0 coerced=7
value=3 direct=0 coerced=3
value=0 direct=0 coerced=0
value=-5 direct=0 coerced=-5
value=1000000 direct=0 coerced=1000000
```
Passing the value read from the `Float64Array` gives 0. Passing `v | 0` gives the right value.

### Additional information
Only numbers that are stored as doubles fail. These also return 0 when passed to an `int` argument: `Math.sqrt(49)`, `Number(f64[0])`, and an element of `[7.5, 7]`. A literal `7.0`, an object property `{ x: 7 }`, `Number("7")` and `Math.floor(7.5)` all return 7.

The argument type matters. With a `Float64Array` value of 7:

| FFI arg type | result |
|---|---|
| `i32` | 0 |
| `u32` | 0 |
| `i16` | 0 |
| `i64` | 7n |
| `f64` | 7 |

I found this in a project that reads integers out of a `Float64Array`. I tested on macOS arm64. The workaround is `| 0` or `>>> 0` on every integer before the call.

Linux 7.0.12+deb13-amd64 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create `package.json`:

  "private": true,

}
```

3. Create `repro.ts`:

```ts
import { match } from 'ts-pattern';

type Input = {
  kind?: 'k1' | 'k2' | 'k3';
  sub?: 's1';
};

export class Repro {
  method(input: Input) {
    const value = { ...input };
    return match(value)
      .with({ kind: 'k1' }, () => 1)
      .with({ kind: 'k2' }, () => 2)
      .with({ kind: 'k3' }, () => 3)
      .otherwise(() => 0);
  }
}
```

4. Run:

```sh
bun install
bunx -p typescript@7.0.2 tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --pretty false
bun check -p tsconfig.json --no-pretty
```

No errors, the same as `tsc` 7.0.2, which prints nothing and exits with code 0.

### What do you see instead?

`bun check` exits with code 1:

```
repro.ts(11,12): error TS2589: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite.
Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 2 files
```

### Additional information

I changed one thing at a time against `repro.ts`:

| Variant | `bun check` |
|---|---|
| As written (class method) | ❌ TS2589 |
| `static method(...)` | ❌ TS2589 |
| Arrow-function class property `method = (input: Input) => {...}` | ❌ TS2589 |
| Same body as a top-level `export function method(input: Input)` | ✅ no error |
| `match({ ...input })` inline, without the `value` local | ✅ no error |
| `match(input)`, with no spread | ✅ no error |
| `sub` property removed from `Input` | ✅ no error |

### Bun version

1.4.3 (`c6da4a4d3`).

### Platform

Linux ARM64, musl, kernel 7.0.14, using `oven/bun:1.4.3-alpine` on Docker Desktop (Apple M4 Pro host).

### Reproduction

A clean project with one npm dependency reproduces a compiler abort. There is no application code or dependency patch.

`package.json`:

```json
{"private":true,"type":"module","dependencies":{"@google-cloud/tasks":"7.2.1"}}
```

`index.ts`:

```ts
const { CloudTasksClient } = await import('@google-cloud/tasks');
console.log(typeof CloudTasksClient);
```

`Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
FROM oven/bun:1.4.3-alpine
WORKDIR /repro
COPY package.json ./
RUN bun install --ignore-scripts
COPY index.ts ./
ARG EXTRA_BUILD_FLAGS=""
RUN bun build index.ts --compile --bytecode --format=esm --outfile=app $EXTRA_BUILD_FLAGS
```

From a directory containing those three files:

```sh
docker build --platform=linux/arm64 -t tasks-bytecode-repro .
```

The build step aborts with exit code 133 before producing the executable:

```text
Bun v1.4.3 (c6da4a4d3) Linux arm64
Linux Kernel v7.0.14 | musl
CPU: neon fp aes crc32 atomics
Args: "bun" "build" "index.ts" "--compile" "--bytecode" "--format=esm" "--outfile=app"
RSS: 0.14 GB | Peak: 0.14 GB | Commit: 0.59 GB
panic(main thread): abort() called
```

[Redacted crash report](https://bun.report/1.4.3/Ub1c6da4a4gCgoggCutuUmoiI23/3tBu589sD+z99sDmy/gvDms0/uD2+98/D+g+8/D+g+8/D+g+8/D+g+8/Dm9ylxB+3qlxB+iqlxB22rprCmjq5rCukq+sC2yxwgCu8l0mCAa)

With the same source and dependency install, disabling only the bytecode optimizer completes the build:

```sh
docker build --platform=linux/arm64 \
  --build-arg EXTRA_BUILD_FLAGS=--no-optimize-bytecode \
  -t tasks-bytecode-repro-no-opt .
```

```text
[226ms] bundle 350 modules
[105ms] compile app
```

This control verifies compilation, not runtime packaging of the SDK's computed JSON asset paths.

### Expected behavior

The compiler should produce an executable or report a diagnostic for unsupported code, rather than aborting in its default bytecode optimization path.

#29351 reports an assertion while starting a previously built bytecode executable on Bun 1.3.12. This reproduction aborts during compilation on Bun 1.4.3. Searches for `@google-cloud/tasks`, `bytecode optimizer crash`, and `no-optimize-bytecode` did not find a matching report.

title: fs.readdirSync returns names in filesystem order; Node returns them sorted
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3 (stable); 1.4.4-canary.1+6c1eb067e behaves the same

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.9 (WSL2) x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// readdir-order.mjs
import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";

const base = process.argv[2] ?? os.tmpdir();
const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(base, "readdir-"));
for (const name of ["b.txt", "c.txt", "a.txt"]) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, name), "");
console.log(fs.readdirSync(dir).join(","));
fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true });
```

```
node readdir-order.mjs            # /tmp is tmpfs
node readdir-order.mjs ./on-disk  # an existing directory on ext4
bun readdir-order.mjs
bun readdir-order.mjs ./on-disk
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The same output as Node (v26.11.1): `a.txt,b.txt,c.txt` on both filesystems. Node's `fs.readdirSync` and `fs.readdir` list a directory's names sorted on Linux because libuv sorts them (`uv_fs_scandir`). Node's docs do not promise an order, but code written against Node depends on it.

### What do you see instead?

```
bun, tmpfs: a.txt,c.txt,b.txt
bun, ext4 : b.txt,a.txt,c.txt
```

Bun returns the order the kernel gives (`ls -U` on the ext4 directory prints `b.txt,a.txt,c.txt`). `fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })` shows the same order. Node's own `fs.opendirSync` also returns raw order (`b.txt,a.txt,c.txt` on ext4), so only the `readdir` family is sorted in Node.

### Additional information

This changed a real program's results. CodeGraph walks a project with `readdirSync` and writes files to its index in walk order; equal-score search hits are then ordered by insertion order. Under Bun the same three identical files were indexed in a different order than under Node, so the same query listed them in a different order. Sorting the entries in our code fixed it, so we are not blocked; filing this so the difference is on record.

Tested with Bun 1.4.3 stable and 1.4.4-canary.1+6c1eb067e on the same machine.

title: macOS: process.memoryUsage().rss and maxRSS miss memory reused after Bun.gc(true) (1.4.3 regression)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```ts
const mb = (n: number) => (n / 2 ** 20) | 0
const ps = () =>
  mb(Number(Bun.spawnSync(["ps", "-o", "rss=", "-p", String(process.pid)]).stdout.toString()) * 1024)
const log = (label: string) =>
  console.log(label.padEnd(12), "rss()", mb(process.memoryUsage.rss()), "ps rss", ps())

log("start")
new Array(8_000_000).fill(1.5)
log("after 8M")
Bun.gc(true)
log("after gc")
const a = new Array(5_000_000).fill(1.5) // ~40 MB, kept live
log("holding 5M")
```

### What is the expected behavior?

After the 40 MB array is allocated, `process.memoryUsage().rss` includes it, as it did in 1.4.2.

### What do you see instead?

```
              1.4.3           1.4.2
              rss()  ps rss   rss()  ps rss
start            4     10        9     10
after 8M        65     72       72     72
after gc         5     73       73     73
holding 5M       5     73       73     73
```

The array is live, but `rss` stays at 5 MB. It catches up later on its own. Polling `rss()` in a loop after the allocation, it climbs from 4 MB to 44 MB over about 0.3 to 0.5 s.

Bun reports the kernel's number accurately. Running `footprint -p <pid>` right after the allocation also shows `phys_footprint: 4657 KB`. The kernel's footprint is what lags.

`process.resourceUsage().maxRSS` misses it too. Free 65 MB with `Bun.gc(true)`, then hold a 96 MB array:

```
1.4.3  holding 96 MB: rss() 35 MB, maxRSS 65 -> 65 MB
1.4.2  holding 96 MB: rss() 102 MB, maxRSS 71 -> 102 MB
```

So on macOS, neither `rss` nor `maxRSS` shows a short-lived allocation that reuses memory `Bun.gc(true)` just freed.

### Additional information

It looks like the combination of two 1.4.3 changes:

- `Bun.gc(true)` and `gc()` return freed memory to the OS before returning.
- On macOS, `process.memoryUsage().rss` reports the physical footprint and `maxRSS` reports its peak.

My guess is that the freed pages are marked `MADV_FREE_REUSABLE`, which drops them from the footprint, and nothing calls `MADV_FREE_REUSE` when the allocator hands them out again, so they're only counted again once the kernel gets to them. WebKit's bmalloc pairs the two calls for this reason.

This breaks tools that measure the memory of a single call with `Bun.gc(true)` followed by sampling `rss`. As a workaround, I read resident size with `ps -o rss=` on macOS.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`index.ts`:

```ts
interface I {
  readonly id: string
}
type Writable<T> = { -readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] }

declare const a: Writable<I> & I
declare const b: { id: string } & I

a.id = 'x'
b.id = 'x'
```

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "types": []
  },
  "include": ["index.ts"]
}
```

```sh
bun check --no-pretty
bunx -p typescript@7.0.2 tsc -p . --pretty false
bunx -p typescript@6.0.3 tsc -p . --pretty false
```


### What is the expected behavior?

Same as `tsc` 7.0.2 (6.0.3 agrees): an error on `a.id`, none on `b.id`.

```
index.ts(9,3): error TS2540: Cannot assign to 'id' because it is a read-only property.
```


### What do you see instead?

✓ No type errors in 1 file

### Additional information

tsc keeps the property read-only when the writable member of the intersection is a mapped type that removes `readonly`. With a plain object member (`b`), both tsc and `bun check` treat it as writable, so only the mapped-type case differs. Swapping the order to `I & Writable<I>` gives the same result, and so does a class that declares the property `readonly`.

The error in tsc doesn't come from the intersection rule. In `lib/typescript.js` (6.0.3), `createUnionOrIntersectionProperty` clears `CheckFlags.Readonly` on an intersection property as soon as one member's property is writable, so the flag alone would allow `a.id = 'x'`. The homomorphic mapped property, though, links to the original declarations (`prop.declarations = modifiersProp.declarations`) and has no `valueDeclaration` of its own, so the merged property takes I's `readonly id: string` as its `valueDeclaration`. `isReadonlySymbol` then finds `readonly` through `getDeclarationModifierFlagsFromSymbol`. In `b` the two members have different value declarations, so the merged property gets none and stays writable.

I found this through a `// @ts-expect-error` above a write like `a.id = 'x'`: tsc accepts the file, and `bun check` reports `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`.

(Replaces #44965, which I filed without the form, so it has no labels.)

title: Assignment to a const in unexecuted code fails at parse time instead of throwing TypeError at runtime
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 and 1.4.3 (macOS arm64)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin arm64 (code path is platform independent)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// c.cjs
const e = 1;
function f() { e = 2 } // never called
module.exports = "ok";
```

```sh
node c.cjs                      # exit 0
bun run c.cjs                   # exit 1
bun build c.cjs --outfile out.js   # exit 1
```

```
error: Cannot assign to "e" because it is a constant
    at c.cjs:1:28
note: The symbol "e" was declared a constant here:
```

The same happens for an ESM file, and for a file that a `bun build --compile` executable loads from disk with `require()` / `import()` at runtime (1.4.2 and 1.4.3).

Non-literal initializers get the other message, also as an error: `const e = foo(); function f(){ e = 2 }` -> `This assignment will throw because "e" is a constant`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Per ECMA-262 (13.15.2 evaluation + `PutValue` -> `SetMutableBinding`), assignment to a `const` binding is a runtime `TypeError`, not an early error. A module where the assignment is never executed must load. Node, V8 and JSC accept this file. esbuild reports it as a warning ("This assignment will throw because ...") when not bundling.

### What do you see instead?

The module fails to load before any code runs.

### Additional information

Real-world hit: Next.js 16.4 Turbopack with `experimental.turbopackModuleFragments` emits server chunks containing assignments to consts in code paths that don't run, so those chunks cannot be loaded by a `bun build --compile` server.

Source: `src/js_parser/visit/visit_expr.rs`, in the identifier assign-target handling. Both branches call `add_range_error_fmt_with_notes`; the second branch ("This assignment will throw because") is the one esbuild emits as a warning. There is also `// TODO: silence this for runtime transpiler` just above. The first branch is taken when the const was recorded in `const_values` (literal initializer, `features.inlining`), which is true for the runtime transpiler, not only for bundling.

TOML parse: confusing error on invalid escape (e.g. Windows path 'C:\Users'); suggest clearer message or lenient mode
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64 (WSL2), also reproducible on macOS

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`Bun.TOML.parse` rejects **basic strings (double-quoted) that contain a lone backslash followed by a letter**, treating `\X` as a Unicode escape. This breaks legitimate TOML values like Windows paths and regex.

```ts
// All of these are VALID TOML per the spec (basic strings allow \" \\ and any
// literal char otherwise; a lone backslash is only special before a known escape).
Bun.TOML.parse(`v = "C:\\Users\\name"`);   // SyntaxError
Bun.TOML.parse(`v = "a\\tb"`);             // OK  (\t is a valid escape)
Bun.TOML.parse(`v = "a\\nb"`);             // OK  (\n)
Bun.TOML.parse(`v = "a\\"b"`);             // OK  (\" )
Bun.TOML.parse(`v = "héllo→世界"`);   // OK  (literal multibyte)
```

The error:
```
SyntaxError: TOML Parse error: A Unicode escape must be followed by exactly 8 hex digits
```

`\U` (from `\Users`) is parsed as the start of a `\UXXXXXXXX` Unicode escape and the parser chokes when it isn't 8 hex digits.

### What is the expected behavior?

Per [the TOML spec on basic strings](https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0#section-8), the valid escapes in a basic string are `\b \t \n \f \r \" \\ \uXXXX \UXXXXXXXX`. A backslash followed by **anything else** (e.g. `\U` in `\Users`, `\d` in `\d+`) is **invalid TOML** — so strictly the parser is right to reject `C:\Users`.

The real problem is the **error message**: it says "A Unicode escape must be followed by exactly 8 hex digits," which misleads the user into thinking their *content* is wrong, when actually they wrote a spec-invalid escape. The message should name the actual rule: "invalid escape sequence `\U` in basic string; escape it as `\\` or use a literal string."

### What do you see instead?

A confusing error that points at hex-digit count rather than "you have an invalid escape, use a literal string ('...') or escape the backslash."

### Suggested fix

Two options, either improves this:
1. **Better error**: when a `\` is followed by a char that isn't a valid escape opener, report "invalid escape `\U` — use a literal string 'C:\Users\name' or escape the backslash as `\\`".
2. **A `relaxed`/lenient parse mode** for config-file use cases where Windows paths and regex are common, treating unknown `\X` as a literal `X` (like many config loaders do).

title: Compile cache: writing NODE_COMPILE_CACHE at exit is ~2.5-3x slower since 1.4.3 (regressed between d316760e8 and 5f554969b)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3 (regression vs 1.4.2+744846f84)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.x arm64 (Apple silicon)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

With `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` set to an empty directory, a process that loads a large amount of code now spends noticeably longer **after** its `exit` event before the OS process ends. The time goes to writing the compile cache: with `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` the post-exit time is ~20-40 ms on both versions.

Generate a ~3.4 MB module and a tiny entry:

```js
// gen.cjs
const fs = require("fs");
let out = "";
for (let i = 0; i < 20000; i++)
  out += `export function f${i}(a, b) { const o = { k: a + ${i}, s: "v${i}" + b }; if (o.k > ${i * 3}) return o.s.length + a; for (let j = 0; j < 3; j++) o.k += j * b; return o.k; }\n`;
fs.writeFileSync("big.mjs", out);
fs.writeFileSync("main.mjs", `import * as m from "./big.mjs";
let s = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 20000; i += 97) s += m["f" + i](i, 2);
process.on("exit", () => process.stderr.write("EXIT_EVENT_MS " + performance.now().toFixed(0) + "\\n"));
console.log("ok", s);`);
```

```sh
node gen.cjs
# cold cache each run; compare wall time with the exit-event timestamp
d=$(mktemp -d); NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=$d /usr/bin/time -p bun main.mjs >/dev/null; rm -rf "$d"
NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 /usr/bin/time -p bun main.mjs >/dev/null
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Time after the `exit` event (writing the compile cache) stays roughly where it was in 1.4.2.

### What do you see instead?

Time from the `exit` event to process end, fresh cache directory each run, 5 interleaved runs per version (ms):

| build | compile cache on | `NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.4.2 (744846f84) | 267, 298, 259, 222, 173 | 36, 33, 31, 19, 18 |
| 1.4.3 (c6da4a4d3) | 711, 915, 798, 523, 388 | 42, 31, 30, 18, 18 |

The cache written is about the same size on both (~7 MB, 2 files).

In a real CLI (a ~MBs bundled app, cold first launch with an empty cache) this shows up as ~0.4 s after the exit event on 1.4.2 vs ~1.2-2.0 s on 1.4.3, i.e. the whole first launch gets ~1 s slower, with ~0.7-1.6 s more user CPU. Warm launches (cache already present) are unaffected.

### Additional information

Bisected with the daily canaries (same repro, plus the larger CLI case):

- `1.4.2-canary.20260906.1` = 1.4.3-canary.1+**d316760e8**: good (CLI help->exit gap ~0.5 s; small repro median ~340 ms)

title: `bun build --compile`: embedded `.node` addon fails to load (ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED) when `TMPDIR` is a relative path
excerpt:
## Versions

- Bun 1.4.2 (latest as of 2026-10-12, via `bunx bun@latest`) - reproduces
- Bun 1.3.14 - reproduces
- macOS arm64 (Darwin 27). Not tested on Linux.

## Description

A compiled executable that `require`s a native `.node` addon extracts the addon to a temp file before `dlopen`. When `TMPDIR` is a relative path (for example `TMPDIR=.`, which several test harnesses and Bazel-style sandboxes set), the extraction path is built from the relative value, but `dlopen` is then called with a path that has been re-rooted to `/`, so the load fails. An absolute `TMPDIR` works. Node-style semantics would resolve the relative `TMPDIR` against the cwd once, up front (or `os.tmpdir()` would return an absolute path).

## Repro

`addon.c` (minimal N-API addon, no dependencies):

```c
#include <stddef.h>
typedef struct napi_env__* napi_env; typedef struct napi_value__* napi_value;
extern int napi_create_int32(napi_env, int, napi_value*);
extern int napi_set_named_property(napi_env, napi_value, const char*, napi_value);
napi_value napi_register_module_v1(napi_env env, napi_value exports) {
  napi_value v; napi_create_int32(env, 42, &v);
  napi_set_named_property(env, exports, "answer", v); return exports;
}
```

`main.ts`:

```ts
const addon = require("./addon.node");
console.log("answer", addon.answer);
```

```sh
clang -shared -undefined dynamic_lookup -o addon.node addon.c   # Linux: cc -shared -fPIC -o addon.node addon.c
bun build --compile main.ts --outfile app

mkdir -p /tmp/abs && TMPDIR=/tmp/abs ./app     # works: answer 42
mkdir -p cwd && cd cwd && TMPDIR=. ../app      # fails
```

## Expected

`answer 42` for both, i.e. a relative `TMPDIR` is resolved against the cwd before the addon is extracted and loaded.

## Actual (Bun 1.4.2)

```
error: dlopen(/.bun-501-e636c7895fdf81dd.node, 0x0001): tried: '/.bun-501-e636c7895fdf81dd.node' (no such file), '/System/Volumes/Preboot/Cryptexes/OS/.bun-501-e636c7895fdf81dd.node' (no such file), '/.bun-501-e636c7895fdf81dd.node' (no such file)
```

On 1.3.14 the extracted file is written to the cwd (`./.bafdb7ef3ebfecdb-00000000.node`) while `dlopen` looks for `/.bafdb7ef3ebfecdb-00000000.node` (`ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`), which shows the write path and the load path disagree.

## Workaround

Make `TMPDIR` absolute before the first `require` of the addon: `process.env.TMPDIR = path.resolve(process.env.TMPDIR)` (works for the process itself; child processes need it passed in their env).

title: Windows: recursive mkdir of `./`, `.\` or `sub/..` throws ENOENT with an empty path
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?
1.4.3+c6da4a4d3

### What platform is your computer?
Windows 11 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const fs = require("node:fs");
fs.mkdirSync("sub", { recursive: true });
for (const p of [".", "./", ".\\", "sub/..", "sub/."]) {
  try { fs.mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true }); console.log("OK", p); }
  catch (e) { console.log("NG", p, e.code, e.message); }
}
```

### What is the expected behavior?
Every path names the existing current directory, so each call should return without an error. Node.js v26.11.1 and Deno 2.9.7 do this.

### What do you see instead?

```text
NG . EEXIST EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '.'
NG ./ ENOENT ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir
NG .\ ENOENT ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir
NG sub/.. ENOENT ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir
OK sub/.
```

`fs.promises.mkdir` and the callback `fs.mkdir` fail the same way.

| Path | Bun 1.4.3 | PR #42014 | PR #42635 | PR #40536 | Node.js / Deno |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.` | ❌ EEXIST | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `./` | ❌ ENOENT | ❌ ENOENT | ❌ ENOENT | ✅ | ✅ |
| `.\` | ❌ ENOENT | ❌ ENOENT | ❌ ENOENT | ✅ | ✅ |
| `sub/..` | ❌ ENOENT | ❌ ENOENT | ❌ ENOENT | ✅ | ✅ |

**#42014 and #42635 do not fix the ENOENT cases.** I tested each PR's Windows x64 CI build, with the SHA-256 checked against Buildkite.

### Additional information

**Cause.** `os_path_kernel32` in `src/runtime/node/types.rs` ([L1072-L1088](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/c6da4a4d3010e5553438c60f6bd76d981976867c/src/runtime/node/types.rs#L1072-L1088)) special-cases only the exact input `"."` before normalizing. `normalize_string_buf` also turns `./`, `.\` and `sub/..` into an empty string, but they miss that check, so mkdir gets an empty path.

**Possible fix.** If the normalized result is empty, use `"."`; in other words, move the `"."` special case after normalization. #40536 joins relative paths with the cwd before normalizing, and it passes these cases.

**Related:** #17332, #44576, #42014, #42635, #40536

Evidence (builds, SHA-256 checksums, verbatim output, source) is [here](https://lightspeedc.com/20261012-bun-mkdir-recursive-problem/issue/bun-mkdir-enoent-issue.html); the repro and tests are in [this repository](https://github.com/LightSpeedC/20261012-bun-mkdir-recursive-problem#readme).

process.stdin.resume() throws "ReadableStream is locked" after Bun.spawn takes Bun.stdin.stream() (regression in 1.4.3)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.1 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
// repro.js
Bun.spawn(["echo", "child ran"], { stdout: "inherit", stdin: Bun.stdin.stream() });
process.stdin.resume();
console.log("resume ok");
```

```sh
sleep 1 | bun repro.js
```

### What is the expected behavior?

As on 1.4.2:

```
child ran
resume ok
```

### What do you see instead?

```
child ran
2 | process.stdin.resume();
                  ^
TypeError: Invalid state: ReadableStream is locked
 code: "ERR_INVALID_STATE"

      at own (5:15)
      at /private/tmp/bun-stdin-repro/repro.js:2:15

Bun v1.4.3 (macOS arm64)
```

### Additional information

Regression in 1.4.3; 1.4.2 runs the same script cleanly.

`process.stdin.resume()` now throws once `Bun.spawn` has locked `Bun.stdin.stream()` for a child's stdin. Before, the two coexisted.

Real-world impact: the Elixir [`bun`](https://github.com/crbelaus/bun) package runs every watcher through a [`wrapper.js`](https://github.com/crbelaus/bun/blob/main/priv/wrapper.js) with exactly this pattern. It forwards stdin to the child, then calls `process.stdin.resume()` and listens for `close` to kill the child when the Elixir side exits. On 1.4.3 the wrapper throws before it registers that `close` handler, so every Phoenix dev server restart leaves an orphaned `bun build --watch` process behind.

Like Node: an `undefined` backlog is skipped and the last function argument is the listening callback.

### What do you see instead?

The callback is never invoked (the server is listening, `'listening'` is emitted).

const server = createServer((req, res) => res.end('ok'))
server.on('upgrade', (_req, socket) => {
  socket.write('HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nUpgrade: test\r\n\r\n')
  socket.on('data', (d) => socket.write(d))
})
await new Promise<void>((r) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => r()))
const port = (server.address() as any).port

// Client: upgrade, echo one chunk, then destroy the client socket.
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
  const req = request({ hostname: '127.0.0.1', port, path: '/', headers: { connection: 'Upgrade', upgrade: 'test' } })
  req.on('upgrade', (_res, socket) => {
    socket.once('data', () => { socket.destroy(); resolve() })
    socket.write('x')
  })
  req.end()
})

const t = setTimeout(() => { console.log('HANG: close never completed'); process.exit(1) }, 3000)
server.getConnections((_e, n) => console.log('connections', n))
server.closeAllConnections()
server.close(() => { console.log('closed OK'); clearTimeout(t) })
```

### What is the expected behavior?

As in Node.js and bun ≤ 1.4.2: the server-side upgraded socket emits `'close'` once the peer tears the connection down, the connection count drops to 0, and `server.close()` calls back:

```
$ ~/bun-1.4.2/bin/bun repro.ts
connections 1
closed OK
```

### What do you see instead?

```
$ bun repro.ts   # 1.4.3
connections 1
HANG: close never completed
```

The server-side upgraded socket receives `'end'` (`readyState === 'writeOnly'`) but never `'close'`; `socket.destroyed` stays `false`, `server.closeAllConnections()` does not close it, and `server.close()` waits forever. Explicitly calling `socket.destroy()` on the server-side upgraded socket makes `close()` complete, so the socket is never released from the server's connection tracking on its own.

### Additional information

Plain request/response connections (including keep-alive via `http.Agent({ keepAlive: true })` and `fetch`) are unaffected — only connections that went through `'upgrade'` hang. This broke a WebSocket-proxy test suite's `afterAll` (`server.close()` timing out) on CI when `setup-bun` picked up 1.4.3.

title: bun fmt: bring back the built-in Svelte formatter
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

In a Svelte app most of the code is in `.svelte` files, and `bun fmt` doesn't format them itself: it hands them to the project's Prettier with `prettier-plugin-svelte`. So the speedup barely reaches a Svelte project, and `prettier` and the plugin have to stay installed. Without them, `.svelte` files are left as they are and the run exits with code 2. The same happens with an `.oxfmtrc.json` that enables `svelte`.

On [sveltejs/svelte.dev](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte.dev/tree/73e3222) (557 `.svelte` files, 305 `.js`/`.ts` files), `--check` with its Prettier config, 32 threads, `1.4.4-canary.1+11b450ca9` (where the command is still `bun format`), prettier 3.9.10, prettier-plugin-svelte 4.1.1:

| Files | `bun format --check` | `prettier --check` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 305 `.js`/`.ts` | 0.01 s | 0.71 s |
| 557 `.svelte` | 1.56 s (handed to Prettier) | 1.66 s |

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Built-in Svelte formatting in `bun fmt`, as Vue and Angular already have.

For a while #44805 had it: [`src/format/svelte`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/44805/commits/8b333f338ab2cfc27c14e0966f3c3e1bff68f127), a port of `prettier-plugin-svelte` 4.1.1. [Its notes](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/8764039427964b6e9e4a757b397972c86caf4e9d/test/cli/format/oracle/svelte/README.md) report the same output as the plugin on 7,043 of 7,147 real components. It was taken out before the merge. If that was for good, fair enough; if it could come back, Svelte users would be glad to have it.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Keep handing `.svelte` files to Prettier, as now. It works, but at Prettier's speed, and Prettier stays a dependency.
- Format `.svelte` files with oxfmt, which means running a second formatter next to `bun fmt` for one language.

title: node:vm: overwriting a context property created by a top-level function/var declaration is not seen by code in the context
toMatchObject checks an expected object only where it first appears (Bun.deepMatch too)
excerpt:
When one object appears more than once in a `toMatchObject` expectation, Bun compares it only where it first appears. If a later property doesn't match it, the test still passes.

### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Save this as `reused.test.ts` and run `bun test reused.test.ts`:

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("a reused expected object is checked at each place it appears", () => {
  const o = { x: 1 };
  expect({ a: { x: 1 }, b: { x: 2 } }).toMatchObject({ a: o, b: o });
});
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The test fails, because `b` is `{ x: 2 }` and its expectation is `{ x: 1 }`. It does fail when the expectation uses two separate objects, `toMatchObject({ a: { x: 1 }, b: { x: 1 } })`. `toEqual({ a: o, b: o })` fails too.

### What do you see instead?

The test passes.

### Additional information

- With the mismatch at the first appearance instead, `{ a: { x: 2 }, b: { x: 1 } }`, the test fails as it should.
- The same happens with the reused object nested one level deeper: `toMatchObject({ a: { q: o }, b: { q: o } })` passes against `{ a: { q: { x: 1 } }, b: { q: { x: 2 } } }`.
- `Bun.deepMatch({ a: o, b: o }, { a: { x: 1 }, b: { x: 2 } })` returns `true`, and so does the nested case.
- This is separate from oven-sh/bun#44405, where an expected `Date` or `Error` that differs passes. Here the trigger is the reuse itself, since the same values in separate objects fail as they should.

Hilda-2253 found this while checking that a test fails when the code under test is broken. A test that reused one expected object for two properties kept passing. A separate expected object for each property works around it.

Reported by Octavia-2298, from Hilda-2253's repro.

title: [tsgo-parity] `bun check`: reports false TS2322 when a generic function typed through a generic type alias is passed to a generic wrapper
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4-canary.1+5ee74f02a

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-1066-aws x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun check` reports TS2322 when a value of a generic-function type (declared through a generic alias `Id<string>`) is passed to a wrapper `wrap(f: (...a: P) => R): (...a: P) => R` and the result is assigned to the same alias type. tsc 5.9.3 and tsgo 7.0.2 keep the type parameter `T` (higher-order generic inference) and accept it.

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "target": "es2022",
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "types": []
  },
  "files": ["index.ts"]
}
```

`index.ts`:

```ts
type Id<A> = <T extends A>(a: T) => T;
declare function wrap<R, P extends any[]>(f: (...a: P) => R): (...a: P) => R;
declare const id: Id<string>;
export const x: Id<string> = wrap(id);
```

Command:

```sh
bun check -p tsconfig.json --threads 1
```

### What is the expected behavior?

No errors, like tsc and tsgo:

```
tsgo (Version 7.0.2): exit 0, no output
tsc  (Version 5.9.3): exit 0, no output
```

### What do you see instead?

```
index.ts(4,14): error TS2322: Type '(a: string) => string' is not assignable to type 'Id<string>'.
  Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'T'.
    'string' is assignable to the constraint of type 'T', but 'T' could be instantiated with a different subtype of constraint 'string'.
Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 64 files [207.39ms]
```

### Additional information

This issue was distilled from running bun check for parity and performance on a large internal monorepo.
Reproduction was done with help of CLaue Opus 5.5 - but I've validated the reproudction. 

---
Furhter LLM context:

Suspected cause: when inferring `P`/`R` from an argument whose type comes from an instantiated generic alias, bun's checker does not apply the higher-order generic function inference (which keeps `T` as a type parameter in the returned signature). It resolves `T` to its constraint instead, so `(a: string) => string` is checked against `<T extends string>(a: T) => T`.

This remains after PR #45097 (tested on 1.4.4-canary.1+5ee74f02a, which includes it).

title: `bun lint`: JavaScript plugin rules get no type information on TypeScript files with `projectService`
`bun lint`, `bun check`: native support for framework components (Vue, Svelte, Astro), as `bun fmt` has
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bun fmt` formats framework components natively: Vue and Angular already, Svelte with #45146. `bun lint` and `bun check` don't yet. In `bun lint`, a `.vue`, `.svelte` or `.astro` file only gets its `<script>` linted with an oxlint config, and with an ESLint config it is handed to the installed ESLint and its framework plugin. `bun check` reads `.ts`/`.js` files only, so components still need `vue-tsc`, `svelte-check` or `astro check`.

So in a framework project, most of the speedup doesn't reach the files where most of the code is. Our SvelteKit app as an example (1,556 files, 577 of them `.svelte`):

| | `.ts`/`.js` (929 files) | `.svelte` (577 files) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bun fmt --check` (with #45146) | native | native: 0.58s for everything, against 23.7s for Prettier, same output |
| `bun lint` | native, 1.3s | handed to ESLint (`svelte-eslint-parser` + `eslint-plugin-svelte`): nearly all of the 36.7s of the run |
| `bun check` | native | not read: still `svelte-check` |

`eslint`, `typescript-eslint` and the framework plugins have to stay installed, as does the framework's type checker.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Native support for components in both, as `bun fmt` has:

- **`bun lint`**: parse components natively, markup included, and port the framework plugins' rules, at least their `recommended` sets, the way the React rules were ported: `eslint-plugin-vue`, `eslint-plugin-svelte`, `eslint-plugin-astro`.
- **`bun check`**: type check components, as `vue-tsc`, `svelte-check` and `astro check` do (each turns a component into TypeScript, e.g. `svelte2tsx`, then runs the type checker on it).

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Keep handing components to the installed ESLint. It works, at ESLint's speed.
- Keep running the framework's type checker next to `bun check`.

title: `[lint.categories]` turns on every built-in plugin, and bunfig cannot turn a plugin off
excerpt: ### What version of Bun is running? 1.4.4-canary.1+40e03510d ### What platform is your computer? Linux 7.2.5-3-omarchy x86_64 ### What steps can reproduce the bug? Configuring `[lint.categories]` automatically enables rules from **every** built-in plugin (including `nextjs`, `jest`, `vitest`, `react-perf`, and `n`), even if the project doesn't use those frameworks or tools. For example, in a plain React project without Next.js: 1. Setting categories to `"error"` reports `` as `@next/next/no-img-element` and triggers `jest/require-hook` and `vitest/require-hook` on regular application code. 2. `nativePluginRules` does not restrict which plugins run. Using the config below still reports `@next/next/no-img-element`, `n/no-sync`, and `jsx-a11y/alt-text`: ```toml [lint] nativePluginRules = ["import", "react", "react-hooks", "@typescript-eslint"] [lint.categories] correctness = "error" ``` ### What is the expected behavior? `bunfig.toml` should provide a way to control which built-in plugins are active (similar to existing CLI flags like `--nextjs-plugin` or `--disable-unicorn-plugin`), taking precedence over `[lint.categories]`. Two possible solutions: **Option 1: Explicitly enable plugins (opt-in)** Only run rules from the specified plugins: ```toml [lint] plugins = ["import", "react", "react-hooks", "@typescript-eslint"] ``` **Option 2: Explicitly disable plugins (opt-out)** Turn off all current and future rules from unwanted plugins: ```toml [lint] disablePlugins = ["nextjs", "react-perf", "jest", "vitest"] ``` ### What do you see instead? Currently, the only workaround in `bunfig.toml` is disabling every unwanted plugin rule individually: ```toml [lint.rules] "nextjs/google-font-display" = "off" "nextjs/google-font-preconnect" = "off" "nextjs/no-img-element" = "off" # ... 18+ more rules just for Next.js ``` This requires listing 21 rules just to silence Next.js, and breaks whenever a future Bun release adds a new rule to an unused plugin.

title: `node:sqlite`: read-only query fails on macOS after closing a WAL-mode database without sidecars
Bun.markdown: table column alignment is mis-attributed when a document has more than one table
excerpt:
### What is the problem?

`Bun.markdown` mis-attributes per-column table alignment when a single document contains more than one table. Each table's alignment should come from its own delimiter row, but a second table corrupts the first table's alignment — and, in the reverse order, a table with **no** alignment in its source borrows the alignment of the aligned table.

### Version

Bun 1.4.0 (macOS arm64)

### Reproduction

```js
const A = "| L | C | R |\n| :--- | :---: | ---: |\n| left | centre | right |";
const U = "| a | b |\n| --- | --- |\n| 1 | 2 |";   // no colons: no alignment

console.log(Bun.markdown.html(A));
console.log(Bun.markdown.html(A + "\n\n" + U));
console.log(Bun.markdown.html(U + "\n\n" + A));
```

### Actual

1. `A` alone — correct:

   `<th align="left">L</th><th align="center">C</th><th align="right">R</th>`

2. `A` **followed by** `U` — the first table loses `left` and `center`; only `right` survives:

   `<th>L</th><th>C</th><th align="right">R</th>`

3. `U` **followed by** `A` — the first table (which has no alignment in its source at all) is handed `left`/`center`, borrowed from the second table:

   `<th align="left">a</th><th align="center">b</th>`

### Expected

Each table's alignment is derived from its own delimiter row and is unaffected by any other table in the document: case 2 should be identical to case 1, and case 3 should produce no `align` attributes on the first table.

### Notes

- No callbacks are involved; `Bun.markdown.html()` is enough to see it.
- It also breaks `Bun.markdown.render()`: the `align` passed in `th`/`td` `CellMeta` is wrong in the same way (e.g. `{ align: "left" }` arrives for a table whose delimiter row has no colons). That is how I hit it — a renderer that honours `meta.align` paints every column left in any document with two or more tables.
- Deterministic and minimal (two tables). `Bun.markdown.ansi()` uses the same parser and would presumably be affected too; I have not tested it.
- I searched the tracker for a prior report of this and found none (the open "alignment" issues are all `console.table`).

title: jsdom >= 30.1 breaks vitest jsdom environment: 'addEventListener' called on an object that is not a valid instance of EventTarget
excerpt:
**Bun version:** 1.4.3 (x64 Linux)
**jsdom:** regression between 30.0.0 (works) and 30.1.0 (fails); still failing on 30.1.2
**vitest:** 4.1.11 and 5.0.4 both affected
**Node:** same repro passes under Node 25.9.0, so this is Bun-specific

## Repro

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro
bun add -d vitest@5.0.4 jsdom@30.1.2
cat > repro.test.js <<'EOF'
// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { test, expect } from "vitest";
test("window works", () => { expect(window).toBeDefined(); });
EOF
bun x --bun vitest run repro.test.js   # fails
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run repro.test.js  # passes
```

## Failure

```
Error: [vitest-pool]: Failed to start forks worker for test files .../repro.test.js
Caused by: TypeError: 'addEventListener' called on an object that is not a valid instance of EventTarget.
 ❯ requireImplForWrapper jsdom/lib/generated/idl/utils.js:144:28
 ❯ addEventListener jsdom/lib/generated/idl/EventTarget.js:102:21
 ❯ catchWindowErrors vitest/dist/chunks/index.*.js
```

## Suspected mechanism

jsdom 30.1 reworked its webidl wrappers to stamp instances with private fields (`WrapperData.#impl`, checked via `#impl in wrapper`). Vitest's jsdom environment populates the worker global from the jsdom window and wraps `window.addEventListener` (`catchWindowErrors`). Under Bun, the bound/wrapped call reaches the brand check with a `this` that fails `#impl in wrapper` — plausibly a cross-realm or proxy object whose private-field brand doesn't survive Bun's fork-worker realm boundary. Under Node the same vitest code passes.

This currently forces projects running vitest under Bun to pin jsdom to 30.0.x.

title: [tsgo-parity] `bun check`: assignment inside a `for…of` loop is lost after the loop (`T | null = null` narrows to `null`), false TS2339 on `never`
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3 (also reproduces on the 1.4.4 canary)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux aarch64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

In a large project (~1.8k root files), `bun check` reports a TS2339 on `never` that `tsc` 7.0.2 does not report (`tsc` gives 0 errors with the default settings, `--checkers 1` and `--singleThreaded`).

The code has this shape. Identifiers are renamed; the structure is the original:

```ts
type Result = { next?: { id: string }; done: boolean }
declare function fetchStatus(id: string): Promise<Result | null> // explicit return type

// inside a long async arrow function passed to a builder method,
// whose return type is inferred and includes `isDone`
let isDone: boolean | undefined
if (items.length > 0) {
  let best: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof fetchStatus>> | null = null
  for (const item of items) {
    const id = (item as { id?: string }).id
    if (!id) continue
    const r = await fetchStatus(id)
    if (r?.next) best = r
  }
  isDone = best?.done
  if (best?.next) {
    const { id } = best.next // bun check: TS2339 Property 'next' does not exist on type 'never'
  }
}
return { isDone }
```

### What is the expected behavior?

No error, same as `tsc` 7.0.2. Right after the loop, the flow type of `best` should be `Result | null`.

### What do you see instead?

`error TS2339: Property 'next' does not exist on type 'never'.`

If I put a probe (`const p: 0 = best`) right after the loop, it shows that bun's flow type there is `null`, while `tsc` reports `Result | null`. Inside the loop, both agree. So the assignment inside the loop body looks lost after the loop, and the declared `T | null` stays narrowed to the initializer `null`.

### Additional information

The bug is deterministic, but it depends on which other files are checked in the same run:

- Checked as the only root file: no error.
- Full project: error, with the default threads and also with `--threads=1`.
- Bisecting the root files with `--threads=1`: a fixed prefix of 1812 roots plus the file gives no error. Adding one trivial extra root (`export const tiny = { a: 1 }`) gives the error. Adding a large unrelated root (about 60k lines) instead gives no error. No single file triggers it.
- Adding unrelated statements near the loop can make the TS2339 disappear, while the post-loop flow type stays `null`.

It looks like the flow type at the loop label gets cached while it is still incomplete, holding only the pre-loop antecedent.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`m.ts`:

```ts

const B = 2;
const C = 3;

export function unused(x: number): number {
  return x + B;
}
```

`m.test.ts`:

```ts

import * as m from "./m";
test("import", () => expect(typeof m.unused).toBe("function"));
```

```sh
bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov
grep ^DA: coverage/lcov.info
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Lines 2 and 3 ran at module load, so they have hits. Only the body of `unused` is uncovered. Node 24.21 (`node --test --experimental-test-coverage`) reports lines 1-5 as hit and 6-7 as 0.

### What do you see instead?

```
DA:1,12
DA:2,0
DA:3,0
DA:4,0
DA:5,0
```

Lines 2-4 report 0 hits although they ran.

### Additional information

- Trigger: a `const` whose initializer Bun's transpiler inlines (string, number including negative and hex, boolean, `null`, `undefined`, a template with no substitutions, or any of these `as const`), referenced from a function that is never called and that starts after the declaration.
- Every line from the `const` declaration to the end of the uncalled function reports 0. That includes executed module-level statements and the bodies of other functions that did run.
- The declaration can be at any scope. A local `const` in a called function, used by a nested uncalled arrow, zeroes the executed lines between the `const` and the arrow.
- `const B = Number(2)`, `let`, `var`, `1n`, `"a" + "b"` and `new Set(...)` do not trigger it. An unexecuted branch inside a function that ran does not trigger it either.
- `new Bun.Transpiler({ loader: "ts", inline: true })` turns `x + B` into `x + 2`. My guess (not verified in the source): the inlined literal keeps the source location of the declaration, so the uncalled function's line range, which the coverage report marks as uncovered, starts at the declaration line.

title: Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone") omits legacy zone names that Intl.DateTimeFormat accepts
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const zones = Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")

console.log("Europe/Kiev listed:", zones.includes("Europe/Kiev"))
console.log("Europe/Kyiv listed:", zones.includes("Europe/Kyiv"))
console.log("Asia/Calcutta listed:", zones.includes("Asia/Calcutta"))
console.log("Asia/Kolkata listed:", zones.includes("Asia/Kolkata"))

// both spellings format fine:
console.log(new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { timeZone: "Europe/Kiev" }).format(new Date()))
console.log(new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { timeZone: "Asia/Calcutta" }).format(new Date()))
```

Output:

```
Europe/Kiev listed: false
Europe/Kyiv listed: true
Asia/Calcutta listed: false
Asia/Kolkata listed: true
14/10/2026
14/10/2026
```

### What is the bug?

`Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")` lists only one spelling per zone — here the post-rename one (`Europe/Kyiv`, `Asia/Kolkata`) — and omits the alias spelling (`Europe/Kiev`, `Asia/Calcutta`) even though `Intl.DateTimeFormat` accepts it and formats correctly, and `resolvedOptions()` echoes it back unchanged.

The same holds for every tzdb rename: `America/Godthab`, `Asia/Rangoon` and `Pacific/Enderbury` are absent from the list while their renamed identifiers are present. (Bun lists 445 zones; V8 lists 418, and picks the opposite spelling of every renamed pair.)

### What do you expect to see instead?

The list and the formatter should agree. A zone name the engine accepts and formats with should be listed — or the list should carry both the canonical and the legacy spelling.

### Why this matters

Zone names arrive from other systems with their own ICU data. Chromium (V8) reports `Europe/Kiev` for Ukraine, and its own list contains that spelling while omitting `Europe/Kyiv` — the exact opposite of Bun. Validating a client-supplied zone against `supportedValuesOf` therefore rejects a valid name; in our case the value silently fell back to UTC for members in Ukraine and India.

title: build: external --build-dir loses the source root during Ninja regeneration
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

`1.4.2+744846f84` as the build bootstrap. The target source was `60acc08cd91687380b03cb16a682ff85f1ec1500`; the failure occurs before the target executable runs.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux aarch64, Debian 13.7 (trixie), glibc 2.41.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

With native build prerequisites installed, start from a source checkout and select an output directory beside it:

```sh
cd /tmp/bun-source
bun bd --build-dir=/tmp/bun-build
```

Initial configuration succeeds. When Ninja invokes the generated reconfigure edge, repository discovery fails because its working directory is the external build directory. The paths above are generic placeholders for the observed layout.

### What is the expected behavior?

An explicitly supplied external build directory retains the source-checkout identity during regeneration. `validateBunConfig()` explicitly permits this layout; it separately rejects symlinked build directories shared between worktrees.

### What do you see instead?

```text
[3/4] reconfigure
FAILED: [code=1] build.ninja
bun <source>/scripts/build.ts --config-file=configure.json
error: Could not find bun repository root
  hint: Run this from within the bun repository
ninja: error: rebuilding build.ninja: subcommand failed
```

The original command was started inside the source checkout. Keeping the build directory beneath that checkout lets the same frozen source build successfully.

### Additional information

Checked upstream main `408c9374b266b45fe6b8260e09be73aa82a957cd` on October 14, 2026. The four implicated build files are byte-identical to the observed source. Current main was inspected, not rebuilt.

- [`scripts/build/bun.ts:982`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/408c9374b266b45fe6b8260e09be73aa82a957cd/scripts/build/bun.ts#L982) explicitly permits external output directories.
- [`scripts/build/configure.ts:225`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/408c9374b266b45fe6b8260e09be73aa82a957cd/scripts/build/configure.ts#L225) persists profile/overrides and emits the regen command without restoring the source cwd.
- [`scripts/build/config.ts:1498`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/408c9374b266b45fe6b8260e09be73aa82a957cd/scripts/build/config.ts#L1498) finds the repository only by walking ancestors of the current working directory.

The source identity should survive configure/replay for both native and codegen builds, while retaining the existing shared-worktree symlink guard.

child_process: piping into a child whose stdin is O_NONBLOCK truncates the stream with EPIPE (Bun 1.3.14, Linux)
excerpt:
When a child process sets O_NONBLOCK on its stdin, as ssh does, piping another child's stdout into it with `.pipe()` loses data. Bun emits EPIPE on the writable and stops writing while the reader is still alive and reading. Node delivers every byte.

I ran into this piping a stream into `ssh`.

Repro on Linux x64, Bun 1.3.14:

```js
import { spawn } from "node:child_process"
const reader = `import os, fcntl, sys, time
fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
fcntl.fcntl(fd, fcntl.F_SETFL, fcntl.fcntl(fd, fcntl.F_GETFL) | os.O_NONBLOCK)
n = 0
while True:
    try:
        b = os.read(fd, 65536)
    except BlockingIOError:
        time.sleep(0.01); continue
    if not b: break
    n += len(b)
print(n)`
const producer = spawn("head", ["-c", "20000000", "/dev/zero"], { stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "ignore"] })
const consumer = spawn("python3", ["-c", reader], { stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "inherit"] })
consumer.stdin.on("error", (e) => console.log("stdin error:", e.message))
producer.stdout.pipe(consumer.stdin)
let out = ""
consumer.stdout.on("data", (c) => (out += c))
consumer.on("close", () => console.log(`received ${out.trim()} of 20000000`))
```

Bun 1.3.14:
```
stdin error: EPIPE: broken pipe, write
received 11377408 of 20000000
```
Node 22:
```
received 20000000 of 20000000
```

How much arrives varies from run to run, between about 0.8 and 11 MB. With ssh as the reader it's often under 2 MB. The O_NONBLOCK flag is what triggers it: the same reader without the `fcntl` line receives everything. Writing a whole Buffer with `stdin.end(buf)` works, and so does piping into a reader whose stdin stays blocking, such as `wc -c`. I haven't looked into where in Bun this happens.

Workaround: connect the two children with a kernel pipe (`sh -c 'producer | consumer'`) so the data never goes through Bun.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3 (1.4.2+744846f84 and canary 1.4.4-canary.1+408c9374b behave the same)

### What platform is your computer?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

}

```sh

```

The same error happens when the stylesheet is linked from an HTML file served through `Bun.serve({ routes: { "/": index } })`. That means a third-party stylesheet that uses this query cannot be bundled at all.

### What is the expected behavior?

The `@container` rule is parsed and emitted. Chrome and Edge support scroll-state container queries since version 133. lightningcss parses them since parcel-bundler/lightningcss@220b39039d83d1d5e9c488c21242bede49834a97 (released in v1.31.0, see parcel-bundler/lightningcss#1128 and parcel-bundler/lightningcss#1135).

```

              ^
error: Unexpected token: scroll-state(
    at style.css:3:11
```

### Additional information

The container condition parser recognises only one function, `style()`. Any other function token is reported as unexpected:

- [`parse_query_condition_with_options`, media_query.rs L1504-L1529](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/b92e2f4704824ad8f28509bda363989add0818c7/src/css/media_query.rs#L1504-L1529)
- [`parse_parens_or_function`, media_query.rs L1575-L1594](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/b92e2f4704824ad8f28509bda363989add0818c7/src/css/media_query.rs#L1575-L1594)
- [`ContainerCondition`, container.rs L196-L210](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/b92e2f4704824ad8f28509bda363989add0818c7/src/css/rules/container.rs#L196-L210) has variants for size features, `not`/`and`/`or` and `style()`, but none for scroll state.

A fix would port the scroll-state query from the lightningcss commit above (`stuck`, `snapped`, `scrollable`).

`use-intl@4.14.9` was published at 2026-10-02T11:05:33Z. Its dependency `icu-minify@^4.14.9` was published 3.5 minutes later, at 11:09:00Z. Setting the gate to a moment between the two makes the failure deterministic:

```sh
mkdir mra && cd mra
echo '{ "dependencies": { "use-intl": "^4.14.8" } }' > package.json

# gate = "published before 2026-10-02T11:07:00Z"
AGE=$(( $(date -u +%s) - $(date -u -d 2026-10-02T11:07:00Z +%s) ))
bun install --minimum-release-age=$AGE
```

With `"use-intl": "4.14.8"` and the same gate, the install succeeds and gets `icu-minify@4.14.8`.

### What is the expected behavior?

`^4.14.8` resolves to `use-intl@4.14.8`, because that version and all of its dependencies pass the gate. If Bun does not want to backtrack, the error should at least say which package required the blocked one.

### What do you see instead?

```
error: No version matching "icu-minify" found for specifier "^4.14.9" (blocked by minimum-release-age: 859333 seconds)
error: icu-minify@^4.14.9 failed to resolve
```

### Additional information

The gate checks each package by its own publish time. For `use-intl`, it picks the newest version that passes. It does not check whether that version's dependencies can be resolved under the same gate. When one of them cannot, `TooRecentVersion` turns into a hard error, and Bun never tries the next older dependent:

- [`search_version_list`, npm.rs L1578-L1645](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/b92e2f4704824ad8f28509bda363989add0818c7/src/install/npm.rs#L1578-L1645). The stability check there only compares versions of the same package.
- [the `TooRecentVersion` error, PackageManagerEnqueue.rs L961-L995](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/b92e2f4704824ad8f28509bda363989add0818c7/src/install/PackageManager/PackageManagerEnqueue.rs#L961-L995)

This affects packages from one monorepo that a release script publishes one after another (`next-intl`, `use-intl`, `icu-minify` here). For a few seconds or minutes after the gate expires, every install that resolves from scratch fails, for example a Docker build without a lockfile. We hit it in CI with a 3-day gate: `next-intl@4.14.6` was 6 s past the gate, and `icu-minify@4.14.6`, published 14 s after it, was still 8 s short. The next build, a few hours later, passed w

### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3 (1.4.2+744846f84 behaves the same)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`worker.ts`:

```ts
declare var self: Worker;
const log = (m: string) => postMessage(m);

self.addEventListener("unhandledrejection", (e: any) => { log("self: " + e.reason); e.preventDefault(); });
globalThis.addEventListener("unhandledrejection", (e: any) => { log("globalThis: " + e.reason); e.preventDefault(); });
(globalThis as any).onunhandledrejection = (e: any) => log("onunhandledrejection: " + e.reason);

Promise.reject(new Error("boom"));
setTimeout(() => log("worker still alive"), 100);
```

`main.ts`:

```ts
const w = new Worker(new URL("./worker.ts", import.meta.url).href);
w.onmessage = (e) => console.log("[main]", e.data);
w.onerror = (e) => { console.log("[main] worker error event"); e.preventDefault(); };
w.addEventListener("close", (e: any) => console.log("[main] worker closed, code", e.code));
setTimeout(() => w.terminate(), 500);
```

```sh
bun main.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

As in browsers and Deno, a `PromiseRejectionEvent` named `unhandledrejection` is dispatched on the worker's global scope (HTML spec, "notify about rejected promises"). The listener runs, `preventDefault()` marks the rejection as handled, and the worker keeps running. Deno rejects classic workers, so to run the repro there, `main.ts` needs `new Worker(url, { type: "module" })`; with that change, Deno 2.9.7 prints all three handler lines followed by `worker still alive`:

```
[main] self: Error: boom
...
[main] worker still alive
```

### What do you see instead?

None of the three handlers runs, with or without `type: "module"`. The rejection is treated as unhandled and the worker exits:

```
[main] worker error event
[main] worker closed, code 1
```

Only `process.on("unhandledRejection", …)` inside the worker sees the rejection. With that listener, the worker survives. The main thread behaves the same: `globalThis.addEventListener("unhandledrejection", …)` is never called. `typeof PromiseRejectionEvent` is `"undefined"`.

title: Bun.serve process exits when an inspector client closes its connection right after opening it
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3, and 1.4.4-canary.1+6c1eb067e

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.8-arch1-2 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```ts
// server.ts
Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response() })
process.on('beforeExit', code => console.error('beforeExit', code))
```

```ts
// repro.ts
const child = Bun.spawn(['bun', './server.ts'], { env: { ...process.env, BUN_INSPECT: 'ws://localhost:9229/x' }, stderr: 'inherit' })

for (const start = Date.now(); Date.now() - start < 1500 && child.exitCode === null;) {
  const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:9229/x')
  await new Promise(resolve => { ws.onopen = resolve; ws.onerror = resolve })
  ws.close() // closed as soon as it opens
  await Bun.sleep(5)
}
await Bun.sleep(300)
console.log('server exit code:', child.exitCode)
child.kill()
```

```sh
bun repro.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`server exit code: null`: the server is still listening, so its process keeps running whatever inspector clients come and go.

### What do you see instead?

```
beforeExit 0
server exit code: 0
```

`beforeExit` fires in the server and the process exits with code 0 while `Bun.serve` is still listening, as if the event loop stopped counting the server. This happens in 10 of 10 runs on 1.4.4-canary.1 and in about 3 of 5 runs on 1.4.3.

### Additional information

- A client that sends one request and waits for its answer before closing never triggers it (0 of 10 runs under the same loop).
- A keep-alive `setInterval` in the server absorbs one such close but not several.
- Hit in practice by a dev server proxying debugger connections: a debugger UI probing the address and closing at once ends the app being debugged. The workaround is to close an inspector connection only after a `Runtime.evaluate` round trip.

Bun.spawn with terminal option hangs forever when the PTY child writes and exits before spawn returns (macOS)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (`bun --revision`: 1.4.2+744846f84)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.1 arm64 (macOS)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`Bun.spawn` with the `terminal` option sometimes never returns. It happens when the PTY child writes output and exits before `Bun.spawn` has returned.

```ts
// minimal.ts: run three copies at once
for (let i = 0; ; i++) {
  console.error('before-spawn', i);
  const child = Bun.spawn(['sh', '-c', 'printf tty'], { terminal: { cols: 80, rows: 24, data() {} } });
  await child.exited;
  child.terminal!.close();
}
```

```sh
bun minimal.ts & bun minimal.ts & bun minimal.ts & wait
```

Within a few dozen iterations, every copy stops printing for good. In my latest run they stopped at iterations 0, 5 and 5 and printed nothing more over 55 seconds.

### What is the expected behavior?

`Bun.spawn` returns, `exited` resolves, and the loop continues forever.

### What do you see instead?

The process hangs inside `Bun.spawn`. A log line placed right after the call is never printed for the iteration that hangs. Here is what we observed in the hung processes:

- `sample` shows the main thread blocked in `__wait4_nocancel`, called from JIT frames.
- The only child is the PTY child, in state `?NEs` (an exiting session leader).
- `lsof` shows Bun still holding the slave tty (`/dev/ttysNNN`) open next to its `/dev/ptmx` master.

Our guess, not proven, is that the exiting child cannot finish until its pending tty output is read, while the thread that would read it is blocked waiting for the child.

### Additional information

Which variants hang (three concurrent processes, about 30 s each):

| Variant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| inline `terminal: {…}`, child runs `printf tty` | hangs in 3 of 3 runs within 2 to 48 spawns |
| inline, child runs `exit 0` (no output) | no hang in 1,700 spawns |
| child sleeps 0.15 s before or after `printf` | no hang |
| pre-built `new Bun.Terminal(…)` passed as `terminal` | no hang in about 3,800 spawns, but the child is not a session leader and has no controlling tty |
| pre-built `Bun.Terminal` with `detached: true` | still hangs, less often |

The rate goes up with host load. We work around it by having the child wait for a release signal sent after `Bun.spawn` returns, and only then `exec` the real command.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.3+c6da4a4d3. Also reproduced on 1.4.4-canary.1+a9c57bdd8, 1.3.9 and 1.2.23.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```js
const r = new Response("hello");
r.body.getReader().releaseLock();
console.log("bodyUsed:", r.bodyUsed);
console.log("text():", await r.text());
```

The same happens for every in-memory body, and for a `fetch()` response whose body has already arrived in full (a small JSON reply). A body backed by a JavaScript `ReadableStream` is not affected:

| Body | `bodyUsed` after `getReader().releaseLock()` (Bun) | `await r.text()` (Bun) | Node 26.11.1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| string | `true` | `TypeError: Body already used` | `false`, `"hello"` |
| `Uint8Array` | `true` | `TypeError: Body already used` | `false`, `"hello"` |
| `ArrayBuffer` | `true` | `TypeError: Body already used` | `false`, `"hello"` |
| `Blob` | `true` | `TypeError: Body already used` | `false`, `"hello"` |
| JS `ReadableStream` | `false` | `"hello"` | `false`, `"hello"` |

### What is the expected behavior?

```
bodyUsed: false
text(): hello
```

Acquiring a reader locks a stream but does not disturb it. In the Streams standard, `[[disturbed]]` is set only by [ReadableStreamDefaultReaderRead](https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readable-stream-default-reader-read), [ReadableStreamBYOBReaderRead](https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readable-stream-byob-reader-read), [ReadableStreamCancel](https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readable-stream-cancel) and [ReadableStreamPipeTo](https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readable-stream-pipe-to). After `releaseLock()` the body is neither disturbed nor locked, so it is not [unusable](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#body-unusable) and `text()` should resolve. Node 26.11.1 prints exactly that.

### What do you see instead?

```
bodyUsed: true
TypeError: Body already used
```

![The repro run on Bun 1.4.3 (bodyUsed true, text() throws TypeError: Body already used) and on Node v26.11.1 (bodyUsed false, text() returns hello)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3eda990-3e59-4894-a03d-559f903ffd79)

### Additional information

The cause looks like the lazy native source being materialized when the reader is acquired. `getReader()` calls `materializeIfNeeded()`, and `materializeNativeSource()` sets `stream->m_disturbed = true` before anything is read:

`ugly.ts` is skipped in all three runs, the way git (and `.gitignore` here) treats it. At minimum, `--ignore-path=.git/info/exclude` should apply the patterns in that file.

### What version of Bun is running?

### What platform is your computer?

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Put the two files below in one directory, then run:

```sh
BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_FORCE_WAITER_THREAD=1 bun test ./repro.test.ts --rerun-each=66
grep " lost " outcomes.log
```

The test spawns `/usr/bin/python3 -u plain.py` with piped stdin and stdout. The child reads one config line, writes three JSON lines and exits normally. The test reads stdout to EOF with a fatal `TextDecoder`, writes and ends stdin, then awaits `exited` with a 5 s bound. When that bound expires, the test checks with `ps` whether the child is a zombie owned by the bun process. If it is, the test logs a `lost` line and stops after three such lines.

There are three cases, which differ only in the bytes the child sends back: a valid UTF-8 sequence, an invalid byte, and an unfinished UTF-8 sequence (where the decoder's final flush throws).

`bun build` (with or without `--compile`) doesn't compose the source maps of its input files. If an input file is itself generated and carries a `//# sourceMappingURL`, the output's map, and the stack traces from a compiled binary, stop at that generated file. The runtime does honour the same input map, so only the bundler drops it.

```sh
mkdir -p src && cat > src/x.ts <<'TS'
type T = { n: number }
const pad: T = { n: 1 }

export function boom(): never {
  // the throw is on line 6 of the source
  throw new Error('boom ' + pad.n)
}
boom()
TS

# step 1: a generated file with a correct map back to src/x.ts
bun build src/x.ts --outdir step1 --sourcemap=linked --target=bun

node --enable-source-maps step1/x.js   # at boom (src/x.ts:6:9)    <- input map honoured
bun step1/x.js                         # at boom (src/x.ts:6:9)    <- input map honoured

# step 2: bundle / compile that generated file
bun build step1/x.js --outdir step2 --sourcemap=linked --target=bun
bun step2/x.js                         # at boom (step1/x.js:5:9)  <- stops at the input

bun build --compile --sourcemap step1/x.js --outfile app
./app                                  # at boom (step1/x.js:5:9)  <- stops at the input
```

### What is the expected behavior?

When an input file has a source map, `bun build` composes it into the output map (as the runtime already does when it runs the file), so `step2/x.js` and the compiled `./app` report `src/x.ts:6:9`.

### What do you see instead?

`step1/x.js:5:9`: the position in the intermediate file, which usually isn't shipped and whose name often carries a build hash.

### Additional information

This bites every framework that builds with Vite/Rollup/Nitro first and then hands the output to `bun build --compile` for a single-file binary: production stack traces name `.output/server/_ssr/<chunk>-<hash>.mjs:<line>` instead of the source file, even though correct maps for that step exist beside the chunks.

title: bun build --compile: build-time options to disable BUN_BE_BUN and BUN_OPTIONS in compiled executables
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

A code-signed `bun build --compile` executable is a trust boundary on macOS: keychain item ACLs and other OS checks key on the binary's signing identity. Today any local process can make such an executable run arbitrary JavaScript under that identity, and nothing at build time turns it off:

- `BUN_BE_BUN=1` makes the executable act as the full Bun CLI, ignoring its embedded entry. It is checked natively in `cli.zig`, before the standalone module graph loads, so the embedded app cannot refuse it.
- `BUN_OPTIONS` is folded into argv for the standalone graph too, so options like `--preload <file>` run caller code before the embedded entry.
- A `bunfig.toml` `preload` in the working directory had the same effect. That one now has a build-time switch (`--no-compile-autoload-bunfig`, see #44262), which is the precedent for this request.

Measured with Bun 1.4.x on a signed and notarized arm64 macOS build. A keychain item created by the embedded app's own code (through `Bun.secrets`) is ACL-pinned to the executable's signing requirement. Any later caller-supplied script run through either path above reads that item with no prompt, while an unrelated binary is refused.

`BUN_BE_BUN` is useful when an app deliberately exposes the Bun CLI. Apps that hold secrets under their signing identity need a way to opt out.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Build-time options for compiled executables, in the style of `--no-compile-autoload-dotenv` / `--no-compile-autoload-bunfig` (and `compile.autoload*` in `Bun.build`):

- `--no-compile-be-bun` (`compile: { allowBeBun: false }`): ignore `BUN_BE_BUN` and always run the embedded entry.
- `--no-compile-bun-options` (`compile: { allowBunOptions: false }`): ignore `BUN_OPTIONS` (and any other env-sourced runtime flags) for the embedded entry.

The default can stay as it is today. Ideally the choice is recorded in the standalone module graph header, so a packaged artifact can be checked after the build.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Checking in the embedded entry: it never runs on these paths, because both are decided natively first.
- Shipping a separately signed stock `bun` for script work and keeping secrets under the app's identity only. That is our mitigation, but it doesn't make the compiled executable itself safe to sign.
- Patching Bun downstream: possible, but every app that signs a compiled executable would carry the same

title: bun fmt is not idempotent: a second run changes the output again (TS object-union return type)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4-canary.1+5f5799ed1

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-142-lowlatency x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Create `repro.ts`:

```ts
class A {
  m(
    a: string,
  ): { aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa: number, bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb: number, cccccccccccccccccc: number } | null {
    return null
  }
}
```

Then run the formatter twice:

```sh
bun fmt repro.ts          # first pass
bun fmt --check repro.ts  # exits 1: "1 file needs formatting"
bun fmt repro.ts          # second pass changes the file again
bun fmt --check repro.ts  # now exits 0
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun fmt` should be idempotent: one pass should reach a stable result, so `bun fmt --check` passes immediately after `bun fmt`.

### What do you see instead?

The first pass keeps the parameter list broken, and the second pass joins it back onto one line:

```diff
 class A {
-  m(
-    a: string,
-  ): {
+  m(a: string): {
     aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa: number;
     bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb: number;
     cccccccccccccccccc: number;
   } | null {
     return null;
   }
 }
```

Full transcript:

```
$ bun fmt repro.ts
repro.ts
Formatted 1 file, 0 unchanged [69.29ms]
$ bun fmt --check repro.ts
repro.ts
1 file needs formatting. Run bun fmt to fix it.
exit=1
$ bun fmt repro.ts
repro.ts
Formatted 1 file, 0 unchanged [41.50ms]
$ bun fmt --check repro.ts
1 file is formatted.
exit=0
```

### Additional information

- On this input, `bun fmt` currently matches `prettier@3.9.10` **byte-for-byte, pass by pass** (verified with the Prettier CLI on a `.ts` file, default options). This is the known upstream bug prettier/prettier#19968 (`area:idempotency`), which has two PRs in flight (#19970, #19971) but no released fix yet. Filing it here so the fix can be ported when Prettier ships it — and in case stability of `--check` right after `fmt` is considered desirable independently of parity.
- The upstream minimal reproduction requires a generic wrapper (`B<{ … }>`); this variant needs no generic — an object type literal in a **union** return type triggers it too.
- User-visible impact: running `bun fmt` once in a pre-commit hook (as the docs suggest) can leave files that fail `bun fmt --check` in CI on the very next step.

hi
