title: Bun.spawnSync never returns: worker spins at 100% CPU beside an exited, unreaped child under a long parallel `bun test` run
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.2 (linux x64). The 1.4.3 release notes name no fix; not tested on 1.4.3.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.1 x86_64 (Fedora 44)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

No minimal repro yet; it shows only in a large suite:

```sh
setsid bun test --parallel=7 --timings=unit-timings.json ./src
```

The suite is about 1,300 files and 4,700 tests, many of which run `git` through `Bun.spawnSync` (piped stdout, often with a timeout), mixed with async `Bun.spawn` children. About 1 full run in 17 has one worker that never finishes its file (3 in about 51 runs; 1 in 25 in a second batch).

What did **not** reproduce it:
- 28 processes each making 3,000 `Bun.spawnSync(["git","--version"])` calls (piped, with a timeout, and plain), each keeping 2 async `Bun.spawn` children in flight: 336k calls, 0 hangs.
- The same pattern as 7 test files under `bun test --parallel=7`: about 78k calls, 0 hangs.

### What is the expected behavior?

`Bun.spawnSync` returns once its child exits.

### What do you see instead?

- The worker is in state R at 100% CPU and stays there (35 minutes in one capture, until killed).
- `/proc` shows its child (`git`, or `mkfifo`) as a zombie (Z): it exited and was never reaped.
- In every capture (3 of them) the program counter was in the same function of the 1.4.2 release binary (offset 0x19222xx), which looks like an atomic queue drain in spawnSync's isolated event loop. None of our code is on the stack.

### Additional information

- `BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_SPAWNSYNC_FAST_PATH` does not apply: piped stdout never takes the fast path (`js_bun_spawn_bindings.rs:1022`).
- Node's `child_process.spawnSync` / `execSync` / `execFileSync` in Bun build on the same `Bun.spawnSync` (going by the binary's strings), so switching to them is no way around it.
- Workaround that held: no `Bun.spawnSync` at all (every child through async `Bun.spawn`): 0 hangs in 30 full runs, against 1 in 25 on the same tree before.
- One capture spun after its file's `afterAll` had run, so the stuck call was in a leftover async chain, not in a test body.

title: Sampling profiler: record the AsyncLocalStorage context with each sample, so CPU profiles can be attributed to requests
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

Today no production CPU profiler runs on Bun. The ones people use on Node are built on V8-only native addons: `dd-trace` and Grafana's `@pyroscope/nodejs` on `@datadog/pprof`, and `@sentry/profiling-node` on `@sentry/node-cpu-profiler`. #21348 and #19230 are users running into that. `bun:jsc`'s sampling profiler is the one thing that could replace them, and a server profiler built on it works: `startSamplingProfiler` plus a `samplingProfilerStackTraces()` drain every few seconds, encoded as pprof, gives correct flame graphs with function names and lines, on JIT and on AOT builds.

What it cannot do is say which request a sample belongs to, and that is what a server profile is read by. Datadog's code hotspots and endpoint profiling, Pyroscope's span profiles and Sentry's transaction profiles all filter or group the samples by request, trace or route. On Node they get that from V8, which records the current async context with every sample: dd-trace's wall profiler reads it back per sample (`asyncContextFrameEnabled` in `packages/dd-trace/src/profiling/profilers/wall.js`).

In Bun, nothing in JavaScript can recover it. The sampler runs on its own thread and records only a timestamp and frames, and `async_hooks.createHook({ before })` never fires, by design (header of `src/js/node/async_hooks.ts`). Matching samples to spans by timestamp is exact only while one request is in flight; with any concurrency, requests interleave at every `await` and the match becomes a guess.

With the context recorded per sample, every one of those tools could support Bun with a JavaScript-only adapter, and so could any framework that wants CPU time per route.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Capture the async context the JS thread is in when a sample is taken, and hand it back with that sample.

Bun already keeps that context in one engine slot, the same role V8's per-isolate slot plays:

- `JSGlobalObject::m_asyncContextData` (oven-sh/WebKit, [`Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSGlobalObject.h#L518`](https://github.com/oven-sh/WebKit/blob/5cfcac0fbf51/Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/JSGlobalObject.h#L518)), internal field 0, holds the current `AsyncLocalStorage` frame. The engine's promise operations snapshot and restore it around every reaction, and Bun's `AsyncContextFrame` / `AsyncContextScope` do the same for native callbacks ([`src/jsc/bindings/AsyncContextFrame.cpp`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bu

title: Please create a security advisory for Bun <=1.4.3
excerpt:
Hi there,

Bun, like much like of the OSS world, was affected by the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates. The impact of this is that every version of Bun prior to the latest one (1.4.4) is susceptible to traffic interception/MITM. This isn't easily mitigable without an upgrade, since `--use-system-ca` *unions* the system and bundled CA certs rather than *intersecting* them.

In the interest of helping people upgrade as quickly as possible, I think it would be helpful for Bun to publish a security advisory. I would recommend assigning it a "high" or "critical" severity, mirroring what other projects have done.

Prior art for similar advisories for this eMudhra CA compromise:

- uv: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/security/advisories/GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62
- certifi: https://github.com/certifi/python-certifi/security/advisories/GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2
- Go: CVE-2026-111943
- Rust:
    - https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0383.html
    - https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0381.html

title: `bun check` widens a callback's returned literal under `NoInfer` over `Api[K][P]` (false TS2322), which tsc 7.0.2 accepts
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4+38afee6c8

It also reproduces on 1.4.3 and on the canary `1.4.4-canary.1+963452075`.

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun check` widens a literal that a callback returns when the callback's contextual type is `NoInfer<…>` over an indexed access whose second type parameter is constrained by the first (`P extends keyof Api[K]`). tsc 7.0.2 and tsc 5.9.3 both accept the file.

Put these 3 files in a new, empty folder.

`package.json`

```json
{
  "private": true,
  "devDependencies": {
    "typescript": "7.0.2"
  }
}
```

`tsconfig.json`

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "module": "preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "noEmit": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "types": []
  },
  "files": ["case.ts"]
}
```

`case.ts`

```ts
type Api = { a: { b: 'on' | 'off' } };

declare function on<K extends keyof Api, P extends keyof Api[K]>(
  key: K,
  procedure: P,
  handler: NoInfer<() => Api[K][P]>,
): void;

on('a', 'b', () => 'on');
```

Then run these commands.

```sh
bun install
bun check --no-pretty
./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p .
```

What I found while reducing it:

- It needs both type parameters, with `P`'s constraint depending on `K`. With `P extends keyof Api['a']`, `bun check` accepts the file.
- It needs `NoInfer`. Without it, tsc reports the same error, which is expected because `P` is then inferred from the handler.
- The same thing happens for a property of a returned object: `() => ({ status: 'on' })` against `{ status: 'on' | 'off' }` reports `Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"off" | "on"'`.
- Putting the handler types in a mapped type first avoids it. `type All = { [K in keyof Api]: { [P in keyof Api[K]]: () => Api[K][P] } }` with `handler: NoInfer<All[K][P]>` passes in both checkers.

### What is the expected behavior?

No errors, as with tsc 7.0.2 and tsc 5.9.3. `NoInfer` keeps the handler from being an inference site, but it should still give the arrow function its contextual type once `K` and `P` are fixed from the first two arguments. The returned `'on'` would then keep its literal type.

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p .
$ echo $?
0
```

### What do you see instead?

```
$ bun check --no-pretty
case.ts(9,20): error TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"off" | "on"'.
Found 1 error in 1 file, checked 1 file [15.58ms]
```

### What version of Bun is running?

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64

### Servers

- StarRocks 4.1.1 (`starrocks/allin1-ubuntu:4.1.1`, handshake `8.0.33`)
- MySQL 8.0.46 (`mysql:8.0.46`)

Compared with mysql2 3.24.4.

### Motivation

We run a Bun service that talks to StarRocks, an OLAP database that speaks the MySQL wire protocol, through mysql2. We want to move to Bun.SQL. A lot already works on StarRocks, thanks to:
- legacy EOF (#28005)
- lossless LARGEINT / DECIMAL / BIGINT strings
- UTC DATETIME on both protocols
- multi-statement text
- the bounded statement cache
- per-query decode failures (#43323)

The gaps below are what still block the switch:
- §2–§5 reproduce on stock MySQL.
- §1 reproduces there only as the `prepare: false` throw; its 1295 needs StarRocks.
- §6–§7 are StarRocks wire quirks that mysql2 tolerates.

```sh
docker run -d --name mysql-bun -e MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=1 -p 3306:3306 mysql:8.0.46

```

### 1. Parameters can't be sent over the text protocol (`prepare: false` throws for MySQL)

StarRocks implements COM_STMT_PREPARE for SELECT only. Every other statement that takes a parameter fails with errno 1295 (`ER_UNSUPPORTED_PS`), and Bun.SQL offers no other way to bind one:

await sr.unsafe("INSERT INTO bun_repro.t VALUES (?, ?)", [1, "a"]);   // same 1295

// TypeError ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE: The property 'options.prepare' prepared: false is not supported in MySQL. Received false

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4 (38afee6c8)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25 arm64 (also reproduced on Linux x64 in GitHub Actions)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun check` 1.4.4 rejects an XState v5 nested state value passed to `snapshot.matches()` when the snapshot type depends on a type parameter. `tsc` and `bun check` 1.4.3 accept the same code.

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
bun add xstate@5.33.2 typescript
```

`repro.ts`:

```ts
import { setup, type SnapshotFrom } from 'xstate'

function createMachine<T extends { id: string }>() {
  return setup({ types: { context: {} as { items: Array<T> } } }).createMachine({
    context: { items: [] },
    initial: 'idle',
    states: {
      idle: {},
      reviewingHits: { initial: 'walking', states: { walking: {}, batch: {} } }
    }
  })
}

type Machine<T extends { id: string }> = ReturnType<typeof createMachine<T>>
type Snapshot<T extends { id: string }> = SnapshotFrom<Machine<T>>

export function step<T extends { id: string }>(snapshot: Snapshot<T>): boolean {
  return snapshot.matches('idle') || snapshot.matches({ reviewingHits: 'batch' })
}

export function stepConcrete(snapshot: Snapshot<{ id: string }>): boolean {
  return snapshot.matches({ reviewingHits: 'batch' })
}
```

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{ "files": ["repro.ts"], "compilerOptions": { "noEmit": true, "strict": true, "target": "ES2022", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "Bundler", "skipLibCheck": true } }
```

```sh
bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json             # exit 0
bunx bun@1.4.3 check -p tsconfig.json # exit 0
bunx bun@1.4.4 check -p tsconfig.json # exit 1
```

### What is the expected behavior?

No errors, matching `tsc` and Bun 1.4.3. The state value type is `"idle" | { reviewingHits: "batch" | "walking" }`.

### What do you see instead?

```
<error file="repro.ts" line="21" column="57" code="TS2322">
Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'undefined'.
```

Only the generic `step` fails; `stepConcrete` passes. The top-level string form `matches('idle')` passes too. The nested value type appears to resolve to `undefined` when the machine type comes from `ReturnType<typeof createMachine<T>>` with `T` unresolved.

### Additional information

Possibly related to the `bun check` performance rework in 1.4.4. Hit in a monorepo where it produced 14 false errors across two XState machines.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4+38afee6c8

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bun check` accepts `Box<string>` as `Box<number>` when `T` is used 100 object levels deep. tsc 7.0.2 rejects it. `bun -p process.versions.typescript` prints `7.0.2`.

The repro needs no dependencies. In an empty folder, create `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "module": "preserve",
    "noEmit": true,
    "types": []
  },
  "files": ["case.ts"]
}
```

Generate `case.ts`. It is 100 nested `{ next: ... }` levels around `T`:

```sh
bun -e 'const depth = Number(process.argv.at(-1)); await Bun.write("case.ts", `interface Box<T> {\n  value: ${"{ next: ".repeat(depth)}T${" }".repeat(depth)}\n}\n\ndeclare const source: Box<string>\nexport const target: Box<number> = source\n`)' 100
```

```ts
// case.ts, abbreviated
interface Box<T> {
  value: { next: { next: /* 97 more levels */ { next: T } } }
}

declare const source: Box<string>
export const target: Box<number> = source
```

Run:

```sh
bun check --no-pretty
bunx -p typescript@7.0.2 tsc -p . --pretty false
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun check` reports an error, because `string` is not assignable to `number`. tsc 7.0.2 reports:

```
case.ts(6,14): error TS2321: Excessive stack depth comparing types 'Box<?>' and 'Box<?>'.
case.ts(6,14): error TS2321: Excessive stack depth comparing types 'Box<string>' and 'Box<number>'.
```

### What do you see instead?

```
✓ No type errors in 83 files [87.87ms]
```

Exit code is `0`.

### Additional information

title: Runtime transpiler cache reuses ordinary-module output for bun test, skipping Vitest import mapping
excerpt:
## Description

A normal Bun process that loads a file importing `it` and `expect` from `vitest` can poison the runtime transpiler cache for a later `bun test` process. The later test entry has identical content but a different filename. It resolves real Vitest rather than Bun's test compatibility mapping and fails before registering the test.

This reproduces with Bun 1.4.2 and the latest release checked, Bun 1.4.4. A fresh runtime cache and `BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0` both pass. The result therefore depends on an earlier, separate process's cache state, not the test itself.

## Reproduction

Reproduction repo: https://github.com/schickling-repros/2026-10-bun-transpiler-cache-vitest-rewrite — it consists of `package.json`, `repro.test.ts`, and `repro.sh`. Run:

```bash
bash repro.sh
```

It installs exactly `vitest@3.2.4`, isolates `HOME` and all Bun cache locations under a fresh temporary directory, and performs these steps:

1. Run `bun test ./repro.test.ts` with a fresh runtime cache: passes.
2. Copy `repro.test.ts` byte-for-byte to `ordinary.ts`.
3. Run `bun -e 'await import("./ordinary.ts")'` with a second runtime cache: throws because real Vitest is being imported outside its runner. This error is expected; it still primes Bun's compilation cache.
4. Run `bun test ./repro.test.ts` with the cache from step 3: fails.
5. Run `BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0 bun test ./repro.test.ts`: passes.

The test's only executable code is:

```ts
import { it, expect } from "vitest";

it("registers through bun:test", () => {
  expect(1 + 1).toBe(2);
});
```

A trailing comment pads the source above 4 KiB so it is eligible for runtime caching. Removing that padding masks the bug. On Bun 1.4.2, a separate synthetic size sweep passed at 4095 total source bytes and failed at 4096 bytes after ordinary-module priming.

## Expected

Bun should not reuse an ordinary-module compilation when it changes the semantics of a test entry. `bun test` should perform its Vitest compatibility mapping regardless of the previous cache contents.

## Actual

Both tested Bun versions produce:

```text
Fresh cache:
 1 pass
 0 fail

Primed shared cache:
error: Vitest failed to access its internal state.
 0 pass
 1 fail
 1 error
Exit status: 1

BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0:
 1 pass
 0 fail
```

The script checks for this specific error and both passing controls; its overall exit status is zero when the bug is reproduced as expected.

## Versions

- Bun 1.4.2 (`744846f84`)

Build failure on rustc 1.99: core::mem::type_info::of removed (multi_array_list.rs)
excerpt:
## What happened

Building `bun` 1.4.4 from source with a newer Rust toolchain fails in
`src/collections/multi_array_list.rs`: `core::mem::type_info` no longer
provides the free function `of`.

```
error[E0425]: cannot find function `of` in module `type_info`
   --> src/collections/multi_array_list.rs:321:29
    |
321 |         let id = type_info::of::<T>();
    |                             ^^ not found in `type_info`
```

Same error at lines 355, 469, 474
(`f.type_id() == type_info::of::<F>()`).

Toolchain: `rustc 1.99.0`, `cargo 1.99.0`.

## Why you haven't seen it

`rust-toolchain.toml` pins `nightly-2026-09-15`, which still ships
`type_info::of`, so CI never exercises the removal. Any move to a newer
nightly (or a distro toolchain built from the 1.99 series) breaks the
build the same way.

## Context from the source

The file's own docs say the port deliberately uses
`type_info::of::<F>()` as "`TypeId::of` without the `'static` bound",
since reflected field ids are not `'static`-restricted. So the obvious
`TypeId::of` substitution changes the bounds the column-caller design
relies on — I'm filing this instead of guessing at a downstream patch.

## Ask

What is the intended migration for these four call sites on toolchains
where `type_info::of` is gone? If there is a new `core` API (or a
`Type::of`-style successor) you plan to move to when bumping the
pinned nightly, a pointer would let downstream carry a correct patch
in the meantime.

## Environment (downstream)

- openSUSE packaging of `bun` 1.4.4, system rustc 1.99.0 (no rustup
  toolchain in the build root, must build with the distro compiler).
- The crate builds cleanly with the pinned `nightly-2026-09-15`.

title: build(android): upgrade Android NDK from r27c to r30+ for prebuilt WebKit
excerpt:
### Summary

The prebuilt WebKit / JavaScriptCore archives for Android used by Bun are currently built with NDK r27c.

### Motivation

NDK r30 enables the `__fits_in_tail_padding` optimization in libc++ for `std::expected`, shifting the offset of `has_val` (from `0xE8` to `0xE2`). When downstream consumers (such as Termux) compile Bun against NDK r30+, this causes an ABI mismatch against the r27c WebKit prebuilts, leading to crashes at runtime unless custom libc++ overlay headers are injected.

Upgrading the NDK toolchain used to build WebKit prebuilts to NDK r30 or newer will align the ABI layout with modern Android toolchains and eliminate the need for downstream libc++ patches.

excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

When `bun add` or `bun install` brings in a newer version of a package that is already in `bun.lock`, Bun keeps the old copy for the existing dependents, even when the new version satisfies their ranges. The lockfile ends up with duplicates that `bun dedupe` could remove right away. npm collapses the same case to one copy.

Repro (Bun 1.4.4). The `minimumReleaseAge` step only simulates a lockfile that was resolved a while ago:

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{ "private": true, "dependencies": { "make-dir": "4.0.0" } }' > package.json
printf '[install]\nminimumReleaseAge = 31536000\n' > bunfig.toml
bun install --lockfile-only   # semver@7.7.3 (make-dir wants ^7.5.3)
rm bunfig.toml

bun add --lockfile-only semver
bun dedupe --check
```

```
~ semver 7.7.3 -> 7.8.5

1 duplicate version can be removed (checked 4 packages in bun.lock)
```

After `bun add semver`, `bun.lock` has `semver@7.8.5` at the root and `make-dir/semver@7.7.3` nested, although 7.8.5 satisfies `^7.5.3`. The same steps with npm 11 (`npm install --package-lock-only --before=2025-10-23`, then `npm install --package-lock-only semver`) leave a single `semver@7.8.5`.

In our monorepo (about 2,800 packages) this happens on roughly 1 in 17 lockfile-changing commits, always ones that add or upgrade dependencies. Duplicates went from 27 to 39 in under a month. Some of these duplicates are packages with module-level state (for example `@mui/utils` and `@radix-ui/react-dialog` contexts), where a second copy is a real bug rather than just extra disk usage.

The only way to keep the lockfile clean today is to gate CI on `bun dedupe --check` and ask people to run `bun dedupe` by hand after every dependency change.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Make lockfile-writing commands (`bun add`, `bun install`, `bun update`) leave `bun.lock` deduplicated. When a newly resolved version satisfies the ranges of existing dependents, move those edges onto it instead of keeping the old copy. Put another way, the lockfile these commands write should already be a fixed point of `bun dedupe`.

That could be the default, or opt-in through something like:

```toml
[install]
dedupe = true
```

### What alternatives have you considered?

- `bun dedupe --check` in CI, which we're adding now. It works, but it fails PRs after the fact for something the installer could have avoided.
- A pre-commit hook that runs `bun dedupe --lockfile-only` w

excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bun upgrade` shows only a raw byte count during download — no total, no speed, no percentage:

```
 $ bun --revision
1.4.4+38afee6c8
 $ bun upgrade --canary
Downloading [4272169]
```

This is a regression of #24266 (merged Nov 11, 2025), which used `std.fmt.fmtIntSizeBin` in `src/Progress.zig` (Zig) to produce:

```
Downloading [23.2MiB/47.2MiB]
```

The Zig → Rust rewrite dropped **both** the human-readable formatting **and** the total size — we now see only the bytes-downloaded count, with no total to compare against.

Problems:
1. **Hard to parse** — `4272169` is bytes; users must mentally convert to ~4.1MB.
2. **No total** — without a denominator, there's no way to know if this is 1% or 99% done.
3. **No speed** — can't distinguish a stalled download from a fast one.
4. **No signal on slow/metered networks** — only speed + percentage tell you whether to wait or abort.
5. **Inconsistent with other tools for example: npm, cargo, curl, wget**, which all show size + speed + percentage.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

**1. Restore human-readable sizes + total** (parity with #24266 — fetch `Content-Length` for the total).
**2. Add transfer speed + percentage** — adjacent concerns in #24226 that #24266 didn't implement.

When the total is known:
```
Downloading [4.1MB/47.2MB] (0.4MB/s, 8.7%)
```

When the total is unknown (no Content-Length):
```
Downloading [4.1MB] (0.4MB/s)
```

Notes:
- #24266 used binary units (MiB); MB or MiB — match the rest of Bun's CLI.
- Fetch `Content-Length` header up front so the total is available.
- Speed = rolling average over ~500ms to avoid jitter.
- Percentage: 1 decimal place below 100%, integer at 100%.
- Bounded to one line so it doesn't wrap on narrow terminals.

**Context:**
- Bun revision: `1.4.4+38afee6c8` (`bun --revision`)
- Command: `bun upgrade` (also `--canary`)
- Original PR: #24266 (Zig, `src/Progress.zig`, `std.fmt.fmtIntSizeBin`)
- Original tracking issue: #24226

### What alternatives have you considered?

1. **Restore-only** — closes the regression but skips the slow-network visibility improvements.
2. **ETA instead of speed** — less actionable on stalled connections (`0MB/s` flags a problem; a flat ETA hides it).
3. **Reuse a Rust crate** — `indicatif` or `humansize` handle edge cases; worth checking if Bun already has one before adding a new dep.
4. **Progress bar** — `[████░░░░░] 4.1MB/47.2MB (0.4MB/s, 8.7%)`. Nicer but

title: S3: support object tagging (x-amz-tagging) on write, writer and presign
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`Bun.S3Client` cannot set object tags. Tags are how S3 lifecycle rules select objects, so a common pattern is to tag staged or temporary uploads and let a bucket rule expire them, then drop the tag when the object becomes durable. Without tagging, an app using this pattern has to keep `@aws-sdk/client-s3` for every write that tags an object, which can be most of its writes.

(Bun 1.4.4. `S3Options` and `S3FilePresignOptions` have no tagging field, and there is no call to read or change an existing object's tags.)

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

A `tagging` option that sends `x-amz-tagging`, wherever an object is created:

```ts
await s3.write(key, data, { tagging: { state: "staged" } });
const writer = s3.file(key).writer({ tagging: { state: "staged" } });
// presigned PUT: the tag header is signed, so the client must send it as given
const url = s3.presign(key, { method: "PUT", tagging: { state: "staged" } });
```

Accepting either a record or the URL-encoded `key=value&...` string S3 uses would both work.

Optionally, object-level calls for existing objects (`GetObjectTagging` / `PutObjectTagging` / `DeleteObjectTagging`), for example `s3.file(key).tags()` and `s3.file(key).setTags({...})`.

If server-side copy lands (#29595), it would need the matching `TaggingDirective` (`COPY` / `REPLACE`) so a copy can drop a staged object's tags.

### What alternatives have you considered?

Keeping `@aws-sdk/client-s3` for tagged writes, which is what we do now. It works, but it keeps a second S3 client, its credentials handling and its error shape next to Bun's for one header.

title: Android: pidfd_open triggers uncatchable SIGSYS crash under seccomp filter
excerpt:
### Problem
In `src/sys/linux_syscall.rs`, Bun invokes raw syscall 434 (`SYS_pidfd_open`) when `target_os = "android"`.

While syscall 434 is part of the standard Linux ABI, default Android unprivileged seccomp policies (which apply to applications, Termux, and unprivileged user namespaces) do not allow `pidfd_open`.

When called on Android:
- The kernel does not return `ENOSYS` or `EPERM`.
- The kernel delivers an uncatchable `SIGSYS` (Bad system call) signal, crashing the Bun process immediately.

### Proposed Solution
Bun already handles unsupported pidfd by falling back to waiter threads and `signalfd` whenever `pidfd_open` returns `Err`.

Returning `Err(libc::ENOSYS)` directly on `target_os = "android"` avoids triggering the seccomp violation and cleanly directs Bun into its existing fallback logic.

title: Android: statx triggers SIGSYS under seccomp filter on older / vendor kernels
excerpt:
### Problem
In `src/sys/lib.rs`, `statx_impl` is gated under `#[cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "android"))]`, invoking `lx::statx` directly.

On Android (particularly devices on kernels < 5.4, Android 9–11, or vendor-customized kernels), `statx` is blocked by the default unprivileged seccomp filter. When invoked:
- The kernel does not return `ENOSYS` or `EPERM`.
- Instead, the kernel delivers an uncatchable `SIGSYS` (Bad system call) signal, crashing the process immediately.

Because the signal terminates execution immediately, Bun's errno-based fallback logic never gets a chance to run.

### Proposed Solution
For `target_os = "android"`, skip the raw `statx` syscall entirely and route directly to `statx_fallback` (POSIX `stat` / `lstat` / `fstatat`).

c-bindings: bun_close_range fails on Android devices running kernels < 5.9
excerpt:
### Problem
In src/jsc/bindings/c-bindings.cpp, bun_close_range directly calls syscall(__NR_close_range, ...).
The close_range syscall was added in Linux 5.9. Millions of Android 9-12 devices run vendor 4.14 or 4.19 kernels where this syscall returns ENOSYS or is killed by seccomp.

### Solution
Return -1 directly on defined(__ANDROID__) to let Bun cleanly use its userspace fallback loop.

title: install: make_executable fails with EOPNOTSUPP when lchmod is called on symlinks on Linux / Android
excerpt:
### Problem
In src/install/bin.rs, make_executable calls sys::lchmod(abs_target, mode).
Linux and Android kernels do not implement lchmod (fchmodat with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW returns ENOTSUP / EOPNOTSUPP). When installing via symlinks, binary permissions in cache are never made executable.

### Solution
If lchmod returns ENOTSUP / EOPNOTSUPP, resolve the target binary via realpath within Bun cache and chmod the actual file directly.

title: Bun.sql (Postgres): `sql.batch()` — statements that share one Sync, so a tenant-bound query is 1 round trip, not 3
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

A common Postgres pattern is "set per-request session state, then run the query." For row-level security that means `set_config('app.tenant', $1, true)` (or `set_config('role', …, true)`) followed by the statement, inside one transaction so the setting can't outlive the request on a pooled connection. With `Bun.sql` today that takes **3 network round trips** for a one-statement unit of work. The protocol allows **1**.

Captured on the wire (Bun 1.4.4, a proxy logging client→server writes as message types):

```
sql.begin(tx => Promise.all([tx`select set_config('app.org_id', ${id}, true)`, tx`select … where …`]))

WRITE Q(BEGIN)                       ← round trip 1 (simple query, awaited before the callback runs)
WRITE B E S | P D B E S              ← round trip 2 (both statements coalesced, but each carries its own Sync)
WRITE Q(COMMIT)                      ← round trip 3
```

On RDS a round trip is ~0.3–0.5 ms same-AZ (1–1.5 ms cross-AZ). A one-statement tenant-bound query pays ~0.6–3 ms it doesn't need, and a request that runs 4–6 such units pays that several times over.

**Why it can't be fixed from user land** (as of `bun-v1.4.4`):

- Every extended-protocol request ends in its own `Sync`. `bind_and_execute`, `parse_and_describe` and `parse_and_bind_and_execute` all finish with `protocol::SYNC` ([`PostgresRequest.rs#L306-L357`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/sql_jsc/postgres/PostgresRequest.rs#L306-L357)). Statements that share one `Sync` run in one implicit transaction, and an error skips the rest of the batch up to the `Sync`. That is exactly the fail-closed behaviour a tenant binding needs, at no extra round trips.
- `sql.begin()` sends `BEGIN` as a simple query and awaits it before running the callback ([`sql.ts#L308-L316`, `#L523-L547`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/js/bun/sql.ts#L308-L316)). Nothing is pipelined behind a simple query ([`PostgresSQLConnection.rs#L1872-L1882`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/bun-v1.4.4/src/sql_jsc/postgres/PostgresSQLConnection.rs#L1872-L1882)).
- A manual `BEGIN` is refused (`UNSAFE_TRANSACTION`) except on `reserve()`/`max: 1`. Even there it's a simple query, so it still costs its own round trip.
- `.simple()` multi-statement text does run under one `Sync`, but it can't carry bind parameters.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

A batch primitive whose statements share one `Sync`:

Run it:

Then, from another shell, request increasing body sizes:

title: CSS: preserve held prefixed background declarations before unparsed values
excerpt:
## Summary

`BackgroundHandler` can reorder prefixed background declarations across an unparsed value. This changes the cascade and can change the rendered gradient.

This defect exists on `main` independently of #46870. Track the handler change separately from that PR's gradient parser changes.

Requested by @robobun in https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46870#discussion_r4370589824.
Related PR: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/46870.

## Reproduction

Reported on `main` at commit `179664ea89`.

Save this as `a.css`:

```css
.r{background:-webkit-linear-gradient(red,blue);background:-moz-linear-gradient(red,blue);background:-webkit-radial-gradient(center,circle cover,yellow,green)}
```

Build with the default browser target:

```sh
bun build a.css --outdir=o
```

Also reproduce with `--target=bun`.

### Actual behavior

Main emits the declarations in this order:

1. `-moz-linear-gradient`
2. `-webkit-radial-gradient`
3. `-webkit-linear-gradient`

The requester reports that Chrome 153 paints the radial gradient for the source and the linear gradient for the output.

### Expected behavior

Preserve source order so that the last accepted background declaration remains the winner.

## Reported cause and affected areas

In `src/css/properties/background.rs`, the `Unparsed` arm of `BackgroundHandler::handle_property` (reported near Line 785) calls `flush`, which writes only the current fields. The prefixed declarations held in `self.decls` are written later in `finalize`, after the unparsed value.

Update the handler so held prefixed declarations are emitted before the unparsed background value. Review the effect on fallback removal, rather than treating this as an isolated serialization change.

Regression coverage belongs in `test/js/bun/css/css.test.ts`.

## Reported impact and direct-fix measurements

These measurements were supplied by @robobun and have not been independently reproduced for this issue:

- Among 2,140 real rule blocks from 407 npm packages, 13 blocks paint differently from their source at `--target=bun` because of this defect. Affected packages include smallipop, stylus-skeuomorphic, mc-wallet, and intro.js.
- A direct fix that writes held declarations before the unparsed value changes 16 of 400 whole real stylesheets.
- Across those whole stylesheets, default-target output grows by 0.043%. Prefixed fallbacks before an `-ms-` gradient line are then retained.
- None of the 15 stylesheets in `test/js/bun/css/files` changes output.

### Summary

V8-format heap snapshots can't exceed ~2 GiB of output. Past that, Bun silently returns an empty snapshot. A server with a few GB of heap therefore can't be heap-profiled at all.

This issue asks for two things:

1. **Bug: throw instead of returning `""`.** Check `hasOverflowed()` and throw a catchable error. This is a few lines per call site; details under "Additional information".
2. **Feature: stream V8 snapshots to a file, so snapshots over 2 GiB can be written.** Add a writer such as `Bun.writeHeapSnapshot(path)` that flushes the JSON in chunks instead of building one in-memory string. Then route `node:v8` `writeHeapSnapshot()`, `--heap-prof` and `worker.getHeapSnapshot()` through it. Details and a design sketch are in the last section.

(1) makes the failure visible. Only (2) lets large heaps be captured; that is the outcome we need.

1.4.4+38afee6c8. The code involved is unchanged on `main` at [`179664e`](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/tree/179664ea89f402c02af3fcd13b9bafeff1b7bcfd).

Windows 11 x64, 96 GiB RAM. The cause is in platform-independent code.

bash completion mishandles colon-delimited script names due to COMP_WORDBREAKS
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4

### What platform is your computer?

Linux / Android (aarch64)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. In a directory with a `package.json` containing colon-delimited scripts:
   ```json
   {
     "name": "repro",
     "scripts": {
       "build": "echo build",
       "build:nightly": "echo nightly",
       "build:release": "echo release",
       "reinstall": "echo reinstall"
     }
   }
   ```
2. Source `completions/bun.bash`.
3. Type `bun build:r` and hit `<TAB>`.
4. Clear the line, type `bun build:` and hit `<TAB>`.

### What is the expected behavior?

- `bun build:r<TAB>` should complete to `bun build:release`.
- `bun build:<TAB>` should display completion candidates: `build:nightly` and `build:release`.

### What do you see instead?

- `bun build:r<TAB>` autocompletes to `bun build:reinstall`.
- `bun build:<TAB>` shows nothing.

### Additional information

Bash includes `:` in `COMP_WORDBREAKS` by default. When completing `bun build:r`, Readline splits the token at the colon boundary into words `build`, `:`, and `r`. 

Inside `completions/bun.bash`, `cur_word` receives `"r"`. It filters the scripts array for entries matching prefix `"r"`, matches `"reinstall"`, and Readline appends that result after the colon delimiter on the prompt, resulting in `bun build:reinstall`.

This can be resolved in `completions/bun.bash` by either utilizing `__ltrim_colon_completions` (when bash-completion helpers exist) or adjusting/localizing `COMP_WORDBREAKS` handling around colon-delimited words.

title: Dynamic import of a file: URL drops its query: two queries give the same module instance
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0 aarch64 (Ubuntu 26.04)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`counter.mjs`:

```js
export let n = 0;
```

`query.mjs`:

```js
const tries = {
  relative: ["./counter.mjs?case=1", "./counter.mjs?case=2"],
  fileUrl: [new URL("./counter.mjs?case=3", import.meta.url).href, new URL("./counter.mjs?case=4", import.meta.url).href],
};
for (const [name, [first, second]] of Object.entries(tries)) {
  const a = await import(first), b = await import(second);
  console.log(name, a === b ? "same module" : "two modules");
}
```

```
$ bun query.mjs
relative two modules
fileUrl same module
```

### What is the expected behavior?

```
$ node query.mjs
relative two modules
fileUrl two modules
```

The module map is keyed by the whole URL, query included, so `file:///…/counter.mjs?case=3` and `file:///…/counter.mjs?case=4` are two modules, as they are with a relative specifier or an absolute path (`/…/counter.mjs?case=3`) in Bun.

### What do you see instead?

With a `file:` URL the query is dropped and both imports return the same module instance. Tests that make a fresh module per case by a query (`import(new URL("./x.ts?case=" + n, import.meta.url).href)`) share one module's state under Bun.

### Additional information

Workaround: pass the absolute path with the query (`fileURLToPath(url) + "?case=" + n`).

title: node:http: ServerResponse destroyed before its headers (after the handler returns) sends an empty `200 OK` instead of closing the connection
--use-system-ca on Windows imports certificates that are in the Disallowed store
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4 (`bun-v1.4.4`, 38afee6c84)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows (source analysis)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On Windows, add a private root CA to the machine `ROOT` store and the same certificate to the `Disallowed` store (explicit distrust). Serve HTTPS and WSS with a leaf issued by that CA, then run:

```ts
console.log((await fetch(process.env.HTTPS_URL!)).status);
const ws = new WebSocket(process.env.WSS_URL!);
ws.onopen = () => { console.log("ws open"); ws.close(); };
ws.onerror = e => console.log("ws error", e);
```

```sh
NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 bun run client.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

A certificate the user or administrator explicitly distrusts (present in `Disallowed`) is never imported as a trust anchor, so both requests fail certificate verification, matching how Windows itself treats it.

### What do you see instead?

From source: `packages/bun-usockets/src/crypto/root_certs_windows.cpp` (L84-L151 at 38afee6c84) enumerates `ROOT`, `CA` and `TrustedPeople` across the machine, enterprise, group-policy and current-user locations and filters by EKU, but never opens or consults `Disallowed`. A certificate that is both in `ROOT` and in `Disallowed` is therefore imported into the BoringSSL store and trusted by `fetch()` and `WebSocket` when system CA mode is on.

### Additional information

Suggested fix: load the `Disallowed` store (machine, group policy, enterprise and current user) first and skip any positive-store certificate whose hash appears there; add a test with a certificate present in both stores. I have not run a live Windows experiment; this is from reading the tagged source.

title: --use-system-ca on macOS imports roots not trusted for SSL (BasicX509 fallback ignores per-policy trust and scoped Deny)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4 (`bun-v1.4.4`, 38afee6c84)

### What platform is your computer?

macOS (source analysis)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Install a private root CA in a keychain with trust settings that trust it only for a non-SSL policy (for example S/MIME or code signing), or with a policy-scoped Deny for SSL. Serve HTTPS/WSS with a leaf issued by that CA and run the same client with `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` (or `--use-system-ca`):

```ts
console.log((await fetch(process.env.HTTPS_URL!)).status);
const ws = new WebSocket(process.env.WSS_URL!);
ws.onopen = () => { console.log("ws open"); ws.close(); };
ws.onerror = e => console.log("ws error", e);
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Only certificates macOS trusts for SSL server authentication are imported; a root trusted only for other policies, or denied for SSL, is not, so both requests fail verification as they would in Safari or `curl` using the system verifier.

### What do you see instead?

From source: `packages/bun-usockets/src/crypto/root_certs_darwin.cpp` (L314-L359, L365-L447, L482-L485 at 38afee6c84) walks user/admin/system trust settings, compares only the SSL policy OID, skips entries with application or policy-string constraints, and when no setting is decisive falls back to `SecTrustEvaluateWithError` with `SecPolicyCreateBasicX509()` instead of an SSL server policy. A certificate whose settings are skipped (scoped or non-SSL) can then pass the BasicX509 evaluation and be imported as a general anchor, which widens trust beyond what macOS grants for TLS.

### Additional information

Suggested fix: evaluate eligibility with `SecPolicyCreateSSL(true, NULL)` (or treat skipped/unsupported constraints as not-trusted) and honour scoped Deny; add tests for a non-SSL-only root and an SSL Deny. I have not run a live macOS experiment that modifies trust settings; this is from reading the tagged source.

--use-system-ca on Linux trusts CAs the distro deselected (scans raw /usr/share/ca-certificates)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4 (`bun-v1.4.4`, 38afee6c84)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux (Debian-based container)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. In a Debian container, put a new private CA certificate directly under `/usr/share/ca-certificates/` and do NOT select it (it is not listed in `/etc/ca-certificates.conf`, or it is deselected with `!`), then run `update-ca-certificates`. The generated `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` does not contain it.
2. Serve HTTPS and WSS with a leaf issued by that CA.
3. Run:

```ts
console.log((await fetch(process.env.HTTPS_URL!)).status);
const ws = new WebSocket(process.env.WSS_URL!);
ws.onopen = () => { console.log("ws open"); ws.close(); };
ws.onerror = e => console.log("ws error", e);
```

```sh
bun run client.ts                       # rejected (expected)
NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1 bun run client.ts  # accepted (unexpected)
bun build --compile --compile-exec-argv=--use-system-ca client.ts --outfile c && ./c   # accepted
```

### What is the expected behavior?

System CA mode trusts what the distribution has selected for TLS (the generated bundle / hashed `/etc/ssl/certs`), so a certificate the administrator deselected stays untrusted.

### What do you see instead?

Both `fetch()` and the built-in `WebSocket` accept the deselected CA when system CA mode is on. The Linux loader appears to scan raw certificate source directories, not only the distribution's generated trust output.

### Additional information

Reproduced in a throwaway container with a throwaway CA. Suggested fix: on Linux, load only the distro-generated bundle(s) (`/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`, `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`) and/or the hashed `/etc/ssl/certs` directory, never `/usr/share/ca-certificates`. Related: #46917 (Windows Disallowed) and #46918 (macOS SSL policy).

title: Bun.build: `export * from` a CommonJS package exports only `default` with `splitting` + `minify` (regression in 1.4.3)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4+38afee6c8 (also 1.4.4-canary.1+a8fcd319b; 1.4.2+744846f84 is correct)

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 unknown

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

With `splitting: true` and `minify: true` (its syntax pass), `export * from` a CommonJS package gives the entry no static named exports. Bun 1.4.2 gave it every name.

`entry.js`
```js
export * from 'react';
export { default } from 'react';
```

`other.js` (a second entry, so `splitting` emits a shared chunk)
```js
export * from 'react-dom';
```

`build.ts`
```ts
const r = await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ['./entry.js', './other.js'],
  outdir: './out',
  target: 'browser',
  format: 'esm',
  splitting: true,
  minify: true,
  define: { 'process.env.NODE_ENV': '"production"' },
});
const entry = r.outputs.find((o) => o.kind === 'entry-point' && o.path.endsWith('entry.js'))!;
console.log((await entry.text()).includes('useEffect'));
```

In an empty directory:

```sh
bun init -y
bun add react@19.3.0 react-dom@19.3.0
# write entry.js, other.js, build.ts as above
bun build.ts
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`true`, as on 1.4.2: the entry ends with `export { …, H as useEffect, …, M as useLayoutEffect, … }`, so `import { useEffect } from './entry.js'` works in a browser.

### What do you see instead?

`false` on 1.4.3, 1.4.4, and 1.4.4-canary.1. The entry is

```js
import{t,r,n,e}from"./chunk-2f3c1kpw.js";var o={};n(o,{default:()=>f.default});t(o,r(e()));var f=r(e());var p=f.default;export{p as default};
```

so a browser import of `useEffect` fails with "The requested module does not provide an export named 'useEffect'".

### Additional information

| Options | 1.4.2 | 1.4.3 | 1.4.4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `minify: true`, `splitting: true` | names | default only | default only |
| `minify: true`, `splitting: false` | names | names | names |
| `minify: { syntax: true }`, `splitting: true` | names | default only | default only |
| `minify: { identifiers: true }`, `splitting: true` | default only | default only | default only |
| `minify: { whitespace: true }`, `splitting: true` | default only | default only | default only |

So the syntax pass used to turn `export *` of a CommonJS module into static named exports, and with `splitting` it no longer does from 1.4.3. Naming the exports (`export { useEffect, … } from 'react'`) works on 1.4.4.

Found in a real project whose browser runtime bundles React as an entry chunk with `splitting`

title: WebSocket ping-pong throughput drops ~45% from v1.4.2 to v1.4.3 (Bun.serve and `ws`)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.8.0-117-generic aarch64 aarch64 (Ubuntu 24.04 container in a 2-vCPU Colima VM on an Apple M1; see Additional information for why this matters)

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This uses the benchmark from Daniel Lemire's post [WebSocket servers in JavaScript: Node.js, Bun and Deno in 2026](https://lemire.me/blog/2026/10/10/websocket-servers-in-javascript-node-js-bun-and-deno-in-2026/). The code is at [lemire/jswebsocket_bench](https://github.com/lemire/jswebsocket_bench) (commit `1b17e03`). The server is a plain `Bun.serve` relay with default options ([`server_bun.js`](https://github.com/lemire/jswebsocket_bench/blob/1b17e03/server_bun.js)): two clients are paired, and every message goes to the peer. The client is a small C program that sends 16-byte text frames, one round trip at a time (client A → server → client B → server → client A).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/lemire/jswebsocket_bench && cd jswebsocket_bench

# bun-1.4.2 / bun-1.4.3 = release binaries from GitHub (bun-linux-aarch64.zip)

Throughput and latency about the same as v1.4.2.

title: bun lint: JS plugin nodes have no start/end in TypeScript files
An empty `Bun.write(Bun.stderr, '')` truncates the file shared by `2>&1`, producing an empty output file with exit 0
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.3.14 (also observed on 1.4.4)

### What platform is Bun running on?

Linux arm64 (Ubuntu 24.04)

### What did you do?

```ts
// repro.ts
console.log('payload');
await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, '');
```

```bash
bun repro.ts > out 2>&1 ; wc -c < out
```

### What did you expect to see?

`8` — the file contains `payload\n`.

### What did you see instead?

`0` — the file exists and is empty. Exit code is 0.

### Isolation

Only the empty write to the `Bun.stderr` sink triggers it, and only when stderr is
redirected into the same file as stdout:

| program | redirect | bytes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `console.log('payload'); await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, '');` | `> out 2>&1` | **0** |
| same | `> out 2> err` | 8 (correct) |
| `console.log('payload'); await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, 'x');` | `> out 2>&1` | 9 (correct) |
| `console.log('payload'); console.error('');` | `> out 2>&1` | 9 (correct) |
| `console.log('payload'); process.stderr.write('');` | `> out 2>&1` | 9 (correct) |

Reproduced 3/3 runs on 1.3.14; a colleague reported the same on 1.4.4.

`strace -f` on the failing run shows the payload is written and then the shared descriptor
is truncated at exit:

```
write(1, "payload\n", 8) = 8
ftruncate(2, 0)          = 0
```

### Real-world shape

A process dispatcher that forwards a child's captured output:

```ts
const proc = Bun.spawn({ cmd: [...], stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' });
const [out, err] = await Promise.all([new Response(proc.stdout).text(), new Response(proc.stderr).text()]);
await Bun.write(Bun.stdout, out);
await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, err);   // empty whenever the child wrote nothing to stderr
```

The caller runs `tool > report.json 2>&1` and gets a valid, complete stdout write followed
by a zero-byte file, with a success exit code — so it looks like the tool produced no
output rather than like a redirect failure.

I have not determined the internal cause; the trace above is the extent of what I measured.

title: bun fmt: `jsdoc = true` is not idempotent on a fenced `@example` (appends `;` to the closing fence)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 24.6.0 arm64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`bunfig.toml`:

```toml
[fmt]
jsdoc = true
```

`a.ts`:

````ts
/**
 * Adds two numbers.
 *
 * @param a - The first number.
 * @param b - The second number.
 * @returns The sum of both numbers.
 *
 * @example
 * ```ts
 * const total = add(1, 2);
 * ```
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}
````

Run `bun fmt a.ts` twice.

### What is the expected behavior?

A fenced code block inside `@example` is formatted as code inside the fence, and the result is stable: a second `bun fmt` changes nothing (`bun fmt --check` passes after one run).

### What do you see instead?

**Pass 1** re-indents the fence (and moves `@example` above `@param`, which is fine):

````ts
/**
 * Adds two numbers.
 *
 * @example
 *   ```ts
 *   const total = add(1, 2);
 *   ```
 *
 * @param a - The first number.
 * ...
````

**Pass 2** treats the closing fence as code and appends a semicolon:

````diff
 *   const total = add(1, 2);
- *   ```
+ *   ```;
````

After pass 2 the comment is stable, but it is corrupted: the fence is no longer closed, so editors and TypeDoc render the rest of the comment as code.

So `jsdoc = true` is not idempotent on a fenced `@example`: after pass 1, `bun fmt --check` fails on a file `bun fmt` just wrote.

### Additional information

It looks like the pass-1 output (an indented fence under `@example`) is no longer recognized as a fence on pass 2, so the whole indented block, including the closing ` ``` `, is parsed as TypeScript. A fenced `@example` is the TSDoc-recommended form, so this blocks enabling `jsdoc` in any codebase that documents with fenced examples.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4+38afee6c8

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.2.11-arch1-1 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

```
// package.json
{ "name": "repro", "version": "1.0.0" }

// .env
FOO=bar
```

```sh
bun install
```

### What is the expected behavior?

`bun install` prints its usual output only, and nothing for a `.env` file it loads. At least one of `--silent` or `--quiet` should remove such a line.

### What do you see instead?

```
[0.03ms] ".env"
bun install v1.4.4 (38afee6c8)
No packages! Deleted empty lockfile

[0.00ms] done
```

With a real dependency (`bun add is-odd`) the first line is still there: `[0.02ms] ".env"`.

Variants tried:

- Without a `.env` file: the `[0.03ms] ".env"` line is gone.
- `bun install --silent`: still prints `[0.02ms] ".env"`.
- `bun install --quiet` with `NO_COLOR=1 CI=1 BUN_DEBUG_QUIET_LOGS=1`: still prints it.
- `BUN_QUIET`, `BUN_DEBUG_ALL=0`, `BUN_DEBUG=0` and `BUN_CONFIG_VERBOSE_FETCH=0`: still print it.
- `bun install --no-env-file`: no line, but see below.
- Canary 1.4.4-canary.1+a8fcd319b (npm `bun@1.4.4-canary.20261026.1`): same output.
- `bun run a.ts` in the same folder does not print the line.

### Additional information

A CLI that runs `bun install` with inherited stdio as one step of a larger command shows these lines among its own output, so the user sees a trace line that means nothing to them and `--quiet` modes of that CLI cannot keep their output clean.

`--no-env-file` is not a workaround: `.env` also feeds bunfig values such as a registry token (`token = "$TOK"` in `[install.registry]`), and with `--no-env-file` that token is no longer sent, so private packages fail to install.

title: node:http2: client originSet keeps the default :443 port, breaks got / got-scraping (still on 1.4.4)
excerpt:
Same bug as #18964 (still open), its still happening on Bun 1.4.4 even after the Rust rework, so opening a fresh one with a minimal repro and the exact cause.

Repro, no deps:

```js
import http2 from 'node:http2'
const s = http2.connect('https://www.google.com')
s.once('remoteSettings', () => { console.log(JSON.stringify(s.originSet)); s.close() })
```

Node v24.16.0: `["https://www.google.com"]`
Bun 1.4.4: `["https://www.google.com:443"]`

`http2-wrapper` 2.2.1 (used by `got` and `got-scraping`) compares `originSet[0]` against the requested origin (`source/agent.js:562`) and rejects with
`Requested origin https://www.google.com does not match server https://www.google.com:443`
so every HTTPS host that negotiates h2 fails under Bun, and works on Node.

Cause is `initOriginSet` in `src/js/node/http2.ts:4018-4020`, it builds `https://${hostName}:${remotePort}` and adds it as is. Node does the same but runs it through `getURLOrigin()` (`lib/internal/http2/core.js:712`), which drops the default port. So the fix should be just:

```js
originSet.add(new URL(originString).origin)
```

Also `removeOriginFromSet` builds the origin without a port, so right now it never matches the seeded entry either.

Workaround from now is `http2: false` in `got-scraping`.

Startup lists every entry of each ancestor directory, so a no-op script slows down linearly with unrelated files in parent folders
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4+38afee6c8 (also reproduced on 1.4.3+c6da4a4d3)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.17.0-41-generic x86_64 x86_64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Startup time for a script that does nothing grows with the number of files in the folders *above* it, even when those files have nothing to do with the program. Before any JavaScript runs, Bun reads every entry of every ancestor directory of the working directory and of the entry point's folder, and hashes each one into the resolver's directory cache.

We noticed it because hook scripts we run hundreds of times an hour were slow whenever they started from a working directory under `/tmp`, which had about 22,500 entries on our dev machine. Moving the same scripts' working directory to a normal project folder took their median CPU per start from about 33 ms down to about 13 ms. That comparison isn't paired, so here is a controlled reproduction:

```bash
base=$(mktemp -d -p "$HOME")   # outside /tmp, so a busy /tmp doesn't skew the control row
: > "$base/bunfig.toml"
for n in 0 4096 24576 100000; do
  mkdir -p "$base/p$n/child"
  (cd "$base/p$n" && seq -f 'noise-%06g' 1 "$n" | xargs -r touch)
done

for n in 0 4096 24576 100000; do
  cd "$base/p$n/child"
  printf '%s siblings: ' "$n"
  strace -f -e trace=getdents64 bun --no-env-file --config="$base/bunfig.toml" -e 'void 0;' 2>&1 >/dev/null \
    | grep -c getdents64
done
```

The `noise-*` files are empty and sit next to the working directory, never inside it. The program is `void 0;`.

I'd love a sanity check on this from someone who knows the resolver: I may be missing a reason the full listing is needed this early.

### What is the expected behavior?

Starting a program that imports nothing should cost about the same no matter how many unrelated files sit in a parent directory. Bun's config and project discovery would still find `bunfig.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` and `node_modules` exactly as it does today.

### What do you see instead?

Cost scales linearly with the sibling count, by roughly 0.4 ms per 1,000 entries, on both 1.4.3 and 1.4.4.

Measured with the official `bun-linux-x64` release binaries, 40 interleaved runs per row after a warm-up, `--no-env-file` and an empty `--config` file, on a 16-core machine that was busy at the time (load average ~25). For comparison, a program that only uses `Bun.serve`, built with the same flags:

```

That build shows no blocker.

### Additional information

Many npm packages import `node:http`, including mongodb (`lib/utils.js`) and ssh2 (`lib/http-agents.js`). On a Hono server with pg, mysql2, mongodb and ssh2, the trim report shows no other blocker once ssh2's optional native `require()` calls are stubbed.

excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`bun test --coverage` writes coverage only as the text table or as `lcov.info`. Jest and Vitest also accept Istanbul's JSON reporters, `json-summary` (`coverage/coverage-summary.json`) and `json` (`coverage/coverage-final.json`). CI steps written for those runners read these files to post a coverage summary, draw a badge or compare against a base branch. Under `bun test` the reporter names are rejected, so those steps need a separate lcov-to-JSON conversion.

Versions checked:

```
$ bun --revision
1.4.4+38afee6c8
$ bun --revision   # canary
1.4.4-canary.1+5c6d4e24c
```

Platform: Windows 11 x64. Newer canaries than `1.4.4-canary.1` were not tested.

Three files in an empty folder:

`src.ts`

```ts
export function pick(flag: boolean) {
  if (flag) {
    return "yes";
  }
  return "no";
}
```

`cov.test.ts`

```ts
import { test, expect } from "bun:test";
import { pick } from "./src";
test("one branch", () => expect(pick(true)).toBe("yes"));
```

`bunfig.toml`

```toml
[test]
coverage = true
```

Run:

```sh
bun test --coverage-reporter=json-summary
bun test --coverage-reporter=json
```

Output on 1.4.4 and on 1.4.4-canary.1 (identical), exit code 1, nothing written:

```
error: invalid coverage reporter 'json-summary'. Available options: 'text' (console output), 'lcov' (code coverage file)
error: invalid coverage reporter 'json'. Available options: 'text' (console output), 'lcov' (code coverage file)
```

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Accept two more values for `--coverage-reporter` and `[test] coverageReporter`, written to `coverageDir` like `lcov.info`:

- `json-summary`: `coverage-summary.json` in Istanbul's summary shape, a `total` entry and one entry per file, each metric as `{ "total", "covered", "skipped", "pct" }`. Bun reports lines and functions today, and branches once #46534 lands.
- `json`: `coverage-final.json`, Istanbul's per-file coverage object.

### What alternatives have you considered?

- Converting `lcov.info` to JSON with a separate script in CI after `bun test`.
- Parsing the text table, which breaks whenever its columns change (#46534 adds a `% Branch` column and moves `Uncovered Line #s`).

### Related

- #6716 asks for Istanbul instrumentation, not for these output formats.

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`import.meta.hot?.accept(...)` is a guarded form that keeps a module working outside a dev server, where `import.meta.hot` is `undefined`.

`index.html`:

```html
<!doctype html><html><body><script type="module" src="./main.ts"></script></body></html>
```

`main.ts`:

```ts

console.log("module ran");
```

Open `bun ./index.html` in a browser and look at the console. Or print what the dev server serves:

`dev.ts`:

```ts

const s = Bun.serve({ port: 0, routes: { "/": index }, development: true });
const html = await (await fetch(s.url)).text();
const src = html.match(/src="([^"]+\.js)"/)?.[1];
const js = await (await fetch(new URL(src!, s.url))).text();
console.log("served:", js.split("\n").find((l) => l.includes("accept(() =>"))?.trim());
console.log("runtime:", js.match(/indirectHot=new Proxy.*?indirectly\.`\)/)?.[0]);
s.stop(true);
```

```sh

```

### What is the expected behavior?

`import.meta.hot?.accept(cb)` behaves like `import.meta.hot.accept(cb)`: the module accepts its own updates and `module ran` is logged.

### What do you see instead?

```

runtime: indirectHot=new Proxy({},{get(e,t){if(typeof t==="symbol")return;throw Error(`import.meta.hot.${t} cannot be used indirectly.`)
```

    at Object.get (http://localhost:41760/_bun/client/index-0000000092079171.js:21:8367)
    at main.ts (http://localhost:41760/_bun/client/index-0000000092079171.js:29:20)

The same line without `?.` (`import.meta.hot.accept(() => {})`) works.

- PR #35009 fixed exactly this (it described the parser skipping the `import.meta.hot` rewrite when `optional_chain` is set). It was closed unmerged by the inactivity bot on 2026-10-20.
- #46836 (open) makes the `accept(dep)` callback optional; it does not touch the `?.` form.

title: `Module._extensions[".ts"] = Module._extensions[".js"]` makes `require()` parse a `.ts` file as plain JavaScript; Node strips its types
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

```
1.4.4+38afee6c8
```

Also reproduced on `1.4.4-canary.1+5c6d4e24c`. Newer canaries were not tested.

### What platform is your computer?

```
Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64
```

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

`types.ts`:

```ts
export type Foo = { value: number };
```

`spec.ts`:

```ts
import type { Foo } from "./types";
const value: number = (1 as number)!;
const typed: Foo = { value };
module.exports = typed;
```

`swapped.cjs`:

```js
const Module = require("node:module");
Module._extensions[".ts"] = Module._extensions[".js"];
try {
  console.log("swapped:", JSON.stringify(require("./spec.ts")));
} catch (e) {
  console.log("FAIL", e.name, String(e.message).split("\n")[0]);
}
```

```sh
bun swapped.cjs
node swapped.cjs
```

Without the assignment, `require("./spec.ts")` returns `{"value":1}` on both runtimes.

### What is the expected behavior?

Node v26.7.0:

```
swapped: {"value":1}
```

In Node, the `.js` handler picks the format from the file name it is given, so it still strips types from a `.ts` file. In Node 26.7.0 `Object.keys(Module._extensions)` is `.js, .json, .node` and `Module._extensions[".ts"]` is `undefined`, so Node already sends `.ts` files through the `.js` handler by default and this assignment changes nothing there. (A handler that throws, assigned to `.ts`, is called on both runtimes, so both consult `Module._extensions[".ts"]`.)

Bun has its own `.ts`, `.cts`, `.mjs` and `.mts` handlers, and each built-in handler forces its own loader. The request is that the `.js` handler choose the loader from the file name, as Node does. Bun's existing test `custom require extension overwrite default loader with other default loader` (test/js/node/module/require-extensions.test.ts), which pins the mirror case `.js = .ts`, would still pass with that.

### What do you see instead?

```
FAIL BuildMessage Expected "from" but found "{"
```

Bun's `.js` handler forces the JavaScript parser on the TypeScript file, so the first TypeScript-only token (`import type`, a `!` non-null assertion, a type annotation) is a parse error.

### Additional information

- Real-world trigger: `@playwright/test` 1.64.1 runs this assignment for `.ts`, `.cts`, `.tsx` and `.jsx` when it runs under Bun, so `bun --bun node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test --list` prints `Total: 0 tests in 0 files` and one `AggregateError: N errors building "<spec>.ts"` (`Expected "from" but found "{"`, `Unexpected !`) per CommonJS

excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

In the current Bun WebKit fork, [WTF::currentProcessMemoryStatus](https://github.com/oven-sh/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WTF/wtf/linux/CurrentProcessMemoryStatus.cpp) opens `/proc/self/statm`, reads a line, and closes the file on every call.

Besides the syscall overhead, each open requires pathname lookup. Linux documents [mount_lock as a global seqlock](https://docs.kernel.org/filesystems/path-lookup.html#mount-lock). For example, [Linux 5.15.167 path_init](https://github.com/gregkh/linux/blob/v5.15.167/fs/namei.c#L2324-L2343) starts by reading the mount and rename sequence counters. Repeated opens therefore expose the caller to pathname-lookup contention even though the desired data is just the current process's memory statistics.

This is a source-based performance/resilience suggestion. It does not imply that Bun causes the underlying host mount contention, or that eliminating this one path would eliminate every possible runtime stall.

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

Consider retaining a process-local descriptor for `/proc/self/statm` and using `pread(fd, buffer, size, 0)` for subsequent samples.

The descriptor would be reused, **not the memory-statistics values**: each call would still read fresh data and use the existing parsing/accounting semantics. Using `pread` also avoids sharing a mutable file offset between callers.

Implementation details to account for:

- Open with close-on-exec and define the descriptor's lifetime.
- Handle fork correctly: an inherited proc descriptor must not make a child report its parent's memory.
- Handle concurrent calls, EINTR, failed opens/reads, and any desired fallback.
- Preserve the existing behavior when statistics cannot be obtained.

Suggested validation: check that repeated calls no longer reopen the pathname, compare reported fields with fresh reads, exercise concurrent callers, and verify child-process behavior after fork.

Would this be an appropriate improvement in Bun's WebKit fork, or should it be proposed directly upstream to WebKit?

### What alternatives have you considered?

Caching the sampled RSS value would introduce stale data, while reducing the sampling frequency changes the freshness of memory-pressure decisions. Retaining only the descriptor avoids both tradeoffs.

Fixing host-side filesystem contention is complementary, but does not remove repeated pathname lookup from this function.

title: Bun.Image: resize(width) with fit: "inside" returns width - 1 (derived height truncated, then re-fitted)
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4 (38afee6c8), Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Any 1001×667 image (PNG or JPEG behave the same), e.g. `magick -size 1001x667 xc:gray a.png`:

```ts
const src = await Bun.file("a.png").bytes();
for (const [w, h, o] of [[400], [400, undefined, { fit: "inside" }], [400, 400, { fit: "inside" }], [150, undefined, { fit: "inside" }]] as const) {
  const img = new Bun.Image(src).resize(w, h, o).png();
  await img.bytes();
  console.log(`resize(${w}, ${h}, ${JSON.stringify(o)}) -> ${img.width}x${img.height}`);
}
```

### What is the expected behavior?

The requested width is kept, the other side follows the aspect ratio:

```
resize(400)                          -> 400x267
resize(400, undefined, {fit:inside}) -> 400x267
resize(400, 400, {fit:inside})       -> 400x267
resize(150, undefined, {fit:inside}) -> 150x100
```

(667 × 400 / 1001 = 266.53; sharp/libvips round it to 267.)

### What do you see instead?

```
resize(400)                          -> 400x266
resize(400, undefined, {fit:inside}) -> 399x266   <- requested width not honoured
resize(400, 400, {fit:inside})       -> 400x267
resize(150, undefined, {fit:inside}) -> 149x99    <- requested width not honoured
```

It looks like the missing height is first derived by truncation (266.53 → 266), then the 1001×667 source is fitted inside the 400×266 box, which brings the width down to floor(1001 × 266 / 667) = 399. Two consequences:

- with `fit: "inside"` the caller cannot get the width they asked for (149 instead of 150, 599 instead of 600 with `withoutEnlargement`). On a sample of 300 real catalogue images, the requested width was missed for 16 % of them at `w=150`;
- the derived side is truncated in the width-only path but rounded when both sides are given (`400, 400` → 400x267), so the same request gives two answers.

### Additional information

Not the same as #44073 (JPEG shrink-on-load reference dimensions): this one also happens with PNG.
Rounding the derived dimension, and not re-fitting a box that was itself derived from the source ratio, would match sharp (`fit: "inside"` keeps the given dimension exactly).

title: Bun.Image: allow resize by height only; resize(0, h) silently returns a 1-pixel-wide image
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4 (38afee6c8), Linux x64

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

With a 1001×667 image:

```ts
new Bun.Image(src).resize(0, 100);          // -> 1x100, no error
new Bun.Image(src).resize(undefined, 100);  // throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE (width is required)
```

### What is the expected behavior?

1. A way to resize to a target height and derive the width from the aspect ratio, like sharp's `resize(null, 100)` / `resize({ height: 100 })` → 150x100. Thumbnails of a fixed height are a common case (ours are 100 px high).
2. `0`, a negative number or `NaN` as a dimension should either mean "auto" or throw — not produce a degenerate 1-pixel image silently.

### What do you see instead?

`width` is required, and `0` / `NaN` / `-1` all yield a 1×h image. The only workaround today is `resize(16383, 100, { fit: "inside" })`, which gives 150x100 but is about 2× slower than sharp on a 4000×3000 JPEG (it seems to defeat shrink-on-load).

### Additional information

Related to #40490 (options not validated).

title: Bun.Image: expose chroma subsampling for .jpeg() (4:4:4)
excerpt:
### What is the problem this feature would solve?

`.jpeg()` always writes 4:2:0 chroma subsampling. Book covers and title pages are mostly coloured text and thin lines; 4:2:0 visibly bleeds red/blue text into the paper. Against the source, a red-on-white text sample measures ΔRMSE 0.0176 with Bun's 4:2:0 vs 0.0106 with sharp `chromaSubsampling: "4:4:4"`. This is the main thing that keeps us on sharp for serving. Passing `chromaSubsampling: "4:4:4"` today is silently ignored (see #40490).

### What is the feature you are proposing to solve the problem?

```ts
img.jpeg({ quality: 82, chromaSubsampling: "4:4:4" });
```

with the sharp option name and values (`"4:2:0"` default, `"4:4:4"`), mapped to libjpeg-turbo's `TJSAMP_444`. `optimizeCoding` (#40494) would be the natural companion.

### What alternatives have you considered?

sharp with `chromaSubsampling: "4:4:4", mozjpeg: true` — what we run in production today.
Mentioned in passing in #32122; this issue isolates the JPEG part.

title: Windows: empty Bun.write to piped stdout/stderr throws EINVAL: invalid argument, ftruncate
excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

`1.4.4-canary.1+11c367163` (Windows x64), installed with `bun upgrade --canary` before this investigation.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The smallest failing operation is:

```ts
await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, '')
```

It fails when stderr is a pipe. To reproduce with an explicit pipe, save the following dependency-free script as `repro.ts` and run `bun repro.ts`:

```ts
const child = Bun.spawnSync(
  [process.execPath, '--no-env-file', '-e', 'await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, "")'],
  { stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' },
)
console.log('exit:', child.exitCode)
console.log(child.stderr.toString())
```

No dependencies or repository imports are needed. I also reproduced it directly with `bun -e 'await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, "")'` under a command runner that captures stderr through a pipe. Native console handles were not tested.

### What is the expected behavior?

An empty write to piped stdout/stderr should write zero bytes and resolve successfully, without attempting to truncate the pipe.

### What do you see instead?

Exit code 1. Complete captured stack below (only the local directory has been replaced with `<repro-dir>`):

```text
1 | await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, "")
              ^
EINVAL: invalid argument, ftruncate
      fd: 2,
 syscall: "ftruncate",
   errno: -4071,
    code: "EINVAL"

      at <repro-dir>\[eval]:1:11

Bun v1.4.4-canary.1+11c367163 (Windows x64)
```

### Additional information

Isolation on the same installed revision (one run per matrix case):

| Operation with piped stdio | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, '')` | exit 1, `ftruncate` EINVAL, fd 2 |
| `await Bun.write(Bun.stdout, '')` | exit 1, `ftruncate` EINVAL, fd 1 |
| `await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, new Uint8Array())` | exit 1, `ftruncate` EINVAL |
| `await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, 'x')` | exit 0 |
| `await Bun.write(Bun.stdout, 'x')` | exit 0 |
| `process.stderr.write('')` | exit 0 |
| `process.stdout.write('')` | exit 0 |
| `const w = Bun.stderr.writer(); w.write(''); await w.flush()` | exit 0 |

Redirecting either descriptor to an existing regular file instead of a pipe makes the empty `Bun.write` exit 0 and truncate an 8-byte sentinel file to zero bytes.

The real-world trigger was a command-line gate forwarding its result:

```ts
const verdict = await gate()
await Bun.write(Bun.stdout, verdict.stdout)
await Bun.write(Bun.stderr, verdict.stderr)
process.exit(verdict.status)

title: Random values repeat in Bun processes restored from one VM snapshot (crypto.randomUUID, getRandomValues, Math.random)
excerpt:
### What happened

We restore many Firecracker microVMs from one memory snapshot of a guest in which a compiled Bun server (`bun build --compile`, Bun 1.4.4 canary) was already running. Every clone then returns **the same** values from:

- `crypto.randomUUID()`
- `crypto.getRandomValues()`
- `Math.random()`

The guest kernel's generator does differ between the clones: `/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid` returned a different value in each. Firecracker exposes a VM generation ID device, and Linux reseeds its own generator when the VM generation changes. Bun's generators keep the state they had when the snapshot was taken.

### Reproduction

1. Run a Bun server in a Firecracker guest. The guest kernel needs `CONFIG_VMGENID`, and Firecracker exposes the device on x86_64.
2. Pause the guest and take a full snapshot.
3. Restore the snapshot into three new Firecracker processes, and resume each.
4. In each clone, call a route that returns:
   ```ts
   return Response.json({
     kernel_uuid: (await Bun.file("/proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid").text()).trim(),
     random_uuid: crypto.randomUUID(),
     get_random_values: Buffer.from(crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))).toString("hex"),
     math_random: Math.random(),
   });
   ```

Observed: `kernel_uuid` differs between the three clones, and `random_uuid`, `get_random_values`, and `math_random` are identical in all three.

### Why it matters

Any token, key, nonce, or ID that a cloned process generates after the restore is the same in every clone of the snapshot. That covers session tokens, UUIDs used as primary keys, and nonces. Snapshot-and-clone is how microVM platforms make cold starts fast, for example Firecracker-based serverless platforms and agent sandboxes. Firecracker documents the hazard in its "random for clones" guide: https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/blob/main/docs/snapshotting/random-for-clones.md

The workaround is to snapshot before Bun starts, and start Bun in each clone after the restore. In our measurements that costs about 18 ms per start, and about 5 MiB more private memory per clone, because the clones no longer share Bun's initialized heap.

### Where the state lives (from reading the source)

- `boringssl_sys::rand_bytes` is BoringSSL's `RAND_bytes`, described in the source as "a thread-local AES-CTR DRBG seeded once from the OS entropy source and then run entirely in userspace".
- `crypto.randomUUID()` takes from a buffered pool, via `rare_data().next_uuid()`.

excerpt:
### What version of Bun is running?

1.4.4+38afee6c8

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

In an empty directory, with no Prettier or Bun config:

```sh
printf '```\nA\n   \nB\n```\n' > x.md
bun fmt --check x.md; echo "exit=$?"
bunx prettier@3.9.10 --check x.md; echo "exit=$?"
```

The third line of the code block holds three spaces and nothing else.

### What is the expected behavior?

The same result as Prettier, which the docs promise ("The same output as Prettier"). Prettier 3.9.10, the current `latest`, flags the file and, when it writes, empties the whitespace-only line. 4.0.0-alpha.13 (`next`) does the same.

```
$ bunx prettier@3.9.10 --check x.md
Checking formatting...
[warn] x.md
[warn] Code style issues found in the above file. Run Prettier with --write to fix.
exit=1

$ bunx prettier@3.9.10 x.md | od -c
0000000    `   `   `  \n   A  \n  \n   B  \n   `   `   `  \n
```

### What do you see instead?

`bun fmt --check` passes the file, and `bun fmt` leaves the three spaces in place:

```
$ bun fmt --check x.md; echo "exit=$?"
1 file is formatted.
exit=0

$ bun fmt x.md && od -c x.md
Formatted 0 files, 1 unchanged [9.14ms]
0000000    `   `   `  \n   A  \n              \n   B  \n   `   `   `  \n
```

### Additional information

The same happens to trailing whitespace on any line. In a code block that neither tool formats as a language, Prettier strips it from every line and `bun fmt` keeps it. A fenced `js` block, which both format as code, comes out the same. Output byte counts from `--stdin-filepath c.md`, same versions:

| Input (`printf`) | In | `bun fmt` | Prettier | `--check` (bun / prettier) |

| ```` ```\nA\n   \nB\n```\n ```` whitespace-only line | 16 | 16 | 13 | 0 / 1 |
| ```` ```\nA   \nB\n```\n ```` trailing spaces after code | 15 | 15 | 12 | 0 / 1 |
| ```` ```\nA\n\t\nB\n```\n ```` tab-only line | 14 | 14 | 13 | 0 / 1 |

| ```` ```js\nconst a = 1;\n   \nconst b = 2;\n```\n ```` | 40 | 37 | 37 | 1 / 1 |

The fence's info string makes no difference for unformatted languages: an untagged fence, `text` and `sh` all give the same result.

Keeping the text is arguably the more faithful reading of CommonMark, since a code block's content is literal. But with the two disagreeing, a file that passes `bun fmt --check` can still fail `prettier --check`.
